english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot in the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much sitting water around the cassava roots starves them of air and allows root-rot disease to grow. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots dry.
ga: nu ni ebɔle he lɛ Kasava shishifãi babaoo tsɔ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni egbiɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young crops when the weeds are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mitso bibioo lɛ He ni jwɛi lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your young crops. Clearing them early allows your crops to grow strong without competing for food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ niyenii akaŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as living shades, protecting the young cocoa plants from drying out during their early growth stage.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties typically begin bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties generally take between 4 to 5 years to start yielding fruit.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa seedlings on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is not advisable to plant cassava with young cocoa because cassava roots expand aggressively and consume large amounts of nutrients and soil moisture, which starves the young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ akɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ adu ŋmei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kookoo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and fall off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants drop leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps keep moisture in the ground during dry months.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa branches fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji Mi-kookoo niji babaoo gbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can naturally support. Flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree naturally sheds excess flowers to save energy for pod growth.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: What causes my small green cocoa pods to turn black and rot on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ? Minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and trimming branches helps keep the air dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I trim or prune the extra branches on my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing and diseased branches so that sunlight and air can pass through the tree. This airflow reduces plant diseases and encourages the tree to channel its strength into producing pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni kɛ hela baaa kɛ helai ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ nɛɛ haa tso helai baa shi ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛfee pod.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, fertile, dark, and well-drained. If rain water gathers and sits on top of your land for days without soaking in, the soil will drown the cocoa roots and is not suitable.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, nɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni eta oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni etsɔɔɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ebaafee nɔ ni esaaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the forest trees above them grow too big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ koo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ dara tsɔ lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need shade, mature cocoa trees need adequate sunlight to produce food, flower, and grow heavy pods. Excessive overhead shade reduces flowering and lowers your harvest.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia kokoo tsei bibii. Kakao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo niyenii, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni tsii. Shade ni fe nine ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ haa fɔfɔi baa shi ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Planting cocoa seedlings too close together forces them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight. This results in tall, weak trees that produce fewer pods and create dense shade where diseases spread easily.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa he ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do some crops grow very well in the Bono Region but struggle in parts of the Ashanti Region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Bono kpokpaa lɛ nɔ shi amɛnaa amanehulu yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Crops thrive based on specific soil types, rainfall patterns, and temperatures. Even neighboring regions or districts have different soil compositions and weather conditions that favor certain crops over others.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ naa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo pɔtɛɛ Kpokpai loo kpokpai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi fe ekrokomɛi.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is good for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Cassava grows best in loose, well-drained sandy-loam soils where its roots can expand easily. Sticky clay soil that holds too much water will cause the cassava roots to rot.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that heavy water logging in the soil is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ loo nu ni ahiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I burn my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã ŋmɔ lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and essential soil nutrients, kills helpful soil organisms like earthworms, and leaves the soil bare and exposed to dry winds and soil erosion.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting and dying from the roots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When the soil stays wet for too long without draining properly, soil fungi attack the plant roots and cause root rot, preventing the plant from taking up water and food.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa tsei shishifãi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress during hot spells, lack vital soil nutrients, or are attacked by small insects like mirids that damage young buds.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔii kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ashwishwɛi ni fiteɔ hiŋmɛii lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do the bunches on my plantain trees stay small and ripen early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ ji bibii ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ?

english: Plantains need regular moisture and fertile soil. Lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or root damage from soil pests causes the tree to mature small fruits early to survive.
ga: Plantains he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Nu ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Loo shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii mra. koni ehi wala mli

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat wave or a short dry spell that can scorch delicate seedlings. It is safer to wait until the rains are steady and regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ kuku loo hɔmɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ fiofio ni ebaa shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing much fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight and space, putting all their energy into growing tall instead of building strong stems and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ he ko he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeefee tsei ashishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai.

english: What causes my yam tubers to develop dark rot spots while still in the ground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato tubers lɛ miifee ŋmeii diji ni egbo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Underground yam rot is usually caused by microscopic worms called nematodes or soil fungi that enter the tubers through wet, infected soil or unclean planting seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ loo dumɔwui ni he tseee nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: You should wait until the rainy season settles with at least two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil deep down. Planting too early during small, scattered rains can cause your seeds to dry up and die before they fully germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba naagbee ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do I need to rotate the crops I grow on my piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every year drains specific food from the soil and allows pests that like that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops, like planting beans after maize, keeps the soil fertile and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛkɛ lɛ ŋmãa. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: How do groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa fe tsei krokomɛi?

english: Groundnuts belong to a special family of plants that can capture nitrogen food directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that food remains in the soil to nourish the next crops you plant.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku krɛdɛɛ ko ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and leaf color. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni saa baa lɛ dalɛ kɛ baa lɛ su he Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam plants use their climbing vines to lift their leaves up high toward the sun to make food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves dry and off the wet ground so they do not rot, leading to larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ wain tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. koni ekafite Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baafee agbo.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so quickly if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya nɛkɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep dropping off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or when the soil becomes too dry. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water sits around them in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and dry up while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black because of a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in dark, damp, and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight into the farm, which dries out moisture and stops the disease.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ hewɔ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni helai akpa.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tight and the plant stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by sudden changes in water supply. Controlling tiny insects early and watering consistently keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu jɛɛhei ni tsakeɔ trukaa lɛ mli Kooloi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra Kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: How do I know if my cassava is mature enough to harvest so that it doesn't end up watery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa koni ekɛ nu akafee nɔ ko?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. Harvesting a test tuber first lets you check if the flesh is firm and starchy before digging up the whole farm.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Kɛ́ oŋɔ bulb lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okwɛ kɛji eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Dani ebaakumɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why do my maize cobs start cracking on the farm before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Leaving mature maize cobs on the stalk for too long in hot sun causes the kernels to lose moisture too quickly and shrink, leading to cracked grains. Harvesting as soon as the outer husks turn dry and papery prevents this loss.
ga: Abɛi ni eda lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee oya tsɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui lɛ amli fãmɔ. Nikpamɔ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ egbi ni efee wolo pɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my green plantains turn soft and yellow so quickly when I pack them in sacks to send to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya beni mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli koni mikɛmaje jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Green plantains trapped in tightly closed sacks trap a natural ripening gas called ethylene and generate heat. Transporting them in ventilated crates or open baskets keeps them cool and slows down premature ripening.
ga: Plantains eŋɔlii ni akɛwo kotokui ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa amɛshwereɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa. Kɛ akɛwo adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli loo tsɛnsi ni agbele mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha edɔ ni ebaaha ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my tomatoes bruise and go bad so fast right after picking them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ oya beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes picked during the heat of the afternoon are warm and fragile, making their skins break easily when stacked. Harvesting early in the morning when the fruit is cool keeps the skin firm and protects it during handling.
ga: Tomato ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebaafee mlɛo. Ehaa hewolo lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ ato he kome Nikpamɔ leebi be mli ni aduawai lɛ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni ebuɔ he yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from sprouting leaves while I store them before sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ baai yɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ dani mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers sprout when kept in warm, damp, or dark places because the tuber thinks it is time to grow a new plant. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated traditional yam barn off the ground keeps them dormant longer.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni edɔ, loo duŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ susuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛdu tso hee. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato blema sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli, ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing small, pale fruits instead of big, bright ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii ni mli tse yɛ aduawai wuji ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need extra food like potassium when they start flowering to build large, thick-walled fruits. If the soil lacks nutrients or dries out during flowering, the plant produces smaller, pale peppers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ potassium, beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi shishi koni amɛfee aduawai agboi ni gbogboi yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai loo egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni mli tse koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my garden eggs develop dark rot spots at the bottom while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egboi yɛ amɛshishi be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark sunken spots on garden eggs are usually blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit when watering is irregular. Giving the crops consistent water helps the roots absorb the calcium needed for strong fruit skins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ diŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli kɛ́ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants drop their flowers without producing any pods during hot sunny weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi gumbo tso lɛ shĩɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli yɛ otsi kome ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Okra sheds its flowers as a defense mechanism when it suffers heat stress or lacks water. Providing steady moisture at the root level during hot spells helps the plant keep its flowers and turn them into pods.
ga: Okra shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛbuɔ ehe kɛji hulutsoo loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ miipiŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsakeɔ amɛ efeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Rolling up leaves is a maize plant's natural way of reducing the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve water. If the leaves unroll in the evening, the plant is surviving, but continuous rolling means it needs urgent watering.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi gbɛkɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Shi shwiemɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu oya he miihia.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my main crops help my farm yield better?
ga: Te cowpea ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This natural soil enrichment feeds neighboring crops without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting plantain trees next to young cocoa provides the necessary shade and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why is my maize staying small and pale green instead of growing dark and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize turns pale green or yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the crop regain its dark green color and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant suffers from heat stress, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Providing steady water and balanced nutrients helps the flowers stay on the stem to form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and hiding inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni akɛteeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in maize fields. Regularly inspecting your farm and applying recommended biopesticides into the leaf funnels early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fɔɔ baa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye amɛnɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates damp soil and high humidity, which spread fungal and bacterial diseases that rot tomato roots and stems. Planting on raised soil beds improves water drainage and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tomato shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in low-lying or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on ridges or raised earth mounds allows excess rainwater to flow away, protecting the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shishi loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii loo gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ joɔ foi, ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the maize crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stems and very small ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops receive all the food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my land produce less crop every year when I plant maize on the same field continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up crop-specific pests. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and dry, and the inside of the pods develops dark brown markings when you open a sample plant.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni pod lɛ mli baaná okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni ogbeleɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Red leaves do not automatically mean insects are attacking your farm. Crops often turn red due to a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus, weather changes, or root stress. You need to investigate the soil and plant before deciding how to treat it.
ga: Baai tsuru lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miitutua oŋmɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei feɔ etsuru yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. loo shishifãi ahe haomɔ Esa akɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ mli dani okpɛ oyiŋ yɛ bɔ ni ooofee otsu he nii oha lɛ he.

english: Does leaf discoloration always mean my crops have pests?
ga: Ani baai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui?

english: No, leaves change color for many reasons including nutrient deficiencies, poor water drainage, or diseases. Pest damage usually leaves holes or visible insects, so you should check under the leaves carefully before assuming it is a pest issue.
ga: Dabi, yiŋtoi srɔtoi ahewɔ ni baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ fata he Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo hela, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa bu loo ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ dani osusu akɛ eji tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagba.

english: Why do my crop leaves change color even when I cannot see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsake amɛhe su lɛ? Ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ nakai baa lɛ nɔ?

english: Plants communicate their internal stress through leaf color. If there are no insects, the crop may be lacking plant food in the soil, getting too much sun, or suffering from root diseases underground.
ga: Tsei tsɔɔ amɛmli haomɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe su nɔ. Kɛji kooloi bɛ lɛ, ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ tsei niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. hulu la ni naa babaoo Aloo eji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã hela ko?

english: How do I determine the right amount of fertilizer and chemicals to put on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ?

english: You must measure your land size and test your soil or consult an extension officer before buying inputs. Putting inputs without calculating what the soil actually needs wastes your hard-earned money and can damage your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ni oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo oyabi extension officer dani ohé nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Data ni oookɛwo mli ni obuuu nɔ ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ he akɔntaa Ebaafite oshika ni okɛtsu nii waa lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Should I buy pest spray immediately when I notice a change in my crop's color?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe su etsake?

english: No, rushing to buy chemicals without knowing the real cause of the color change wastes your money. If the issue is caused by a lack of nutrients, buying pest spray will not fix the problem and will hurt your farm's profitability.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ oyahe tsofai oya ni oleee nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni kɛ su ni tsakeɔ lɛ baa lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika. Kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba lɛ ba lɛ Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hemɔ tsuuu naagba lɛ he nii ni ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Will putting extra chemical spray on my crops fix my farm problems faster?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baatsu miŋmɔ lɛ mli naagbai lɛ ahe nii oya?

english: Applying extra chemicals without diagnosing the exact problem can burn your crops, harm the soil, and waste your resources. Always identify the specific cause before applying any input.
ga: Tsofai krokomɛi ni okɛbaafata he ni okwɛɛɛ naagba pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui ni ofiteɔ onibii. Tsɔɔmɔ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni kɛbaa lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ nɔ ko awo mli.

english: Why is it important for me to track how much money and inputs I spend on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makwɛ shika kɛ nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tracking your inputs helps you know if your farm is making a profit or a loss. It prevents you from over-investing in chemicals or fertilizers that do not add value to your total harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ saji ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ miiye sɛɛnamɔ loo efiteɔ nii. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ ni okɛ shika babaoo awo tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm issue is caused by pests or a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ naagba ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tso hela ko mli?

english: Insects typically leave physical damage like chew marks, holes, or webs on leaves. Diseases usually cause spreading spots, color fading, wilting, or rotting throughout the plant leaves and stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni fiteɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ he okadii, bu, loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ mli fãji egbɛɔ eshwaa, ehiɛ su tsakeɔ, egboɔ, loo egboɔ.

english: What steps should I take first when I notice my crops look sick in the field?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Instead of rushing to buy chemicals, closely inspect the affected plants. Check the stems, look under the leaves for insects, inspect the soil moisture, and seek advice from an extension officer to confirm the cause.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee oya ni oyahe tsofai lɛ Kwɛmɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ, kwɛmɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ, ni otao kooloi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obi ŋaa kɛjɛ hiɛyaa he nitsulɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ koni oma nɔ ni kɛba lɛ nɔ mi.

english: Can I accurately diagnose what is wrong with my crops just by looking at my field from a distance?
ga: Ani manyɛ mana nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ ni makwɛ kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Looking from a distance only tells you that the crop is stressed. To know the true cause, you must walk into the farm, look closely at individual plants, check for insects, and inspect the roots and soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ojɛ shɔŋŋ okwɛ lɛ, no pɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao. Bɔni afee ni ole nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni kɛ enɛ baa lɛ Esa akɛ onyiɛ kɛbote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko jogbaŋŋ, kwɛmɔ kɛji kooloi yɛ mli, ni okwɛ shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked for too long, plant roots cannot breathe and struggle to absorb nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a virus they spread that stops normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni haaa baai lɛ adalɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tight during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a natural way plants protect themselves from the heat; by hiding parts of the leaf from the direct sun, the plant saves moisture from evaporating until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ fãi komɛi ni akɛteeɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi dani kpamɔɔ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines often happens when beetles or fungal diseases attack the roots underground, cutting off water and food supply from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbimɔ oya lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii helai tutua shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with lots of leaves but only produce small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa ni tsii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato e-bulbs lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do my crops dry out faster in light sandy soil than in dark soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ duŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has larger spaces between particles so water drains away quickly, while dark organic soil acts like a sponge and holds moisture for roots to drink over a longer time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ nibii bibii lɛ ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa oya. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ehiɛɔ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nuɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow well and help the soil when planted near maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen food from the air and release it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring crops.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets too hot, when they do not get enough water, or when pest insects attack the stems holding the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei ni hiɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree drop its small young pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods when the tree does not have enough water or nutrients to feed every pod, or when diseases like black pod set in.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ. aloo be mli ni hela ko tamɔ black pods yɔɔ

english: Why do my cabbages grow open leaves instead of forming a tight, hard head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni agbele naa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if the weather is too warm, if they are planted too close together, or if they do not receive a steady supply of water while growing.
ga: Kaabaji ehiŋ shi shiŋŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ amɛnáaa nu daa be mli ni aduɔ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa plants lose their leaves and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and sensitive leaves that dry out under harsh sunlight. Without enough shade trees or water during the dry season, the heat stresses the plant, causing leaves to turn yellow and drop to conserve moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛji tsei loo nu bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo be ni sa aba lɛ, Heat haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi bɔni afee ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are the flower buds on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree suffers from stress, such as prolonged drought, poor soil nutrients, or attacks by pests like mirids. Maintaining good soil nutrients and protecting the trees from insects helps the flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kpe. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen tutuamɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does the type of water I use to mix my farm chemicals affect how well they work?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ saa bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ he?

english: Yes, clean water is essential. Muddy or dirty water contains soil particles that can bind to the chemical and reduce its strength, while also clogging the nozzle of your spraying machine.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli tse he miihia. Nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji lɛ mli sũ mli nibii ni baanyɛ akpɛtɛ tsofai ahe ni eha amɛhewalɛ aba shi lɛ yɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ.

english: How long after spraying my crops do I need to wait before rain washes the chemical away?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ afɔ tsofai lɛ ahe?

english: Most farm chemicals need about two to four hours of dry sunlight after spraying to be fully absorbed by the plant. If it rains immediately after you spray, the chemical will wash off and lose its effectiveness.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ hulu la ni egbi ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ be mli ni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ kwraa. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Tsofai lɛ hoɔ ni amɛtsuuu nii dɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the chemical I am spraying is actually killing the pests on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ miigbe kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will notice a clear decrease in insect activity within a few days, and new leaves or pods will grow without fresh bite marks or damage. If insects continue to multiply, the chemical mixture may be too weak or the wrong type.
ga: Obaana akɛ kooloi anitsumɔi lɛ eba shi kwraa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Ni baai loo ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃ ni ŋmeii heei loo nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii lɛ tee nɔ amɛfa babaoo lɛ, ekolɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ loo eji nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Ani abaanyɛ akɛ enɛ atsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young cocoa is very beneficial. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide essential shade to protect young cocoa trees from the sun while providing food and extra income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii kɛ shika kroko baa dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: How can I reduce the amount of money I spend on buying pesticides every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ amli daa afi lɛ shi?

english: You can cut chemical costs by practicing good farm sanitation, such as regular weeding, pruning dense branches to let in light, and removing diseased pods promptly. This naturally reduces pest habitats so you need less chemical treatment.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ahe nyɔmɔwoo aba shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ kpakpa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni eha la aba ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ lɛ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofai fioo pɛ atsu nii.

english: Should I hire a trained spraying officer or spray my farm chemicals myself?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maŋɔ tsofai ni atsɔse amɛ ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai anɔ lɛ loo mi diɛŋtsɛ mafo tsofai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hiring a trained spraying operator ensures the chemicals are mixed in correct proportions and applied safely without wasting money or damaging crops. If you spray yourself, you must use proper protective gear to prevent health risks.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko ni atsɔse lɛ ni ekɛ tsofai fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ afutu bɔ ni sa, ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii shweshweeshwe ni shika efiteee loo efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie ohe Esa akɛ okɛ hebuu nibii ni sa atsu nii koni okɛtsi helatsamɔ he osharai anaa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning excess branches to improve airflow helps prevent the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What is the best way to clean and maintain my knapsack sprayer so it lasts longer?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsumɔ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ mli ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Always flush the sprayer tank with clean water right after every use to prevent chemical buildup. Wash the nozzle carefully to avoid clogs, and store the sprayer in a cool, shady place so the heat doesn't crack the plastic.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ he yɛ be fɛɛ be ni akɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ koni tsofa akabua ehe naa. Tsɔɔmɔ nozzle lɛ he jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi ehe. Ni okɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ ahi he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Bɔni afee ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akaha plastic lɛ mli agbala.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sun and heat. Keeping some taller shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool umbrella that protects the young cocoa until its roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kookoo tso ko nɔkwɛmɔ koni eda loo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ emasɛi Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested my maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nitrogen food from the soil. Crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally feeding your soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ niyenii haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it best for me to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Heavy rain washes expensive fertilizer away into streams or deep into the soil before root systems can soak it up. It is better to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but heavy rain is not actively falling.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ amli kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ enɛko waa.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, won't I harvest more cassava from my field?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmei babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant room to grow thick, healthy tubers instead of thin, weak roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs ni mli wa, ni mli wa. Mohu ɔ, sisifã ɔmɛ be he wami nɛ a he tsɔ.

english: Why do some of my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs while others nearby are thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ ekomɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Plants grow thin and weak when they are overcrowded or shaded by weeds. Giving every seed equal distance and keeping weeds down ensures all plants get equal food and sun to make big cobs.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛhe eyi tsɔ loo jwɛi ewo amɛhe shade. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ to amɛhe pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds from the agriculture office instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du wuhi nɛ i he kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Seeds saved over many seasons gradually lose their strength and yield less. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, survive dry spells better, and give you a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abaanyɛ akɛto be babaoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛ ni laajeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ nibii babaoo baa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the plant lacks sufficient water. Giving your plants steady water at the base and light shade during hot dry spells helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu yɛ eshishi kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a plant virus they carry. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying organic or recommended neem oil remedies can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛ neem fɔ ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli loo ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass and leaves around the stems of my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai mabɔle he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating into the hot air, allowing your crops to stay hydrated for a much longer time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops flowering at unusual times of the year compared to when my elders used to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei ni yɔɔ srɔto mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mi onukpai lɛ duɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Weather patterns and temperatures are changing, causing rains to start earlier or later than before. Crops respond directly to these shifts in rain and heat, so adjusting planting dates based on current forecasts helps prevent crop stress.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ dɔlɛ miitsake, ni no haa nugbɔ nɛɔ oya loo ebaaa blɛoo fe tsutsu lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ kɛ dɔlɛ tsakemɔi ahe nii tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsake gbii ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe haomɔ naa.

english: What does grafting a fruit tree mean, and why should I do it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni yibii tso ni akɛwoɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Grafting joins a branch from a sweet, fast-producing tree onto the root of a tough, disease-resistant plant. This helps your tree grow faster and bear high-quality fruit much earlier than growing from a regular seed.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ he ji ni akɛ tso ko ni woɔ yibii oya ni ŋɔɔ lɛ niji kɛ tso ko ni wa ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ aaafata he. Enɛ baaye abua ni otso lɛ adara oya ni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ oya fe bɔ ni ejɛɔ dumɔwui ni anáa daa lɛ mli baa lɛ.

english: Why do improved seeds from the agriculture office yield better crops than seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds developed by agricultural research colleges are specifically bred and selected to fight off local diseases, withstand dry spells, and produce bigger yields compared to seeds saved year after year.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni Agricultural Research College lɛ fee lɛ anɔ pɔtɛɛ ni ahala koni akɛwu ashi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ shiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ehaa yibii babaoo kɛ akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow before the plants are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green growth, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, lack enough water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ baa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my cassava help my crops grow better?
ga: Te cowpea ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes hungry crops like cassava while keeping weeds down.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni egbeɔ jwɛi hu.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing water during intense heat. It is a natural defence to trap moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ ko ni akɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree, which prevents black pod disease and forces the plant to focus its energy on growing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ ama pods ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava variety if I want to sell to gari processing factories?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei srɔtoi ni sa? Kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ oha Gari nitsumɔhe ko.

english: Look for improved varieties recommended by extension officers that mature within 10 to 12 months, have a high starch content, and resist the mosaic virus.
ga: Taomɔ srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 mli. Amɛyɛ starch babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye mosaic hela lɛ nɔ.

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if insects and fungi in the soil damage the seeds before they can germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the soil is ready for planting after the early rains start?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the soil has received two or three good, deep rains so that moisture settles deep enough into the root zone to sustain young shoots if a short dry period follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ enyɔ loo etɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛbu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko ba.

english: Why do some of the crop seeds you give us mature in just three months while others take much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni okɛhaa wɔ lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi heɔ be babaoo fe nakai?

english: Early-maturing three-month varieties are bred to complete their life cycle quickly so you can harvest food early in the season, while longer-duration types take more time to build up larger, heavier yields.
ga: Afɔɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni daa nyɔji etɛ pɛ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa niyenii yɛ be lɛ mli mra. yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni tsii.

english: Why should I plant both a fast-growing small crop variety and a large crop variety on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting fast-growing small varieties gives your family quick food within three months, while the larger, longer-maturing varieties produce heavy yields later to feed big households and store for the long term.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ, ebaaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni dara ni daa oya lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli koni akɛha shiabii wuji niyenii ni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the right crop varieties if I have a large family to feed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso srɔtoi ni sa? Ni kɛ́ miyɛ weku agbo ni esa akɛ makwɛ amɛ hu?

english: Large families benefit from high-yielding, heavy-producing varieties that provide plenty of food, combined with short-term three-month crops that offer quick harvests to cover hunger gaps while the main crop grows.
ga: Wekui wuji náa ŋmeii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni woɔ nibii ni tsii ni haa niyenii babaoo lɛ ahe sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛ nyɔji etɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kuku ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa oya koni akɛha hɔmɔ ni yeɔ mɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miida lɛ fata he lɛ.

english: What makes a three-month crop variety different from crops that take a full year to mature?
ga: Mɛni haa tso ni yeɔ nyɔji etɛ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ tso ni heɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani edaa lɛ he?

english: Three-month crops are designed to flower and produce food quickly using less water, making them ideal for short rainy seasons, whereas full-year crops spend months building deep root systems and larger produce.
ga: Afee nyɔji etɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo niyenii oya kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Ni afee ni ehi kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ daa afi lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ,

english: Why are some crop varieties naturally big while others stay small even when grown on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi daraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi ji bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he kome po.

english: Different crop varieties carry different genetic traits; some are naturally bred to produce many small fruits or roots quickly, while others focus their growth energy into producing fewer, much larger outputs.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo aduawai bibii loo shishifãi. babaoo oya yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi kɛ amɛdalɛ hewalɛ lɛ maa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ wuji babaoo ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant a three-month crop today, can I harvest and use it immediately when the three months are up?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eye nyɔji etɛ ŋmɛnɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ni mikɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, three-month varieties reach full maturity around the 90-day mark, meaning their grains or roots are fully formed and ready to harvest, consume, or sell right away.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni eye nyɔji 3 lɛ daa yɛ aaafee gbii 90 mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdumɔwui loo amɛshishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa, aye, loo ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Does planting a larger seed piece mean I will automatically harvest bigger crops?
ga: Ani dumɔwui wuji ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Bigger seeds contain more initial energy to help the young plant sprout stronger, but the final crop size depends mostly on the variety's genetics, plant spacing, soil nutrients, and rainfall.
ga: Dumɔwui wuji lɛ yɛ shishijee hewalɛ babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni he wa. Shi naagbee tso lɛ dalɛ baadamɔ tso lɛ mli fɔmɔ su lɛ nɔ. tsei amli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ ji nɔ ni fe fɛɛ

english: Why is it helpful to plant crops that mature at different times instead of harvesting everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaakpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Staggering maturity times ensures your household has a continuous supply of food and income over several months, preventing hunger and reducing the risk of produce spoiling before it can be eaten.
ga: Be ni tsakeɔ ni shwereɔ lɛ haa oshia lɛ náa niyenii kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni baa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ hɔmɔ naa ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ aduawai kɛ aduawai baafite dani ayeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I leave short-duration crops in the field after they mature until I am ready to use them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni amɛfee klalo akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to harvest short-duration crops as soon as they reach maturity at three months, because leaving mature crops in the field exposes them to rain damage, fungal rot, insects, and animal pests.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji tso lɛ shɛ nyɔji etɛ mli pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, nugbɔ, ŋmeii, kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui.

english: Why do extension officers advise farmers to plant more than one variety of the same crop in a single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ okwaafoi ŋaa koni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli nibii ni fa fe ekome yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Growing multiple varieties spreads your risk; if unexpected weather or a pest attacks one variety, the other variety may survive, ensuring your family still gets a harvest.
ga: Srɔtoi babaoo ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshara ni oyɔɔ lɛ afee srɔtoi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua kooloi srɔtoi lɛ Kooloi srɔtoi krokomɛi baanyɛ ahi shi. Enɛ baaha oweku lɛ anyɛ akpa nikpamɔ lɛ lolo.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my field instead of soaking deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ taraa ŋmãa ŋmɔji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When soil becomes compacted from foot traffic or heavy land clearing, the tiny pores close up. Adding organic compost or lightly tilling breaks up hard ground so water can penetrate down to where crop roots feed.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi kɛjɛ tsɔnei ni hoɔ babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fata he lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shi kɛyashɛ shishifãi ni adu lɛ anɔ.

english: How does deep water penetration in the soil help my crops survive dry days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: When water sinks deep into the soil, crop roots grow longer to chase it. Deep root systems keep plants green and hydrated even when rain stops falling for a few days.
ga: Kɛ́ nu lɛ bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ koni amɛshɛ he. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right after a heavy rain has flooded my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the soil is overflowing with water, added fertilizer simply washes away into rivers or sinks too deep for roots to reach, wasting your money.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ Fertilizer ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaho yɛ faa lɛ mli loo ebaabote mli tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika.

english: Why should I ask an agricultural officer to inspect my soil before planting this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛdu nii yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: An agricultural officer can test your soil to see what nutrients it lacks. This prevents you from wasting money on the wrong fertilizers and helps you choose the right crops for your land.
ga: Okwaayeli nitsulɔi baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ ahe. ni eye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell with my own hands if my soil is holding enough water for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ miniji ale akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of moist soil into a ball; if it holds its shape gently without dripping water or falling apart into dry dust, it has good moisture retention for roots.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ahiɛ mli blɛoo ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ Ni nu shwieee shi loo efooo ni etsɔ powda ni egbi. Ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds struggle to sprout when the top of the soil dries into a hard crust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi ni etsɔ ŋmei ni wa lɛ?

english: A hard soil crust acts like a physical lid. Young, delicate shoots do not have the strength to push through hard dry earth, which causes seeds to rot under the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi fã lɛ. Tsofɔi bibii ni waaa lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow after a prolonged rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil gets waterlogged, water fills all the air gaps, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, roots cannot absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ he lɛ mli obɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: How do I know if my crops are drooping from too much water or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo loo nu fioo pɛ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: If crops droop and the soil feels wet and soggy, they are drowning from too much water. If they droop and the soil is dry and dusty, they are simply thirsty.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gbee shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiho ejaakɛ nu fa babaoo. Kɛji amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Kumai ye amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big green leaves but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen water-logging the root area, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding its food stores below ground.
ga: Beni nitrogen eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo aahu akɛ tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What happens to crop roots when the soil stays dry for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei ashishifãi anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: When soil remains dry, roots stop growing and harden, making it impossible for the plant to take up food, which leads to stunted crop growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baakpa dalɛ ni amɛbaafee shiŋŋ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii Ehaa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my high-yielding maize harvest produce smaller yields when I plant them the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many high-yielding crops are hybrids, which are bred from two distinct parent plants. The seeds saved from a hybrid harvest do not retain the exact strong combination of traits from the parents, leading to lower yields and weaker plants in the second generation.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo ji tsei ni akɛfee ekome, ni ajɛ fɔlɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli afɔ amɛ. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hiɛɛɛ sui krɛdɛɛi ni jɛ amɛfɔlɔi adɛŋ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: I have been planting saved seeds from the same tomato farm for many years, so why are my fruits getting smaller every season?
ga: Mikɛ afii babaoo edu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tomato ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ. Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ feɔ bibii daa be lɛ?

english: Reusing seeds from the same farm repeatedly causes inbreeding over time. Without introducing fresh seed stock or new varieties, the crop gradually loses its strength, resulting in smaller fruits and lower disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ahaaa dumɔwui heei loo henɔi heei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe baajɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii ni helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: If I plant sweet pepper right next to hot pepper on my farm, will my sweet peppers start tasting spicy?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ masɛi Ani mi-bell ŋmeii lɛ baaje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Insects transfer pollen between nearby pepper plants, causing cross-pollination. While the sweet pepper fruit harvested this season will usually remain sweet, the seeds inside that fruit will carry hot pepper traits if you plant them next year.
ga: Koolooi kɛ pollen yaa pepper tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ateŋ. causing cross pollination Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii ni akpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ lolo moŋ, Shi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ baafee tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ kɛji odu amɛ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How far apart must I plant two different maize varieties so that they do not mix together?
ga: Abɛi srɔtoi enyiɛ esa akɛ madu koni amɛkabɔ amɛhe?

english: Maize pollen travels through the air on wind currents. To keep varieties pure and prevent unwanted cross-breeding, you should plant different varieties at least 200 to 400 meters apart, or plant them a few weeks apart so they flower at different times.
ga: Abele pollen lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ nɔ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ahi shi ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ataooo lɛ naa. Esa akɛ odu srɔtoi srɔtoi. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ha amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 200 kɛyashi 400, loo du amɛ otsii fioo komɛi koni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: Why do plants grown from seeds taken from the very same cocoa pod grow at different speeds and produce different amounts of beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ daa oya yɛ srɔtoi amli ni amɛwoɔ kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Seeds from the same pod inherit different genetic combinations from the parent plant and the pollen source. Just as human children from the same parents do not look or perform identically, seeds from the same fruit carry individual variations in growth rate and yield potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ pod kome mli lɛ gboshinii ji gboshinii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ kɛ pollen jɛɛhe lɛ mli. Taakɛ adesai abii ni jɛ fɔlɔi kome mli lɛ, amɛhiɛ su loo amɛjeŋba jeee ekome lɛ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ aduawai kome mli lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ srɔtoi.

english: If I buy high-yielding cocoa seeds but do not apply fertilizer or clear the weeds, will they still give me a bigger yield than my old cocoa trees?
ga: Kɛ mihe kookoo yibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo shi mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jwɛi wooo mli lɛ, Ani ebaawo yibii babaoo lolo fe mi kookoo tso momo lɛ?

english: Improved seeds have higher yield potential, but that potential can only be expressed under good growing conditions. Without adequate soil nutrients, water, and weed protection, even superior seed varieties will produce poor harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo. Shi abaanyɛ ajie nakai nyɛmɔ lɛ kpo yɛ shihilɛi kpakpai ni haa mɔ daa lɛ pɛ shishi. Kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ jwɛi ahebuu bɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ po woɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does planting a plantain sucker give me an exact copy of the mother plant, but planting a seed gives me a plant with different traits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu ko ni mikwɛɔ lɛ haa mináa tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ he mfoniri pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa mináa tsei ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi.

english: Suckers are vegetative shoots that come directly from the parent stem, acting as exact genetic clones. Seeds, on the other hand, are formed when flowers mix pollen from different plants, creating a new combination of traits.
ga: Shoot ji tso nine ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ wala yibii pɔtɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui baa kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ jɛ tsei srɔtoi amli, ni enɛ haa sui heei ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baa.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise us to graft a sweet mango branch onto a wild mango rootstock instead of just planting sweet mango seeds directly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mango niji ni ŋɔɔ atsu nii kɛdu koo mli mango lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu mango dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ lɛ kɛkɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Wild mango roots are tough and resistant to local soil diseases, while sweet mango branches produce desirable fruit. Grafting combines the root strength of the wild plant with the fruit quality of the sweet variety into a single strong tree.
ga: Koo mli mango shishifãi lɛ wa ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni mango niji ni ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni asumɔɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa koo mli tso lɛ shishifã hewalɛ kɛ yibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tso kome ni he wa.

english: Why does a cassava variety that yields heavily in the Ashanti region perform poorly when I plant it on my farm in the Volta region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Volta kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop varieties develop optimal performance under specific soil conditions, rainfall patterns, and temperatures. When moved to a location with different soil texture or climate, the crop may struggle to adapt and produce lower yields.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ feɔ amɛnitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo pɔtɛɛ Kɛji aya he ko ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ srɔto lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana naagba yɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi.

english: If my cassava crop gets infected with mosaic disease, can I use stem cuttings from that crop to start my new farm?
