ga: Kɛji akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ emɔ mosaic hela lɛ Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ nakai dumɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Stem cuttings carry the sap and diseases of the mother plant. Planting stem cuttings from a diseased cassava plant transfers the virus directly into your new farm field, ensuring the new crop will also be infected.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehiɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli nu kɛ hela. Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmei tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii heei hu náa hela.

english: What makes my cocoa leaves burn and drop off after I spray weed killer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Spraying weed killer too close to cocoa trees causes chemical drift onto the leaves. This damages the crop's leaves, preventing them from making food, which causes them to dry up and drop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie cacao tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkahoo Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weed control chemicals kill the weeds in my farm but leave my maize crop safe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi ehaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe lɛ?

english: Selective weed killers are designed to target specific types of plants like broadleaf weeds, while narrow-leafed crops like maize can safely process and tolerate the chemical.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ koni akɛtutua tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsu tsei ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ahe nii shweshweeshwe ni tsofai baanyɛ atsu he nii.

english: How does heavy rain right after I spray chemical input affect my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain washes the chemical off the leaves before the plant or pest can absorb it, reducing the chemical's effectiveness and potentially burning root zones if washed into the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ baa shi, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã kɛji akɛ ahoo amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi e-tuber lɛ ji bibioo lɛ?

english: Cassava plants focus their energy on leaf growth instead of roots when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when plants are crowded too closely together.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ yeɔ hiɛ moŋ fe shishifãi beni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ

english: Why do young cocoa plants need shade trees, but older cocoa trees produce better in sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ? Shi cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under hot sun, but mature cocoa trees need direct sunlight to generate enough energy to grow abundant cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ cacao ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers fall over easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers fall over when underground pests like root nematodes weaken their roots, or when they are planted too shallowly in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ root nematodes lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ nɔ

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips attack the crop, or when a virus spread by insects stunts the crop's flower development.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, tutua ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kɛ́ helai ni kooloi gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten patches at the bottom while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Bottom rot occurs when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering patterns during hot growing periods.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow from the bottom before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, forcing the plant to pull energy from old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee niyenii.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the daytime even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Crops wilt in wet soil when root diseases or underground pests destroy the root system, stopping the plant from taking up water.
ga: Tsei lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛ́ shishifãi ahe helai loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantain or cassava planted next to them to block the harsh heat until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and hiding inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni akɛtee tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants to feed on tender growth, which can be managed by applying recommended treatments directly into the plant whorls early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛaawo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are missing vital nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. This happens when the same land is used repeatedly without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer to replenish the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fataaa he

english: Why should I measure and space my seeds far apart instead of putting many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ni mafo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Proper spacing gives every single plant enough soil, sunlight, and water to grow big. When too many seeds share one spot, they compete with each other, resulting in weak stems and very small yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shikpɔŋ, hulu la, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo. Kɛji dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe baatswa akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: It is best to water early in the morning when temperatures are cool. Watering in the afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ awo nu lɛ leebi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Weeds are naturally hardy plants with strong root systems designed to absorb nutrients and rainwater instantly. They easily overpower cultivated crops, which is why early and regular clearing is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa ni afee koni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nugbɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kunim yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ mra ni afeɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava tubers so they do not rot?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ koni amɛkafite?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving tubers in wet soil for too long after maturity causes them to turn woody or decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei loo amɛgboi.

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize improves the soil. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, which naturally fertilizes your maize while giving you a second crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ awo ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha bo ŋmãa ni ji enyɔ.

english: What causes dark spots to appear on my tomato leaves after heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa tomato baa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Dark spots on tomato plants are usually caused by fungal diseases spread when rain splashes mud onto lower leaves. Trimming lower branches near the ground and covering the soil with straw helps prevent splash-back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ nugbɔ ni mli edɔ nɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ha amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Clearing wet weeds and pruning excess branches lets air flow through the farm, reducing dampness and stopping the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Jwɛi ni efɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo be lɛ shi ni okpa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots compete fiercely for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant enough space ensures the roots have room to expand into larger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve water when the soil is dry.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi.

english: Why is my farm yield reducing every year even though I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli mli yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same soil every season drains specific nutrients and allows pests to accumulate. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvest perform worse than the certified seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength, yield potential, and disease resistance in the next generation. Certified seeds are specially produced to deliver high yields and resist local pests and diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Yibiiwoo ni baanyɛ aba kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ aha kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: Trimming lower leaves prevents soil-borne diseases from splashing onto the plant during rain and allows the plant to send its food and energy directly into growing larger tomatoes instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akashwie tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ehaa tsei kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ majeɔ tomatoi wuji ni miida lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize fields mostly early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo leebi loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide in the central whorl of the maize plant during the hot day to avoid heat. They come out to feed when temperature drops during early morning and late evening.
ga: Fall flukes lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi yɛ leebi maŋkpa kɛ gbɛkɛ teŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn brown and dry up after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer too close to the stem or applying it on dry soil draws water out of the plant roots, causing 'fertilizer burn.' Fertilizer should be applied a short distance away from the plant stem when the soil is moist.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ekɛ ‘ŋmɔshi nibii ashã’. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and full of insects when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ kooloi kɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Maize rots and attracts insects if it is bagged before it is fully dried. Grains must be sun-dried until the moisture level is low and stored in clean, dry, well-ventilated areas or airtight bags.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Ni okɛto he ko ni he tse, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli loo vacuum bag mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the living shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: This is typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to prevent this disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa fe fɛɛ ji Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during cool, wet rainy seasons. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight in and helps air dry out the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ mli. Niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la abote mli ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I make high soil mounds before planting my yam sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ awó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmeii akuu ko lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand properly. Making high mounds creates space for big tubers to grow and prevents standing water from rotting the roots during heavy rain.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa gbɛ baa koni bulb agboi akwɛ̃, ni ehaaa nu ni ekã shi lɛ akafite shishifãi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Extreme heat causes tomato plants stress, making their flowers dry out and drop off without setting fruit. Mulching the soil and keeping it moist helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ahaa ehiɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to come up after I buried them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too deep, the young shoots exhaust all their stored food before reaching the surface. Planting maize at a shallow depth of about 2 to 3 centimeters gives the best germination.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific plant food from the soil year after year. Rotating your plot with cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen back to the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii komɛi jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my young crops slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars creating big holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii feɔ buji wuji yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cabbage moths lay eggs on the leaves, which hatch into hungry caterpillars that chew through the plant. Removing them by hand or using suitable biological sprays keeps the crop healthy.
ga: Kaabaji ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ tsei. Nine ni ajieɔ loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates living umbrellas that block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni hiɛ ka ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa naa lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: I noticed small caterpillars eating holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants, what is happening to my farm?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko ni miiye bu ko yɛ mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli. Mɛni ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of maize plants. If untreated, they destroy the plant's ability to develop leaves and dramatically reduce your grain harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaafite nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo baai lɛ ni ebaaha dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow leaves, especially after heavy rains wash nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts catch nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil that feeds whatever crop you plant after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients year after year and causes crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my cassava tubers if I plant the stems too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, tiny roots instead of thick, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baa yɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni tsii ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Extra shoots suck water and food away from the mother plant. Removing excess shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak, so weeds will quickly steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients they desperately need to establish strong roots.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ baafee mɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi ni wa amamɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sun to make energy. Lifting them off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and helps underground tubers grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ awó nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper plants early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to soak up water before the hot sun evaporates it, giving the plant's roots the hydration needed to survive the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa nu ni he hia amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture so the young cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Watering in the hot afternoon causes water droplets on leaves to act like tiny magnifying glasses that scorch the plant. Also, most of the water evaporates into the air before the plant's roots can soak it up.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. ni haa tsei shãa Kɛfata he lɛ, nu lɛ fa babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-loving pests to build up. Rotating maize with crops like beans or cassava keeps the soil balanced and healthier.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ja ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When they rot, they leave natural fertilizer behind that helps future crops grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ egbo lɛ, eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Excess rain floods the soil and suffocates crop roots by cutting off oxygen. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ekpaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly when the afternoon weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves inward to expose less surface area to direct heat, helping it preserve moisture during hot periods.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when the water stays on the farm too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil fills these air spaces, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui nɛɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save energy for survival instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvest without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ amɛ shwieee shi?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when their green leaves and vines begin to turn yellow, wither, and dry up naturally. This shows the plant has finished storing energy underground.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants have lots of leaves but very few nuts under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If the soil is packed too tightly or contains too much nitrogen, the groundnut plant will focus on growing leafy foliage above ground while the pegs struggle to push into the hard soil to form pods.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Peanut tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. They need shade from taller plants like plantains to protect them from harsh sun and keep the soil moist while they establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni oduɔ nii lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to save water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu akafite ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: This is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves whatever food it has from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young top leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I give my crops the exact same type of fertilizer from the day I plant until harvest time?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛjɛ gbi ni midu amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: No, crops need different nutrients as they grow. Early on, they need nutrients like phosphorus for strong roots, but when they start flowering and fruiting, they need higher amounts of potassium and nitrogen to make healthy fruits.
ga: Dabi, niyenii srɔtoi he miihia tsei beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shishijee lɛ, niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs he miihia amɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Shi kɛ́ ebɔi fɔmɔ ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ Amɛbiɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen babaoo koni amɛfee yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my maize look weak even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than maize and will eat up the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crop gets a chance to use them. You must clear weeds so your crops get all the food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni ebaaye ŋmãa, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ koni onibii fɛɛ aná niyenii.

english: What will happen to my cassava plants if I place the stems too close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If crops are planted too close, their roots fight over water and soil nutrients, while their leaves fight for sunlight. This competition leaves you with thin stems and very small tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ. be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ baawu Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii waa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating with crops like groundnuts refreshes the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ mli

english: This is damage from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (whirl) during the day to feed on the tender tissue away from the hot sun.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ efite. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ (kɔɔyɔɔ) yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking, and the stem turns a darker, woody brown.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko egbɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ tso.

english: Why do I need to cut off some branches from my young orange trees if I want them to produce big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ akutu tso niji bibii lɛ ekomɛi kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or extra branches so the tree does not waste energy feeding parts it does not need. Instead, it directs all its energy and water into growing strong stems and large, high-quality fruit.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ tsei ni ehe ehiaaa lɛ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e kudɔɔ e he wami kɛ e nu ɔ tsuo kɛ yaa tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nguahi nɛ a hi wawɛɛ ɔ a nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily and dry out. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains or gliricidia around them to filter the sunlight and retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo glicidia lɛ abɔle amɛhe. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ mli ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi dani eda lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot support due to a lack of water, nutrients, or excessive shade. It can also be caused by fungal infections like black pod disease during heavy rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cherelle lɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ yɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo hulutsoo babaoo ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Fungal helai hu baanyɛ ekɛba, tamɔ black pod hela yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves, turning the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year if I plant it in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time to recover. It also lets pests and diseases that attack maize build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain leaves water sitting on the land without proper drainage, the roots suffocate from lack of air and fungal rots quickly attack the soft tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ oya.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for tuber growth. Staking also lifts the leaves away from wet ground pests and fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, their huge leaves block light from one another, and their roots fight for the same water and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plant to form large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai wuji lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaafee aduawai akui wuji.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your main crops can reach them, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ baanyɛ aná. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil, which prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: If the nearby river water is muddy and smells bad, will it affect my vegetable crops if I use it for irrigation?
ga: Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji ni eŋɔɔɔ. Ani ebaana mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ hewalɛ kɛji mikɛtsu nii kɛshwie nu nɔ?

english: Yes, contaminated water carries harmful chemicals and toxins into the soil. These can burn crop roots, stop the plant from absorbing nutrients, and leave toxic residues on the leaves and fruits that make them dangerous to consume.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsofai fɔji baa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ ni eshiɔ tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛɔ yɛ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ ni haa amɛfeɔ oshara kɛha niyenii.

english: Why are my tomato fruits splitting open on the sides before they are even fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani eshɛɔ kwraa po lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when there is a sudden abundance of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli fã lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and bent instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle shi moŋ ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when their growing tips hit hard, compacted soil, rocks, or shallow beds. Creating deep, soft mounds gives the tubers space to stretch straight down without resistance.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛshishifã ni miida lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. ni shitee-kɛ-woo bɛ mli

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little food it has from the older bottom leaves up to nourish the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su eŋɔli lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning thick and leathery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or thrips under the leaves, or by virus infections transmitted by whiteflies. The feeding damages the leaf cells, causing them to distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa ni whiteflies kɛbaa lɛ mli. Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli wala yibii. kɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ baa

english: Why do my crops grow poorly over time if I clear my bush by burning it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli kɛji mijie mi-hedgerows lɛ kɛtsɔ shãa ni mishãa amɛ daa afi lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms and microscopic soil organisms that break down dead leaves into natural plant food. Over time, burning leaves the soil dry, hard, and hungry.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ. ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii waa. ni gbálaa baai ni egboi amli ewoɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii mli Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ewaa, ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ.

english: Excess rain fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, root tissues die, making it easy for soil fungi and bacteria to attack and turn the tubers into a soft, foul-smelling rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifã lɛ baagbo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my okra plants without forming any okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi okra tso lɛ nɔ ni okra ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, poor soil moisture, or lack of pollination can stress the plant. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to support fruit it cannot feed.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔɔɔ loo pollination ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni otao aduawai ni anyɛɛɛ aye lɛ,.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize look like someone punched neat rows of holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko tswa amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the young leaf unrolling inside the stalk. As the leaf expands and grows out, the single insect bite turns into a row of visible holes across the leaf.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baai bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Beni baai lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛdaraa kɛjeɔ kpo lɛ Kooloo kome ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ buji ni anaa ni tsɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that heavy rains have flooded the roots so they cannot absorb food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nugbɔ enɛ waa, ni eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ nu aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season gets too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess water stays around the roots without draining away, fungi grow and rot the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lolo ni ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ Fɛ̃i lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Is it better to water my cabbage farm early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha kaabii ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the plants to soak up moisture before the heat of the day, whereas afternoon watering causes quick evaporation and can scald leaves or promote fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai lɛ loo ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why do older farmers spread dry grass and cocoa leaves around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ kookoo baai amɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, holds in water longer, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops during their early years to protect their leaves and keep the air around them moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground exposes them to direct sunlight for making food, prevents them from getting burned on hot soil, and protects them from ground pests.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛhoo nii. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees give me small, light bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ haa mi ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: All the extra suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Cutting away most suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to feed a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi fɛɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without ever turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when beneficial insects like bees are not around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii bɛŋkɛɛɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and powdery droppings inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋ lɛ feɔ bu?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the soft growth inside the heart of the maize plant during the early stages of growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni daraa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ amɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or plantain suckers alongside them creates living umbrellas that shade the young cocoa and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo plantain ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ hulutsoo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which young plantain shoots should I dig up and plant on my farm to get big bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei bibii esa akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná tsei niji wuji?

english: You should pick 'sword suckers,' which have narrow, blade-shaped leaves and a thick base. Avoid 'water suckers' with broad leaves, because they grow into weak plants that yield very small plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘sword shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ he beni edaa ni etsɔɔ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ plantain tsei bibii waa lɛ.

english: Yellow and twisted leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by local agricultural officers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mixing organic manure into the soil helps the tomato plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oookwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant. Early spraying with recommended biopesticides or neem leaf extractions can clear them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Abaanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shihilɛ mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly if I do not remove weeds early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwieee amɛnɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the early weeks, weeds grow much faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks leaves enough nutrients for your crops to build strong roots and leaves.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make the soil better for my next maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the plants decay, this natural nitrogen acts as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their broad leaves can catch direct sunlight. When the leaves get enough sun, the plant produces more energy to grow large yam tubers under the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ koni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ baajie hewalɛ babaoo kpo ni ekɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience severe heat or water stress. Watering your crop regularly during dry weather and keeping the soil covered with mulch helps the plants hold onto their flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and die right after I transplant them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes 'transplant shock' because the delicate roots get damaged and dried out by the hot sun. Transplanting late in the afternoon or on cloudy days and watering immediately gives the roots time to recover.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ haa ‘Transplant shock’ baa ejaakɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ. Akɛwoɔ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni nu ni afɔɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow best under partial shade. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains to block the harsh sun, young cocoa leaves burn, lose water rapidly, and cause the plant to die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baashã. nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa tsei gboiɔ

english: Why does my yam produce bigger tubers when I use tall wooden sticks to lift the leaves off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking spreads the leaves out to catch more light while keeping them off the damp soil where fungal diseases usually spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking gbɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli koni la babaoo aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, or the soil may simply be tired.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ sũ lɛ etɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm make the next season's maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, it leaves that free plant food behind for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsina tso lɛ gbo Eshiɔ tso niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely soaked with water, air cannot reach the roots. This lack of air causes the cassava tubers to drown and allows rot-causing fungi and bacteria to destroy the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmei kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots grow deeper and spread out better when the soil is broken up loose before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ dani adu lɛ?

english: Loose soil makes it easy for tender root tips to push through the earth in search of water and nutrients. Hard, unbroken ground acts like a wall that traps root growth near the hot surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ aaatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ko ni wa ni etseee lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo, ni emɔɔ shishifãi ni eda yɛ he ni mli edɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, why do I get thin stalks and small cobs instead of a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona yibii babaoo?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick cobs, the maize plants spend all their energy stretching upward to compete for light.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeedu ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ, Abele kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛyeɔ la he akaŋ.

english: Extra sucker shoots steal water and plant nutrients from the mother plantain stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers directs all the soil food to the main stem, producing larger bunches of fruit.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ tso mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Akɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha yibii lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before they can turn into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. High temperatures prevent pollination from happening successfully, causing the flower to drop off.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baatsi fɔfɔii lɛ amli pollination naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Weeds are wild species naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions and take up soil nutrients quickly. They aggressively steal water and sunlight before domesticated crops can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ hulu la kɛ yiwalɛ dani shĩa tsei baanyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up before the bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani panicles lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a shortage of nutrients like potassium or water stress in the soil. It can also be caused by root pests like nematodes that prevent the plant from drinking water properly, so adding compost and protecting roots keeps leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium, loo nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Ebaanyɛ ejɛ shishifã mli tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ nematodes, ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛ nu nu jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni obu shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is ready for harvesting to take to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa koni akɛba jara nɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits become plump and lose their sharp outer ridges, and when the dried flowers at the tips of the fruits fall off easily.
ga: Plantain tsei akui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔjɔ ni esɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efo mli lɛ. Ni kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ gbi yɛ aduawai lɛ anaagbee lɛ, amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do some of my heavy plantain plants fall over easily during strong wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and if stem borers or root pests weaken the base, the heavy plant loses its grip in the soil. Mounding soil around the base and supporting heavy bunches with wooden poles helps keep them standing.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmeii wo tso lɛ shishi loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. Muji ni abua naa kɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Can I plant new plantain suckers directly in the exact same hole where I harvested an old plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantain tsei heei yɛ bu ni mikpa tso momo lɛ yɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is best to plant suckers slightly away from old stumps because decaying roots can attract pests like corm weevils and harbor fungal diseases that immediately attack the new sucker.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ ŋmeii momo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni egboi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi amli ŋmeii ni ji fungal helai ni tutuaa ŋmeii heei ni nuɔ nu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops curling up tight during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural way of protecting itself from water loss. When the sun is hot and soil moisture is low, the plant rolls its leaves to conserve water until the cool evening.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni efiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ koni ehiɛ nu mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my crop needs fertilizer just by reading the color of its leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ahe su ni makaneɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops show hunger through leaf colors: pale yellow leaves usually mean a lack of nitrogen, purplish leaves point to low phosphorus, and dry or burnt leaf edges indicate a need for potassium.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe su nɔ: bei pii lɛ, baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Ni baai lɛ ahe ni egbi loo eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium he miihia.

english: Why do my vegetable crops produce plenty of flowers but fail to form fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to produce leaves and flowers without setting fruit. It can also happen if there are no bees or insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen too quickly and rot while I am transporting them to long-distance markets like Madina?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ oya tsɔ ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛyaa jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tamɔ Madina lɛ?

english: Harvested fruit releases heat and a natural ripening gas called ethylene. Stacking produce tightly in airless bags under hot sun traps this gas, causing rapid ripening and spoilage during transit.
ga: Yibii ni akpa lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ to vacuum kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaamɔ gas nɛɛ. Enɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil within just two or three days of harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots undergo rapid natural chemical reactions once cut from the stem and exposed to air, which turns the inside dark. Keeping them buried in moist soil or processing them immediately prevents this spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ ko ni yaa oya mli kɛji afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni akɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha emli afee duŋ. Kɛ́ afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ loo atsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Why is it important to space out my crops properly instead of planting them very close to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ kɛ su a he konɛ o ná yiblii babauu.

english: Proper spacing ensures every crop receives sufficient sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without fighting its neighbors, resulting in stronger stems and larger harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enaaa akutsoŋbii anɔ hewalɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Maize leaves roll up during dry spells to protect themselves. By rolling up, the leaves reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant retain water and survive until the next rain.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: How does irregular rainfall affect the flowering and pod formation of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ saa fɔfɔi kɛ pod ni yɔɔ cacao tsei amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees need steady rain to support flowering. When rainfall is irregular, the tree becomes stressed and drops its blossoms early to conserve water, which results in fewer cocoa pods developing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi mra koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ haaa cocoa pod lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves yellow and drop naturally when water is scarce as a survival response. The plant sacrifices older leaves to lower its water demand and protect its core stem until moisture returns.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo. Tso lɛ kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛba nu he hiamɔ shi ni ebu tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their leaves when the sun becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop leaves to prevent water loss through evaporation. Providing light shade or mulching around the roots helps keep the soil cool and reduces leaf drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ ha chili tsei lɛ gbee shi. Bɔni afee ni nu akafite kɛjɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli Ŋmɔɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it harmful to farm the exact same crop on my plot of land year after year without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ matsu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo.

english: Why does my soil lose its strength so quickly after I clear a bush to start a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ baa shi oya beni mijie jwɛi koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: When bush cover is cleared, direct sunlight and heavy rains quickly break down organic matter and wash away topsoil nutrients. Adding compost or cover crops helps restore that lost soil strength.
ga: Kɛ́ ooha tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ oya ni ejieɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɔmpost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after a heavy downpour immediately following planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can pack the soil tightly over seeds, cutting off the oxygen they need to germinate, or wash seeds too deep into the ground where they cannot push through to the surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ dumɔwui. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli. aloo okɛ dumɔwui lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers begin to rot inside the soil if I leave them unharvested for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni mikpaaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain alive in the ground, but once they fully mature, excess soil moisture and fungi penetrate the tubers, causing the starch to break down and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi yɛ wala mli lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii baabote ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy vines but give me very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea wain tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to put all their energy into leafy foliage instead of producing flowers and pods. Balanced soil nutrients encourage proper pod development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai amli moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa pod lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings always bend toward the direction of the morning sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa leebi hulu lɛ he be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Plants naturally bend toward light in a process called phototropism. They do this to position their leaves to absorb maximum sunlight, which they use to manufacture food for growth.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ shi kɛyaa la nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ fototrofism nɔ. Amɛfeɔ enɛ koni amɛkɛ baai lɛ ato he ko ni hulu la lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha dalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a protective canopy that lowers temperature and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little nutrient it has from its older leaves up to feed the new, growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground before I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when soil remains soaked in water for too long because the roots cannot breathe without air in the soil. Excess water encourages soil-borne fungi and bacteria that attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agboi.
