english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers drop off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when plants experience water stress. Extreme heat dries out the flower pollen, preventing proper pollination and causing the plant to shed the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awoko mli lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally enrich the soil with nitrogen, which helps feed demanding crops like corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaahã nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are small green worms eating the central whorl of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that prefers hiding inside the tender, rolled center of corn leaves where they can feed safely on soft plant tissue before the leaves unfold.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa baa ni afolɔ mli lɛ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo shweshweeshwe dani baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same food, water, and light. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one strong shoot to produce a larger, healthier cluster of fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kome he akaŋ. Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to put stakes or sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso loo tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need vertical stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for underground tuber growth. Keeping vines off the damp ground also reduces leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia ni atswa amɛ tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baa shi.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses spread by them. These insects suck sap from the leaf, causing uneven growth that twists the leaf tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer only when the soil is moist and not when it is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ? Jeee be mli ni egbi lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat dry fertilizer directly; fertilizer must dissolve in soil water before roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can also burn and damage the plant roots.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ; esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ nu mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates living shade that shields the young cocoa from burning while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plant turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and helps them grow big ears, so adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ toi wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rains leave standing water around the roots, the tubers cannot get air and soil fungi quickly cause them to rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers when I let weeds grow tall around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs bibii beni mihaa jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food for the growing tuber under the ground. Tall weeds steal sunlight and soil nutrients, forcing the yam plant to waste energy instead of growing big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime heat gets too intense or when soil moisture dries up suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps cool the root zone so the plant can hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩ trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. The nearby maize uses this free nitrogen to grow stronger stalks and larger leaves without extra chemical input.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai wuji ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: Why do my maize stalks stay very thin and tall when I plant many seeds in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ nɛkɛ be mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing leaves enough room for each stalk to grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes right through the center leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This destruction is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which prefer eating the tender central leaves of young maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended treatments keeps the main growing leaf healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai titrii ni miida lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than at mid-day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu babaoo leebi fe gbi lɛ?

english: Watering during the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can absorb it, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch them. Morning watering lets roots take up water safely before the hot sun arrives.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu shweshweeshwe dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa.

english: Why is my pepper plant growing very bushy leaves but no pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy producing green leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Balancing the soil with nutrients like phosphorus encourages the plant to stop making extra leaves and start setting peppers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli nibii tamɔ fɔsfɔs to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekpa baai krokomɛi ni ekɛbaafata he lɛ feemɔ ni ebɔi ŋmeii ŋmɔmɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantain or shade trees to retain soil moisture and protect them while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to build green leaves and healthy stalks. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi biɔ ni afee baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and encourages soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts replenishes soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbɔle amɛhe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni efo adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: How do crops like groundnuts and cowpeas make my farmland richer for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii aha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes have microscopic helpers on their roots that take nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen stays behind as free, natural food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes yɛ yelikɛbualɔi bibii ni anaa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baaya nɔ afee adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground when the heavy rains last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits on flat land, it cuts off air to the cassava roots, causing underground fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry periods because it cannot support fruit growth without steady water. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps the ground cool and moist so flowers stay attached.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo be mli ni hulu lɛ egbi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ kɛji nu bɛ mli daa. Organic mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viral diseases from plant to plant. Controlling insect pests early using neem oil spray prevents the disease from taking hold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ helai ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Mra Be Mra Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni helai akabɔle he.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little when I sow seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and resources to mature and produce a large harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ni ekpa ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crops' growth even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and will aggressively consume the fertilizer, water, and light intended for your plants. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting ensures your crops get all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ la ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How do I know the safest time to plant my crops when the rainy season starts unpredictably?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: Planting after the very first rain is risky because a dry spell can quickly follow and scorch seeds. It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently wet for several consecutive days to guarantee good seed germination.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ oya ni eshã dumɔwui lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are not strong enough yet to absorb enough water. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the leaves from sunlight and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa anáa ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and weak even after planting them right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: The early rain in the season is often followed by a short dry period. Maize seeds need steady moisture over several weeks to build deep roots, so planting too early during erratic rainfall causes the seedlings to stall in growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia ni nu ahi shi daa yɛ otsii babaoo mli koni amɛtswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ehiii lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in heavy soil without draining away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Ehiɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juice and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap early on keeps these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of full fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo pole or branched wooden stick holds the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni eda ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ ŋmei tso loo tso nine ni niji yɔɔ mli lɛ afi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers fall off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Extreme heat prevents flowers from pollinating properly, causing the plant to shed the blossoms to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are small caterpillars boring holes into my cowpea pods just as they start to fill up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifo bu yɛ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ amli beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs inside cowpea flowers, and when the eggs hatch into caterpillars, they feed directly on the developing seeds inside the pods. Applying organic control sprays during the flowering stage stops the caterpillars before they enter the pods.
ga: Moths woɔ amɛwui yɛ cowpea fɔfɔi amli. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akpa dani amɛbote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and build tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni mafo he ko ni matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up high in full sunlight to create energy for growing large tubers underground. Keeping the leaves lifted off the wet ground also prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look healthy, but the shells under the soil are completely empty when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli efolo beni mifo mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells occur when the soil lacks calcium during the pod development stage. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil before planting provides the calcium needed for the nuts inside to fill up completely.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni pod lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha calcium ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize crop growing huge green leaves but making very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leafy green growth instead of forming fruits. Crops need balanced fertilizers containing phosphorus and potassium to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛha baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Tsei he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can I plant other crops inside my existing cocoa farm without harming my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli ni mifiteee kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, you can mix crops like plantains or food crops with cocoa, but you must leave proper spacing so the extra plants do not compete with your cocoa trees for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii afutu kookoo. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ gbɛ ni sa awo mli bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ kɛ cacao tsei lɛ akashi akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: If I plant cassava or plantain next to my young trees, will they steal food from my main crop?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ tsei bibii ahe Ani amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli?

english: If planted too close, food crops will compete aggressively with young trees for root space and fertilizer, but keeping a recommended safe distance allows both crops to feed without choking each other.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Niyenii tsei kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛhiɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛhi shi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aye nii ni amɛtsiŋ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and wither when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Mixing them with fast-growing plants like plantains provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ futu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, no hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between trees when planting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni ka tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ?

english: Spacing depends on the size the tree will reach at maturity. Leaving enough space prevents leaves from overlapping and blocking sunlight, and stops roots from fighting underground.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ damɔ tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ beni edara lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: What actually happens underground when two different crops are planted too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ shishi diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ adu tsei enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Underground, root systems fight for the same pool of water and nutrients. The stronger or faster-growing plant will starve the weaker one, leading to stunted growth and poor yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu jɛɛhe kome kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tsei ni he wa loo ni daa oya lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why do trees need wider spacing if I plan to keep them on the land for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atse tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mito gbɛjianɔ koni mikɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo hu?

english: As trees mature over many years, their branch canopy expands wide and their roots spread deep. Wide spacing ensures mature trees do not crowd each other out as they grow to full size.
ga: Beni tso lɛ daa afii babaoo lɛ Amɛniji lɛ mli lɛɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu mli kwɔ. Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ ehiɛɛɛ amɛhe nɔ be mli ni amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my entire land with a single crop all at once or plant in small stages?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu mishikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ tso kome shikome loo yɛ fãi bibii amli?

english: Planting your entire land at once creates a uniform farm that matures together and simplifies maintenance, but it requires more labor and money upfront compared to planting in smaller phases.
ga: Kɛ́ odu oshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ kome ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa ekwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Shi ebiɔ nitsumɔ kɛ shika babaoo yɛ hiɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ he.

english: What happens to my farm if I choose to plant only one type of crop across my whole land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mihala akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ?

english: Single-crop plantations make harvesting and management easier, but if a crop-specific disease or severe drought strikes, your entire farm faces the risk of total loss at the same time.
ga: Nibii kome ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Shi kɛji akɛ hela ko ni kɔɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ko he loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa ba Oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ afee oshara akɛ fɛɛ baafite yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why does my goal for the farm determine how I arrange and space my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ otii ni mikɛma mihiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni matoɔ mitsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ahaa kɛ he ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: If your intention is quick food harvests, you space short-term crops closer together, but if your goal is long-term cocoa or timber production, you must arrange the farm to give long-term crops priority space.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ji ni okpa niyenii oya. Ebaabi ni okɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe. Shi kɛji akɛ oti ni ma ohiɛ ji kookoo loo tso ni ooofee be kakadaŋŋ hu? Esa akɛ osaa oŋmɔ lɛ he ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye be kakadaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does too much tree shade affect the way my crops produce fruit later on?
ga: Te tso mli ŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While young plants need shade to survive, mature crops need adequate sunlight to produce heavy yields. Too much shade on mature trees reduces fruiting and creates a damp environment where diseases spread.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi moŋ, Shi tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ha tsei ni eda lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ baa. Ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ shade kɛ sũ mli nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil, or the soil has too much water which is drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛfiɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to capture sunlight and make food for the yam tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from rot and ground pests.
ga: Atomɔ tso lɛ kɛ ebaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii eha sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni fiteɔ kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Curled, spotted leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or transferred through infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often triggered by uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, insufficient soil moisture, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Water your pepper plants regularly and avoid over-fertilizing when they start flowering.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo Ha o-pepper tsei lɛ nu daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants with very small yields. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to produce maximum fruit or tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii loo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why should I wait for the major rainy season to settle before planting my main seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ dani madu dumɔwui titrii lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain is risky because the soil can dry out if rain stops for a week, killing the new sprouts. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures your seeds get reliable moisture to build strong root systems.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei lɛ agboi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from the soil that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get full nourishment to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni otsei lɛ he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs farmyard manure or bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii loo mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: If your soil gets dry and hard quickly, animal manure helps hold water and build long-term soil health. Chemical fertilizers give crops a quick boost of food but do not improve the soil structure itself, so using a mix of both works best.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ni ewa oya lɛ Manure yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii oya shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my corn plants turn yellow before the corn is even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. The plant is pulling food from its lower leaves to feed the young growing parts at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli Tso lɛ miigbala niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ niyenii.

english: If my cassava plant grows very tall with lots of leaves, does it mean I will harvest huge tubers?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ da waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo hu? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ manyɛ mahiɛ yitso agbo mli?

english: Not necessarily. When cassava has too much leaves and grows very tall, it often means the plant is spending all its energy above ground instead of sending that energy down to swell the tubers.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Be mli ni ŋmei lɛ baa babaoo tsɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu kɛya shi koni eha bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or the soil gets too dry. When the plant feels stressed by heat, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiihao kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ekɛhi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines to climb up wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves up on stakes lets them catch full sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber. It also keeps the leaves off the wet ground where diseases easily attack them.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni aaawo nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ. Ebaafee mlɛo akɛ abaatutua.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the specific nutrients maize needs and gives maize-loving pests a permanent home. Alternating with crops like beans restores the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ hoɔ. Ni ehaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa. Tsei tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rain will wash your fertilizer off the field into nearby gutters before the roots can drink it, wasting your money and hard work.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha o-fertilizer lɛ ashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya nubui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Eheɔ bo shika kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants usually mean tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, or they have spread a sickness to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops small and weak even if I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are like aggressive thieves on your farm. They drink the water, steal the soil food, and block sunlight from your crops, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. amɛnuɔ nu Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: How do airtight storage sacks keep my harvested maize safe from insects without using chemicals?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni vacuum kotokui lɛ aha mi-abele ni akpaa lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: These special storage sacks are made to shut out all outside air. Without oxygen inside the sack, insects and weevils cannot breathe or reproduce, which stops them from eating and destroying your stored grain.
ga: Afee kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtoɔ nii nɛɛ koni ekɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ naa. Kɛji oxygen bɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ Kooloi kɛ ŋmeii nyɛŋ amu loo amɛfɔ bii. Enɛ haaa amɛye dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so quickly after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or kept in hot, damp conditions. Unseen fungi enter through small cuts, so drying the tubers in a cool, well-ventilated shade lets wounds heal and stops rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fung ni anaaa lɛ boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii amli No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua pilamɔ lɛ ni etsa ni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to put my harvested grains directly into storage sacks while they are still slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ baawo kotoku lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ fioo lolo lɛ?

english: Damp grain creates a warm, wet environment inside the sack where dangerous molds can quickly grow. These molds cause spoilage and create toxic chemicals called aflatoxins that make the food unsafe to eat.
ga: Pellets ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli. he ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ ada oya Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ haa nibii fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins ni haaa niyenii afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller yields now than it did when my elders farmed it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo kwraa fe be mli ni mi onukpai lɛ ye nɔ nakai afii fɛɛ ni eho lɛ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients after many seasons of continuous planting without giving the land time to rest or adding compost and fertilizers to rebuild the food supply in the dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ be babaoo ni akɛduɔ nii daa lɛ sɛɛ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need for green growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen from heavy manure but lacks potassium, the plant spends all its energy expanding leaves above ground instead of sending food down to grow big tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni tsii mli shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛwo bulb agboi.

english: What does scientific farming mean for a small farm like mine, and how does it help crops produce more?
ga: Mɛni jeŋ nilee mli okwaayeli tsɔɔ kɛha ŋmɔ bibioo ko tamɔ mi nɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Scientific farming means using simple, tested rules—like planting in straight lines with accurate spacing, testing soil nutrients, and using improved seeds—so each crop gets enough space, light, and food to thrive.
ga: Jeŋ nilee mli okwaayeli tsɔɔ mlai fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii. ni aka amɛ akwɛ, tamɔ dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ Nibii ni He Waa lɛ He Kasemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi fɛɛ aná he ko, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ aná plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture to keep cocoa seedlings healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha hɔɔŋ ni ohiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat causes stress to the tomato plant, drying up pollen before it can fertilize the flower. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and water until cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. ni okɛ pollen lɛ agbi dani okɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm seem to feed on my maize leaves mostly at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars hide deep inside the plant funnel or in the soil during the hot day to avoid drying out in the sun. They come out to feed at night when temperatures cool down and moisture rises.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni hulu lɛ akagbi amɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when there is too much standing water drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get extremely high or when the plant experiences irregular watering during flowering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plants set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ naa nu ni ejaaa be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these small insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa tsu nii lɛ ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why are holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko eba trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the growing tip of the plant to feed on fresh leaves. Applying recommended controls or neem extract into the leaf funnel early in the morning helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishi koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛyeɔ nɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ wo tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks with very small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akafo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and suppresses weeds that steal food from your pepper plants.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni ojie jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How does putting animal manure into my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves the soil's structure so it holds water longer and gradually releases essential plant foods like nitrogen and phosphorus, keeping crops healthy over a long time.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ejieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fiofio. Ehaa tsei náa hewalɛ kpakpa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if left too long during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in waterlogged soil cuts off air supply to the underground cassava roots, causing fungal rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep producing new flowers even after I harvest the ripe peppers every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ fɔfɔi heei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikpaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ daa otsi moŋ.

english: Harvesting mature peppers regularly prevents the plant from using its energy to mature seeds, which signals the plant to keep producing new flowers and fruits for continuous yields throughout the season.
ga: Kɛ́ akpaa ŋmeii ni edara lɛ daa lɛ, ehaaa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ ebaawo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei. Koni aná nibii ni yaa nɔ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: If I harvest my vegetables every ten days, will my soil run out of nutrients quickly?
ga: Kɛ́ okpa aduawai daa gbii 10 lɛ, ani niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaho oya?

english: Yes, frequent harvesting continuously removes nutrients from the soil. Adding compost, manure, or fertilizer regularly replenishes what the crops take out, ensuring your soil stays rich and productive.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmaa ni akpaa shii abɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejie lɛ aya hiɛ daa. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in intense heat is a plant's natural defense to reduce water loss through its surface area, allowing it to survive until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛha tsei koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Ha ni ehi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Okra pods mature very rapidly. When left too long, the plant shifts energy into creating seeds and tough fiber, so harvesting every two to three days keeps the pods tender and high quality.
ga: Okra ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa. Kɛji ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ hewalɛ koni amɛfee dumɔwui kɛ tsɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii daa gbii 2-3 lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee blɛoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my garden eggs very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to compete for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants that bear smaller and fewer fruits.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atswa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai fioo.

english: Flower drop often happens when plants experience water stress or high heat, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to prioritize leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nu mli haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. aloo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and produce fewer pods during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry winds and low humidity dry out the soil and air. Cocoa trees shed leaves and slow down flower production to conserve water and protect themselves from dying.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my young maize crop during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-baby corn lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to local soil and rainfall, allowing them to absorb water and fertilizers faster than cultivated crops like maize.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and fibrous if I leave them in the ground past their normal harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛhe yɔɔ tsɔi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa lɛ he lɛ?

english: As cassava plants age past full maturity, they use stored starch in their roots to support older stems and leaves, turning the once-tender root tubers into tough, woody fibers.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ etsɔ be ni ekɛbaa lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfi tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ asɛɛ. Ehaa shishifãi ni tsutsu lɛ amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni wa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen; it moves the remaining nitrogen from older, bottom leaves up to nourish the younger, growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ekɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I increase the total yield of my cassava crop to match modern farm outputs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔji amli yibiiwoo lɛ akpã gbee?

english: To get higher yields, you need healthy stem cuttings, proper spacing between plants so they do not compete for sunlight, and applying manure or fertilizer at the right time during the early growing stage.
ga: koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ Ehe miihia ni oná tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. He ni sa ni ka tsei ateŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkaye hulu la he akaŋ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers recommend planting crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui ashwã lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every seed gets enough space and sunlight to grow properly, makes weeding easier, and helps you estimate the exact amount of fertilizer needed for your farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni osusuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ he.

english: Why do my stored maize grains spoil and turn to dust so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ sũ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stored grains spoil because tiny insects called weevils eat them from the inside if the grains were not completely dried before storage. Properly drying grains and storing them in airtight bags stops these pests.
ga: Kplukai bibii fiteɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaye nii kɛjɛ mli kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree produce good fruit before it grows too old and dies?
ga: Afii enyiɛ kookoo tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ ni egbo?

english: A cocoa tree starts bearing fruit around 3 to 5 years after planting and can keep producing good pods for 25 to 30 years if it is pruned regularly and protected from black pod disease.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii kpakpai afii 25 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ daa ni atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkaye yibii diji hela.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die shortly after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers die if they are transplanted during the heat without enough shade, or if stem borer insects damaged their roots before planting. Transplanting at the beginning of the rainy season helps them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii baagboi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii wo tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfite shishifãi lɛ dani amɛdu. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in flooded water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving farm drainage turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil lacks water, or if pests damage the blossoms. Regular watering during dry weather helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during intense heat to conserve moisture and protect the plant from drying out. Putting dried grass around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How do fall armyworms destroy my young maize plants so quickly?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni fall cutworms lɛ akpata mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahiɛ oya?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the growing center of the maize plant where they eat the soft leaves, preventing the crop from developing unless treated with pest control early.
ga: Fall caterpillars lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ, ni no haaa tso lɛ aya hiɛ ja akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmãa lɛ tsu nii mra.

english: Why does my soil produce lower harvests after two or three years of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its strength when crops continuously feed on its nutrients without replenishment. You can restore the soil by rotating your crops, planting legumes like cowpeas, or adding animal manure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa kɛji akɛ aha tsei lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewooo mli ekoŋŋ. Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ tsina ŋmei dumɔ loo kooloi ŋmei ni akɛfataa he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. Applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea near the roots will help the plant regain its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni ehiɛ wa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same farm bed every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to build up. Switching to legumes like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen naturally back into your dirt.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight which scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil too fast. They need temporary shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he waa. Enɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight. Staking helps the leaves process sunlight efficiently, which creates the energy needed to produce large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ hulu la lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and growing small white spots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread mosaic disease. Clearing infected plants early stops these insects from spreading the sickness to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɛ hela amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are holes appearing in the leaves of my cabbage plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji je kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars and pests that feed on soft leaves during the cooler night hours. Inspecting your plants early in the morning and using bio-pesticides or neem oil can protect the leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Should I keep all the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makɛ tsei bibii abɔle plantain wulu lɛ shishi?

english: No, allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to compete with the main plant for food and water. You should trim them so only one or two strong suckers remain, ensuring the main stem gets enough energy to produce a big bunch.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shaded during hot afternoons prevents flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ he amanehulu. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akashwie shi.

english: Why does putting dried grass around the base of my crops help them grow better in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why do my tomato fruits rot and turn black at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛmiitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to uneven watering. Water your tomato plants regularly so the roots can continuously draw calcium from the soil.
ga: Rot diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa koni shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Do my young crop seedlings need the same type of fertilizer as my fully grown plants?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsei ni eda lɛ he hiaa midumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: No, just as young children need different food than adults, young seedlings require lighter fertilizer higher in phosphorus to build roots, whereas mature crops need more nitrogen and potassium to build heavy leaves, flowers, and fruits.
ga: Dabi, taakɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ srɔto he hiaa gbekɛbii bibii fe onukpai lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ hu dumɔwui bibii he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi. Beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, nitrogen kɛ potassium babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛwo baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why does a maize plant need different care when it starts producing ears compared to when it is just a young shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ eyɛ toi hee fe be mli ni eji ŋmãa bibioo lɛ?

english: When maize is young, it uses its nutrients to grow green leaves and tall stalks, but when it enters the fruiting stage, it demands heavy feeding and moisture to fill out the corn grains completely.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Shi kɛ́ ebote yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ Ebaabi niyenii kɛ nu babaoo koni ekɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli kwraa.

english: Why can't I use the exact same fertilizer amount for every crop on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni falɛ kome pɛ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops have different dietary needs; leafy crops like spinach demand high nitrogen, while tuber crops like yam and cassava need extra potassium to develop thick roots underground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ spinach lɛ he miihia nitrogen babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii biɔ potassium kroko koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa shoots dry up in direct sunlight while mature cocoa trees survive fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young crop shoots are delicate like newborn babies and burn easily under harsh sun, so they need shade crops like plantains to protect them until their roots and bark are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ. ni etswaa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ amɛhewolo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cassava plants wilt quickly in dry weather while big cassava plants stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ? Be mli ni ŋmei tsei wuji lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Newly planted cassava has short roots that cannot search deep for water, while mature cassava has deep, established roots and thick tubers that store moisture and food to survive long dry spells.
ga: Kasava ni adu ehee lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ atao nu mli shɔŋŋ. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa lɛ, eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni toɔ nu kɛ niyenii koni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants need water every few days while my mature yam plants can go longer without watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ he hiaa nu daa gbii fioo komɛi, yɛ be mli ni sweet potato tso ni eda lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni awooo lɛ nu lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants like peppers have soft stems and shallow roots that drink water quickly and dry out fast, while yam plants store water and reserves in their underground tubers.
ga: Aduawai tsei tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nuɔ nu oya ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, sweet potato tsei lɛ toɔ nu ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli.

english: Which specific crops can I grow on my farm that are best for making porridge for small infants?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfeɔ gbekɛbii bibii?

english: Crops like orange-fleshed sweet potato, yellow maize, and cowpeas are excellent because they are soft when mashed and packed with the vitamins and protein young babies need to grow strong.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni hiɛ loo ni ji ŋmei yellow corn Kɛ cowpea ji tso kpakpa ejaakɛ eyɛ blɛoo kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ ni eyi kɛ vitamini kɛ protein ni he hiaa gbekɛbii bibii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What kind of crops should I plant to support the health of pregnant or nursing mothers in my family?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu kɛha nyɛmɛi ni hiɛ musu loo ni haa amɛbii nu yɛ weku lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ?

english: Dark leafy vegetables like kontomire (cocoyam leaves), along with groundnuts and beans, provide rich iron, protein, and minerals that help mothers regain strength and produce healthy milk.
ga: Aduawai ni tsuɔ tamɔ contomire (kokoo baai), kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa dade, protein, kɛ mineral babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nyɛmɛi náa hewalɛ ni amɛhaa mliki ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does the nutrient content of orange sweet potato differ from regular white cassava when fed to young children?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmei yam mli lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmei yɛŋ ni afeɔ daa lɛ he kɛ́ akɛha gbekɛbii bibii?

english: While white cassava mostly provides raw energy for working adults, orange sweet potato contains high levels of Vitamin A, which builds healthy eyesight and immune systems in growing children.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ babaoo haa onukpai ni tsuɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ, shi vitamin A babaoo yɛ Orange sweet potatoes mli.

english: Can I grow crops on the same field that satisfy both energy needs for adult workers and high growth needs for young kids?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ ni haa nitsulɔi ni eda lɛ ahewalɛ he hiamɔ nii kɛ gbekɛbii bibii ashweremɔ he hiamɔ nii ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ kpãa gbee?

english: Yes, intercropping staple energy crops like cassava or maize alongside protein-rich legumes like groundnuts allows you to harvest food suited for both hard-working adults and developing children from one farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, hewalɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dumɔ. Enɛ, kɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni sa kɛha onukpai ni tsuɔ nii waa kɛ gbekɛbii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: My father only farmed cocoa and oil palm, but can I grow short-term food crops on the same land?
ga: Mitsɛ ŋmɔɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei fɔ pɛ. Shi ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant short-term crops like plantain, cassava, or maize alongside young cocoa or oil palm trees. This is called intercropping, and it provides you with food and income while your main trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ plantains, cassava loo ŋmãa yɛ kookoo tsei bibii loo mu tsei ahe. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli. ni eha bo niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni otso titri lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I buy new hybrid cocoa seeds instead of replanting seeds saved from my old farm harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases, handle drought better, and bear fruits much faster—often within 2 to 3 years compared to older traditional seeds that take up to 5 years.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ hɔmɔ kpeɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibii oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni baanyɛ ahé afii 5 lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I start using fertilizer if my family has always farmed successfully without it for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nitsumɔ kɛji miweku lɛ eye omanye yɛ okwaayeli mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli afii babaoo?

english: Over time, plants draw natural nutrients out of the soil with every harvest. Fertilizer acts like nutrient food for the soil, putting essential nourishment back so your crops continue to produce large yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛbaaku sɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller harvests now compared to when I first started farming years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when planted repeatedly without resting or replenishment. Without adding compost, manure, or fertilizers to restore nutrients, crop yields naturally decline year after year.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiteɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ajɔɔ ehe loo awo mli ekoŋŋ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How long does a newly planted oil palm tree take before it starts producing palm fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ mu?

english: Improved oil palm varieties usually begin fruiting around 3 to 4 years after field planting, reaching their peak production period between 8 and 15 years of age.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. ni eshɛɔ ehiɛyaa he yɛ afii 8 kɛyashi afii 15 teŋ.

english: Why are my older cocoa trees producing fewer pods every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo daa afi lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees pass 25 to 30 years of age, their natural productivity declines, and they become more vulnerable to diseases like black pod and pests, signaling that the farm needs pruning or gradual replanting.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni helai tamɔ black pods kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ waa. Etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afo ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo adu ekoŋŋ fiofio.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my crops more frequently now than in past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ fe afii ni eho lɛ?
