english: Changes in local weather patterns and the loss of surrounding forest cover mean pests like mirids reproduce faster and face fewer natural predators, making regular monitoring and treatment necessary.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli kɛ kooi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni laajeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋulamiiaŋ sũ baanyɛ afɔ oya ni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ fioo pɛ akpee. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ lɛ daa ni atsa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry out faster during dry spells now than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli bianɛ fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Land cleared of shade trees exposes the topsoil to direct heat, causing water to evaporate rapidly. Covering the soil with leaves or straw (mulching) helps trap moisture around crop roots.
ga: Hei ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ lɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do officers recommend cutting excess branches off my cocoa trees when leaves help plants grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Akɛni baai yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa hewɔ lɛ

english: Pruning removes diseased or crowded branches so sunlight and air can flow through the canopy. This airflow prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spread and helps the tree direct energy into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Will planting cassava right next to my young cocoa trees harm the cocoa growth?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baafite kookoo lɛ dalɛ?

english: Cassava feeds heavily from the upper soil. If planted too close, its roots will steal water and nutrients from young cocoa trees, so safe distance spacing is required between them.
ga: Cassava naa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ahi kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: How many years does a cocoa seedling take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties typically start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years, while traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years. Once mature, a well-managed cocoa tree can keep producing pods for 30 years or more.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii kɛyashi afii 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25–30 years, their natural vigor declines, branches become woody and weak, and the soil loses nutrients over time. Pruning, applying fertilizer, or gradually replanting young seedlings helps restore high yields.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye afii 25-30 lɛ, ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Niji lɛ bafeɔ tsei ni amɛhe waaa. Ni niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui bibii ni afolɔ, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, loo adu fiofio lɛ baaye abua ni aná yibii babaoo.

english: What makes cocoa a good crop to plant for my children and grandchildren to inherit?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo feɔ tso kpakpa ni obaanyɛ okɛha obii kɛ obii lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop, meaning once established, it yields valuable harvest seasons year after year for decades without needing to be replanted every season like maize or cassava.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ni yeɔ daa, ni tsɔɔ akɛ kɛji ato shishi pɛ lɛ, Ebaawo ŋmaa ni jara wa afi fɛɛ afi kɛyashi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu lɛ ekoŋŋ daa be, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or cassava on the same land with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with food crops like plantain is recommended because plantains provide essential shade to keep young cocoa trees from burning in the sun while giving you early harvests and income.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu kookoo bibii kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains, ejaakɛ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo tsei bibii akashã yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa anáa ŋmaa oya kɛ shika.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and look weak during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during dry weather to save water. Applying mulch—like dry leaves or cocoa pod husks—around the base of the trees keeps the soil moist and cool, helping the tree survive dry spells.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ baai ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔji, wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why do cocoa trees need large shade trees growing around them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei he hiaa tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect delicate cocoa trees from harsh sunlight and strong winds, lower the temperature of the farm, and drop leaves that decompose into rich organic fertilizer for the soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do so many tiny cocoa flowers fall off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects. High heat, heavy rain, or lack of soil nutrients can also cause the tree to shed excess flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Tsei fioo ko pɛ ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli, latsaa ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi babaoo ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ.

english: Will cutting off branches from my cocoa tree hurt it or help it produce more fruit?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ baafite lɛ loo ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Regular pruning helps the tree by removing dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to flow through. This prevents fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ. koni eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli Koni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning dense shade, and removing infected pods quickly helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. weeding Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli wa. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ oya. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are lacking nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa trees lack nutrients, their leaves often turn yellow, growth becomes stunted, and the tree produces small or misshapen pods. Adding compost or specialized cocoa fertilizer restores soil health and tree productivity.
ga: Kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. ni tso lɛ baaná ŋmeii bibii loo ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ aná yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baa hee lɛ nɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden change in weather. If the plant gets too stressed or lacks enough water during flowering, it sheds flowers to save its energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛ yashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa. Kɛji tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ babaoo shishi loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ehe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same piece of land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Groundnuts belong to the bean family, which actually puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally, helping restore fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua ni okɛ fɔmɔ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. You can test-harvest just one or two plants at the edge of your farm to check if the tubers are mature and full.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni okpa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ okwɛ kɛji bulb lɛ edara ni eyi obɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. During hot and dry weather, tomato leaves curl inward to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yam tubers become bent or short when the soil underneath them is too hard, stony, or compacted. Yams need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil so the tubers can easily expand downwards.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kukuji kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, yitso lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shi oya.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars always attack the inside roll of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-babi corn leaf rolls lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the center leaf roll (the whorl) of young maize because it shelters them from the hot sun and birds while giving them direct access to the softest, most tender part of the plant.
ga: Asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai (rings) lɛ amli ejaakɛ ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛyaa tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees dry up and drop many of their small young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ? lots dani etsɔ agbo

english: This is known as 'cherelle wilt.' Cocoa trees naturally produce more young pods than they can feed, so the tree discards excess pods to focus its energy and water on maturing the strongest remaining pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle wilting’ Cacao tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ enu lɛ atsu ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ he nii.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and greener than my planted crops right after a rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local soil and climate, so they absorb rain and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early stops them from stealing food from your farm plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure without enough phosphorus, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and large leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli.

english: Why is it helpful for my field if I plant groundnuts or beans after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that have special roots capable of taking nitrogen from the air and putting it back into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores soil fertility for your next crop without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni ooodu yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and drop off when I clear all the big shade trees from my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji mijie kookoo tsei wuji kɛjɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Cocoa trees—especially young ones—are naturally understory plants that burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Retaining shade trees shields the cocoa leaves from intense heat, retains moisture in the soil, and creates a humid environment for healthy growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ bibii Eji tso ko ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ otso lɛ wo hulutsoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛha dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight so the leaves can make food for the plant. Staking lifts the foliage off the wet ground, which boosts growth and prevents fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai afite baai lɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete directly with the main plantain stem for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong followers, ensuring the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa ahi shi koni ekwɛ akɛ tso titri lɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do farmers cover the bare soil around vegetable beds with dry grass or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai aŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry organic material—a practice called mulching—keeps moisture in the soil by preventing evaporation from the sun. It also keeps the soil cool, stops weeds from taking over, and prevents rain from washing away soil nutrients.
ga: Mulching kɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli Atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off the stems without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off unfertilized when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when insects damage the flowers. Keeping the soil consistently moist and offering light shade during the hottest part of the day helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo fɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft and rotting underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because air cannot reach the roots when the ground stays soaked for too long, allowing waterborne fungi to attack them. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Curled, twisted pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant growing normally.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: What is causing small green and brown caterpillars to eat holes through the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that burrows into the funnels of young maize plants. Detecting them early and applying organic neem oil solutions or recommended insecticides into the central whorl helps protect the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni boteɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ona amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛwo ŋaa akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo teŋgbɛ kooloo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my crops have received enough water so I don't waste it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa? Bɔni afee ni okashɛrɛ jwɛi oshwie?

english: Crops have enough water when the soil around their roots is moist to a finger's depth without forming standing muddy pools. Stopping the water at this point prevents root rot and saves water.
ga: Tsei lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ. Shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ kɛyashɛɔ inchi kome pɛ. Kɛji akɛ afeee sũ ni damɔ shi lɛ, nu lɛ ni oookpa yɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite ni ebaaha nu akafite.

english: Early morning is best because the soil is cool, allowing crop roots to absorb maximum moisture before the intense sunshine evaporates the water off the ground.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu babaoo. Dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use a flexible rubber pipe to direct water straight to my plant roots?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ hose ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔɔ nu gbɛ kɛya shishifãi ni adu lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, using a rubber hose at the base of plants delivers water right to the root zone, which saves water from evaporating and keeps crop leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ hose ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, nu lɛ yaa shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ baai lɛ mli egbiɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: What is the difference between hybrid maize seeds and the ordinary local seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa daa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in high-tech facilities to produce much bigger yields, resist diseases, and grow uniformly. Local seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over time, resulting in smaller plants and lower overall yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli titri yɛ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ ŋaa nitsumɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni amɛná yibiiwoo babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to give more fertilizer and care to hybrid seeds compared to ordinary seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui folo lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops are built to produce a massive harvest, which means they are much 'hungrier' than regular seeds. To reach their full yield potential, they require proper feeding with fertilizer, consistent water, and clean field conditions.
ga: Abɔɔ tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he koni amɛwo ŋmaa babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ ‘hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ’ babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa lɛ. bɔni afee ni amɛwo nyɛmɔ fɛɛ Amɛhe miihia niyenii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli tse

english: Will buying expensive hybrid seeds still give me a bigger harvest if I cannot afford fertilizer?
ga: Ani hybrid dumɔwui ni jara wa ni miheɔ lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba lolo kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, planting high-quality hybrid seeds without fertilizer will not give you good results. Good seeds need nutrients to grow; without fertilizer, a hybrid crop will perform just as poorly as ordinary local maize.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ekɛ yibii kpakpai baaa. Dumɔwui kpakpai he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. kɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa fɛɛ

english: Can I harvest seeds from my hybrid maize crop and plant them again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended. Seeds collected from a hybrid harvest lose their special traits in the second generation, leading to uneven crop height, weaker plants, and a significant drop in yield.
ga: Akɛ yijiemɔ haaa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ agbɔjɔmɔi lɛ feɔ ekome, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: What is compound fertilizer, and why should I apply it when I am planting my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ mikwɛ tsei?

english: Compound fertilizer contains a balanced mix of basic nutrients—usually Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium—that help young plants build deep, strong root systems and sturdy leaves right from the start.
ga: Nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ potassium lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso bibioo lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. kɛ baai ni he wa kɛjɛ shishijee

english: What does 'top dressing' mean when feeding my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘top dressing’ shishi kɛji akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miiha niyenii?

english: Top dressing means applying a second round of fast-acting fertilizer directly to the soil around the base of growing plants weeks after planting, giving them a vital nutrient boost when they are growing rapidly.
ga: Top dressing tsɔɔ akɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii oya ni ji enyɔ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Aduɔ tso lɛ shishi otsii komɛi yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Koni akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa afata tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa oya lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I put all my fertilizer into the soil on the day I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny seedlings cannot consume large amounts of fertilizer at once. Splitting application into planting time and later top dressing ensures nutrients are available when the plant actually needs them, preventing fertilizer from washing away in heavy rain.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amlijaa kɛyaa be ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ sɛɛ mli atade ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa be mli ni tso lɛ he hiaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear signal that your soil lacks Nitrogen. This tells you that your crop has used up its initial food and needs a top-dressing fertilizer application immediately to stay healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite shishijee niyenii lɛ, ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etee hiɛ waa awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I remove weeds before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that will consume the fertilizer before your crop's roots can reach it. Clearing weeds first ensures your crop gets the full benefit of the fertilizer you purchased.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni daa oya ni baaye ŋmɔshi nibii dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana ŋmɔshi nibii ni oheɔ lɛ he sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I test whether a new crop variety performs better than my traditional variety?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji tso henɔ hee ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe mi shishijee tso lɛ?

english: You can plant a small patch of the new variety alongside your traditional crop on the same piece of land, give both the exact same fertilizer, water, and care, and compare their yields at harvest time.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu srɔtoi heei bibii. Yɛ nyɛ blema tsei lɛ asɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ, ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ kwɛmɔ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ haa. ni okɛ yibiiwoo ni anáa yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ato he

english: If I have a huge piece of land, why shouldn't I just clear and plant all of it at the same time?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ wulu ko lɛ Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni miduɔ nii yɛ be kome mli?

english: Planting everything at once can overwhelm your labor and resources. Phasing your planting schedule allows you to manage weeding, watering, and harvesting in stages so your crops do not spoil before you can reach them.
ga: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni oookwɛ shikome lɛ baanyɛ aye onitsumɔ kɛ onibii anɔ kunim. Gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ ashwiemɔ, nu ni oooha, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ akafite dani amɛbashɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Applying composted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the fuel it needs to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná tsofa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants take much longer to grow when I plant them very close to my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together compete for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each crop enough space ensures they get the resources needed to grow fast and yield well.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ náa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I avoid burning all the grass and bush on my land before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops. Clearing by hand or letting cut grass decompose leaves valuable natural nutrients in the ground.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Nine ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ loo ni ashiɔ lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense heat. Providing proper shade or ensuring adequate soil moisture helps the plant recover quickly.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Shade ni sa ni akɛhaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ oya.

english: Why are holes appearing in my cabbage leaves even though I water the plants every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ kaabe baa nɔ lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa tsei lɛ daa gbi?

english: Watering helps plants grow, but it does not stop insects like caterpillars from eating the leaves. You need targeted pest management, such as spraying neem leaf extract, to protect your foliage.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa. Shi enɛ tsiii kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ anaa. Ohe miihia ni okwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. koni akɛbu obaai lɛ ahe

english: How do green leaves on top of the ground help my yam grow big underground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-sweet potato lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Leaves act like solar panels that catch sunlight and make food for the plant. That food travels down into the soil and gets stored, which is what causes the yam tuber to swell and grow large.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, amɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii. Nakai niyenii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛtoɔ, ni no ji nɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cowpea crops manage to stay green even when there is little rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have deep root systems that search for hidden water deep underground, and their leaves are naturally built to conserve moisture during dry spells.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ nu ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni amɛbaai lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers rot in the soil after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots need air in the soil to survive. When water collects around the stem and cannot drain away, the roots suffocate and decay. Planting on mounds helps excess water drain.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia plantain shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ he ni anyɛɛɛ ajie lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year if I plant cassava in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo faaa daa afi kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like beans helps restore the soil's natural strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Kasava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I build a shade cover over my young cocoa seedlings instead of leaving them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe hulutsoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛhi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender like young children and burn easily under strong heat. Providing shade protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ gbekɛ bibioo, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: How do I know my tomato seedlings are ready to be moved from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaajɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are ready to transplant when their stems are thick, steady, and have at least four to six leaves. Moving them too early when they are soft and weak will cause them to collapse and die.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ egbɔ, amɛhe wa ni kɛ hoo lɛ, amɛyɛ baai 4-6. Kɛ́ otsi amɛ oya tsɔ beni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbee shi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is it bad if I leave four or five maize plants growing in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mishi ŋmãa tsei ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many plants grow in one spot, they fight each other for nutrients and water. Thinning them out allows the remaining plants to stand steady, develop thick stems, and produce big corn ears.
ga: Kɛ tso ko da babaoo yɛ he kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ mlɛo lɛ, tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ, amɛnáa ŋmeii ni mli tse, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground so they can get plenty of sunlight and stay stable. Without support, wet soil will rot the leaves and the tubers beneath will stay small.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbo ni bulbs ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahi shi bibii.

english: Why must I be so careful when clearing weeds around very young cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi miikpa ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cassava shoots have delicate roots near the surface. If you dig too aggressively near them while weeding, you can damage their roots and ruin the plant's growth early on.
ga: Kasava tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji otsi obɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ beni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ, Obaanyɛ ofite amɛshishifãi lɛ ni ofite tsei ni daa mra lɛ.

english: Is it fine for me to plant plantain and cassava together on the same farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu plantain kɛ cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, managing multiple crops together makes good use of your land. Plantains provide useful shade early on, while cassava grows steadily alongside it without ruining either crop's harvest if spaced properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ooofee ekome kɛtsu nii lɛ haa okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Plantains haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ he kome ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he jogbaŋŋ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one tree, they steal food and water from the main plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha plantains akuu ko ni dara ni ehe wa aba.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings bend over and rot when I pour water on them directly from a heavy bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwie baagi ni tsii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pouring heavy streams of water damages delicate stems and pushes weak roots out of the soil. Young plants need gentle watering with a fine spray so they stay upright and healthy.
ga: Nu babaoo ni ashwieɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ekɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni akɛ nu ni mli tse fioo afɔ amɛ nɔ blɛoo. Koni tso lɛ ahi shi ja ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves on my young plantain trees tear and fall over during strong windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain stems are soft and their root systems are not fully established yet. Planting border trees like Gliricidia acts as a windbreak to protect and keep your crop steady.
ga: Plantain tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ shishifãi lɛ eshɛko he kwraa lolo. Husu tsei tamɔ gliricidia ni ooodu lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi.

english: What happens if I harvest my maize early while the cobs and husks are still wet and green?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ mra? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ efɔ ni amɛji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Harvesting too early before the grains mature and dry properly will cause the corn to shrink, mold quickly in storage, and ruin the value of your hard work.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ shwere jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbɔjɔ. Mold baa oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. ni efiteɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young green maize turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that captures nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. When the groundnut plants die and rot, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ gbo ni egbo lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmei ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground even when the stem looks green and healthy above?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli lolo ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋwɛi?

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long, which smothers the roots and allows soil fungi to attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ajɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early using neem leaf spray or recommended soap mixtures stops the damage from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem baa mli tsofa loo samla ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfutu mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɔ ni efite lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak if I plant too many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the young plants compete with each other for sunlight and stretch upward too fast. Spacing seeds properly gives every stem room to catch sun, breathe air, and grow thick enough to hold heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaagbala amɛhe oya tsɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso lɛ shishi tsu fɛɛ tsu lɛ naa hulu la, emuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, ni edaraa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Yam vines produce food for their underground tubers using light caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the dark, wet soil into full sunlight, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the underground yams grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ la ni amɛbaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects or if the tree suffers from sudden drought or pest attacks. Preserving shade trees and avoiding unnecessary chemical sprays protects the beneficial midges that help turn flowers into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ yeɔ trukaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni abuɔ he jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni he ehiaaa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when planted under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ panicles bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require direct sunlight to produce the high energy needed for large, heavy fruit bunches. Deep shade from large forest trees reduces their energy, resulting in small bunches with thin fingers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia plantains tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai wuji ni tsii lɛ aba. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei niji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I water my vegetable garden in the middle of a hot, sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ nu woɔ o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering in intense afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening so the soil absorbs and holds the moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni ehi mli.

english: Why do weeds make my young tomato plants stay small and fail to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tomato tsei bibii lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight away from your main crop. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks gives your tomato plants full access to the resources they need to grow strong and set fruit.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii titrii amli lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, o-tomato tsei lɛ baaná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ dani madu tsei?

english: Rich, fertile soil is usually dark in color, soft to dig, holds moisture well, and is filled with decomposed leaves and organic matter that provide nutrients for strong plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni woɔ yibii lɛ yɛ diŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛji atsa, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyi obɔ kɛ baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa tsei lɛ anáa hewalɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes soil rich enough to produce big tubers like yams?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ewo ŋmeii wuji tamɔ ŋmeii?

english: Yams need loose, deep, nutrient-rich soil mixed with organic matter so the roots can easily expand underground without hitting hard earth or stones.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi.

english: How can I make my farm soil richer without spending a lot of money on artificial fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: You can naturally enrich your soil by spreading decomposed animal manure, letting crop leaves rot into the ground, and leaving parts of the farm to fallow and rest.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni ooogbɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ agbo ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ. ni eshi ŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejɔɔ ehe.

english: Why do my yams turn out small and deformed when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ehiii kwraa kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams become small or deformed when the soil is too hard, rocky, or depleted of nutrients, preventing the tuber from expanding freely underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii loo efiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi yɛ nɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi amɛha amɛhe.

english: Why do plantain trees require rich soil to produce large bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that require high amounts of soil moisture and nutrients like potassium to develop strong trunks and carry heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium koni ekɛma tsei ni wa kɛ panicles ni tsii.

english: Why does farmland that used to give big harvests start producing small yields after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔji ni be ko ni eho lɛ ewoɔ yibii lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming removes vital nutrients from the soil over time, leaving the land tired and depleted unless organic matter or fertilizers are added back.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Ja akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii efata he ekoŋŋ.

english: How does growing a cocoa tree differ from growing annual crops like yams?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro kookoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ afi mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he?

english: Food crops like yams mature and are harvested within a single season, while cocoa is a long-term tree crop that takes several years to establish and stays in the soil for decades.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes lɛ shwereɔ kwraa ni akpaa yɛ be kome mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take several years to yield pods while my plantains produce fruit quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni mi plantains lɛ woɔ yibii oya lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees spend their first few years developing strong trunks and deep root systems to support long-term production, whereas plantains grow quickly and complete their fruit cycle within 12 to 15 months.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛnáa amɛshishifãi ni mli wa kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaye abua ni amɛná be kakadaŋŋ. Beni plantains lɛ daa oya ni egbeɔ ewomɔ be lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant plantains on the same land where I am planting young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping plantains with young cocoa is beneficial because the plantains grow quickly to provide shade and cool soil conditions for the young cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ni akɛduɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ plantains lɛ daa oya koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ aha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees struggle to grow when planted in open, unshaded land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn easily under harsh sunlight, so they require shade crops to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ kookoo tso lɛ kɛ ehe afɔ̃ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu ehe kɛyashi ebaashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: How many weeks after planting my maize should I expect to see the cobs starting to form?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu ŋmãa lɛ? Ani esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mana ŋmei ko ni miibɔi feemɔ?

english: Maize typically begins to flower and form cobs around 8 to 10 weeks after planting, depending on the variety, as the plant needs this time to grow strong roots, stems, and leaves first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi ni efeɔ ŋmeii aaafee otsii 8 kɛyashi 10 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ he miihia be nɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛbaai ni mli wa klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and bushy for weeks before any flowers appear on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji otsii babaoo dani fɔfɔii jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants must first build a strong structure of roots, stems, and leaves to support heavy fruit; once they reach full maturity at around 6 to 8 weeks, they naturally switch to producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ama shishifãi, ŋmeii, kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛ́ amɛshɛ otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 he lɛ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai amli yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting cassava before the tubers under the ground are ready for harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ŋmei lɛ afee klalo akɛ obaakpa?

english: Cassava plants need time to store starch underground, which usually takes between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety and rainfall conditions.
ga: Be he miihia cassava tsei koni amɛkɛ starch ato shikpɔŋ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my plantain tree is mature enough to start producing a bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: A plantain tree usually produces about 30 to 40 large leaves over 9 to 12 months before it naturally shoots out a broad flag leaf and the main flower heart from the center of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains woɔ baai wuji 30 kɛyashi 40 yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli dani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwoɔ aflaŋaa baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ fɔfɔi titri lɛ tsui kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants sometimes drop their flowers instead of turning them into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat or poor water supply, which interrupts the plant's internal process of converting flowers into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo loo nu ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ gbalaa tso lɛ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa fɔfɔii feɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: How do the small flowers growing on my cocoa tree trunk actually turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called midges pollinate the small cocoa flowers, after which the flower base gradually swells and develops over 5 to 6 months into a mature cocoa pod filled with seeds.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baakwɛ fiofio. Efɔ̃ɔ ni edaa yɛ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 mli ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do some yellow flowers on my watermelon vine produce fruits while other flowers just dry up and fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi wooo yibii lɛ? Ani ebaagbi ni egbee shi?

english: Watermelon vines produce separate male and female flowers; only the female flowers, which have a small fruit swelling at their base, turn into melons after bees pollinate them.
ga: Watermelon wain tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ, ni yɔɔ aduawai bibii ni efuu yɛ amɛshishi lɛ, bafeɔ melon beni ŋmeii ewo amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How does a rice plant form grains at the top of its stem as it matures?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa tso feɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii yɛ eshishifã lɛ yiteŋgbɛ beni edara kwraa lɛ?

english: After several weeks of stem growth, the rice plant forms a hidden flower head inside the stem that emerges, opens, and fills with liquid starch that hardens into rice grains over 30 to 40 days.
ga: Yɛ otsii babaoo ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eda lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Omɔ tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yitsei ni akɛtee tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Ejeɔ kpo, egbeleɔ ehe, ni eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni mli wa ni etsɔɔ ŋmaa yɛ gbii 30 kɛyashi 40 mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants flower all at once after just a few weeks of leaf growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shikome yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni baai lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cowpeas are short-season crops designed to mature quickly, triggering flower development around 4 to 6 weeks after planting so they can produce seeds before dry weather sets in.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Koni enyɛ ewo dumɔwui dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up when the yams under the ground are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: When yam leaves yellow and dry out after 6 to 8 months, it shows that the plant has finished transferring all its energy into the underground tuber, signaling that the crop is fully mature.
ga: Kɛ́ sweet potato baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ tso lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I use household waste like kitchen scraps and dry leaves to feed my crops without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ shia jwɛi tamɔ shĩa mli nibii ni efite kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egboi lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aheee?

english: You can make compost by piling organic waste like kitchen scraps, dry leaves, and animal manure together. Over a few weeks, these break down into rich, natural fertilizer that improves your soil quality and feeds your crops for free.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ, baai ni egboi, kɛ kooloi ashwiei ni ooobua naa lɛ nɔ. yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli Enɛɛmɛi baafite ni amɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: I noticed a few insects starting to chew my vegetable leaves; should I treat the farm right away or wait to see if it gets worse?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ kooloi bibii komɛi miibɔi mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Ani esa akɛ matsa ŋmɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo mamɛ ni makwɛ ni hela lɛ he okadii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: You should act immediately when you spot early signs of pests. Taking quick action when trouble first appears stops insects from multiplying and prevents widespread damage to your entire farm.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee nɔ ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ona klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba. Kɛ́ ofee nɔ ko oya beni naagbai ba klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii ni baafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Can I use wood ash from my cooking fire to protect my garden crops from insects?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso sũ ni jɛɔ la ni akɛhooɔ nii mli lɛ atsu nii kɛbu mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Yes, sprinkling dry wood ash around plant stems or lightly dusting leaves creates a natural barrier that repels soft-bodied pests like caterpillars and beetles while adding beneficial potassium to the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso sũ ni egbi ni ashwieɔ nɔ kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi loo baai lɛ ahe sũ fioo ko feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. kɛ potassium ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fata he

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough nourishment to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is mulching, and how does spreading dry grass on my farm help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji mulching? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Mulching means covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves. This keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching tsɔɔ akɛ abaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai aha onibii ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long does it take to see improvements in my crops after applying organic manure to the soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mana hiɛyaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Organic manure breaks down slowly, so you must be patient. You will usually begin to see greener leaves and stronger growth within two to three weeks, but the greatest benefits happen over time as your soil gets richer.
ga: Organic fertilizers lɛ fiteɔ fiofio no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ oto otsui shi. Bei pii lɛ, obaaje shishi ona baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Shi sɛɛnamɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baa yɛ be mli ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate that the plant needs extra nutrients like nitrogen or is receiving inconsistent water. Removing dead leaves and applying compost will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɔ nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni egboi lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my cassava on soil mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ hi fe ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges create loose, soft soil that allows cassava roots to expand easily into large tubers. Mounding also improves drainage so excess rainwater does not rot the roots underground.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Pile lɛ hu haa nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ efiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme afternoon sun helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ shwane hulu lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops to get the best results?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: The best time to water your crops is early in the morning. Morning watering lets the plant roots drink deeply before the afternoon heat dries up the water, helping the crop stay hydrated all day.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ gĩɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when I clear all the large trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Ani ŋmɔ lɛ etee?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas that shield cocoa leaves from burning, keep the soil cool, and help the young plants retain moisture until they are mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my plantain shoots bend and lean toward one side of the field instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally turn and stretch toward the direction that receives the strongest sunlight. If taller trees block sunlight on one side, the plant will lean toward the open sky to capture enough light to produce food.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa lɛ. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsi hulu la lɛ naa yɛ fa kome lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ koni amɛná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I put many seeds in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crop seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Because no single plant gets enough nutrients, they stretch upward for light but remain too weak to develop large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛmɔ la lɛ shi amɛgbɔjɔ tsɔ lolo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension officer lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny modules on their roots that capture free fertilizer from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds heavy-eating crops like cassava without needing as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ modules bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning pale yellow from the tips, even though we have good rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Yellowing on older lower leaves is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green. The maize plant moves its remaining nitrogen up to nourish new leaf growth at the top, leaving the old bottom leaves starving.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Abɛi tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce plenty of bushy green leaves above ground, but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii akui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much chemical nitrogen or is too loose, the cassava plant spends all its food energy growing thick leaves above ground instead of sending starch down to build thick tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsofa ni ji nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu starch kɛba shi koni efee ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight exposure to produce starch for underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to full sun while preventing soil-borne rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee starch kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai ni shikpɔŋ kɛbaa lɛ naatsii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look weak and wilting in the hot afternoon heat, but stand firm again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi koni enyɛ edamɔ shi ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than roots can drink it from the dirt, causing temporary wilting to save water. Overnight, when temperatures drop, the roots catch up on drinking water, lifting the leaves back up.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛhere nu. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ nu ni anuɔ lɛ he ni amɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off the plant before turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or lack of wind and bees to pollinate the blooms. Without successful pollination or under high heat stress, the plant drops the flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye loo eyɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I see small jagged holes on my young corn leaves and fine powdery dirt inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni akɛ powda fee jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding deep inside the tender central leaf funnel of young maize. They feed on the soft growing leaves where birds and sprays cannot easily reach them, leaving holes as the leaf unrolls.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni okpoi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he oya ni amɛshwieɔ nɔ. Ehaa buji baa kɛji baai lɛ gbele.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry and need extra plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni maná tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Just like people show signs when they are hungry, plants show signs like pale or yellow leaves, weak stems, and slow growth when they lack nutrients. Providing proper plant food helps them stay healthy and grow plump.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi feɔ amɛnii kɛ́ hɔmɔ ye amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli. Tso niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Will giving my crops more fertilizer automatically make the harvest bigger?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Feeding your crops helps them gain size and stay healthy, but too much fertilizer can burn their roots or cause lots of leaf growth without producing actual fruit. Balanced feeding is what gives the best yield.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha amɛ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã eshishifãi lɛ loo eha ebaakwɛ̃ babaoo ni ewooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ. Niyenii ni ja ji nɔ ni haa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why do my neighbour's cassava roots grow so big while mine stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ miida waa shi minɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and rich soil nutrients, especially potassium, to expand. If the plant doesn't get enough nourishment or the soil is too hard, the tubers cannot swell up and gain size.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo. titri lɛ potassium ni akɛbaagbɛ eshwa Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Yitso lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ eshwa ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: What makes my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper aduawai?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Feeding the plant properly helps it hold onto its flowers so they turn into heavy fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi ni tsɔɔ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: How can I make my tomatoes grow plump and juicy instead of small and hard?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-tomato lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee bibioo ni ewa?

english: Tomatoes need steady water and key soil nutrients like potassium to fill out. Good plant food allows the tomato plant to move sugars into the fruit so it swells up full and healthy.
ga: Tomato he miihia nu daa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, koni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Tso niyenii kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa tomato tso lɛ ni ekɛ sugars lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong leaves and stems. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does animal manure help my crops grow better than using plain soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as a rich, slow-release food for your crops. It feeds the beneficial living things in the soil and holds moisture, allowing crops to continuously feed and grow healthy.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni jara wa, ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo kɛhaa onibii. Ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa anáa niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer all at once or spread it out as the crop grows?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ shikome loo mawo ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Crops need different amounts of food at different growth stages. Giving food in smaller split applications ensures the plant has steady nourishment as it gains size, rather than wasting fertilizer.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Niyenii ni akɛhaa kɛtsɔ mligbalamɔ mli bibii bibii anɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa be fɛɛ be beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why are my maize cobs not filling up with grains all the way to the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii eyiko kɛyashiɔ eshishi lɛ?

english: Poor cob filling happens when the maize plant lacks water or nutrients during the flowering stage. Giving the plant enough food and water at this stage ensures the cob develops plump grains right to the tip.
ga: Cob filling ni ehiii lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tsei lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ.

english: What can I give my plantain trees so that the bunches grow large and heavy?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ maha mi plantain lɛ koni niji lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee shwiili?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that require plenty of organic matter, potassium, and water. Proper soil feeding gives the tree the energy required to support a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli, potassium, kɛ nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfi fãji wuji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture to protect young cocoa seedlings during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves in young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or excess water around the roots, which prevents the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmã bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn my bush before planting crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã mi jwɛi lɛ dani midu tsei lɛ?

english: While burning clears land quickly, it destroys rich organic matter, kills beneficial soil organisms, and leaves the soil dry and exposed to heavy rain erosion.
