ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ hu. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my land is good for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava prefers loose, well-drained sandy-loam soil. Soil that holds too much water or stays sticky like heavy clay will cause cassava roots to rot instead of growing thick tubers.
ga: Cassava sumɔɔ ŋã ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni hiɛɔ nu babaoo loo ni shwieɔ shi tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excess moisture and shade. Pruning overhead branches to let sunlight and air into the farm helps reduce its spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋɔ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji fɛ̃i kɛ shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up pollen, causing the flowers to drop off before they can be pollinated and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Early morning is the best time to water crops because the roots can absorb moisture before the daytime heat causes high evaporation, and leaves dry quickly to prevent fungal growth.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba ni baai lɛ agbi oya koni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Why does my yam yield get smaller every year even when I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? ni midu yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Growing yam on the same plot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients. Rotating yam with legumes or leaving the land to fallow allows the soil to restore its fertility.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsake loo ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over before the bunches are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots. As the heavy bunch matures, strong winds can pull the plant down; supporting the stalk with bamboo or wooden props prevents this.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ eda kwraa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do I have to put sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing under the ground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet soil so all the leaves get sun and stay safe from rotting.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe koni amɛkafite.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or when there is too much water sitting around the roots. Adding fertilizer or compost helps the leaves become green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer to my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer because the crop cannot take it in without water.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɛji nu bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce flowers, and does that mean the cassava roots under the ground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Flowering is just a natural part of the cassava plant's lifecycle and does not mean the tubers are ready. Cassava tubers reach full size based on age—usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko kɛkɛ ni kɔɔ ŋmei wala shihilɛ he. Ni etsɔɔɔ akɛ yitso lɛ efee klalo. Cassava shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants have small holes in them and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center of the plant and eat the fresh leaves, which slows down growth if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall caterpillars kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Amɛ teɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ teŋ ni amɛ yeɔ baai heei lɛ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by insects. Treating the farm for pests helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ atsamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During peak heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They droop to protect themselves from heat, but usually stand up straight again in the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛkotoɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he. shi bei pii lɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land stop producing good yields if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛho lɛ aya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a clear sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen helps crops stay green and grow leaves, so when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the newer top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie emli nibii lɛ fioo kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I avoid putting too much chemical fertilizer on my cowpea crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ amli lɛ he?

english: Legumes like cowpeas can naturally trap nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. If you give them too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant gets lazy and grows only big leaves and branches instead of producing flower buds and bean pods.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ Tso lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai wuji kɛ niji pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ fɔfɔihi kɛ ngmahi nɛ a ngmaa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain leaves water standing in the field for too long, the soil gets waterlogged, choking the roots and allowing soft-rot bacteria and fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade cover for the dirt. It keeps the sun from drying out the ground too quickly, holds water in the root zone longer, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa nu hiɔ shishifã lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die within a few days even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne sickness that enters the plant roots and blocks the tiny tubes carrying water up to the leaves. Because the water cannot move up the stem, the plant wilts even in moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ tsɔnei bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa lɛ kɛbaa. ni woɔ nu kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya tso lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ po nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and twisted leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, thrips, or aphids feeding on the tender young leaves. As they suck the plant juices, they cause leaf damage and can spread crop viruses.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛmuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to push tall bamboo sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi ŋmei lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers based on how much sunlight their leaves can catch. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground into the sunlight, prevents rot from wet soil, and allows the plant to make enough energy to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ hulu la ni baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ naa. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ naa. ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down easily when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like hardwood trees; their roots are shallow and stay near the topsoil. When a heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the tree becomes heavy on top and strong winds can pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni wa. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ja tso ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ fiɔ esɛɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their blossoms before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or attack by sucking bugs like mirids. Keeping proper shade trees in the farm and controlling insect pests helps the flowers stay on the tree to become cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni nuɔ amɛ lɛ tutua amɛ. Tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ atsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my rice plants in low-lying swampy fields turn pale yellow and grow very slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi lɛ? Ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eda blɛoo waa?

english: In flooded lowland soil, oxygen gets used up quickly, which causes iron in the soil to react in a way that harms the plant roots, a problem called iron toxicity. Proper field drainage allows fresh air back into the soil so the roots can absorb food again.
ga: yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu afua nyɛɔ eshɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Oxygen lɛ fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa dade ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yeɔ tsei shishifãi awui nɔ. Naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dade ni gbeɔ mɔ. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow fine together when they are small, but start choking each other when they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni eji gbekɛ lɛ? Shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsiɔ amɛhe beni edaa lɛ?

english: When crop seedlings are young, they only need a tiny amount of water, fertilizer, and light, so they easily live close together. As they grow into adult plants, their roots and leaves expand, causing them to fight heavily with each other for the limited food and sunlight in that small space.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ darako lɛ, nu, ŋma, kɛ la fioo pɛ he hiaa amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ewaaa akɛ aaahi shi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe. Kɛ amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ tsei ni eda lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baadara. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛtao niyenii kɛ hulu la waa yɛ nakai kpokpaa bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave wide spaces between my cocoa trees when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ miidu nii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings look small at first, but mature cocoa trees spread wide roots and thick leaves. Spacing them properly prevents adult trees from blocking each other's light and competing for food in the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shishijee mli. Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ baatsi tsei ni eda lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe la naa ni amɛkaye niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akaŋ.

english: Is it bad if I plant three or four pepper seeds in one hole and leave all of them to grow?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli ni miha amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, because as the pepper plants grow into adults, they will fight for the same soil nutrients like hungry children sharing a small bowl of soup, resulting in weak plants with tiny peppers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ onukpa Amɛbaawuu amɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni gbekɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small tubers when I plant them right next to my yam crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ yɛ mi sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Both cassava and yam are heavy feeding crops. When planted too close together, their underground roots struggle against each other for space and plant food, leaving neither crop with enough energy to build big tubers.
ga: Kasava kɛ sweet potato fɛɛ ji tsei ni ayeɔ waa. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ baaná lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee bulbs agboi.

english: Why do I need to remove pepper seedlings from the nursery bed and spread them out in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie pepper dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the nursery, small seedlings can share a tight space peacefully. But as they mature, they need their own space in the field so their roots can spread without fighting neighboring plants for nutrients.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ aja he ko ni mli wa yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ mli. Shi kɛ amɛdara kwraa lɛ Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe miihia amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why are my plantain trees growing very tall, thin, and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ daa, egbɔjɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are crowded, they compete fiercely for sunlight by stretching upward as fast as possible to reach above their neighbors, which makes their stems thin, weak, and easily fallen by wind.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do I need to prune away extra branches from my tomato plants as they get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As a tomato plant matures, its branches start competing with each other for the plant's food and energy. Trimming extra branches stops this internal struggle and directs energy into producing bigger tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato tso lɛ da lɛ Eniji lɛ hu jeɔ amɛhe akaŋshii shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛ tso lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ haa mligbɛ naagbai kpaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tomatoi wuji.

english: Why do crops in the middle of my crowded field look yellow, while the ones on the edges look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji.

english: The crops at the outer edges have free space to gather sunlight and fresh air. The crops in the crowded middle are trapped in a tough competition with surrounding plants for light and soil moisture.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ haa gbɛ ni akɛbuaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ebɔi akaŋshii ni naa wa. Koni ana la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Can I plant cowpea next to my maize without the two crops fighting for food in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi ni tsei enyɔ lɛ ewuuuu yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, because cowpeas and maize use soil nutrients differently. Cowpeas actually capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, so instead of fighting the maize, they help nourish it.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛni tsinabii kɛ ŋmãa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ hewɔ lɛ, tsinabii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ baawu Moŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds damage my young crops so easily compared to my big, fully grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gbeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ oya kɛ akɛto miŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young crops are still weak and easily overwhelmed by fast-growing weeds that steal their sunlight and water. Fully grown crops have large leaves that shade out weeds, winning the battle for sunlight.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la kɛ nu lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ eye hulu la lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant lacks sufficient water. Extreme heat damages the pollen, preventing the flower from forming a tomato, so keeping the soil moist and providing partial shade during peak heat can help.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi afee tomato. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha ŋmɔlɔ fioo ko aba yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. These pests suck the sap out of young leaves, causing them to distort as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon even if it rained earlier in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In the intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. This temporary wilting is the plant's defense mechanism to reduce surface area and conserve water until the temperature cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu lɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and allows the plant to produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, share food, water, and soil nutrients with the main plantain stem. By cutting away the extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones, all the energy goes into producing a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ jaa niyenii, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ ni ahiɛɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛfee plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and green, but the corn cobs remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo.

english: Maize plants that grow tall with few or small cobs often have too much nitrogen fertilizer but lack phosphorus and potassium, which promote fruit and grain development. It can also happen if the plants are packed too closely together, preventing proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ ni ŋmeii fioo loo bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shi ebɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium. ni haa aduawai kɛ dumɔwui lɛ yaa hiɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni ekɛtsi pollination ni sa naa.

english: If I plant maize on the same piece of land every year, why does my yield drop each season?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. It also lets crop-specific pests and soil diseases build up in the field, which reduces plant growth over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow so slowly if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures your young plants get all the resources they need during their most critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni mli wa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni onaa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need to be planted under plantain shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots underground are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare stems, and the base of the main stem thickens. You can also carefully dig up one plant to check if the roots are thick and firm before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eshwɛ ni tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome hu he nii ni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my local mango trees take longer to produce fruit compared to the new varieties people are planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe tsei heei ni gbɔmɛi duɔ lɛ?

english: Local mango varieties naturally rely on weather patterns and seasonal cycles to bloom at their own slow pace, whereas modern or introduced varieties are bred to mature faster and respond quickly to growth stimulants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ be mli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛfɔ̃ blɛoo, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ loo tsei ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ koni amɛshwere oya ni amɛtsu nibii ni haa amɛdara lɛ ahe nii oya.

english: Why do improved fruit varieties need so much more chemical input than the old local trees my father planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso yibii ni atsake amɛmli lɛ biɔ tsofai babaoo fe maŋ tsei ni mitsɛ du lɛ?

english: Older local trees were selected naturally to survive tough conditions with zero care, while newer improved varieties are bred specifically for high yield, which requires regular feeding and management to perform.
ga: Ahala maŋbii tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, afɔɔ ŋmeii heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enɛ biɔ ni aha lɛ niyenii ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa.

english: How do I know if my fruit tree is a local type or an improved variety that needs special inputs to bear fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tso yibii lɛ ji maŋ lɛ mli tso loo tso ni atsake lɛ ni biɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi koni ewo yibii?

english: Local varieties usually grow very tall, take many years to start fruiting, and produce naturally during the main season, while improved varieties are typically shorter, often grafted, and require special care to yield well.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli henɔi lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ ni yaa shɔŋŋ waa. Eheɔ afii babaoo dani ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be titri lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ feɔ kuku, bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii woɔ mli, ni ebiɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko koni amɛná yibii kpakpai.

english: What are these chemical medicines people spray on mango trees to make them flower before the main season?
ga: Mɛi kɛ tsofai nɛɛ woɔ mango tsei amli koni amɛwo fɔfɔi dani be titri lɛ aba?

english: These are chemical flower inductors or growth regulators—often called 'force materials'—that signal the tree to stop growing leaves and start producing flowers ahead of its normal calendar time.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsofai ni haa fɔfɔii yaa hiɛ loo ni haa amɛdaraa. ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Regulatory material’ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekpa baai lɛ adalɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ dani kalanda be ni sa lɛ aba

english: Can I use flower-forcing chemicals on my traditional local mango trees to make them bear fruit faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai anyɛ fɔfɔi anɔ yɛ maŋbii mango tsei anɔ koni amɛwo yibii oya?

english: Traditional local varieties do not react as well to forcing chemicals because they have strong natural internal clocks, so using these chemicals on them may give poor results or waste your money.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ haaa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai nɛɛ ni okɛaatsu nii yɛ tsofai srɔtoi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko akajɛ mli aba loo ebaafite oshika.

english: Will forcing my crops to produce fruit out of season give me good quality fruit?
ga: Ani kɛ́ minyɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwo yibii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Out-of-season fruit can be high quality if the tree receives enough water and extra nutrients, but if you force the tree without feeding it properly, the fruit will be small and poor in taste.
ga: Yibii ni bɛ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji tso lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he. Shi kɛji onyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ohaaa lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Yibii lɛ baafee bibioo ni ehiii.

english: If I start using chemical flower inductors on my fruit trees, do I have to keep using them every single year?
ga: Kɛji mibɔi tsofai ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ aduawai tsei anɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mikɛtsu nii daa afi?

english: Yes, once an improved tree becomes accustomed to chemical induction for fruiting, it develops a reliance on those inputs and will likely fail to flower predictably if you stop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tso ni atsake lɛ lɛ etsɔ tsofai ni tsirɛɔ lɛ koni ewo yibii pɛ. Tso lɛ baadamɔ nakai nibii ni haa anáa nii lɛ anɔ. Ni esumɔɔ ni efee fɔfɔi bɔ ni atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ lɛ kɛji okpa.

english: What happens to my fruit trees if I suddenly stop giving them the yield-boosting chemicals I usually apply?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛgboi trukaa? Mikpa tsofai ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni mifɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ hamɔ.

english: When you stop applying the chemicals, the tree goes into a resting or recovery phase and may produce little to no fruit for a couple of seasons until it resets its natural growth pattern.
ga: Kɛji okpa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ Tso lɛ baabote hejɔɔmɔ loo hewalɛwoo be mli. ni ebaanyɛ ewo yibii fioo ko loo ewooo yibii ko kwraa yɛ bei fioo komɛi amli kɛyashi be mli ni bɔ ni edaraa ehaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baaje shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it bad for the long-term health of my tree if I force it to bear fruit every season using medicine?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa tsu nii ni minyɛ mitso lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii daa be lɛ, ani ebaana hewalɛnamɔ nɔ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ?

english: Forcing a tree continuously without giving it rest, adequate water, and fertilizer drains its stored energy, which can weaken the tree, shorten its lifespan, and make it vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Ni anyɛɔ tso nɔ be fɛɛ be ni ahaaa lɛ hejɔɔmɔ Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite hewalɛ ni ato lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ, eha ewala be lɛ afee kuku, ni eha helai srɔtoi baanyɛ amɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why won't my improved fruit tree produce a good harvest on its own if I stop applying the fruiting medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso yibii ni mifee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ wooo yibii kpakpai kɛji mikpa tso yibii tsofa lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Improved varieties are not naturally self-sufficient like wild local trees; they are designed to produce heavy crops only when supported by a continuous schedule of inputs and proper management.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ mli tamɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Afee lɛ koni ekɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa pɛ atsu nii koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii aba.

english: Why do my crops grow so much better on the land near the river after the floodwater goes down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko nɔ yɛ nu afua ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When river water overflows and recedes, it leaves behind silt—a fine mixture of nutrient-rich soil and organic matter. This natural sediment settles on your land and enriches the soil, giving your crops essential nutrients to grow faster and healthier.
ga: Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ Eshiɔ ŋmeii, ni ji shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ efutu. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli sũ nɛɛ shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ. Ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Is the brown mud left on my farm after heavy rain bad for my crops, or does it help them?
ga: Ani sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii loo eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ?

english: That brown mud is actually silt carried by moving water. Instead of harming your farm, it acts as a natural fertilizer by depositing fresh minerals and rich topsoil onto your land, which helps feed your crops.
ga: Muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji sũ ni nu ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ woɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite oŋmɔ lɛ Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ sũ heei kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa ni ekɛwoɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the plants on my low-lying land stay greener than the ones on higher ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ fe mishikpɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Water naturally runs downhill, carrying fine soil particles called silt with it. When that water collects and settles on low-lying land, it leaves behind rich nutrients and moisture that keep your crops green and healthy.
ga: Nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Ekɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ sediment lɛ yaa. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa ni egbee hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ Nu shĩɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ esɛɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Can dirty water from run-off actually make worn-out soil fertile again?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, water that looks dirty is usually carrying silt and decomposed plant material from upstream. When this water settles on your land, it deposits a fresh layer of rich soil that restores nutrients to tired land.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, nu ni tamɔ nɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei amli nibii ni egbo kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ nu nɛɛ gbee oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebua shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Should I clear away the dark layer of soil that settles on my field after the valley floods?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie sũ ni mli edɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli nu afua ko sɛɛ?

english: No, you should leave it there. That dark layer is silt, which is full of natural plant food washed down from higher areas. Leaving it on your field improves your soil quality without you needing to buy expensive fertilizers.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi yɛ jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ ji sũ. Eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni akɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛbaa lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why does my maize grow taller when planted in river mud compared to regular dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ faa mli muji mli kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi daa lɛ he lɛ?

english: River mud contains fine silt particles that are packed with minerals and retain moisture very well. This combination of natural food and consistent water allows your maize roots to easily absorb what they need to grow tall.
ga: Faa mli muji lɛ yɛ sũ bibii bibii ni eyi kɛ shika tsuru ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-corn shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ oya.

english: What is inside river silt that makes it act like fertilizer for my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli ni haa efeɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: River silt is made of tiny soil particles mixed with decayed leaves and organic matter washed from many places. When it settles on your soil, it breaks down easily and releases nutrients that your vegetables can immediately use.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ji nɔ ni feɔ faa mli ŋmeii. Akɛ baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ahoɔ kɛjɛɔ hei babaoo kɛbaa lɛ efutu mli. kɛji egbee shikpɔŋ Efiteɔ oya ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni o-vegetables lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ kpo.

english: Why does soil that receives mud deposits from streams stay moist longer during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni nine shɛɔ muji ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ faai amli lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The fine silt particles deposited by stream water create a smooth, dense soil layer that holds onto water much better than coarse, sandy soil. This keeps moisture trap near the roots even when the rains stop.
ga: Nibii bibii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa po.

english: Why do my crops look so fresh and strong a few weeks after water collects and dries up on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ehee ni amɛhe wa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nu ebua naa ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: As water slowly drains or evaporates from your land, the heavy nutrients and fine silt suspended in it sink into the ground. Your crop roots absorb these freshly settled nutrients, giving the plants a quick growth boost.
ga: Beni nu lɛ hoɔ fiofio loo ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Niyenii mli nibii ni tsii kɛ sũ bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ sũ lɛ mli. Otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii heei ni eba shi nɛɛ. Ha tsei akwɛ̃ oya

english: How can I tell if floodwater has added good soil to my farm or just damaged it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu afua lɛ miiha miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miifee fɛo loo eefite lɛ?

english: If the water leaves behind a soft, fine layer of dark or brown dirt (silt) once it drains away, it has nourished your land. As long as standing water doesn't drown the plants for too long, that settled dirt will boost crop growth.
ga: Kɛji nu bibioo ko ni ji muji ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ (sediment) eshwɛ sɛɛ beni ajie lɛ No yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Shii abɔ ni nu lɛ ehiɛɛɛ nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes right through the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing center of maize plants to feed on tender leaves. Catching them early with appropriate organic or chemical sprays prevents severe crop damage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni sa loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer crops every year even when I plant the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops or adding compost replenishes lost soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why must I clear all the weeds before planting my seeds instead of letting them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the space and resources they need to sprout strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage, creating wet conditions where fungal diseases thrive and destroy the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ adara ni efite shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too quickly, the intense sun will dry out the soil and kill the germinating seeds before the true rainy season established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if I sprayed too much weedkiller on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi babaoo eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: If you apply too much chemical weedkiller, your crop leaves may turn brown, curl up, or stop growing entirely, because excess chemicals burn the crops alongside the weeds.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi babaoo tsu nii Otso lɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, abɔle amɛhe, loo amɛkpa dalɛ kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni fa fe nine lɛ baashã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer heat or drought stress. Without sufficient water during hot weather, the plant drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛbote dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do tiny black bugs show up inside my stored dried maize after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji No hewɔ lɛ ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: These bugs are weevils, which lay invisible eggs inside the grain before harvest. If maize is stored with moisture or without proper drying and protection, the eggs hatch into active bugs.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ dumɔwui amli dani akpaa. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ loo ahaaa egbi jogbaŋŋ ni abuuu he lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni hiɛ ka.

english: What is NPK fertilizer, and why should I put it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium, which are the three main foods crops need. Nitrogen helps leaves stay green and grow big, Phosphorus builds strong roots, and Potassium helps the plant fight off diseases and produce good fruits.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha Nitrogen, Phosphorus, kɛ Potassium, ni ji niyenii titrii etɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Fosforo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some farmers' crops grow so much bigger and greener than mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi aŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops usually grow bigger and greener when the soil has enough essential nutrients. Farmers who add fertilizers like NPK early on are giving their crops the exact nutrients needed to grow strong right from the start.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni fa bɔ ni sa. Okwaafoi ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK woɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: If your crops from the previous harvest were weak, had yellowing leaves, small stalks, or gave low yields, it is a sign that your soil has lost its natural food and needs NPK fertilizer to rebuild its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni okpa yɛ tsutsu kpamɔ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii, loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Eji okadi akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ miifite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni ehe miihia NPK ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Can I put NPK fertilizer into the soil before I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Yes, putting NPK fertilizer into the ground before or during planting gives your seeds instant access to food as soon as their roots sprout, helping them grow faster and stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu loo yɛ be mli ni oduɔ lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer before planting or wait until the seeds start sprouting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu loo mamɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Applying NPK fertilizer right at planting or just before is usually best because young crops need nutrients immediately to establish strong roots. Waiting too long can cause early growth to stall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔ be mli loo dani aduɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai he miihia tsei bibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ akpa.

english: How long before planting my seeds should I apply fertilizer to the ground?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Applying NPK fertilizer around the time of planting or within a short window of a week or two before planting ensures the nutrients stay in the soil ready for the seeds, rather than washing away in heavy rains.
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be mli loo yɛ be kukuoo mli Otsi kome loo enyɔ dani aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he kɛha dumɔwui. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho kɛya

english: What happens if I miss the best two-week window to put fertilizer in my soil during land preparation?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifo otsii enyɔ samflɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: If you miss the early application window, your young crops may start off weak or yellow. However, you can still apply fertilizer near the roots shortly after they sprout to help them catch up.
ga: Kɛji otsi ohe kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he Otsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi amɛgbɔjɔ loo amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, shi kɛlɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lolo beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛshɛ he.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow healthy shoots even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain gives plants water, but water alone is not food. If the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, seeds cannot build strong stems and leaves regardless of how much rain falls.
ga: Nugbɔ haa tsei nu. Shi nu pɛ jeee niyenii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛ waa ha.

english: Will putting fertilizer directly into the soil burn my seeds when I sow them?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã midumɔwui lɛ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: NPK fertilizer will not burn your seeds as long as it is mixed slightly into the soil or placed a small distance away from the seed itself rather than touching it directly.
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãŋ odumɔwui lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fioo loo akɛwo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛaabɔ tɛ̃ɛ

english: How does putting fertilizer into the ground early affect my final harvest?
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra Te enaa minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Feeding the soil early gives plants a strong head start, resulting in thicker stalks, healthier leaves, and ultimately a bigger, richer harvest at the end of the season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ nii babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: How many months does it usually take for cassava to fully mature before I can harvest it?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ dani akpaa?

english: Most cassava varieties take between 9 to 12 months to mature completely. Harvesting before 9 months yields small tubers, while leaving them past 12 months can cause the roots to become woody and tough.
ga: Cassava tsei babaoo heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Nikpamɔ dani nyɔji 9 baashɛ lɛ baaha bulbs bibii aba. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ nyɔji 12 lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my plantain bunches taking longer than 10 months to mature this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ he nɔ ni fe nyɔji 10 dani ekwɛ afi nɛɛ?

english: Plantains typically mature in 9 to 12 months, but extended dry periods, poor soil nutrients, or lack of water can slow down the plant's growth and delay fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, shi be ni ekɛgbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo nu ni faaa Ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ni eha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do some crops like maize finish growing in 3 months while crops like cassava stay in the field for almost a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ agbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi lɛ?

english: Grain crops like maize have short life cycles designed to grow seeds quickly, while root crops like cassava need many months to store food energy in their underground roots.
ga: Dumɔwui tsei, tamɔ abɛi, yɛ wala be kuku ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ adara oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkɛ niyenii hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my maize is ready for harvest without just counting the months?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa ni okaneee nyɔji lɛ?

english: Maize is mature when the outer silk turns dark brown, the leaves turn yellow or dry, and the kernels become hard with a visible black spot at their base where they attach to the cob.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ siliki lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbiɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii diji ni anaa yɛ shishigbɛ he ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What will happen to my yam tubers if I leave them in the soil past their normal harvest month?
ga: Mɛni baa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nyɔŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature yams in the ground too long makes them vulnerable to rot, beetle damage, and termites, or causes them to sprout again when the next rains arrive, which ruins their market value.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni edara lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ oshara baa akɛ amɛbaafite. Efiteɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii loo eha amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ba. Enɛ baafite jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to harvest all my vegetable crops at once or pick them month by month as they ripen?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpã aduawai lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo makpã amɛ daa nyɔŋ nɔ be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables like peppers and garden eggs ripen gradually, so it is best to pick mature fruits every few days to encourage the plant to keep producing new flowers and fruits.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ aduawai kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii shwereɔ blɛoo, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ daa otsii fioo. gbii fioo komɛi koni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei.

english: If I plant my crop late in November as the dry season begins, will it survive?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei yɛ November naagbee gbɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ani amɛbaahi shi?

english: Planting at the start of the dry season in November is risky because young seedlings need consistent moisture to establish roots; without irrigation, intense dry winds like the Harmattan will wither them.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ November mli lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ tsei bibii lɛ he miihia nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná shishifãi. Kɛji nu shwiemɔ bɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa tamɔ Harmattan lɛ baagbo.

english: How do the major and minor rainy seasons affect when I should clear my land and plant?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔi wuji kɛ bibii lɛ saa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei adumɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The major rainy season provides longer water supply for slow-maturing crops, while the minor season is better suited for fast-growing crops that can finish before the dry weather returns.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ baaha tsei ni miida blɛoo lɛ aná nu be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be ni ji enyɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni daa oya ni baanyɛ agbe naa dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season change the way my crops mature in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ etsake bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds dry out soil and air rapidly, which speeds up the drying process of mature grains like corn and rice, but can stunt the growth of young crops that still need water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ oya. Shi ebaanyɛ etsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni he hiaa nu lolo lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new fruits after a few months even though the plants are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ aduawai heei yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants slow down production when nutrients in the soil are depleted or when weather is extremely hot; adding compost or manure and removing old fruits helps restart growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ haa amɛshweremɔ baa shi kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni ajie aduawai momo lɛ, ebaawo dalɛ he hewalɛ ni ebɔi daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and harsh Harmattan winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside cocoa creates a living shield that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to make the food that grows the underground tuber. When vines climb stakes, the leaves spread out toward the sun instead of crowding together on the damp ground where they can rot or get shaded out.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo amɛfee hulutsoo.

english: Why must I make sure cassava stem cuttings are planted facing upright instead of upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ koni mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ moŋ fe ni aaatsɔ hiɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small growth buds that point upward toward the top of the stem. If planted upside down, the shoots have to bend all the way around underground to reach the light, which wastes energy, weakens the plant, and leads to tiny, weak roots.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa tso lɛ yiteŋ Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi. shikpɔŋ shishi koni ana la ni fiteɔ hewalɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: A single plantain root system only has enough food and water to produce one big, heavy fruit bunch at a time. Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight each other for food, resulting in small, weak plantain bunches from all of them.
ga: Plantain shishifã kome pɛ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii agbo kome ni tsii yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛwuu yɛ niyenii he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ amɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green and grow strong. As the maize plant grows larger, it drains nitrogen from its old lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Amɛji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmãa tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of plants called legumes that can pull nitrogen food directly out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Peas kɛ beans ji nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ legume weku lɛ mli bii, ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive root systems that drink up water and swallow fertilizer far quicker than your crops can. If weeds are present, they end up taking the majority of the food you put down, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛmiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ lɛ, amɛbaaye niyenii ni okɛwoɔ amɛnɔ lɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and twist together into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by insects. As these pests drink the plant's sap, they cause the leaf tissue to grow unevenly and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tso mli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Amɛhaa baa lɛ mli fãji ni ejaaa ni efite lɛ daa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or erratic watering. When temperatures get too hot, the pollen inside the flower dies before it can fertilize the plant to form a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ dani ekɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ abɔ ni ekɛfee tomato.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead during hot afternoons even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water vapor into the air faster than the roots can draw it up from the ground. The plant temporarily droops its leaves to reduce exposed surface area and save moisture, recovering naturally when the afternoon cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu lasu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi. Ebaatsa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni shwane lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: What is a two-stage nursery, and why should I consider using one for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔsemɔhe ni yɔɔ fãi enyɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ baatsu nii?

english: A two-stage nursery means starting your seeds in a primary bed to sprout, and then moving the young sprouts to a main nursery bed. This allows you to select only the healthiest sprouts and give them enough space and nutrients to grow faster before planting them in the field.
ga: Nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ abaaje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. No sɛɛ lɛ, ajie dumɔwui lɛ kɛtee tsei akwɛmɔhe wulu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Ni oha amɛ he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara oya dani okɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli.

english: Is it better to plant my coconut seeds directly in the main field or start them in a nursery bed first?
ga: Ani aduɔ ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo ehi akɛ aaadu yɛ ŋmei dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting coconut seeds in a nursery bed allows you to easily protect them, water them regularly, and monitor their sprouting. It ensures that only strong, early-sprouting seedlings make it to your main farm.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔi ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe mlɛo. Nu daa ni onyiɛ ekwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daa oya lɛ pɛ shɛɔ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How does preparing a fresh nursery bed help my newly sprouted plants?
ga: Te ŋmɔ mli tsei heei ni misaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A properly prepared nursery bed provides loose, nutrient-rich soil with good drainage. This makes it easy for young, delicate roots to spread quickly and absorb the food and water the plant needs to grow.
ga: Nɛsi saatso ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni eda lɛ oya.

english: Why do some of my coconut seeds sprout early while others take many weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Seeds naturally wake up at different times depending on their maturity, moisture level, and position in the soil. It is normal for coconuts to sprout unevenly over several weeks rather than all at once.
ga: Dumɔwui teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ dalɛ nɔ Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ otsii babaoo mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ shikome lɛ

english: Why is it important for me to separate sprouted seeds from unsprouted ones in the seedbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ magbala dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ ateŋ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Sprouted seeds need plenty of sunlight and soil nutrients to grow leaves, while unsprouted seeds just need moisture to germinate. Separating them lets you give each group the exact care it needs without crowding.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná baai. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ he hiaa nu pɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa kuu fɛɛ kuu nine shɛɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ nɔ ni amɛyimɔɔɔ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Why do some of my seedlings grow much faster than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi daa oya kwraa fe ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings that sprout first get a head start on gathering sun and nutrients. If left together, the bigger ones will shade out the smaller ones, causing uneven growth across your farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ mra lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni abua naa. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ekome lɛ Nɔ ni da lɛ baaha bibioo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Should I move my coconut seedlings to a new bed immediately after they sprout or wait until they are bigger?
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ ajie kɛya shikpɔŋ hee nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo esa akɛ emɛ kɛyashi ebaada?

english: Moving seedlings right when they sprout helps them establish early roots in a fresh bed with more space. This early boost helps them grow much faster than if they stay in a crowded germination bed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛyaa he kroko kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi oya yɛ saatso hee ni gbɛ babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. mra be mli stimulation Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya fe shĩa ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen if I leave my sprouted coconuts in the initial seedbed for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving sprouts in a crowded initial bed causes their roots to become tangled and fight for food and light. This stunts their growth and makes it harder to transplant them later without damaging the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishijee saatso ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛye niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ ni ehaa ewaa akɛ aaawo lɛ sɛɛ mli ni efiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I make sure all the seedlings in my nursery grow at a steady and equal pace?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ ada be fɛɛ be ni amɛfee ekome?

english: You can group seedlings by the time they sprout. By moving early sprouters to their own section, you stop them from shading out late sprouters, giving every plant a fair chance to catch up.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ akui amli yɛ be ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ naa. Tsei bibii ni aaawo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ fã lɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni akakwɛ̃ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli.

english: How does moving a sprouted coconut to a larger nursery bed speed up its growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋmei ŋmei agbo ko mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eda oya?

english: A larger nursery bed gives the plant more root space and removes competition from neighboring seeds. With extra room and individual attention, the young coconut can direct all its energy into fast leaf and root growth.
ga: Nursery saatso ni da lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná shishifãi babaoo. kɛ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ he ko krɛdɛɛ kɛ aŋkroaŋkroi ajwɛŋmɔ nɔ lɛ, Kokooi baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛha baa kɛ shishifãi ni yaa oya.

english: If I invest my time and money into farming cashew or mango in Ghana, how am I sure it will support my family?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ be kɛ shika wo cashew loo mango ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ Ghana. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ebaaye ebua miweku lɛ?

english: Cashew and mango are high-value tree crops that can yield consistent financial returns for over 30 years once established. Because local and international demand for these fruits and nuts is high, combining them with short-term food crops gives you both immediate food and long-term financial security.
ga: Cashew nuts kɛ mango ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni abuɔ waa ni enyɛ ekɛ shika ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be eha nɔ ni fe afii 30 nɛ beni ato shishi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni taoɔ aduawai kɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fa babaoo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ majimaji ateŋ fɛɛ. Kɛ akɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ fata he Ebaaha oná niyenii kɛ shika fɛɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Where can smallholder farmers like me get technical help or assistance when starting a new crop farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana ŋaa gbɛ nɔ yelikɛbuamɔ loo yelikɛbuamɔ kɛji amɛje ŋmɔshi nibii hee shishi?

english: You can get free assistance from Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) extension officers in your district. They offer guidance on modern planting methods, soil health, pest management, and connecting with local farmer organizations for subsidized seeds and tools.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná yelikɛbuamɔ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) Extension Officer ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Amɛhaa ŋaawoo yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii, shikpɔŋ hewalɛnamɔ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ he. kɛ akutsoŋ okwaafoi akui ni akɛ amɛ aaabɔ kɛha dumɔwui kɛ nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting cashew trees before I can start harvesting nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ odu cashew tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ?

english: Standard cashew trees planted from seeds usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 5 years. However, if you plant grafted seedlings from a certified nursery, they can start producing nuts in as early as 2 to 3 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ odu dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ, Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii awomɔ shishi kɛjɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli tɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my mango trees falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers often drop due to water stress, poor soil nutrients, or attacks from pests and diseases like anthracnose fungus. Proper watering during early flowering and timely application of recommended organic or chemical sprays can protect the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tamɔ anthracnose ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Nu ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli mra kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baanyɛ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young cashew trees, or will it harm the trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mi cashew tsei lɛ ateŋ? Aloo ebaaye tso lɛ awui?

english: Intercropping maize, legumes, or cassava between young cashew trees for the first 2 to 3 years is safe and recommended. It suppresses weeds, protects the soil, and gives you food and income while waiting for your trees to mature.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ adu ŋmãa. legumes loo cassava yɛ cashew tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to trim or prune the branches of my tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to reach the inner leaves and flowers. Sunlight boosts fruit development, reduces moisture that causes fungal diseases, and makes harvesting easier.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Hulu la haa aduawai lɛ daalɛ yaa hiɛ. Ha hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: How do I know if my farmland is good enough for growing cashew or mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha cashew loo mango tsei adumɔ?

english: Cashews and mangoes need deep, well-draining soil where water does not sit for days after heavy rain. If water pools on top of your soil for long periods, the roots will rot, so sandy loam or well-drained soils are preferred.
ga: Cashew kɛ mango biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu lɛ ehiŋ shi gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kɛ́ nu hi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, no hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋã loo sũ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsu nii.

english: How can I tell when my cashew nuts are completely mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cashews lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cashew nuts are fully ripe when the soft apple fruit above the nut turns bright red or yellow and drops naturally to the ground. You should collect the fallen fruits from the ground rather than picking green ones off the branches.
ga: Cashews lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ apple bibioo ni yɔɔ nut lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Esa akɛ okpa aduawai ni egbee shi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛjɛ tsei aniji amli.

english: What can I do to keep my harvested crops from spoiling before I reach the market?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mikpamɔ lɛ akafite dani eshɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvest during the cool early morning hours, dry nuts and grains properly to reduce moisture before bagging, and keep your harvest in a dry, shaded, and well-ventilated storage area elevated off the ground.
ga: Kpamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli leebi maŋkpa. Agbiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmaa jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmɔtɔ aba shi dani akɛwoɔ kotoku mli. ni okɛ nibii ni adu lɛ ato he ko ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, yɛ he ko ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why did my farm give a huge harvest last season but very little crop this season on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wo ŋmaa babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli shi be nɛɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every season, so without adding fertilizer or compost, the soil becomes exhausted. Additionally, weather changes and natural cycles in fruit trees (alternate bearing) can cause heavy yields one year and low yields the next.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsakemɔi ni baa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli kɛ bɔ ni tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ (Alternating carrying) baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo babaoo aba afi kome mli, ni yibiiwoo aba shi yɛ afi kroko mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when the hot dry wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants drop leaves during the dry Harmattan season to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Planting shade trees around your farm and putting dry grass around the base of the stems helps keep moisture in the soil.
