ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the heavy wind blows during fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and get very top-heavy when carrying a heavy bunch of fruit. Removing extra shoot suckers so the mother plant stays strong and using bamboo poles to prop up the fruiting stem prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo aduawai ni tsii. Ajieɔ suckers krokomɛi koni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ ŋmei tsei atsu nii ni okɛfi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the bottom up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellowing that starts from the bottom leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes in that field will restore the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need air, moisture, and warmth near the soil surface to break open and grow. If planted too deep, the seed runs out of stored energy before the tiny shoot can reach the top and see the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ dɔlɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ baa shi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ daa. Obaashɛ ŋwɛi ni ona hulu la lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in soaked soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the tuber underground. Raising the vines on stakes gets the leaves into the sun and off the ground where pests and damp soil could rot them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ baanyɛ aha amɛgboi lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts with my crop makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ du tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil through tiny lumps on their roots. When the plant dies, that food stays in the ground for other crops to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ kɛ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli koni tsei krokomɛi kɛtsu nii.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant pepper on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting pepper in the same spot continuously allows pests and diseases that attack pepper to multiply in the soil. Switching the plot to a crop like maize breaks the life cycle of those pests.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. He ni atsakeɔ koni adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just dry up and fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil, which stresses the plant. Watering your plants regularly at the roots during hot weather helps the flowers stay healthy and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating holes deep inside the middle of my young crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mibaai bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm lay eggs on leaves, and the hatched caterpillars hide inside the leaf funnel to eat the soft young growth. Applying recommended organic sprays like neem water directly into the funnel kills them before they ruin the growing point.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai amli ŋmeii amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa, tamɔ neem nu lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my maize right after the very first rain or should I wait a bit?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ fioo?

english: It is usually better to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell, which can dry up and kill young germinating seeds before their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu baakpe lɛ.

english: Why do I have to replant my cassava every year instead of letting the old plants keep growing in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsei momoi akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach their best size, starch content, and taste within 9 to 12 months. If you leave the plant in the ground too long, the tubers become woody, tough, and lose their nutritional value, which is why fresh planting produces a better harvest every cycle.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ, starch ni yɔɔ mli, kɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli. Kɛji oshi tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Eshishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei, amɛhe wa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui heei woɔ yibii kpakpai be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce a lot of pods in one year, but very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi mli lɛ? Shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nɔ ko fioo pɛ ji nɔ ni afee?

english: Cocoa trees spend a massive amount of energy and nutrients to produce a heavy harvest. After a big crop, the tree is exhausted and needs time and good plant food to rebuild its strength before it can produce a high yield again.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo yibii babaoo. Beni ekwɛ tso agbo ko sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ hu egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia be kɛ tso niyenii kpakpa koni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani ekɛ yibii babaoo aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over and die after giving me just one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbo beni ekɛ ŋmei kome pɛ ha mi lɛ?

english: Each individual plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit only once. After fruiting, that main stem naturally dies, but it leaves behind young shoots called suckers around its base to continue growing the next crop.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛ́ ewo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Mohu ɔ, e siɔ tso bibihi nɛ a tsɛɛ ke suckers ɔ ngɛ e se. shishi koni ekɛkwɛ tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade from plantain trees, but big cocoa trees do fine in open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantains mli lɛ? Shi kookoo tsei wuji lɛ hia hulutsoo yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ faŋŋ.

english: Young crop seedlings have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out easily in direct sunlight. Older trees have deep roots to pull water from deep underground and tough leaves that can turn direct sunlight into food without drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ, kɛ baai ni wa ni baanyɛ atsake hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ efee niyenii ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients out of the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before any tomatoes actually start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani tomatoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protecting plants during extreme hot weather helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are commonly caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by insects. Treating the crop with approved pest controls early prevents this stunt in growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Mra be mli ni akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii Etsiŋ amɛdalɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the soil before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when water settles around them in heavy or waterlogged soil, or when tiny worms in the soil bite the tubers and let disease in. Building high soil mounds helps water drain away easily and protects the yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babɔle amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔ yitso ni eha hela lɛ bote mli.Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm right after I apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plants in the soil equally, including weeds. Because weeds naturally grow faster than crops, you should clear all weeds out of your farm before applying fertilizer so that your crops get all the food instead of the weeds.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni jwɛi hu fata he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jwɛi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and turn yellow when the rain stops for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain stops, plants cannot absorb essential nutrients because soil water acts as the delivery system. Without water, crops lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink, causing them to wilt and turn yellow as a stress response.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ejaakɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kɛ nibii lɛ yaa. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hewɔ.

english: Is there any way I can keep my crops alive in the farm when the rains fail?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ?

english: You can practice mulching, which means covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop stalks. This acts like a blanket that shades the soil, traps moisture in the ground, and keeps roots cool during hot, dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching akase nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ahe tsei. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do some crops survive dry weather much better than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root systems and water needs. For example, cassava and sorghum have deep roots that can reach water deep underground, while crops like maize have shallow roots that suffer quickly when topsoil dries out.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ shishifãi kɛ nu he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yeɔ amanehulu oya kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩ.

english: It is often safer to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain can be a false start followed by a long hot dry spell, which will cause your seeds to germinate and then dry up and die in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ waa. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up like tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun. By rolling up, the plant slows down water loss through evaporation during intense afternoon heat.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa baa he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Kɛtsɔ Tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers before producing food when the weather gets too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ niyenii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When a crop does not get enough water, it switches into survival mode. Producing fruit or grain requires a lot of water and energy, so the plant drops its flowers to save its own life until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ebaaya wala shihilɛ mli. Yibii loo ŋmaa ni aaawo lɛ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are just stressed by heat or actually dying from lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe dɔlɛ loo amɛmiigboi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ?

english: If crops droop during the hot afternoon but bounce back and stand tall by early morning, they are managing heat stress. If the leaves remain dry, limp, or crispy even in the cool morning, the plant is severely dehydrated and dying.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gbee shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Shi efo mli ekoŋŋ leebi maŋkpa. Etsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ miikpe. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ egbi, efee bɔdɔɔ, loo efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli po lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli waa ni egbo.

english: What happens to the fertilizer I put on my farm if the rain does not fall?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Without rain, the fertilizer sits unused on top of dry soil, and strong heat can sometimes cause dry fertilizer to scorch nearby tender crop roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baata shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni akɛtsuuu nii. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ ashã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why does adding animal manure or compost help my farm during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Compost and decayed manure work like a sponge in the soil. They improve the soil's structure so it can soak up water like a reservoir during rain and hold onto that moisture long after the rains stop.
ga: Kompost kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛhaa bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ejie nu tamɔ nutoohe yɛ nugbɔ be mli, ni ehiɛ nakai nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How does planting seeds too deep in the soil affect them when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli baa?

english: When soil is dry, it hardens into a tough crust on top. Seeds planted too deep exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the dry soil and may die before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ, ewaa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baajie amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deeper into the soil away from young roots, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea around the plant helps it recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and leaving brown powder inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves during the day and eat the growing plant from the inside out, so you need to spray recommended treatments directly into the center funnel early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni miida kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and keeps the soil moist, acting like a protective cover until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away, which drowns the roots and encourages fungal rot. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo fungal rot he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I get tiny corn ears if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ ŋmãa toi bibii kɛji midu ŋmãa yibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper space ensures every plant gets enough food to grow tall stalks and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers just fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil moist through mulching and watering regularly during hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa tamɔ calcium bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũu kɛtsɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha enyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up so they catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tubers below. It also prevents the leaves from resting on damp soil where fungal diseases can easily infect and spoil the plant.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai hu anaa koni amɛkamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baanyɛ atswa tsei lɛ mlɛo ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why did my crops dry up and turn brown after I put chemical fertilizer right against the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts that will pull water directly out of the plant's roots if placed in direct contact with them, causing 'fertilizer burn.' Fertilizer should always be buried a few inches away from the stem in a ring or line.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji ekɛ amɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ, ni ekɛ ‘ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shãa’ baa. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ 2-3 inches yɛ ring loo line mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small wrinkles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually a viral infection spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. Spraying organic or insecticidal soaps early to control these pests keeps them from spreading the virus across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Organic soap loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi mra koni akɛye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why does a weed with small pink flowers make my sorghum dry up even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Koni mi-sorghum lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: This weed is Striga, also known as witchweed, which attaches its roots directly to the roots of sorghum or maize underground to steal their water and food. Rotating your farm with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps starve and eliminate Striga seeds in the soil over time.
ga: Nɛkɛ jwɛi nɛɛ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed, ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hɔmɔ aye Striga dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight and harsh dry winds. Without temporary shade crops like plantains, the hot sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya.

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. Adding organic mulch around the root area helps keep the soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Organic mulch ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires high amounts of nitrogen to maintain healthy green leaves and produce full ears.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to direct its energy into leafy stem growth above ground rather than storing starches in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ sisi a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, leaving behind natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ akɛ tso niyenii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and falling off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination and stops the fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ wo mli. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daalɛ kpaɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers dry up and drop without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require high humidity and tiny pollinating insects like midges to set fruit. High heat, lack of shade, or dry air prevents these flowers from being pollinated.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ hulutsoo ni fa kɛ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges koni amɛwo yibii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tsiɔ fɔfɔi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers from my plantain mat instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ plantain ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates heavy competition for water and nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches. Keeping only two or three suckers ensures larger and healthier bunches.
ga: Tsoi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baaha akaŋshii ni naa wa aba kɛha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ to he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward direct sunlight so they can make food for underground tuber growth, while also keeping leaves off wet soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ akpee tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my rice heads end up with empty husks when the field dries out during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yitsei lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants require continuous water while flowering to fill the grain kernels. If the soil dries out during this stage, the plant cannot move nutrients to the heads, leaving husks empty.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa tsei be fɛɛ be be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ yɛ nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli nibii kɛya bulb lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli efee efolo.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava usually mean your crop has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Removing infected plants early stops the disease from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, cool, and overly shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning extra branches lets sunlight dry out the pods and keeps the fungus away.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ Black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why does an entire section of cocoa trees have to be cut down when Swollen Shoot disease appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ efuu lɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus has no chemical cure once inside a tree. Cutting down infected trees along with surrounding target trees creates a buffer zone that stops mealybugs from spreading the deadly virus to healthy farms.
ga: Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ bɛ tsofa ko ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ kɛji ebote tso lɛ mli pɛ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ kɛfataa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe lɛ Ehaa buffer zone ni tsiɔ mealybugs lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn purple instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ green ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is struggling to get enough phosphorus from the soil, often because the soil is too cold, too dry, or lacking nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ená fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ, egbi tsɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, whereas rotating crops keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did my crop leaves wither and burn after I applied chemical fertilizer near the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ efata he yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that pull water out of plant roots if placed directly against the stem. Fertilizer should always be buried a few inches away from the plant stem in moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: What are these caterpillars eating the centers of my young maize leaves, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, aggressive pests that hide deep inside the funnel of young maize plants. Spraying safe treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed helps destroy them before they kill the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋshɔi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite amɛ dani amɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, tomato pollen dries out and becomes sterile. The plant naturally drops its flowers to conserve energy until cooler weather arrives.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why can't I just save and plant the seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Grains saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation, resulting in much smaller yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to grow when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need direct sunlight and plenty of water to grow fast. Large trees block sunlight and their big roots steal water and nutrients from the soil, slowing down the plantain's growth.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu babaoo koni amɛ dara oya. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to visit my farm regularly throughout the year instead of just waiting for harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Regular farm visits allow you to spot early signs of weeds, pests, and diseases before they spread. Consistent attention keeps your crop healthy and ensures the trees can produce a strong yield when harvest season arrives.
ga: Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ daa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona jwɛi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ helai ahe okadii mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa kɛ́ kpamɔ be lɛ shɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm require so much work even when the trees are not producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔ babaoo he hiaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ? Ni tso lɛ wooo ŋmeii?

english: Even outside the main harvest season, cocoa trees are preparing for the next crop. Tasks like weeding, pruning, and clearing dead pods prevent disease buildup and allow the trees to store energy for flowering.
ga: Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ hu miisaa amɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ. pruning Ni ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ anaabuamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabua amɛhe naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ fɔfɔi ahe

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot survive full sun exposure. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their foliage and retain moisture in the soil until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantain loo hulutsoo tsei, koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: What makes the small pods on my cocoa trees turn black and wither away?
ga: Mɛni haa pods lɛ feɔ bibii? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo.

english: This is often caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection spread by moisture and rain. Clearing heavy weeds and pruning low branches improves air flow, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ afolɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow other crops alongside my cocoa trees to earn extra income during the year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ kookoo tso lɛ masɛi koni maná shika kroko yɛ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can grow temporary shade crops like plantains or food crops during the early years of your farm. However, avoid heavy root crops too close to mature trees so they do not fight for the same water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo niyenii tsei yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛ tsei wuji ahe tsɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni amɛkatswa akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches, allowing sunlight and breeze to pass through the tree canopy. This prevents fungal growth and directs the tree’s food energy into growing pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ashishi. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from stress. Maintaining ground cover and shade trees helps protect the soil moisture so flowers stay on the branches longer.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛfee hulutsoo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil in my farm lacks the nutrients my cocoa trees need?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: If cocoa leaves start turning pale yellow, grow slowly, or produce very small pods, it usually means the soil lacks essential plant food like nitrogen or potassium, signaling a need for fertilizer or organic compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when their color fully changes from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange-yellow. Plucking them too early leaves underdeveloped beans, while leaving them too long causes beans to sprout inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ red kɛtee yellow-orange Kɛ́ ajie mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni edarako lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree will give a good yield before the harvest season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: A cocoa tree likely to yield well will show lush dark green leaves, a clean trunk free of fungus, and a dense clusters of healthy, undisturbed flowers along the bark after the light rains.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ jieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa kpo. Tso lɛ mli tse ni ŋmeii bɛ mli. kɛ fɔfɔii akui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitato tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the soil too fast and keeps the roots cool. It also prevents weeds from growing and taking food away from your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie niyenii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is not getting enough food—especially nitrogen—from the soil, or when heavy rain washes nutrients away. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green again.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Titri lɛ, nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing many flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water. Giving your plants consistent water during dry periods helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my orange trees drop their small green fruits before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaafee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit when they do not receive enough water during hot spells or when insects like fruit flies damage the peel. Regular watering and keeping pests away will help the fruit mature on the tree.
ga: Orange tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai bibii kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii fite ŋmei lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai akwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in the soil and starves the roots of air. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some of my seed yams fail to sprout after I plant them in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams fail to sprout if they were bruised during harvest, stored in a place that was too hot, or attacked by tiny worms called nematodes before planting. Choosing healthy, undamaged seed yams ensures good sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Okɛto he ko ni edɔ waa. loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa lɛ dani aduɔ. Kɛ́ ohala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee lɛ, ebaaha aná ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are natural soil healers. They trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, which feeds the maize plants nearby and makes the soil richer for future crops.
ga: Cowpea ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tsamɔ tsofa. Amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: What is causing small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my corn plants and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks maize. They feed inside the young leaves, but checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or soapy water into the plant tops can control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Shi kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo nu ni akɛ samla woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and turning yellow and green mixed together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni efutu lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems provided by extension agents stops the sickness from spreading across your field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ helai ni onajiaŋdamɔlɔ lɛ kɛha lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves wilt, curl, or turn brown and dry. When they get too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow, feel soft or mushy, and the roots can rot due to lack of air in the soaked soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi, amɛbaakpãtã, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaagbi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ani enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ? Ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into narrow tubes when the sun is very hot around noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during the hottest part of the day as a natural protection mechanism to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the heat, which prevents the plant from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get too hot, when water supply is irregular, or when there is poor pollination from wind and insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa shwane loo gbɛkɛ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of big green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put all their energy into leafy growth rather than flower and pod formation. Cowpeas naturally produce their own nitrogen, so high-nitrogen fertilizers are usually unnecessary.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ, Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni akwɔ koni ewo ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for sunlight to make food for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stays dry, which also prevents fungal leaves diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná niyenii kɛha amɛ tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha amɛhe agbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ fungal leaf helai hu anaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their lower leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water, allowing the plant to save energy and protect its roots until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shiiɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ, ni ebuɔ eshishifãi ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Black cocoa pods are usually caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which spreads rapidly during heavy rains or under dense, damp canopy shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo diji baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo yɛ ŋwɛitsu ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ shishi.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and tear easily during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbalaa oya yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds carry very low moisture and pull water out of plantain leaves faster than the roots can pull it from the dry soil, making the leaves brittle and torn.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi waa baa ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etseɔ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts in my farm field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnut plants trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave nitrogen in the soil, which feeds the maize crop that comes next.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite Amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my pineapple crop is stressed or needs more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pineapple tso lɛ miihao loo nu babaoo he miihia lɛ?

english: Pineapple leaves act as visual signals for the plant's health; when the leaves start turning reddish-purple or curling inwards, the crop is showing that it lacks water or is suffering from heat stress.
ga: Pineapple baai tsuɔ nii akɛ okadi ni anaa kɛha tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ. Beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ purple-red loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli loo ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ miikpe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my pineapple plants turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pineapple tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the roots are struggling with poorly drained soil (waterlogging) or are lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, causing the plant to slow down its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiwuu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ (ni nu eyi mli obɔ) loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli, ni no haa tso lɛ daa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How long does it usually take for a pineapple plant to produce fruit in Ghana?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anana tso woɔ yibii yɛ Ghana?

english: A pineapple plant generally takes between 12 to 18 months from planting to harvest, depending on the variety, soil fertility, and weather conditions during its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pineapple tsei heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 kɛjɛ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ nɔ

english: What is the best season of the year to start planting pineapples on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting at the beginning of the major rainy season (around April to May) gives young shoots enough moisture to establish strong root systems before the drier months arrive.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ he miihia waa. Latsaa be lɛ shishijee (aaafee April kɛyashi May) haa tsei bibii lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa dani nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds early affect the growth of my pineapple crop?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Te enaa mi-anana tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pineapples grow slowly in their early stages and cannot compete well with weeds, so clearing early ensures all sunlight, fertilizer, and water go directly to building strong pineapple plants.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, pineapple daa blɛoo ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ yeee akaŋ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, eka shi faŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee. Enɛ baaha hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛma ŋmei tso ni wa.

english: Should I plant pineapple crowns, slips, or suckers to get the fastest harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu pineapple yitsei, slips, loo ŋmeii koni ewo yibii oya?

english: Suckers and slips grow much faster than crowns (the tops of the fruit) and will produce harvestable fruit several months earlier because they are already more mature when planted.
ga: Tsoi kɛ suckers lɛ daa oya kwraa fe crown (yitso lɛ yiteŋ) ni ebaawo yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa nyɔji babaoo mra ejaakɛ eda fe tsutsu lɛ kɛji adu lɛ pɛ.

english: Is it true that pineapples need less water compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ, ŋmeii biɔ nu fioo?

english: Yes, pineapples are drought-tolerant because their thick, trough-shaped leaves trap and store water, though they still require occasional rainfall or irrigation to produce large, sweet fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, pineapple baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ naa ejaakɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ feɔ ŋshɔ ni mɔɔ nu ni ehiɛɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni ashwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ he miihia amɛ lolo koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ moŋ.

english: Can I force all my pineapple plants to flower and yield fruit at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ manyɛ mi-anane tsei lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, extension officers can guide you on using flower-inducing treatments (such as ethephon or calcium carbide), which trigger uniform flowering across your farm so you can harvest all at once.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo bo ŋaa yɛ tsofai ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ (tamɔ etefon loo calcium carbide) ni baawo fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ he hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why do pineapples from countries like Costa Rica often look bigger than the ones on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ maji tamɔ Costa Rica lɛ amli lɛ dara fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farmers in Costa Rica use precise plant spacing, controlled flowering schedules, and strict soil nutrient management; adopting these standardized field practices helps Ghanaian farmers achieve similar size and quality.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Costa Rica kɛ tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ tsuɔ nii. Kudɔ fɔfɔii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa Nɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ nɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ eye ebua Ghana okwaafoi ni amɛná shweremɔ kɛ kpakpafeemɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: What causes the base of my young pineapple shoots to rot and smell bad in the field?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pineapple tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ gboɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: This is heart rot or root rot caused by fungal infection, which happens when planting material is placed too deep in overly wet, poorly drained soil.
ga: Enɛ ji tsui mli fitemɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko kɛbaa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps keep the leaves green and boosts your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can pull natural plant food directly from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant roots rot after harvest, they leave behind rich nitrogen that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni baanyɛ ajie adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and strong winds. Keeping some shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain next to them acts like a sunshade, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa stems grow tough.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ darako ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Ha tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ahi amɛmasɛi. Amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ feɔ enii tamɔ hulutsoo be. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ fãa trukaa kɛ́ amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they suddenly absorb a lot of water after a dry period, making the inside grow faster than the skin can stretch. Watering your tomatoes evenly and regularly, rather than all at once, keeps the fruit skin smooth and intact.
ga: Tomato baatse trukaa. Amɛheɔ nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tomato ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nu ni oooha tomato daa ni ekɛ nu awo mli pɛpɛɛpɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ nu shikome lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: What happens to my yam crop if I do not put tall stakes for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ emaaa shi koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need to reach up high into full sunlight to make the energy needed to grow big tubers underground. If the vines lie on the shaded ground, the leaves receive less sun, resulting in much smaller yams at harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ adara kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ akɛ wain tso lɛ fɔ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaná hulu la fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ, amɛfeɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when the soil becomes too dry or when the daytime sun gets extremely hot. Placing dry grass mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the soil so the flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ shwane mli tsɔ. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why are the cassava roots under my soil rotting even though the leaves look healthy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long in heavy or flat soils. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off easily, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants full of small holes and green waste?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the leaf funnel during the day to chew on young leaves. Checking your field early and applying recommended neem mixtures or insecticides directly into the funnel kills the pest before it ruins the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem ni akɛfutu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo kooloi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe kooloi lɛ dani tso lɛ baafite.

english: Why are my corn stalks stunted and yellow even though a purple-flowered weed is growing happily around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ miishɛɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he moŋ.

english: That purple-flowered weed is likely Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches its roots to your corn underground and steals its food and water. Rotating your field with crops like soybean or cotton starves the Striga seeds in the soil so your corn can grow tall again.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔii yɛ mli lɛ ji Striga, ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa o-ŋmã lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ejuɔ eniyenii kɛ enu lɛ. Oŋmɔji ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ soybeans loo cotton baatsake lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye Striga dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ o-corn lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my last hybrid maize harvest give me a smaller yield than the certified seed I bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only for their first generation. When you save and replant those seeds, the offspring lose their special power and uniformity, leading to smaller cobs and uneven growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Seshibii lɛ baafite amɛ hewalɛi krɛdɛɛi kɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their tender foliage and dries out the topsoil. Keeping large shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains protects the young trees until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo be kukuoo mli tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the right nutrients to make the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Always pick stems from healthy, fully grown cassava plants that are about 8 to 12 months old. Select thick stems from the middle section of the plant that have strong, undamaged buds along their sides.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eda ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12. Halamɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ esɛɛgbɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the daytime temperature gets too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when there are no small insects around to help spread pollen between the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ he ni baaye abua ni amɛgbɛ pollen amɛshwã fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put tall wood stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food through their leaves, and lifting the vines off the ground allows every leaf to catch sunlight easily. Staking also keeps the foliage away from wet soil, preventing diseases and helping the roots grow bigger tubers.
ga: Atomɔ tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaa lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo akɛ ebaaná hulu la. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bɔɔlu bibii ni wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny bugs early keeps new leaves coming out flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ aje kpo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dust in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni mishi sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That damage comes from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the central shoot of the maize plant to feed. Checking plants early and applying safe insecticides or neem solutions helps kill the caterpillars before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ amli. Tso lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni agbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ tso lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for growing maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays behind to act as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing together, they fight with the main tree for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Removing extra shoots leaves just one or two strong stems, which results in larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Ekɛ tso wulu lɛ baawu koni ená nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ehiɔ shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable beds early in the morning rather than late in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun warms up the ground. Watering late in the day leaves the leaves wet overnight, which creates the damp conditions that cause plant diseases and rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsei ahe helai kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too wet and suffocating the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps the leaves turn deep green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and giving the plants light shade during extreme heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ahaa tso lɛ hulutsoo bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and need shade from larger trees or plantain plants to protect their young leaves from scorching hot sun and to keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbiɔ ni tsei wuji loo plantains aná hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room and food to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden sticks to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight and fresh air, which makes the plant produce bigger tubers while keeping leaves off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni no ji helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ jɛɛhe.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and small if I do not clear the weeds around them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji mijieee jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? amɛ kɛjɛ shishijee tɔ̃ɔ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the nourishment they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, mikpamɔ lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up pests. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are there small holes chewed into the center leaves of my young maize plants?
