ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani oooye baa ko ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Small holes inside the central leaves of young maize are usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar eating the plant. Checking your field early allows you to apply safe remedies before they destroy the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tso lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. He ni oyɔɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii dani okpãtã he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does it help my cocoa farm produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ ni ekɛ pods babaoo aba?

english: Hand pollination is a practice where farmers manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small tools like tweezers. It helps trees produce many more pods than relying only on natural insects like midges.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ji nifeemɔ ko ni okwaafoi kɛ amɛdɛŋ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ nibii bibii tamɔ tweezers nɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii pɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not properly pollinated by insects or human hands, or if the tree lacks water and nutrients to support new pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo adesai ekɛ amɛhe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni baaye abua ŋmeii heei lɛ.

english: How do small insects in my farm help cocoa flowers turn into fruits?
ga: Bɔ ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ cacao fɔfɔi amli amɛfeɔ aduawai

english: Insects like tiny midges carry pollen from flower to flower as they search for food. This natural fertilization allows the flower to grow into a healthy pod.
ga: Kplukai, tamɔ midges, hiɛɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ beni amɛtaoɔ niyenii lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What is the difference between the main crop season and the light crop season for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ be titri ni kookoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ kɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ fioo lɛ teŋ?

english: The main crop season occurs during the major rainy period when cocoa pods are larger and yields are high, while the light crop season happens during drier periods, producing smaller pods and lower overall yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ titri lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be ni shwereɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa pods bibii kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I do artificial pollination on my cocoa trees during the light crop season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee kookoo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: No, hand pollination is generally not recommended during the light crop season because the trees experience drier weather and do not have enough water and strength to mature additional pods.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, atsɔɔɔ akɛ akɛ niji afee pollination yɛ be mli ni kane fioo pɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi. Ni nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara babaoo bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need different care during the dry season compared to the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: In the dry season, trees face heat stress and low moisture, so they need water conservation practices like mulching rather than heavy production practices like artificial pollination.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi mli baa lɛ kpeɔ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni amɛbu nu he, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii babaoo ni afeɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii.

english: What daily maintenance activities must I focus on to ensure my cocoa farm yields well?
ga: Mɛɛ daa gbi nitsumɔi ni esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ koni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii?

english: Daily activities include clearing weeds, cutting off diseased pods, removing unwanted tree shoots (pruning), and checking for insect pests before they spread.
ga: Nɔ ni fata daa gbi nifeemɔi ahe ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ. ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ afolɔmɔ Ajie ŋmeii ni ataooo (afolɔ) kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akwɛmɔ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã

english: Why is regular pruning necessary for my cocoa trees to grow healthy pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ daa koni eshishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree, which reduces fungal diseases like black pod and directs energy into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ baa shi ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dalɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees giving a high yield while my farm keeps producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Higher yields depend on applying proper farming practices consistently, such as timely fertilization, regular weed control, proper pruning, and using recommended pollination techniques.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be naa lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ daa Jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ pollination ŋaai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii.

english: Where can I get expert advice on the best methods to manage my cocoa farm in Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔ nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ he?

english: You can talk to local COCOBOD extension officers who are trained to teach cocoa farmers proper land management, pest control, and yield-boosting techniques.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ COCOBOD extension officers ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ cocoa okwaafoi lɛ bɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ awie. tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋaai ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains or shade trees act like an umbrella over young cocoa, protecting them from direct sun and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ. Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn yellow from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the nutrient boost it needs to make deep green leaves and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehiɛ baai lɛ amli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the land without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows fungal rot to develop underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too hot, lacks water, or doesn't get enough nutrients. Keeping the soil covered with grass mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ fe nine, nu faaa yɛ emli, loo ahaaa tso lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize leaves so quickly during the dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-abele baai lɛ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day where they stay safe from the heat and feed continuously, multiplying fast before you notice them.
ga: Fall caterpillars lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ latsaa mli ni amɛyeɔ nii daa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya dani oyɔseɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big leaves but giving me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of storing energy in the roots underneath.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why is it recommended to plant my maize immediately after the first major rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first big rain releases trapped nitrogen in the warm soil, creating a sudden natural fertilizer boost that helps young maize seedlings grow faster than weeds.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpo. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa bibii ni amɛdaraa oya fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my pepper plants look weak and small even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your pepper plants, leaving the crop starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: What causes black spots to cover my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a microscopic organism that thrives in wet conditions and spreads when raindrops splash soil or infected water onto the cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ kɛ Black pod hela lɛ baa. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie shikpɔŋ loo nu ni hela emɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra stems growing around my main plantain shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni bɔle mi-plantain titri lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Extra shoots compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Removing them leaves only one or two strong suckers, which produces larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha plantain tsei lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe afee tsiimɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage and stems are delicate. Planting plantains or shade trees beside them acts as a canopy, giving cocoa seedlings the soft shade and moist soil they need to survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ waaa. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi. Ebaatsu nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo blɛoo. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wala yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps feed the maize so the leaves stay green and produce healthy, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛye kooloi lɛ niyenii. Baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot periods helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do some types of cassava taste bitter while other types taste sweet straight after boiling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔi komɛi ŋɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ŋɔɔ kɛji ahoo amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Bitter cassava varieties contain natural chemical compounds that protect the plant against insects and pests. These bitter types must be soaked, fermented, or boiled thoroughly to break down those natural defense compounds before eating.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ nɛkɛ tsofai ni mli edɔ nɛɛ awo nu mli, afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ahoo lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni efite amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ dani aye.

english: Will planting cowpea between my rows of young cassava harm my harvest or help it?
ga: Ani cowpea ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-cassava bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ?

english: Planting cowpea between cassava helps your crop because cowpea spreads across the ground to suppress weeds, keeps moisture in the soil, and feeds natural nitrogen back into the earth to benefit the cassava.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei teŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ebua ŋmei.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into thin tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up as a defense mechanism to conserve water when the afternoon sun gets too strong. Rolling the leaves reduces the surface exposed to the sun so the plant doesn't dry out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu he kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads rapidly in humid, overgrown areas. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunshine into the farm to stop the fungal spread.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ kookoo diji baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni jɛmɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛkpa ŋmei lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my stored seed yams sit for months without sprouting leaves or roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo ni baai loo shishifãi ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural sleep period called dormancy right after harvest. The tuber will not sprout until this sleep period naturally ends, which lines up with the return of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Tubers lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛyashi nɛkɛ wɔɔhe be nɛɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ekɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why does my land produce smaller corn yields when I plant maize on the exact same piece of ground three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains specific plant foods and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your plot with legumes like groundnuts refills soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmã yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ ekomɛi ajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes twisting and curling up tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding under the leaves. Spraying organic solutions like neem oil controls these insects so fresh, healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ koni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even when I give them plenty of water from my well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ mi-po lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Well water in many parts of Ghana has a high pH level, meaning it is too alkaline. High pH water prevents crops from absorbing food from the soil, causing leaves to turn yellow even when fully watered.
ga: Nubu mli nu ni yɔɔ Ghana hei babaoo lɛ yɛ pH ni nɔ kwɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ alkaline tsɔ. Nu ni pH yɔɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu babaoo po.

english: What does water pH mean, and why should I care about it for my pepper farm?
ga: Mɛni ji pH ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu nu ni yɔɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ pH he?

english: Water pH measures how acidic or alkaline your water is. Vegetables like peppers need balanced water to absorb nutrients properly; water that is too high in pH blocks roots from taking in food.
ga: Nu pH lɛ susuɔ bɔ ni onu lɛ ji acidic loo alkaline ha lɛ he. Nu ni sa he miihia aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni pH lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: How can I tell if the borehole water on my land is too harsh for my vegetable nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni yɔɔ nubu ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha mi greenhouse lɛ?

english: If young seedlings develop curled leaves, stunted stems, or pale leaves despite receiving sunlight and soil manure, your borehole water may have a high pH that needs balancing before watering.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tso bibioo lɛ yɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, etsitsi lɛ egbɔjɔ Aloo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu la kɛ ŋmeii eshɛ enɔ po sɛɛ. Ekolɛ nu ni yɔɔ o-borehole lɛ mli lɛ yɛ pH ni nɔ kwɔ ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani awo mli nu.

english: Can tap water from the pipe harm my okra plants if I pour it on them directly?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ paipi mli lɛ baanyɛ aye mi gumbo lɛ awui kɛji mikɛshwie nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Tap water often has high pH levels or treatment chemicals that stress crop roots. Leaving the water in an open bucket for a day helps lower its harshness before you apply it to your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ mli pH lɛ fa babaoo loo tsofai ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ haoɔ lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi nu lɛ yɛ tanki ni agbele mli gbi kome lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ mli wamɔ baa shi dani okɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Is clean plain water enough to grow cassava, or do I always need to add liquid growth boosters?
ga: Ani nu ni mli tse lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛduɔ ŋmei? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni haa mɔ daa lɛ afata he be fɛɛ be?

english: Plain, clean water is sufficient for healthy growth. Adding extra chemical boosters unnecessarily can burn crop roots and damage the natural growth cycle of the plant.
ga: Nu ni mli tse fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa. Tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni he ehiaaa fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni efite bɔ ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Can I mix pest medicine and liquid fertilizer together in the same watering can to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ afutu nu kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing different plant medicines or chemicals together can cause bad reactions that make them stop working or create toxic solutions that destroy your crop's roots.
ga: Tsofai ni jɛ tsei loo tsofai amli ni akɛfutuɔ amɛhe lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee nɔ ko ni ehiii ni baaha tsofa lɛ akpa nitsumɔ loo amɛfee tsofa ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ otso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Why do my cabbage seedlings look burned after I put growth promoter powder into their water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ powder ni haa mɔ daa lɛ ewo nu lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growth promoters contain strong concentrated chemicals. When mixed too heavily into water, they can shock and burn young seedling roots, causing leaves to wither.
ga: Tsofai babaoo yɛ nibii ni haa mɔ daa lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ nu babaoo futu mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ etswa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ ni eha amɛshã. ha baai lɛ agbo

english: Does adding extra chemical medicine to my crop water help sick plants recover faster?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni mikɛfataa midumɔ nu lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛhe waaa oya?

english: No, overloading crop water with extra medicine increases chemical toxicity in the soil, which hurts the plant roots further instead of curing them.
ga: Dabi, tsei amli nu kɛ tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my tomato plants stop growing even after I apply good manure to the bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ekpa shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo saatso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: If the water you use to irrigate has a high pH, it locks the nutrients from the manure inside the soil so the tomato roots cannot drink them up.
ga: Kɛji nu ni okɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ pH lɛ fa lɛ, ebaatsi niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tomato shishifãi lɛ akafee nɔ ni anuɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants drop their blossoms before fruiting even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water with unsuitable pH levels stresses the crop internally, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Nu ni pH lɛ ejaaa lɛ baaha tso lɛ mli aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei baa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains drown the roots. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thin with very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build a strong stalk and produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during heavy rainy seasons and high humidity. Pruning overgrown branches to let in air and sunlight, along with early fungicide spraying, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. kɛfata tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like whiteflies or aphids that transmit viruses to the plant. Spraying neem oil or appropriate organic insecticides helps eliminate these pests and keeps new leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and planting at the start of the favorable season helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the farm before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they receive a sudden surge of heavy water after a dry spell. The inside grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, so watering your field evenly prevents the skin from bursting.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji amɛna trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo hewolo lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha hewolo lɛ akagbala.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily get scorched by intense sunshine. Plantains grow quickly and produce large broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ amɛhe oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin and crooked instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ agboi ni ja lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, loose soil to push through as they expand underground. Hard or stony soil blocks the tubers from growing outward smoothly, resulting in thin, bent shapes.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni egbɛ eshwa koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli beni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ bulb lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni ebɔle ehe.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem. You can also gently dig around the base of one plant to check if the tubers have grown thick enough before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ tso titri lɛ efolo. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo hu abɔle tso kome shishigbɛ he koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi obɔ bɔ ni sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither and die even when the soil feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo po lɛ?

english: If crops wither in moist soil, tiny microscopic worms called nematodes may be eating the roots underground, or excess water has rotted the root system. When roots are damaged, they cannot drink water, causing the plant above ground to dry out.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ gbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ efite lɛ Enyɛŋ enu nu. Gbimɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to change the type of fertilizer I give my maize after six to eight weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhaa mi-ŋmei lɛ yɛ otsii enumɔ kɛyashi kpaanyɔ sɛɛ?

english: Crops need different food as they mature. In their first few weeks, plants need nitrogen to build strong leaves, but around 6 to 8 weeks, they reach a flowering milestone where they need a different fertilizer blend rich in phosphorus and potassium to form big cobs.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, nitrogen he miihia tsei koni amɛwo tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, shi yɛ aaafee otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 mli lɛ, tsei ni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ baabi ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: What do the different numbers printed on fertilizer bags actually mean for my crops?
ga: Mɛni yibɔi ni akala yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kotokui anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The numbers show the mix formula of key plant foods—Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium. Changing from a standard mix like 12-12-17 to another ratio like 14-14-14 adjusts the strength of each nutrient depending on whether the plant is growing leaves or producing fruits.
ga: Yibɔi lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni tso mli niyenii titrii lɛ yɔɔ ha: naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiɔm. Kɛ́ atsake kɛjɛ niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni afɔɔ feemɔ, tamɔ 12-12-17 lɛ nɔ kɛtee nɔ kroko ni akɛfutuɔ nii, tamɔ 14-14-14 lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli hewalɛ tsakeɔ. Edamɔ tso lɛ baa miikwɛ̃ loo eewo yibii nɔ.

english: Why are the young flowers and small fruits falling off my pepper plants, and what food can I give them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni aduawai lɛ hu daraaa lɛ? Koni egbee shi kɛjɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ Ni mɛɛ niyenii manyɛ maha lɛ?

english: When crops drop their flowers or leaves, it means they are stressed or lacking essential nutrients. Changing to a targeted food formula high in calcium and potassium strengthens the stems so the plant can hold onto its fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii fite fɔfɔi loo baai lɛ No tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ edɛŋ. Kɛji akɛ otsake kɛtee tsofa ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ ni calcium kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawaje tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ yibii.

english: How do I know it is the right time to change my tomato plants' feeding routine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ matsake mi-tomato tso lɛ niyenii ni mikɛhaa lɛ?

english: You can tell by watching key milestones in the plant's growth, usually between 6 to 8 weeks after planting, when flowers start to open. That is the signal to switch from growth food to fruiting food.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yaa nɔ yɛ tso ko dalɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔmɔɔ. No ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ atsake kɛjɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ daa lɛ nɔ kɛya niyenii ni woɔ yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my crop seem to stop growing for a short period after I apply a new fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa shweremɔ be kukuoo ko lɛ? Beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei fata he sɛɛ

english: Plants take a little time to adjust whenever their food formula changes. The crop is being patient while its roots absorb the new nutrients before using them to push out new leaves and flowers.
ga: Tsei heɔ be fioo dani amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe be fɛɛ be ni niyenii lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baatsake. Esa akɛ tso lɛ ato etsui shi yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii heei dani ekɛtsu nii ni ekɛtsi baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei kɛje kpo.

english: Can I use the exact same plant food from the day I clear my land until harvest time?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛjɛ gbi ni mikpaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: No, using only one food type limits your yield. Young plants need a starter formula to build healthy roots and leaves, while older plants need a modified food formula to develop heavy, healthy crops.
ga: Dabi, niyenii henɔ kome pɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha onibii ni obaaná lɛ afee bibioo. Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia shishijee fɔmla koni amɛfee shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni egbɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii ni atsake lɛ koni amɛná tsei ni tsii ni he wa.

english: What should I do if my cocoa tree starts dropping its yellow pods prematurely?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ bɔi ŋmɔtɔ ni ji yellow pods lɛ shwiemɔ mra?

english: Pod dropping happens when the tree suffers a nutrient drop or water stress. Feeding the tree a specialized nutrient formula helps restore its strength and stops the loss of young pods.
ga: Pod drop baa kɛji tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nu he haomɔ eba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛ ko ha tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ekpa ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: How many weeks after planting should I wait before switching to heavy fruiting fertilizer for my vegetables?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii lɛ, otsii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani matsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ nɔ?

english: Most vegetable crops reach their main growth milestone around 6 to 8 weeks. Waiting until this stage ensures the plant has built a strong enough frame before shifting its energy toward making food.
ga: Aduawai tsei babaoo tsɔɔ amɛ shishijee dalɛ mli yɛ otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 mli. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ mli ewoɔ niyenii feemɔ mli.

english: If my crops look weak, should I just double the amount of fertilizer I normally give them?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ Ani Esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli shii enyɔ?

english: Giving too much of the same food can burn the plant's roots. Instead of giving extra food, you should switch to a formula designed to revive stressed crops so the plant can recover safely.
ga: Niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayeɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ niyenii kroko ni oooha lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Esa akɛ otsake kɛya tsofa ko ni afee koni ekɛha tsei ni haoɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plant leaves change color or drop when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When weather conditions drop or become harsh, crops conserve energy by dropping older leaves. Adjusting their feeding routine gives them the resilience to endure the heat until growing conditions improve.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ fite loo ebafee nɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ baai momoi ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ latsaa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the price of my crops drop so much when everyone in my village harvests at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajara baa shi waa nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When every farmer harvests at once, the market gets flooded with produce. Because buyers have so many options to choose from, they offer lower prices, causing the market value of your crops to drop.
ga: Beni okwaafoi fɛɛ kpa amɛŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayelihe lɛ eyi kɛ nibii ni amɛduɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ nibii babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhala mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ jara ni baa shi ha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jara ni okɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I get much higher prices if my crops mature and reach the market early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa nɔ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyɔɔ jara nɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early in the season, very few farmers have harvested crops to sell. Since the supply in the market is low and demand from buyers is high, buyers are willing to pay top price for the first batch of produce.
ga: yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli Okwaafoi fioo ko pɛ kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛhaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ faaa, ni nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ hu fa babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo nyɔmɔ ni fe fɛɛ kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ nibii ni amɛbaahe lɛ.

english: Should I lower my crop price when buyers refuse to pay my asking price during a heavy harvest season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ajara shi beni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ kpoo akɛ ebaawo mi jara ni mibiɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni mli wa mli lɛ?

english: Yes, when there is a glut in the market, holding onto perishable produce for a high price can lead to rot and total loss. Adjusting your price lower helps you sell off your stock quickly before it spoils.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa tsɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni fiteɔ oya ni akɛtoɔ jara ni wa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛfite ni amɛfite kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ jara lɛ ba shi lɛ, obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ oya dani efite.

english: Why do crop prices change so quickly from week to week right after harvest begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ otsi mli kɛyaa otsi mli yɛ nikpamɔ lɛ shishijee sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Prices change rapidly based on how much food arrives at the market each day. As more trucks bring in harvest daily, supply increases quickly, forcing prices down continuously.
ga: Niyenii ni shɛɔ jara nɔ daa gbi lɛ jara tsakeɔ oya. Beni lɔlei babaoo baa koni amɛbakpa nii daa gbi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ hu tee hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ajara yaa nɔ ebaa shi.

english: Why do traders pay less for my produce when there is plenty of food available everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi woɔ mi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ fioo lɛ? Beni niyenii babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Traders pay less because consumers have plenty of choices. When produce is abundant everywhere, traders cannot resell it at high prices, so they pass that lower price back to you, the farmer.
ga: Jarayelɔi woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ nɔ ni amɛbaahala. Beni nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fa yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Jarayelɔi nyɛŋ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ jara ni baa shi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa bo, okwaafonyo lɛ.

english: What is the difference between the major season and the minor season for selling my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ be ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: The major season brings heavy rains resulting in massive crop production and lower market prices, while the minor season produces smaller yields, making crops scarcer and market prices higher.
ga: Be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa baa, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa ni jarayeli jara baa shi. yɛ be mli ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe waaa ni jara hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do early-planted crops often bring in more money than crops planted during the peak of the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ mra lɛ haa anáa shika babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Early-planted crops reach the market before the peak harvest period when produce is scarce, allowing you to sell at maximum prices before the market becomes oversaturated.
ga: Tsei ni adu mra lɛ boteɔ jara nɔ dani kpamɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baa be mli ni nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ nɔ dani jara lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield so much more during the major rainy season compared to the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto be ni ji enyɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: The major season provides longer and more consistent rainfall, allowing crops to grow bigger and produce more fruits or grains than during the shorter, lighter rains of the minor season.
ga: Be titri lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ni mli waaa ni ji be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does the total amount of harvest in my region affect how much profit I can make on a single crate of produce?
ga: Te ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ saa sɛɛnamɔ ni manyɛ maná kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ adeka kome mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When overall regional harvest is high, high supply drives the price per crate down, reducing your profit per unit. When total harvest is low, scarcity raises the price per crate, increasing your profit margin.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ fa lɛ, nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ babaoo baaha adeka kome jara aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji sɛɛnamɔ ni baa shi yɛ unit kome mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ ba shi lɛ Scarcity baaha jara ni akɛwoɔ adeka kome mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sɛɛnamɔ ni onáa lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Is it better to sell my produce immediately at harvest time or wait for a few weeks?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni adu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo abaamɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: If you can store non-perishable crops safely without pest damage, waiting a few weeks after the main harvest rush passes can help you sell at higher prices when market supply starts dropping.
ga: Kɛji obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteee lɛ ato shweshweeshwe ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteee amɛ lɛ, Otsii fioo komɛi ni ooomɛ beni ŋmaakpamɔ oyaiyeli titri lɛ eho lɛ baaha onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ beni jarayeli nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi lɛ.

english: Is there a single chemical or medicine I can buy that will cure all diseases on my farm?
ga: Ani tsofa loo tsofa kome yɛ ni manyɛ mahe ni mikɛtsa helai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No single medicine can treat every crop disease. Plant sicknesses are caused by different things like fungi, bacteria, viruses, or insects, and each requires a specific treatment. Using the wrong chemical wastes money and can harm your crops.
ga: Tsofa kome pɛ bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa tso hela fɛɛ hela. Nibii tamɔ ŋmei, muawai, muawai, loo koolooi kɛ tsei helai baa, ni eko fɛɛ eko biɔ tsamɔ krɛdɛɛ. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ heɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why do pests and crop diseases keep coming back even after I spray my farm with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Spraying often kills only the adult pests, leaving eggs or fungal spores behind in the soil or nearby weeds. Also, using the exact same chemical repeatedly can cause pests to build resistance, making the spray stop working over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni eda pɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ashiɔ yɛ sũ loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kpaɔ nitsumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn dark green after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer supplies nutrients like nitrogen, which helps plants produce chlorophyll—the green substance that captures sunlight to make food. Dark green leaves show that your crop is well-fed and growing actively.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ klorofil. ni ji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops looking pale yellowish instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale or yellowish leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen and nutrients. Without enough food in the soil, the plant cannot produce its normal green color and struggles to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia onibii. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ ajie amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kpo ni amɛna naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli.

english: How long does it usually take to see changes in my crops after feeding them fertilizer?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani minaa tsakemɔi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If there is enough moisture in the soil, you will usually start seeing the leaves turn greener and new shoots appear within three to seven days after applying fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaaje shishi ona baai ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo yɛ gbii etɛ kɛyashi kpawo mli yɛ be mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Should I spread fertilizer across the whole land or put it at specific spots near the plant roots?
ga: Ani esa akɛ afɔse ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ loo akɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe pɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer at specific spots near the base or root corners of the plant ensures the crop absorbs the nutrients directly instead of wasting it on surrounding weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he pɔtɛɛ ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifã lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ lɛ oshwie jwɛi ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why does the irrigation water in my farm channel sometimes look greenish instead of clear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ eŋɔli moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Greenish water usually contains tiny natural plant nutrients and organic matter like algae. This nutrient-rich water can actually help feed your crop roots when used for irrigation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei amli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ nu eŋɔli mli. Nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ baanyɛ aha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ akɛtsu nii kɛshwie nɔ.

english: How can I easily check with my hands if my liquid fertilizer mix is strong enough for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛtsɔ minine nɔ mlɛo akɛ mi-liquid fertilizer mixture lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You can dip your hand into the mixture; if it leaves a rich, visible greenish or cloudy coat on your skin rather than looking like clear water, it contains enough dissolved nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ oniji awo nibii ni akɛfutu lɛ mli. Kɛji eshi ŋmɔtɔ loo atatu ni anaa faŋŋ yɛ ohewolo nɔ lɛ Moŋ lɛ etamɔ nu ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What happens to my plants if I put too much fertilizer in one place?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo he kome?

english: Applying too much fertilizer in one spot can burn the plant roots and cause the leaves to turn brown or wither, so it is best to apply moderate amounts evenly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛgboi, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fioo po awo mli.

english: Why does adding animal manure change the appearance of my farm soil after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: As manure breaks down, it releases organic nutrients and humic material that darken pale soil, turning it richer and better at holding water for crop roots.
ga: Kɛ kooloi ashishifãi lɛ fite Ejieɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ humic nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ ni etsake su lɛ feɔ duŋ lɛ kpo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛha tsei shishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops growing near the edges of nutrient-rich water channels grow faster than those on dry land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ nu gbɛi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops near nutrient-rich water have a continuous supply of moisture and dissolved food, allowing their roots to feed constantly without waiting for rainfall.
ga: Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii be fɛɛ be ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ.

english: How can I tell if my sickly crops are starting to recover after treatment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ ebɔi helatsamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Recovery starts when pale, weak stems produce fresh, dark green leaves and the overall plant stops looking faded and begins to stand firm.
ga: Hewalɛwoo jeɔ shishi be mli ni tsei bibii, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ jieɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse. ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ efooo ni ebɔi shidaamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Can I plant crops on land in my village that has been lying untouched for many years?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ nɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etako he afii babaoo nɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, idle land often gathers rich natural nutrients as fallen leaves and bushes decompose over time. Clearing this land gives hardy crops like cassava or maize a fertile environment to grow well without requiring expensive fertilizers immediately.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ fɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai kɛ tsei bibii ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei aba. Eyɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Which crop is good to farm if I want to stay in my village and earn a reliable income?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji miisumɔ ni mahi akrowa lɛ mli ni maná shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ?

english: Cassava is one of the most reliable options because it handles harsh weather well, has constant market demand for staple foods like gari and fufu, and requires lower startup money compared to vegetables.
ga: Cassava ji nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome. Ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ etsu kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ghari kɛ fufu he miihia jarayeli be fɛɛ be ni ebiɔ ni akɛ shika fioo awo mli koni akɛje shishi kɛ akɛto aduawai ahe.

english: Why is cassava able to survive long dry seasons without dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni egbooo lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss and uses its deep root system to pull moisture from deep underground, allowing it to remain alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi. ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Ha ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi shishifãi fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or when the plants do not get enough direct sunlight. Cassava needs full sun and soil balanced with potassium to transfer its energy down into expanding the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yucca he miihia hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ awo bulbs ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How long can mature cassava stay underground before it starts to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi dani ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: Unlike crops that spoil quickly on the stem, mature cassava roots can remain safely stored underground for several months up to a year until you are ready to harvest and take them to market.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi afi. Etamɔɔɔ tsei ni fiteɔ oya yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛba jara nɔ.

english: Why do people say cassava is an easy crop to manage if I cannot be on the farm every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ji tso ko ni nɔkwɛmɔ waaa lɛ? Akɛni minyɛɛɛ mahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi hewɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava plants grow tall and form a thick canopy of leaves, they shade the ground and naturally suppress weed growth. This makes them much less demanding than delicate crops like tomatoes or cabbages.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ da ni eyɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ, Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛbiɔ nibii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato loo kaabe.

english: Can I use the leftover stems from my cassava crop to plant a new farm without buying seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli ni miheee dumɔwui?

english: Yes, cassava does not grow from seeds; it grows from stem cuttings. You can cut mature, healthy stems from your previous harvest into short pieces and plant them directly into the soil to grow your next crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei jɛɛɛ dumɔwui amli ekwɛɛɛ. Ejɛɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ mli edaa. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ mli kukuji. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: What will happen to my land if I keep planting cassava on the exact same plot for ten years?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii nyɔŋma?

english: Cassava extracts nutrients from the soil as its large roots develop. Planting it continuously on the same plot without resting the land, rotating crops, or adding compost will gradually exhaust the soil and lead to smaller harvests over time.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji shishifãi wuji eda. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe. ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ Loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni efee shikpɔŋ lɛ fiofio. Efiteɔ ni kpamɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if my cassava is mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is getting ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging up the soil around one plant to check the tuber size.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ miisaa amɛhe kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Plant lɛ he lɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni bulb lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cassava roots start going bad just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots undergo rapid chemical changes and rot quickly because the skin is injured during harvest, exposing the starch to air and decay. Processing the roots quickly into products like gari preserves them for a long time.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ, tsofai tsakeɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewolo lɛ yeɔ awui yɛ be mli ni akpaa nii lɛ. Enɛ haa powda lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpeɔ ni efiteɔ. Kɛ́ afee shishifãi lɛ oya ni afee nɔ ko tamɔ gari lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does cocoa have a major harvest season starting around October in Ghana instead of fruiting all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kpamɔ be ni he hiaa waa jeɔ shishi yɛ October aaafee yɛ Ghana lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ

english: Cocoa trees naturally follow Ghana's rainy patterns. The heavy rainy season allows trees to produce abundant flowers that turn into pods, which naturally mature and ripen together by October for the main harvest.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyiɛɔ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔi asɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nugbɔnɛmɔ be ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo ni tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Amɛdaraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ kɛyashiɔ October kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees have two different harvest periods in a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ náa ŋmaakpamɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ?

english: Ghana experiences two rainy seasons. The major rains lead to the main crop harvest around October, while the smaller rainy season creates a smaller yield known as the light crop mid-year.
ga: Ghana yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei enyɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ October mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be bibioo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa flower to turn into a full pod ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: It takes about 5 to 6 months from the time a cocoa flower is pollinated for it to grow into a fully mature, ripe pod.
ga: Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 kɛjɛɔ be mli ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do many tiny, young cocoa pods shrivel up and die on my tree before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛi babaoo gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It is a natural process where the tree reduces its pod count to ensure it has enough water and nutrients to feed the remaining healthy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ shi koni amɛkwɛ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main trunk of the tree instead of just the smaller branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are heavy fruit. Growing directly on the sturdy trunk and thick branches gives the pods strong support so they do not break the tree as they grow.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ji aduawai ni tsii. Kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehãŋ tso lɛ akumɔ kɛ́ eda.

english: How does the dry Harmattan weather affect my cocoa trees and their yields?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ Harmattan lɛ saa mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of the soil and leaves, causing trees to drop flowers and young pods to save water, which lowers yield if the dry spell is severe.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli. Ha tsei ajie fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival trick. Trees shed leaves to cut down on water loss through transpiration when the soil is too dry.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji teemɔŋ sane ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ.

english: How do I know that a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: Ripe pods change color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn bright orange—and produce a hollow sound when gently tapped.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kpɛɔ. ni ehaa gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji baa kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ fioo.

english: What happens to cocoa beans if I harvest pods before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛshwere kwraa?

english: Unripe pods have small, flat beans with low sugar content, which stops them from fermenting properly and results in poor-quality, bitter beans.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni sugar fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni edako lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni mli edɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do cocoa beans need to be fermented under plantain leaves for several days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atswa kookoo yibii yɛ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the seed to prevent it from sprouting, removes natural bitterness, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color that buyers require.
ga: Fɛ̃i gbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ, ni ehaaa amɛkwɛ̃. Ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds because their roots are shallow. Without taller trees or plantains around them to provide shade and trap moisture, the heat scorches their delicate leaves and dries them out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛji tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha amɛgbi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers, but the tiny pods dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi, shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt' or mirid insect attacks. When the tree feels stressed from lack of water or nutrients, or when insects suck the sap from young pods, the tree naturally drops them to save its energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ‘cherelle wilt’ loo mirid kooloi ni baa tso lɛ nɔ beni nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii miinu nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them and look like something ate them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko ye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central shoot (funnel) of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni teɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa (cone) lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli, ni eyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow in the shape of a 'V' from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ‘V’ su mli kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, leaving the plant hungry.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, or when plants are crowded too close together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and helping the plant direct more energy into growing big tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: The main plantain tree shares water and soil nutrients with all the young shoots growing at its base. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong successors, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛyelɔi ni he wa kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then suddenly very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni trukaa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. The damaged leaves cannot open fully to catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ agbele kwraa kɛha hulu la.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass make them stay green longer during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents sunlight from evaporating groundwater, allowing the crop roots to stay cool and drink water even when it does not rain.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How can official weather advisories or seasonal rain reports help me plan my planting schedule?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he ŋaawoo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ he amaniɛbɔɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mato midumɔ be he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Seasonal weather forecasts predict whether rains will start late, end early, or suffer long breaks. Using this information helps you select early-maturing seed varieties or adjust your planting dates so your young plants don't die during sudden dry spells.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa tsɔɔ kɛji nugbɔ baaje shishi sɛɛ, ebaagbe naa mra, loo ebaakpa be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ okɛ saji nɛɛ tsu nii lɛ obaanyɛ ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra loo otsake gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei bibii lɛ akagboi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa trukaa lɛ.

english: Should I hold off on planting my crops if the initial rains are light and unpredictable?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo dumɔ mli kɛji akɛ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ waaa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba?

english: Yes, it is safer to wait until the rains become steady. Planting after weak or erratic early rains risks poor germination and leaves young seedlings vulnerable to drying up if a dry period follows immediately.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baashɛ shi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra ni bɛ hewalɛ loo nɔ ni bɛ faŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii lɛ ahe oshara mli. ni ekɛ dumɔwui bibii woɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaagbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What happens to my young crops if a dry spell of two to three weeks occurs early in the farming season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji otsii enyɔ loo etɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: A prolonged dry spell early in the season causes young plants to wilt, stop growing, or die because their roots are not deep enough to reach subterranean moisture. This forces plants into survival mode instead of building stems and leaves.
ga: Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkpaa dalɛ loo amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ehiɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ eshishifãi kɛ baai.

english: Can I still spread chemical fertilizer on my farm if the soil is dry and no rain is falling?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lolo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nugbɔ enɛko?

english: No, fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Spreading fertilizer on dry ground wastes your money because heat causes nutrients to vaporize into the air, and concentrated granules can burn the plant roots.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooofee lɛ baafite shika ejaakɛ latsaa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ni pellets ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop look yellow and burnt after I apply fertilizer during a hot, dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Without rain to dilute the fertilizer, high concentrations of mineral salts build up around the roots. This draws water out of the plant roots rather than feeding them, causing leaf tip burn and scorching.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, abaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mineral salts ni fa babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛshãa.

english: What is the best way to time my fertilizer application when rainfall is uncertain?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii beni nugbɔ lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a good rainfall, ideally when moderate rain is expected within a day or two. Avoid applying fertilizer during extended dry periods or right before violent downpours that wash topsoil away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli loo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the first 50 days after planting rice so crucial for a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii 50 ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa kpakpa lɛ?

english: The first 50 days are when rice develops its tillers (main stems) and root network. Stunting growth during this early window permanently reduces the number of grain heads the plant can produce later, even if water returns.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbii 50 lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ tillers (shishifãi wuji) kɛ shishifãi. Dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ayitsei ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi kwraa. Kɛji nu lɛ ku esɛɛ po

english: Why does rice seem to suffer faster from dry weather than crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmãa yeɔ amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice has a relatively shallow root system and high water requirements compared to cassava or maize. It cannot reach deep underground water tables, making it extremely sensitive to dry topsoil.
ga: Omɔ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ, ni ehe hiaa nu babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he. Enyɛŋ eshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ waa.

english: How does an early-season drought affect the final harvest weight of my crop at the end of the year?
ga: Te hɔmɔ ni baa mra be mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaagbee kpamɔ lɛ he yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Early dry periods limit the overall size and vigor of the plant, leading to fewer shoots, weaker flowers, and smaller panicles. Even if late-season rains are heavy, the plant cannot regain lost early growth, resulting in lighter grain yields.
ga: Be ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa, fɔfɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee moŋ Shi tsei nyɛŋ aná mra be mli dalɛ ni elaaje lɛ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ shi.

english: What simple practices can I use to keep moisture in my soil if a short dry spell is expected?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ nifeemɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni obaanyɛ ofee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi kɛji akɛ akpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaagbi be kukuoo ko?

english: Leaving crop residues on the field as mulch, minimizing tilling, and adding organic manure retain moisture in the soil longer, helping your crops survive short dry periods between rainfalls.
ga: Shi ŋmɔ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli akɛ mulch, tsi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ organic fertilizer afata he koni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does growing crops inside one help my tomatoes grow better than in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tomato lɛ ni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A greenhouse is a structure covered with clear plastic or net that creates a controlled environment for plants. It protects crops like tomatoes from heavy rainfall, extreme heat, and pests, allowing them to grow faster, stay healthier, and produce higher yields all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsũ ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni akudɔ amɛ. Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni owo yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do tomato plants grown inside a covered structure get so tall like vines, while the ones on my regular farm stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsũi ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ lɛ amli lɛ daa tamɔ wain tsei lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tomato tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ kuku.

english: Greenhouses often use special plant varieties that keep growing upward continuously because they are supported by ropes and protected from wind. This vertical growth allows the plant to produce fruit for many months instead of dying off early like short bush varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsũi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ejaakɛ kpãai fiɔ amɛsɛɛ ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Nɛkɛ dalɛ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii nyɔji babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbo oya tamɔ tsei kukuji lɛ.

english: My tomato plants drop their flowers whenever the afternoon sun becomes too hot. Why does this happen?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi be fɛɛ be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ shwane mli tsɔ. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants experience heat stress and cannot properly pollinate their flowers. As a self-defense mechanism, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy, which stops fruit from forming unless the crop is shielded or cooled.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Enɛ haaa aduawai afee. ja abu tso lɛ he loo afee lɛ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my open-field tomatoes crack open on the plants right after a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmɔ mli tomatoi ni agbele naa lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When a dry plant suddenly gets a sudden rush of heavy rain, the inside of the tomato absorbs water faster than its skin can stretch. This sudden pressure causes the skin to split open, which is why controlling water through covered farming helps prevent cracked fruits.
ga: Beni tso lɛ gĩ trukaa lɛ Nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa. Enɛ hewɔ ni nu ni akudɔ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai amli gbalaa lɛ.

english: How is it possible to grow and harvest fresh vegetables during the long dry season when everywhere is dry?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni adu ni akpa aduawai heei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni he fɛɛ he egbi lɛ?

english: Crops can grow in the dry season if they are protected from scorching sun with netting or plastic and given precise daily water through drip pipes. This keeps the crop moist and cool without relying on rainy weather.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋshɔŋ loo plastic bu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ekɛ nu pɔtɛɛ aha daa gbi kɛtsɔ paipi ni hoɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa nu ni amɛhe jɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be nɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my vegetable farm less when the crops are covered with netting or plastic?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fioo pɛ tutuaa mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akɛ ŋshɔŋ loo plastic ehà tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Many damaging insects fly in from neighboring bushes to land on exposed crops. Covering crops creates a physical shield that keeps insects from reaching the leaves and laying eggs, reducing the need for chemical sprays.
ga: Kplukai babaoo ni fiteɔ nii lɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛbaa shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkashɛ baai lɛ ahe ni amɛkawo ŋmeii. Ehaa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: Why do the stems and roots of my pepper plants rot when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?
