english: Excess rain creates soggy soil with no oxygen, which allows dangerous fungal diseases to attack the plant roots. When roots rot, the plant can no longer drink water or food from the soil, causing the whole crop to wilt and die.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara tutuaa tsei shishifãi. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛnu nu loo niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ gboi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is dripping water directly at the root of a crop better than spraying water all over the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ hi fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Wet leaves attract dangerous plant diseases like black spots and mold. Dripping water directly at the roots feeds the plant without wetting the leaves, and it also saves water from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Baai ni efɔ lɛ gbalaa tsei ahe helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ black spot kɛ fungus. Nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ baai lɛ efɔɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I grow my crops under a plastic canopy, will they still get enough light to grow properly?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ plastic ŋwɛitsu tsu nii kɛdu tsei Ani tso lɛ baaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, greenhouse plastic is specially designed to let in the light crops need for growth while filtering out harsh radiation that causes sunburn. This scattered light reaches lower leaves better, helping the plant manufacture food efficiently.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee plastic ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni eha tsei lɛ aná la fioo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ la ni naa wa ni kɛ hulutsoo baa lɛ. Nɛkɛ kane ni gbɛ eshwa nɛɛ shɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grown in places like Akomadan produce better tomatoes when protected from excess rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hei tamɔ Akomadan lɛ woɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ he lɛ?

english: Akomadan has great soil for tomatoes, but heavy rains during peak seasons wash away soil nutrients and spread leaf diseases. Protecting the plants from direct rain keeps the soil balanced and prevents disease spores from splashing onto the leaves.
ga: Akomadan yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha tomato. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant cannot get enough nitrogen from the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the nutrients it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally refreshes the land for the next crop without buying expensive chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that create necessary shade and keep the soil cool while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy rains stay on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the land without draining, it smothers the roots and allows water-loving fungi to decay the cassava under ground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni efooo kɛyaaa lɛ. Ebaatswa shishifãi lɛ ni eha hydrophilic fungi lɛ afite shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass keep them from wilting in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks direct heat from the sun and prevents soil water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ni etsĩ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya

english: Why do leaf-eating caterpillars attack my crop much more when there is a short dry spell in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Dry and warm weather helps insect eggs hatch faster, and without heavy rains to wash young caterpillars off the plants, their numbers multiply rapidly.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi awɔlɔi ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. Ni kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baafɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ? Amɛyibɔ ​​baaya hiɛ oya.

english: Leaf curling on peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes too drastically, causing stress that prevents fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ aduawai anaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up and turning brown when harvest time is near?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally die back once the tubers under the ground have finished growing and storing starch, indicating that the yam is fully mature and ready to be dug up.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbe amɛdamɔ naa ni amɛbua ŋmeii anaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and produce tiny yields if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil food; if left uncleared during early growth, they steal the essential resources your crops need to flourish.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni atsɔɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ Amɛbaaju nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ni onibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops fail if I do not pay close attention to them every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ emaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa otsi lɛ?

english: Crops need regular monitoring for pests, diseases, and weeds early on. Catching small problems early prevents major harvest loss and ensures your time and money do not go to waste.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli daa mra koni ana kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai kɛ jwɛi bɛ mli. Tsu naagbai bibii ahe nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ ŋmaa nibii wuji ni baafite lɛ anaa. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni obei kɛ oshika akafite.

english: Is it harder to manage an organic crop compared to using chemical inputs?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ wa fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Organic farming often requires more close attention and physical work, such as weeding and soil management, because you are relying on natural care rather than quick chemical sprays to fix problems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli kwɛmɔ nɔ moŋ fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ oya koni akɛsaa naagba lɛ.

english: What kind of problems cause farmers to struggle when they neglect their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛɛ naagbai okwaafoi kɛkpeɔ kɛ́ amɛku amɛhiɛ amɛshwie amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Neglecting a cocoa farm allows aggressive weeds to steal soil nutrients, while unchecked pests and diseases can destroy young stems and pods before you even notice them.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahiɛ dani oyɔse amɛ po.

english: What does it mean if I choose to grow my cocoa without applying chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji mihala akɛ makwɛ kookoo ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Growing cocoa without synthetic fertilizers means you are producing organic cocoa. This method relies entirely on the natural nutrients already in the soil and organic matter like compost.
ga: Kookoo ni ooodu ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oofee kookoo ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli. Gbɛ nɛɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kwraa.

english: Will my crops grow slower if I do not put chemical fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, crops grown without chemical fertilizers often grow at a more natural, gradual pace because they depend on natural soil fertility, but they cost less in chemical inputs and preserve long-term soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ fiofio. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ nii anɔ. Shi tsofai ni akɛfeɔ lɛ he ehiaaa tsɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does supplying extra water to my crops change how fast they grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu kroko ni mikɛaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsake bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ?

english: Watering your crops regularly keeps them fed and hydrated continuously, which speeds up their development compared to crops that must wait for natural rainfall.
ga: Nu ni oooha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ baaha amɛná niyenii ni amɛná nu be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa oya kɛ akɛto tsei ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the same crop take a full year to mature in my village, but matures faster on a farm with proper watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ heɔ afi muu fɛɛ yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi edaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu shwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: In many rural areas, crops depend only on rainfall and stop growing during dry months. Farms with artificial watering systems keep crops growing steadily all year without drought delays.
ga: Yɛ akrowai babaoo amli lɛ, Dumɔwui damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ ni amɛkpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli. Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛfee lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ ni hɔmɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa plants if they suffer from a lack of water during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni faaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa plants do not get enough water, their growth slows down, leaves may wither, and the tree delays producing pods because it is using all its energy just to stay alive.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. Baai lɛ baanyɛ agbi. Ni tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ pods feemɔ mli ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ.

english: Can I harvest my crops earlier in the season if I feed them with regular water instead of waiting for rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli? Kɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ daa moŋ fe ni mamɛ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: Yes, providing a consistent supply of water prevents growth pauses during dry spells, allowing the crop to complete its growth cycle and be ready for harvest months earlier.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha nikpamɔ nyɔji komɛi dani eba.

english: How long does cocoa normally take to be ready for harvest under standard rainfall conditions?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani kookoo feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni sa mli lɛ amli?

english: Under typical village conditions that rely purely on natural rain cycles, young cocoa trees generally take longer to mature and bear ready fruit—often a year or more depending on rainfall patterns.
ga: Yɛ akrowa lɛ shihilɛi ni damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afi loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Applying balanced fertilizer like NPK or adding animal manure restores nitrogen so the maize can grow healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge branches and leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excess shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top foliage instead of storing energy in the roots. Balancing soil nutrients and ensuring full sunlight helps the plant build bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ mli. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrink on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and high-humidity weather. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air inside the cocoa farm and removing infected pods helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How can I stop caterpillars from chewing holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye bu yɛ kaaba baa mli?

english: Caterpillars hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by butterflies. You can pick them off by hand on small plots, or spray a mixture made from neem tree leaves or recommended organic insecticides early in the morning to protect the leaves.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ okɛ onine afɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ. Aloo okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛ neem baai fee loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi koni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my yam plants curling up and covered in sticky liquid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni nu ni mli tse ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and sticky spots are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids. They feed on the leaf juices and excrete honeydew, which weakens the plant. Spraying with soapy water or targeted pest control eliminates these insects.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ amɛhe shwieɔ shi. Amɛyeɔ baai amli nu ni amɛjieɔ wuo, ni no haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants wither and die suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by soil fungi that rot the roots and block water tubes inside the stem. Rotating your bean crop with maize or cassava every season helps clear these disease organisms from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsĩɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa duɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorch under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf shade like umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme changes between dry soil and heavy watering. Keeping soil evenly moist with mulch and watering regularly helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo tsakemɔi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ waa lɛ teŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the field during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the soil without draining away, oxygen cannot reach the roots, allowing waterlogged rot fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha ŋmeii ni egbo ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my pepper crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli?

english: Applying fertilizer works best a few weeks after transplanting when roots are established, and again when flowering begins. Always ensure the soil is damp before applying fertilizer so the crop roots can absorb it without burning.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ shishifãi lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɛji fɔfɔi je shishi Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ ni amɛshãaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves to provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it gets strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji koni ekɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi lɛ? No pɛtɛɔ tsei ahe lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid weather. High moisture helps the fungal spores spread quickly from pod to pod through raindrops.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ.

english: Which side of the cassava stem cutting should point upwards when I plant it in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ fã esa akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli?

english: You should plant the stem with the leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them right-side up allows the buds to sprout easily toward sunlight, whereas upside-down stems grow weak and yield fewer tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ odu tso lɛ yibii lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ hiɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni etse amɛhe lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves helps the plant make food efficiently, which goes straight into expanding the tubers growing underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa niyenii feɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni kɛ bulbs ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ baa tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why will my cassava roots stay very small if I plant the stem cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete against each other for water, soil nutrients, and space. Planting them too close leaves little room and energy for the tubers to expand.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ He ni Aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa he kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ baa bulb lɛ nɔ koni amɛshwere.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any small tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is excessively hot or when the plant experiences water stress from very dry or over-watered soil, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo nu babaoo mli. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look soft and wilting during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During peak heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and usually bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves start turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for healthy leaf growth, or that waterlogged soil is drowning the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli lɛ.

english: Cowpeas and beans fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. When left in the ground, this nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ mli Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Tomatoes spoil rapidly after harvest due to high heat, humidity, and rough handling, which speed up rotting and bacteria growth. Storing them in well-ventilated crates in a cool, shaded area helps keep them fresh much longer.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ yɛ dɔlɛ, latsaa babaoo kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa hewɔ. ni haa fitemɔ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli mli yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my stored maize from insects eating it in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-nitoohe lɛ ahe?

english: Insects like weevils thrive on grains that contain moisture. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until it is hard before putting it into airtight storage bags starves the insects of air and moisture.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa dani akɛwoɔ vacuum kotoku mli. Ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ aje kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: What happens if I pack my harvested crop into bags while it is still a little damp?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ wo kotoku mli be mli ni edɔ fioo lolo lɛ?

english: Bagging damp crops creates a warm, humid environment where harmful mold grows rapidly. Mold ruins the quality of the crop, makes it unsafe to eat, and causes it to rot quickly.
ga: Nibii ni efɔ ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. he ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa oya lɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ ni ehaa egboɔ oya

english: Why do my cut plantains turn soft and yellow so fast after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ni mifo lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains naturally produce a gas that triggers fast ripening, especially when exposed to direct sunlight and heat. Keeping them under shade in a cool area delays this process.
ga: Kɛji akpa Plantains lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ekwɛɔ oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ miitswa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo hulutsoo shishi yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ lɛ, ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: How should I store my harvested yams so they do not rot before I sell them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yams need to be stored in a dry, well-ventilated raised barn away from direct sunlight. Keeping them off the ground and removing damaged ones prevents rot from spreading to healthy yams.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato ato ŋmɔ ko ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. He ni hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie hei ni efite lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is hot. Watering your crops early in the morning helps the roots absorb enough moisture before the midday heat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving tubers in the ground too long makes them hard, woody, and difficult to cook.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfee tamɔ tsei, ni ebaawa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding compost or appropriate fertilizer supplies the nutrients needed for healthy yields.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba.

english: Bean flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, dry soil, or poor nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and rich in organic matter helps the plant retain its blooms.
ga: Pea fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant vegetables between my main food crops to grow extra food for my house?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ mi niyenii titri ni miduɔ lɛ ateŋ koni mikɛdu nibii ni akɛfataa he kɛha mishia lɛ?

english: Yes, growing fast-yielding vegetables like okra between main crops helps produce extra food for your household, provided you leave enough space so they do not compete for sunlight and water.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ odu aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra yɛ onibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii krokomɛi aba oshiabii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji akɛ oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkaye hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight without protection. Shade trees protect them from sunburn, keep the soil moist, and protect them from strong winds during their early growth stage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and grow well, so you may need to add organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: How does putting dried leaves around the base of my crops help them stay alive in the dry season?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dried leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and keeps the soil cool and moist for root growth.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits in the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots and promotes fungal growth, causing the tubers to decay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat, stress, or lack of water during the flowering stage. When weather conditions are too harsh, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, haomɔ, loo nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars chew small holes through my young corn leaves during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ bu bibii lɛ? Kɛtsɔ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which thrive in warm weather and attack young corn leaves. They hide deep inside the growing center of the plant and feed on new leaves if not controlled early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛtutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: What will happen if I plant my crops too close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak, thin plants that produce smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ baa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows specialized pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my cultivated crops after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local environment, allowing them to absorb moisture and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crop varieties.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why should I plant my maize seeds in neat straight rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each seed enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow fully without competing. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my bean leaves fold and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean plants fold their leaves in the heat of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water and to shield themselves from intense sun damage. They will usually bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Bean tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa ni fiteɔ nii lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my yam vine turning brown and dying off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: When a yam plant reaches full maturity, it stops growing top leaves and sends all its remaining energy down into the ground. The vine dying back is a natural sign that the tuber underneath is fully formed and ready to dig up.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ekpaa ŋwɛi baai lɛ adalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Wein tsei ni miigboi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ etsɔ amɛhe kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer, or that heavy rains have waterlogged the soil so the plant's roots cannot breathe properly to absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ miinɛ waa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewoɔ nu. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, inconsistent watering, or a lack of plant nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ko he, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo tso mli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ

english: Why do some of my cassava roots taste bitter after I cook them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifã lɛ ŋɔɔ kɛji ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava produces natural defense chemicals that taste bitter when the plant goes through long periods of drought or is harvested too late. Consistent rainwater and harvesting on time keep the roots soft and sweet.
ga: Cassava feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni mli edɔ waa kɛ́ tso lɛ ye hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during the rainy season when humidity is high and there is too much shade around the cocoa branches.
ga: Hela ni ji black pod lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ gangrene nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Ni hulutsoo babaoo yɛ kookoo niji lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up into small, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sucking pests like whiteflies or aphids, which feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛyeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni haaa baa lɛ adara lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do I find holes and small caterpillars inside the growing tips of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii? Yɛ mi ŋmãa nine bibioo lɛ naagbee mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest whose caterpillars burrow into the central leaves of young corn plants to feed on the tender tissue.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni etsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding results in thin, weak stalks and very small corn cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant immediately, your seeds might sprout but then dry up and die before the regular rainy season fully begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ be ni baa daa lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, a vital plant food. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to its newer upper leaves, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei niyenii ni he hiaa Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high off the ground to catch sunlight, which allows the plant to produce food and grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii ni amɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack. You can gently dig up one tuber to check if it has reached a good size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ Ofo tuber kome fiofio koni ona kɛji elɛɛmɔ sa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your vegetable bed.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha o-vegetables shikpɔji lɛ anɔ

english: Does leaving weeds around my cassava plants really reduce the size of my tubers?
ga: jwɛi ni ebɔleɔ ŋmei tso lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Ani ebaanyɛ eye ebua diɛŋtsɛ ni eba yitso lɛ dalɛ shi?

english: Yes, weeds act like thief plants that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crop. Removing weeds early gives your cassava full access to soil nutrients so it can grow large tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-cassava lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ bulb agboi.

english: What is causing small holes to appear in my tomato leaves and fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi tomato lɛ baai kɛ aduawai anɔ

english: Small holes are typically caused by insect pests like caterpillars or armyworms eating the crop. Spraying with organic mixtures like neem leaf extract or applying recommended bio-pesticides early will protect your leaves and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo asraafoi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ bu bibii baa. Akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu obaai kɛ oyibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to pour out and sun-dry my grain after harvesting instead of leaving it in the bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔse dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛgbi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ kotoku lɛ mli?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain hidden moisture. If you keep them in a bag wet, heat builds up, causing mold to grow and rotting the entire bag. Sun-drying removes this moisture so your harvest stays safe and clean.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛji okɛwo kotoku ni mli efɔ mli Dɔlɛ baabua ehe naa Enɛ haa ŋmeii daa ni ehaa kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ejieɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ koni onibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛhe atse.

english: How can I tell if my harvested crops are dry enough to be stored safely in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto kotokui amli shweshweeshwe?

english: You can test dry grain by biting a seed with your front teeth. If it makes a sharp cracking sound without bending or feeling soft, it is fully dry and ready for safe storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni okɛ ohiɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakpa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ gbee ni naa wa ko ni tswaa ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ebɛ blɛoo lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ egbi kwraa ni efee klalo akɛ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my bag of grain become lighter after I spread it out to dry in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã kotoku lɛ mli shwie shi beni mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Crops hold water inside them when harvested. When you dry them in the sun, the water evaporates into the air. The grain gets lighter, but it becomes much stronger against rotting and pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ toɔ nu yɛ mli kɛ́ akpa amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo hulu lɛ mli Nu lɛ baaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ baafee mlɛo. Shi ebaawa babaoo yɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: What happens if I harvest my crops and store them in my room without drying them first?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛto tsu ko mli ni migbiko lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Wet crops stored in a dark room will heat up, turn black, develop mold, and attract insects within a few days. You will end up losing most of your harvest to decay.
ga: Nibii ni efɔ ni akɛto tsu ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ baadɔ. Etsɔɔ ediŋŋ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Obaafite onibii babaoo koni egbo.

english: How can I produce enough crops from my farm to fill more than one bag during harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni manyɛ mawo kotoku ni fe ekome mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: To harvest more bags, give your crops enough space when planting, apply fertilizer at the right growing stages, and control weeds early so the plants can produce bigger, heavier grains.
ga: Koni akpa baagi babaoo Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdu. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa ni edaa lɛ mli. ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do market buyers offer lower prices for my bags of harvested crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi-baagi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Buyers pay less if your crops contain dirt, wet grains, or broken seeds. Cleaning your crop properly and drying it thoroughly ensures you get the maximum value and price per bag.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji akɛ onibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ. dumɔwui ni efɔ loo ni ekumɔ, ni oootsumɔ oŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onine shɛɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ kɛ jara ni akɛwoɔ kotoku kome mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to just sweep my harvested grain off the bare ground after threshing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaashwie ŋmaa ni akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sweeping grain directly off bare ground mixes dirt, small stones, and sand into your crop. This lowers the quality, makes it unsafe to eat, and reduces the price buyers will pay.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha muji, tɛi bibii, kɛ ŋã afutu onibii amli. ni haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi Ehaa niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa jara ni esa akɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ awo lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I store my crop immediately after a machine processes it?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni tsɔne lɛ etsu he nii?

english: No, harvesting or threshing machines only separate the grain from the husks or stalks; they do not dry the crop. You must still pour the grains out in the sun to dry before bagging them.
ga: Dabi, nikpalɔ loo ŋmaakpalɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa loo ŋmaa lɛ mli pɛ. Amɛhaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmaa lɛ ashwie shi koni egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli dani okɛwo kotoku mli.

english: How do processing machines help me during harvest time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Machines quickly strip grains from husks or pods, saving you hours of manual labor and helping you process large harvests faster before rain or pests damage them in the field.
ga: Mashiŋ lɛ gbalaa dumɔwui lɛ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii lɛ baa. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ ŋmaa wuji ahe nii oya dani nugbɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What causes mold to grow on my crops right after I gather them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mibua amɛnaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mold grows because wet crops trapped in warm piles create damp heat. Air cannot move through a tight pile of wet crops, making it easy for mold fungi to grow quickly.
ga: Fungi lɛ daa ejaakɛ tsei ni efɔ ni amɔmɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei ni efɔ lɛ ni abua naa lɛ mli. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baakwɛ̃ oya

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding balanced fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores nitrogen to the soil, turning leaves green and helping the plants grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer is concentrated like salt, and direct contact can burn the stem and kill the plant. Placing it in a small ring around the plant, where the leaves end, allows the underground roots to drink it safely.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle ehe tamɔ ŋoo. Ni kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ. Ni akɛ amɛ baawo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli ni bɔle tso lɛ he yɛ he ni baai lɛ naagbee yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ anu.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my land after harvesting a maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Groundnuts put vital nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Curling and pale leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by small whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems prevents whiteflies from destroying your crop yield.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni hiɛɔ lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii yɛŋ naa koni amɛkafite onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars show up on my cabbage right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warm, humid rain creates perfect conditions for moths to lay eggs under leaves, which quickly hatch into hungry caterpillars. Checking leaf undersides regularly helps catch them before they eat your crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ baai ashishi. ni baatsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant many maize seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ yɔɔ srɔto lɛ? Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛaato bu kome mli lɛ ehiii.

english: When seeds grow too close together, they fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each stem develops a thick stalk and produces full, large corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa wuji baa.

english: Why does removing weeds early make my crops grow so much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all soil nutrients go directly to growing your crops instead of wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe koo mli tsei.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without turning into fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop blossoms to save water and energy. Mulching around the base keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture, helping blossoms form tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Mulching around Cones lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ

english: How can I tell underground yam tubers are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam vines and leaves naturally yellow and dry up when the tubers finish growing. This signals that the plant has stored all its energy underground and the yams are ready to dig up.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ eda. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni yams lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni awo mli ŋmãa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen. This happens if heavy rain washes the fertilizer away, if the fertilizer was applied incorrectly, or if the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli jogbaŋŋ Aloo kɛji akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture, helping young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing big yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach sunlight instead of growing strong stems and thick fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu lɛ, moŋ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni mli tse.

english: Why did the seeds I bought from the market fail to sprout after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were stored in high heat or damp conditions before sale, if they are too old, or if they are poor quality. They can also fail if the soil was too dry or flooded right after planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni latsaa waa loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli dani ahɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo amɛhe ehiii Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Why does the certified maize seed give a better harvest than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwu ni awo he odase lɛ haa ŋmaa kpakpa fe midumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and dry conditions while producing uniform, high yields. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni fa babaoo baa. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does my land produce lower yields every time I plant cassava on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the ground time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than planted crops, so they steal most of the water, fertilizer, and sunlight in the soil, leaving your crops starving for nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaf curling is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The disease stops leaves from trapping sunlight properly, preventing the tubers underground from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden heavy soaking of water or rain after a dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. Clearing tall trees leaves them exposed to heat, so intercropping with plantains or leaving shade trees keeps the soil cool and protects cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei kakadaji ni afoɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulutsoo. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui duɔ loo ni ashiɔ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi kookoo baai lɛ ashãa.

english: Does it really make a difference if I don't put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ebaaha srɔtofeemɔ aba diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ efɔɔɔ shi?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground to prevent rot and helps the plant capture sunlight, producing much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baajie tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni akafite ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hulu la. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more from my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ mihe bibioo lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This causes thin, weak stalks that produce small ears or no grain at all.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa aahu akɛ toi lɛ feɔ bibii loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: How do weeds affect my pepper plants even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from crop roots. Clearing weeds early ensures all nutrients go into making pepper plants bushier and higher-yielding.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa koni eha pepper tsei lɛ aná deka ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves, but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of roots. Balancing nutrients ensures the plant directs food into swelling the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi. Niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eŋɔ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Can I apply fresh chicken manure directly to my crops as soon as I clean out the coop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji mitsumɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too hot and strong, which can burn plant roots. Leaving it to rot and dry in a compost heap for a few weeks makes it safe and nutrient-rich for crops.
ga: Kokoo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbo ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: I found small caterpillars inside the central leaves of my young maize; why are they destroying the crop so quickly?
ga: Miyana ŋmei bibioo ko. Eyɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Mɛni hewɔ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya nakai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which feed directly on the growing center of maize plants. Because they multiply fast and eat constantly, early detection and control are required to protect the yield.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ nii daa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ana ni akudɔ mra. koni akɛbu nibii ni adu lɛ ahe

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants look crumpled with yellow patches, and how does it spread?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ, ni te amɛfeɔ tɛŋŋ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by planting infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this spread.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout properly if I plant right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain only wets the top layer of dirt, leaving hot, dry soil underneath. Seeds need consistent soil moisture to germinate, or the heat kills tender roots before major rains settle in.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbi yɛ shishi. Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Aloo latsaa lɛ baafite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba.

english: Why do flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil consistently moist and protecting roots helps plants hold flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around young cocoa acts like an umbrella, providing the cool shade and moisture the cocoa needs until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo lɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ kɛyashi ebaashɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Excess rain and damp air cause a fungal disease called Black Pod. When bushes are overgrown or shade is too thick, air cannot dry the pods after rain, allowing the fungus to spread and turn the pods black.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods baa. Beni jwɛi lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ agbi pods lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay small and pale green even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants turn pale green and stay small when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build strong stems and green leaves. Regular water is not enough if the soil itself does not have nutrients from manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Nu folo pɛ faaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli, ŋmɔshi nibii amli, loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil during growth. Groundnuts and beans are special because they take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring richness for the next crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii ji nɔ krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. Spacing them properly ensures every plant has enough room to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the early rains are irregular?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ jeee nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ?

english: Seeds need continuous soil moisture to germinate and survive. It is safest to wait until the rains become steady rather than planting after just one quick shower, which can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up under the returning heat.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ke o nu nu si kake pɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi yɛ la ni miiku esɛɛ eba lɛ shishi.

english: Why do tiny holes keep appearing on my cowpea leaves during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Holes in leaves are caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles and caterpillars that feed on soft foliage. Using natural pest sprays like neem water early in the morning helps repel these pests before they eat too much of the leaf.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem nu wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshwie kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛye baai babaoo.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer. Keeping the soil damp around the base with organic mulch helps maintain cooler temperatures so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛ organic mulch haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my yam sprouts after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmeii ni shwereɔ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to take immediate advantage of cleared soil, sunlight, and early rain. Removing them early gives your cultivated crop like yam a fair chance to establish its root system without competing for survival.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni aheee nɔ ko, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ atsu nii. Jiemɔ amɛ mra. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkɛto shishifãi ahe gbɛjianɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I cut off the extra low branches near the dirt on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishi titri yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing the lower leaves prevents dirt from splashing onto the plant during rains, which stops soil diseases from spreading. It also forces the tomato plant to send its food and energy into growing bigger fruits at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ebaatsi muji ni shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. Enyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ hu koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ amaje aduawai wuji ni miida yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil is short on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build strong stalks. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or strong dry winds. Keeping the soil moist and applying mulch around the roots cools the plant down so the flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ koni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ awo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems too close together causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving them proper space allows the roots room to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa shishifã tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts on land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, which helps replenish and heal soil that was made tired by heavy feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ mli woɔ la ekoŋŋ ni etsaa lɛ.

english: What fast crops can I plant to make money while waiting for my oil palm tree plantation to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu oya koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi-oil palm ŋmɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like maize, watermelons, or tomatoes produce harvests within three to four months, providing regular cash flow while your long-term tree crops grow over several years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, watermelon, loo tomato woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa shika ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa be mli ni otsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ daraa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when planted under heavy shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains need direct sunlight to make food for fast growth. Deep shade starves the plant of light energy, slowing down leaf growth and delaying fruit production.
