ga: Hulu la he miihia plantains tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara oya. Shade ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aye la hewalɛ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ baa sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do tiny holes appear on my pepper leaves, and does it hurt my final yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi pepper baai lɛ anɔ Ni ani enaa mi naagbee nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Holes on leaves are made by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating the leaf tissue. Since leaves act like food factories for the plant, losing leaf area means fewer and smaller peppers at harvest time.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa mli fãji lɛ kɛ bu yɛ baa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe lɛ. Baai lɛ ahe ni elaaje lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ baaba yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Do I really need to stake my yam vines, or can I just let them spread on the ground?
ga: Ehe miihia waa ni mafolɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli. Aloo manyɛ maha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking holds yam vines up so the leaves can catch direct sunlight while keeping them off wet soil where fungal diseases spread. Sunshine on staked leaves helps the underground tubers grow much larger.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ baawo tso lɛ nɔ koni tso lɛ yibii lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni ehi shi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: How do I know my sweet potatoes are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the vines start turning yellow and drying up, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack slightly from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo beni wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa fioo kɛjɛɔ bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my cocoa seedlings stunt their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ miitsi amɛdalɛ naa.

english: Weeds grow faster than young cocoa trees and steal water, light, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing a circle around young cocoa trees ensures the tree gets all the food it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, kane kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ŋwɛibɔfoi ni afoɔ abɔleɔ Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I start my tomato seeds in a small nursery box instead of planting them straight into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Young crop seedlings are delicate like babies and easily die from harsh direct sun, heavy rains, or pests. A sheltered nursery allows you to protect, water, and care for them until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii ni hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbeɔ amɛ oya. He ni akwɛɔ kooloi yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe, ohaa amɛ nu, ni okwɛɔ amɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: When my seedlings are ready in the nursery, can I move them straight into full sunlight, or do I need to prepare them first?
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ Ani abaanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛya he ko ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo esa akɛ masaa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Seedlings get shocked if moved suddenly from shade to burning sun. You should slowly expose them to outdoor sunlight for a few hours each day over a week so they get used to the heat before final planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakpokpo kɛji trukaa lɛ amɛshi hulutsoo be mli kɛtee hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli fiofio yɛ kpo nɔ. ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi daa gbi yɛ otsi kome mli Enɛ ji koni amɛtsɔse amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli dani amɛdu naagbee.

english: What is the best time of day for me to transplant my young crops into the main farm field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to transplant seedlings in the cool late afternoon or on a cloudy day so the heat of the sun does not dry out their roots and stress the young plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shwane ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli loo gbi ni atatu ewo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shishifãi lɛ ni ekɛhao tso bibioo lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together in the field, why do the crops grow thin and produce small ears?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for limited nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. This struggle leaves all the plants weak and poorly fed.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ nɔmɔ nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why are weeds so harmful to my young cassava plants during their first few weeks in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ awui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and light that your cassava needs to build strong stems and big roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ la ni he hiaa o-cassava lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ shishifãi wuji.

english: How do I know if my crops are struggling to get enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops do not get enough plant food from the soil, their leaves turn pale green or yellow, their growth slows down, and their stems stay very thin.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ tse niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. ni tso lɛ mli tse waa

english: Why do my young cocoa shoots wither and dry up so quickly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa shoots have short roots that cannot reach deep groundwater yet. High sun heat dries out their leaves faster than their small roots can drink water from the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. koni enyɛ enu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How often should I water my crop nursery during the dry season to keep the young plants healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Nursery seedlings need light watering once in the early morning and once in the cool evening so the soil stays gently moist without soaking the roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ nu fioo leebi maŋkpa, ni afɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around young crops with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from baking the ground, keeps moisture in the soil, and protects the young roots from heat.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he

english: Why should I remove temporary shade fronds from over my crops once they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie be kukuoo mli baai kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Once young crops develop deep roots and strong leaves, they need full sunlight to make their own food and grow high-yielding fruit.
ga: Beni tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli wa lɛ Amɛhe miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I test if the new seeds I received are healthy enough to sprout before I plant them all?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui heei ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ dani madu amɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a quick germination test by placing 10 seeds on a moist cloth or paper towel in a warm place. After 3 to 5 days, count how many have sprouted; if 8 or more sprout, the seed batch is healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛbaawo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo toilet wolo yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ Gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ lɛ, kanemɔ yibɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ mli wa ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow while others sprout right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems must be planted with the growth buds pointing upwards towards the sky. If you plant the stem upside down or use dry, woody stems from the very bottom or top of the plant, they will not sprout properly.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishigbɛ loo okɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni egbi ni jɛ tso lɛ shishi loo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets excessively hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if small pests damage the blooms. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow thin and bent instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Mohu ɔ, sweet potato ɔ mi tsɔwi ɔmɛ agbo nɛ a ngɛ tsɔ.

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil underneath them is packed hard or filled with stones. Making high, soft soil mounds or ridges allows the yam root to expand smoothly downwards without hitting hard obstacles.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni amɛtswaaa gbɛtsii nii ni wa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa moist and protected during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crop actually slow down my farm's growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. When weeds surround your crop, the crop starves and grows thin and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbaafee bibioo ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants full of small holes and ragged edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋwɛigbɛi ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Small chewed holes in the center whorl of maize are usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm hiding inside. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts early prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ŋmɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akafite tip ni miida lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛya. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛji akɛ atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens inside the soil to my seeds if a long dry spell comes right after planting?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ba yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ?

english: When seeds absorb initial moisture, they start the process of waking up and sprouting. If the soil dries out completely before the root penetrates deep, the fragile sprout inside the seed dries up and dies before reaching the surface.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwu lɛ ŋɔ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaje gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛteɔ shi ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa dani shishifãi lɛ bote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Fragile seedlings ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa gives them living umbrellas that block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aná hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which eat the growing centers of maize plants. You can control them early by applying approved pesticides or dropping clean dry sand or wood ash into the leaf whorls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ he ni ŋmãa tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ ŋã ni he tse, ni egbi loo tso sũ awo baai lɛ amli.

english: Cassava rot happens when water settles around the roots in heavy or flat soil during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava fitemɔ baa kɛji nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas on the same land where I just harvested my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but legumes like cowpeas fix nitrogen back into the soil naturally. Rotating them helps restore soil fertility so your next crop grows strong without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛsaa nitrogen lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni okɛbaatsake lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding lime or organic manure helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and making the whole plant stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly spread by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids feeding on the sap. Using organic neem oil sprays early on keeps these pests away and stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Organic neem oil spray ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow around one main plantain stem?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe? trunk wulu kome

english: You should limit it to 2 or 3 suckers of different heights per main stem. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients, which results in smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ohe awo suction cups 2 loo 3 ni kɛlɛ ji srɔtoi yɛ tso titri kome mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii babaoo shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛwuu koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves into the sunlight. When leaves get plenty of light, they create more energy, which fuels the growth of larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. ni ji tsofa ni haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daa lɛ

english: Is it better to clear weeds from my farm when my crops are small or wait until the crops grow tall?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ loo mamɛ ni tsei lɛ adara?

english: It is best to weed early within the first few weeks after planting. Young crops are weak and will lose the fight against weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food if weeds are left to grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafite ta ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi lɛ ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall with pale leaves but produce very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa kɛ baa ni tsuɔ shi ewoɔ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually means your soil is missing essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or the plants were sown too close together. Giving plants enough space and applying NPK fertilizer at the right time helps produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kɛji akɛ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Should I plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is usually better to wait until the rains become consistent. The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can scorch fragile new seedlings before their roots are established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni bɛ hewalɛ dani shishifãi lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground has too much water, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when the crop is under stress from high heat, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: What happens if I harvest my cocoa pods before they turn fully yellow?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii dani amɛ fɛɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Harvesting cocoa pods too early means the beans inside will not ferment properly, leading to poor flavor, lower bean quality, and a reduced price at the buying shed.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baa shi ni jara ni yɔɔ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ baa shi

english: How do I keep my dried maize safe from weevils while I store it for a few months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehiɔ shi nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Maize must be dried completely until the kernels are hard, then stored in sealed, airtight bags or treated with approved storage dust in a cool, dry storehouse.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kwraa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto vacuum kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli. Aloo kɛ sũ nitoohe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ nitoohe ni mli ejɔ ni egbi atsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when left unharvested during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni kwɛɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil pushes out oxygen, causing waterlogged conditions that allow soil fungi to attack and rot the mature cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Enɛ haa nu ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cowpea farm produce plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the crop put all its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of forming flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do my plantain suckers dry up quickly after I transplant them into my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Transplanted suckers lose part of their root system during digging, so direct sunlight dries them out before new roots can absorb water from the ground.
ga: Suckers ni adu lɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fã ko laajeɔ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha amɛgbi dani shishifãi heei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell underground yam tubers are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines on top stop growing, turn completely yellow, and begin to dry up naturally.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛji baai kɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kpa dalɛ. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa ni ebɔi gbimɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Leaf curling is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or it can be the plant reacting to severe heat and dry conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo ebaanyɛ efee akɛ tso lɛ feɔ enii waa kɛji edɔ kɛ egbi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil is lacking nitrogen, which the plant needs to build strong stems and healthy green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's life will restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni esa akɛ tsei lɛ aná tsei ni wa kɛ baai ni wa, ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on the soil and uses up most of its nitrogen. Legume crops like groundnuts or beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop you plant.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii babaoo ni ekɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii babaoo. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight during their first couple of years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler environment and protects the young cocoa trees from burning until they are mature enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off during the hot dry season without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: High heat and lack of water cause severe stress to tomato plants, leading them to drop their flowers to save energy. Watering your plants consistently at the soil level early in the morning helps maintain soil moisture and keeps the flowers intact to form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛkafite hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same line?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water and fertilizer, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. This competition results in tall, thin plants that produce tiny ears or no grain at all.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ ŋmãa kome. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee aahu akɛ amɛyɛ toi bibii loo amɛbɛ dumɔwui kwraa.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into high mounds before planting my yam sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ato dani odu ŋmɔshi nibii akuu ko lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil so they can easily expand downwards and sideways as they grow. Making high mounds loosens compacted soil, improves water drainage to prevent rot, and gives the tubers space to grow long and thick.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shishi kɛ amɛsɛɛ oya beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akafite. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small wrinkled shapes and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips that feed on sap and transmit viruses. Spraying the underside of the leaves with recommended organic or chemical insecticides early prevents these insects from spreading the condition.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã shihilɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Muji ni ashɛre kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing stem of the maize plant to feed. Applying targeted pest control into the plant funnel as soon as you spot early damage will kill the worms and save your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli koni amɛye niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awo tsei ahe kɛji ona nɔ ni efite mra pɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ ni ehere onibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, which is usually indicated by the lower leaves turning yellow and naturally falling off. You can test maturity by carefully digging around one representative stem to inspect tuber size before harvesting the full plot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kadiɔ enɛ. Obaanyɛ oka dalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni oookwɛ bɔ ni bulb lɛ da ha dani okpa shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow on my field cause my crops to give a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal the fertilizer, moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early in the crop cycle ensures all available soil nutrients go directly into growing your produce.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa akwɛɔ koni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛkwɛ onibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade from nurse crops like plantains during their early stages to protect them and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ shishijee mli koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall green stems and big leaves but only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is heavily compacted, the cassava plant directs all its food and energy into leaf and stem growth instead of expanding its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering, which prevents the flowers from pollinating properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii titri lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is stressed from lack of water during the day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-corn lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni faaa yɛ emli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water, their leaves roll tightly inward like narrow tubes during the hottest part of the day to prevent water loss.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ kɛyaa mli tamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni nu lɛ akafite.

english: Crowding forces plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and thin instead of building strong stems and roots.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená tsei kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my rows of maize help my main crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpea plants take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize while covering the ground to reduce weeds.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa jwɛi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and turn hard during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that suck the sap from the underside of leaves, causing them to warp and stunt crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ srɔtoi ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to provide wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa tso ko kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to make energy, which flows down to build large underground tubers while keeping leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni ekɛfee hewalɛ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ready for harvesting when they are hidden under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and drying, and the inside of the harvested seed pods turns dark or brownish when shelled.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛji ajie amɛhe.

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were stored in warm or humid places that destroyed their viability, planted too deep in the soil, or eaten by insects before sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo loo fɛ̃i mli, ni fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashihilɛ. Adu kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ. aloo kooloi ye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shelter and holds soil moisture during hot months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture after the early rains to plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Dig down about a hand's depth into the soil; if the earth forms a moist ball when squeezed without dripping water, it is safe to plant. Planting too early after a brief rain can cause seeds to dry out if a heat wave follows.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee nine kome mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fee bɔɔlu ni mli efɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ ni nu ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli. Abaanyɛ adu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji latsaa ko nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores green color and helps the crop grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do neighboring farmers tell me to plant cowpeas in the same field with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural feeding enriches the soil, helping the surrounding maize grow better without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa babaoo.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my corn leaves and white powder inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central leaf whorl and feeds on young leaves. Spraying early with neem extract or recommended organic controls kills caterpillars before severe damage occurs.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem mli nu lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Aloo, tsofai ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni agbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Leaf twisting is caused by a plant virus transmitted by tiny insect pests like whiteflies and mites. Controlling these insect pests early and pulling up badly infected plants keeps the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies kɛ mites kɛ baa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of underground roots. Proper plant spacing ensures energy goes into expanding the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa hewalɛ yaa bulbs ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become excessively high or when water supply is uneven. Keeping soil consistently moist and applying straw mulch cools root zones and helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ jwɛi wo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, space, and sunlight directly from crop roots. Clearing weeds during the crop's first few weeks prevents them from taking food away from your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ otsi klɛŋklɛŋ ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekajie niyenii kɛjɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my harvested maize inside my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay eggs inside stored maize kernels if the grain is not dried completely before storage. Drying maize thoroughly until seeds crack cleanly and storing grain in sealed airtight bags prevents insect destruction.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baatsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui wo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite nii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the crop the push it needs to grow strong and turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet quickly. When the plant gets stressed by these weather changes, it drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ oya waa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ha tsei hao lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛhere nu kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and stay small when the soil under them is too hard, compact, or full of stones. Building high, soft earth mounds with loose soil gives the yam tuber room to push straight down and expand easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato tuber room lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi tɛ̃ɛ. ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ mli oya

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei adu tsina loo ŋmei?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull free nitrogen out of the air and put it straight into the soil through their roots. This feeds the soil naturally, helping your cassava grow better while giving you a legume harvest while you wait for the cassava.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa bo ŋmeii be mli ni omɛɛɔ o-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from the high-yielding hybrid maize I harvested to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a great harvest only the first time they are planted. Seeds saved from that harvest will lose their special strength, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and weaker plants next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be pɛ ni adu amɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tight during the hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink the leaf area exposed to the sun, preventing them from losing precious water quickly in hot weather. However, if leaves stay curled even in the morning, tiny pests under the leaf might be sucking the sap.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ haaa nu ni jara wa lɛ afite oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi po. ŋmeii bibii Yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, abaanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the soil surface. When a heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the ground. Propping the main trunk with a strong bamboo pole helps carry the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua muji lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa pods are mature and ready for harvest when their color completely changes—usually turning from dark green to bright yellow, or from deep red to orange-yellow. Picking them at this stage ensures the seeds inside ferment properly into high-grade beans.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛtsake amɛhe su kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ. Kɛ́ ahala dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni no baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why do my cabbages grow big outer leaves but fail to form a hard head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji shi ebɛ shiŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to keep making wild outer leaves, or when temperatures are too hot during the head-forming stage.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli kponɔgbɛ baai aba. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ yitso lɛ feemɔ be mli lɛ.

english: Cassava usually matures between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Can I leave my cassava tubers in the ground past their normal harvest time if I am not ready to sell them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mifeee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ hu?

english: Yes, cassava can safely stay underground for several months as a form of natural storage, but leaving it too long can make the roots hard, woody, and less suitable for cooking or processing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee tamɔ tso, ni esaaa akɛ ahoɔ loo atsuɔ he nii.

english: Does the variety of cassava I plant affect whether it is better for pounding fresh fufu or making gari?
ga: Ani ŋmeii srɔtoi ni miduɔ lɛ náa fufu loo ghari hee ni mifeɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ babaoo?

english: Yes, cassava varieties with high starch and lower water content yield more flour and are best for processing into gari, while varieties with softer roots and higher moisture are easier to boil and pound into fresh fufu.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei henɔi ni mli ŋmei babaoo kɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo baa, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ ni akɛfeɔ gari. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ewaaa akɛ aaaho amɛ ni atswa amɛ ni amɛfee fufu hee.

english: Why do some of my harvested cassava roots taste bitter, and is it safe to boil and eat them fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ? Ni ani ehi akɛ aaahoo ni aye ŋmɔŋ?

english: Bitterness is caused by naturally occurring chemical compounds in the root. Highly bitter cassava varieties contain higher levels of these compounds and must be fermented or processed into gari or flour before they are safe to eat, rather than just boiled fresh.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. Cassava henɔi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ fa babaoo. Ni esa akɛ atsɔ mli loo afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ dani aye lɛ shweshweeshwe. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ahoo ehee

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and rotting just a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi duŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a thick protective skin like yams, so once removed from the ground, exposed tissue reacts rapidly with air and causes the root to spoil within 48 to 72 hours unless processed quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, fãji ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli ja atsu he nii oya.

english: Shedding leaves is a natural survival trick where the cassava plant conserves water during dry spells. Once the rains return, the plant will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and resume growing.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ teemɔŋ sane. Cassava tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava plants to grow tall with plenty of big leaves but produce very small roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava tso lɛ daa, ni eyɛ baai wuji waa, shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibii waa?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. The excess nitrogen forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding its roots below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbala amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut to use as planting material for my new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: The middle section of a healthy, mature stem makes the best planting material because it contains enough stored nutrients and mature buds to sprout quickly, unlike the soft top or old, woody bottom.
ga: Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yɛ ni ato ni ŋmeii ni eda lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Etamɔɔɔ tso bibioo loo tso momo ko shishi.

english: At what growth stage is weed control most critical for my young cassava farm?
ga: Jwɛi akudɔmɔ yɛ mɛɛ dalɛ be mli he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeding is most critical during the first three to four months after planting. Once the cassava grows tall and its leaf canopy covers the ground, it naturally shades out most weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ da ni baai lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ebaaha jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I plant legumes like cowpea alongside my young cassava stems, or will they steal nutrients from my cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ahe? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mi-cassava lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Intercropping young cassava with legumes like cowpeas actually helps your cassava because legumes capture nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil while shade-covering the ground to prevent weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa dudu ŋmãa bibii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua o ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shade koni ekɛbu he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together to try to get more crops on my small land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This makes the plants grow weak and thin, resulting in smaller harvests or no fruit at all.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fioo loo nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny without making big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Crops grow tall and thin when they are crowded together. They stretch upward to fight for sunlight instead of using their energy to develop strong stems and big, healthy cobs or fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛlɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ amɛyi obɔ kɛ amɛhe. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ tsei agboi loo aduawai ni wa ni amɛbaafee lɛ he.

english: How does the distance between my plants affect how much harvest I get in the end?
ga: Te gbɛ ni kã mi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ saa nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ naagbee lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food, air, and light to produce at its best. Having the correct spacing gives you the ideal number of healthy plants per acre, which maximizes your total yield.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ oyɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ayibɔ ni sa yɛ acre kome mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni oná nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ babaoo.

english: Can planting my crops too far apart reduce my total harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha minibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, if your plants are spread too far apart, you leave empty soil and sunlight wasted that weeds will use. Even if individual plants grow big, you will have too few plants on the land to get a large total harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ egbɛ eshwã amɛhe tsɔ. Obaafite shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni jwɛi baanyɛ afite lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso fɛɛ tso daa moŋ Shi nyɛ hu nyɛyɛ tsei fioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni nyɛnyɛŋ nyɛkpa babaoo.

english: Why do commercial farms that use tractor planters seem to have fuller fields than when I plant by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jarayeli ŋmɔji ni kɛ ŋmɔji tsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni da fe be mli ni mikɛ minine duɔ lɛ?

english: Planting machines place seeds at the exact same depth and distance every time, which helps almost all seeds germinate successfully. Planting by hand often leads to uneven depth, leaving empty gaps where seeds fail to grow.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ niji du nii lɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ mli kwɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Enɛ haa gbɛ ko baa he ni dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Will using a simple planting tool or machine help me get a better yield than my hoe and cutlass?
ga: Ani nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha maná yibii kpakpai fe tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii?

english: Yes, planting tools improve seed placement and soil contact, ensuring more of your seeds sprout into healthy plants. This keeps your plant population high and reduces wasted space on your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛbaashɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa he ni afiteɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Does planting my crops in straight lines actually help them grow better?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Straight lines ensure every crop receives an equal share of sunlight and ground space. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and walking through your farm much easier without accidentally damaging plants.
ga: Linei ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kome. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee tsei yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do many of the seeds I plant fail to come up, leaving empty patches across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ? Ani ekɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come up if they are planted too deep, left too near the dry surface, or eaten by insects. Poor seed placement leads to a low plant population, meaning fewer crops reach maturity.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ashi ni egbi tsɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. loo kooloi ŋmɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ehiii lɛ haa tsei ayibɔ baa shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni edaaa kwraa.

english: Why does my neighbor get twice as many bags of maize as me when our farms are the same size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa ŋmãa kotokui ni fa fe mi lɛ shii enyɔ be mli ni wɔŋmɔji lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Your neighbor likely achieved a higher plant population by planting efficiently with fewer empty gaps. More healthy plants surviving per acre directly leads to more bags harvested from the same land size.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ baaná tsei ayibɔ ni yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni amɛbaadu jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni hiɔ shi yɛ acre kome mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akpa kotokui babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: How do I know if I have enough crops growing on my one acre of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 lɛ nɔ?

english: Every crop has a recommended number of plants that should grow on an acre. You can check by counting the living plants in a small section of your field to see if you have met the right population target for a full harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsei ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ adu yɛ acre kome nɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ he bibioo ko lɛ akanemɔ nɔ. ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ona kɛji oshɛ gbɔmɛi ayibɔ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he.

english: Do I need to clear every single tree from my forest land before I start planting my crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie tso fɛɛ tso kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: No, completely clearing everything is not necessary and can harm your land. Removing only selected trees gives your crops room to grow while leaving enough forest cover so the land can recover and stay productive.
ga: Dabi, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa ni ebaanyɛ eye oshikpɔŋ lɛ awui. Tsei ni ahala pɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa koo mli he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ehi shi ni ewo yibii.

english: Is there a safe way to remove large trees without destroying the surrounding forest on my land?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni aaatsɔ nɔ ajie tsei wuji ni akpataaa koo ni ebɔle mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ hiɛ?

english: Yes, using controlled methods or machines to selectively remove specific trees allows you to create space for your crops while keeping enough forest structure intact so the land does not get degraded.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛi ni akudɔɔ loo tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhalaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi lɛ haa onyɛɔ ofeɔ gbɛ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ kooi amli bɔ ni sa nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Can forest land recover on its own after I prepare it for farming?
ga: Ani kooi amli hei baanyɛ aya hiɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni asaa amɛhe kɛha okwaayeli sɛɛ?

english: Forest land can recover well if you practice selective clearing instead of removing everything. Keeping some trees allows the natural environment to bounce back while you cultivate your crops.
ga: Kooi amli hei baanyɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe wo nibii ni ohalaa lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ooojie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ. Otsei lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo be mli ni oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my farm land feel so hot and dry after I cut down all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbi beni mifo tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you cut down all the big trees, there is no shade left to block direct sunlight. The intense sun bakes the bare ground, raising the temperature significantly and drying out the soil.
ga: Beni ofoɔ tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ Shade ko bɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee efolo. ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbiɔ

english: Why are my young crops struggling under the full open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young crops struggle when exposed to direct, unfiltered sunlight without tree cover. Keeping a balanced amount of natural tree shade reduces extreme heat and protects your crops from burning.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei bɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni ja lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: How do forest trees help lower the temperature on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni hulutsoo be aba shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Forest trees act like large natural umbrellas. Their leaves block direct sunlight from hitting the bare ground, keeping the soil cool and retaining moisture for your crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ agbo ko. Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does clearing all vegetation make the heat so severe on my plot during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tree leaves absorb and filter a massive amount of solar radiation. When you clear all vegetation, there is no barrier left, causing direct sunlight to heat up the land severely.
ga: Tsei ahe baai gbalaa hulu la babaoo ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛji ojie tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, gbɛtsii nii ko eshwɛɛɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ waa.

english: How can I prevent my farm land from becoming completely damaged and useless after a few seasons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nibii ni midu lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kwraa ni amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: You can protect your land by avoiding total clearing. Leaving strategic forest trees prevents extreme soil heating and erosion, allowing the land to continuously recover its strength.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni oootsi ohe kwraa lɛ nɔ. Koo mli tsei ni he hiaa waa lɛ ni aaashi lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: What causes farm land in forest areas to lose its quality so fast after clearing?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaayeli shikpɔji ni yɔɔ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Clearing all trees exposes the soil directly to intense heat and weather, which destroys soil structure and nutrients. Selective clearing keeps the land protected and fertile for longer.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa tɛ̃ɛ. ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ahalaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Will leaving some forest trees on my farm benefit my crops in the long run?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná he sɛɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, leaving selected trees protects your soil from scorching heat and prevents land loss, ensuring your farm remains healthy and productive over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oshi tsei ni ahala lɛ ni abu he lɛ, ebaabu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny ears when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow strong stalks and produce large ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds bought from agri-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Many modern certified seeds are special hybrids bred for high yield in their first generation. When you save and replant seeds from a harvest, those high-yielding traits break down, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Beni okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni oduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Nakai sui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my crops give less yield when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ foɔ daa be, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ aba. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after my seeds germinate before applying fertilizer instead of putting it right next to the seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani mikɛ amɛ awo mli moŋ fe ni mikɛbaawo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against a tender seed can burn and kill the young shoot as it tries to sprout. Waiting until the seedling has established roots allows the plant to safely absorb nutrients and grow fast.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni egbe ŋmeii bibii lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ mɛɔ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ etswa shishifãi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eŋɔɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe ni edaa oya.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the leaves at the top of my young maize plants and eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on tender growth, and can be controlled using early detection and recommended organic or chemical sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (whorls) koni amɛye ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ. Ni abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ mra be mli nibii ni ana lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by planting infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava stem varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this issue.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ yɛ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the day even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually Bacterial Wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks the plant's internal tubes so water cannot reach the leaves. Once present in the soil, planting resistant crop varieties or rotating with grass crops helps reduce the problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ tsei amli paipii lɛ anaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bɔni afee ni nu akashɛ baai lɛ ahe Kɛji ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shikome lɛ Tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nii lɛ adumɔ loo jwɛi tsei ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni naagba lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees on new farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi miidu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily damaged by intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture to protect the young cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing their flowers to dry up and fall off before fruit can set. Providing light shade or maintaining consistent soil moisture during hot spells helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be fioo ha loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on to produce large tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food, which is then stored underground in the tuber. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and off the wet soil where diseases can easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ yitso lɛ mli Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ la he ni ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off, or abort, when the plant feels too much stress from excessive heat, dry soil, or improper feeding. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkpaa shi kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ hulutsoo babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa ha lɛ lɛ haoɔ waa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my tomato plants bloom with plenty of flowers but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers need proper pollination from wind or insects to turn into fruit. If it is too hot, too wet, or if there are no insects around to shake the pollen, the flower cannot form fruit and will fall off.
ga: Fɔfɔi biɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi atsɔ amɛmli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo kɛji kooloi komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ otsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ, ewooo yibii ni ebaagbee shi.

english: How can I stop my crop flowers from dropping off during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your crop flowers by watering early in the morning, putting dry grass around the base of the plant (mulching) to trap soil moisture, and ensuring the plants are not starved of nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu fɔfɔi ni odu lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha amɛ leebi lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi abɔle tso lɛ shishi (mulch) he koni ekɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. ni okwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ akashɛ tsei lɛ ahe

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that heavy water is sitting at the roots and suffocating them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ. Aloo muji ko yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to save water, but usually recovers when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my crops to curl up and become sticky?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves are a sign of tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. They suck the juice out of the plant and leave behind a sticky liquid.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi. Amɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛ shĩɔ nu ni kpɛtɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Can heavy rainfall cause my crops to lose their flowers?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ afite?

english: Yes, heavy rainfall can physically knock delicate flowers off the stem and wash away fertilizers in the soil, making the plant weak and unable to hold onto its blossoms.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ fɔfɔii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly during the long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara blɛoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Without enough water, crops cannot transport nutrients from the soil up into their stems and leaves, which slows down their overall growth and delays flowering.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ Dumɔwui hu nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why is it bad to put too much fertilizer on my flowering crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi fɔfɔi tsei lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ ehiii lɛ?
