english: Too much fertilizer, especially nitrogen, makes the plant produce plenty of big green leaves while forgetting to hold onto its flowers, causing the flowers to drop off.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo titri lɛ nitrogen Ha tso lɛ aná baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni ehiɛɔ nɔ akɛ etaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ, ni no haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Should I clear weeds from around my crops even when the crops have already flowered?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛmiifɔ fɔfɔi momo moŋ?

english: Yes, because weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops desperately need to feed their flowers and grow big fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni he hiaa onibii koni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai wuji akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, a vital nutrient. When the plant does not find enough food in the soil, it steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same farm with my maize make the soil richer for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have special bacteria on their roots. These roots pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil, providing free natural food for crops planted alongside or after them.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Shishifãi nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi loo yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ yaka

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny ears of corn when I plant many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo abele toi bibii lɛ? Kɛji oodu dumɔwui babaoo Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, all of them remain weak and produce smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why am I advised to cut off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, drink water and steal nutrients away from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii loo suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ baanu nu lɛ ni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant is stressed by hot dry winds, extreme afternoon heat, or irregular watering. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rain falls heavily for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil for days, oxygen is pushed out, causing the roots to suffocate and decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Akɛ oxygen lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot sun spell before the main rainy season starts. If your seeds sprout during this dry gap, the tender young roots will dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with dark droppings inside the growing tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that crawls deep into the center shoot of the maize plant to feed on tender new leaves before they open.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei dani amɛgbele.

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves with aggressive root systems. When you apply fertilizer, the weeds drink up the food faster than your crops can, starving your farm plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji julɔ ni daa oya ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa yɔɔ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baanu amɛ niyenii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I clear and prepare a piece of wild land before planting my crops for the first time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ mi koo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he dani madu mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: To start on fresh land, clear the bush, remove big roots and stumps, and loosen the topsoil with a hoe. Loosening the soil makes it soft enough for young roots to spread easily and reach water and food.
ga: Kɛha shishijee yɛ he hee Ha wɔjie jwɛi lɛ. Jiemɔ shishifãi wuji kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. ni okɛ shɔvel ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds so they grow healthy and strong?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa?

english: Plant maize with enough distance between rows and holes—usually about a arm's length between rows and a stride between plants. Proper spacing stops plants from shading each other and stealing water from nearby roots.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɛ ŋtayaai kɛ buji ateŋ—bei pii lɛ, ŋtayaai ateŋ aaafee nine kome kɛ ŋtayaai ateŋ ŋtayaa kome. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkaju nu kɛjɛ shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli.

english: How should I handle young pepper seedlings when removing them from the seedbed to plant on the main farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miyadu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Gently lift seedlings with a small clump of wet soil around their roots instead of pulling the bare stem. Transplanting them late in the afternoon prevents the hot sun from drying out and killing the delicate roots.
ga: Okɛ sũ bibioo ni mli efɔ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ awo dumɔwu lɛ nɔ blɛoo moŋ fe ni ooogbala tso lɛ shishifã lɛ. Kɛ́ atsake tso lɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa egbi ni efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why should I pull out extra seedlings if three or four sprout in the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui krokomɛi kɛji akɛ etɛ loo ejwɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔ bu kome mli?

english: When too many plants grow in one hole, they fight for food and stay small and weak. Removing the weaker ones leaves one strong plant that can produce full, large yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli Amɛyeɔ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Where exactly around my crop should I place fertilizer so I don't damage the plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli koni mikafite tsei lɛ?

english: Place fertilizer in a small hole or ring about a hand's width away from the plant stem, then cover it with soil. Putting it directly against the stem will burn the plant, while placing it too far makes it hard for roots to reach.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu bibii lɛ amli. loo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee ŋmei kome kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ashã. Shi kɛ́ akɛwo shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaashɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that create a living umbrella, giving the cocoa trees shade and moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to turn pale yellow and grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they suck up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛmuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking holds tomato stems off the ground so heavy fruits do not lie on wet dirt. Keeping leaves and fruit off the bare soil prevents rots and diseases from destroying your harvest.
ga: Staking haa tomato tsei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni aduawai lɛ akatsi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛ aduawai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite kɛ helai. Kpatamɔ onibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs extra plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei niyenii krokomɛi afata he?

english: If your crops grow slowly, look pale light-green instead of deep green, or produce small fruits even when there is good rain, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. loo ha yibii bibii Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans inside my maize farm, and how will it affect the maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni te ebaaná ŋmãa nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is helpful. Beans grab nitrogen food from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better while giving you two different harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Beans mɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is fertile enough to expand my maize farm this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ magbɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Good soil for maize feels dark and crumbly in your hand, drains excess water easily, and supports healthy weed growth like guinea grass. If the soil is pale, hard, or sandy, you will need to add compost or manure before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nine mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ mlɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi ni mli wa tamɔ guinea jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ewa, loo ŋã lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he dani odu.

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand properly underground. If the soil is hard or full of stones, the tuber cannot push outward easily, so building high, loose soil mounds gives them the room they need to grow large and straight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ kɛya kponɔgbɛ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni ooofee lɛ baaha oná hegbɛ ni oda ni oda shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantain or banana to protect them from heat stress until they grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall but only yield tiny ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ toi bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil food. The plant spends all its energy stretching tall to reach the sun instead of putting energy into growing big ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eshɛ ekwɔlɛ he ni eshɛ hulu lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu ŋmãa toi agboi lɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants shed their bottom leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping lower leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water when there is no rain. By shedding extra leaves, the plant reduces water loss and keeps its root tubers alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha nu ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani etsɔɔ aduawai?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. High heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop blossoms to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie amɛbai lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛná hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How long does a newly planted oil palm tree take before it starts producing fruit bunches?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibii akui woɔ shishi?

english: Improved oil palm varieties typically begin flowering and producing their first small fruit bunches between 2 and 3 years after being transplanted into the field, provided they are weeded and well cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. Klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ afii 2 kɛ 3 teŋ beni adu awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, which causes the fresh leaves to twist, pucker, and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai heei lɛ tsɔɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about 3 to 4 months, leaving the slower-growing cassava plenty of space to expand and mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni daa blɛoo lɛ naa gbɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni eda sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants spread across the ground instead of growing straight up like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Many cowpea varieties naturally grow as creeping vines to cover the ground. This spreading behavior is helpful because the dense leaf carpet shade out weeds and prevents the tropical sun from drying out the topsoil.
ga: Cowpea henɔi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe akɛ wain tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ subaŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa nɛɛ he ejaakɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees like plantains planted alongside them, the intense sun scorches the leaves, causing them to yellow, dry up, and fall off to conserve water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, hulu ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛbaagbi, ni amɛbaagbee shi koni nu akafite.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the leafy vines off the ground, maximizing sun exposure and airflow while preventing soil-borne diseases from rotting the stems.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ naa koni ekafite tsei lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small dark droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji egbɛ eshwa ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is a typical sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the central growing funnel of the maize plant, feeding on leaves before they unfold and leaving behind dark waste material called frass.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo. ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ frass lɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and turn yellow even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes is usually caused by Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, which is transmitted by tiny whitefly insects. The virus disrupts normal plant growth, preventing leaves from expanding properly and reducing fruit yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. Virus tsiɔ tsei adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai baa shi.

english: Why did my cassava plants grow very tall with dense green leaves but produce only tiny roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse shi shishifãi bibii pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy tops. To grow thick, starchy tubers underground, cassava needs balanced nutrients with sufficient potassium rather than excess nitrogen.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni akwɛ̃ tubers ni starch ni mli wa yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Cassava he miihia niyenii ni sa kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ

english: Extra suckers compete with the main stem for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. By cutting back side suckers and leaving only one strong replacement, you ensure the main plant gets enough nutrients to produce heavy, high-quality bunches.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ Kpãa ŋmeii lɛ amli ni oshi nɔ kome pɛ ni he wa ni akɛbaato najiaŋ. Obaanyɛ oná nɔmimaa akɛ tso titri lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the plant stem causes fertilizer burn because high salt concentrations pull moisture straight out of the plant tissues. Fertilizer should be spread in a ring a short distance from the stem where feeding roots absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã ejaakɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo lɛ mli. he ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ

english: Shallow standing water suffocates competing weeds that would otherwise rob young rice of light and nutrients. Rice roots are unique because they can thrive in submerged conditions where most weed seeds cannot germinate.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haa jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni baanyɛ ajie la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Omɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ nu shishi ni jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into pencil-like tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji ni tamɔ pɛnsil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival trick maize uses during hot parts of the day. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to sunlight and wind, preventing excessive water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ naa kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cowpea plants without forming seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee dumɔwui akutsei lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from intense dry spells, extreme temperatures, or sap-sucking pests like thrips. When stressed, the plant drops blossoms to conserve energy and water for its own survival.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kpe. hulutsoo ni naa wa waa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: How should I care for young tree seedlings right after I put them in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui bibii anɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings need reliable shade from strong direct sunlight and light watering every morning or evening until their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater on their own.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fioo daa leebi loo gbɛkɛ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient found in good fertilizer or well-rotted manure that helps plants grow strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ amli, ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa tsei ahe tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look droopy during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl during hot afternoons to protect themselves from water loss; the plant is saving its moisture and will usually bounce back once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu akafite. Tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji hulu lɛ jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa trees on new farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like leafy umbrellas, giving the cocoa trees shade and moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Will my pepper plants give me more pepper if I plant them very close together?
ga: Ani mi-pepper tsei lɛ baawo pepper babaoo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: No, planting peppers too close together makes them fight for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients, which leads to weak stems and fewer, smaller peppers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: How do I know it is safe to start planting my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become regular for at least two to three continuous weeks so the soil stays moist enough to nourish germinating seeds without them drying up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa kɛ hoo lɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii ahe baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in crop leaves are typically caused by small insects or beetles chewing on them, which weakens the plant and requires insect traps or safe crop sprays to control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli buji baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehe bahiaa ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsofai ni buɔ tso lɛ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii koni akɛkudɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant receives irregular water, or when there are no bees around to transfer pollen so fruit can develop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen lɛ koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Dried animal manure adds vital food back into the soil and helps soil retain water longer, giving crops a steady feed of nutrients for healthy growth.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ daa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak if I leave them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil fertilizer that your crops need to build strong stems and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up in the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight because their roots are not deep enough to draw enough water. They require shade plants like plantains to shield them from sun heat and keep the soil moist until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but can only support a small percentage as full pods. Flower drop happens due to incomplete insect pollination, dry weather stress, or the tree self-regulating how much fruit it can feed at one time.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo pɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ aye abua beni ŋmeii lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli Aloo tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehe aduawai babaoo ni ebaanyɛ eye yɛ be kome mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded environments. Rain drops splash the fungal spores from the soil or infected leaves onto healthy pods, spreading the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha hela ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches that waste the tree's energy and block sunlight. Opening up the tree's canopy improves air movement, reduces disease build-up, and directs nutrients toward growing healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni wooo yibii ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. Tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ehaa helai ni buaa amɛhe naa lɛ baa shi ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow leaves, so when soil nutrients are low, the plant takes nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, no lɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when it rains heavily for a long period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the ground without draining properly, water replaces the air pockets, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nu jogbaŋŋ. Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ anajiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain plant stop producing big fruit bunches when there are many smaller shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kpaɔ aduawai wuji ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he?

english: The smaller shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main stem for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing excess suckers keeps the main plant strong enough to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni tsii baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves but produce no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani oyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi bɛ ohe?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leaf and stem growth instead of flowering. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus encourages the plant to form blooms and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly and produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds growing near my young crop seedlings make the crop plants grow thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal essential sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer away from young seedlings. Without enough light and food, the seedlings stretch upward too quickly, making them weak and fragile.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la ni he hiaa, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Kɛji la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bɔjɔmɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main plant food, or the soil has too much water around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Small holes inside the central leaves of young corn are usually caused by fall armyworms hiding in the funnel. You can control them by spraying early in the morning or late evening, or by placing a pinch of clean sand or wood ash directly into the leaf funnels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni oooshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛtsɔ ŋã loo tso sũ ni he tse fioo ni okɛbaafata baa lɛ ŋmei lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains or cassava next to them creates temporary living shade to protect the cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa koni ebu kookoo lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds after the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain falls steadily for a few consecutive days and deeply soaks the ground. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry period follows immediately.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage, drowning the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra rainwater to flow away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, dry soil, or lack of water. Keeping soil covered with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps hold moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo baai ni egboi (mulching) kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are my maize stalks so thin and light even though I planted many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ lɛ? He ni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil food. Spacing seeds out properly gives every stem enough room to grow thick and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my farm with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ ŋmei shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Turning over the soil brings hidden weed seeds up into sunlight, where they quickly sprout. Covering the bare earth around your crop with dry grass or leaves blocks sunlight from reaching those seeds and stops them from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha onibii ahe, ni otsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ahe, ni otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I harvest smaller crops when I plant maize in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your field with beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts puts vital natural food back into the soil for future crops.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii, tsina loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize will produce weaker plants and much smaller yields in the second year. To get a strong harvest every season, it is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds from a trusted supplier.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo kwraa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni oná kpamɔ kpakpa daa be mli lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii haa lɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is short on nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green and bushy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the energy it needs to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei ni miida lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi ŋmɔji amli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is tired and needs fertilizer or rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ajɔɔ mihe?

english: If your crops are growing slowly, look pale, or give you a much smaller harvest than past years even when there is good rainfall, your soil has run out of nutrients and needs compost, fertilizer, or a rest period.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ miida blɛoo, etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo hejɔɔmɔ be.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or beans on my land makes the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has tiny bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the dirt to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that loves hiding in the funnel of young maize plants. Applying recommended crop sprays or neem leaf extract early in the morning or evening helps kill them before they destroy the stem.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ atsɔnei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ he ŋaa akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe amɛ dani amɛkpãtã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and developing bright yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by small whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. You can stop it from spreading by pulling out sick plants and planting disease-resistant cassava varieties.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ akɛ mɛi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ Obaanyɛ okpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hela nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large trees and plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ ni midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full sun because direct heat burns their tender leaves and dries out their roots. They need shade from taller trees or plantains during their first two years to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo plantains amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do crop leaves curl or droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, which keeps the plant from losing too much water through sweating. If the leaves bounce back in the evening, the plant is managing the heat naturally.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle loo egbee shi koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná nu babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ yeɔ dɔlɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil regularly damp and avoiding excess chemical fertilizer helps fruit to set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli babaoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ama shi.

english: Why is it harmful to drop three or four maize seeds in one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso ni miida lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight your plants need. If weeds are left in the farm, your crops suffer from hunger even if there is plenty of water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ waa. Kɛji jwɛi komɛi eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Kɛji Nu babaoo yɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii.

english: Why does water collect in some parts of my farm and wash away my crops whenever heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi ni ekɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: Water pools in low or uneven areas of your field. Measuring the slope of your land helps you create proper drainage channels so rainwater flows safely away without flooding or destroying your crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishi loo he ni etseee yɛ oyale mli lɛ Oshikpɔŋ lɛ shishitoo lɛ susumɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni ofeɔ nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛi ni sa koni nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe ni nu afua loo efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents air from reaching the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the root environment healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifã shihilɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi

english: Why do crops planted on sloping land grow smaller than the ones at the bottom of the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ daraaa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes rich topsoil and fertilizers down the slope to the bottom. Building contour ridges across the slope slows down water flow and keeps plant food near your crop roots.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ. Kɛ́ ofee ŋmeii yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha tso niyenii lɛ abɛŋkɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni edara lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct sun. Plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants from intense heat while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow during dry spells even when I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu fioo haa lɛ moŋ?

english: Shallow watering leaves moisture near the surface where heat evaporates it quickly. Watering deeply encourages maize roots to grow down into the soil where it stays cool and damp.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Dɔlɛ lɛ baaho oya. Nu ni awoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, he ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin without producing much fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When tomato plants are planted too close together, they shade each other and fight for sunlight. This makes them stretch tall and weak instead of using their energy to bear fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baawo yibii.

english: Why does my farm soil become hard like concrete just a few days after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter. Adding dried leaves, compost, or animal manure acts like a sponge, keeping the soil soft and helping it hold moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does digging small ditches across my vegetable beds help my plants stay healthy?
ga: Te bibioo ko ni afoɔ lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ni mikɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Small ditches direct water evenly across your farm during irrigation or rain, ensuring every plant gets watered without creating muddy pools that rot plant roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ bibioo ko baaha nu aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni nu shwieɔ shi loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa nu ahaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ekɛ muji ni fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaa.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crops more when the weather is very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather stresses plants and weakens their natural defenses, while also causing insects to breed faster and feed more aggressively on stems and leaves for moisture.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hewalɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ waa koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seeds take so long to sprout when planted in the cold rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds need warm soil to sprout quickly. Cold, wet soil slows down germination and can cause seeds to rot before they ever break through the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he miihia pepper dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni efɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agboi dani amɛbote sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Taller trees provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the young plants until they are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and getting holes chewed in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔ bu mli lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by fall armyworms or other insect pests, while yellowing often means the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai krokomɛi ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when I plant them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the new buds to grow downwards before turning up, which weakens the plant and severely reduces your tuber yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that restores nutrients for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to steal water and food from the main mother plant, leading to smaller, lighter plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to capture maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy that travels down to form larger yam tubers.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni emɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni yaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering, causing stress that prevents the flowers from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo yibii baa.

english: Why is it useless to spread fertilizer on my crop when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Dry fertilizer stays on the surface and can even burn the roots when water is absent.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni egbi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ kɛji nu bɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crop produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your farm, competing directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and space, leaving your plants starved of nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ ŋwɛi, ni no haa otsei lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do small insects appear inside my bags of dried maize after sitting in storage for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii je kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ kotoku lɛ mli beni mikɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevil insects or their hidden eggs often enter maize while it is still in the field, hatching inside the bag if the grain was not thoroughly dried or treated before storage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. ni efo yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ.

english: If plantains do not have seeds inside them, how am I supposed to plant new ones on my farm?
ga: Kɛji plantain lɛ bɛ dumɔwui yɛ mli Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains do not grow from seeds like maize or tomatoes. Instead, they reproduce through shoots called 'suckers' that grow out of the base of a mature plant. You dig up these suckers and replant them to grow new plantain trees.
ga: Plantains lɛ jeee dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa loo tomato. Mohu ɔ, a guɔ tso nɛ a tsɛɛ ke ‘tso’ nɛ jeɔ tsohi nɛ a wa a sisi ɔ mi kɛ guɔ a nɔ nɛ a gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ofoɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni oduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ koni dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do plantain crops produce fruit without seeds, unlike other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei woɔ yibii ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ? Esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ tso kroko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Plantains are specially bred variety of wild bananas that developed without seed formation. Because they produce fruit naturally without needing seeds, all the fruit energy goes into soft flesh, making them easy to eat while requiring farmers to propagate them using root suckers.
ga: Plantain ji koo mli banana henɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni shwereɔ ni dumɔwui baaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni dumɔwui he ehiaaa. Yibii lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ yaa loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa eyeɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii kɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How can I tell if my plantain trees are suffering from a sickness before the whole farm gets ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ mi-plantains lɛ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ akpata?

english: Early signs of disease include leaves turning yellow or brown prematurely, dark spots or streaks appearing on the leaves and stems, stunted growth, or plantains wilting even when there is enough rain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ hela lɛ mra lɛ ahe ji baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ mra. Hei ni tsuɔ loo ŋmeii yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. stunted growth Aloo dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: What causes dark spots and marks to appear on the stems and leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii kɛ okadii jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by fungal or bacterial infections that spread through excess water, contaminated tools, or infected planting suckers. Proper field sanitation and buying healthy planting material help prevent them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. nibii ni mli ewo muji loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni sa kɛ dumɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ahemɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: My physical strength is low these days due to age and illness, so how can I manage my farm with less heavy labor?
ga: Nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ migbɔmɔtso lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ afii kɛ hela hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ nitsumɔ fioo?

english: You can reduce heavy work by using mulch (dry leaves and grass) around crop roots to stop weed growth, using cover crops to suppress weeds, and focusing on proper crop spacing so you spend less time clearing bushes.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha nitsumɔ ni wa lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. (Baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi) ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ahe koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ko nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni akɛkudɔ jwɛi Ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa nɔ koni okɛ be fioo atsu nii kɛtsumɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: How does clearing weeds around my plantains help the crop grow better fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from your plants. Removing weeds ensures that all the plant food in the soil goes straight to strengthening your plantains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei aniyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛwoɔ odumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ mli.

english: Why are my plantain bunches coming out small and light even though the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Small bunches usually mean the soil lacks critical nutrients like potassium, or too many shoot suckers are growing around one mother plant and competing with it for food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo suckers babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he. Nyɛ kome duɔ ni ekɛ niyenii miitswa akaŋ

english: It is best to leave only 2 or 3 healthy suckers of different ages around the main stem (the mother, a daughter, and a shoot). Cutting away extra suckers prevents competition and gives you bigger bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ tso titri lɛ he (nyɛ, biyoo kɛ tso lɛ). Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi akaŋshii naa ni eha oná ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize in the middle of my plantains, or will they damage each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ? Aloo ebaafite?

english: You can plant quick crops like maize or cassava between young plantains during their first few months. However, leave enough space so they do not block sunlight or steal nutrients from the plantains as they grow tall.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkatsi hulu la lɛ naa loo amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak during hot and dry weather, and what can I do to keep them strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ? Ni mɛni mafee koni mitsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Hot weather causes water to evaporate rapidly from leaves and soil. Covering the base of your plants with dry vegetation (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture so the crops stay hydrated.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ sũ mli. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulch) ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi ni nu yɔɔ mli.

english: If I eat a very sweet mango and plant its seed on my farm, will the new tree produce fruit that tastes just as sweet?
ga: Kɛ miye mango ni ŋɔɔ waa ni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani tso hee lɛ baawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Trees grown directly from seeds often mix traits from two parent trees, so the fruit might turn out less sweet or different from the original fruit. To get the exact same taste and quality, farmers use grafting rather than planting seeds directly.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ sui ni jɛ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ amli lɛ feɔ ekome, no hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ fioo loo esoro amɛ kwraa yɛ shishijee aduawai lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni aná ŋmɔlɔ kɛ kpakpafeemɔ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ Okwaafoi kɛ grafting tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛaadu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some imported fruits bought in the market taste different or less sweet compared to our local Ghanaian fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ srɔto loo amɛhe ŋɔɔ waa kɛ akɛto wɔ Ghana aduawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Imported fruits are often harvested early before they naturally ripen so they don't rot during long ship journeys. Because they ripen in crates rather than on the tree under full sunlight, they do not develop their full natural sugars and flavor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akpaa aduawai ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ mra, dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ lɛlɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshwereɔ yɛ adekai amli moŋ fe tsei anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛnáaa adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ flavours fɛɛ.

english: How many years will I have to wait for a mango tree grown from a seed to start giving me fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mango ni ajie kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ abɔi yibiiwoo?

english: A mango tree planted directly from a seed takes about 5 to 8 years to start producing fruit. However, if you plant a grafted mango seedling from a nursery, it can start bearing fruit much faster, usually within 2 to 3 years.
ga: Mango tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi, kɛji akɛ odu mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, Mango lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa, bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli.

english: What causes harvested fruits like mangoes to develop a strange smell or bad taste after picking?
ga: Mɛni haa aduawai ni akpa, tamɔ mango lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ naakpɛɛ loo amɛhe ŋɔɔ waa beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Strange smells or off-flavors are usually caused by fungal infections like anthracnose, harvesting during hot afternoon hours, or keeping harvested fruits in airtight containers where heat and moisture build up and cause spoiling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe, tamɔ anthracnose lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baa. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli. aloo ni akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ ato tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli, he ni dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i buaa amɛhe naa ni ehaa efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Can seeds brought from foreign, cold countries grow well and produce good yields in our hot Ghanaian climate?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ maji kɛ maji ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Crops from cold regions usually struggle in tropical heat and heavy rains because they are not adapted to local soil conditions, temperature, or local pests. It is always safer to plant certified local varieties or varieties tested for tropical climates.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhe esaaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, hulutsoo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe shihilɛi amli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ ooodu maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo tsei srɔtoi ni aka amɛ akwɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant fruit seeds directly in the main field or start them in polybags first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu aduawai lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mabɔi amɛ yɛ poly bags amli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting seeds in polybags inside a sheltered nursery allows you to protect tender young shoots from harsh sunlight, dry spells, and insects. You can then transplant only the strongest, healthiest seedlings to your main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni oooje shishi yɛ polybags mli yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, hulutsoo be, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe. No sɛɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni he wa fe fɛɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ aya he ni oyɔɔ lɛ titri.

english: What is grafting, and why do agricultural officers recommend it over regular seed planting for mangoes?
ga: Mɛni ji grafting? Ni mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu mango moŋ fe ni aaadu mango dumɔwui daa lɛ?

english: Grafting is taking a small branch from a healthy, sweet-bearing adult tree and joining it onto a strong seedling root. This guarantees that your new tree matures quickly and produces the exact same sweet, high-quality fruit as the parent tree.
ga: Grafting ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsei niji bibii. Tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli ji he ni dumɔwu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shishifã lɛ jɛɔ. Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ otso hee lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaawo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Does the type of soil I plant my fruit trees in affect how sweet my harvest will be?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ mi tso yibii lɛ nɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, soil quality directly influences fruit sweetness. Soils rich in organic matter and nutrients like potassium, combined with good sunlight, help the tree produce the sugars needed to make the fruits sweet and flavorful.
ga: Hɛɛ, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa bɔ ni aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium eyi mli obɔ, ni hulu la kpakpa fata he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ sugars ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee fɛo lɛ aba.

english: How can I prevent worms and insects from ruining the flavor and look of my mangoes before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-mango lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ ehefɛo dani akpa?

english: Fruit flies are the main insects that lay eggs inside ripening fruit, causing worms and rot. You can control them by setting up fruit fly traps, clearing dropped rotten fruit from the ground, or wrapping growing fruits in protective bags.
ga: Fruit flies ji kooloi titri ni woɔ wɔji yɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ parasaiti kɛ fitemɔ aba. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni oootswa amɛ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ aduawai ni egboi ni egbee shi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Aloo okɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ awo kotoku ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a seed taken from a fresh fruit is good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ aduawai heei amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: A good seed should be firm, plump, clean, and free from cracks or insect holes. You can test it by putting it in water—seeds that sink are usually healthy and ready to grow, while floating seeds are usually hollow or damaged.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehe atse ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bu bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ dumɔwui ni hoɔ lɛ mli ewo muji loo efite.

english: Why should I put medicine on my seeds before planting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo midumɔwui lɛ tsofa dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Treating seeds with protective medicine before planting kills hidden germs and stops soil pests from destroying the seed before it has a chance to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsu dumɔwui ahe nii dani adu lɛ, egbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can germs or tiny insects live inside my seeds without me seeing them?
ga: Muawai loo kooloi bibii Ani ebaanyɛ ehi midumɔwui lɛ amli ni minaaa amɛ?

english: Yes, many fungi and microscopic pests can hide deep inside seeds or planting materials unnoticed, which is why preventive treatments are used to clean them out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui amli shɔŋŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko yɔseee. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni akɛ gbɛi ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Should I treat my cassava stem cuttings or yam setts with medicine before putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa atsa mi-cassava loo sweet potato ni afo lɛ dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, dipping or treating your planting materials cleans away rot-causing germs and protects the young plants underground as they begin to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ wo nu mli loo atsu he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie helai ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ kɛjɛ mli. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui lɛ ahe beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Is it better to apply chemical medicine before pests appear or wait until I see damage on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai atsu nii dani tsɛŋemɔ helai aba loo mamɛ kɛyashi miŋmɔ lɛ baafite?

english: Applying preventive measures early protects your crops from damage before it starts, which is much easier and cheaper than trying to cure a heavy disease attack later.
ga: Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa mra Ebaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he dani eje shishi. Enɛ waaa ni ejara hu waaa fe bɔ ni aaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni atsa hela ko ni naa wa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How does applying preventive medicine actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Preventive medicine creates a clean, protective barrier around plants, keeping out harmful germs so the crop can direct all its energy into growing strong and producing high yields.
ga: Tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ni he tse ni bɔleɔ tsei ahe, ni ejieɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops look sick even when I cannot see any bugs or caterpillars on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii komɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Crops can be attacked by microscopic germs or internal fungi that live inside the plant tissues, which require protective sprays or treatments to clear up.
ga: Helai bibii ni anaaa loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ atutua tsei. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa loo tsofai ni akɛbaatsu nii koni akɛjie lɛ.

english: What causes my young seedlings to rot and die right after they come out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni miiha midumɔwui lɛ miifite ni amɛgboi kɛji amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: Seedlings often die due to soil-borne germs and fungi attacking their delicate stems; applying a preventive fungicide or seed treatment prevents this rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui gboiɔ be mli ni helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Fungicides ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa loo dumɔwui ahe tsofafeemɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: How can I make sure my harvested farm produce stays clean and free from pests in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ ahe baatse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Applying safe, recommended storage treatments kills hidden insect eggs and prevents mold, keeping your harvested crops clean and safe for selling or eating.
ga: Gbɛi ni akɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsu nii lɛ baagbe koolooi wuji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa. Ha okpamɔ lɛ he atse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jarayeli loo niyeli.

english: Can taking small preventive steps really make a big difference in my final harvest?
ga: Ani gbɛi bibii ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa lɛ baanyɛ aha srɔtofeemɔ kpele aba minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, simple preventive actions taken early protect your crops from unseen losses, ensuring healthier plants and a much bigger, cleaner yield at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nifeemɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tsiɔ hela naa. Afee nakai kɛjɛ shishijee. Ebaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ nibii ni anaaa ni baafite lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da babaoo ni he tse yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How do I know if a medicine is meant to prevent disease or to cure an existing plant sickness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ko ji nɔ ni akɛtsiɔ tso hela ko ni yɔɔ momo lɛ naa loo akɛtsaa lɛ?

english: Preventive medicines are used on healthy crops to shield them from incoming germs, while curative medicines are applied after signs of sickness appear to stop further spread.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli koni akɛbu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni baa lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii beni etamɔ nɔ ni hela lɛ he okadii ekpa gbɛfaŋnɔ kroko lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight dries out their weak roots and burns their tender leaves before they can establish properly.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbi ni ebaashã baai bibii lɛ dani amɛfee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to plant cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, well-drained fertile soil that holds moisture well, without water pooling on top during heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower heavily but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?
