english: Heavy flowering without pod production happens when beneficial insects fail to pollinate the flowers or when the tree lacks sufficient water and nutrients to nourish the growing pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi babaoo ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing and falling leaves can be a sign of nutrient deficiency in the soil, severe drought stress, or an attack by pests like capsids.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids tutuamɔ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions, especially when trees are overgrown and lack air circulation.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: How does weed growth affect the yield of my young crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ ayibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete with young crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing the main crops to grow weakly and yield poorly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How can working with government programs like COCOBOD help my cocoa farm?
ga: Te nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko tamɔ COCOBOD ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Partnering with government agricultural bodies gives farmers access to reliable technical guidance, approved inputs like fertilizers, and subsidized farm support services.
ga: Nɔyeli okwaayeli nitsumɔhei ni akɛ amɛ feɔ ekome lɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ náa ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ nitsumɔi ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa

english: Is it safe for me to use cocoa spray chemicals on the vegetable crops I grow for my family?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ cocoa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ni miduɔ mihaa miweku lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: No, agrochemicals approved for cocoa are formulated specifically for cocoa trees and can be toxic or unsafe if applied to food crops meant for household consumption.
ga: Dabi, afee agrochemicals ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ aha kookoo tso lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ ayeɔ yɛ shia lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to prune excess branches from mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches so the tree directs its energy into pod growth while allowing sunlight and airflow to reduce fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baawo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he koni ŋmeii helai aba shi.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans after harvesting them instead of drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli beni akpa amɛ lɛ, moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the bean seed, stops germination, changes the color from purple to brown, and develops the rich chocolate flavor required by buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gboɔ, ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ, ni etsakeɔ ehiɛ su kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni amɛná tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow better when I plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize, helping them grow stronger without needing expensive chemical inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my corn plants turning yellow before they even produce ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth. Heavy rains or poor soil can wash nitrogen away, leaving the plant too weak to produce healthy ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekɛ toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year make the crop yields drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls large amounts of specific nutrients out of the earth every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil; rotating with crops like legumes gives the land time to recover its fertility.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be, ni kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together to get more plants, why do I end up with a smaller harvest?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo hu? Mɛni hewɔ mitsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of many healthy plants, you get crowded, weak plants that produce tiny fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, tsehi fuu nɛ a ngɛ he wami ngɛ. Obaagbe naa kɛ tso ko ni bɛ hewalɛ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ yibii bibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight, which causes them to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Shade trees protect young cocoa from burning heat while their roots develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Enɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does trimming off excess leaves and small branches from my tomato plants make the fruits grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ? kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli, ni no haa aduawai lɛ feɔ agboi

english: When a plant has too many leaves, it wastes energy feeding leaf growth. Removing extra branches forces the plant to send its food and energy directly into growing large, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ baai babaoo Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa baai lɛ adalɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn pale and stop growing when water sits around their roots for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ beni nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe and absorb nutrients. Standing water smothers the root system, causing root rot and stopping the plant from taking in food and water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: How does leaving dead plant leaves on top of my soil help keep my crops alive during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ahe baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: A layer of organic matter acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks harsh sunlight from drying out the earth, keeping moisture trapped near the roots so crops can survive dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli fãi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do pests like fall armyworms cause much more damage to my maize during dry periods than during rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather stresses maize plants and makes them too weak to defend or heal themselves, while rain helps crops grow faster and can physically wash young caterpillars off the leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ haoɔ. ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe loo amɛtsa amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crops' growth even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds naturally grow much faster and aggressively steal water, light, and fertilizer from the soil long before your crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are small green worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-babi corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of maize to eat the soft tissues, which can destroy the crop if you do not spray them early with recommended insecticides or organic neem oil mixtures.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo organic neem fɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii mra.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and getting light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is usually Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. When leaves curl and lose color, they cannot make enough food, resulting in very small cassava roots at harvest time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enyɛŋ ehoo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil rot or wilt diseases. Harmful fungi or bacteria in the dirt block the stem from carrying water up to the leaves, causing the plant to dry out from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ loo shwiemɔ hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fung loo bacteria ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekɛ nu ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ naa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in a 'V' shape usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ 'V' su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, onibii lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su eŋɔli kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant does not get steady water. Heat stress stops the flowers from forming fruit, so the plant sheds them to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Dɔlɛ he haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do people say planting beans or cowpeas makes the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the season ends, that nitrogen stays in the soil to act as free plant food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in bright sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and have broad leaves that create living shade umbrellas, keeping young cocoa cool and moist during its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is moist before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it in. Putting dry fertilizer on dry ground in hot sun can burn plant roots or evaporate into the air before the crop can use it.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I leave many young shoots growing around one plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow around one mother plantain, they all fight for the same food, water, and sunlight. Removing extra shoots leaves energy for the main plant to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji plantain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Dumɔwu kome fa tsɔ. Amɛshiɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread, helping the leaves make maximum food to grow large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed to make leaves green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or drown the roots. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of storing food in the roots. To grow big roots, cassava needs balanced soil containing phosphorus and potassium rather than heavy nitrogen.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okwɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia Cassava moŋ fe nitrogen ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when water is unpredictable. Heat stress and dry soil stop the flowers from pollinating properly, so keeping the soil moist with regular watering and mulch helps the plant hold onto flowers and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nu lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Extra suckers compete with the parent plantain for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Leaving too many shoots weakens the main plant and results in small bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures the largest fruit yield.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii bibii aba. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the leaf funnel. Applying recommended botanical extracts like neem or appropriate insect sprays directly into the center of the plant stops the pest before it destroys the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli tamɔ neem loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ akpa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward full sunlight, which generates energy to expand the tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, protecting them from leaf fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ baai amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper bushes curling upward and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, thrips, or aphids, or by a virus they carry. Controlling these insects using soapy water sprays or recommended treatments stops new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsaa helai nɛɛ tsu nii ni akɛye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai heei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in humid, damp conditions with low airflow. Pruning excess canopy branches and clearing weeds beneath cocoa trees allows air and sunlight to dry the pods, stopping the fungal spores from multiplying.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli, ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ adalɛ

english: Why is it helpful to spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-vegetables lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, shields soil from harsh sun heat so water stays in the ground longer. It keeps roots cool, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down to feed the soil with organic matter.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural survival mechanism to protect moisture. By curling inward, the plant reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly so the plant can survive until rain comes.
ga: Abɛi baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baaha he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: How can I safely store my harvested cowpeas so insects do not destroy them while I wait for market prices to go up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-cowpea ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni mikafite kooloi bibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: You can store thoroughly dried cowpeas in airtight triple-layer plastic bags (PICS bags). Sealing the bags tightly cuts off oxygen, which suffocates any insect pests or eggs inside without needing expensive or dangerous chemicals.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsina ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo plastic kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (PICS kotokui) ni yɔɔ fãi etɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsĩ kotokui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa loo ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but only produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Adding potassium-rich fertilizer or manure helps tubers grow larger.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai eŋɔli ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and drop off without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛjieee cacao ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water stress, lack of shade, or a shortage of tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers. Maintaining proper shade trees and keeping moisture in the soil helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji nu mli haomɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ amɛhe lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hulutsoo ni sa, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: If I plant groundnuts and maize together on the same farm, will they steal plant food from each other?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Ani amɛbaaju tsei niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: No, groundnuts and maize actually cooperate. Groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the maize plant and keeps the soil fertile for both crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ. Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and wither when there is too much rain on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates crop roots by removing oxygen from the soil. This causes root rot, making it impossible for the plant to drink water or intake nutrients, which leads to yellowing leaves and wilting.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ anu nu loo amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn even before the planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ po baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms that enter a natural rest period after harvest. Once heat and humidity rise in the storage barn, the tuber naturally wakes up from dormancy and sprouts to start growing a new plant.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i tee hiɛ yɛ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ, Tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ koni amɛje tsei heei ashishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily as soon as the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread out sideways rather than deep down into the soil. As the heavy bunch grows, the tree becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with sturdy bamboo poles prevents strong winds from uprooting it.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa afãi moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their young green fruits before they are ready for picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miishwie aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli dani amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruit when they experience sudden stress, such as extreme sun heat, irregular watering, or damage from small pests like thrips. Keeping the moisture steady and checking for pests protects the fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ trukaa, tamɔ hulu la ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips mli baa lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be, ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: What fast-maturing crops can I plant if the rainy season starts late and ends quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni daa oya abaanyɛ adu kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ ni egbeɔ naa mra?

english: You can plant early-maturing varieties of cowpeas, sweet potatoes, or short-duration maize. These crops require less total water and can mature in 60 to 90 days, allowing you to harvest successfully even with a short rainy season.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ biɔ nu babaoo kwraa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli, ni no baaha oná ŋmaa ni yeɔ omanye yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo po mli.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. This temporary wilting is the plant's natural way of reducing surface area to save water, and the leaves usually bounce back when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa ehiɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the suckers around my plantain stem to grow at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Plantain tsei lɛ feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to fight for the same water and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant gets enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aná hewalɛ, ni ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants automatically move whatever nitrogen they have from older bottom leaves up to feed the young growing leaves at the top, showing that your field needs fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dirt inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the leaf funnel (whorl) during the day to feed on soft new leaves, leaving behind chewed holes and small dark droppings that look like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai (rings) amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Amɛshiɔ bu ni ashɛreɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ. ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ sɛɛ

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantains next to my new young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn and dry out under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Excessive heat damages the pollen inside the flower, so the plant drops unpollinated flowers to conserve its remaining strength.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, leaving a bare stem. You will also notice cracks in the soil around the base of the plant where the expanding tubers are pushing the earth upward.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli hu he ni ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsiɔ sũ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots of my crop help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the ground from the direct sun to keep moisture in the soil, stops weeds from sprouting, and slowly rots into natural plant food.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Why do seeds fail to come up properly if I push them too deep into the ground when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds contain only a small amount of stored food energy to sprout. If buried too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching sunlight to start making its own food.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ niyenii hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato kɛha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he koni amɛje amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii feemɔ shishi.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but no heavy rain is falling. Applying fertilizer right before a downpour causes the water to wash the nutrients away into gutters before the roots can absorb them, while dry soil prevents the fertilizer from dissolving.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ ni naa wa bako. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ enɛ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ nubu lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains around them provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil, protecting the delicate seedlings while they establish roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Plantain leaves curl or droop in intense heat as a natural defense to limit water loss through evaporation. As long as the soil has adequate moisture, the leaves will usually bounce back once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛtsi nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops end up competing with each other for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. This leaves the stalks thin and weak, resulting in much smaller maize cobs and a poorer overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa, ni ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Is it safe for me to cut off some of the bottom leaves on my tomato plants, or will that damage them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi? Aloo ebaafite amɛ?

english: Trimming the lower leaves—known as pruning—actually helps tomato plants. It allows better airflow around the base, reduces moisture-loving diseases, and helps the plant direct its energy into growing larger fruits.
ga: Ale shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua o-tomato tsei lɛ waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa helai ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji

english: Why should I avoid heavy weeding or spraying pesticides when my pepper plants start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni tsii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he beni mi-pepper tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi kpojiemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Disturbing pepper plants during their flowering stage causes stress that can make the delicate blossoms drop off prematurely. If flowers drop, the plant cannot produce pepper fruits, which directly lowers your harvest.
ga: Pepper tsei ni haoɔ mɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo oya baa. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo pepper yibii. Enɛ baaha nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that excess rainwater is pooling around the roots and suffocating them. Improving soil drainage and adding compost can help bring back healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ebua ehe naa. roots and suffocates Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do other farmers cover the bare soil around their yam vines with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or straw—a practice called mulching—keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and prevents weeds from stealing nutrients away from your yam roots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it better for my garden crops if I give them a deep soaking occasionally rather than a little light water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo nu mli shɔŋŋ lɛ? Bei komɛi lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu ni mli jɔ Fioo daa gbi

english: Deep watering encourages roots to grow deeper into the soil where it stays cool and moist. Plants with deep root systems are much stronger and can easily survive hot dry spells compared to plants with shallow roots.
ga: Nu ni mli kwɔ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ he wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli oya fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and gives local pests and diseases a permanent home. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eye ebua ni eha akutso lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai lɛ aná shia ni baahi shi daa. Okɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong and can burn the tender stem and roots if placed too close. Applying fertilizer a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to safely draw in the nutrients without burning the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai ni haa tso lɛ shãaa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it important to leave proper distance between my maize plants when sowing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Maize needs enough space so sunlight, air, and soil nutrients are not blocked by neighboring plants. Proper spacing allows every stalk to grow strong and produce large, full cobs.
ga: He ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa bɔni afee ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akatsi hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and thin without fruiting when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants need full sunlight to make energy. When heavy tree branches obstruct direct sunlight, the plants stretch upwards searching for light instead of developing strong stems and flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ tso niji ni tsii tsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ Tso lɛ baagbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa.

english: What is the main difference between growing seasonal crops like cassava and permanent crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ nibii ni aduɔ daa tamɔ kookoo teŋ?

english: Seasonal crops like cassava are harvested and replanted after a short cycle, whereas permanent crops like cocoa stay rooted in the farm for decades, yielding continuous harvests year after year once established.
ga: Akpaa be mli nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmei, ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ kookoo lɛ shishifãi ewo ŋmɔji amli afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Etee nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii afi fɛɛ afi kɛjɛ be mli ni ato shishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantains when starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains beni mijeɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and provide temporary, living shade to protect tender cocoa plants until the cocoa trees grow large enough to form their own canopy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsitsi.

english: What do the three numbers like 15-15-15 on a bag of NPK fertilizer actually mean?
ga: Mɛni yibɔi etɛ tamɔ 15-15-15 ni yɔɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Those numbers show the balanced proportion or fraction of nutrients in the bag: Nitrogen for leaf greenness, Phosphorus for root development, and Potassium for fruit strength.
ga: Yibɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ fa ha loo bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha, ni nitrogen ni haa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fata he. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kɛ potasium kɛha aduawai lɛ ahewalɛ

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients when my crop leaves turn yellow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often show that your soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is missing, crops cannot build food properly, causing old leaves to turn yellow and growth to slow down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ laaje lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa fioo.

english: Why must I remove all tree stumps and heavy roots before planting groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni tsii lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods develop underground. Clearing obstructions like tree roots and hard soil gives the pegs free space to enter the ground and expand into healthy pods.
ga: Bean pods lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nibii ni tsiɔ gbɛ tamɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I cut off chupons and extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jupon kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing extra shoots opens up the tree canopy, letting light and air move freely. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and ensures plant energy goes directly into making pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, no gbeleɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Ha kane kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aya he fɛɛ he. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa ni ehaa hewalɛ yaa tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni efee tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing leaf rot and encouraging bigger tubers to form below ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Can I plant pepper between my young plantain trees without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu pepper yɛ dumɔwui bibii ateŋ? Ni ekɛ awuiyeli baaa loo ekɛbaaa?

english: Yes, you can intercrop pepper with young plantains as long as you leave clear space around the plantain base so their roots do not fight each other for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ plantains bibii akwɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Shii abɔ ni obaashi he ko yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akashi akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees the protection they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ buɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when I put them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava niji lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives each plant enough room underground to grow large tubers. If you plant them too close together, the roots will compete for food and water, resulting in thin, small tubers.
ga: Ha ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome, ni oha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. Kɛji odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to make green leaves. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eda waa.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔ nii lɛ amli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is shortly after the crop sprouts, usually around two to three weeks after planting, and again when the plant starts flowering. Applying it early ensures the roots can feed on it while the plant is growing rapidly.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ji beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli mra lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the soil of the same specific nutrients over and over again. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake o-corn lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: These caterpillars are pests, often called fall armyworms, that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by moths. They feed on tender leaves to grow, but catching them early and applying appropriate control measures can save your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ amɛ fall armyworms. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli amɛfɔ̃ɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii koni amɛdara. Shi kɛji omɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a plant sickness, or by heat stress from dry soil. Managing the insects early and keeping the soil moist helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi anɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: What will happen to my crop seeds if the rains stop for two weeks right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to swell up and sprout roots. If the soil dries out completely after planting, the seeds can dry up and die in the dirt, which means you will need to replant once the rains come back.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui hu baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air is too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water and food. Watering regularly and placing mulch on the ground around the stem helps keep the soil cool so the flowers can turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Okɛ nu awo mli daa ni oshi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ yibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: How soon do I need to start clearing weeds away from my newly sprouted crops?
ga: Te ehe baahia ni mabɔi jwɛi ni jɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ amli lɛ jiemɔ mra tɛŋŋ?

english: You should clear weeds within the first month after your crops sprout because weeds grow fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from young plants. Keeping the farm clean early allows your crops to get strong.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni otsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil quickly before their roots grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnaa nu.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up toward the sunlight to produce the food required to grow big tubers underground; climbing stakes help them capture maximum light and keep leaves off the wet soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ amɛkwɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ la ni fa fe fɛɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieee shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential plant food needed to build healthy green leaves and help the crop grow tall.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tsei niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and produce less food if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni niyenii ni baa lɛ faaa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away fertilizer from the topsoil or push it too deep into the ground before your crops' roots can drink it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains flood my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely soaked in water, air cannot reach the crop's roots, causing the roots to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu mli kwraa lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any fruit during the hottest dry season weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko yɛ otsii ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry conditions stress tomato plants, causing them to shed their flowers to save water and energy rather than trying to develop fruits.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oná yibii lɛ

english: Why do mature plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds hit the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni edara lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally have shallow roots, and microscopic pests in the soil can damage these roots, making the plant unable to hold itself firmly in the ground during wind storms.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsei ni ji plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap out of young leaves or passing viruses into the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ loo ni kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by stealing the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to develop strong stalks and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crops rotting in the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Crops usually rot because of excess water staying around the roots, fungal infections, or insect attacks. Creating raised soil ridges helps water drain away, and applying the right fungicide early stops fungal rot before it spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei fiteɔ yɛ nu ni fa babaoo ni bɔleɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hewɔ. Fungal hela. loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋta ni awo nɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli. kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are my maize stalks turning soft and falling over on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ efee blɛoo ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soft and falling stalks are usually caused by stem rot fungi or stem borer insects weakening the plant from inside. Clearing infected plant leftovers from the field and using recommended crop medicine early prevents this stem damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ emli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and spoiled underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rain makes the soil waterlogged or when root rot disease attacks. Planting on mounds or sloped land allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots firm and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu loo kɛ́ shishifãi fitemɔ hela ko ba. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa

english: How can I tell if my sick crops need liquid medicine or soil fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni ji nu loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii he miihia mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and slow growth usually mean the crop is hungry and needs fertilizer. Spots, holes, white webs, or rotting stems mean pests or diseases are attacking, which requires crop protection medicine like pesticides or fungicides.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Hei, bu, ŋmeii yɛŋ, loo tsei ni egboi tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi loo helai miitutua. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋmeii atsu nii.

english: What happens if I use too much crop medicine on my plants?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Using too much crop medicine can burn the plant leaves, weaken crop growth, damage the soil, and waste money. Always mix the exact amount recommended by an extension officer to keep plants safe.
ga: Tso tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tso baai lɛ ashã. Ehaa tsei lɛ daraaa, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni efiteɔ shika. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni o-extension nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ afutu mli koni otsei lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Can rain wash away crop medicine immediately after I spray my field?
ga: Ani nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ tsofa lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ efɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, heavy rain right after spraying washes the medicine off before the plant can absorb it. It is best to spray in the early morning or late afternoon on clear days when rain is not expected for at least 4 to 6 hours.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaho tsofa lɛ dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ tsofa lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, akpaaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 4 kɛyashi 6.

english: Why did my neighbor get a good harvest after spraying medicine while my crops still failed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Spraying only works if you use the right medicine for the specific disease, apply it at the correct growth stage, and use the right mix. Your neighbor may have sprayed earlier before the pests caused permanent damage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni sa kɛha hela pɔtɛɛ lɛ tsu nii pɛ kɛkɛ ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Okɛtsu nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli. ni okɛ nibii ni sa atsu nii Okutsoŋnyo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre mra dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ afite nii kɛya naanɔ.

english: Is it good practice to spray medicine on only half of my crop field to see if it works?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafɔ midumɔi lɛ fã pɛ nɔ koni mana kɛji ebaatsu nii?

english: Leaving an unsprayed section helps you see if the medicine is effective compared to untreated plants, but pests can easily jump from the unsprayed section back onto your treated crops if left unchecked.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi fã ni afɔɔɔ nɔ tsofa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsei ni atsako amɛ lɛ ahe. Shi tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ajɛ hei ni afɔɔɔ amɛ tsofa lɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛya tsei ni otsa lɛ amli oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start spraying medicine on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwiemɔ?

english: The best time to start spraying is as soon as you notice the very first signs of insect damage or leaf spots. Waiting until the crops are heavily damaged or rotting makes the medicine far less effective.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ oje tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ shishi ji be mli ni ona klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite loo baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite waa loo ebaagbo lɛ, ehaa tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do my crops look healthy and green but produce very little food at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji shi niyenii fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plants need extra nutrients and protection during their flowering and fruiting stage. If insects damage the flowers or the soil lacks nutrients during this key period, the plant stays green but cannot produce good fruits or seeds.
ga: Tsei he miihia niyenii krokomɛi kɛ hebuu yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔii ahiɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ be ni he hiaa nɛɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baakã he afee eŋɔli shi ewoŋ yibii loo dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: Why should I apply potassium fertilizer to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Potassium helps your cocoa trees build strong, full pods and improves fruit development, which leads to heavier cocoa beans and a bigger income during harvest.
ga: Potassium yeɔ ebuaa o-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii ni tsii waa kɛ shika babaoo ni anáa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baa.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is damp, allowing the roots to easily soak up the nutrients.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods tough and difficult to crack open during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ abaafo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods become tough to crack when the tree lacks key nutrients like potassium or experiences water stress, which causes the husk to grow unevenly.
ga: Ewa akɛ aaakumɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo nu he ehia lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why are the cocoa beans inside my pods small and light instead of heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ mi-pods lɛ amli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa moŋ fe ni amɛtsii lɛ?

english: Lightweight beans usually happen when the tree does not get enough nutrients or moisture while the pods are filling out, resulting in dry or underdeveloped seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ egbi loo amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready for picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: A fully ripe cocoa pod changes color completely from green or red to a bright yellow or orange, and it makes a dull, hollow sound when tapped gently.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ. Ni kɛ́ atswa lɛ fioo lɛ, eyɛ gbee ni mli ejɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes my small cocoa pods to turn shriveled and black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree sheds extra young pods it cannot feed due to nutrient shortages, high heat, or insufficient shade.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso ko shwie ŋmeii bibii tsɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye niyenii yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I increase the total number of pods my cocoa trees produce each season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmeii ni cacao tso ko woɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ fɛɛ aya hiɛ?

english: You can increase your yield by feeding your soil with balanced fertilizer, pruning dead branches to let light in, and weeding regularly so nutrients go straight to the tree.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okɛaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ koni la abote mli. Ni ojie jwɛi lɛ daa koni niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low on essential plant food like nitrogen, or the roots are struggling to absorb nutrients due to packed soil or poor water flow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa, loo shishifãi lɛ miitao ni amɛŋɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that get scorched by strong, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains around them to protect them in their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ ni amɛshãa amɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What are the early signs that my cocoa farm is receiving the right plant nutrients?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiná tsei ahe niyenii ni sa?

english: You will see deep green leaves, steady flowering, healthy pod growth without early shedding, and trees that stay strong even during drier periods.
ga: Obaana baai ni tsuɔ waa. fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ Tsobii lɛ daa waa ni amɛgbeeee shi oya. kɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi po lɛ.

english: Why should I buy hybrid maize seeds from the store every season instead of just saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Hybrid seeds give very high yields only in the first generation. If you plant seeds saved from a hybrid harvest, the offspring will grow unevenly, produce smaller cobs, and yield significantly less grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ hybrid kpamɔ mli Gbekɛbii baadara yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ha cob lɛ afee bibioo. ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow patches with tiny white flies under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by whiteflies. Using certified disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural agencies is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhei ema nɔ mi lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunshine and hot temperatures. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa acts as a protective shield, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ naa. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise planting groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer stays in the ground to nourish your maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha o-corn tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it necessary for me to heap high soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand deep underground into large tubers. High mounds also allow excess rain to drain away easily so the yam roots do not rot in flooded ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ hu haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had thin stems, or showed pale yellow leaves, your soil is low on essential nutrients. A simple soil test or observing weak weed growth can confirm if fertilizer is required.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Aloo jwɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ baanyɛ ama nɔ mi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark waste inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ gunk ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Regularly checking your field early in the season allows you to spray recommended organic or chemical treatments before the pest ruins the central growing tip.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ amli daa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa helai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awoɔ mli dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ afiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly damp and mulching around the plants helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, while allowing wet leaves to dry quickly so fungal diseases do not develop.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from tiny weevils without using dangerous liquid chemicals in my store?
ga: Mabu ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe. Ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii yɛ mishwapo lɛ mli?

english: Ensure your maize is dried completely until the grains are hard, then store them in airtight hermetic bags. These special bags cut off oxygen, smothering any insects naturally.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli. Nɛkɛ kotokui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. ni eshwieɔ kooloi bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct, strong sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving mature shade trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains nearby keeps the seedlings cool and moist until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their young vegetable plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sunlight. This keeps the soil cool, prevents rainwater from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. Ha jwɛi akakwɛ̃ ni ebatsɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛji egbo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow before the corn matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant nutrient. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the plant regain its rich green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the land after I harvest my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but beans and cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores soil fertility naturally for your next crop without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni okɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ aheee.

english: Why is it a bad idea to put chemical fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ahum baa lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away off the surface of the land or pushes it too deep into the mud before plant roots can drink it. Applying fertilizer when the ground is moist, but heavy rain is not falling, ensures your plants actually get the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ sũ lɛ mli tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ enɛko waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them and starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots healthy.
