ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua amɛhe naa. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft, growing heart of corn plants. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts protects the plants before severe damage occurs.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei atsui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni kɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by sucking pests. Keeping soil moisture steady and using shade or protective sprays stops the blossoms from falling off so fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ mli lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ shade loo tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does removing weeds early make my crop harvest so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds while your crops are still small gives your plants all the resources they need to grow fast and produce a heavy harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy that builds large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch plenty of sunlight and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa. Staking baajie tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I take a sample of my farm soil to a laboratory before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ aya laboratori lɛ dani mije dumɔ shishi?

english: Testing your soil in a lab tells you exactly what nutrients your land is missing and whether it is too sandy or acidic. This keeps you from wasting money on the wrong fertilizers and helps you choose the right crops for your land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni afeɔ yɛ laboratori mli lɛ baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã loo ŋã tsɔ? Enɛ baaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ ahe. ni eye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does sandy soil lose its strength and nutrients so quickly compared to dark soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shi oya kɛ akɛto shikpɔji ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles with big spaces between them, which causes rain to wash away water and nutrients easily. Adding compost or animal manure helps hold the sand together so it can store water and food for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ gbɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋã lɛ feɔ ekome koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ahi onibii amli.

english: How can I turn sandy, light soil on my farm into rich soil that supports healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ ŋã kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ mafee shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni fiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ asɛɛ?

english: You can improve sandy soil by continuously mixing in organic matter like dried leaves, crop residues, and animal dung. Over time, these materials break down and transform the loose sand into rich humus that holds moisture and nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, kɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni okɛfutuɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhaa ŋã ni etse ehe lɛ feɔ humus ni fa babaoo ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ.

english: Is it true that crops need iron from the soil, and what does iron do for them?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ dade ni jɛɔ sũ mli lɛ he miihia tsei? Ni mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dade he?

english: Yes, crops need small amounts of iron to produce chlorophyll, which gives leaves their green color and allows plants to make energy from sunlight. Without iron, plants grow weak and their leaves turn pale yellow.
ga: Hɛɛ, dade fioo ko he miihia tsei koni amɛfee klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli. Kɛji dade bɛ Tso lɛ he baajɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse.

english: Why are the young leaves on my crops turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking essential soil minerals like iron or nitrogen. When the soil lacks these elements or is too hard for roots to absorb them, the plant cannot feed properly and loses its green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hia, tamɔ dade loo nitrogen. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii nɛɛ loo shishifãi lɛ wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ amɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ baaje mli.

english: How do crop roots absorb solid minerals like iron from the ground if they can only take in liquid?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ sũ mli nibii ni wa, tamɔ dade kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Kɛji amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu pɛ

english: Crops cannot eat solid minerals directly; their roots drink nutrients dissolved in water. Natural soil acids and tiny beneficial organisms break down minerals like iron into tiny liquid particles that roots can easily suck up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye shika tsuru ni wa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ acid ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ gbálaa sũ mli nibii, tamɔ dade mli, ni amɛfeɔ nu bibii. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer wash away so fast without helping my plants when I use it on sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni eyeee ebuaaa tsei lɛ beni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers dissolve quickly in water, and in loose sandy soil, heavy rains wash them deep underground past the roots before the plant can feed. Mixing fertilizer with organic manure helps trap it near the root zone.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu mli oya. kɛ yɛ ŋã mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ, ni etsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ lɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: What nutrients do my crops need so their stems stay strong enough to carry heavy yields?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa mitso lɛ bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Crops need a balance of key minerals like potassium, calcium, and iron from the soil to build thick, sturdy stems. These nutrients strengthen the cell walls, helping the plant hold heavy fruit or grain without breaking.
ga: Tsei he miihia ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, calcium kɛ dade ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛma ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛhe wa. Niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ haa wala yibii lɛ ahe gbogboi lɛ mli waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui ni tsii toɔ ni amɛkuuu.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over at the base when the ears grow big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni toi lɛ dara ni etsii lɛ?

english: Plants fall over when their lower stems and roots lack structural strength, usually caused by missing soil minerals or planting too closely together. Strong, well-fed roots and thick stalks act like legs to support the plant's weight.
ga: Tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishigbɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ shishitoo hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji minerals ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Shishifãi ni wa, ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ni mli tse tsuɔ nii tamɔ naji ni amɛkɛfiɔ tso lɛ muji lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some crops growing in the same field look thick and heavy while others remain thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Crops grow thick and heavy when their roots hit patches of soil rich in essential minerals and organic food. Thin crops usually suffer from nutrient starvation, crowded roots, or soil that is too hard for roots to expand.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni shika tsuru ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ amanehulu. shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plant roots suck up to stay green and healthy. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its oldest bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii titrii lɛ ji nɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ yeɔ koni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly even after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. If the soil is too dry, or if weeds are competing for the same water and nutrients, your crops won't be able to use the fertilizer properly.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Sunburn damages their tender leaves, so they need shade trees or companion crops like plantain to provide shelter and keep the air humid while they are small.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ fiteɔ ebaa bibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of producing thick stalks and big ears, the plant spends all its energy stretching upwards to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ baaná tso lɛ shishifã ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi koni ekɛmɔ la lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. As long as the stems revive by evening or early morning, it is a normal defense behavior to reduce heat stress.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni tsɔne lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ. Eji hebuu subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ koni akɛba dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet, humid weather. Excess shade and weeds trap moisture around the trees, allowing the fungus to grow and destroy the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shade kɛ jwɛi ni fa babaoo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ powder ni mli ewo muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The moth lays eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaf funnel where they chew on soft young leaves during the day.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ ewui yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni fɔɔ lɛ baahi amɛhe yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between wet and dry. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating, causing the plant to abort the blossom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsei kpaɔ fɔfɔi

english: How do I know my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mifolɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava shows maturity when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You can test-dig one or two plants: mature tubers feel firm, full, and snap cleanly when broken.
ga: Cassava shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome loo enyɔ okwɛ. Yitsei ni eda lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa, amɛyi obɔ ni amɛkuɔ hetsemɔ kɛji amɛkumɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to white powder and get full of tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛŋ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ebaayi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: This is caused by grain weevils eating the inside of the seeds. If maize is stored before it is completely dry or without protective storage bags, weevils multiply rapidly and hollow out the grains.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to dani egbi kwraa loo akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ faa oya ni ehaa bulɛ baa dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: How can I stop my harvested maize from spoiling while I wait for a better market price?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when it is stored with too much moisture or exposed to pests like weevils. Drying your grain thoroughly until it crackles when bitten, and storing it in airtight bags or clean, treated granaries, protects it for months so you can sell when market prices rise.
ga: Abele fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo akɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii amli. Gbimɔ oŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaakumɔ kɛji emɔ bo. ni okɛto vacuum bag loo ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni mli tse mli. Ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nyɔji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become woody and dry if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are energy storage units for the plant. If left in the ground past full maturity, the plant starts using up the starch inside the root to grow new stems and leaves, leaving behind tough, fibrous wood instead of fresh food.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaada kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei akwɛ̃. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ tsɔji ni wa ni ashiɔ yɛ niyenii hee najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a living canopy that shades the leaves and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the tree establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Young cocoa masɛi lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tso lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, inconsistent watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Crops take up nutrients from the ground every season to grow. Planting the same crop on the same land repeatedly drains the soil's natural strength. Adding compost, animal manure, or rotating crops restores nutrients so yields remain high.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii daa be koni amɛdara. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni yibiiwoo lɛ aya nɔ aya hiɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my soil moist during short dry spells without watering every day?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli? ni ehe ehiaaa ni afɔ lɛ nu daa gbi

english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It stops the sun from baking the soil directly and prevents groundwater from evaporating into the air.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi loo baai, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hu shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How can I plant my vegetables so I have crops to sell every month instead of all at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu aduawai koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni mahɔ̃ɔ daa nyɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ shikome?

english: You can practice staggered planting by sowing small portions of your field every two to three weeks rather than planting everything in one day. This creates a continuous cycle of maturity, giving you fresh produce to sell regularly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fãi bibii ni ooodu daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkase dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome mli Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa onáa nibii heei ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ daa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my peppers so they do not rot on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Peppers are ready to harvest when they reach full, firm size and change to their mature color (such as bright green or deep red). Leaving them on the bush too long weakens the stem and makes them vulnerable to fruit flies and rot.
ga: Peppers efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ su ni egbɔ (tamɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ). Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ fitemɔ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil and are adapted to wake up and grow immediately with the slightest moisture. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from stealing light, space, and fertilizer from your young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaju la, he ko kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ odumɔwui bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant tomatoes on the exact same patch of ground every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Pests and soil diseases that target tomatoes build up and stay in the soil year after year. Rotating your plot with non-related crops like maize or cassava breaks this cycle by starving out tomato-specific pests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ helai ni yeɔ tomato nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ Efoɔ nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ mli kɛtsɔ tomatoi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How should I store my harvested corn at home so it doesn't spoil quickly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato shia koni ekafite oya?

english: Harvested corn needs to be stored in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated room, kept off the ground on wooden pallets, and protected from pests so mold and insects do not destroy your yield.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ. ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe Enɛ baaha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my stored beans get tiny holes and turn into dust after a few weeks in the house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ sũ beni ehi shĩa lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ

english: Tiny holes are caused by bean weevils eating the crop from the inside. Storing thoroughly dried beans in airtight containers or using approved storage dust keeps these insects away.
ga: Bean weevils ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo akɛ sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahe.

english: Is it bad if I stack my grain sacks directly on the bare floor inside my room?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmaa kotoku lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ tsu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, bare cement or dirt floors pass dampness directly into the sacks. This trapped moisture makes the grains rot and grow mold very quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, simɛnti shikpɔŋ loo muji baajie nu kɛya kotoku lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli nɛɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya waa.

english: How can I safely store my harvested crops if I only have a very small room in my house?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ ato shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ tsu bibioo ko pɛ miyɔɔ yɛ mishia lɛ?

english: You can maximize a small room by stacking sacks neatly on raised wooden platforms, leaving gaps between the stacks and walls to allow air to pass through.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha tsu bibioo ko mli he lɛ aya hiɛ. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ kotokui lɛ ni akɛaama tso kpoku ko ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ fɛfɛo lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ lasu tsu lɛ kɛ gbogbo lɛ teŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my grains spoil faster when I lean the sacks right against the room wall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ gbogbo lɛ he lɛ?

english: House walls absorb moisture from the ground and heat from outside, which transfers straight into the sacks touching them and causes the grains to rot.
ga: Shĩa lɛ gbogboi lɛ gbalaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ. ni ajieɔ kɛyaa kotokui ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ

english: How high off the ground should I raise my grain bags when keeping them indoors?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi dumɔwui kotokui lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ beni mikɛtoɔ shia lɛ?

english: Grain bags should be raised at least 15 to 20 centimeters off the floor on wooden pallets or logs to let air flow underneath and block dampness.
ga: Esa akɛ awo dumɔwui kotokui lɛ anɔ kɛ hoo lɛ sɛntimita 15 kɛyashi 20 kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei loo tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know if the spot where I keep my maize in my house is too damp for storage?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji he ni akɛ ŋmãa toɔ yɛ oshia lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni onyɛɛɛ okɛto?

english: If the room feels stuffy, smells musty, or you see water drops sweating on the inside of the storage bags, the location is too damp and poorly ventilated.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ona latsaa ŋmɔtɔi yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ he lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu nyɛɛɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I store different grains like beans and corn together in the same room?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ato. Ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee ekome yɛ tsu kome mli?

english: Yes, you can store different grains in the same room as long as each crop is dried properly, kept in separate closed bags, and raised off the floor.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui anaa. Abaanyɛ akɛ amɛ ato tsu kome mli kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbi jogbaŋŋ. Okɛto kotokui ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni aŋã mli. ni ewó ehe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why does my stored maize start smelling musty after sitting in my room for a month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni eta tsu lɛ mli nyɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: A musty smell means mold is growing because the maize was either not dried long enough before storage or absorbed moisture from damp air in the room.
ga: Musty smell tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ miikwɛ̃ ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbiko be kakadaŋŋ dani akɛto loo eŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: What happens if my grain storage area gets direct afternoon sunlight through the window?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ he ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ toɔ lɛ shɛɔ shwane mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ samflɛ mli?

english: Direct sunlight warms the room and makes leftover water inside the grains sweat out, creating trapped moisture that causes mold to grow inside the sacks.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tsu lɛ mli adɔ ni eha nu ni eshwɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ atsɔ latsaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Can all crop diseases be cured if I buy medicine from the agro-chemical store?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsa tsei ahe helai fɛɛ? Kɛji ohe tsofa kɛjɛ okwaayeli tsofafeemɔ shwapo ko mli?

english: No, some plant diseases caused by viruses, such as the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, have no chemical cure or medicine. The only way to stop them from spreading to healthy crops is to cut down and remove the infected trees.
ga: Dabi, tsei ahe helai komɛi ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ bɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛbaatsa amɛ. Gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli ji ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni ajie amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a sickness or just suffering from a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miigboi kɛkɛ?

english: A thirsty plant usually wilts during the heat of the day but revives when the soil is watered or when temperatures drop in the evening. A diseased plant often shows dark spots, leaf yellowing, oozing sap, or rot that does not improve even after watering.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. Shi ebaahi shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji, baai ni tsuɔ, nu ni hoɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii kwraa kɛ́ awo amɛ nu po.

english: Why is sticky liquid coming out of the trunk of my fruit tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ejɛ mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ shishi?

english: Trees often produce gum or sap as a defense mechanism when they are stressed, damaged by insects, or infected by fungal and bacterial diseases, attempting to seal the wound to protect themselves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ akɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛmiihao. ni kooloi efite loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ emɔ lɛ Kɛtsɔ bɔ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eŋa pilamɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water and reduce moisture loss, allowing the roots to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the middle of the afternoon even when the soil still feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water up from the soil. This causes temporary afternoon wilting to help the plant conserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane mli koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that plants need to produce chlorophyll and grow healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee klorofil ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do the roots of my yam plants rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam root rot is usually caused by waterlogged, poorly drained soil combined with fungal infection or pests like nematodes that attack the tubers while they are developing in heavy moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi fiteɔ. Okɛ enɛ afata tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes ni tutuaa bulb lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛyɛ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their blossoms when they experience extreme temperature changes, irregular watering, or poor pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni ehiii Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Crops planted in heavy shade stretch rapidly toward the sunlight to survive, which uses up their energy and leaves them with thin, weak stems and very few leaves.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ yeɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Who can I contact in Ghana if my farm suffers from an unusual crop sickness that I cannot identify?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matswa yɛ Ghana? Ni kɛji akɛ tso hela ko ni yɔɔ srɔto ni minyɛɛɛ mayɔse lɛ miiye miŋmɔ lɛ hu?

english: You can contact your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) extension officer or organizations like COCOBOD, who offer technical assistance, field inspections, and plant diagnosis to support farmers.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyana omaŋ lɛ mli Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) Extension Officer loo gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ COCOBOD, ni kɛ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ yelikɛbuamɔ haa lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ tsei amli kwɛmɔ Koni aye abua okwaafoi

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight because high heat burns their delicate leaves. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy and retains soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing starting from leaf tips in a V-shape usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure will help the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbee yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and sticky powder inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing central leaf whorl. Applying neem oil spray or approved insecticides early in the morning or late evening can effectively manage them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo mɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for extended periods, usually due to poor water drainage. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to flow away from the root system.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I tie their vines to tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji mikɛ wain tso lɛ fĩ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture energy for stem and tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the light and reduces leaf diseases caused by contact with damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛ na hewalɛ kɛha tso lɛ yitso kɛ eshishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa la lɛ he. ni ebaa baa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ shi

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and using grass mulch around the base of the plant lowers root temperature and stops flowers from falling.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i aba shi ni ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking, curling up, and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ, amɛmiibɔle amɛhe, ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit leaf curl virus. Spraying plants with mild soapy water or organic insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted in the hot afternoon but look healthy again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Plants lose water faster through their leaves during the hottest hours of the day than their roots can pull from the ground. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass helps conserve soil water so the plants stay upright.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and top-heavy fruit, making them vulnerable to strong winds. Supporting the fruiting stalk with sturdy wooden or bamboo props prevents the plant from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi aduawai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje shishi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my field better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decay, this nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as natural food for future crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite Nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight because their leaves are tender. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to block the harsh sunlight while their roots establish in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellow and staying small even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting leguminous crops like cowpea can help restore nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpea alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This natural fertilizer feeds nearby crops like maize, helping them grow stronger without competing for food.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot quickly during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and humid conditions. High moisture allows the fungal spores to spread easily from wet soil or infected pods to healthy ones.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa spores ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the stems of my cocoa trees swelling up and the leaves turning bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efu ni amɛbaai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread by small insects called mealybugs. The virus disrupts how nutrients travel through the tree, causing stems to swell and eventually reducing pod production.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Hela lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the cassava roots. Without oxygen, the roots begin to suffocate and rot under the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination. If the weather is too hot or dry, the plant saves its energy by dropping flowers instead of growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not reach deep into the soil. If root-damaging pests like nematodes are present, or if too many suckers grow around the main stem, the root system weakens and cannot hold the heavy plant upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi, tamɔ nematodes, loo ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔ tso ni tsii lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most cultivated crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Applying fertilizer while weeds are present actually feeds the weeds, allowing them to overpower your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ. ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli beni jwɛi yɛ lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ aye nii diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: Why do certified seeds from research centers perform better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agricultural research bodies are specifically bred for high yield, disease resistance, and local climate tolerance. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over generations and are more likely to carry diseases from the previous crop.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni Agricultural Research Agency lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ mli pɔtɛɛ akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ helai ni jɛ tsei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ aba

english: Why do seeds collected from my best-performing maize plants still produce some weak plants next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lolo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even when you select seeds from healthy parent plants, the offspring naturally inherit a mix of different traits. Because plants from the same parents do not grow equally, some will naturally be weaker and struggle to survive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ohala dumɔwui kɛjɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli po lɛ, Shi seshibii lɛ baaná sui srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni jɛ fɔlɔ kome mli lɛ edaaa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Adebɔɔ mli kooloi srɔtoi komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: If I cross two high-yielding tomato varieties, will all the resulting seeds produce big tomatoes?
ga: Kɛ mifo tomatoi enyɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ, Ani dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ baawo tomatoi wuji?

english: Bringing two good parent plants together does not mean all offspring will be equal. Some plants will inherit the best traits, while others will be disadvantaged, produce smaller fruit, or grow poorly.
ga: Nyɛ tsei kpakpai enyɔ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ seshibii fɛɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Tsei komɛi baaná sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ akɛ gboshinii. Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi baafee mɛi ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ, amɛhaa aduawai bibii loo amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of always saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli be fɛɛ be yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ ato?

english: Saved seeds produce crops with high variations in strength, causing weaker plants to get crowded out and die. Certified seeds are bred to ensure more uniform and equal growth across your field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. A fɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛ daa, po yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops wither and die when I plant too many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow too closely together, they do not grow equally. The weaker plants face intense hardship competing for soil, light, and water, which eventually causes them to die.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ edaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ naagbai ni mli wa kpeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ, la, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no baaha amɛgboi yɛ naagbee.

english: Why do smaller plants in my field dry up faster during a dry spell compared to the bigger ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛ akɛto tsei wuji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plants in the same field grow unequally. Stronger plants take up most of the water and sunlight, leaving the smaller, disadvantaged plants under severe hardship that causes them to dry up.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Tsei ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ baaŋɔ nu kɛ hulu la lɛ babaoo. Tsei bibii ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo lɛ ni ashiɔ koni amɛkɛ naagbai ni mli wa ni haa amɛgboɔ lɛ akpee.

english: Why is it necessary for me to pull out the small, weak seedlings from my crop rows early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra lɛ?

english: Weak seedlings struggle to compete with stronger plants. Removing them early prevents them from dying uselessly later and allows the stronger crops to use all available food and water.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛkɛ tsei ni he wa lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Amɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagboi ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he sɛɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why don't the smallest plants in my farm catch up to the bigger ones even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso bibioo fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsei wuji lɛ yeee eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Once a plant falls behind in growth, neighboring stronger plants shade it out and absorb nutrients faster, keeping the weaker plant in continuous hardship.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara blɛoo Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ naagbai kpeɔ daa.

english: Why are some cocoa seedlings in my nursery growing very tall while others from the same pod stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ ekomɛi miidara waa lɛ? be mli ni kookoo tsei krokomɛi Kɛjɛ pod kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ebatsɔ bibioo.

english: Just like children from the same mother and father grow differently, seeds from the same pod are never completely equal, leading to natural differences in growth speed.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛbii ni jɛ tsɛ kɛ nyɛ kome mli lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ pod kome mli lɛ yeee egbɔ kwraa kɔkɔɔkɔ. Enɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli srɔtofeemɔi baa bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ mli.

english: Why do cassava plants on the exact same farm patch produce very different sizes of tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dalɛi srɔtoi kwraa lɛ?

english: Inequality in plant strength means some cassava plants absorb food better than others, leaving the weaker stems disadvantaged and able to produce only small tubers.
ga: Tso lɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmei tsei komɛi ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ shweremɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii bibii pɛ.

english: Why do some pepper plants die shortly after transplanting while others in the same soil do very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tsei komɛi gboiɔ beni adu amɛ awo he kroko etsɛɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni pepper tsei srɔtoi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings vary in strength and resilience. The stress of transplanting creates hardship that stronger plants overcome, while weaker plants cannot survive it.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ hewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ mli. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ tsei ni atsakeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ kɛ naagbai ni tsei ni he wa lɛ baanyɛ aye nɔ kunim baa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe afii 10 ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 15 to 20 years, their root systems grow less efficient at taking up nutrients from the soil, causing pod production to naturally decline.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei ye fe afii 15 kɛyashi 20 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa pod feemɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to cut down cocoa trees infected with swollen shoot disease instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsofa ko kɛkɛ?

english: Swollen shoot disease is caused by a virus living deep inside the tree's sap, so surface chemical sprays cannot cure it; cutting down infected trees is the only way to stop the virus from spreading through the soil and air to healthy neighboring trees.
ga: Virus ko ni hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ji nɔ ni kɛ bud swollen hela lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does cocoa swollen shoot disease spread from one farm tree to another?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ji cocoa bud lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: The disease is carried by tiny insects called mealybugs, which are often moved around by ants or blown by the wind from infected branches onto healthy surrounding trees.
ga: Hela nɛɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii amli kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tsiɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ tswaa kɛyaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ. yɛ hewalɛ

english: If I cut down old cocoa trees, can I immediately plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same soil spots?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso momo lɛ Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Old cocoa soil often lacks key nutrients and may harbor hidden root diseases, so the land needs organic matter, proper soil treatment, and a short rest period before new seedlings are planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo shikpɔŋ momo lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ mli, ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ shishifã helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ be kuku dani adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight; fast-growing plantain trees provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas to shade and protect the cocoa during its early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛhaa kookoo lɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and drop leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots that struggle to reach deep groundwater during dry weather, so without sufficient shade and water retention in the soil, they shed leaves to preserve moisture.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni hulutsoo akahi shi.

english: How long will it take for new hybrid cocoa seedlings to start producing pods after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties are bred to mature early, typically starting to flower and yield pods within 2 to 3 years, compared to older traditional cocoa trees which took up to 5 years.
ga: Atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli, kɛ akɛto cacao tsei ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii enumɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What makes the new hybrid cocoa varieties better than the traditional cocoa trees our fathers planted?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ hi fe blema kookoo tsei ni wɔblematsɛmɛi lɛ du lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees grow faster, resist dry weather conditions better, and produce higher numbers of pods per tree than older traditional varieties.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe Ni ŋmeii ayibɔ ni yɔɔ tso kome mli lɛ fa fe ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ waa lɛ.

english: What short-term crops can I plant to feed my family while waiting for new tree crops to start yielding?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ tsei heei ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Quick-harvest crops like cassava, maize, and vegetables can be grown alongside young tree crops to provide food and fast household income during the first couple of years.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa mra tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe. koni akɛ niyenii kɛ shia shika ni anáa oya aha yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why is it important to prune extra branches off my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak and overcrowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree, which reduces fungal diseases like black pod and helps the tree direct its energy into producing large pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize make my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmã lɛ, ehaa mi-ŋmã lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans are special plants that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize growing right next to it.
ga: Beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground mainly because the soil holds too much water and does not drain well during heavy rains. Planting on ridges or raised mounds helps excess water drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi babaoo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni etsɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves wilt and curl during the hot afternoon to save moisture. If they get too much water, the leaves turn soft and yellow because the roots drown in the soggy soil.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ blɛoo ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a virus to the plant. Protecting young plants with nets or using neem oil spray can keep these insects away and save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ muawai kɛyaa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋshɔŋlooi bu tsei bibii ahe loo okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akabote ohe ni ehere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: What is eating holes in the central leaves of my maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the maize plant during the day. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract early stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔji akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they do not get enough water, when insects like mirids attack them, or if the soil lacks nutrients. Ensuring good shade and controlling pests during flowering helps the flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui batutua amɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli lɛ He ni akɛhaa hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their fruits while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pee tso lɛ shwieɔ eyibii fɛɛ lɛ? Ni eji bibioo lolo?

english: Pepper plants drop small fruits when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plants hold onto their fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai bibii. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ aduawai amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which is sent down to make the tuber under the ground grow big and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii, ni akɛmajeɔ shi, ni no haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Too many small shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for food and water in the soil. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tso lɛ) kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa saplings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four maize seeds into the exact same hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and small, poor quality cobs instead of strong, heavy-yielding plants.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmeii lɛ hu ji bibii ni ehiii kwraa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ tsii, nɛ e ngɛ he wami, nɛ e woɔ yiblii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. When the plant does not get enough food from the soil, it pulls nutrient reserves from its bottom leaves to keep the top growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Egbalaa niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eha ŋmei lɛ aya nɔ eda.

english: Why is it bad for me to grow maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant loves from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts resets the soil health.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing chewed holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the tops of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni atsɔ mli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves before the plant can fully grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water fills all the air gaps in wet soil, choking the roots and allowing fungal diseases to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry leaves and straw around the stems of their tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ amɛhe lɛ? Tomato tso lɛ shishi?

english: This practice is called mulching. Dry grass shields the ground from hot sun, preventing soil moisture from evaporating quickly and stopping weeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shɛɛɛ la he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ

english: Why should I wait until the rains become steady before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If you plant after just one heavy rain followed by a long dry spell, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die in the hot ground before their roots can reach deep water.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa kome ni hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress or sudden dry weather. The plant discards the flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do weeds in my garden make my crop yield much smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than cultivated crops. They steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your plants, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up even when I water them with river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ faa mli nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves despite watering often mean the water source is contaminated with harmful chemicals or heavy sediments, which damages the plant's roots and prevents it from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmeii ni tsii ewo nu jɛɛhe lɛ mli muji ni baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ nu ni awoɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaaa eŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can using polluted stream water to mix my crop sprays damage my plants?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ afite mitsei lɛ?

english: Yes, polluted or chemically affected water can react badly with crop sprays, reducing their effectiveness and causing chemical burns or sickness on plant leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji loo tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ. kɛ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ baa shi ni ekɛ shãa loo hela ni jɛɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baa lɛ mli baa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the surrounding soil too quickly for their young roots to absorb moisture.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, extreme dry spells, or irregular watering, which forces the plant to conserve energy by dropping flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are holes appearing all over my cassava leaves and causing them to fall off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Holes and early leaf loss on cassava plants are usually caused by insect pests like green mites or caterpillars feeding on the leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to make food and grow large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ baai ni fiteɔ mra yɛ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the stems of my tomato plants turning black and rotting right near the ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Black, rotting stems near the soil line are caused by fungal diseases that thrive in overly wet, poorly drained soil, which chokes the stem and cuts off water to the rest of the plant.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei diji ni fiteɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ nu kɛyaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, skinny plants with small or empty ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmãa toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is missing nutrients before my crops start failing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi amɛfite?

english: You can spot nutrient deficiencies early if older leaves turn yellow between the veins, growth slows down unnaturally, or plants bloom much later than expected.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mra. Kɛji baai ni egbɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ateŋ lɛ Dalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Aloo tsei lɛ fɔfɔi yɛ sɛɛ mli kwraa fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers rotting quickly inside my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miifite oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot rapidly in storage if they were bruised during harvesting, exposed to excess moisture, or stored in hot areas without proper airflow.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛfite yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine mli loo ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Can I harvest my cassava tubers bit by bit, or do I have to dig up the whole plant at once?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ okpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ fãi bibii amli? Aloo esa akɛ mafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: You can harvest tubers gradually by carefully digging around the base and cutting off mature roots while leaving the plant in the soil to keep the remaining tubers fresh.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ shishifãi ni eda lɛ ni oshi tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi ehee.

english: Why is it better to collect small amounts of food from the farm daily instead of harvesting everything at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaabua niyenii fioo ko naa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Many fresh crops like vegetables and roots spoil quickly after picking. Leaving crops attached to the living plant in the soil acts as natural storage until you are ready to eat or sell them.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ ehee babaoo, tamɔ aduawai kɛ shishifãi lɛ, fiteɔ oya kɛji ajie amɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni okɛkpɛtɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaaye loo obaahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield only a few pounds of harvest every few days instead of producing everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii pound fioo pɛ daa gbii fioo komɛi moŋ fe nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Crops produce flowers and fruit in stages based on sunlight and water. This natural staggered growth means food matures gradually over days or weeks rather than all on one day.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ nu nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ ni bɛ fã kome nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ekwɛɔ yɛ gbii loo otsii babaoo mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ

english: Why is it so difficult to completely uproot a plant after it has been growing on the farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ abaajie tsei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: As crops mature, their root systems grow thick, deep, and woody to hold the plant firmly in the ground and draw water from deep underground, making them strong and hard to pull out.
ga: Beni tsei daraa Amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse, amɛmli kwɔ, ni amɛji tsei ni baaha tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛhe wa ni ewaa akɛ abaajie amɛ.

english: Why do some crops keep sprouting back even after I think I have pulled them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ misusuɔ akɛ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Certain crops and weeds store energy in underground roots or tubers. If even a small piece of the root remains buried after uprooting, it can grow back into a full plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ jwɛi komɛi kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifã lɛ fã bibioo ko po Ehi shi ni afu yɛ be mli ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eda ekoŋŋ ni etsɔ tso ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do tree crops build such thick roots deep down in the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Deep roots act like heavy anchors to support large plants against strong winds, while also searching deep into the soil for groundwater to survive dry seasons.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔkei ni tsii ni akɛfiɔ tsei wuji anaa koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛtaoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when a long-term crop has reached the end of its life and needs to be totally cleared from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eshɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee ni ehe miihia ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa?

english: A crop needs complete uprooting when its stems become overly woody, leaf production slows down significantly, and it stops producing meaningful yields despite good care.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii kwraa kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ batsɔ tsei tsɔ. Baa lɛ feemɔ baa shi waa. ni ebaakpa yibiiwoo ni shishinumɔ yɔɔ he lɛ hamɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why does it take so many days of hard labor on the farm just to collect a small harvest at first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni otsu nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli gbii babaoo dani okpa nɔ ko fioo yɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: In the early stages of harvesting, plants are still developing, so mature food is spread out. Initial work yields small amounts, but continued care leads to larger accumulated harvests over time.
ga: Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli Tso lɛ miiya hiɛ lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni egbɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Shishijee nitsumɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo ko pɛ. Shi kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni abua naa babaoo baa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Is it safe to leave mature root crops in the ground for a long time before taking them home?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi tsei ni eda lɛ ashishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani akɛba shia?

english: Root crops can stay safe in dry soil for a while, but leaving them too long during heavy rains can cause them to rot, become woody, or get eaten by soil pests.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ shweshweeshwe be ko. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo. etsɔ tso loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye

english: Why do some long-term crops require so much work that farmers end up spending days living on distant farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo aahu akɛ okwaafoi yeɔ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Perennial crops and root plants need continuous clearing, weeding, and staggered harvesting over long periods. Staying near the farm saves energy and time during heavy harvest seasons.
