ga: Nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo kɛ shishifãi biɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli daa, ajie jwɛi, ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ obɛŋkɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ kɛ be baa shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be ni mli wa lɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my banana plants free from diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-banana tsei lɛ akaye helai?

english: Keeping banana plants free from disease involves maintaining clean field hygiene, removing dead or infected leaves regularly, and giving plants proper care step-by-step so they stay strong enough to resist infections.
ga: Nɔ ni fata banana tsei ahe ni helai akamɔ amɛ lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ hetsemɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli. Jiemɔ baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa. kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ ni sa, fitsofitso, koni amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai.

english: What usually causes crop diseases to spread so quickly on a farm?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Crop diseases are often caused by microscopic fungi or bacteria that thrive when fields are neglected, overly damp, or when sick plant materials are left near healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi bibii ni shwereɔ kɛji aku hiɛ ashwie he ko nɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ahe helai baa. ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nibii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Can I protect my crops from sickness just by changing how I do my daily farm work?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hela he kɛtsɔ bɔ ni mitsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi lɛ tsakemɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, carrying out routine tasks like weeding, pruning, and clearing dead plants consistently and carefully helps eliminate places where diseases hide and spread.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitsumɔi ni afeɔ daa tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ ajiemɔ daa kɛ hiɛdɔɔ baaye abua ni ajie hei ni hela baanyɛ ahi shi ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ.

english: Why is it better to clear and care for my farm gradually instead of doing all the heavy work at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooŋɔ blɛoo lɛ? Tsɔɔmɔ ni okwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nitsumɔ ni wa lɛ fɛɛ shikome najiaŋ?

english: Working on your farm step-by-step prevents plant stress, reduces the chance of damaging roots or stems, and allows you to catch and fix early disease signs before they cover the whole field.
ga: Kɛ́ otsu oŋmɔ lɛ he nii shikome shikome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akatse tsei ahe haomɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ shishifã loo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baafite lɛ shi. ni ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ helai ahe naagbai ni otsuɔ he nii yɛ amɛshishijee be mli dani amɛhaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Does pruning my plants slowly over time help keep them healthier?
ga: Mi tsei lɛ ni mikɛfoɔ mli fiofio Ani eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, pruning bit by bit allows the plant to heal its wounds safely, preventing open cuts from attracting pests and disease-causing organisms.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ bibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsaa epilamɔi lɛ shweshweeshwe. Etsiɔ pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nibii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ.

english: How does attending to my crops little by little improve my final harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ nɔ fioo fioo lɛ baanyɛ aha minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Giving your crops consistent, gradual attention ensures each plant gets adequate nutrients, sunlight, and air, leading to cleaner, disease-free fruits.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nii lɛ akwɛmɔ daa kɛ fiofio lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibii lɛ ahe baatse ni hela ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do crops react better when I introduce changes to my field routine step by step?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mifee tsakemɔi fiofio yɛ miŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi amli lɛ?

english: Crops need time to adapt to new growing conditions, so gradual adjustments prevent soil shock and allow plants to build up immunity against common diseases.
ga: Be he miihia tsei koni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi heei ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsakemɔi ni afeɔ fiofio lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akahoso. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni tsiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa lɛ anaa

english: How do I test a new farming practice I saw in another community on my own field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka okwaayeli nifeemɔi heei ni minaa yɛ akutsei krokomɛi amli yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ makwɛ?

english: You can start by applying the new technique on a small section of your farm first, taking time to learn how your crops respond before adopting it across your entire field.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje shishi kɛtsɔ ŋaa hee ko ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fã bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ be akase bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa dani okɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to visit other farms to observe their methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mayasara ŋmɔji krokomɛi koni mayakwɛ gbɛi ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Visiting other farms allows you to see practical techniques that work in real life, helping you learn practical steps to control diseases and improve crop growth.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi krokomɛi anɔ saramɔ Ebaaha ona ŋaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ shihilɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ gbɛi ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni oootsɔ nɔ oye helai anɔ ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do banana plants become weak and sick when regular field care is ignored?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ nɔ daa lɛ?

english: Without regular maintenance like removing old suckers and clearing weeds, moisture builds up around the banana stem, creating an ideal environment for pests and diseases to attack.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ daa tamɔ ŋmeii momoi ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ, Moisture buaa ehe naa yɛ banana tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant rebuild its green chlorophyll and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛsaa amɛ chlorophyll eŋɔli lɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: What causes my pepper plants to produce flowers that drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, lack sufficient water, or lack pollinators like bees. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding strong chemicals during flowering helps fruits to set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollinators tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ. Kɛ́ ahã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ajie tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛwaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miishwie amɛbii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods often wither and turn black—a condition known as cherelle wilt—when the tree lacks water or nutrients, gets too much direct sun, or is attacked by fungal diseases. Providing shade and keeping the soil fertile reduces pod drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Beni tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa lɛ Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ haa pod ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I rotate my farm land between planting maize and planting groundnuts or cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake mi-acreage lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ kɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which restores land naturally after heavy-feeding crops like maize have used up the soil nutrients.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akuɔ adebɔɔ mli hei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ beni kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become small and distorted when the soil is hard, compact, or stony, which physically blocks the root from expanding downward. Building high, loose soil mounds allows the tubers room to swell easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa yitso lɛ he gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to give me a good harvest of cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmei kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil for cassava feels loose and crumbly in your hands, drains excess water easily, and contains dark organic material from old leaves or manure, which feeds the roots without causing them to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmei baanu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ oniji amli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up so fast during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water rapidly in hot, dry winds. During dry periods, the plant intentionally sheds its outer leaves to conserve water in its main trunk so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni edɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ eshwieɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛ nu ato tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How does heavy rainfall immediately after a dry spell affect my tomato fruits?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa mi tomato yibiiwoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Sudden heavy rain after drought makes tomato plants soak up water too quickly, causing the inside of the fruit to swell faster than the skin can stretch, which splits the skin open and invites rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ fuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ. Enɛ haa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ gbeleɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do I need to prune extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to move freely through the tree. This dries out excess moisture that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ agbi, ni ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crop seeds after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui titrii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and can lie dormant in the soil for years waiting for water. Crop seeds are more delicate and require extra care, proper planting depth, and weed clearing to compete successfully.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ ni emɛ nu afii babaoo Dumɔwui lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ ni ebiɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ. Dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli koni aye omanye yɛ akaŋshii mli.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot so quickly after I harvest them, even before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and release heat after being picked. Stacking them tightly in non-ventilated crates traps heat and moisture, which speeds up decay before they can reach buyers.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kpo beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ baaha efite oya dani eshɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have weak root systems and delicate leaves that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates living shade that cools the soil and protects the seedlings.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start turning black and bitter just two days after digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ lɛ bɔi ediŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ beni atsa lɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is severed from its root system, a natural chemical reaction begins as oxygen enters the flesh. This reaction causes rapid internal decay within 48 hours unless the tubers are cooked or processed into gari.
ga: Beni afoɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ ko jeɔ shishi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ boteɔ loo lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa mligbɛ fitemɔ baa oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli ja ahoo ŋmeii lɛ loo afee amɛ Gari.

english: Why do my maize plants fall flat on the ground whenever rain and heavy winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over easily when planted too close together or when soil lacks proper nutrients like potassium. High planting density leads to thin stalks, while poor nutrients prevent roots from anchoring firmly into the earth.
ga: Abele shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa tamɔ potassium bɛ lɛ, dumɔwui ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esaaa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers have a natural resting period called dormancy. Once this natural period ends, internal plant hormones automatically signal the tuber to sprout and grow shoots, regardless of whether it is buried in dirt or stored on a shelf.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli be nɛɛ ba naagbee lɛ, tso mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ haa bulbs lɛ leɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ kɔɔɔ he eko kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo akɛto adeka nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning small instead of growing broad and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a plant virus. These pests feed on leaf sap, which disrupts the leaf's normal growth pattern and causes it to wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo mites, loo tsei amli helai ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ gbalaa bɔ ni baai lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ mli, ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches so small when I leave many shoots growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: All the sucker shoots attached to a main plantain tree compete for the exact same ground nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers allows all the soil energy to feed a single plant, resulting in larger fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tso kome mli. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Sudden heavy rain after a dry period makes the watermelon absorbs water faster than its outer skin can expand. The rapid pressure build-up inside the fruit causes the outer rind to crack open.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa watermelon lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔnyɛɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why is my farm producing smaller harvests every year even though I use the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Every crop absorbs specific food elements from the soil to grow. Planting the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains those specific nutrients out of the earth unless you rest the soil, add manure, or rotate crops.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ja okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ohe, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli, loo otsake ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do insects appear inside my sealed bags of dried maize even when I cleaned the grain before storing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛwo mli lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii dani mikɛtoɔ moŋ.

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside the maize grains while the crop is still standing in the field. When the grain is stored in warm conditions, these hidden eggs hatch inside the sealed bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni mli edɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the intense sun scorches their leaves and dries out the soil before their root systems are strong enough to absorb enough water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baatsi hulu lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping your maize grow stronger and yield better without requiring as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii kpakpai ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why does my cassava turn tough and woody if I leave it in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As a cassava plant grows older, it uses the starch in its roots to build strong woody fibers to support the plant. Harvesting at the right time ensures the roots remain full of soft, soft-cooking starch rather than hard fiber.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ eda Ekɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni mli wa ni baaye abua ŋmei tso lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli eyiɔ lolo kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ahoo yɛ ŋmeii ni wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do the central leaves of my maize plants look like they have holes eaten through them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu yɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This pattern of damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide deep inside the growing point (funnel) of the maize plant during the day and feed on the young leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛhei (cones) lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce a tiny bunch if I let all the shoot suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Ni kɛji miha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain lɛ he hu?

english: All the suckers growing around a plantain stem share the same food and water source from the main plant. Leaving too many suckers forces the mother plant to divide its energy, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhe kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ aja. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Plant roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant roots and cause the fertilizer to sit uselessly on the surface until it blows away or loses its nutrient value.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he kɛyashi ebaaho loo ebaafite niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ.

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and inactive, preventing flowers from being fertilized. The plant naturally drops these unfertilized flowers to conserve its energy and moisture.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato pollen lɛ baagbi ni ebaafee nɔ ni tsuuu nii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli nɛɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my seed yams rot in the mound when heavy rains fall right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam seed tubers need oxygen in the soil to wake up and sprout. If the mound stays waterlogged from heavy rains, oxygen cannot reach the tuber, causing it to suffocate and attract rotting fungi and bacteria.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, nu eyi gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ, Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Ehaa mɔ mumɔ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and taller than my crops early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, meaning their roots spread faster to grab water and nutrients before crop seeds can fully establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛmu nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually a sign of insect attack, such as aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or a virus transmitted by those insects that stunts overall plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miinu nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ miitutua amɛ. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ Enɛ haaa tso lɛ adara kwraa.

english: Is growing watermelon as profitable as growing cocoa in Ghana?
ga: Ani watermelon dumɔ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ kookoo dumɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: While cocoa takes several years to produce but gives steady income, watermelon matures in just 2 to 3 months, allowing for faster returns on investment and multiple harvests in a single year.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ afii babaoo dani anyɛɔ afeɔ kookoo moŋ, shi ehaa anáa shika ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi watermelon lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli, ni no haa anáa shika ni awo mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo oya, ni akpaa nibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli.

english: How do I know if I will make money after spending time and cash to plant my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji maná shika beni mikɛ be kɛ shika etsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Profit comes from good yield and market timing; choosing crops with high market demand and planning harvest during off-peak seasons ensures higher prices and better profits.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi jɛɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ jarayeli be mli. Nibii ni jara wa ni ataoɔ waa lɛ ni ahalaa kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ lɛ baaha jara aya hiɛ ni sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai hu aba.

english: How do I find market women or buyers for my fruits when harvest time comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana jara nɔ yei loo mɛi ni baahe mi yibii lɛ beni kpamɔ be shɛɔ lɛ?

english: You can connect with buyers early by visiting local market centers, joining a local farmers' group, or informing agricultural extension officers who often link farmers directly to traders.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ abɔ mra. Kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ yaa nɔ Okɛ ohe awo maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko mli Aloo ha okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni fɔɔ okwaafoi kɛ jarayelɔi tsakpaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ale.

english: Are there official government prices for selling fruits like watermelon, or do I set my own price?
ga: Ani nɔyeli ko yɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ aduawai tamɔ watermelon jara? Aloo mi diɛŋtsɛ mawo jara lɛ?

english: Unlike cocoa which has a fixed price set by the government, fresh fruits like watermelon operate on a open market where prices are negotiated between you and the buyer based on supply, demand, and fruit size.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ kookoo, ni nɔyeli lɛ eto jara ni ato lɛ, aduawai heei tamɔ watermelon tsuɔ nii yɛ jara ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ, he ni bo kɛ hɔlɔlɔ lɛ susuɔ jara he yɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa, nɔ ni ataoɔ, kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ.

english: If I plant five acres of land, how much crop yield should I expect?
ga: Kɛji midu shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre enumɔ lɛ Yibii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ?

english: Yield depends on seed quality, soil fertility, and proper spacing; on average, five well-managed acres of watermelon can produce thousands of marketable fruits.
ga: Yibiiwoo lɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ he ni sa Kɛ aja mli lɛ, watermelon ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni dalɛ ji acre enumɔ baanyɛ awo yibii akpei abɔ ni abaanyɛ ahé.

english: How does watermelon vine growth behave across a large field?
ga: Te watermelon wain tsei lɛ adalɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ mli?

english: Watermelon plants grow by spreading long vines along the ground, which cover the soil, reduce weed growth, and help keep the soil moist.
ga: Watermelon tsei daa kɛtsɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do some of my crops grow healthy leaves but fail to bring heavy fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ tsei ni wa shi amɛwooo yibii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants grow excess leaves instead of flowers; crops need balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to turn flowers into big, heavy fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai ni fa fe nine yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsei hia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiam. Koni etsake fɔfɔi lɛ ewo aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect watermelons when they are ripening?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa watermelon he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ ekwɛ̃?

english: Excessive rain near harvest time causes the fruits to absorb too much water, which can cause them to split open or become less sweet.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛfee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fioo.

english: How do I know that my watermelon is fully mature and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ watermelon lɛ eda ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A watermelon is ready when the ground spot underneath turns from white to creamy yellow and the small curled tendril closest to the fruit stem turns brown and dry.
ga: Watermelon lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ he lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eyɛŋ kɛbatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. kɛ niji bibii Bend ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai lɛ tso lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ.

english: How long can harvested watermelons stay on the farm before they start to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ watermelon ni akpa lɛ baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: Harvested watermelons can stay good for 1 to 2 weeks if stored under shade in a cool, dry area away from direct sunlight.
ga: Watermelon ni akpa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto hulutsoo shishi yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi. Ekɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ teŋ jɛkɛ

english: If I need food right away, is it better to harvest all my cassava at once or leave some in the ground?
ga: Kɛji niyenii he miihia bo amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ani ehi akɛ obaabua ŋmei lɛ fɛɛ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Cassava acts as its own underground storage and can stay safe in the soil for months after maturing. Harvesting the whole field at once can cause the roots to rot within days if you cannot consume or sell them all quickly.
ga: Cassava tsuɔ nii akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nutoohe ni ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Gbɛ muu fɛɛ ni oookpa shikome lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji onyɛɛɛ oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it does not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Maize is ready for harvest as dry grain when the outer leaves turn completely brown and dry, and a small black spot appears at the base of each kernel where it connects to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmeii ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni kɛ ŋmei lɛ tsa lɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a plant disease or just because of lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ahe helai miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Drought makes whole fields wilt evenly during hot sun, but plants bounce back a bit in the cool evening. Disease usually starts on a few plants, causing spots, color patterns, or rotting that spreads to nearby plants regardless of rainfall.
ga: Hɔmɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ hu shwieɔ shi. amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Shi tso lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ fioo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei komɛi amli, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ, sui, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baa ekɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are stronger and grow faster than farm crops. They act like unwanted guests, stealing the water, soil food, and sunlight that your crops need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ahe wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa bo koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller crops every year even though I work hard on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every season to grow. If you keep planting without adding organic manure, compost, or fertilizer to replenish the land, the soil becomes exhausted and yields decrease.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli bɔni afee ni amɛdara. Kɛji odu ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he kɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plants grow thin and produce small fruits when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. Giving plants proper space allows each one to feed well and grow full yields.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, he ko, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso yeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans or cowpeas in the same farm with their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This acts like natural food for the maize, helping it grow stronger without tiring out the land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ. Ye obua ni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛhaaa sũ lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I pluck off some leaves from my tomato plants while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ be mli ni amɛmiida lolo lɛ?

english: Removing lower, old, or extra leaves directs the plant's water and nutrients into growing bigger tomatoes instead of wasting energy on maintaining unnecessary foliage.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ, loo ni fa fe no lɛ, ebaaha nu kɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ lɛ baaha tomatoi wuji aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: You can save traditional seed varieties, but modern hybrid seeds lose their strength after the first harvest. Planting saved hybrid seeds usually leads to weak crops and lower yields, so buying certified seed gives better results.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shishijee dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ ato he. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do my harvested grains get destroyed by insects in my storehouse after a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi nitoohe lɛ kpata dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛkɛ?

english: Grains spoil mainly because they were not completely dry before storing or because storage bags were not airtight. Drying grains thoroughly under the sun and keeping them in tightly sealed bags starves insects of air and moisture.
ga: Ŋmãa babaoo fiteɔ ejaakɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ loo akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote kotoku ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli hewɔ. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ baaha kooloi bibii lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees dry up and die when there is a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even big, established cocoa trees need a steady supply of soil water. During long droughts, groundwater levels drop deeper than root systems can reach, causing the leaves to dry out and the whole tree to eventually wither.
ga: Kookoo tsei wuji ni etswa shi shiŋŋ lɛ po he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu daa. Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baa shi fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are suffering from a lack of water before they start dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu efo mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli dani amɛgboi?

english: When cocoa trees lack water, their leaves wilt, turn yellow or brown at the edges, and start dropping early as the tree tries to conserve moisture.
ga: Beni nu bɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. Eshishigbɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Ni ejeɔ shishi efoɔ oya beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite lɛ.

english: What can I put on the soil around my crops to keep the ground from drying out quickly?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ? Miŋmɔshi nibii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi oya?

english: Covering the ground around crop bases with dry leaves, grass, or crop waste—a practice called mulching—traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and reduces water evaporation.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Base tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching lɛ—haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why do I need to keep large trees on my farm when growing cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tsei wuji anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Large shade trees protect cocoa leaves from harsh, direct sunlight and help keep the soil cool and moist, which protects the cocoa trees during dry spells.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: What kind of soil conditions should I look for before buying land to plant cocoa?
ga: Dani obaahe shikpɔŋ ni okɛbaadu kookoo lɛ, mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ esa akɛ osusu he?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, fertile soil that drains well so roots do not rot, but can still hold enough moisture during dry months.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo. Shi ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa hu yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for me to plant my land all at once or grow my cocoa farm gradually over several years?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo fiofio? Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ adu kookoo?

english: Planting gradually allows you to properly clear land, establish shade trees, and manage water supply for small sections at a time, lowering the risk of mass seedling loss.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu fiofio lɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔɔ tsei ni baaha hulutsoo aba. ni akwɛ nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ nɔ yɛ fãi bibii amli yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo baafite lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die so easily in direct heat compared to older trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ mli kɛ akɛto kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender stems, meaning they cannot reach deep soil moisture or store water like older, established trees.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kookoo tsei nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he loo amɛhiɛ nu mli tamɔ tsei ni edara lɛ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods turn black and fall off the tree during very hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. When the tree experiences severe heat or water stress, it sheds young pods to save its energy and stay alive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ Eshwieɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn pale green or yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean the tree is under heat or drought stress, causing it to slow down food production and shed leaves to save water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ latsaa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. Enɛ haa niyenii ni afeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo, ni baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he.

english: How does strong sunlight affect cocoa trees that do not have any shade over them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa kookoo tso ni hulutsoo bɛ he lɛ he?

english: Without shade, strong sunlight overheats cocoa leaves, burns their surfaces, and forces the tree to lose water faster than its roots can pull from the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha kookoo baai lɛ adɔ fe nine, ebaashã ŋwɛi ni enyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni eha nu lɛ afite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans or groundnuts with maize helps the soil. Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer to help your maize grow taller and produce larger ears.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ehaa toi lɛ daraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and strength. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the crop's growth will keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing huge and bushy, but the roots underneath stay very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji bibii kwraa lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, sweet potatoes put all their energy into growing big top leaves instead of underground tubers. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers allows the plant to focus on swelling its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Sweet potatoes kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai wuji anɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni efuu lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or insecticidal soap removes these pests and stops leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni ekpa baai lɛ afitemɔ.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to drop off without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting in suitable seasons ensures the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off, keeping the roots oxygenated and safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody so quickly when rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni amɛtsɔɔ tso oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the okra plant panics and tries to quickly dry its pods to produce seeds before it dies. Regular watering keeps the pods soft, tender, and good for harvest.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Okra tso lɛ baashe gbeyei ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya koni ekɛ dumɔwui aba dani amɛgboi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: How can I tell if my yams are fully mature and ready to dig up without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa ni efiteee amɛ?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up. This change shows that the plant has finished feeding and storing energy down in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cabbage plants produce loose, leafy tops instead of forming a tight, hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ miiwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii ni wa ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head properly if they lack water during their middle growth stage or if the soil lacks potassium. Providing steady water and balanced nutrients ensures the center leaves wrap tightly together into a solid head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ atsɔ yitso jogbaŋŋ kɛji nu bɛ emli yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ yitso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grown inside a greenhouse look healthier than the ones I plant directly in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ feɔ fɛo fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Greenhouses create a controlled environment that protects crops from extreme heat, heavy rainfall, pests, and soil-borne diseases. In an open field, crops are exposed to unpredictable weather and local pests that can stress the plants and reduce growth.
ga: Greenhouses lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii naa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ jɛmɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha amɛdalɛ aba shi lɛ.

english: Why do imported high-yielding seeds sometimes fail to grow well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Imported seeds are often developed for cooler or controlled climates with specific soil conditions. Without the exact water, temperature, and nutrient levels they were bred for, they struggle to adapt to the local climate and native soil conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ loo akudɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, kɛji nu, latsaa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi bɛ. Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why did my crop leaves turn brown and dry up after I applied fertilizer during a hot week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs sufficient moisture in the soil to dissolve properly. When applied during hot, dry weather, the concentrated salts draw water out of the roots instead of feeding them, which burns the plant leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛtsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ Nuŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why does adding animal manure help my soil stay moist longer than using only chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure adds organic matter that acts like a sponge, improving the soil's structure so it can hold water and nutrients over long periods. Chemical fertilizers feed the plant directly but do not improve the physical structure or water-holding capacity of the soil.
ga: Manure kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji fataa he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ shi ehaaa sũ lɛ mli nibii loo bɔ ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise against planting cassava too close to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ adu cassava yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava grows rapidly and has aggressive roots that steal water and essential soil nutrients from the cocoa roots. It also grows tall quickly, blocking the sunlight young cocoa trees need to build strength.
ga: Cassava daa oya ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Kɛfata he lɛ, ekɛlɛ ni eyaa oya ni etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ama amɛhewalɛ nɔ amɛma shi.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different pesticides together to spray my vegetable farm at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ srɔtoi enyɔ baafutu koni mikɛshwie mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Mixing different pesticides without expert guidance can cause a chemical reaction that reduces their effectiveness, damages crop leaves, or leaves harmful toxic residues on the food crops you plan to sell.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛfutuɔ mli Kɛji ŋaawoo ni he esa bɛ lɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ aba shi, efite tsei ahe baai, loo eshi nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii ni oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp shade. Rain drops splash the fungal spores from the ground or infected leaves onto the pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my young maize leaves after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworm kpata mi-baby corn baai lɛ ahiɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The warm, moist conditions following early rains trigger adult moths to lay eggs on the fresh, tender maize leaves. The eggs hatch rapidly into hungry caterpillars that feed on the soft plant tissue.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni nyiɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ha ŋmeii ni eda lɛ wo amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Wɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ tso lɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, making it impossible for fertilization to occur. When the flowers cannot be fertilized, the plant sheds them to save its remaining water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Beni fɔfɔi ko nyɛɛɛ ashɛre ŋmɔshi nii Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do crops harvested from saved hybrid seeds yield less than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ amli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically created by crossing two distinct parent plants for high yield in the first generation. When you save and replant those seeds, the second generation loses that combined strength and yields fewer, less uniform crops.
ga: Abɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Beni okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ toɔ ni oduɔ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli daa.

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: How long should my cocoa seedlings stay in the nursery before I transplant them to the farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa seedlings typically need about 5 to 6 months in the nursery so their stems become sturdy and root systems grow strong enough to survive being moved into the open field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cocoa dumɔwui lɛ biɔ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa. Ni shishifãi lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and lose moisture faster than the roots can absorb water, which is why they require shade from crops like plantain or shade trees during their early years.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Should I cut down all the large wild trees on my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ koo mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: No, leaving selected tall trees provides natural shade, maintains soil moisture, and protects fragile cocoa plants from harsh heat and strong winds.
ga: Dabi, tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni obu kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield plenty of pods in some months but almost nothing in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, ni ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ ekrokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa production follows rainfall patterns, creating a main harvest season (usually from October to February in Ghana) and a smaller light crop season later in the year.
ga: Cocoa feemɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛjianɔtoo sɛɛ. ni haa ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ baa (bei pii lɛ October kɛyashi February yɛ Ghana) kɛ dumɔ be bibioo kɛha tsei bibii yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why do so many small cocoa flowers drop off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage form pods because of limited nutrients, dry weather, or inadequate insect pollination.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ feɔ pods yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Can I continue growing cocoa on the same piece of land for many years?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo ni baaba lɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa is a long-term tree crop that can stay productive on the same land for 25 to 30 years or more if the soil is properly fertilized and weeds and pests are managed.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ daa ni baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛji akɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I do not trim off the unnecessary extra branches?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifolɔɔɔ niji ni fata he ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Unpruned branches block sunlight and airflow while wasting plant energy, which leads to fewer cocoa pods and creates damp conditions that encourage diseases.
ga: Niji ni afolɔko amɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ tsei ahewalɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ baa shi. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ helai srɔtoi ahe hewalɛ baa

english: Continuous rain creates wet conditions that allow the black pod fungus to grow and spread rapidly across green pods if humidity remains trapped in the farm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ eha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi eba. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni ji black pod lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ oya. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo

english: If my old cocoa trees stop bearing good fruit, do I have to cut them all down and start over?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ kpa yibiiwoo hu? Ani esa akɛ mafo mli fɛɛ ni mabɔi ekoŋŋ?

english: Not always; old trees can often be pruned heavily or grafted with fresh shoots to rejuvenate them without having to clear the entire farm and wait for new roots to grow.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be; Bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ afo tsei momo lɛ amli waa loo akɛ ŋmeii heei awo mli koni ekɛha amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni amɛmɛ ni shishifãi heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow with small holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with holes are usually a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves and stealing nutrients from the plant. Catching them early and applying recommended neem oil or pest control early in the morning can protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu yɔɔ mli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ awo ohe leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap and spreading viruses. Spraying your plants with a mild soapy water solution or neem extract helps control these insects and stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ekɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ekpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet soil, protecting the plant from fungal rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni ji hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does planting my maize seeds too close together give me smaller corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form large, fully filled cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) forces the main plantain tree to share its water and food, leading to small fruit bunches. Leaving only the main stem and one or two healthy suckers ensures you get large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ baaha ehe bahia ni plantain titri lɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii. nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso yibii bibii Kɛ́ oshwɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ pɛ kɛ tso yibii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha onine ashɛ plantain tso agbo ni tsii nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them in heavy clay soils during rain. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss when soil moisture is low. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby helps retain soil moisture and protects young cocoa trees from direct sun damage.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu nii?

english: If your soil is very hard, pale, or produced weak crops with light green leaves last season, it lacks nutrients. Mixing well-rotted animal manure or compost into the soil before planting rebuilds its fertility naturally.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo sũ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha eshishitoo mlai lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to extreme heat or irregular watering, which stresses the plant. Watering steadily at the base and placing dry grass mulch around the soil keeps roots cool and helps flowers stay on to form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni esaaa lɛ hewɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Numɔ shishitoo lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo ehe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛ tomato su lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm when crop seedlings are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop seedlings and quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need to survive. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks gives your crops a strong head start for a bigger yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Groundnuts and beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow stronger without exhausting the land.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni edaraa waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato flowers become stressed and cannot pollinate properly, causing the plant to shed its flowers to save energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up quickly even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellowing plantain leaves during heavy rain often mean poor drainage around the roots or a fungal attack like Sigatoka disease, which stops the leaves from taking in food and sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ sigatoka, ni haaa baai lɛ aná niyenii kɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions, especially during the rainy season when moisture stays on the pods for too long.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize farm have small holes and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: Chewed leaves on maize are usually caused by armyworms or caterpillars that hide inside the leaf whorl and feed on the soft leaf tissue while the plant is growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii lɛ amli fãji beni tso lɛ miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni amɛyeɔ yɛ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I heap up soil into high mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo sũ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ dani madu ŋmeii?

english: Making high soil mounds creates loose, soft earth that lets yam tubers expand easily without hitting hard soil, while protecting the seed yam from rotting in standing water.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo baa. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry cut grass help my pepper plants grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mulch wo mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and reuse seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize crop for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their specialized breeding strength after the first harvest, so planting saved hybrid seeds will result in uneven crop growth, weak plants, and small yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛhe saji awo mli ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni dalɛ ejaaa, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have flooded the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haaa aná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my pepper fruits turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is often caused by uneven watering during hot periods, which prevents the plant from moving calcium from the soil to the tip of the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ kɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tso yibii ni miida lɛ naa.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support; however, excessive flower drop happens when the tree suffers from water stress during dry spells or lacks adequate soil nutrients.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil for the next crop instead of exhausting it.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite.

english: Why do I need to raise soil mounds or ridges before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo gɔŋ lɛ loo ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand into large, smooth tubers; planting them in soft mounds makes root growth easier and prevents waterlogging around the growing tubers.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni etsɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya, ni ehaaa nu akabɔle bulb ni miida lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward during high afternoon heat as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce surface area and limit water evaporation while waiting for cooler temperatures.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni akɛtsi nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Why are narrow, sword-shaped suckers better for planting plantains than suckers with broad, wide leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ klante lɛ hi kɛha plantains ni miida lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Narrow-leaf sword suckers have strong, undamaged food reservoirs in their corms and established roots, allowing them to grow faster and yield bigger bunches than wide-leaf water suckers.
ga: Klante suckers ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni efiteee yɛ rhizomes kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, meaning their root systems absorb moisture and fertilizer much faster than cultivated crop seeds, allowing them to steal sunlight if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ ni ehe wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ oya.

english: What happens if I leave my cassava tubers in the ground for too long past maturity?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If cassava is left in the soil too long past its peak maturity, the edible starch turns into tough wood fibers, making the tubers hard, watery, and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashi eho eshishijee he lɛ, ŋmei ni ayeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ wa, amɛmli nu, ni amɛhoomɔ wa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil or get small holes in them during storage in the room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ egbo loo eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Be mli ni akɛ nibii toɔ tsu lɛ mli?

english: Insects called weevils attack maize if the grain was not dried fully before storage; damp grain attracts pests and molds that feed on the inside of the seed.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa Tso lɛ baaye shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ hɔmɔ koni ekɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf shade and cool moisture that protect the tender cocoa seedlings during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden drought stress, which prevents the plant from successfully pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ ba. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee pollination ni amɛwo yibii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy rains flood my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching cassava roots, effectively suffocating them and allowing rot-causing soil fungi to quickly infect the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ. ni oha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the undersides of the leaves or spreading a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why did my maize germinate well but then completely stop growing after three weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ shi no sɛɛ lɛ, ekpaa dalɛ kwraa yɛ otsii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses stored energy in the seed for its first few weeks, but once that food runs out, hard soil or a lack of soil nutrients will cause the young seedling to stall.
ga: Abɛi kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Shi kɛ niyenii lɛ ba naagbee Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ afee mɛi ni ŋmɛɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to absorb nutrients and water faster than domestic crops can after dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe bɔ ni shia tsei baanyɛ afee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing lots of lush green leaves but producing almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni ebɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes legumes to focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than producing the flowers that turn into food pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni bafeɔ niyenii ŋmɔji

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing seeds with empty spaces on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni bɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Empty spaces on a maize cob happen when dry heat damages the silk during flowering, preventing proper pollination of every individual seed on the cob.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa kɛji la ni mli egbi lɛ kpata siliki lɛ hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmei fɛɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Under intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up, so the plant wilts temporarily to conserve moisture until evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my young seedlings more than fully grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are tender, easy for pests to chew, and full of soft shoots and moisture. Mature plants have tougher stems and leaves that make it harder for insects to feed on them.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye. ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ tsei kɛ baai ni mli wa, ni no haa ewaa kɛha koolooi akɛ amɛ baa ye.

english: Can small insects really kill a young crop plant, or will the plant just recover on its own?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii lɛɛlɛŋ, aloo tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatsa amɛhe?

english: Yes, small insects can kill young plants quickly because seedling stems and leaves are soft. If insects eat the central shoot or main stem, the small plant usually dies before it can grow strong enough to recover.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii oya yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛji kooloi ye tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, bei pii lɛ tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.
