english: What happens if heavy rain traps water inside the leaves or stems of my small crops?
ga: Ni kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mɔ nu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe baai loo amɛshishifãi amli hu?

english: Trapped water softens the plant tissue and creates a wet environment that attracts pests. Insects like stem borers or beetles use this wet area to lay eggs, which leads to rotting and insect damage inside the plant.
ga: Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa tsei ahe fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa. Kplukai tamɔ stem borers kɛ beetles kɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ amɛwui. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli fiteɔ ni kooloi fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn rot and die when water sits inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects in the funnel of a young maize plant, it prevents oxygen from reaching the growing tip and attracts insects. The leaves start rotting, and pest damage at that tender point can destroy the plant's heart.
ga: Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ naa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii. Baai lɛ bɔi fitemɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ tsui lɛ.

english: How can I tell if small insects on my crops are actually harming them or just sitting there?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miipila amɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo ota jɛmɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Check for signs of damage like tiny holes in leaves, curled shoots, yellowing leaves, or sticky sap. If you see these signs alongside insects, those pests are feeding on your crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji nɔ ko efite, tamɔ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli, amɛyiteŋ ni ebɔle, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo nu ni mli tse. Kɛji ona okadii nɛɛ yɛ kooloi ahe lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ nakai kooloi lɛ miiye onibii.

english: Where on my crop plants should I look first to check if insects are starting to invade my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni mana kɛji kooloi bibii miibɔi miŋmɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ?

english: Check under the leaves, inside young leaf folds, and around the base of the stem close to the soil. Insects prefer to hide and feed in these warm, moist, sheltered spots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ shishigbɛ, baa bibioo lɛ mli. kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Kplukai sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛtao niyenii yɛ nɛkɛ hei ni mli edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɛɛ.

english: Why do insects multiply so fast on my farm right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain brings fresh, tender leaf growth for pests to eat, and high moisture creates the perfect wet condition for insects to hatch their eggs rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ haa baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kwɛ̃ɔ koni kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ aye. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni kooloi bibii lɛ afɔ oya.

english: How can I protect my small seedlings from insect attacks during the rainy season?
ga: Ebaabu dumɔwui bibii ahe. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ojie kooloi bibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Clear weeds around the farm to remove insect hiding places, ensure rainwater drains away easily so water does not sit on young crops, and inspect your plants early every morning to catch pests early.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Okwaafoi ni akɛbaajie hei ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ Kwɛmɔ ni nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya. Bɔni afee ni nu akakpɛtɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Ni kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli mra daa leebi koni onyɛ omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ mra.

english: Why is it risky to leave weeds growing very close to my small, newly sprouted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ? Mihe ni kwɛ̃ ehee lɛ

english: Weeds harbor harmful insects and hold extra moisture around your crops. Once insect numbers grow on the weeds, they easily jump onto your delicate young crops and destroy them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ hiɛɔ koolooi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛbɔleɔ onibii ahe lɛ. Amɛtuɔ tsei bibii ni waaa lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: What information should I give an extension officer over the phone if I see strange bugs on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ saji esa akɛ mikɛha extension agent lɛ yɛ tɛlifoŋ nɔ? Kɛji mina kooloo ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Describe the insect's color and size, where it is on the plant (like inside stems or under leaves), the age of your crops, and what damage you see so the officer can help identify the pest.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ kooloi bibii lɛ ahe su kɛ amɛdalɛ. He ni kooloi bibii lɛ yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ (tamɔ tso lɛ shishi loo baai lɛ ashishi), afii abɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye, kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efite ni onaa. Bɔni afee ni onukpai lɛ aye abua ni ana tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Is it true that yams have male and female plants, and how does that affect my crop?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ sweet potato yɛ tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, yam plants can be male or female. The male flowers produce pollen and the female flowers produce seeds after pollination. However, most farmers plant tuber cuttings directly, which don't require male and female plants to mix in the field to grow food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato tsei baanyɛ afee nuu loo yoo. Fɔfɔi hii woɔ pollen ni fɔfɔi yei woɔ dumɔwui yɛ pollination sɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, okwaafoi babaoo duɔ bulb tsei tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei hii kɛ yei afutu yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli koni akɛdu niyenii.

english: Do all the food crops on my farm need both a male and female plant to produce a harvest?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni niyenii tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aná tsei hii kɛ yei fɛɛ koni amɛná ŋmaa?

english: No, not all crops require separate male and female plants. Some crops have both male and female parts on the same plant or even within the same flower, while others, like certain yams or papayas, have distinct male and female plants that rely on wind or insects to transfer pollen.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi biɔ ni ajie tsei hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi fɛɛ yɛ tso kome nɔ loo yɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ po. yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi, tamɔ sweet potatoes loo papaya Tsei hii kɛ yei srɔtoi yɛ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi anɔ koni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya.

english: Can I grow new yam crops directly from true seeds instead of planting pieces of the yam tuber?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ ŋmeii akutsei amli bibii bibii?

english: Yes, true yam seeds come from the female yam flower after pollination by a male plant. While you can grow yams from these seeds, it takes longer and yields unpredictable results, which is why farmers usually plant tuber setts to get reliable crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, anɔkwa sweet potato dumɔwui jɛɔ sweet potato fɔfɔi yei amli yɛ be mli ni tso nuu ko kɛ pollination ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ adu sweet potato moŋ, Shi eheɔ be babaoo ni ekɛ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa. Enɛ hewɔ ni bei pii lɛ okwaafoi duɔ ŋmeii koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the new crops grown from my harvested seeds sometimes look different from the parent plant I saved them from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei heei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ amli lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ fɔlɔ tso ni mikɛto lɛ he lɛ?

english: When male and female plant flowers cross-pollinate, the resulting seeds inherit a mix of traits from both parent plants. Just like human children are not identical to their parents, seeds produce offspring crops with slight variations in size, taste, and growth.
ga: Beni fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei foɔ pollination mli. Dumɔwui ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ yeɔ sui ni akɛfee ekome kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amli lɛ gboshinii. Taakɛ bɔ ni adesai abii kɛ amɛfɔlɔi jeee ekome lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi fioo yɛ dalɛ, ŋɔɔ, kɛ dalɛ mli.

english: If I want an exact copy of my best yam crop, should I use its seeds or its tuber?
ga: Kɛji miitao mi-sweet potato tso lɛ eko ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii?

english: You should use pieces of the tuber. Growing from a tuber is vegetative propagation, which creates an exact clone of the parent plant, whereas growing from true seeds mixes genetic traits from male and female parents.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ yitso lɛ fã ko atsu nii. Tubers mli dalɛ ji tsofafeemɔ mli shweremɔ. ni feɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he mfoniri pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ be mli ni edaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ, ekɛ fɔmɔ nii ni jɛ fɔlɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How do male and female plant flowers cross with each other if plants cannot move?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso nuu kɛ yoo fɔfɔi lɛ afo mli kɛji tso lɛ tsiii ehe?

english: Plants rely on natural helpers like bees, ants, small insects, and the wind to carry fine dust called pollen from the male flower to the female flower so that fertilization can take place.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni amɛjie sũ bibioo ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen lɛ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli kɛha fɔmɔ.

english: Why do some of my yam vines produce small flowers while other vines in the same field do not flower at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni wain tsei krokomɛi Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, fɔfɔi ko bɛ kwraa?

english: Flowering depends on the sex and maturity of the yam plant. Male and female plants produce different flower types for reproduction, but some plants remain non-flowering if they are focused purely on growing their underground tuber.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ damɔ bɔ ni sweet potato tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo kɛ edalɛ nɔ. Tsei hii kɛ yei woɔ fɔfɔi srɔtoi kɛha fɔmɔ. Shi tsei komɛi baafee fɔfɔi lolo kɛji akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs pɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens inside a crop plant when it reaches full maturity?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ ekwɛ̃?

english: Once a crop reaches full maturity, it completes its vegetative growth and focuses its energy on reproduction—producing flowers, completing fertilization between parent traits, and forming seeds or mature tubers for the next generation.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaada ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔmɔ nɔ, ni ji fɔfɔii ni ebaawo. Fɔlɔi asui ateŋ fɔmɔ kɛ dumɔwui loo bulbs ni eda kɛha yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do crop scientists create new, stronger crop varieties using parent plants?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi afee tsei srɔtoi heei ni he wa kɛtsɔ tsei ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ anɔ?

english: Scientists select a male plant with good traits (like drought resistance) and a female plant with good traits (like large yield), combine their pollen intentionally, and grow the resulting offspring seeds to produce a new, improved crop variety.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi halaa tsei hii ni yɔɔ sui kpakpai (tamɔ hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ) kɛ tsei yei ni yɔɔ sui kpakpai (tamɔ yibiiwoo babaoo) kɛtsɔ amɛyiŋtoo ni amɛkɛ pollen futuɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsei dumɔwui ni seshibii jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ mli koni akɛfee tsei srɔtoi heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I select the best parent crops on my farm to get strong planting material for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala fɔlɔ tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná dumɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Choose planting material from healthy, high-yielding parent plants that stayed free of diseases throughout the season, as these strong physical traits are passed down to the offspring crops.
ga: Halamɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tsei ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Helai bɛ ehe yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yaa tsei ni fɔɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and leafy. Giving the soil nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans before maize helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani ŋmeii baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very thin and small even when the leaves on top look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ, shi.

english: When cassava plants get too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves instead of growing tubers under the ground. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to store food in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai kakadaji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs najiaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and damaging your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo virus ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during the heavy rainy season when the farm is too shady and humid. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ hela nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, be mli ni ŋmɔji lɛ amli ewo hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo tsɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the leaves and central whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni elaaje yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ ring lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaves at the center of the corn plant. Catching them early and applying approved pest treatments inside the leaf funnel stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worms in the soil called nematodes often eat the roots, making the plant weak. Staking the mature trees with strong poles and clearing weeds around the base keeps them stable against strong wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ niyenii. gbɔjɔmɔ tso lɛ Tsei wuji ni akɛ tsei ni wa fĩɔ shi ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die off when I cut down all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Keeping taller trees or planting food crops like plantain alongside young cocoa creates vital shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛdara loo niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains kɛ kookoo bibii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too hot or when the plants do not get enough steady water during flowering. Keeping the soil covered with mulch conserves moisture and cools the roots, helping flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Ye obua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai

english: Why does my land produce much less food when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ faaa kwraa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously removes the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have small nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay after harvest, they leave behind rich fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ mli efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni baai kɛ shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaashi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What does 'moisture content' mean when officers talk about my maize grains?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘muji ni yɔɔ mli’ lɛ shishi kɛ́ onukpai lɛ wie mi-ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ahe?

english: Moisture content is simply the amount of water trapped inside the grain kernel. Just like fresh fruits hold water, grains hold water, and knowing how much water is inside tells you if the grain is safe from rotting.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ ji nu ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ pɛ. Taakɛ aduawai heei hiɛɔ nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ŋmãa toɔ nu. Ni kɛ́ ole nu abɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, no baatsɔɔ bo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my maize grains feel dry on the skin even when they are still wet on the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe egbi yɛ hewolo nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛmli edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: The outer skin of a grain loses water quickly when exposed to heat, but water remains trapped deep inside the center. That is why testing the inside moisture is necessary to know the true condition of the crop.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛgbɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shi nu lɛ kã teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ lolo. No hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni aka hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ koni ale bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ.

english: Why is 18 percent water level often recommended for maize before processing or storing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ajieɔ nu ni falɛ ji oha mlijaa 18 kpo yɛ ŋmãa mli dani atsuɔ he nii loo akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: At 18 percent moisture, the maize grain is soft enough to shell without crushing into dust, but dry enough that destructive molds and heat will not easily build up.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ mli oha mlijaa 18 lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ sũ. Shi egbi bɔ ni sa ni ŋmei kɛ dɔlɛ nyɛɛɛ abɔ he mlɛo.

english: Why do agricultural officers take a small sample of my maize crop to test?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ ŋɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ eko koni ekɛka lɛ ekwɛ lɛ?

english: Officers test a tiny portion of your crop to measure its exact water level without damaging the rest of your yield. This testing gives you accurate advice on when it is safe to stop drying or start harvesting.
ga: Amralofoi lɛ ka ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã bibioo ko amɛkwɛ. onɔ lɛ koni osusu nu lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛfiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ. Ka nɛɛ baaha oná gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni ja yɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii agbimɔ loo obɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ.

english: Will officers taking small crop samples reduce the total harvest I get to sell?
ga: Ani nitsulɔi ni buaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: No, officers only take a handful of grains to run the test. That small sample saves your entire harvest by preventing you from storing wet crop that would rot in the bag.
ga: Dabi, onukpai lɛ kɛ ŋmãa fioo ko pɛ tsu nii kɛfee kaa lɛ. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko Ni baaye abua ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahi shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ ni baanyɛ afite ni okɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my harvested maize has dried enough for me to stop drying it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni ebaakpa ŋmɔlɔ?

english: You stop drying when the moisture level inside the grain drops to the required target percentage. Extension officers use moisture meters to give you the exact day to stop so your crop stays in peak condition.
ga: Obaakpa ŋmɔlɔ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ba shi kɛyashɛ oha mlijaa ni ataoɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ moisture meters tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsɔɔ bo gbi pɔtɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii koni onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize need to dry over a period of several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ agbi gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Water deep inside the grain moves out slowly to the surface. Drying over two to three days gives the grain time to release this trapped water evenly without cracking the kernel.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ laajeɔ fiofio. Tsi ohe blɛoo kɛya nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ agbi fe gbii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛjie nu ni emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaaa amɛtswa.

english: Can leaving my maize to dry in the sun for too many days harm my grain?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni ashiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaye ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, over-drying makes grains very brittle and light. When you shell over-dried maize, the kernels break easily into dust, which reduces the total weight and price you get at the market.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ egbi fe nine lɛ, ehaa ŋmaa lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni efeɔ mlɛo. Kɛji ogbala ŋmãa ni egbi tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ fãa oya ni amɛfeɔ sũ. Enɛ haa shwiili lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ jara fɛɛ ni onine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What will happen to my maize if I bag and store it while it is still wet?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli ni mikɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Wet maize creates heat and sweating inside storage bags. This warm, moist air makes mold grow quickly and attracts insects, ruining the entire bag in a short time.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa baa kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmei daa oya ni egbalaa kooloi bibii. Kpata kotokui lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How does sudden rain affect my maize while it is drying outside?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ saa mi-ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater gets soaked back into the dry outer skin of the grain, raising the water level again. If it rains, you must cover or move the maize and continue sun-drying once the weather clears.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ eboteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛgbɛ ni egbi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nu lɛ baaya ŋwɛi ekoŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehe baahia ni oha ŋmãa lɛ nɔ loo otsi ohe ni okɛwo hulu lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their green color and energy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their strength and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhaa hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hewalɛ kɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm's soil is tired and needs fertilizer or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Tired soil shows clear warning signs: crops grow very slowly, leaves look pale, and your harvest gets smaller each season. Adding organic manure or crop fertilizer puts essential food back into the earth so plants can produce well again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ haa: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo waa, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni okpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out thin and watery instead of big and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ amli tse ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli fe cassava shishifãi wuji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to swell properly, and too much trapped water or hard, compacted ground stops them from expanding. Planting on raised mounds or ridges gives roots the soft space they need to grow thick and heavy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛfuu jogbaŋŋ. Ni nu babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe afee shwiili.

english: Young cocoa pods drop off when the tree lacks enough water and food to support all of them, or when insect pests attack. Clearing weeds, pruning properly, and nourishing the soil gives the tree energy to hold its pods until harvest.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛye amɛhe. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ jwɛi lɛ tutuaa jwɛi lɛ Tsemɔ ni sa Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa tso lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛmɔɔ jwɛi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop bringing out flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause pepper plants to drop their flowers to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Placing dried grass around the base as mulch keeps the ground cool and moist so flowers can stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa chili tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛ mulch tsuɔ nii kɛbɔleɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why do some of my tomato plants produce plenty of leaves but very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ baai babaoo shi tomato fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer without balanced nutrients, they put all their energy into making giant leafy branches instead of fruit. Balancing fertilizer allows the plant to switch energy from leaf growth to fruiting.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ tsei niji wuji ni yɔɔ baai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ tsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai ni ato lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting plantains next to my young cocoa trees help them survive?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Te mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ amɛhiɔ shi?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with wide leaves, acting as living umbrellas that shade young cocoa trees and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã, ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same place?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks that produce tiny cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Why do I need to trim off extra branches and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tso niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Extra, unneeded branches waste valuable water and nutrients that should be going into making cocoa pods. Pruning removes useless growth, lets sunlight reach the main trunk, and reduces plant diseases.
ga: Niji babaoo ni he ehiaaa lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ niyenii ni esa akɛ akɛfee kookoo ŋmeii. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he ni ehaa tso helai baa shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to grow weak and yield poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tsei titrii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm, quickly drinking the water and taking the soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early leaves all the water and food for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ nu ni ooonu oya ni oná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaafee nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni baaha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living shade cover, protecting young cocoa seedlings from intense sun and heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Will my young cocoa seedlings die if I leave them exposed to direct sunlight without cover?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, direct sunlight can scorch young cocoa leaves and dry out the surrounding soil quickly, which kills young plants before their root systems are established enough to fetch underground water.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ gbeɔ tsei bibii dani shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baa.

english: Can planting plantains alongside my cocoa help provide food for my family while I wait for the cocoa to mature?
ga: Ani plantains ni miduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aha weku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains produce food within 9 to 12 months, providing early harvests for food and quick income long before cocoa trees start bearing pods after a few years.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, ni enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa niyenii mra kɛ shika ni anáa oya dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: What is the benefit of building raised soil mounds or heaps before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ni atswaa dani aduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he?

english: Building soil heaps loosens the ground so roots can spread easily, improves water drainage to prevent roots from rotting, and keeps topsoil concentrated where crops need it most.
ga: Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hiɔ he ni tsei he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I gather weeds and crop leftovers and bury them inside soil heaps to help my crops grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ anaa ni mafu amɛ yɛ sũ mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, burying plant material inside soil heaps allows it to break down into natural compost, releasing essential plant nutrients into the soil as it decays to feed your growing crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe nibii ni afuɔ yɛ sũ ni abua naa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ojie tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛfiteɔ koni amɛkɛha onibii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: What should I do with cleared vegetation on my farm instead of burning it off?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tsei ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Instead of burning, you can gather cleared weeds into mounds or use them as mulch around your plants; as the plant material decays, it turns into free fertilizer and improves soil health.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ, obaanyɛ obua jwɛi ni ajie lɛ anaa kɛfee ŋtayaa loo okɛtsu nii akɛ ŋtayaa. Kɛ tsei amli nibii fite Ebaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do plantain trees help keep the soil damp around my young cocoa trees during dry spells?
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ. Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anáa nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Plantain trunks contain a lot of water and their broad leaves shield the ground from drying winds, keeping the soil cool and retaining moisture for nearby cocoa roots.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ plantain tsei lɛ amli. Ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛha kookoo shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: How can I get new plantain plants for my farm without having to spend money buying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana tsei heei kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛ shika tsuuu he nii?

english: Mature plantain trees naturally produce young shoots called suckers around their base. You can carefully dig up these suckers and replant them elsewhere on your farm for free.
ga: Plantains ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. atsɛɔ lɛ surrounding shoots natural base Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahe nii ni okɛdu yɛ he kroko yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yaka.

english: Is it better for me to have all my farm plots in one place or spread across different locations?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafee miŋmɔ shikpɔji lɛ fɛɛ yɛ he kome loo magbɛ amɛ mashwã hei srɔtoi?

english: Having plots in different locations protects you against total loss; if pests, disease, bad weather, or bushfires affect one plot, your crops on another location can still survive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi Ebaabu ohe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kwraa he kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii. loo koo mli la ni saa shikpɔŋ kome he Oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lolo.

english: Why is it valuable to listen to the practical farming advice given by the elders in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ mabo okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni jɛɔ mi akrowa onukpai lɛ adɛŋ lɛ toi lɛ?

english: Older farmers have spent decades learning local weather patterns, soil behavior, and crop performance, giving them reliable practical experience that complements modern farming techniques.
ga: Okwaafoi ni eda lɛ kɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ekase bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ amɛmaŋ lɛ mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ subaŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anitsumɔ Enɛ haa amɛnáa niiashikpamɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni baaha ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai aya hiɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to leave large trees standing inside our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi tsei wuji yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young and mature cocoa trees naturally prefer a cool environment. Large shade trees protect cocoa leaves from harsh midday sunlight, help keep moisture in the ground, and protect the crop from strong winds.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ sumɔɔ hei ni mli ejɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Why should I cover the ground around my young vegetable crops with dry grass or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass acts like a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the ground so the soil stays wet longer, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing easily.
ga: Akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the ground has too much standing water. Adding fertilizer like NPK or compost gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to drink water and take food from the soil much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets too stressed from heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. When the plant feels weak, it sheds its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛ waa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ egbɔjɔ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: If too many plantain shoots grow around one main plant, they steal nutrients and food away from the main stalk, leading to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri kome he lɛ, Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains akui bibii.

english: Why do I need to trim off the side branches of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ?

english: Trimming extra side branches forces the tomato plant to send its energy and food directly into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tomato tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛyaa aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by hot, dry weather. If you plant too quickly and the rains pause for weeks, your seeds will dry up and die before their roots can reach deep soil water.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some coconut trees take almost seven years to bear fruit while others start much earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afii kpawo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii oya waa lɛ?

english: Coconut trees come in different varieties. Tall coconut varieties take between 6 to 7 years to start producing fruit, whereas dwarf coconut varieties grow faster and can start bearing fruit in just 3 to 4 years.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmei tsei srɔtoi babaoo. Kokooi srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ daa oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli.

english: How can I be sure if the coconut seedlings I am buying are the fast-fruiting type or the long-waiting type?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmei tso ni mihe lɛ baawo yibii oya loo ehe baahia ni mamɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Dwarf varieties that fruit early often have distinct shoot colors like yellow, orange, or light green, but the best way to be sure is to buy certified seedlings directly from verified agricultural officers or nurseries.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dwarf henɔi ni woɔ yibii mra lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ahe sui srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Shi gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ana nɔmimaa ji ni ahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: If my coconut trees will take seven years to produce fruit, can I grow other crops on the same land while waiting?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmei tso lɛ he afii kpawo ni ewo yibii Ani manyɛ madu tsei krokomɛi yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, while waiting for tall coconut trees to mature, you can intercrop the land with short-term food crops like maize, vegetables, or cassava to get food and income from the land during those early years.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni emɛɔ ni ŋmei tso lɛ atsɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa, aduawai, loo ŋmãa. koni amɛná niyenii kɛ shika kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli

english: What is the main advantage of planting dwarf coconut trees on my farm instead of the traditional tall ones?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ blema tsei kakadaji lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Dwarf coconut trees start fruiting much sooner, are easier to harvest because they remain short, and allow you to fit more trees onto a small plot of land.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa. Amɛkpamɔ waaa ejaakɛ amɛji bibii lolo. ni ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei babaoo yɛ he bibioo ko

english: Is it possible to harvest just one root from a mature cassava plant and leave the rest in the ground?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmei shishifã kome pɛ ni eda ni ashi fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, this practice is called piecemeal harvesting. You can carefully dig up one mature tuber for cooking or selling, then cover the root area back up so the remaining tubers stay fresh and keep growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa ŋmei kome ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni okɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii homɔ loo jarayeli mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ha shishifã lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi ehee ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do farmers harvest cassava tubers one by one instead of digging up the whole plant at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ekomekomei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly after being dug out of the ground. Harvesting tubers one by one keeps the rest alive and fresh underground until you are ready to use them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ bulb lɛ shwie shi komekomei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi ni efee ehee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Will removing one root from a cassava stand cause the rest of the plant to die or spoil?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ajie shishifã kome kɛjɛ ŋmei tso mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ agbo loo egbo?

english: No, as long as you do not snap the main stem or damage the other roots, carefully covering the open hole with soil will keep the plant alive and healthy.
ga: Dabi, be fɛɛ be ni okɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ekuuu loo ofiteee shishifãi krokomɛi lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ sũ ha bu ni agbele lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some tubers on my cassava plant big and mature while others on the same plant are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bulbs ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi dara ni amɛdara waa lɛ? yɛ be mli ni yitsei krokomɛi lɛ darako lolo yɛ tso kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Roots under the same plant receive different amounts of water and nutrients from the soil, causing some tubers to mature earlier than others under the same stem.
ga: Shishifãi ni yɔɔ tso kome shishi lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi srɔtoi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa bulb komɛi daraa oya fe ekrokomɛi. yɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shishi

english: How long can mature cassava tubers stay under the soil without getting spoiled?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda kwraa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfiteee?

english: Depending on the variety, mature cassava tubers can stay safely stored underground for several months to over a year as long as the plant remains alive.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi afi be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ yɔɔ wala mli lɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ.

english: If I harvest the biggest tuber from a cassava plant, will the remaining smaller tubers grow bigger?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmei tso ni da fe fɛɛ lɛ Ani yitso bibioo ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsɔ agbo?

english: Yes, taking away the biggest tuber reduces the struggle for nutrients underground, allowing the plant to push more food into the smaller remaining roots so they can expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni dara fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha ta ni awuɔ kɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛyaa shishifãi bibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why is it important for me to trim or cut off certain branches from my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji komɛi ni jɛ mitso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning removes dead, weak, or overcrowded branches, which helps air and sunlight reach the tree while encouraging healthier growth and better fruit yield.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ loo afolɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ajieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: How can I tell if a broken or split branch needs to be cut off completely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni afo tso nine ni ekumɔ loo ejara mli lɛ kwraa?

english: If a branch is split or hanging loose, it leaves an open wound that can rot; cutting it off cleanly allows the tree to seal the damage and protect the rest of the trunk.
ga: Kɛji akɛ niji lɛ ekumɔ loo amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe Ebaashi pilamɔ ko ni agbele ni baanyɛ afite. Tso lɛ ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ he ni efite lɛ naa, ni ebuɔ tso lɛ shishi ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Is it safe to use my regular cutlass to cut branches off my tree?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsɔne kuku ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ baafolɔ tso niji?

english: While a cutlass works for general clearing, it often leaves rough or torn edges on branches that take longer to heal, making the tree vulnerable to rot.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ nibii fɛɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, amɛshiɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni etse yɛ tsei niji anɔ ni heɔ be babaoo dani etsaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ ebaafite.

english: What are pruning shears and why would I need them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ tsei? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning shears are specialized scissor-like tools designed to cut small branches cleanly without crushing or tearing the plant's skin, helping the tree stay healthy.
ga: Pruning shears ji dɛŋdadei krɛdɛɛi ni tamɔ sɛkɛs ni afee koni akɛfo tsei niji bibii. Ehe tse ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewolo lɛ shwieee shi loo efolɔɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why does it matter if my blade is sharp when I am trimming my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-blade lɛ mli atse beni mifoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: A sharp tool makes a smooth cut in one go, while a dull tool crushes and tears the stem, leaving open damage that takes a long time to close up.
ga: Dɛŋdade ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ afoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɛŋdade ko ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ baakumɔ ni ebaagbala tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa fitemɔ ni agbeleɔ naa ni heɔ be babaoo dani agbeɔ naa lɛ baa.

english: How do tree branches heal after they have been cut?
ga: Te tsei aniji tsaa amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ afo amɛ?

english: Trees heal by growing new bark tissue over the cut area to seal it shut, but this sealing process can only happen quickly if the cut surface is clean and smooth.
ga: Atsaa tsei kɛtsɔ ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni afo lɛ nɔ koni akɛtsi naa lɛ nɔ. Shi nɛkɛ naatsii gbɛ nɛɛ baanyɛ aba mli oya pɛ kɛji akɛ he ni afo lɛ he tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some tree stems rot after I trim them during farm cleaning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei akui komɛi fite beni mifo amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Stems rot when cuts are messy or jagged, which allows rainwater to collect in the open wood and create a breeding ground for fungus.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji pilamɔ lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ kooi ni mli tse lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Can insects enter and destroy my tree through places where I cut branches?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ atsɔ hei ni mifoɔ tsei lɛ anɔ amɛbote mitso lɛ mli?

english: Yes, open wounds left by bad cuts attract pests like stem borers, which can burrow into the exposed wood and weaken or kill the tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, pilamɔi ni agbele ni pilamɔi gbohii kɛbaa lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ stem borers. ni baanyɛ atsɔ koo lɛ mli ni eha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ loo amɛgboi.

english: How can bad cutting habits spread diseases across my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii gbohii agbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Rough or haphazard cuts leave open wounds that stay wet and raw for a long time, allowing fungal and bacterial diseases to easily infect the tree.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni afee lɛ trukaa lɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa tso lɛ nɔ oya.

english: What can I do immediately after cutting a branch to protect my tree from sickness?
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ he agbe naa lɛ, mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni akɛbu tso lɛ he koni hela akamɔ lɛ?

english: Making sure the cut is smooth and clean helps the wound dry and seal quickly, stopping diseases and pests from entering the exposed wood.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ koni pilamɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbiɔ ni ehaa ehe tseɔ oya. Ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ tsei ni ajie amɛ kpo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the ground is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every time I plant on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu nii lɛ, mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Continuous farming drains essential nutrients from the soil. Without adding compost, manure, or fertilizers, the ground becomes exhausted and cannot support strong crop growth.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni daraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When water collects around the roots for too long, oxygen cannot reach them, allowing harmful soil fungi and bacteria to cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ ashɛ Oxygen he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei kɛ muawai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ afite.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize during the major rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli?

english: You should wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked the soil deeply, ensuring the ground stays moist long enough for seeds to germinate and take root.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when air temperatures become too hot, water supply is irregular, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and showing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow spots are often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by fungal infections that thrive in hot, humid weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive intense, direct sunlight. Shade trees protect fragile young cocoa plants from heat burn and keep soil moisture from evaporating.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni amɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin stems and smaller, lighter bunches of fruit.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai akui bibii ni waaa.

english: Weeds are wild, naturally tough plants that absorb water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower young farm plants quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni he wa ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsei. Amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ kunim oya.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots even when stored indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ toɔ shĩa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally enter a rest period after harvest, but warm room temperatures and humidity signal to the tuber that it is time to use its stored energy to grow new shoots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ aleɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii heei.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for healthy plant growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, signaling that your soil needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants look curled up and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the most effective way to protect your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells. When water is irregular, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival rather than making fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil underneath them is packed too hard or contains too many rocks. Building tall, soft soil mounds allows the tubers to expand freely and grow large.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi tsɔ. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods dry up and turn black while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛji ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods turning black and shriveling is often caused by Cherelle Wilt or fungal diseases like Black Pod. Cherelle Wilt happens naturally when the tree cannot support all its pods, but good pruning helps reduce disease risks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii helai, tamɔ Cherelle Wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ baa. Pods diji baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ pod muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa helai baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so much longer to produce fruit when planted under tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantains need direct sunlight to produce the energy required for flowering and fruiting. Under heavy shade, the plant grows slowly because it lacks enough light to make food.
ga: Hulu la he miihia plantains tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ejaakɛ amɛbɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaahoo nii.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form large cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does spear grass cause my crops to grow so weakly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep, aggressive underground stems that rob your crops of water and soil food. Its root system is so strong that it chokes out crop roots nearby.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii. Eshishifãi lɛ amli wa waa aahu akɛ etsiɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing lots of thick green leaves but very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi tomato fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages tomato plants to grow abundant leaves instead of flowers. To get more fruit, the plant needs nutrients rich in phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha tomato tsei lɛ aná baai babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium he miihia tsei koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnuts start sprouting roots inside their shells before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut lɛ bɔi shishifãi shwiemɔ yɛ eshishifã lɛ mli dani mifo mli lɛ?

english: If heavy late rains fall when groundnuts are fully mature, the seeds absorb the moisture and react as if it is time to plant again, causing them to germinate while still in the soil.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee beni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why do some pineapples taste very sweet while others grow much bigger but less sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ŋɔɔ waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi dara fe tsutsu lɛ shi amɛhe ehiaaa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties of the same crop carry different traits. For example, Sugarloaf pineapples are naturally sweeter and softer for fresh eating, while Smooth Cayenne pineapples grow much larger and firmer, making them ideal for juice processing.
ga: Tso kome lɛ henɔi srɔtoi lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, sugarloaf pineapple lɛ ŋɔɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo kɛji aye lɛ ŋmɔŋ. Shi Cayenne pineapple ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ da kwraa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha aduawai amli nu feemɔ.

english: Can I plant different varieties of the same crop side-by-side in the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei babaoo ni ji tsofa kome lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is better to separate different varieties into distinct plots. They often mature at different times, grow to different heights, and require different amounts of water and nutrients, which makes managing and harvesting them easier when kept apart.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara srɔtoi lɛ amli awo shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛdaraa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Edaa yɛ hei srɔtoi. ni ebiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi srɔtoi Enɛ haa nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ ajie mli.

english: How do I decide which variety of a crop I should plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: You should choose based on what buyers in your local market want, how much rainfall your land gets, and how well the specific variety resists local pests and diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ odamɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ nɔ ohala. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ falɛ. kɛ bɔ ni srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi teɔ shi amɛwoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ helai jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do buyers in the market pay more money for certain types of fruits over others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ aduawai srɔtoi komɛi ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Market prices depend on buyer preference and intended use. Sweet, soft varieties are bought quickly by consumers for daily eating, while processing factories prefer larger, firmer fruits that yield more juice and survive long transport without rotting.
ga: Jarayeli jara lɛ damɔ hɔlɔ lɛ hiamɔ nii kɛ nɔ ni esusuɔ akɛ ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miihe ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ oya koni amɛye daa gbi. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ aduawai ni dara, ni wa. Enɛ haa nu babaoo baa, ni abaanyɛ akɛwo he kroko be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee.

english: Why is it important for me to try a new crop variety on a small patch before planting my entire land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka tsei heei akwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ? Dani abaadu shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ

english: Testing a new crop on a small plot helps you observe how well it handles your soil, weather, and local pests without risking your main income or entire land on an unfamiliar plant.
ga: Nibii heei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ lɛ Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni tsei lɛ kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ kpeɔ jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa. Ni okɛ oshika titri ni onáa loo oshikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ tsei ni oleee lɛ awo oshara mli.

english: Why do insects damage one type of plant on my farm while leaving a different variety next to it alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ tso henɔ kome ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛshiɔ henɔ kroko yɛ emasɛi lɛ? mipɛ

english: Some crop varieties have natural defenses, such as thicker skin, tougher leaves, or natural bitter tastes that discourage insects, while sweeter or softer varieties attract pests more easily.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu tamɔ hewolo ni mli wa. Baai lɛ wa fe tsutsu lɛ. aloo eyɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kɛha kooloi yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni ŋɔɔ loo ni mli jɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii oya.

english: Why do crops of the same age harvest at different times on different farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpaa tsei ni eye afii kome lɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ?

english: Harvest times depend on the seed variety used, the amount of sunlight, water, and soil fertility. Improved fast-maturing varieties produce yields much earlier than traditional local varieties.
ga: Nikpamɔ be lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ, hulu la falɛ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe blema maŋ lɛ mli tsoi srɔtoi lɛ.

english: Do all varieties of a crop require the exact same amount of fertilizer?
ga: Ani tsei fɛɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni falɛ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: No, fast-growing and high-yielding crop varieties usually need more fertilizer to support their rapid growth compared to local varieties that grow slowly and produce smaller yields.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni daa oya ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni eye ebua amɛdalɛ oya. Kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: How do I get new planting materials from my mature pineapple plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná dumɔ nii hee kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ mli?

english: Pineapples produce small side shoots called suckers and slips near the base and fruit. You can carefully detach these healthy shoots from mature plants and plant them directly into prepared soil to grow new crops.
ga: Pineapple yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii, ni amɛyitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ agbala nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ amli. ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni tsei heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young crops turn yellow when exposed to strong afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have delicate leaves that lose moisture quickly under strong sunlight. Some crops need temporary shade trees or nursery covers to protect them until their root systems grow deep enough to drink enough water.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi biɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it good for me to plant plantain and cocoa on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu plantain kɛ cocoa yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, planting plantain alongside young cocoa is a great practice. The tall plantain plants grow quickly and provide natural shade to protect sensitive young cocoa trees from hot sunlight while keeping the soil cool.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop trees if I do not prune them at all?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifooo lɛ?

english: If you leave trees unpruned, they grow too thick and bushy. This blocks sunlight from reaching all parts of the plant, reduces fruit production, and creates a humid environment where pests and fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Kɛji oshi tso lɛ ni ofoko lɛ Tsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. ehaa yibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How do big leaves like plantain leaves help catch and direct rainwater to my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai wuji tamɔ plantain baai yeɔ ebuaa ni ebua nugbɔ nu naa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Broad leaves act like natural gutters. When rain falls on them, the shape of the leaf guides the water straight down toward the base of the trunk, concentrating moisture right where the plant's roots can reach it.
ga: Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ŋshɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ Baai lɛ ahe mfoniri lɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛyaa shi kɛyaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa he ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Do young cocoa trees need direct sunshine or shade to grow well?
ga: Ani hulu la loo hulutsoo he miihia cacao tsei bibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade to survive. Their leaves burn easily in full sun, so growing taller shade plants around them keeps them cool and helps them build strong roots during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Is light drizzle enough to keep my cocoa and plantain crops healthy during dry times?
ga: Ani nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha mi-cocoa kɛ plantain tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Light drizzle helps cool down the leaves, but deep-rooted crops like plantain and cocoa need heavier rains to soak deep into the soil so their main root systems can drink and take up soil nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shi tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa Ehe miihia nugbɔ ni naa wa koni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ anu nu ni ená niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to prune my trees when it is raining heavily?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ tsei kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ waa?

english: It is better to avoid pruning during wet rainy weather. Fresh cuts on a tree stay wet during rain, making it easier for fungal diseases and rot to enter the fresh wounds and harm the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Pilamɔi heei ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii baabote pilamɔi heei amli ni amɛye tso lɛ awui.

english: How close should I plant my plantain trees next to my cocoa trees?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛbɛŋkɛ kookoo tso lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantains should be planted about 3 meters apart from cocoa trees. This distance gives the young cocoa enough shade without the plantain roots stealing all the water and food from the cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantains kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ he aaafee mitai 3. Nɛkɛ he ni jɛkɛ nɛɛ baaha kookoo bibioo lɛ aná hulutsoo babaoo. Plantain shishifãi lɛ ejuuu nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does the soil under plantain trees stay wet longer after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves funnel rain directly to their base, and their large broad canopy protects the ground underneath from direct sun, preventing the rainwater from evaporating quickly from the soil.
ga: Plantain shwieɔ nugbɔshiimɔi yɛ shishigbɛ. Ni ŋwɛitsu agbo ni mli kwɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Can heavy rainfall damage my young cocoa trees if they are left out in the open?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ akpata mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋwɛi?

english: Yes, heavy raindrops hitting young cocoa directly can strip delicate leaves and wash away the soft topsoil around their shallow roots. Taller companion crops help break the force of the falling rain.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni tswaa cacao tso ko tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni bɔle shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ afɔ. Hefatalɔi tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my farm trees sprout so many branches rapidly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries natural nitrogen and gives plants the maximum moisture they need to grow. This sudden boost causes trees to flush out many new branches and leaves very quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɛɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei lɛ nu ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere. Nɛkɛ shweremɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ eniji kɛ baai heei oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cocoyam planted around them to protect their soft leaves from burning until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantain loo ŋmei tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ baatsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã kɛyashi baai lɛ baafee hewalɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni amɛhi ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for soil food and their leaves block each other from sunlight, resulting in thin, weak plants with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni ebaai lɛ buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips inwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛmligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every year drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, the roots drown and rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water flow away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather becomes extremely hot or when the soil dries out suddenly. The plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save its remaining water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa. Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking juices from the underside of leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying appropriate controls stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni sa ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool, keeps water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why is it recommended to cut off some of the small side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ afo tsei aniji bibii lɛ? yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ

english: Removing extra side branches, called suckers, forces the plant to direct its energy into producing fewer, but much bigger and healthier tomatoes rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
