ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoo lɛ ni ajieɔ Ebaanyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo tomato. Shi amɛdara kwraa ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: If a dam is built near my community to store water, can I use that water to farm during the dry season?
ga: Kɛji ama faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi akutso lɛ koni akɛ nu ato. Ani manyɛ mikɛ nakai nu lɛ atsu okwaayeli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, stored dam water can be channeled or pumped to your farm for irrigation. This allows you to grow vegetables, maize, and other high-value crops all year round instead of relying only on rainy seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni ato yɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ amaje loo ajie kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni akɛshwie nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ aduawai, ŋmãa, kɛ nibii krokomɛi ni jara wa waa. Afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ pɛ nɔ

english: How does digging a small water storage pond on my farm help my crops survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ŋshɔ bibioo ko ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli?

english: A farm pond collects rain runoff during heavy storms. When the rains stop for a week or two, you can use that trapped water to keep your crops moist so they do not dry out and die.
ga: Koolooi atoohe lɛ buaa nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome loo enyɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or late at night?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. This gives crop roots time to absorb water before the hot sun arrives. Watering late at night leaves the leaves wet in the dark, which encourages fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ duŋ mli. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa

english: How can I tell if my maize is suffering from too little water versus too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ mli loo nu lɛ fa tsɔ?

english: When maize has too little water, its leaves roll up tightly like needles to save moisture. When it sits in too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow because drowned roots cannot absorb air or plant food.
ga: Beni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ nu babaoo mli lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ejaakɛ shishifãi ni ebote mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo tso lɛ mli niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during severe heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and slow down water loss. Providing steady soil moisture early in the morning helps prevent extreme heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into fruits during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they feel stressed by excessive heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil around the plants moist during flowering stops the blossoms from drying up and falling off.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ feemɔ Ha tso lɛ mli atsɔ fɔfɔi be mli koni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: What happens to my crop roots when floodwater sits on my farmland for several days?
ga: Mɛni baa mi tso lɛ shishifãi anɔ kɛ́ nu eyi he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ gbii babaoo?

english: Plant roots need oxygen in the soil to stay alive. When water sits on your land for days, it smothers the roots, causing them to rot and turning the whole crop yellow and weak.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Egboɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eegbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods on purpose to reduce water loss and protect its roots underground. The plant is not dead; as soon as rain or irrigation water arrives, fresh leaves will quickly sprout back.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ba pɛ kɛkɛ ni baai heei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees like plantains, but full-grown cocoa trees need less shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ? Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo babaoo.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under full sunlight and lose moisture too fast. Plantain trees provide large leaves that shade young cocoa, whereas mature cocoa trees develop a dense top layer that tolerates stronger sunlight.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi fã ko ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out into hard blocks after rain stops, and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ? Ni te ebaaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard clay soil loses moisture quickly under strong heat and bakes solid, making it hard for crop roots to expand or drink water. Adding decomposed animal manure or decayed leaves creates a spongy soil structure that holds moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ baaje mli oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi ni ebaawa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã loo amɛnu nu. Koolooi ashishifãi ni egboi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to take young cocoa plants from my neighbor's farm to start my new field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ cacao tsei bibii ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli baaba koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: It is risky to take plants from a neighbor's farm because they may carry hidden diseases or pests that will spread to your land. Getting certified seedlings from an official government nursery like the Cocoa Board ensures your plants are healthy and disease-free from day one.
ga: Tsei ni okɛbaajɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara ejaakɛ ekolɛ helai loo kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni baagbɛ ashwã oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ. Ni ooona dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli tamɔ Cocoa Board lɛ Ebaaha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni hela akamɔ amɛ kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I go to the Cocoa Board nursery for seedlings instead of growing seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya Cocoa Board ŋmɔ ko mli koni mayahe dumɔwui moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: The Cocoa Board breeds specialized hybrid seedlings that grow faster, resist common diseases, and yield many more cocoa pods than random seeds saved from a regular harvest.
ga: Cocoa Ajinafoi Akuu lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ni ji hybrid ni daa oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ehaa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa seedling is healthy before I bring it home to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani mikɛ amɛ aya shia koni miyadu?

english: A healthy cocoa seedling has deep green leaves, a sturdy stem without cracks, no visible insects or black spots, and roots that are firmly held together in soil within its nursery bag.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Tso lɛ mli wa ni ebɛ ŋmeii. Kplukai ni anaa loo ŋmeii diji komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ. Ni shishifãi komɛi yɛ ni kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Will taking pods from an old cocoa farm to make my own seedlings pass diseases to my new field?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ agbɛ hela ashwã ŋmɔji heei amli?

english: Yes, older cocoa trees often carry fungal diseases like black pod or viruses like swollen shoot that can hide in the seeds and infect your whole new farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni efuu ni baanyɛ ahi dumɔwui lɛ amli ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do young cocoa seedlings behave when I move them into the main field?
ga: Te kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily stressed by dry soil or harsh direct sunlight. They need shade crops around them and good soil moisture to survive transplanting and grow strong roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo hulu la ni naa wa haa amɛ haoɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo. ni amɛná shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni baaha anyɛ akwɛ nɔ ni aduɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: When is the best time for me to collect my seedlings and plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mabua dumɔwui anaa ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: You should plant your seedlings at the start of the main rainy season so the young roots get plenty of water to establish themselves before the hot dry season arrives.
ga: Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu babaoo koni amɛma shi dani hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: What basic work do I need to do to care for my young cocoa trees so they grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔi titrii esa akɛ matsu koni manyɛ makwɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Caring for young cocoa trees requires clearing surrounding weeds regularly so they do not steal water, providing shade plants to protect them from heat, and checking for insect damage.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. daa koni akaju nu Ha hulutsoo be ni baabu he kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni okwɛ kɛji kooloi bibii efite

english: How many years will it take for a good cocoa seedling to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwu kpakpa ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: High-quality hybrid cocoa seedlings from official nurseries usually begin producing pods within two to three years, whereas wild or uncertified seeds can take five years or longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii enumɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Can I use the small wild seedlings growing naturally under my old cocoa trees to start a new plot?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ koo mli dumɔwui bibii atsu nii. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kookoo tsei momoi ashishi koni ekɛje shikpɔŋ hee shishi?

english: Wild seedlings under old trees are usually weak, produce fewer pods, and are easily affected by diseases. Planting fresh seedlings from a certified nursery gives you a far stronger and more uniform farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tsei momoi ashishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ, ni helai yeɔ amɛ oya. Dumɔwui heei ni ooodu kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli awa ni efee ekome.

english: Why is investing time and effort into good cocoa farming better than leaving the trees to grow on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ be kɛ hewalɛ awo kookoo kpakpa dumɔ mli fe ni oooha tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to proper care. Using strong nursery stock and managing your farm well produces bigger harvests, yields high-quality cocoa beans, and provides a continuous income for many decades.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mli wa tsu nii ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa. Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa. ni ekɛ shika ni yaa nɔ eba afii nyɔŋmai abɔ

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit when the heat becomes too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When weather conditions become overly stressful or hot, tomato plants drop their blossoms to preserve energy and water, delaying fruit production until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does weeding too close to my cassava roots slow down how big the tubers grow?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, heavy soil disturbance right around the base can damage delicate feeding roots and cause stress, which slows down tuber growth and lowers yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni ebɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ekɛ haomɔ aba. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their tiny pods before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani amɛbaadara kwraa?

english: Cocoa trees drop immature pods (cherelle wilt) when stressed by sudden weather changes, lack of shade, or nutritional deficiency, as the tree prioritizes its own survival.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni edarako lɛ shi (amɛgboiɔ) kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei susuɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to minimize their surface exposure to the sun, preventing moisture loss and protecting the crop from extreme midday heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he yɛ gbi lɛ mli

english: How does strong wind affect my plantain farm before the trees bear fruit?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ dani tsei lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Strong winds shred the broad leaves of plantain trees, reducing their ability to make food through sunlight, which delays fruiting and weakens overall plant production.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fiteɔ plantain tso lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni ayɔɔ ni akɛhooɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn yellow and drop off after heavy flooding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nu afua ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the soil air pockets, suffocating the roots and preventing them from taking up nutrients, causing stress that leads to yellowing and leaf loss.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops yield so much less when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving every plant weak and low-yielding.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very leafy and tall but yield only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Shi ejieɔ ŋmei bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess nutrients or unbalanced growth causes cassava to focus all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of transferring energy underground to build thick tubers.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine loo dalɛ ni ejaaa haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e pee yi nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do my pepper vines stop setting fruit when insects start eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper wain tso lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo beni kooloi bibii jeɔ baai lɛ yeli shishi lɛ?

english: Leaves are a plant's food factories; when insects damage them, the plant loses energy and stops producing new fruits to conserve its remaining resources.
ga: Baai ji tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii kpata tsei ahiɛ lɛ, amɛhewalɛ baa shi ni amɛkpaa aduawai heei ni amɛwoɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam vines look stunted when I allow weeds to grow unchecked around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe ni mɔ ko mɔ ko tsiii enaa

english: Tall weeds shade yam vines from essential sunshine and steal moisture and nutrients from the soil, preventing the yam from growing thick tubers.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa lɛ he. ni ejuɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa sweet potato lɛ yitsei ni mli edɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my cocoa trees instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving enough space allows air to flow freely through the farm, which prevents fungal diseases and helps each tree grow strong enough to produce more pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu cocoa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Cocoa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa.

english: It is better not to plant cassava close to young cocoa. Cassava roots grow aggressively and take away too much water and soil food from the young cocoa. Additionally, digging up cassava during harvest disturbs and damages the delicate young cocoa roots. Plantain or cocoyam is much safer for shade.
ga: Ehi akɛ aaaduŋ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii. Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmei ni atsa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ gbaa ŋmei shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa ni efiteɔ amɛ. Plantain loo cocoa ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha hulutsoo.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and short root systems that cannot reach deep underground water. The harsh sun and dry winds draw moisture out of the leaves faster than the roots can pull it from the dry soil. Providing temporary shade trees like plantains protects them from getting scorched.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tamɔ plantains baaye abua ni shãa akafee nɔ ko.

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or useless branches (suckers) that waste the tree's food. Opening up the tree allows sunlight to reach the inner trunk and lower branches, which encourages more flowering and makes it harder for pests and diseases to hide.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni he ehiaaa (tso lɛ shishi) ni shwieɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Tso lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ kɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. ni haa fɔfɔii babaoo yaa hiɛ Ni ehaa ewaa ahaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, very wet weather. Rain drops bounce the fungal spores from the soil onto the low pods, and excess shade traps damp air around the pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by drought or lack of soil nutrients, or when there are no tiny insects (midges) to pollinate them. Spraying harsh liquid chemicals directly onto flowers can kill these helpful pollinating insects.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao tso lɛ. Aloo, kɛ́ kooloi bibii (ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ) bɛ ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbe nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ.

english: What causes small dark patches and dead spots on the fresh young shoots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii diji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ hei ni gboi yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: These dark spots are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects called mirids (capsids). They bite into young stems and branches to feed, leaving poisonous saliva behind that burns and kills the shoot tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (capsids) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tsei akutsei kɛ tsei aniji bibii kɛha niyenii. Amɛshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shãa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ fãji lɛ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my food crops turn pale yellow when the soil stays waterlogged after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on your land for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil. Without air, root systems suffocate and stop taking up key nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the green leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer to help my crops yield more?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba?

english: If your crop plants grow slowly, produce small yellowish leaves, or yield very few flowers and fruits despite getting enough rain and sun, your soil has run low on basic plant nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛyɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo aduawai fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting only fully ripe pods ensures the beans inside are mature enough to ferment into high-quality cocoa.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su tsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsake kɛya ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaafee kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same land where I just planted my young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo bibii amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have huge leaves that shade the young cocoa from intense heat, keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to leave so much space between my oil palm seedlings when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ mu tso dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees grow very large fronds and wide roots as they mature. Giving them enough distance prevents them from shading each other and competing for soil water, which ensures each tree gets enough resources to produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ebaatsi amɛhe gbɛ ni amɛkaye nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant moves what little it has to newer growth, causing the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ hee lɛ kɛyaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mishiɔ jwɛi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow quickly, they steal these vital resources away from your main crops, leaving your plants weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso ko fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight to make food. Staking the vines lifts the leaves high into the air to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant store energy and produce larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni amɛhoo nii. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience environmental stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Under stress, the plant drops flowers to conserve its energy to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo pollination ni ehiii yɛ haomɔ shishi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Maize heavily uses up soil nutrients like nitrogen. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ sũ mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen tsuɔ nii waa. Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, protects the ground from direct sun, preventing water from evaporating quickly. It keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from sprouting, and slowly rots to add rich organic matter back into the soil.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity when its lower leaves turn yellow and naturally drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You may also notice the soil cracking around the base of the plant as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Yucca baajie dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Ekolɛ obaana sũ ni egbɛ eshwa he lɛ. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it better to sow my maize seeds right after a good rain rather than during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need constant moisture to swell and germinate. If you plant in dry soil, the seeds can dry out, get eaten by insects, or rot, whereas moist soil gives seeds the immediate water they need to sprout quickly and build strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛfuu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi. ŋmeii yeɔ loo egboɔ Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my young coconut palms drop their small green fruits before they get big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada bɔ ni sa ni abaakpa?

english: Early fruit drop in coconuts usually happens because the tree is not getting enough water or potassium from the soil, or because sudden dry spells stress the tree while it is trying to feed the growing nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni woɔ yibii mra lɛ baa ejaakɛ tso lɛ naaa nu loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo ejaakɛ trukaa, trukaa ŋmɔlɔ haa tso lɛ haoɔ beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a few get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. If there is too much shade or the air is too dry, these insects cannot do their job and the unpollinated flowers simply shed.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn dark brown and rotten while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni miida lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil moisture changes too drastically between wet and dry spells, preventing the plant from absorbing enough calcium to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be teŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Why are some of my maize cobs missing grains or filling out only halfway?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo amɛyi fã pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize needs rain and gentle wind when its silks first emerge so pollen can land on every single silk. Hot weather or dry spells during this pollination period cause grains to fail to form on the cob.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni waaa he miihia ŋmãa. Beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ Bɔni afee ni pollen lɛ anyɛ akpɛtɛ siliki tsɔne fɛɛ tsɔne he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni mli egbi yɛ nɛkɛ pollination be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkafee yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce so many green leaves but very small potatoes underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji bibioo kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the sweet potato plant spends all its strength expanding leaves and branches on top instead of sending nutrients down to grow big root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛgbala ebaa kɛ eniji kɛya ŋwɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes instead of just growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting the vines onto stakes spreads the leaves out to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which is sent down into the ground to build a large tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la ashɛ he babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains soak the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that need loose, well-draining soil. When water logs the ground, the roots rot and lose their grip, making the top-heavy tree fall under its own weight or light wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu ho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ amɛhe. Ha tsei ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ shishi loo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa fioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism for cassava during dry weather. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces the amount of water it loses to the hot air, keeping its roots alive until the rain returns.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala yɛ ŋmei be mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baaha nu ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni oha eshishifãi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off when the weather gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants conserve water by dropping their flowers. High heat also damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to abort the blossoms.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pepper tsei lɛ buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hu fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ fɔfɔi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the middle vein of older maize leaves is a clear sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the crop needs to stay green and grow tall.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen lɛ miiho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why should I buy packaged seeds from a store instead of using seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo mli yɛ shwapo mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Packaged seeds from certified suppliers are specifically selected and treated to prevent seed-borne diseases and ensure high germination rates. Saved seeds from previous harvests often lose their vigor, produce lower yields, and carry pests or diseases into your new field.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ adɛŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni akɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ anaa ni eha amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ he waaa. ni haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai baa oshikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: If maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants will compete heavily for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground water. This competition causes the stalks to grow thin and weak, resulting in small or poorly filled ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ waa Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ yɛ toi bibii loo ekɛ ehe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell. Planting immediately after the first rain can cause seeds to germinate, only for the young shoots to dry up and die when the soil loses moisture before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Tsobii bibii pɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of the plant are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, meaning the plant lacks the fuel needed to stay green and grow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ tsofa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants behave like shade-loving crops; their leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Big trees act as natural umbrellas that keep the air cool and soil moist, which is necessary for young cocoa plants to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo. Baai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni he hiaa koni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves, but producing tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much water or excess nitrogen fertilizer, it focuses all its energy on leaf and stem growth. Because the top of the plant is taking all the energy, the plant stops storing food down in the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nu babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ. Ebaagbala ejwɛŋmɔ kɛba baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii. Tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when there is irregular watering. High heat stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni sa. Ha tsei agbee shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why have my pepper plants stopped producing new flowers even though the leaves still look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants slow down production when fully ripe peppers are left hanging on the plant too long. Picking mature peppers regularly signals to the plant that it needs to blossom again and produce more fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baaha amɛhe afee mlɛo kɛji akɛ ashi pepper ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eda lɛ tsu nii daa lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ehe miihia ni ewo fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my crops at night, but I cannot find them on the leaves during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii gbɛkɛ lɛ? Shi minaaa amɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli?

english: Armyworms are sensitive to direct heat and predators like birds. They hide in the soil or deep inside the plant whorls during the day and come out at night when temperatures cool down to feed on the leaves.
ga: Armyworms lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛbaye baai lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better during dry dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun. This prevents soil water from evaporating quickly, keeps plant roots cool, and slows down the growth of weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akatsɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni eha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni enyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which maize needs to stay healthy and green. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure restores nutrients so the plant can grow thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water cuts off oxygen in the soil, allowing fungal diseases to multiply. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain off safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ fo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids that suck sap and pass viruses to the plant. Controlling these pests early keeps leaves expanding properly to feed developing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛhaa muawai kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering stress. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering and mulching prevents flower drop and encourages fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ mli baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines on wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch sunlight efficiently to produce energy. This energy flows directly into building larger, healthier tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ aba. Hewalɛ nɛɛ hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu cowpea yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating these crops restores natural soil fertility for future seasons.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mango trees when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning thick inner branches lets sunlight and air circulate inside the canopy. This reduces fungal diseases and channels energy into growing fewer, but much larger and sweeter, mango fruits.
ga: Niji ni mli tse ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha mango lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Shi eda ni eyɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces seedlings to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting seeds at recommended distances ensures each plant gets enough resources to yield a good harvest.
ga: Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do tall weeds make my vegetable plants grow weak and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your vegetables. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop receives full nutrition to build sturdy stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni jɛ o-vegetables lɛ ahe Jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which acts as essential food for the crop. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves the nutrients they need to grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land continuously allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating tomatoes with crops like legumes breaks this disease cycle and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso pɔtɛɛ ko he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cassava together with maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ akɛ amɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Intercropping cassava and maize helps you get the most out of your land. Maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space after the maize is removed.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onáa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, edaa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni ajie ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. If planted too deep, the seed will exhaust its energy before reaching the surface, and if planted too shallow, birds or heat can ruin it.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. ni kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ Okpoi loo latsaa hu baanyɛ akpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even though I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering can drown the roots by taking away air from the soil, leading to root rot. Additionally, soil diseases like bacterial wilt can block the plant's internal tubes, causing it to wilt regardless of water.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai tamɔ bacteria wilt baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. ha egbo ni nu kɔɔɔ he eko

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or when they lack sufficient water and nutrients like calcium. Providing shade or consistent water helps the flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ eba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha fɔfɔi lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops in the middle of the day or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu yɛ gbi mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can drink before the sun gets hot. Mid-day watering causes water to evaporate quickly from the soil without reaching the roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni tsei lɛ aná nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eshɛɛɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are weeds so harmful to my young yam shoots when they start coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ awui kɛji amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young yam shoots and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that the crop needs. Clearing weeds early ensures the young yam plant gets enough energy to form big tubers later.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe sweet potato bibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato tso bibioo lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji sɛɛ mli.

english: How can I check if my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can check maturity by carefully digging around the base of one plant to see if the tubers have grown thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome shishi ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji bulb lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller cobs than the hybrid seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mihe lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a high yield in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special yield qualities in the next generation, resulting in smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai yibiiwoo sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like straws during the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss during intense heat. By curling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant conserve moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize grains weigh less when there is drought during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ tsiimɔ waaa beni hɔmɔ baa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Water is essential during the grain-filling stage for the plant to transport starches into the kernels. Without enough water, the plant cannot properly fill the grains, resulting in light, shriveled kernels that reduce total bag weight.
ga: Nu he miihia yɛ be mli ni awoɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ ŋmãa lɛ aya ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ awo amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgboɔ, ni no haa kotoku lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi.

english: Why do Fall Armyworm caterpillars cause my maize plants to stunt and produce empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiha mi-abɛi tsei lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiiwo ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Caterpillars eat the fresh leaves and the growing point of the maize plant. Since green leaves act as solar panels to make food for the crop, losing them prevents the plant from producing enough energy to build cobs.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ baai heei kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai eŋɔli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni akɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmei lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more plants, why do I end up with fewer total bags at harvest?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ total bags fioo nɔ beni mikpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces plants to compete fiercely for light, water, and soil nutrients. This stress results in tall, weak stalks that produce tiny cobs or no cobs at all, leading to a lower total yield than properly spaced crops.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo ebɛ kwraa Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi fe tsei ni aduɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my maize plants produce two full cobs while others only grow one small cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo ŋmeii enyɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmei bibioo kome pɛ lɛ?

english: A plant only grows a second cob if it has surplus water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When soil fertility is low or plants are stressed, the crop focuses all its energy on securing just one cob for survival.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ adara kɛyashɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ kɛji nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa loo tsei lɛ miihao lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmei kome ni amɛbaaŋɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The maize plant naturally moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the young growing leaves and developing cobs to protect new growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii amli ni ehaa ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii ni buɔ dalɛ hee he.

english: Why does applying fertilizer after my maize has already flowered fail to make the cobs bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni ŋmãa lɛ ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, ehaaa ŋmãa lɛ afee wuji lɛ?

english: Maize determines its cob size and the maximum number of kernel rows early in its vegetative stage. Once flowering begins, the plant stops making new cob structures and focuses only on filling the existing kernels.
ga: Abele tsɔɔ cob lɛ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ kɛ kernel rows ayibɔ yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli mra. Be ni esa akɛ aje fɔfɔi afeemɔ shishi Tsei lɛ kpaɔ cob structures heei amamɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ni amɛaawo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds produce heavier bags than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ kotokui ni tsii fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds carry high genetic vigor specifically bred for strong root systems, uniform growth, and dense grain filling. Saved seeds lose these strong genetic traits in the next generation, leading to uneven growth and lighter cobs.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ. Afɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ ŋmaa ni mli eyi obɔ Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: How can I tell by looking at the maize plant that the grains have reached their maximum weight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛ́ mikwɛ ŋmãa tso ko akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ amɛhewalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: When the crop matures, a small black layer forms at the tip where the grain attaches to the cob, and the husks dry out completely. This black spot shows that the plant has stopped transferring nutrients into the grain, meaning it has reached full weight.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko ni ji ediŋŋ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ. Efeɔ yɛ naagbee he ni dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ. ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baagbi kwraa Nɛkɛ ŋmãa diŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: Why does freshly harvested maize weigh more in the bag than maize that has been dried in the sun for a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ tsiimɔ yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli fe ŋmãa ni hulu egbi otsi kome lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains high amounts of water trapped inside the kernels. Sun drying evaporates this excess moisture, making the grain lighter but safe from mold and pests during long-term storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu babaoo ni etsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo shi ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: When is the best month for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Applying fertilizer in the month of April is ideal because the early rains will help dissolve the fertilizer into the soil so your cocoa trees can easily absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ April mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm during the April season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ April mli?

english: Yes, applying fertilizer in April allows the April rains to dissolve the fertilizer into the dirt, making it possible for cocoa roots to soak it up and nourish the trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ April mli lɛ, ebaaha April nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii.

english: What happens if I put fertilizer on my cocoa farm when the ground is dry and there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo kookoo ŋmɔ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs rain to work properly. Without rain to dissolve it into the soil, the cocoa trees cannot absorb the nutrients through their roots.
ga: Nugbɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ bɛ ni baashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm need rain right after I spread fertilizer on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ he hiaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater breaks down and dissolves the fertilizer into the soil, which allows the cocoa trees to drink in the nutrients they need to grow well.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni enuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do cocoa trees take in the nutrients from the fertilizer I buy?
ga: Te cacao tsei lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees absorb nutrients through their roots in the soil, but this only happens after rainwater dissolves the fertilizer into the ground.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shi enɛ baa mli pɛ kɛkɛ ni nugbɔ nu lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do the early April rains help my cocoa crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ April shishijee gbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: The April rains melt applied fertilizer into the soil, allowing the cocoa trees to absorb the food they need to start flowering.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ April mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ nyɛɔ enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ebɔi fɔfɔi.

english: How can I get my cocoa trees to produce plenty of flowers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cacao tso lɛ aná fɔfɔi babaoo?

english: Applying fertilizer in April helps, because when the April rains dissolve it into the soil, the cocoa trees absorb the nutrients and gain the strength to flower.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ April mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ April mli lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahewalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Does putting fertilizer on my farm directly help my cocoa trees flower?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, when fertilizer is washed into the soil by rain, cocoa trees absorb it, which gives them the nutrients required to trigger flowering.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kakao tso lɛ baaŋɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why aren't my cocoa trees flowering even though I left fertilizer on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi beni mishiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees can only use fertilizer once rain falls to dissolve it into the soil, enabling the roots to absorb it and push out flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii pɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ koni amɛkɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: What basic steps should I take in April to improve flower growth on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee yɛ April mli koni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Apply fertilizer to your farm in April so that the incoming rains dissolve it into the earth, allowing your cocoa trees to feed on it and flower.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ April mli koni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni oha o-cacao tso lɛ afee tsofa ni ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant moves what little it has from the older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big leaves but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji waa shi eshishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy building thick stem growth and foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle intense direct sunlight and heat. Planting them alongside fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the young plants from drying out while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to grow up wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need direct exposure to sunlight to manufacture energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli ni ebaatsi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee. Enɛ baaye abua ni baa helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth, making them top-heavy when carrying bunches. Heaping extra soil around the base and supporting the trunk with bamboo or wooden props keeps them standing upright.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛji akɛ awo lɛ kui amli. Okɛ sũ krokomɛi ato shishigbɛ lɛ he ni okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my young oil palm trees forming small flowers that dry up without producing any palm fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? ni gbiɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Young oil palms often produce only male flowers during their early growth stages or when experiencing dry weather stress. As the palm gets older and receives consistent moisture and food, it naturally begins producing female flowers that form fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso dumɔwui woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee be mli loo kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Beni tso lɛ daa ni enine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii nɔ daa lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaje shishi kɛ fɔfɔi yei ni feɔ aduawai akui.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any fruits are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off without producing fruit when temperatures get extremely hot or when soil moisture swings rapidly from very dry to very wet. Consistent watering and light shade during extreme heat keep the blossoms healthy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni mli wa yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into tight bundles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled, distorted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the leaf sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and allows normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni eye ebua ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cowpea crops lose many of their blossoms when continuous rains fall during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ fɔfɔii babaoo fiteɔ nɛkɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains physically wash pollen out of open cowpea blossoms and create high humidity that encourages fungal rots, causing the flowers to drop before seed pods can develop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ pollen ni jɛɔ cowpea fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ni ehaa hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni woɔ fungal rot he hewalɛ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baa.

english: Why are my cabbage plants spreading wide with big leaves instead of forming a hard, round center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaabe lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to form tightly if the weather stays too hot during development or if the crop experiences irregular watering, which forces the plant to stay in a leafy growth phase instead of packing leaves tightly together.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛyaa hiɛ lɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ be mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ekome.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important food for plant leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ahe baai Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the plant. Spraying approved treatments early in the morning while they are active helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi be mli ni tsofa lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ akpa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, the plant suffocates, allowing fungi in the soil to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbo ni amɛgbo.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the afternoon weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps save the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why does clearing weeds make my crops grow so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ to he ko lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck plant juice and spread plant diseases. Spraying neem oil or insect soap controls these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo kooloi ahe samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and prevents heavy rains from washing away good topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and misshapen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and loose soil to expand easily. If the soil is packed hard or full of stones, the tuber struggles to push outward, leading to crooked or small yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tubers baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsi ehe kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo efeɔ bibioo.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to sow seeds after two or three steady rains have wet the soil deeply. Planting too early after just one light rain can cause seeds to dry up if the rain pauses.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food that helps crops grow strong and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Amɛji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli.

english: Why does planting beans on my farm make the maize I plant next grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes capture natural nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts as a free, natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Mɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread all over the soil but produce very small potatoes underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi potato ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: When sweet potatoes get too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant puts all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of expanding the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji sweet potatoes ná nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ bulbs yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot or the soil runs out of water, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.
