english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, causing the cassava tubers to drown and rot from underground fungi that thrive in excess water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni fa fe nine mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do weed plants grow so much faster than my pepper crops after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsei lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal available water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your planted crops have a chance to settle and absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu ni yɔɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Dani tsei ni oduɔ lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛŋɔ amɛ,.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and short instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee kuku moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing downward into the earth, so if the soil is hard or full of rocks, the tubers cannot push through easily and become deformed.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ yitso lɛ mli mlɛo ni efite.

english: Maize should be planted after the first two or three steady rains have soaked the ground well so the seeds stay moist enough underground to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei 2-3 ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are insects attacking my cowpea plants right when the flowers begin to open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet sap that attracts pests like pod borers, which eat the young pods unless protective measures are used right before flowering.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ pod borers, ni yeɔ pod bibii lɛ. ja atsu gbɛi ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal stems become weak at transporting nutrients from the roots to the branches, leading to lower pod yields.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, tso lɛ mli tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pod yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans put nitrogen back into the earth through their roots. Rotating them refreshes your soil naturally for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ otsake ohe lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: What does mulching mean, and why should I spread dry grass around my garden vegetables?
ga: Mɛni ji mulching shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Mulching means covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or straw. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps moisture in the soil, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps the plant roots cool in heat.
ga: Mulching tsɔɔ akɛ abaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi, baai loo jwɛi aha onibii lɛ niyenii. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛji akɛ edɔ amɛ

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Giving your plants steady water at the root level and protecting the soil with mulch helps save the blossoms so tomatoes can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ bu shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni o-tomato lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet, and crowded farms. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight and fresh air into your farm helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ, niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves. Spraying a natural neem leaf extract or recommended insecticide clears the pests and allows fresh leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni ji neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi lɛ kɛjɛ mli, ni eye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Cassava cuttings should ideally be planted about 1 meter apart from each other in all directions. Proper spacing gives the underground roots enough room to expand into big, heavy tubers without fighting for soil food.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Yams need deep, loose soil or high mounds to grow smoothly downwards. If the soil is too hard, stony, or poorly prepared, the growing tuber gets blocked and becomes stunted or crooked.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo asaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsofai ni miida lɛ atsĩ naa ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ.

english: What is the safest way to keep weevils from destroying my harvested maize in storage?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ ŋmeii ni mikpaa yɛ nitoohe lɛ naa koni ekafite?

english: Make sure your maize grains are dried completely until they are hard before storing. Storing them in airtight containers, such as PICS triple-layer bags, starves insects of air so they cannot survive or damage your grain.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn kernels lɛ agbi kwraa ni efee shiŋŋ dani okɛto. Kɛ́ akɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, tamɔ PICS tri-layer bag lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ashwie kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkahi shi loo amɛkafite odumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so it doesn't spoil underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Most local cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop. Leaving cassava in the ground too long makes the tubers woody, watery, and poor for eating.
ga: Kasava henɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee tsei, nu yɔɔ mli ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Plant canopy shade helps keep the seedlings cool and retains moisture in the soil while their root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli gĩɔ. Tso lɛ shade yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the primary element plants use to build green foliage and capture energy from the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji nɔ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛheɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the cassava roots underneath are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: When soil has too much leafy nitrogen or the plants are spaced too closely, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ tsɔ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do I need to spend time putting long wooden poles for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Ha sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high above the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Exposure to sunlight allows the plant to produce food energy, which travels down to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛha niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato tuber lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and slowing down fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa fioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on tomatoes is commonly caused by viruses spread by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies. When insects pierce the leaves to feed, they transmit infections that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle tomato lɛ he lɛ baa, kɛ́ kooloi lɛ bote baai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ tsei anaa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before any fruit can grow from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to environmental stress, such as dry soil, irregular watering, or extreme heat during the blooming stage, causing the plant to abort fruit production to conserve water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant the exact same crop in the same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the topsoil while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating different crops gives the soil a chance to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow around one plantain tree causes them to fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Removing extra shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce heavy, large bunches.
ga: Ni aaaŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ Dumɔwu kome pɛ he lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa niji ni tsii ni dara.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most cultivated crops. They aggressively suck up soil nutrients and fertilizer before your crop roots can reach them, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ. Amɛkɛ ekãa heɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on growing tomatoes are caused by calcium deficiency in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. When soil moisture fluctuates dramatically, the plant cannot transport calcium up to the fruit cell walls.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato ni adu lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli baa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake waa lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ agbogboi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do traders at the market reject my garden eggs when some are very large and others are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔ lɛ kpoo mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ekomɛi dara waa ni ekomɛi hu daraaa moŋ?

english: Market traders prefer medium, uniform-sized produce because they are easier to package, measure, and sell to buyers. When plants receive uneven water, nutrients, or spacing, they produce mismatched crop sizes instead of a consistent yield.
ga: Jarayeli mli jarayelɔi sumɔɔ nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ kɛ nɔ ni dalɛ ji ekome lɛ ejaakɛ ewaaa akɛ abaawo mli, asusu he ni ahɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo gbɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ yibiiwoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I encourage my cassava plants to grow roots that are all a good, medium size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-cassava tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ shishifãi kpakpai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ?

english: To get uniform tubers, space your stem cuttings evenly so no plant starves for sunlight or nutrients, and weed regularly so the growing roots do not have to compete with wild plants for soil food.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná yitso ni feɔ ekome lɛ, Ha tso lɛ niji lɛ afee ekome bɔni afee ni hulu la loo niyenii kpakpai akashɛ tso lɛ he. Ni jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni shishifãi ni miida lɛ kɛ koo mli tsei akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch light instead of putting energy into growing strong stalks and large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ moŋ, ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ fataa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii agboi ni wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant naturally moves its remaining food to the young, active leaves at the top to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and produce less yield each year when I use the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo daa afi beni mikɛ he kome tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same ground repeatedly exhausts specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops—like planting legumes after cereal crops—helps restore natural fertility to the earth.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake, tamɔ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa sɛɛ Ye obua ni okɛ je lɛŋ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the middle of hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ baa baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the farm right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruits crack open when plants receive a sudden heavy watering or rain after a dry period. The inside of the fruit expands rapidly with water faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ nu nu babaoo trukaa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya kɛ nu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of visiting insects like bees for pollination. Without successful pollination or enough water, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves look burnt and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living shelter that protects the young cocoa from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Will masɛi lɛ, ebaaha ená he ko ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my cassava plants help or harm my cassava growth?
ga: Ani cowpea ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi yucca lɛ dalɛ awui?

english: Intercropping cowpeas helps cassava because cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. They also spread over the ground to suppress weeds and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cowpea ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua cassava. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu koni amɛgbe jwɛi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no taller plants grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo be mli ni cacao tsei komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa creates living shade umbrellas that keep the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow starting from the tip, it shows the soil lacks enough nitrogen. The plant is moving whatever food nutrients it has from its old bottom leaves to keep the young leaves on top alive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward on hot days to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to heat, which keeps moisture from escaping. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, it is just the plant's natural way of surviving heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛba baai ni hulutsoo baa lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ No ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ kɛkɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves but giving me very tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into growing green leaves and tall stems on top instead of sending that energy down to build big tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or lack water. The plant discards the blossoms to protect itself and save energy until moisture levels improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food that builds big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing fungal rot caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni feɔ bulbs wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ŋmɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi fungal rot ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie Mi plantain titri lɛ.

english: Having too many shoots around one main plantain stem creates competition for nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the main stem to produce larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Ni aaana ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle Tso titri kome he lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws when it stops raining for a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsi kome nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize rolls its leaves into tight tubes during dry spells to hide the inner surface from the direct sun. This survival trick reduces water evaporation and helps the plant stay alive until rain comes.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ ewoɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni ekɛtee emligbɛ lɛ koni hulu la akatswa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa nɛɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsei hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and light away from your crops. When weeds share the soil, your crops cannot feed properly and will struggle to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ jaa shikpɔŋ lɛ Onibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same land continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear my farmland every single year before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa afi dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing your land annually removes aggressive weeds and brush that compete with your crops for light, space, and nutrients. Regular clearing prevents wild vegetation from taking over and keeps your soil manageable for planting.
ga: Kɛ́ otsi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ, ejieɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, he ko, kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ otsi ohe daa lɛ, ebaatsi koo mli tsei anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nɔ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui.

english: When is the right time for me to start preparing my land for the upcoming farming season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ?

english: You should start clearing and preparing your land shortly before the main rains begin. This ensures the soil is clean and ready to capture rainfall, allowing seeds to germinate immediately without weed competition.
ga: Esa akɛ oje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ ehe saamɔ shishi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ he atse ni efee klalo kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ jwɛi akaŋ.

english: Why can't I just clear my land once and plant crops for several years without clearing again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikome ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii afii babaoo ni mafooo nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tropical vegetation and weeds grow back rapidly every season due to heat and rain. If you do not clear your land every year, wild weeds will quickly overpower your planted crops and steal their water and soil food.
ga: Tsoi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ daa oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji otsiii shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid cutting down all the green bush on my farm during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni mifoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he?

english: Clearing all vegetation down to bare soil during extreme heat exposes the ground directly to harsh sunlight. This bakes the soil, burns essential nutrients, and causes the earth to dry out completely before planting season.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei fɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ashã. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ atsake ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi kwraa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Should I burn the weeds and clearing waste on my field, or leave them on the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared plant material on the ground as mulch is usually better than burning. Mulch shades the soil to keep it cool, preserves soil moisture, and naturally breaks down into rich organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe nibii ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi fe ni ashãa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha hulutsoo aba. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli

english: Is clearing my land with a cutlass better for my soil than using chemical weedkillers?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi fe tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Manual clearing with a cutlass protects beneficial earthworms and keeps soil structure intact. Relying heavily on chemical weedkillers can damage the natural biology of the soil over time if not used correctly.
ga: Nine ni akɛ tsɔne ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ he nii lɛ baabu shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops help them grow bigger and yield more?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink the water and eat the nutrients meant for your crops. Removing them gives your crops direct access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture so they can yield better.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ ni nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hulu la. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwo yibii kpakpai

english: Why do weeds sprout back so quickly on my farm even right after I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil waiting for sunlight and air. When you clear the top cover, sun hits the soil surface and signals those buried seeds to sprout immediately.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, amɛmiimɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛji ojie ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ Hulu lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can leaving my farm uncleared for too long bring insect pests to my crops?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, overgrown weeds and bushy clearings create hidden breeding grounds for pests like grasshoppers, armyworms, and rodents. Keeping your farm well-cleared removes these insect hiding spots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ feɔ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii, asraafoi akui, kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to cut down all the big shade trees when clearing land for young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafo tsei fɛɛ ni eda lɛ beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Young crops can easily scorch under intense sun. Leaving some large shade trees provides natural canopy cover that protects young plants from heat stroke and preserves moisture in the topsoil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do rice fields need so much water on the soil compared to maize farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji biɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ŋmɔji ahe lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in wet conditions, and keeping standing water in the field helps suppress weeds that would otherwise compete with the rice for food and sunlight, while keeping the soil temperature steady for better plant growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Ni nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi ni baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ hulu la lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ hiɔ shi daa koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so the grains do not fall off and waste in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ akagbee shi ni ekɛ jwɛi akashwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the seed heads turn from green to a golden-yellow color and the grains feel hard when you bite or squeeze them.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmɔ loo okɛmimɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water, and once the rainy season returns, the plant will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry up the pollen inside tomato blossoms, causing the plant to shed its flowers to protect itself from losing too much water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkafite nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why do crops grow tall and dark green in some spots on my farm but stay short and yellowish in other spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shi amɛfeɔ kukuji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Uneven growth usually happens because soil quality varies across a farm; areas with richer organic matter and better water retention support stronger growth, while washed-out or hard soils starve the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Hei ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ kɛ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ahoɔ loo fɛ̃i baaha tsei aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize and keeps the land healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too close together instead of giving them space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni maha amɛ gbɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants fight each other for limited sunlight, ground nutrients, and moisture, leading to thin stems and a poor harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulutsoo ni faaa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the middle of the afternoon even when the ground was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot afternoons, leaves lose water to the dry air faster than roots can soak it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ aya oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehe woɔ mli be kukuoo mli koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm more right after the main rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The warm humidity and sudden sprout of fresh, soft plant leaves after early rains create ideal feeding and breeding conditions for insects to multiply rapidly.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ kɛ tsei ahe baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa niyenii kɛ fɔmɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni kooloi lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why do black spots appear on my vegetable leaves when rain falls continuously for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ diji kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous moisture and wet leaves allow fungal spores carried in the air and splash-back from the rain to settle, germinate, and cause leaf spot diseases on vulnerable crops.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa fungal spores lɛ yaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ mli koni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe, amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛha baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ aba tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. When they get too much sun without enough shade, their leaves burn and turn yellow. They need temporary shade plants around them to protect them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Beni enine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Baai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantain suckers on the same land as my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ kookoo tsei heei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow much faster than cocoa trees and have wide leaves that work like natural umbrellas. They shade the young cocoa plants from intense sunshine and help keep moisture in the soil during the hot season.
ga: Plantains daa oya fe cacao tsei, ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Amɛhaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɛɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe, ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize grow tall with green leaves but produces tiny corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni ebaa eŋɔli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: A maize plant needs different nutrients at different times. Plenty of leaf growth comes from nitrogen in the soil, but big, healthy cobs require phosphorus and potassium. If those nutrients are missing when the plant flowers, the cobs stay small.
ga: Abɛi tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Baai babaoo ni daa lɛ jɛɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa lɛ he miihia fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. Kɛji nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ laaje beni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ lɛ Cob lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its strength and needs fertilizer or a rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he waaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ awo mli?

english: If your crops grow slower than usual, turn pale green, or give you smaller harvests every year even when there is good rain, your soil has run out of nutrients and needs compost, fertilizer, or a break.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli tse Aloo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo najiaŋ.

english: Why do black spots start appearing on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Rainy weather combined with heavy leaf shade traps moisture on the pods, allowing the fungus to grow and spread fast.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ baa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long without draining away. Excess water suffocates the roots underground and lets soil fungi attack and rot the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni amɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before tiny pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing lots of yellow flowers but no actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi tomato diɛŋtsɛ ko bɛ.

english: Tomato flowers need to be pollinated by wind or insects to turn into fruit. Extreme heat or lack of water can cause the flowers to dry up and fall off before fruit can grow.
ga: Esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi dani aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak and reduces your overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so poorly even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm. They take up the water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil before your main crops can reach them, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baashɛ. Shimɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can help the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛshishijee su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open clear field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that get scorched under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides shade and cools the air around the young cocoa trees until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ feɔ fɛo. Akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ fɛ̃i mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four maize seeds in the same hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing stalks fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. This competition results in thin, weak stems and very small ears of maize.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa.

english: Why do elders always say we must build high soil mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai kɛɔ wɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand downward into large, long tubers. Mounding loosens the hard topsoil so the expanding yam encounters no resistance while growing.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi. Mounding baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni wa lɛ afee mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potatoes ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ bɛ nɔ ko ni teɔ shi ewoɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving dirt-like powder inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko ni tamɔ muji yɛ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when soil stays soaked with standing water for too long. Excessive water causes root rot fungus to develop, destroying the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why do my vegetable beds dry out so quickly during the dry Harmattan season even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable saat lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind and hot sun pull water straight out of bare soil very fast. Covering the bare ground around your crop stems with dry grass or leaves (mulching) traps moisture in the soil.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ oya waa. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into tomato fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot or soil moisture drops suddenly, tomato plants get stressed and shed their flowers to conserve energy, preventing fruit formation.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi trukaa. Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and yield less food at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like unwanted thieves on your farm; their roots drink the water and eat the plant food intended for your crops, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching your plants.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni ataooo amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eshishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ tsei aniyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the distance between my crops matter so much when I am planting my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he hiaa waa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops at the right distance ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, ground nutrients, and water without fighting its neighbors. Proper spacing allows you to fit the ideal number of plants per acre for the highest harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ akutsoŋbii awui Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsei ayibɔ ni sa woɔ acre kome mli koni oná ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How do I know the right number of seeds or plants to put on one acre of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui loo tsei abɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ adu yɛ acre kome nɔ?

english: Every crop has a recommended plant population per acre based on how wide it grows and how much light it needs. By measuring the distance between your rows and plants, you can place the exact number of plants needed for the best yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsei ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ehi acre kome mli. Enɛ damɔ tso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ kɛ la babaoo ni he hiaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ susumɔ nɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa koni yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ awo mli.

english: What happens to my harvest if I try to crowd too many crops into a small space?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo he bibioo ko?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they block sunlight from each other and fight for soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems, small fruits, and lower total harvests than if they were spaced correctly.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ Amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, aduawai bibii kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa shi fe kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers often encourage us to adopt farming ideas from dry countries like Israel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔkɛ okwaayeli he susumɔi ni jɛ maji ni nɔ egbi tamɔ Israel lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii lɛ?

english: Countries like Israel have learned to produce high crop yields in hot, dry conditions using precise plant spacing, controlled water delivery, and smart soil care, which helps farmers elsewhere grow more food with fewer resources.
ga: Maji tamɔ Israel ekase bɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ, ni egbi kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa ni akudɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yɛ nilee mli Enɛ haa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ kɛ nibii fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ niyenii babaoo.

english: How does using drip water systems help my crops perform better than waiting for rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ ni mimɛɔ lɛ?

english: Drip systems deliver water directly to the roots in exact amounts, preventing crops from stressing during dry periods and keeping them growing steadily all year round.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ nu yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ bɔ ni sa mli. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: How can I make a small piece of land produce enough food to feed my whole household?
ga: Mafee shikpɔŋ bibioo ko Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shia muu lɛ fɛɛ aye?

english: You can maximize a small plot by using proper plant spacing, improved seed varieties, and good soil nutrients to grow the highest possible number of healthy crops per square meter.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he bibioo ko aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ he ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ otsu nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ Koni akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ sqɛɛ mita kome mli.

english: What is the difference between planting crops just for my kitchen and planting for industrial buyers?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ni miduɔ kɛhaa mi-kpataashi pɛ kɛ tsei ni miduɔ kɛha nitsumɔhei ni heɔ nii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Planting for industries requires consistent crop sizes, larger quantities, and strict row spacing so that processing factories can easily buy, transport, and process your produce in bulk.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ tsei adalɛi ni yaa nɔ daa. babaoo kɛ sɛɛkuu ni mli wa bɔni afee ni nitsumɔhei ni feɔ nibii lɛ anyɛ ahe, amɛkɛya, ni amɛtsu onibii lɛ ahe nii babaoo yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers get huge harvests from small farms while others with large fields get very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi náa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji wuji lɛ naa yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: High harvests depend on proper crop population, good seeds, and soil care rather than field size alone. A well-spaced, properly fed small farm will often produce more than an uncared-for large farm.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni fa babaoo damɔ tsei ayibɔ ni sa nɔ. dumɔwui kpakpai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ Fe ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ dalɛ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔji wuji ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stunt in growth even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need plant food like nitrogen from the soil to stay green and grow. Rain provides water, but if the soil lacks nutrients or is packed too tightly, the plants cannot feed properly.
ga: Tsei hia tsei niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some plants in my field ripen and give fruits much earlier than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii mra fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ?

english: Uneven plant growth happens when seeds are planted at different depths, when soil fertility varies across the plot, or when crowded plants are shaded out by faster-growing neighbors.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ loo be mli ni akutsoŋbii ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants producing tassels when they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Ni eyɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: When maize experiences severe stress from dry weather or poor soil nutrients early in life, it stops growing tall and flowers early to produce seeds before it starves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa na haomɔ ni naa wa kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli yɛ eshihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ŋmãa kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛ fɔfɔii mra koni ekɛ dumɔwui awo dani hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack open in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba yɛ shikpɔŋ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers usually crack when heavy rains arrive suddenly after a long dry period. The sudden surge of water causes the inside of the tuber to expand faster than its skin can stretch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato tsei lɛ amli fãa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni eho lɛ sɛɛ. Nu ni hoɔ trukaa lɛ ha yitso lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛɛ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant lacks adequate water, which prevents successful pollination from happening.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa pollination lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why do my orange trees drop a lot of small green fruits early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Ehe babaoo gbeeɔ shi oya?

english: Citrus trees naturally shed excess young fruit if the soil does not have enough water or nutrients to support all of the fruits to full size.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baajie aduawai bibii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ fɛɛ afee nɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my cowpea crop have lots of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Twisted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viruses spread by sap-sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ

english: If cocoa leaves turn pale green or yellow, look smaller than usual, or if the trees stop producing flowers and fresh shoots, the soil is low on essential plant nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Etamɔ nɔ ni efee bibioo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ loo kɛji tso lɛ kpa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei feemɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tsei.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops' roots, while also acting as hiding places for insects and diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli.

english: Why should I buy improved maize seeds like Obaatampa instead of just saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ Obaatampa lɛ dumɔwui moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred by scientists to give high yields and resist local diseases. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in smaller harvests and weaker plants in future seasons.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ewo dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa yɛ sɛɛ mli bei amli.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a crop variety is 'improved' or research-backed?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ‘afee tso henɔ ko jogbaŋŋ’ loo niiamlitaomɔ fi sɛɛ?

english: An improved variety means scientists selected and combined the best traits of a plant—such as faster growth, higher nutrition, or drought resistance—so farmers get a bigger and more reliable harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ srɔtoi ni etee hiɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jeŋ nilelɔi ehala tso lɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni edaa oya lɛ, ni amɛkɛfee ekome. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa loo hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ Koni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ ana nibii babaoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do some corn varieties stay short but still yield bigger cobs than tall traditional corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi hiɔ shi be kukuoo shi amɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji lolo fe ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ, ni ji blema ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Modern bred varieties use their energy to produce heavy cobs rather than growing super tall stalks. Shorter stalks are also stronger and less likely to break or fall over during heavy rains and winds.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa. Tsoi ni yɔɔ kukuji lɛ hu mli wa ni amɛkumɔ loo amɛgbee shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, leaving the plant with too little energy to grow full-sized cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni ekɛbaashɛ eshishifã lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow even though it is raining well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Rainfall feeds the plant water, but the crop still needs nutrients from healthy soil or fertilizer to stay green and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Can a seed variety that was developed in one country or region perform well if I plant it in my town?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee yɛ maŋ loo kpokpaa ko nɔ lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many research-backed crop varieties are bred to be adaptable, meaning they can thrive across different soil types and weather conditions across various regions.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔ tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni niiamlitaomɔ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ.

english: What makes certain crop varieties handle dry weather better than traditional ones?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe blema ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant crop varieties are bred to grow deeper roots that pull moisture from far underground, and their leaves lose less water during hot dry spells.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni nu fioo pɛ amɛbaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do pests attack my grain in storage, and how do breeding programs help prevent this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ fɔmɔ he gbɛjianɔtoi baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa?

english: Storage pests feed on soft or exposed grains. Researchers breed certain crop varieties with harder grains or tighter husk covers that make it physically difficult for insects to penetrate and ruin the stored harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo dumɔwui ni eje kpo lɛ. Nibii amlitaolɔi efɔ tsei komɛi ni amɛdumɔwui ni wa loo amɛshishifãi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ kɛhaa kooloi bibii akɛ amɛaabote nibii ni ato lɛ amli ni amɛfite.

english: How do I know if the seeds I am buying will actually sprout into healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baatsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Certified seeds undergo laboratory quality testing to guarantee high germination rates. You can identify them by official certification tags on the bag showing they are clean, undamaged, and disease-free.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ kaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ laboratori mli koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ oyɔse enɛɛmɛi kɛtsɔ odaseyeli wolo ko ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe tse, amɛfiteee, ni hela ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my maize crop has fully matured and is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is fully mature when the outer husks turn brown and papery, the leaves dry up, and a small black spot forms at the base of each hard kernel.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee tamɔ wolo, baai lɛ egbi, ni ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji jeɔ kpo. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui ni wa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. Keeping or planting shade plants like plantains or forest trees creates a cool environment and preserves moisture in the soil for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo amɛdumɔ Ehaa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to feed properly and produce larger bunches of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up, turning yellow, and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo waa lɛ?

english: This leaf behavior is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects or infected stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected stems early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ su nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Aduɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food. Staking also lifts the foliage off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases while helping the tuber grow much larger underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing thin and weak with small ears when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds close together causes the maize plants to compete aggressively for water, light, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and room to grow thick stems and large ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and yellow dust inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ sũ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on the tender growing center of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps protect the crop before the pest destroys the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ fiteɔ he ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant produce leaves instead of fruit. Consistent watering and balanced fertilizer help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphid-transmitted viruses. Controlling these tiny insects with soap sprays or targeted pest treatments keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo helai ni gbeɔ aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔ loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow well during the first year of planting, but give me smaller harvests by the third year on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mikɛdu lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ewo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kuku nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Every time you harvest crops, they remove essential nutrients from the dirt. Continuous farming without adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer drains the soil's strength, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put natural fertility back into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores soil richness for the next crop cycle.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between growing tomatoes inside a greenhouse tent and growing them directly on my open land?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ greenhouse buu mli kɛ adumɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Greenhouse farming protects crops inside a plastic or net structure where water, temperature, and pests are controlled, while open-field farming relies entirely on natural rainfall and weather, leaving plants exposed to outdoor pests and rain damage.
ga: Greenhouse okwaayeli buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋloo ni kudɔɔ nu, latsaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli damɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ kwraa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa kponɔgbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Is it true that starting a greenhouse farm costs a lot of money compared to regular farming on open ground?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shishi lɛ biɔ shika babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, setting up a greenhouse requires a large starting budget to buy materials like metal or wooden frames, special plastic covers, drip pipes, and high-quality seeds, whereas open-field farming mainly requires land preparation and basic tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsũ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ maa biɔ shishijee shika babaoo koni akɛhe nibii tamɔ dade loo tso ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Plastic krɛdɛɛ ni akɛhaa nɔ, paipi ni hoɔ nu kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli ni agbele naa lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kɛ shishijee nibii titri.

english: Why do my open-field tomato plants get damaged so easily during the heavy rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes mud onto leaves, spreads fungal diseases, washes away soil nutrients, and floods roots, which causes tomato plants to rot or lose their leaves when grown without cover.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa muji shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ ni nɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do tomato flowers sometimes dry up and fall off my plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks enough water, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni nitrogen fertilizer fa babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do buyers in the market often pay a higher price for greenhouse tomatoes than open-field ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara babaoo fe ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Greenhouse tomatoes are usually smooth, uniform in size, free from insect bites, and last longer without spoiling, which makes market women and supermarket buyers willing to pay a premium price.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni akɛwoɔ greenhouse mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa Ebɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ. ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee Enɛ haa jarayeli yei kɛ jarayeli hei wuji amli jarayelɔi sumɔɔ ni amɛwo jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: How can I plan my vegetable planting so I do not harvest at the same time when the market is flooded with cheap tomatoes?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ato gbɛjianɔ koni adu aduawai koni akakpa amɛ yɛ be kome mli? Kɛ tomato ni jara waaa ni eyi jara lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: By using simple irrigation or planting slightly before or after the main rainy season starts, you can harvest during off-peak months when tomatoes are scarce and market prices are high.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo dumɔ fioo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi loo yɛ no sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ, be mli ni tomatoi faaa ni jara wa waa lɛ.

english: What is the difference between buying packaged imported seeds and using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ ni akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ ahemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛto kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Packaged hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce higher yields and resist diseases, while seeds saved from your previous harvest may grow into weaker plants with lower yields and less uniform fruit.
ga: Atsɔse dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ paketi lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai akamɔ amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tamɔɔɔ amɛhe.

english: How do I know if my crop needs extra fertilizer or if my soil is already fertile enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he loo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii momo?

english: If your plant leaves turn pale yellow, grow slowly, or produce very small fruits, the crop is showing signs that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, eda blɛoo, loo ewo yibii bibii waa. Tso lɛ miitsɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly before I can transport them to the city market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fite oya dani mikɛmaje maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot fast if they are harvested when fully ripe, stacked in heavy wooden crates that crush them, or exposed to high heat and direct sunlight during transport.
ga: Tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ beni ekwɛ̃ kwraa. Akɛto tso adekai ni tsii ni akumɔ mli. aloo ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ
