english: At what stage should I harvest my tomatoes so they stay fresh long enough for market women to buy them?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ makpa mi-tomato lɛ koni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni jara nɔ yei lɛ ahe?

english: Harvest tomatoes when they reach the 'breaker' stage—when the green skin just begins to turn light orange or pink—so they can finish ripening during transport without getting bruised.
ga: Kpãa tomatoi beni amɛshɛɔ ‘breaker’ fã lɛ he, beni hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ. Enɛ baaha tomato lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli.

english: How can I stop my harvested maize from spoiling quickly when I have a large surplus?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya? Akɛni miyɛ nɔ ni fa fe nine babaoo hewɔ lɛ

english: To prevent spoilage, maize must be dried thoroughly until the grains are hard before storage. Keeping them in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) prevents moisture build-up and keeps weevils from attacking your crop.
ga: koni akafite lɛ Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani akɛto. Kɛ́ okɛwo kotoku ko ni mli ewo muji mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni baatutua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot within just a few days after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly when exposed to high heat and rough handling during harvest. Picking them early in the morning, placing them gently in crates rather than sacks, and keeping them in a shaded, cool area slows down decay.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ekɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Okɛ amɛ awo adekai amli blɛoo moŋ fe kotokui amli. Ni kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite fioo.

english: Yellow, curling leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting stems taken from already infected plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei ni miida ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo lɛ anɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in damp, overly shaded farms. Pruning excess leaves to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la lɛ abote mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are my plantain plants falling over before the bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and can easily be knocked over by strong winds or weakened by banana stem weevils. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo poles helps support the heavy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa amɛ shi loo banana ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they do not rot underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? Koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Yams are generally ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely, which shows the tuber has stopped growing and is ready to be dug out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ.

english: How can I make sure my pond fish stay healthy and grow fast during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni loo ni yɔɔ mi-po lɛ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛdara oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Fish need cool water and good oxygen levels to grow well. Top up your pond with fresh water regularly, create shade over parts of the water, and feed them during cooler hours like early morning or late evening.
ga: Nu ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he miihia loo koni enyɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Okɛ nu kpakpa awo nubu lɛ mli daa. Ehaa hulutsoo ko baa nu lɛ nɔ. ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ bei ni mli ejɔ tamɔ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to your soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does adding animal manure help my vegetables grow better than just using chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves the soil's structure so it retains moisture longer during hot days, feeds helpful soil microbes, and releases nutrients steadily over a longer period.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Ehaa niyenii kɛha sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: What quality standards do buyers look for if I want to sell my pepper produce outside my local market?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai ni hi jogbaŋŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ pepper nibii yɛ mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ kponɔ?

english: Buyers outside local markets look for peppers that are clean, free of insect damage or rot, uniform in size and color, and harvested with intact stems to ensure longer shelf life.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ kponɔ lɛ taoɔ chili ni he tse. Ebɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo fitemɔ. Amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe su yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli. ni akpaa ni eshishifãi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat vegetables that I have sprayed with farm chemicals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye aduawai ni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, crops are safe to eat after spraying as long as you use the recommended dose and wait for the specific 'harvesting waiting period' listed on the chemical bottle, which allows the chemical to break down safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ beni afɔse tsofa lɛ sɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛhaa lɛ baatsu nii ni omɛ ‘kpamɔ be’ ni aŋmala awo tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ, Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why did my crops turn yellow and burn after I applied weed killer to my field last month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshã beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ wo ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ nyɔŋ ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops burn when chemicals are mixed too strong, sprayed in the hot afternoon sun, or applied incorrectly. Measuring exact doses and spraying during cooler morning or evening hours prevents crop damage.
ga: Tsei baashã kɛ́ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Spray yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Kɛ́ asusu yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: I am afraid that using chemicals will ruin my land and food; why should I consider using them?
ga: Misheɔ gbeyei akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii. Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ekɛ nitsumɔ he lɛ?

english: Agrochemicals act like medicine for crops to protect them against diseases and pests. When handled correctly according to expert instructions, they safeguard your crop yield without harming your health or soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa kɛha tsei ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ otsu he nii jogbaŋŋ taakɛ ŋaawolɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ Amɛbaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni amɛyeee ohewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ awui.

english: How do I know the correct amount of pesticide to mix in my knapsack sprayer so I do not destroy my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ayibɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛfutu mi-sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni mikafite miŋmɔ lɛ.

english: You should use the standardized measuring cup that comes with the product and follow the recommended ratio on the label or ask an extension officer to demonstrate the exact mixing ratio for your tank size.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo ni akɛbaa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ ratios ni atsɔɔ akɛ aŋma yɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Aloo bi mɔ ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ ni eha nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ aya hiɛ koni etsɔɔ bɔ ni tsɔne lɛ mlifutumɔ lɛ fa ha pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha o-tanki lɛ dalɛ.

english: Should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees, or will cutting them harm the plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ? Aloo ani nakai tsei niji lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye kookoo tso lɛ awui?

english: Pruning excess branches helps the tree by opening the canopy to light and air, which stops diseases from spreading and encourages the plant to put its energy into producing fruits rather than useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ ni egbeleɔ ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ awo yibii moŋ fe baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: Can I just trim my crop stems anywhere I want to keep them from growing too tall?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he koni amɛkakwɛ tsɔ?

english: No, cutting plants carelessly creates rough open wounds where fungal infections and pests can enter. Pruning must be done carefully at specific branch joints using clean, sharp tools.
ga: Dabi, tso ni afoɔ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa pilamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ abote mli lɛ Esa akɛ akwɛ niji pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ.

english: How will changing from my traditional farming methods to new recommended practices improve my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mitsake kɛjɛ mi blema okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ anɔ kɛtee nifeemɔi heei ni ajieɔ yi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Modern practices like proper plant spacing, timely fertilizer application, and correct chemical use help plants grow stronger and produce higher yields compared to older, unguided methods.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi tamɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ be naa Kɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto gbɛi ni eho lɛ ahe. ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔi bɛ mli

english: Why does it take a long time to see the benefits after I start using a new farming technique?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani minaa sɛɛnamɔi beni mibɔi okwaayeli he ŋaa hee ko kɛ nitsumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil and plant systems recover and adapt slowly over time. The benefits build up gradually season after season as the soil quality improves and plants develop stronger root systems.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei ahe gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ he baa shi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Sɛɛnamɔi lɛ baaya nɔ abua naa fiofio. Yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hilɛ yaa hiɛ ni tsei lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ,

english: Should I change all my farming practices at once or start small on a small plot of land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsake mi okwaayeli nifeemɔi lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mabɔi bibioo? Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ?

english: It is best to start small and make changes step-by-step. This allows you to learn the new techniques properly without taking big financial risks on your entire farm at once.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ obaaje shishi bibioo ni ofee tsakemɔi shikome shikome. Enɛ haa okaseɔ ŋaai heei jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ shika he oshara wulu ko wooo oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli shikome.

english: Why do insects keep destroying my crops even after I sprayed pesticide on them once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie amɛnɔ shikome moŋ?

english: A single spray usually kills adult pests but may miss eggs hidden under leaves. Pest control requires monitoring and properly timed repeat applications to break the insect's life cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa kome ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni eda lɛ. Shi ekolɛ obaasusu ŋmeii ni akɛtee baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ahe. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ biɔ ni akwɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ koni akɛfo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa acts like a living umbrella, shielding young plants from intense heat and conserving moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small bunches when many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for food, water, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers so that only one or two strong ones remain allows the main stem to concentrate its energy on producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso ŋmɔji (ŋmɔji) babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli babaoo bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ 1-2 pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tso lɛ yibii wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it necessary to erect wooden stakes for my yam leaves to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ato tso ko he gbɛjianɔ koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts yam vines off the ground so their leaves get maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows leaves to make food, which travels down to build much bigger and healthier yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking woɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe tsei lɛ awo hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when the rain becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges helps drain excess rainwater away and protects the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-rotted manure early in the plant's life restores the green color and keeps growth strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, tsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes holes in my young maize leaves that look like insects chewed them overnight?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai ni tamɔ kooloi ni ŋmɔ amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This leaf damage is often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central growing part of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying neem-based sprays or recommended pest control helps protect the crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ni fiteɔ waa aba.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow poorly when the soil completely dries out between rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice relies on flooded or consistently wet soil to absorb nutrients properly and suppress weed growth. When the soil dries out completely, root growth slows down, and competing weeds quickly choke the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu afua loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni etsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baafee mlɛo. Ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience stress from high heat, sudden dry soil, or a lack of water. Keeping soil consistently moist and applying mulch around the base of the plant helps cool the roots and keep flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi loo nu efo mli trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by viruses spread by these insects. Spraying plants early with organic insecticidal soap or neem oil keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem fɔ afɔ tsei anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help my soil for the next season's crop?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay after harvest, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil, feeding the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that keep the soil moist and shelter the cocoa leaves until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the center in a V-shape indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer around the base of the maize plant restores healthy green growth.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Abɛi tso shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like waste inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's funnel. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the whorl helps destroy the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water prevents oxygen from reaching them. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu lɛ ehi shi, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ ayashɛ amɛhe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to maximum sunlight, allowing the plant to produce more energy through photosynthesis. This extra energy is transferred to the underground tuber, making it grow larger.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Akɛ hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ yaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. ha efee agbo

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and placing dry grass mulch around the base protects the root zone from temperature stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ muji awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifã lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ he.

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, which can also spread plant viruses. Regular inspection and applying neem oil or appropriate pest sprays control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ hu ashwã tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akwɛ mli daa ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Excessive leaves with low pod production usually result from too much nitrogen in the soil or insect pests like thrips attacking the buds. Spraying for thrips just as flowering begins helps protect flower buds so pods can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ jɛɔ nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ afɔ thrips he tsofa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii afee ŋmeii.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crop plants help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into natural soil food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during strong winds before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when their root systems are weak or overloaded by too many stems growing from one spot. Pruning extra suckers so that only two or three stems remain per stand gives the roots strength to support heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo shishifãi babaoo ni miida kɛjɛ he kome lɛ fa babaoo. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi yɛ shidaamɔ kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the crop is fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaasaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do people recommend planting cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the surrounding maize grow stronger without exhausting the land.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight because their leaves get burned and lose water quickly. Planting them under fast-growing shade plants like plantains protects them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained onto tall wooden sticks to give me large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔse sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛwo bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in their leaves when exposed to sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which creates more energy to feed and expand the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa koni akɛtao niyenii ni akɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground when the soil gets soaked with heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rainfall leaves water standing in the ground for too long, the roots drown and soil fungi quickly attack, causing root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does crop sickness or leaf spot spread so fast through my farm right after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela loo baai ahe tsɔi gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Raindrops hit infected leaves with force and splash water carrying tiny germs onto healthy nearby plants. This water movement is the main way fungal diseases spread quickly across a wet field.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi tswaa baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ. kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi ni hiɛ helai bibii Yaa ni okɛ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ awo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Nu ni hoɔ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any fruit during the very hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot, tomato plants experience extreme heat stress. They drop their blossoms to preserve their own water and survive, which stops new fruits from forming.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli baa lɛ baakpe. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnu lɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa aduawai heei baa.

english: Why are tiny worms hiding and eating inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that seek out the softest, newest leaves at the center of the young maize plant because it offers them food and protection from predators.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni taoɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ejaakɛ ehaa amɛ niyenii kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops turn out thin and produce small yields when I put many seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one spot forces the young plants to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛaawo he kome lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bibii fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to wilt much faster during brief dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that drink up stored soil moisture faster than your crops can. Removing weeds leaves more water in the soil for your crops during hot days.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ato lɛ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooogbe lɛ baaha nu babaoo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which acts as the main food for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii titri ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of lush green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: When bean plants get too much nitrogen from fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowering. Reducing high-nitrogen inputs encourages the plant to form flowers and yield more pods.
ga: Beni bean tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni baa shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely, causing stress to the plant. Providing consistent watering and slight shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight cups and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil solution helps control these pests and protects new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebuɔ shweremɔ hee he.

english: Why do small holes keep appearing on the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars feeding on the plant. Removing weeds around the farm and using safe insect sprays keep these foliage pests from damaging the crop.
ga: Koolooi ni yeɔ baa tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa baa lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii koni nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots begin to rot underground during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them in poorly drained soil. Planting cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haa amɛmuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate energy to store in their underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground where they can catch more sunlight and stay clear of soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akashɛ ehe.

english: Why do the young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in high humidity and damp conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into the farm helps dry out dampness and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds come during fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can struggle to hold the weight of heavy fruit bunches in loose soil. Propping up the fruiting stems with strong bamboo poles provides extra physical support against wind.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Yɛ hei ni aduawai akui ni tsii nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ, tsei ni woɔ aduawai ni akɛ ŋmeii ni wa maa shi lɛ haa abuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he babaoo.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like stone and dry out very fast a few days after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa ni egbiɔ oya waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves and manure, which normally hold soil together like a sponge. Adding manure or organic mulch improves soil structure so it holds water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome tamɔ sponji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni ehiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from high heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cowpea plant leaves fold up during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves when the sun is hottest to reduce water loss from evaporation. It is a natural defence mechanism that helps the plant stay cool and preserve moisture until temperatures drop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ fɛ̃i mli ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my groundnut plants close up completely at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut leaves naturally fold together at night to trap moisture and protect the delicate surface of the leaf from cold winds and heavy nighttime dew.
ga: Peanut baai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa gbɛkɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa gbɛkɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the main plant food responsible for deep green growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their rich green colour.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Eji tso niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and weak even though I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering fills all the small air spaces in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly. Letting the soil dry out slightly between waterings keeps roots healthy and helps the plant grow taller.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ fioo yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: What causes the roots of my cassava plants to turn soft and rot underground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess water sitting around cassava roots starves them of air, causing rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and keeps the tubers safe.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni ehaa egboɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees easily burn under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade and humidity, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow sturdy enough to endure full sun.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden heavy rains stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season, showing that the plant has finished storing food in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my maize after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe mi-ŋmã lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong, aggressive seeds that are adapted to jump up quickly after rain to capture light and nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your maize gets the water and plant food it needs to catch up.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli wa ni feɔ basabasa. Amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛjo foi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-abele lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow first, it means your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The maize plant is pulling nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top because the soil lacks enough food.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abele tsei miigba nitrogen kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii ejaakɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year even when I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every growing season. If you plant the same crop on the same land repeatedly without adding manure, fertilizers, or letting the soil rest, the earth becomes depleted, causing yields to drop gradually over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ, Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ohaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ni no baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio. lɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and tender roots that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from plantain trees or taller forest trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo koo mli tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin roots when I plant the stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo beni miduɔ shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight underground for the same limited water and nutrients. Giving each cassava stem enough space allows the roots to expand fully and store energy, producing thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aha cassava tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ. ni kɛ yitso ni mli tse baa

english: Why do small worms start eating the middle leaves of my young maize as soon as the dry spell begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yeli shishi kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Warm and dry weather helps pest eggs, like the Fall Armyworm, hatch much faster. During short dry spells, the moths quickly lay eggs inside the leaf funnel of young maize plants where it stays moist, giving the worms easy food.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ, ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. Yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui lɛ oya yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli he ni akwɛɔ koni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii akɛ amɛaaye niyenii

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny whiteflies that spread cassava mosaic virus while feeding on the leaves. Whiteflies multiply faster in dry, hot conditions, making the disease spread quickly across the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ baai lɛ Whiteflies fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's maize harvest grow weaker than the certified seeds I buy from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are special hybrids bred for maximum strength in a single generation. The seeds collected from that harvest lose those special parent traits, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs if planted again.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ koni ená hewalɛ babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔlɔi asui. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaana ŋmei bibioo kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize make my maize look greener and healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work with tiny soil organisms to trap nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. Nearby maize plants absorb this extra plant food, which makes their leaves darker green and grow faster.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni emɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress or sudden dry weather. When a tomato plant feels too hot or thirsty, it drops its flowers to save water and energy just to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ nu he akɛ amɛhe edɔ tsɔ loo kumai miiye amɛ lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and taller than my crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit deep in the soil and are naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they wake up and drink water instantly when it rains. Domesticated crops take longer to settle their roots, allowing wild weeds to steal soil food and light first.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛnuɔ nu. Shia tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛhiɔ shi. Ha koo mli jwɛi lɛ aju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if I give them too much fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can 'burn' crop roots due to excessive salts, causing the leaf tips to brown, dry up, and potentially kill the plant instead of helping it grow.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ‘ashã’ tsei shishifãi yɛ ŋmei babaoo hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔɔ asarasu, egbiɔ, ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda.

english: Why do my crops look scorched or burnt after I put fertilizer right near the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã loo eshã yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. If placed directly against the stem without being mixed into the soil or watered down, it pulls moisture out of the plant tissues, leading to direct chemical burns.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ masɛi tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛfutuuu sũ lɛ mli loo awooo mli nu. Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli fãji amli. Ekɛ tsofa shãa tɛ̃ɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy branches but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ niji kɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to direct all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves above ground, leaving very little energy to store starch in the roots below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛya tsei kɛ baai ni mli ewo wu ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi shi ni akɛtoɔ starch yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does putting dried manure or compost around my tree crops help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fataa he lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ awo mi tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Organic materials like manure act like a sponge in the soil, holding water near the root zone for longer periods while releasing nutrients slowly without burning the tree.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fiofio ni ehaaa tso lɛ ashã lɛ fata he

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete heavily for sunlight. They stretch upwards as fast as possible to reach light, sacrificing stem thickness and strength in the process.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishifã kɛ ehewalɛ baa shi yɛ nifeemɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by sudden dry spells, high heat, or a lack of specific nutrients like potassium, which the tree needs to hold and nourish young pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium, ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛma shi shiŋŋ ni eha ŋmeii bibii lɛ niyenii lɛ ha amɛhao.

english: Is it true that weeds can steal fertilizer away from my crops?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ jwɛi baanyɛ aju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients and water much faster than your crops, leaving your main plants starved even if you applied fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otso titri lɛ kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though I already added fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil is too wet, preventing roots from breathing, or that the soil is missing a specific nutrient that your current fertilizer type does not provide.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɛɛ haaa lɛ?

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi moŋ?

english: In hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it. Curling up is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun and conserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Curling ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Bɔni afee ni ajie baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi ni aha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are damaged by insects or by a lack of plant food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii efite mitso lɛ baai lɛ loo tso niyenii faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Insects physically bite, chew holes, or leave sticky waste on leaves, whereas nutrient shortages cause smooth yellowing, pale spots, or brown edges across the leaf without physical holes.
ga: Kplukai ŋmɔɔ bu loo amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ, yɛ be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bu bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: What is the difference between spraying fertilizer on my crop leaves and putting granular fertilizer into the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baa nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Spraying fertilizer directly on leaves gives plants a quick food boost, especially when they look weak or during dry conditions. Granular fertilizer goes into the soil so the roots can drink it up over a longer period. Both work well to nourish crops as long as you use quality fertilizer correctly.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii oya. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ loo eyɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen fertilizer or are sitting in waterlogged soil. When plants lack proper nutrients, they cannot make the green color needed to feed themselves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛye amɛhe niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant's sap, or by a plant virus. These pests weaken the plant, preventing it from having enough energy to develop healthy pepper pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee pepper pods ni mli wa.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in direct sun without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch and dry out under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your crops properly gives each plant enough root space and light to grow big and produce high yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shishifãi kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my cassava plants make them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiha amɛmiidara oya?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. When you remove weeds, all the natural nutrients and water in the soil go straight into nourishing your cassava roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la. Adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaya tɛ̃ɛ koni eyaha o-cassava shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant in the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best not to plant saved hybrid maize seeds because the crops in the next season will grow unevenly and yield much smaller cobs. Buying fresh certified seeds every season ensures strong plants and high yields.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ejaakɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo ŋmãa bibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Too much rain causes water to collect around the roots, choking off air to the soil. This waterlogged environment creates ideal conditions for soil fungi to infect and rot the cassava tubers before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. suffocating in the dirt Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná hela ni amɛfite ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why does burning bush on my field before planting hurt the soil over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ mli lɛ ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Burning kills beneficial soil organisms and destroys organic matter that keeps the soil rich and moist. Leaving plant clearing waste to rot naturally turns it into manure, which improves your soil fertility over time.
ga: Shãa gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary canopy shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when the bunches start getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have a very shallow root system and top-heavy fruit bunches. As the fruit grows heavier, wind or even the fruit's weight can pull the roots out of the ground; propping up the main stem with sturdy wooden Y-stakes prevents the plant from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa kɛ aduawai akui ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ tsii fe tsutsu lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ loo aduawai lɛ tsiimɔ po baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tso ni wa fee lɛ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the middle of the leaf outwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip and moving along the central vein (midrib) of a maize plant is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ naagbeehei ni nyiɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize in the exact same spot on my farm season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows soil-borne pests to build up year after year. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas replenishes nitrogen in the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ ekome afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa sũ mli nitrogen lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating holes right inside the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the heart (whorl) of young maize plants. Applying recommended organic sprays or insecticidal dust directly into the whorl early in the morning stops them from destroying the central growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tswaa ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ atsui (ring) lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ sũ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite he ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and getting tiny and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Upward curling and crinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf sap and transmitting viruses. Spraying neem seed oil extract or soapy water under the leaves helps suppress these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my bean crop as soon as the flowers start to open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-pea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Insects like flower thrips are attracted to the sweet nectar and tender leaves of bean flowers. If they damage the blossoms, the flowers drop off and seed pods cannot form, so protective organic or mild chemical sprays are needed right as flowering starts.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips Amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ amli nu kɛ baai bibii. Kɛji nibii nɛɛ kɛ fitemɔ ba fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni dumɔwui akutsei lɛ efeŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he ni ji organic loo tsofai ni bɛ mlɛo atsu nii. Be ni esa akɛ aje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground when heavy rains last for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water drives out oxygen, causing the roots to drown and fungal rot organisms to multiply. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps rainfall drain away quickly so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ hoɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed all their flowers before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden swings between dry soil and heavy watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots by applying grass mulch helps stabilize moisture and protect blossoms.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo he haomɔ loo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni mli wa teŋ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ po ni aaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and stake my yam vines on wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ko ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground so leaves receive full sunlight and are kept away from fungal diseases living in the wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni ekɛha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ naa

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight can scorch their delicate leaves. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves, acting as a natural umbrella to protect young cocoa trees from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or leaves the ground too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of healthy leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ baai ni wa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the tomato plant spend all its energy growing big stem and leaves. To get good fruit, the plant needs a balanced nutrient mix containing phosphorus and potassium, which encourage flowering and fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji. Bɔni afee ni oná aduawai kpakpai Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium fata he. ni haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo baa

english: What causes black spots to spread across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. When heavy rains arrive, the fungus spreads easily from pod to pod through water droplets. Pruning extra branches helps air and sunlight dry out the trees to reduce infection.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nu mli ŋmeii anɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tso lɛ mli gĩɔ koni helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Look for small ragged holes in the central leaves of young corn plants and small piles of light brown waste that looks like sawdust inside the leaf funnel. Early detection helps you protect your crop before the caterpillars eat the growing tip.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abua naa Etamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baa ŋmei mli. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room underground to grow large, thick cassava tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: How does a sudden dry spell right after planting affect my bean seeds?
ga: Te trukaa ni egbiɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ saa mi-beans lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Bean seeds need consistent moisture to sprout and push roots into the soil. If the soil dries out completely right after planting, the seeds will stop germinating and die inside the dirt before emerging.
ga: Bean dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛjeɔ kpo.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds from the agricultural store give better yields than seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate brief dry spells, and produce uniform, larger cobs. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over time, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Eŋmɛɔ be kukuoo mli nugbɔshiimɔ he gbɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my stored grains get moldy even when I keep them inside dry sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛtoɔ kotoku ni egbi mli?

english: If grains are not dried completely under the sun before putting them into sacks, trapped internal moisture creates a warm, damp environment inside the bag. This moisture breeds mold and attracts insects during storage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi kɛbaa be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Most cassava varieties are ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off. Leaving tubers in the ground for too long makes them woody, tough, and prone to rotting.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha efee tsei, ewa ni ebaanyɛ egbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the heat becomes intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha edɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps restore soil fertility and breaks the cycle of crop diseases.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. ni ekpa tsei ahe helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning dense leaves to let in light and clearing weeds helps keep the farm dry and prevents the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ duŋ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli koni la abote mli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive pest that feeds on tender young maize shoot funnel leaves. Applying approved treatments early into the center of the plant help protect your crop from total yield loss.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni Akpɛlɛ Nɔ lɛ ni Akɛtsuɔ Nii Mra Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ yibiiwoo ni baafite kwraa lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my garden pepper plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that drain sap from fresh leaves. Spraying organic soaps or approved pesticides controls these insects and stops them from spreading viral infections to your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic soap loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã onibii amli.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to plant cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei?

english: Healthy cassava soil should feel loose, dark, and crumble easily so roots can expand without effort. If the soil is heavy clay that holds too much standing water, the cassava roots will rot underground.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni efoɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɔɔ mli. Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When is the right time to start clearing bush and preparing my land before the major rain starts?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje brɔshi shwiemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ shishi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?
