english: Clearing bush late in the dry season (around January or February) gives you enough time to remove stump obstacles and till the soil so you can plant immediately after the first steady rains begin in March or April.
ga: Ajieɔ tsei bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee Enɛ (aaafee January loo February) baaha oná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛjie tsei bibii ni tsiɔ amɛhe naa lɛ ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni onyɛ odu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ March loo April mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they suffer from dry soil, extreme heat, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the roots mulched and watered consistently prevents heat stress so fruits can set.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni oha amɛ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akatsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to produce a bunch after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains require heavy nutrients and plenty of water to fruit quickly. Leaving too many suckers attached to one mother plant forces them to compete for food, so pruning extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to fruit.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii kɛ nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ewo yibii oya. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔlɔ kome he lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye niyenii he akaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my cassava, and how does it help my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas cover the bare ground to stop weed growth and capture nitrogen from the air to naturally feed the cassava, giving you two harvests from one plot while building up your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii haa hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ anɔ koni ekpa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii enyɔ be mli ni otswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much direct sun, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to cocoa provides temporary living umbrellas that shield the seedlings and keep the soil moist until the trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa lɛ he lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before they even produce ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and build strength. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season helps keep leaves green so the plant can make big, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hewalɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it true that planting cassava on the exact same piece of land every year ruins the soil?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava pulls heavy amounts of nutrients out of the earth as it forms big tubers. Growing it repeatedly on the same plot without giving the land a rest or rotating with crops like groundnuts will wear out the soil, leading to smaller harvests each year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ efee ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni he ko bɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he loo atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my crops look soft and withered during the middle of the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot days, plant leaves lose moisture into the warm air faster than their roots can suck water out of the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water, but it usually stands back up in the late afternoon once the heat reduces.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛteɔ shi shwane beni hulutsoo be lɛ eba shi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extended dry periods, or too much strong nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during dry weather helps protect the blossoms so they can mature into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Gbimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ be mli ni gbii egbi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit leaf curl virus, or by extreme weather fluctuations. Keeping weeds away from your bed reduces where insects hide and helps keep your crop healthier.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tsakeɔ waa lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ tsi he kɛjɛ saatsoi ahe lɛ, ebaaha hei ni kooloi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see small holes chewed into my cassava leaves, and will it destroy my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu bibioo ko lɛ? Chew cassava baai Ani ebaafite wɔŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually made by insects like grasshoppers or beetles feeding on your crop. A few holes will not kill the crop, but if pests eat too many leaves, the plant cannot gather enough sunlight to grow big tubers under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ onibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Buu fioo komɛi egbeŋ oŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ye baai babaoo hu? Tso lɛ nyɛŋ abua hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I space out my maize seeds instead of putting three or four in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala ŋmãa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni makɛ etɛ loo ejwɛ awo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing stalks fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing seeds out properly ensures each individual plant gets enough energy to build a thick stem and large ears.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji.

english: How does growing groundnuts next to my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. Maize plants feeding on this natural nitrogen get free plant food, making them greener and stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmãa kooloo ni yeɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nɛɛ naa tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko. Ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants take so long to produce fruit when I leave all the smaller shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the parent plant. Pruning away the smaller suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main stem to focus all its energy on producing large fruit bunches faster.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ashi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai wuji ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crops use to make leaves green, and when the soil is empty, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee efolo Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: How does using organic fertilizer help my crops grow differently than using chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Organic fertilizer acts like dark, rich bush soil by feeding tiny living organisms underground and helping the soil hold moisture for a long time. Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly and quickly, but it does not improve the soil structure or help it hold water.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ niyenii ni amɛhaa lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ shishi ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ ni oya. Shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo loo eyeee ebuaaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize yields when I plant on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves without giving the soil time to rest. It also allows crop-specific insects and diseases to multiply in the soil, attacking your crops earlier and reducing your harvest.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ hu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tutua oŋmɔshi nibii oya. ni okɛ nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings brown and dry out during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The hot dry winds during harmattan suck water out of leaves faster than fragile young roots can pull water from the dry ground. Without natural shade trees to block the sun and wind, young cocoa leaves burn up and drop off.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi yɛ harmattva beaŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baatsi adebɔɔ mli hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ, kookoo baai bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when we get too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the ground to breathe. When excess rain floods the soil for too long, water fills those air pockets, drowning the roots and encouraging rot fungi to attack the wet tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant feels too much stress from sudden hot dry spells or unbalanced nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself rather than spending power to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejaaa lɛ miigba amɛnaa tsɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ohewalɛ baatsu nii ni okɛdu aduawai

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward and stay small instead of expanding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. Their feeding damages the leaf veins and can transfer plant viruses that stop the leaves from growing flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni haaa baa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do insect pests seem to appear on my farm in huge numbers right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: Many farm insects lay eggs or sleep inside the dry soil during the dry season. The moisture and warmth of the first rains act as a signal for all those dormant insects to hatch simultaneously and feed on tender new green leaves.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo woɔ amɛwui loo amɛwɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli latsaa kɛ latsaa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ okadi kɛha koolooi ni ewɔ. Mɛi ni fɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Okɛto he ni oye baai bibii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why are the vines on my yam farm wilting and turning black before the yams are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani sweet potato lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Black, wilting yam leaves are usually caused by a leaf fungal disease called anthracnose. The damp air during heavy rainy months helps fungal spores spread across leaves, stopping the plant from making food to grow big underground tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baa lɛ diŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ fɛɛ amli. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni eda ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like timber trees; they have shallow fibrous roots that stay close to the topsoil. When a bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet ground.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ fiber ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Okɛ ohe awo hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ amli oya

english: How long does a young oil palm tree take before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso bibioo ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Oil palm trees usually take about 3 to 4 years after planting in the field to start bearing their first fresh fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu mu tsei yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, eheɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛjeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii heei ni akui lɛ woɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do oil palm trees need so much space between them when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mu tsei ahe hiaa ni gbɛ babaoo ahi amɛteŋ beni miduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees grow very large, wide fronds and deep root systems. Giving them 8 to 9 meters of space ensures every tree gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with nearby palms.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ daa waa, ni amɛbaai lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ. He ni akɛhaa mitai 8 kɛyashi 9 lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce flowers but fail to form any actual fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifɔlɔ shi amɛwooo aduawai babaoo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palms have separate male and female flowers. If there are no pollinating insects (like the oil palm weevil) or wind to transfer pollen from male to female flowers, the female flowers dry up without producing fruit.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa (tamɔ ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ) bɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yei anɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm trees turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves can happen naturally as fronds age, but if widespread, it usually means the palm lacks essential soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, or is experiencing water stress during dry weather.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni baai lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nu he haomɔ ni enaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How does a long dry season affect my oil palm tree yield?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa mi-oil palm lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palms require continuous moisture to develop fruit. A long dry season causes trees to slow down flower and fruit development, which reduces the number and size of fruit bunches several months later.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛwo yibii. Hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai adalɛ. Enɛ baaha aduawai akui lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ aba shi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ.

english: What can I do to protect my young oil palm trees from pests in the field?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu oil palm dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Young oil palms are vulnerable to pests like rhinoceros beetles and rodents. Clearing weed debris around the base of the palms and inspecting the central shoot regularly helps prevent severe damage early on.
ga: Oil palm dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ rhinoceros ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni okwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite waa mra.

english: How can I tell when an oil palm fruit bunch is ready to harvest for the mill?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mu tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛha nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: A fruit bunch is mature and ready for harvest when its color turns deep orange-red and a few individual ripe fruits naturally break loose and fall to the ground beneath the tree.
ga: Yibii akui lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛtsɔ red-orange ni mli kwɔ. Ni aduawai ni etsu lɛ ekomɛi baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: What happens to my oil palm fruits if I do not take them to the mill immediately after cutting them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-oil palm yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛteeee ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Harvested palm fruits spoil quickly. Leaving them on the ground for more than 24 to 48 hours increases free fatty acid levels in the palm fruit, which degrades the oil quality and reduces its market value.
ga: Tso yibii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ni fe ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 lɛ, ehaa fatty acid ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baaha mu lɛ afee fɛo, ni ebaaha jara ni eyɔɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How do processing mills determine the quality and price of my harvested palm fruit?
ga: Te nitsumɔhe ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ale bɔ ni mi-palm yibii ni mikpa lɛ hi ha kɛ bɔ ni ejara wa ha?

english: Mills look at the overall weight of fresh fruit bunches, their freshness, and how well-matured the individual fruits are, as ripe and undamaged bunches yield higher quantities of good palm oil.
ga: Mil lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai heei akuu lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ. aduawai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni ekwɛ̃ Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni efiteee lɛ jieɔ ŋmei fɔ kpakpa babaoo.

english: Is planting oil palm a reliable investment compared to seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Ani mu tso ni aduɔ lɛ ji shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa he?

english: Unlike seasonal crops that must be planted every year, oil palm is a long-term perennial crop that can produce harvested fruit continuously for 25 to 30 years once mature, offering steady year-round income.
ga: Mu tso ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ adu daa afi lɛ ahe. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmaa ni yaa nɔ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Ehaa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to be cut?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantain tso lɛ eda kwraa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Plantain bunches are ready to harvest when the individual fingers become plump and rounded rather than angular, the tiny dried flowers at the tips drop off easily, and the upper leaves of the plant begin to turn yellow.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji akɛ inchi fɛɛ inchi mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. fɔfɔi bibii ni egbi Naakpa lɛ baagbee shi oya. Ni tso lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What is the safest way to cut down a heavy plantain bunch so it does not get bruised or destroyed?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ plantain agbo ko koni amɛkafite loo amɛkafite?

english: Cut halfway into the stem about middle-height on the plant so the weight of the bunch causes the top half to bend down gently toward you. This allows you to hold and cut the bunch cleanly without it crashing to the ground.
ga: Kpãa tso lɛ shishi kɛyashɛ aaafee ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ. tso lɛ he aaafee gbɛ lɛ fã Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋtayaa lɛ tsiimɔ aha ŋwɛi fã lɛ abɔle ehe blɛoo kɛba oŋɔɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ofoɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ ni ohaaa egbee shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops perform so much better when I inspect my farm daily instead of just sending workers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni matsu nitsulɔi kɛba lɛ?

english: Walking through your farm regularly helps you spot early signs of crop stress, disease outbreaks, or pest attacks before they spread, allowing you to take immediate action and protect your yields.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ ni ofeɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao. helai ni baa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuamɔ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni obuɔ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: How can daily monitoring help me get bigger and healthier plantain yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ daa gbi kwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná plantain yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Regular visits allow you to prune dead leaves on time, cut away excess shoots, support heavy fruiting stems before wind knocks them down, and harvest bunches at the exact moment of peak maturity.
ga: Saramɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ haa onyɛɔ ofoɔ baai ni egboi lɛ ahe yɛ be ni sa mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa amɛ. Ni okpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop off before the bunch is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Early leaf yellowing in plantains is usually caused by lack of water during dry spells, poor soil nutrients (especially nitrogen and potassium), or root damage from soil pests like nematodes.
ga: Baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ plantains nɔ, bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii (Titri lɛ nitrogen kɛ potassium) loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing all but two or three healthy shoots ensures the main plant gets enough strength to produce a thick stem and a large fruit bunch.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) bibii babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni mli wa kɛ aduawai akui wuji baa.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over when the weather gets windy?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots. When a heavy fruit bunch develops, the plant becomes top-heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi tso lɛ shishi.

english: How do I tell if my farm crops are suffering from lack of water in the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Crops suffering from drought show clear signs like leaves curling inward during the hottest part of the day, wilting, stunted growth, and premature yellowing or drying of lower leaves.
ga: Tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbiɔ mra.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly absorb soil moisture and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from blocking sunlight and starving your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ sũ mli nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi hulu lɛ naa ni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe hɔmɔ.

english: How can I prevent my crop produce from spoiling quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Harvest crops during the cool morning hours, handle them gently to avoid bruising, and store them in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight.
ga: Kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ mli. Okɛtsu nii blɛoo koni akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu yɔɔ. Ekɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ teŋ jɛkɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks essential plant nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Applying the right fertilizer provides the necessary strength for the crop to build green leaves and grow healthy cobs.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa aba.

english: What kind of plant food should I give my seedlings to help them grow strong early on?
ga: Mɛɛ tso niyenii esa akɛ maha midumɔwui lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara waa mra?

english: Young seedlings need starter fertilizer containing phosphorus, such as NPK, which acts like foundational strength food to help them build deep roots and absorb moisture quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná tsofa ni ji phosphorus ni akɛjeɔ shishi, tamɔ NPK, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shishijee hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya.

english: How long does it usually take for cassava to mature and be ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Most cassava varieties in Ghana take between 9 to 12 months (around 40 to 50 weeks) to fully mature. Harvesting too early results in small roots with low starch content.
ga: Cassava ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 (aaafee otsii 40 kɛyashi 50) dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii kɛ starch ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa.

english: How can I tell that my maize crop has reached full maturity and is ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is mature when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and a small black layer forms at the tip of each grain kernel, showing that the plant has finished sending energy into the grain.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients. Without enough energy and water, the plant drops its flowers to save its strength.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛji hewalɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei hu baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use during hot hours to hide from direct sunlight and prevent moisture from evaporating from their leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa

english: Why are the small pods on my cocoa tree turning black and dying before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods wither when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients or water to support all of them, causing the tree to drop extra pods so it can direct its remaining energy to a few healthy ones.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ awo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do plantain trees help my young cocoa trees grow better when planted together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui yeɔ ebuaa mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide protective shade, keeping the soil moist and reducing sun stress on young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni baa kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the nutrients go directly into making your crops grow big.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ekwɛɔ koni niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ koni eha onibii lɛ adara.

english: Is taking a small loan to buy crop fertilizer a smart decision for my farm?
ga: Ani shika fioo ni mikɛbaahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji yiŋkpɛɛ ni ja kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Taking a loan for fertilizer can be very effective because feeding your crops properly significantly increases harvest yield, generating enough extra profit to cover the loan burden and increase your income.
ga: Shika ni akɛfaa koni akɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ aye ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Na sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaatsu onyɔmɔwoo jatsu lɛ he nii ni oha oshika ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do crops get the energy they need to grow big and yield good harvests?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛnáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Crops naturally trap sunlight using the green pigment in their leaves and combine it with air and water to manufacture their own food energy for growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu feɔ ekome koni amɛná amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither even when I give them plenty of water during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: When the sun is extremely hot, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it, causing them to temporarily wilt to protect themselves.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: How does a crop disease move so fast from one plant to cover my whole farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko agbɛ ashwã oya kɛjɛ tso kome mli ni eha miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Crop diseases are caused by tiny microscopic organisms that travel easily through wind, rain splashes, farm tools, or pests from one infected plant to surrounding healthy ones.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii amli kɛ tsei helai baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli mlɛo.

english: Can standing water on my farm cause my crops to catch diseases?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ hela?

english: Excess standing water chokes the roots by cutting off air, which weakens the plant and allows soil-borne fungal diseases to attack and rot the roots.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do some crop varieties resist diseases better than others without chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ helai ahe fe ekrokomɛi ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Some crop varieties have built-in natural traits and stronger immune systems developed over time that stop disease germs from entering or harming them.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi yɛ sui kɛ gbɔmɔtso mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai ni he wa ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ amɛmli loo eyeee amɛ awui.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense behavior crops use to reduce the leaf surface exposed to direct heat, conserving their internal water supply.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Koni akɛbu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he

english: How do plant roots know where to search for water deep underground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei shishifãi leɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ?

english: Plant roots naturally grow in the direction of moisture and chemical signals in the soil, expanding outward and downward to anchor the plant and drink water.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛma tso lɛ nɔ ni enu nu.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen from manure, they direct all their energy into growing top leafy foliage instead of storing food energy in the roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ Amɛkudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Do crops have any natural ways to defend themselves when insects start eating their leaves?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɔi baai lɛ yeli?

english: When attacked, many plants produce bitter chemicals, thick sap, or scents that repel insects or attract beneficial bugs to eat the pests.
ga: kɛji akɛ atutua Tsei babaoo jieɔ tsofai ni mli edɔ, latɛs, loo tsofai ni ŋɔɔ ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii loo egbalaa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ koni amɛye kooloi bibii.

english: Does using dirty river water to mix my crop treatments reduce how well they protect my crops?
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faai amli ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofai lɛ baaha bɔ ni amɛbuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi.

english: Dirty or muddy water contains particles and minerals that bind to crop chemicals, making them far less effective at protecting plants against pests and diseases.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji mli nibii bibii kɛ minerals ni kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kpaa gbee yɛ mli. Enɛ haaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe lɛ mli.

english: Can I save seeds from the maize I harvest this season to plant next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, saving seeds from mature, healthy crops is a standard practice that allows you to extract seeds after harvest and plant them again when the next rainy season arrives.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ ji nifeemɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ, ni ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shɛ.

english: Why do many farmers in my village reuse seeds from their previous harvest instead of buying new ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni amɛkpa tsutsu lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui heei

english: Reusing seeds allows farmers to rely on crops that have already proven they can grow well in the local soil and climate, while also saving money each planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ haa okwaafoi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ shika toɔ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time during the crop's growth to collect seeds for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ tsei koni akɛbua dumɔwui anaa kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: You should wait until the crop fully matures before extracting seeds, as fully developed seeds store better and have a higher chance of germinating next season.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ dani ogbala dumɔwui lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni edara kwraa lɛ toɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Will seeds extracted directly from my harvested crops grow as well as new seeds?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi tsei ni mikpa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ tamɔ dumɔwui heei hu?

english: If you select seeds from healthy, fully matured plants, they will sprout and grow reliably because they come from plants that successfully completed a life cycle in your environment.
ga: Kɛji ohala dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ amli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara bɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjɛɔ tsei ni yeɔ omanye yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do some crop varieties survive harsh heat and dry spells better than others in our region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Some crops are adapted to your specific environment, meaning they have developed resilience over time to withstand local heat, rainfall patterns, and soil conditions.
ga: Atsakeɔ tsei komɛi kɛyaa he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ ená hegbɛ ni amɛtsake amɛhe yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi anaa.

english: How do I choose which crops are most likely to give me a good harvest in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Look for crops that local farmers prefer and have grown successfully over many seasons, as their continued success shows they are naturally resilient and suited to your local environment.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ bei babaoo mli. Taakɛ amɛ omanyeyeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ, tsei nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛhi kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: What does it mean when people say a crop is 'resilient' to our local weather?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mɛi kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ‘nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi’ yɛ wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ naa?

english: A resilient crop is one that can handle unfavorable local conditions—like poor rainfall or high heat—and still mature successfully without dying off easily.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi ji nɔ ni baanyɛ akpee shihilɛi gbohii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa. ni edaa lolo yɛ omanyeyeli mli ni egbooo mlɛo

english: Why do traditional local crops often perform better than new crop varieties introduced from outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsei heei ni akɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛbaa lɛ?

english: Local crops have been grown in your specific environment for many generations, proving over time that they are adapted to the exact soil and weather conditions of your area.
ga: Adu maŋ tsei yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo nɛ. Enɛ maa nɔ mi yɛ be ni sa mli akɛ tsei nɛɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I reduce the chance of my crops dying if the weather becomes bad this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã hegbɛ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagboi lɛ aba shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli bawo wu yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Plant crop varieties that have proven resilient in your local area over past seasons, as adapted crops withstand weather stress much better than unproven varieties.
ga: Dumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni etsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe wa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ bei ni ho lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni atsake amɛ lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe naagbai anaa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei srɔtoi ni atsakeee amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my neighbors keep planting the exact same crop varieties year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ duɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Farmers prefer crops that consistently survive and yield well in their environment, so they stick with proven, adapted varieties rather than taking risks on unknown crops.
ga: Okwaafoi sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ ahi shi be fɛɛ be ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛshihilɛhe lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkpɛtɛɔ henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tso ko ni aleee lɛ awo oshara mli lɛ

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works very well. Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slower and takes up space only after the maize has already been harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa pɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Staking yam vines allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant needs to build large underground tubers. It also keeps leaves off the wet ground, protecting them from rot and disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ afee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ koni ekafite kɛ helai.

english: How often should I water my vegetable seedbed during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Vegetable seedbeds should be watered twice daily—early in the morning before the sun gets too hot, and late in the afternoon. This keeps the soil constantly moist so delicate seedlings do not dry out.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ aduawai dumɔwui ashishi nu shii enyɔ daa gbi. No ji leebi dani hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. kɛ nu ni awoɔ yɛ shwane mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koni dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ akagbi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for healthy leaf growth, or that the soil is holding too much standing water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot feed, but it can also be triggered by a lack of water, insufficient shade, or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ ejɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hu kɛba. Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When heavy fruit bunches grow, strong winds can push them over unless you support the stem with a strong wooden prop pole.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to seeds right when I put them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: No, fertilizer should not touch raw seeds directly because it can burn them. It is best to wait until seedlings sprout and establish roots, or place the fertilizer a few inches away from the seed in the soil.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛshishifãi. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: What causes the bottoms of my green tomatoes to turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually brought on by irregular watering when the soil dries out completely between rain or irrigation.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ teŋ lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are tiny white insects gathering under my pepper leaves and curling them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: These are whiteflies that suck vital sap from the leaves, causing leaf curling and weakening the plant. Clearing weeds around the field and using simple soap-water sprays can help manage them early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Omɔ ŋmɔji kɛ nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ Baanyɛ aye abua ni akwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ mra.

english: Why should I leave big trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down when clearing land for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Leaving large shade trees creates a canopy that protects delicate cocoa trees from intense sunlight and extreme heat. This keeps the farm cooler, prevents heat stress, and helps your cocoa trees live longer and yield steadily for decades.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛitsu ko ni buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsi hulutsoo he haomɔ naa Ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-cocoa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: How do shade trees protect my young cocoa plants during hot weather?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, filtering strong sunlight so the young cocoa gets just enough light to grow safely without drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo bibii lɛ naa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: How do trees on my farm help my soil stay moist during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees block direct sunlight from hitting the ground, which slows down water evaporation from the soil. Their deep roots also pull water up from deep underground, keeping the topsoil cool and damp even during dry spells.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ blɛoo. Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do leaves that fall from shade trees make my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves decompose on the ground and turn into rich organic fertilizer. This natural compost returns key nutrients back into the soil, improves its ability to hold water, and saves you money on commercial chemical fertilizers.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ humus ni jara wa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kuɔ sɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Ha nyɛmɔ ni akɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni akɛ shika ato jarayeli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe

english: Will keeping tall trees on my farm reduce the number of cocoa pods I harvest?
ga: Ani tsei kakadaji ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: As long as you prune the branches so about half the sunlight gets through, shade trees will not reduce your yield. Instead, they protect your cocoa from sun damage and pest attacks, leading to consistent harvests year after year.
ga: Shii abɔ ni obaafo tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ aaafee fã atsɔ mli lɛ, Shade tsei lɛ haŋ onibii lɛ aba shi. Shi ebaabu o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nikpamɔi ni yaa nɔ daa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Will the deep roots of large trees steal water and nutrients from my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ashishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mikookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Most large shade trees have taproots that feed deep underground, while cocoa roots feed closer to the surface. Because they draw nutrients and moisture from different soil depths, they rarely compete with your cocoa.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ shishifã ko ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni ayeɔ kookoo shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkɛ okkoo lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Do big trees on my farm attract harmful insects to my cocoa?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛbaa mikoo lɛ nɔ?

english: Most shade trees actually attract natural predators like birds, ants, and spiders that eat harmful pests like mirids (capsids). Keeping beneficial trees creates a balanced ecosystem that naturally reduces pest outbreaks.
ga: Shade tsei babaoo gbalaa adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ. Tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ haa shihilɛ ni ja ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa.

english: How do tall trees help protect my farm against strong winds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei kakadaji baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he?

english: Tall trees act as windbreaks by breaking the force of heavy storm winds. This prevents strong gusts from snapping your cocoa branches, tearing off leaves, or blowing away delicate flowers and young pods.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei kɛtsɔ ahum ni naa wa ni tswaa lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekafo kookoo niji, ebaagbala baai, loo efo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know which trees are good to leave on my cocoa farm and which ones to remove?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni sa akɛ mashi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Good trees like Emire or Asanfena have light foliage and deep roots. You should cut down trees like the Silk Cotton (Ceiba) tree, as they can harbor diseases like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus or grow canopies that are too dense.
ga: Tsei kpakpai tamɔ emerald loo asanphena lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei tamɔ Silk Cotton (Ceiba) tsei lɛ ahe, ejaakɛ amɛhiɛɔ helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus loo amɛduɔ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: If I leave valuable timber trees growing on my cocoa farm, can I harvest and sell them later?
ga: Kɛji mishi tsei ni jara wa koni mikwɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli Ani manyɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, under Ghana's tree registration policies, farmers who nurture and register economic trees on their farmland acquire legal rights over them. This allows you to earn extra income from timber or control who harvests them.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ Ghana Tsei Ahe Woloŋmaa Mla lɛ shishi. Okwaafoi ni kwɛɔ shika helɛtemɔ tsei anɔ yɛ amɛŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛŋmalaa amɛgbɛi awoɔ wolo nɔ lɛ naa hegbɛi yɛ mla naa yɛ tsei nɛɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa onáa shika kroko kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli loo okudɔɔ mɔ ni kpataa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide shade with their large leaves and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist, giving the young cocoa plants time to establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ kɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn dark green again and support strong plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves with tiny green worms eating the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hu yɛ. Ye nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworms, a destructive caterpillar that feeds on young maize leaves. Inspecting your field early and applying neem oil mixture or recommended crop protection products directly into the central whorl of the plant helps destroy them.
ga: Fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu loo tsei ahebuu nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni efite amɛ.

english: Why should I leave dried crop leaves in my farm instead of burning them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and dries out the land. Leaving dried crop leaves on the soil creates a protective blanket that traps moisture, keeps the soil cool, and naturally decomposes into valuable nutrients for your next crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Tso baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛfeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why will my plants produce smaller yields if I plant seeds very close together to squeeze more onto my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni mikɛmimɔ babaoo miwo mi saatso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed properly and grow large, healthy produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall will wash the loose fertilizer away off your land into streams before the crop roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, or lightly covering it with soil, ensures the roots take up the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ loo okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture at the root zone and keeping soil mulched helps the plant maintain flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ ahã shishifã lɛ mli nu lɛ shwie shi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ashɛre lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔmɔ tomatoi.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites that damage new foliage and spread diseases. Spraying the leaves with a gentle soapy water solution or targeted bio-pesticides controls these tiny bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai heei ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the best stem cuttings when I am preparing to plant cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei niji ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ́ miisaa mihe koni madu ŋmei?

english: The best cassava cuttings come from the firm, middle section of healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 18 months old. Avoid the soft green top parts or dry bottom stems, as middle cuttings sprout faster and yield larger tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ jɛɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi fãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo shishigbɛ tsei ni egbi lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baadara oya ni amɛbaawo tsei wuji.

english: Why do I need to use long wooden sticks to support my climbing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ani oofiɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves fully into the sunlight, which feeds the underground tubermaking process. Staking also keeps the foliage off wet ground, reducing leaf diseases and boosting harvest size.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ji niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber feemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa baa helai shi ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do wild crop seedlings I collect from the forest fail to produce good yields when I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ahe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants taken from their natural forest environment suffer from shock when moved to a farm. Without the natural forest shade, rich moist soil, and shelter they are used to, their growth slows down and their harvest drops significantly unless you learn to recreate those conditions.
ga: Tsei ni ajie kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli koo mli shihilɛ mli lɛ baafee naakpɛɛ kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli koo lɛ mli shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baa nii kɛ amɛshihilɛhe ni amɛle lɛ mli hulutsoo bɛ lɛ Amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo ni ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Ja okase bɔ ni ooofee okɛ nakai shihilɛi lɛ afee ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does a cassava variety that yields heavily in another part of the country perform poorly on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops are sensitive to changes in soil type, rainfall, and heat. Moving a crop to a new environment causes stress, which reduces its food production unless you adjust your management practices to suit the new location.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsakemɔi, nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa he waa, ni nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa he ko hee lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni anáa lɛ aba shi. Ja otsake bɔ ni okwɛɔ nibii anɔ ohaa lɛ koni ekɛ he hee lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large forest trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie koo mli tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops that naturally grow under forest canopy cannot handle full sunlight. Removing shade trees causes the heat to dry them out quickly, preventing them from growing to maturity.
ga: Tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi oya. Etsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the young fruits on my pepper plants falling off before they grow big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences heat stress or lack of nutrients, it drops its young fruits to survive. Feeding the soil properly and keeping it moist helps the plant support its crops until full maturity.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ kpe Ebaashi aduawai bibii yɛ esɛɛ koni ehi shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa ni aha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce plenty of flowers but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi anɔkwa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Plants may produce many flowers, but stress from pests or hot weather can stop those flowers from turning into mature pods. Proper farm management protects the flowers so they can complete their lifecycle.
ga: Tso lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ fɔfɔi ni eda kwraa. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa.

english: Why does my soil produce lower crop yields every year compared to when I first cleared the virgin bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi afi fɛɛ afi lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mijie jwɛi ni ji obalayoo fro lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ he?

english: Soil in the wild naturally refills its nutrients through rotting forest leaves. Once you clear the land and farm continuous seasons without adding fertilizer or manure, the soil gets tired and crops yield far less.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ tsɔɔ baai ni egboi lɛ anɔ ewoɔ niyenii mli nibii amli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni ojieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni otsaa okwaayeli nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do many of the maize seeds I plant fail to grow into mature plants even after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ adara kɛfee tsei ni eda yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Sprouting is only the first step; young seedlings easily die if they face poor soil, dry spells, or pest attacks. Proper seed depth and soil care are needed to help seedlings grow all the way to harvest.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ pɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii. Dumɔwui bibii gboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he miihia koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why do my tomato plants remain small and produce tiny fruits even though I bought improved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Kɛji mihe dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ po.

english: Good seeds carry high potential, but they cannot perform on their own. Without proper farming techniques like regular watering, weeding, and soil feeding, even the best seeds will struggle and produce poor yields.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ nyɛmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ. Shi onyɛŋ okɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji akɛ okwaayeli he ŋaai ni sa tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ Dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ po baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and stop growing for days right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ gbii komɛi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes transplant shock because their delicate roots get disturbed. Watering them immediately and providing light shade helps them recover quickly without losing growth time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ he shoofeemɔ baa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haoɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ oya kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe feɔ oya ni amɛfiteee be ni amɛkɛdaraa.

english: Why are my maize plants weak and producing small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for the same food, water, and sunlight. This stress weakens the plants, preventing them from maturing into strong crops with full cobs.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekatsɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why are insects always eating the leaves of my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warm, rainy weather creates moist conditions that encourage crops to grow soft, tender leaves, which attracts many pests looking for easy food and water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni taoɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni anyɛɔ anáa mlɛo lɛ.

english: Are all the insects I see crawling on my crops bad and trying to destroy them?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni minaa ni amɛmiikplekeshi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ehiii ni amɛmiitao amɛfite amɛ?

english: No, some insects like ladybugs, spiders, and bees actually help your farm by eating harmful pests or helping flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ amɛbuaa oŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni amɛyeɔ loo amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do pests attack some of my crops more than others in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Pests are attracted to specific plant scents, leaf sweetness, or softer stems, meaning they will target their favorite crop varieties first before moving to others.
ga: Tso lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. sweetness of leaves loo soft trunk Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ tsei ni amɛsumɔɔ waa lɛ anɔ dani amɛya tsei krokomɛi anɔ.

english: How do crops naturally defend themselves against pests before I apply any chemical?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani amɛkɛ tsofai komɛi atsu nii amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops can produce tough outer bark, thick leaf skins, or natural bitter juices that discourage insects from feeding on them.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni wa, baa hewolo ni mli wa, loo nu ni mli edɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni haa kooloi nijiaŋ jeɔ wui koni amɛkaye amɛ.

english: If I spray chemicals to kill pests, will it stop my crops from growing well?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ Ani ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When mixed correctly and applied in small amounts, crop chemicals kill the targeted pests without harming the plant, allowing it to grow healthy and strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afutu mli jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsu nii fioo lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni akɛtaoɔ lɛ ni eyeee tso lɛ awui. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do you advise me to keep chemical use minimal instead of spraying my field all the time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai fioo pɛ atsu nii bɔ ni manyɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofai baashwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Using too many chemicals can burn crop leaves, kill beneficial insects that protect your farm, and waste money, so it is best to spray only when necessary.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai ashã. Gbemɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ. kɛ shika ni afiteɔ No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ashwie nɔ kɛji ehe miihia pɛ.

english: How does spraying chemicals with a knapsack machine protect my farm better than pouring it by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ buɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe ni akɛ nine shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying machines turn liquid chemical into a fine mist that covers all leaf surfaces evenly, reaching hidden pests while using much less chemical overall.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai anɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ feɔ afua bibioo ko ni haa baa lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni eshɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ekɛ tsofai fioo ko pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Can the chemical spray I use on my maize affect my neighbor's vegetable farm nearby?
ga: Ani tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baaná mikutsoŋnyo lɛ aduawai ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, wind can carry chemical mist across farm borders onto nearby sensitive crops, which can burn them or leave unsafe chemical residues.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ekɛ kemikal afua afo ŋmɔ husui kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ loo eshi tsofai ni bɛ shweshweeshwe ni eshwɛ.

english: Will my crops produce lower yields if I do not spray pesticides every week?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii fioo kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieee nɔ daa otsi?

english: Not necessarily; keeping your farm free of weeds and allowing helpful predator insects to live in your field often controls pests well without weekly spraying.
ga: nɔ ni he ehiaaa; Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha jwɛi akafee nɔ ko Ni bei pii lɛ, ohaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baahi oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ otsi fɛɛ otsi shwieee nɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if pesticide spray gets directly onto the food parts like cassava roots or tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ fãi komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei loo tomato shishifãi kpe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Chemicals sprayed directly on crop fruits or tubers can leave chemical residues that make the harvest unsafe to eat until a specific waiting period has passed.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashi tsofai ni haa aduawai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ kɛyashi be pɔtɛɛ ko ni akɛbaamɛ lɛ baaho.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees or plantains around my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and can easily dry out and die. Shade trees protect them from sunburn and keep the soil cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ egbi ni egbo oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava stems have tiny buds or 'eyes' where the leaves will sprout. You must plant the stem with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky, otherwise the shoots and roots will struggle to grow properly.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmei’ ni baai jɛɔ mli baa. Esa akɛ odu tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ebaawa akɛ ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Is it really necessary to put stakes or poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani tso loo tso ko he baahia mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni makwɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, staking keeps yam leaves spread out off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which leads to much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking baaha sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the plant food responsible for healthy green growth. Adding urea fertilizer or well-rotted chicken manure can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ urea loo tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas or beans in the same farm where I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo beans yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them alongside or after maize naturally enriches the land with free nutrients for your crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ aba mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are there ragged holes appearing in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yaafo nu ko jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes inside the central leaf funnel of corn are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the tender foliage during the day and chew on the leaves, which can stunt the plant if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Wrinkled or curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips living on the undersides of the leaves. They suck out the plant sap, causing the young leaves to distort and twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Sudden heat stress or drought causes the plant to shed its flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ahaaa tsei lɛ nu yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Should I remove some of the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
