ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ani midumɔwu titri lɛ je kpo?

english: Yes, you should prune away extra shoots (suckers) and keep only one or two strong ones. Leaving too many shoots causes them to compete for soil food and water, resulting in much smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ (ŋmeii) ni okɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do people spread dried grass around the base of their crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwereɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dried grass or leaves (called mulching) acts like a protective cover over the soil. It traps moisture so water doesn't evaporate quickly in the heat, and it keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni nu lɛ akafee oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are my okra pods splitting open before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbalaa dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Okra pods split open when they are left too long on the plant or when there is a sudden intake of water after a dry spell. Harvesting early while the pods are small and tender prevents them from bursting open and becoming tough.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ baafo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nu ba trukaa yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ sɛɛ. early harvest Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, amɛtsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbala ni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my okra?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa okra?

english: Pick your okra when the pods are young, firm, and snap easily at the tip—usually about 2 to 3 inches long. If you wait until they get very big, they turn hard, woody, and split easily.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ okra be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako, amɛhe wa ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ naagbee lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛlɛɛmɔ ji aaafee inchi 2 kɛyashi 3. Kɛji omɛ ni amɛdara diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaafee tsei, ni amɛbaakumɔ oya.

english: Why are tiny insects destroying my okra flowers and leaving holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi roselle fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛmiishi bu yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Insects like beetles and caterpillars love feeding on tender okra leaves and blossoms. Spraying safe crop medicine or natural neem liquid early in the morning can stop these pests before they reduce your yield.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye roselle baai bibii kɛ fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ okɛ tso tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo adebɔɔ mli neem nu shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛha onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What does potassium fertilizer actually do to help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni potassium ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ diɛŋtsɛ koni eye ebua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Potassium acts like a shield and strength builder for crops. It helps plants develop strong stems, resist drought, fight off crop diseases, and produce larger, better-quality fruits.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa. Hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni ewoɔ aduawai ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the edges of my crop leaves turning brown as if they are burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burnt or yellowed leaf edges are often a sign of potassium deficiency in the soil. Adding potassium-rich fertilizer helps restore the plant's health and keeps the leaves green and functional.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ashã loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are missing essential soil food like nitrogen or potassium. Water alone is not enough; adding manure or the right fertilizer gives plants the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can severe afternoon sunlight hurt my young crops during the hot season?
ga: Ani shwane hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aye mi tsei bibii lɛ awui yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, extreme heat and sun can dry out soil fast, burn tender young leaves, and cause plants to wilt. Using light shading or spreading dry grass around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and moist.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya, eshã baai bibii, ni eha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ shading loo jwɛi ni egbi tsu nii ni akɛha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How does intense heat affect how plants absorb nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ saa bɔ ni tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When the sun is too hot, plants lose water quickly through their leaves and can struggle to take up fertilizer from dry soil. Keeping the soil moist helps crops absorb plant food smoothly even in hot weather.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai akpee yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he akaŋshii mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ, yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ po mli.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to spray medicine on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Apply crop medicine at the first sign of damage, such as leaf holes or spots, ideally early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cool so the sun does not dry up the medicine too quickly.
ga: Okɛ tsofa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ awo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ efite, tamɔ baai amli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii, ni ebaahi jogbaŋŋ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la akagbi tsofa lɛ oya tsɔ.

english: Is it safe to spray pest medicine on my crops right before selling them at the market?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ dani mikɛ amɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: No, every crop medicine has a safe waiting period listed on the container. You must wait a specific number of days after spraying before harvesting so the chemical breaks down completely and the food is safe to eat.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fee lɛ yɛ be ni sa ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ ni aŋmala awo tsofai lɛ amli. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii babaoo yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okpa. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afite kwraa ni abaanyɛ aye niyenii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How much space do I need to leave between coconut seedlings when planting them on my farm?
ga: Kɛ́ miidu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, gbɛ enyiɛ he hiaa mi yɛ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ?

english: Coconut trees grow very wide fronds and large root systems, so they need about 7 to 8 meters of space between each tree. Giving them enough distance prevents them from crowding each other out and competing for water and nutrients as they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ waa kɛ shishifãi wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei tsei biɔ ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 8. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Can I plant quick crops like cassava or maize on the same land while my coconut trees are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be mli ni ŋmei tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, while coconut seedlings are young and small, there is plenty of open space and sunlight. Planting food crops like maize or legumes between the young trees allows you to harvest food and make income while waiting for the coconuts to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo ni eyɛ bibioo moŋ, Shi he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. Niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni onáa shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ.

english: What should I do when my tree crops grow so big that I can no longer plant food crops underneath them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mitsei lɛ dara aahu akɛ minyɛɛɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ amɛshishi dɔŋŋ?

english: When long-term trees grow full branches and shade the ground completely, you should focus your energy on managing and harvesting the tree crop itself, or prepare a separate piece of land if you want to continue growing seasonal food crops.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ amɛniji fɛɛ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ, Esa akɛ Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛkpamɔ nɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo saa he ko ni yɔɔ srɔto kɛji oosumɔ ni oya nɔ odu be mli niyenii.

english: Why do people say that large trees like coconuts eventually take over the land from other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛɔ akɛ naagbee lɛ tsei wuji tamɔ ŋmeii miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛmiijɛ tsei krokomɛi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: As coconut trees grow tall and mature, their wide leaves block sunlight from reaching the ground, and their roots spread deep and wide to absorb most of the soil nutrients and moisture, making it difficult for smaller crops to survive underneath.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ da ni egbɔ lɛ Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Ni eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable yields dropping when I plant them under the shade of big farm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food and produce good yields. When planted under heavy tree shade, they do not get enough light energy, which causes weak growth and small harvests.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi lɛ, enaŋ la hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni waaa kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: How many years will a coconut tree keep producing fruit once it starts growing on my land?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ŋmei tso ko baawo yibii kɛji ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: Coconut trees are long-term investments; depending on the variety, a healthy coconut tree can continue producing fruits for 60 to 80 years if it is well cared for.
ga: Kokoo tsei ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kɛyashi afii 60 kɛyashi 80, ni enɛ damɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: How long does it take for a newly planted coconut seedling to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: It depends on the variety: dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 8 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Edamɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What care do young coconut seedlings need in their first year to survive the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ he hiaa ŋmei tso bibioo ko yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Young seedlings need regular watering during dry spells, mulching with dry grasses around the base to keep soil cool and moist, and protection from bushfires and grazing animals.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. shishitoo koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ koo mli la kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ jwɛi shikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around young tree seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young tree seedlings and will quickly steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that the seedling needs to build strong roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe dumɔwui bibii. Ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa oya lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli.

english: How do I know if my farmland has the right soil for growing healthy coconut trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Coconut trees prefer loose, well-drained sandy or loamy soil that holds moisture but does not collect standing water, which is why they grow very well in coastal areas and near riverbanks.
ga: Kokoo tsei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni etse, ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni etse. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ shi ehiɛɛɛ nu Nɔ hewɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa hei kɛ faai ahe lɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground is thoroughly soaked by two or three good rainfalls before planting, rather than planting right after the very first light shower which can dry out quickly and kill the seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ kpakpa fioo ko aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbi oya nɛ e ma nyɛ maa gbe dumɔwu ɔmɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die even when rains fall until December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kɛyashi December mli lɛ?

english: Even if rains fall throughout the year, plants can dry up if the soil cannot hold water well, or if the rains are spaced too far apart, causing the roots to starve of moisture during hot spells.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ Tsei hu baanyɛ agbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛ tsɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even after spending a whole year in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa yɛ be mli ni miyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small when planted in hard, compacted soil where roots cannot expand, or when the plant lacks enough nutrients and sunshine to build strong tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather conditions get too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: What causes the leaves of my young maize plants to turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or that excess water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded farms; clearing weeds and pruning branches lets light in to stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ koni la abote mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akpa.

english: What is eating small round holes into the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth larva that hide under the leaves and feed on them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛyeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa cabbage baai lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper crops too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, they compete for light, air, and soil food, making them grow weak and tall while yielding very few peppers.
ga: Kɛji pepper tsei lɛ bafee ekome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ.

english: Will applying a lot of chemical fertilizer make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: Using too much fertilizer actually burns plant roots and turns leaf edges brown, which can stunt crop growth or kill the plant completely.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa loo eha tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to the soil, so their roots quickly grab water and food before domestic crop seeds have time to fully establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni ejɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya dani shia dumɔwui lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaa shi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your young cocoa tree is getting too much direct sunlight or lacks soil moisture. Providing temporary shade using nurse crops like plantain protects the tender leaves while the root system develops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ tsei ni ji nurse tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii kɛhaa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting before my cocoa trees start bearing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii agbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani enyɛ ewo ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take about 3 to 5 years to start fruiting, but improved hybrid cocoa varieties can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years with good farm management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje pods feemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shady, and humid conditions. Pruning heavy tree branches to let sunlight reach the farm floor and removing infected pods helps control it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni hulu la ashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny insects to make small brown patches on the young stems of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii? Yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ tso bibioo lɛ nɔ

english: These insects are called capsids or mirids. They suck the sap from tender cocoa shoots and pods, causing shoots to die back; they can be controlled by timely spraying with approved insecticides.
ga: Atsɛɔ kooloi nɛɛ akɛ capsids loo myrids. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ gboiɔ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava on the same farm with my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kookoo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping cocoa with food crops like plantain or cassava is recommended during the first 2 to 3 years because it provides necessary shade for young cocoa trees while giving you food and income.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava adu cocoa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli ejaakɛ enɛ baaha cocoa tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. kɛ niyenii kɛ shika ni akɛhaa bo lɛ fata he

english: Why should I leave some big shade trees standing when clearing land for a cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ sɛɛ beni miisaa ŋmɔ ko kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Permanent shade trees protect full-grown cocoa from harsh sunlight and drying winds, maintain soil moisture, and create a cooler climate that prolongs the lifespan of your cocoa farm.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ buɔ kookoo ni eda lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni haa o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ wala sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce many tiny flowers, but very few turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo nɛkɛ, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmɔji diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges for pollination. If drought occurs, or if natural pollinators are missing, many flowers fall off without growing into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba loo adebɔɔ mli pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvest when its color changes fully from green to bright yellow, or from red to deep orange, depending on the variety. Unripe or overripe pods lower bean quality.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ Edamɔ tso lɛ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ Pods ni edako loo ni ekwɛko fe nine lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mlihilɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees giving me fewer pods every year even though the trees look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni kookoo tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their natural productivity drops and soil nutrients become exhausted, requiring pruning, fertilizer application, or gradual replanting.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ewoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hu baa shi. Ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo adu ekoŋŋ fiofio.

english: How do I protect my cocoa soil from drying out completely during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kokoo shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Mulching—covering the soil around the base of cocoa trees with dried leaves, grass, or cocoa husks—helps trap moisture in the ground and keeps the roots cool during dry spells.
ga: Mulching—ni ji shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai, jwɛi, loo kookoo ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my young oil palm trees are ready to start bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-palm tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaawo yibii?

english: Oil palm trees usually start producing fruit bunches between 2 to 3 years after being planted in the main field. You will see small fruit bunches forming at the base of the lower fronds, which turn bright orange-red when they are fully ripe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei lɛ jeɔ yibii akui ahe shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 teŋ beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana aduawai lɛ yɛ kui bibii amli yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ashishi, ni kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse.

english: Why do my palm trees produce plenty of fruit during some months but very little during others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ nyɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Palm fruit production depends heavily on rainfall patterns. Heavy rains help the tree develop flowers and fruit, so about 5 to 6 months after a good rainy season, you will harvest the most fruit, while dry spells lead to lower yields later.
ga: Palm aduawai afeemɔ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ be ni hi jogbaŋŋ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ lɛ, obaakpa yibii babaoo. yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaha nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How many years can an oil palm tree keep producing good fruit before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mu tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: An oil palm tree can produce good harvests for 25 to 30 years. After this age, the tree becomes too tall to harvest safely and its fruit production naturally slows down, which means it is time to clear and replant.
ga: Mu tsei baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai afii 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ afii nɛɛ sɛɛ. Tsei lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa nii shweshweeshwe. Ni tso lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ajie ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my oil palm trees while the palms are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mu tsei ateŋ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years before the palm leaves grow large enough to shade the ground, you can safely intercrop food crops like cassava, maize, or vegetables. This provides food and early farm income while keeping weeds down around young palms.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli dani tso lɛ baai lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai shweshweeshwe. Enɛ ji koni akɛ niyenii kɛ shika aha ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ mli kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do weeds stop growing under my mature oil palm trees after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kpaɔ mi-oil palm tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: As oil palms mature, their large leaf fronds spread out to form a thick canopy that blocks sunlight from reaching the ground. Since weeds need direct sunlight to grow, the shade naturally stops weed growth.
ga: Kɛ́ mu tso lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, baai wuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Shade lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ daalɛ kpaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my oil palm trees turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: While older leaves naturally dry up and turn brown as the tree grows, widespread yellowing on younger leaves usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium, or the tree is suffering from drought.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, baai bibii ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ miikpe.

english: Why is it necessary to prune and cut off the old leaves from my palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tsei ahe baai momoi ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning old and dead fronds makes it easier to see and harvest mature fruit bunches. It also prevents pests and plant diseases from breeding in dead leaves and allows the tree to direct its energy into growing big fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni egbɔ ni egboi lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana aduawai akui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpa amɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai hu anaa koni amɛkakwɛ baai ni egboi lɛ anɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: What causes big holes in the leaves of my young palm trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-palm tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Holes in palm leaves are typically caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars. Because leaves make food for the plant using sunlight, damaged leaves slow down the tree's growth and reduce future yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni yeɔ baa tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baa lɛ mli baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai kɛ hulu la haa tsei niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ baai ni efite lɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nɔ ni ebaaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I buy nursery seedlings instead of planting seeds I collect from wild palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ koo mli ŋmei tsei amli lɛ?

english: Wild palm seeds usually grow into trees with thick shells and very little oil. Certified nursery seedlings are high-yielding hybrid varieties bred to produce much more oil, produce fruit faster, and stay at a manageable height longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni amɛhe tsɔi lɛ mli tse ni fɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Nursery dumɔwui ni awo he hegbɛ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni akwɛɔ koni amɛná mu babaoo. Ha hetooi oya ni ohi he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii be kakadaŋŋ

english: If I tap my oil palm tree for palm wine, will the tree still produce oil palm fruit later?
ga: Kɛ mita mu tso ko he koni manu ŋmei wain Ani tso lɛ baawo mu tso yibii lolo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: No, tapping an oil palm tree for palm wine involves cutting into the central growing point at the crown of the tree. This process kills the tree completely, meaning it can no longer produce leaves or fruit.
ga: Dabi, ni oootswa mu tso ko koni onu ŋmei wain lɛ biɔ ni afo lɛ kɛyashɛ he ni edaa yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baagbe tso lɛ kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo baai loo yibii dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my pawpaw trees flowering heavily but not growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi waa shi ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male trees produce flowers with pollen but will never grow fruit themselves, while female trees need pollen from male or hermaphrodite trees nearby before their flowers can turn into pawpaw fruits.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen yɔɔ mli. Shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewoŋ yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni ji yei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ pollen kɛjɛ tsei ni ji hii loo hermaphroditic ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli dani fɔfɔi lɛ afee pawpaw yibii.

english: Why do small pawpaw fruits drop off my tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ paw paw lɛ ji bibioo nɛkɛ? Koni migbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ agbo?

english: Pawpaw trees drop small fruits when they do not get enough water or nutrients, or when the weather gets too hot. Water the tree regularly during dry spells and feed the soil to help the tree support full fruit growth.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii. Be mli ni onine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Ha tso lɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni edara kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does growing moringa on my farm benefit my other crops and soil?
ga: Moringa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ. Te minɔ lɛ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Moringa has long roots that pull nutrients from deep underground up to its leaves. When moringa leaves drop and decay, or when you use them as compost, they enrich the topsoil with rich nutrients for nearby crops.
ga: Moringa yɛ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Beni Moringa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboi Aloo beni okɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Moringa baai lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which it needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water prevents air from reaching the roots underground. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away quickly, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ aya shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates living umbrellas that protect the leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo baa koni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one strong mother stem and one small follower sucker ensures the plant has enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yitso kome ni mli wa kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ bibioo kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant diseases. Keeping the farm clear of weeds and using physical pest traps helps protect tomatoes from insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɔnei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otomatoi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: High heat and dry soil cause pepper plants to drop flowers to save their energy. Covering the soil around the roots with dried leaves or grass helps keep the roots cool and holds moisture so flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas before maize help my maize grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes with roots that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil. When the cowpea harvest is done, that stored nitrogen acts as free food for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni shishifãi yɔɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbe tsina ŋmãa lɛ naa Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ baafee niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is a key nutrient that helps plants make food, and when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves nitrogen from its older lower leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen from the soil or fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing thick green leaves instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, tsina tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod Disease. It thrives in wet weather and heavy shade, spreading quickly from tree to tree through rain splashes and insects when farms are not properly cleared.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kooloi bibii anɔ kɛ́ ajieee ŋmɔji amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning pale green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji eŋɔli kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curling and yellowing cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus. This sickness is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kplukai bibii ni foɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni gbɛɔ hela nɛɛ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly, ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves look like something is eating tiny holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko eye bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny holes on pepper leaves are typically caused by small insects like flea beetles or caterpillars feeding on the soft tissue of young leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering, which causes stress and prevents pollination from succeeding.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Enɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni ehaa pollination baa.

english: Why do my yams stay long and thin instead of growing big and fat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ fɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers remain thin when the soil is too hard or compacted for them to expand easily, or when the soil lacks enough potassium and organic matter to feed the growing tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakã he ahi shi mlɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ebɔle ehe kɛyashɛ he ko ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua bulbs ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my young papaya fruits fall off the stem long before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young papaya fruits drop when the tree suffers from root stress caused by poor water drainage, prolonged drought, or sudden changes in soil moisture.
ga: Papaya yibii bibii lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shishifãi ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he amanehulu. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakemɔi trukaa

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily as soon as the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛtsiimɔ pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be damaged by microscopic worms called nematodes or softened by excess water, making the tree top-heavy and easily blown over when carrying a full bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ mlɛo ni efoɔ kɛyaa he fɛɛ he oya kɛ́ ehiɛ tso ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the outer tips of my groundnut leaves look brown and scorched during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ asɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Scorched leaf edges on groundnuts happen when the roots cannot draw enough water from dry soil fast enough to replace moisture lost to the sun, or when the soil lacks calcium needed for strong leaf tissue.
ga: Baai ni shã yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛto nu ni hulu la lɛ laajeɔ lɛ najiaŋ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight dries out their delicate leaves and soil too quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides canopy shade, protecting the young plants until they grow strong enough to withstand full sunlight.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is a key nutrient that helps plants stay green and grow leaves, and when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the newest growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mli. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside or in rotation with maize acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding the soil and helping your maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ loo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is making holes in my young maize leaves and leaving tiny dark dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu ni amɛshi muji bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ? yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that feeds inside the leaves of young maize plants. Farmers can manage them by inspecting crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa titri ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ. Okwaafoi baanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛɔ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack slightly from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa fioo kɛmiijɛ bulb ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flower drop in pepper plants often happens because of extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and ensuring the plants receive adequate organic nutrients can help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato roots rot and the leaves turn yellow when water sits on my farm after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off oxygen, causing root rot and preventing nutrients from being absorbed. Creating raised soil beds or drainage channels allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the root zone healthy.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ abote mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ saatsoi ni awó nɔ loo nu homɔ gbɛi ni afee lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli waa

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with low yields when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough light and root space to grow strong stems and produce bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ha gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa la kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo yibii loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: Yam vines need wooden stakes so their leaves can climb high to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food for the plant, which builds larger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my maize farm so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. For maize, applying a small amount about two weeks after germination, followed by a second application when the plant is knee-high, ensures the plant absorbs the nutrients effectively.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. kɛha ŋmãa Okɛ fioo ko awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji shi ni ji enyɔ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ. Ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best month for me to start planting cocoa on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mabɔi kookoo dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant cocoa is during the main rainy season, usually from March to April. The regular rain provides young cocoa seedlings with the heavy moisture they need to build strong roots before drier months arrive.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛjɛɔ March kɛyashi April. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa nu babaoo ni he hiaa koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to wait for the rains to start before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi dani manyɛ madu nii?

english: Seeds and young plant seedlings need constant soil moisture to sprout and survive. Planting in dry soil without rain will cause the sun to dry out and kill the young roots before they can establish.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tsei bibii hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulu lɛ agbi ni efite shishifãi bibii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know my field is properly prepared for me to plant cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui akwɛmɔ?

english: Your soil is ready when the early rains in March or April have thoroughly soaked into the ground, making the soil soft, dark, and wet enough to keep young root balls hydrated.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra yɛ March loo April mli lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni eha efee bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it good to apply fertilizer to my farm when there is no rain falling?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata ŋmɔ lɛ he beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: No, applying fertilizer when there is no rain is ineffective and can damage your crops. Plants need soil moisture to dissolve the fertilizer so their roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ tsuuu nii, ni ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does rainwater actually help the fertilizer I spread on my farm work?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ nu yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwãa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves solid fertilizer granules into a liquid form underground. Once dissolved, the plant roots can easily drink up the nutrients alongside the water.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛfata nu he mlɛo.

english: Why are my crops not growing even though I bought and applied fertilizer during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miheɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer cannot feed a plant on its own without water. In dry soil, the fertilizer sits unused, and without moisture, the crop's roots cannot suck up the food.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei niyenii yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛji nu bɛ mli. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii. Ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: What will happen to my cocoa plants if I give them fertilizer while the ground is very dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ?

english: Without rain to dilute the fertilizer, the strong concentrated chemicals can burn the roots of your cocoa trees, causing the leaves to dry up, turn brown, and drop off.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, abaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsofa lɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo shishifãi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni egbi Etsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbeeɔ shi.

english: Should I put fertilizer on my crops before it rains or after the rain starts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni eje shishi sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after the rain season has started, as this helps it dissolve properly without being washed away by sudden heavy downpours.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ shwieee lɛ.

english: Can extra fertilizer help my cocoa trees survive if the rain stops completely?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko baaye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa kwraa?

english: No, fertilizer cannot replace water. Think of fertilizer as food and water as drink; without water, a plant cannot digest food and will wilt regardless of how much fertilizer is in the ground.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ aye nu najiaŋ. Susumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe akɛ niyenii kɛ nu akɛ nii ni anuɔ. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ agbɔ niyenii ni amɛgboi bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baawo sũ lɛ mli.

english: How do the early March and April rains change the growth of cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ March kɛ April shishijee gbɛ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ?

english: The March and April rains wake up the cocoa trees after the dry season, encouraging them to flush with soft green leaves and begin forming new flowers and young cocoa pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ March kɛ April mli lɛ teɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Ekanyaa kookoo tso lɛ koni ená baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ejeɔ fɔfɔi heei kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ahe fɔmɔ shishi

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the hot sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself during its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo lɛ jeɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen. This happens when the soil is depleted or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa niyenii mli nibii kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to lift and stake my yam vines with wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛ tsei adu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up into full sunlight so the plant can make more food for the growing tuber. It also keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and soil-borne diseases.
ga: Staking baaha wain tso lɛ baai lɛ aje kpo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ helai anaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and rotting within just two or three days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ duŋ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a natural protective skin once detached from the living plant. Exposure to air causes rapid chemical breakdown, meaning cassava must be eaten, sold, or processed into gari or flour immediately after harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmei lɛ, esa akɛ aye, ahɔ̃ɔ, loo afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What is causing the central leaves of my young corn plants to become full of holes and look like they were chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ bu ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the soft green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before the fruit even ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium, which is often caused by irregular watering or dry spells during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to multiply and survive in the ground for the next season.
ga: Nibii komekomei ni aduɔ daa lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa kooloi kɛ helai komɛi feɔ babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) shields the ground from hot sunshine, keeping the soil cool and moist for longer periods while also preventing weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he lɛ naa. oŋmɔshi nibii hu

english: Why should I wait for several steady rains before planting my maize instead of planting right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani maduɔ ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If your seeds sprout after one rain and no more rain falls, the delicate young seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ. Tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop harvest even if I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli po?

english: Weeds grow faster and more aggressively than crops. When you add fertilizer, the weeds will steal the water, light, and nutrients first, leaving your main crop weak and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa onibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and look tired during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ ni ebɔle ehe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to harvest my fresh leafy vegetables so they stay fresh?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makpa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai heei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Harvesting in the early morning before the sun gets strong keeps the crops cool and full of moisture, which prevents them from wilting quickly after picking.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ leebi dani hulu lɛ tso waa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli afee fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akagbo oya beni ajie amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their lower leaves during dry periods to conserve water, saving their energy to keep the underground tubers healthy until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. ni akɛ hewalɛ ato koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow much faster than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that respond instantly to early rainfall, quickly taking up surface water and soil nutrients before crop seeds can fully establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ oya. Amɛheɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my field has enough soil moisture for my crops without any tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mibɛ dɛŋdadei komɛi?

english: You can dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil; if it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping water or crumbling, your soil has good moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nine. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni ekɛ ehe shwieee shi loo efoŋ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kpakpa.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots rot when water stays on the farm for too long after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe, and standing water blocks oxygen from reaching the soil, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my maize farm make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural food source that nourishes nearby maize plants.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow if I bury them too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry limited stored energy and need air to sprout; planting them too deep causes them to exhaust their energy before reaching the surface light.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite dani eshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: How do I know that my cocoa pods are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their pod skin turns from green or dark red to a clear bright yellow or orange, showing the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I leave my harvested grain sitting in the open sun during peak midday heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme midday heat dries the outer layer of the grain too quickly, causing the seeds to crack and shatter, which ruins their store quality.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛgbɛ fã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ baafite dumɔwui ni abua naa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to shed their blossoms to save energy and water. Providing temporary shade or mulching the soil helps keep the plant cool enough to hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very big, bushy leaves but end up with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ baai wuji kɛ jwɛi shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil pushes the cassava plant to put all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Balance the soil with nutrients like potassium to encourage the plant to grow thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ potassium afee ekome koni ewo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a sign of a viral infection carried by tiny insects like whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and removing severely infected plants stops the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender, but produce very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants stretch thin to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Planting with proper spacing gives every plant enough space and food to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe bibii koni amɛkɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Tso ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them randomly across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ? Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, agbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa.

english: Planting in straight rows makes it easy to walk through your farm to remove weeds, apply fertilizer, and harvest without stepping on your crops, while ensuring each plant gets equal sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ oodu nii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooonyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa nibii ni okɛ onaji efɔɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and dry out quickly under harsh sun and dusty dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa protects them until they are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Young cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it harmful for me to water my vegetables in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli nu ni mikɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Watering in midday heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it, and hot water sitting on leaves can scorch them or encourage disease. Watering early in the morning allows the soil to soak up water properly.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni ta baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ loo ewo helai ahe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn purple or dark yellow when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ purple loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Yellow or purple leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus. Applying the right crop fertilizer early helps the leaves turn deep green so the plant can grow quickly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo purple ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada oya.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts go moldy and rot so quickly after I pull them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested groundnuts hold a lot of hidden moisture inside their pods. If you store them immediately without drying them thoroughly in the sun, mold will grow and spoil the entire harvest.
ga: Peanuts ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni akɛtee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛto amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ, Fɛ̃i lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open or grow into strange, twisted shapes under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miitswa loo amɛmiidara ni amɛmiitsɔ naakpɛɛ nibii ni efite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams bend and split when the soil is hard, stony, or poorly prepared, making it difficult for the tuber to expand smoothly. Digging deep, soft mounds or ridges gives the yam clear space to grow straight and smooth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo asaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ atsa gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ehaa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɔni afee ni eda tɛ̃ɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees do not have strong roots yet and cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a umbrella that lowers heat, holds air moisture, and protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni wa lolo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shade ni haa dɔlɛ baa shi lɛ baa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Why does covering the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass keep them alive during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from hitting the earth. This traps moisture in the soil longer, keeps root systems cool, and stops weeds from taking water away from your tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tomato mli.

english: Yellowing leaves that form a V-shape down the middle leaf vein mean your maize is starving for nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build green leaves and grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia abele koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall stems with lots of leaves but leaves me with small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen compared to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of sending food down into the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ niyenii baa shi kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help the maize crop I plant next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants with powdery waste in the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai anɔ ni starch ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant to feed on tender new leaves before the plant matures.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei dani tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight like cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, or by a virus spread by those insects. They drain the plant's nutrients and cause new leaf tissue to twist and deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ nɔ Amɛjieɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ mli fãi heei lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I give the vines tall sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ fe wein tso lɛ haa lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the tuber through sunlight reaching their leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, opening every leaf to sunlight while keeping the plant clean from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa amɛ bulbs lɛ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ baa fɛɛ baa ni agbeleɔ ahaa hulu la lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tsei lɛ ahe atse kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the plant without forming any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile, preventing flowers from fertilizing. Without fertilization, the plant drops the blossoms to save its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Tsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔ Kɛji fɔmɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is soaked deep after multiple rains before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi babaoo sɛɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: The very first rain usually only wet the surface. Planting immediately risks seeds sprouting and then dying if a hot dry spell follows before the second rain arrives.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ kɛ oshara baa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagboi kɛji hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ ba dani nugbɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ ba.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but many fall due to strong winds, dry spells, or sap-sucking insects like thrips. Ensuring the trees receive adequate water during flowering and spraying appropriate biopesticides helps retain flowers for fruit production.
