ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips lɛ ahewɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ni okɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni ekɛwo aduawai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can burn under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have large leaves that shade young cocoa plants, protecting them from heat while keeping moisture in the soil during their early growth stage.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is too waterlogged for roots to breathe. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps leaves turn healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and dark powder inside the center stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the leaf whorl and leaves behind dark waste. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract directly into the center leaf whorl early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava usually matures between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety, when lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. Harvesting too early yields thin tubers, while leaving them too long after maturity makes the tubers tough and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Be ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo aba. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni egbɔ lɛ, ebaaha yitso lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni efee tamɔ tso.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and bushy but fail to produce flowers and tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji shi amɛwooo fɔfɔi kɛ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus energy on growing leaves and stems rather than fruit. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit formation.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ fe aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like mites, aphids, or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus transmitted by these pests. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap helps suppress these insects and protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni haa baai shwieɔ shi ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Is it better for my crop soil to use animal manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani kooloi aŋmei loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha mi sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ?

english: Both serve good purposes: animal manure improves long-term soil structure and moisture retention, while chemical fertilizer supplies quick nutrients directly to plants. Combining well-rotted manure with balanced chemical fertilizer gives crops the best results.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ yiŋtoo kpakpa he nii: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ futu tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crops too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close forces them to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stalks and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough air circulation and room to grow strong and resist diseases.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ helai akpee.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon even after I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In hot afternoon heat, plants lose water through leaves faster than roots can absorb it from soil, causing temporary wilting. Watering deeply early in the morning and adding mulch like straw around plant bases helps retain moisture in the soil throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko Nu jogbaŋŋ leebi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ jwɛi, afata tsei lɛ ashishi he koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crop field if I apply more pesticide or fertilizer than recommended?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii?

english: Overusing farm chemicals can burn crop leaves, kill beneficial organisms in the soil, and leave toxic residues that stop seeds from growing properly in the next farming season.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai ashã. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eshiɔ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and scorched after I sprayed chemicals to kill pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitswa beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ amɛ lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using chemicals that are too strong or applying them in excessive amounts stresses the crop, damaging the leaves and preventing the plant from making food naturally.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa tsɔ loo ni fa fe nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Efiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ afee niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can using too much chemical fertilizer cause my cassava or yam tubers to grow poorly?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, excessive fertilizer causes the plant to grow too many leafy leaves above ground while leaving the food roots underneath small, soft, or weak.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ bibii, ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: How can using a mechanical seed planter help my crop yield compared to planting manually with a hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ? Kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ ŋmei lɛ he

english: Planting machines place seeds at the precise depth and distance apart, ensuring every seedling gets equal sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to grow strong and uniform.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ kɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu aná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ekome

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving all of them malnourished and weak.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my seeds take so long to germinate when the soil is packed tight and hard after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil traps delicate young sprouts underground and prevents air and water from reaching the seed, making it difficult for the plant to push through.
ga: Sũ ni wa, ni mli wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu naa koni ekashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss and protect itself from drying out under intense sunshine.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from lack of water or from an attack by crop diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ nu ni faaa loo tsei ahela hewɔ?

english: Water-stressed plants usually wilt during hot daylight and bounce back at night, whereas diseased plants show dark spots, powdery spots, or rotting stems even after it rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu haa amɛhe feɔ shoo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛshishijee shihilɛ mli gbɛkɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji, ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ po sɛɛ.

english: What is the best step for me to take when I notice unfamiliar pests damaging my crop stems?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ kɛ́ mina akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni mileee lɛ miibote miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Instead of buying unknown chemicals immediately, take a sample of the damaged plant to an extension officer so they can identify the exact pest and give you the correct, safe treatment plan.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe tsofai ni aleee lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Kɛ tsei ni efite lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii aba extension officer lɛ ŋɔɔ. Bɔni afee ni amɛyoo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ekɛ tsamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe aha bo.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on my farm plot every season lower my total harvest year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil, causing poor growth in future seasons.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shweremɔ kpakpa aba yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut for planting on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select thick, mature stems from healthy cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Make sure the stems show no signs of pest damage or diseases and have clearly visible nodes or buds.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni eda kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli. Kwɛmɔ akɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ etsɔɔɔ nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai efite. ni eyɛ nodes loo buds ni anaa jogbaŋŋ

english: How far apart should I space my cassava plants if I want to expand my crop field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli kɛji miisumɔ ni magbɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli?

english: Plant cassava stems about 1 meter apart from each other in rows spaced 1 meter apart. Giving the plants enough space ensures their underground tubers have room to grow large.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ aaafee mita kome, yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji mita kome. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: What is the correct way to cut stem cuttings before putting them into the soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ afo tsei aniji jogbaŋŋ dani adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ?

english: Cut the mature stems into smooth pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long using a sharp cutlass. Each cutting should have around 4 to 7 healthy nodes or eyes.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni mli wa atsu nii ni okɛfolɔ tsei ni eda lɛ amli bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afo lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ahi aaafee 4 kɛyashi 7 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ji nodes loo buds.

english: When is the best time of year in Ghana to start planting cassava?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni esa akɛ aje ŋmei dumɔ shishi?

english: It is best to plant at the start of the main rainy season. Early rain gives the young stem cuttings enough water to develop strong roots before any dry weather sets in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa tsei niji bibii lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Why is my cassava farm producing very small tubers and low yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa ni yibiiwoo faaa lɛ?

english: Low yield usually happens if the soil lacks nutrients, if weeds compete with young plants during their first three months, or if poor-quality stem cuttings were planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii miitswa akaŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli loo kɛji tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Is cassava a good main crop to plant if I want to make sure my family always has food?
ga: Ani ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni miweku lɛ aná niyenii be fɛɛ be?

english: Yes, cassava is reliable for food security because it survives tough weather and poor soil, and mature roots can safely stay in the ground until you are ready to harvest and eat them.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ ŋmei nɔ kɛha niyenii he shweshweeshwefeemɔ. Ejaakɛ ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Ni shishifãi ni edara lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni oye.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is mature enough to harvest for food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛha niyenii?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can test maturity by carefully digging around one plant to check if the roots are thick enough for consumption.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka ehewalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ he ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. Tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ aye.

english: What is the proper way to dig up cassava tubers so they do not get damaged?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsa ŋmei shishifãi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee?

english: Cut the main stem down to a short stub first, then gently loosen the soil around the base of the plant with a hoe or cutlass before pulling the roots out carefully to avoid bruising.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ niji kukuji klɛŋklɛŋ, no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ blɛoo dani ojie shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni akafite.

english: How quickly must I use or process cassava tubers after digging them up from the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ otsi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, te ehe hiaa ni okɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ atsu nii loo otsu he nii oya ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fresh cassava spoils quickly within 2 to 3 days after harvest. You should peel and boil them for food immediately or process them into products like gari or cassava flour to store them longer.
ga: Cassava hee fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ otsi amɛhe ni okɛshã amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo okɛfee nibii tamɔ gari loo ŋmei ashikiŋsha koni okɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Shedding leaves in dry weather is a natural way for cassava plants to conserve water. As long as the stems stay alive, the plant will sprout new leaves once rain returns.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni ŋmei tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he. Be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ yɔɔ wala mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow early instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or aren't getting enough moisture from the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer early gives them the food they need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ he miihia amɛ nitrogen loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra. Enɛ baaha amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and spoil so fast before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Once cut from the stalk, plantains naturally release a ripening gas that speeds up softening, especially in warm weather. Keeping them covered in a cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight slows down this process so they stay fresh longer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Plantains lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbɔjɔɔ oya lɛ kpo. titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Amɛ ni oooha amɛhi he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛhiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods dry up and turn black while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ be mli ni miyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives when the air around the tree is very damp and shaded. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunshine and air to flow through, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tsei lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo babaoo. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after waiting a whole year to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa yɛ be mli ni mimɛ koni akpa amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, soft soil to expand its tubers. If the soil is hard or tightly packed, the roots cannot push through to grow fat, so loosening the soil around the planting mounds makes a big difference.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia cassava koni ekɛdu ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ fɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Planting gɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa.

english: When the weather gets too hot or the plants don't get steady water, they get stressed and shed their flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of using energy to grow big fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers crack open in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba yɛ shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when a sudden heavy rain follows a dry spell. The quick rush of water makes the inside of the tuber swell faster than its skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to split.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tswaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fãa.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking my young corn so heavily right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn lɛ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay their eggs on fresh green growth that pops up right after the rain starts. The young leaves are soft and easy for the newly hatched worms to eat, which is why infestations happen so quickly early in the season.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛha ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ akɛ amɛaaye. Enɛ hewɔ ni helai ni baa lɛ baa oya yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: Why do my garden vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry grass helps keep the soil moist and cool throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots that absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get to drink the rainwater and feed on the soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nuɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains rot or get destroyed by insects so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛhe feɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If grain is not dried completely before storage, moisture stays inside and causes mold or attracts insects. Storing well-dried grain in airtight bags or sealed containers prevents air and bugs from getting in, keeping your harvest safe for months.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i baanyɛ ahi mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba loo egbala kooloi bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okpamɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off. You can carefully dig up one plant to check if the tubers are big enough before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome he nii ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so fast in the hot weather before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and soften quickly in high heat. Keeping harvested tomatoes in crates stored under shade with good air movement slows down spoilage and keeps them firm longer.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ wo adekai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha efitemɔ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha ehi shi shiŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer gives the soil the nutrients your maize needs to grow dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmei lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the dried grass on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and useful soil organisms that help crops grow. Leaving cleared grass to rot back into the ground feeds the soil and helps it hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni he tse ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni egboɔ ekoŋŋ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yam tubers rot when rain water sits around them for too long in poorly drained soil. Planting yams on high mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ta amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu kroko ni fa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from around my young crops so frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ shii abɔ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds gives your young plants full access to what they need to grow fast and produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ naa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come up when I plant them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need light soil pressure, air, and warmth to sprout. Planting seeds too deep uses up all their stored energy before they can push through the surface to reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa shikpɔŋ nɔnyɛɛ fioo, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by intense direct sunlight, lack of water, or insect damage. Planting shade trees like plantains helps keep the air humid and protects the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo koolooi fite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects sucking sap from under the leaves or by a plant sickness spread by pests. Controlling insects early with neem spray or recommended controls stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ loo tsei ahe helai ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Mra Be mli Kooloi Akudɔmɔ Kɛtsɔ neem spray loo nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaakpa curling lɛ.

english: Why are my garden egg plants not growing even though I pour plenty of water on them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ edaaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli waa daa gbi moŋ?

english: Pouring heavy water directly onto garden eggs (aubergines) can compact the soil and drown their tender roots. They prefer gentle, steady moisture around their base rather than being flooded.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ muji awo abɔɔ mli ŋmeii (eggplant) anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha eshishifãi bibii lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Amɛsumɔɔ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni ebɔle amɛhe po. Nu shwie shishitoo lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Does pouring water heavily directly onto my small crop leaves help them grow faster?
ga: Nu ni ashwieɔ baai bibii anɔ Ani minɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdaraa oya?

english: No, heavy pouring can damage delicate young leaves, break stems, and wash away topsoil. Water should be applied gently to the soil at the base of the plant so the roots can absorb it smoothly.
ga: Dabi, nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ shi waa lɛ baanyɛ afite baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, efo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the way I am watering my vegetable crop is actually damaging it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji bɔ ni mikɛ nu woɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ miifite amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If your plants turn yellow, drop leaves, or stop growing despite getting plenty of water, you may be overwatering or using too much force, which suffocates the roots and halts growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ebaaji lɛ shwie shi, loo ekpa dalɛ beni enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ po lɛ. Ekolɛ ooha nu fe nine loo okɛ hewalɛ babaoo miitsu nii. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings require so much patience and care before they show big leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai bibii lɛ ahe hiaa tsuishitoo kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo dani amɛfee baai wuji lɛ?

english: Young seedlings spend their first few weeks building a strong root network underground. They need gentle moisture and shelter from harsh heat before they can support rapid leaf and fruit growth.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni mli jɔ kɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua baa kɛ aduawai ni yaa oya lɛ.

english: Why does my young crop look like it is doing nothing even when I give it water daily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ efeee nɔ ko eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: When young plants receive too much water at once, their roots cannot get air from the soil. This suffocates the plant, making it pause its growth until soil drainage improves.
ga: Kɛ tsei bibii lɛ ná nu babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kpaa dalɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I keep pouring water on my small crop every time the top layer of soil looks dry?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ nu? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi be fɛɛ be?

english: Not necessarily. Check an inch deep into the soil first; if it is still moist below, the roots have enough water. Overwatering the surface starves roots of oxygen and stops plant development.
ga: Halamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli inchi kome klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo Tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nu ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ akadara.

english: Is it better to use an irrigation watering device or just pour water on my crops using buckets?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ atsu nii loo mikɛ baagi afɔse nu kɛkɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Irrigation devices spread water evenly and slowly like natural rain, allowing soil to absorb moisture without washing away nutrients or compacting root zones like heavy bucket pouring does.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ jaa nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni blɛoo. tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efɔɔɔ shi loo ekɛ shishifã lɛ he eyimɔ obɔbɔ tamɔ baagi ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: How does slow, gentle watering help my crops perform better than heavy splash watering?
ga: nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi blɛoo Ni te nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni tsii?

english: Slow watering gives soil time to soak up moisture deeply into the root zone without suffocating the plant, encouraging roots to grow deep, strong, and healthy.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, amɛhe wa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: What causes my aubergines or garden eggs to stop producing fruit and just sit idle in the field?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ yibii ni amɛtaraa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Aubergines often go idle when soil conditions around the roots are too waterlogged or hard-packed. Improving water drainage and allowing root aeration encourages new growth and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eggplants tsuuu nii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ehiii kwraa. Nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ loo eyi obɔ kɛ mɛi babaoo. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai heei.

english: Why do some of my crops survive heavy watering while crops like garden eggs fail to respond?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi yeɔ wala yɛ nu ni mli wa mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yeee wala mli lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root sensitivities. Garden eggs have sensitive roots that easily suffocate in overly wet soil, whereas other crops can tolerate wetter field conditions.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ shishifãi ni nuɔ he lɛ srɔtoi. Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine nɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi baanyɛ aŋmɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Adding NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nitrogen needed to make the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and stops pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Aduawai ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, holds moisture in the ground so you water less, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akafɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that create living shade, protecting the cocoa plants from heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni haa hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need stakes to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight. When the leaves get enough sunlight, the plant makes more food, which results in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishitoo mla ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kɛyaa hulu la nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo aba. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves. Spraying the plants early with neem leaf oil or an approved insect spray controls these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Akɛ neem baa mli fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ashwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Abaanyɛ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How do I know if Fall Armyworm is attacking my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworm miitutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworm damage appears as large, ragged holes eaten into the young leaves and the central funnel of the maize plant, accompanied by sawdust-like waste. Catching them early and spraying recommended insecticides saves your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm fitemɔ jeɔ kpo akɛ buji agboi ni ayeɔ awoɔ baai bibii amli kɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋshɔi lɛ amli. kɛfata he lɛ, jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii Omɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baahere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience severe heat stress or uneven watering. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the base early in the morning helps the plants keep their flowers and form healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tomato nɔ nu daa yɛ shishigbɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is cool. Applying fertilizer when soil is slightly moist prevents the sun from scorching the plant roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la ni mli ejɔ baa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil has lost its strength and lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Adding organic compost or the right fertilizer gives the soil back its strength so your maize can turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ efo mli, ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ tsɔɔ eŋɔli ni edaa waa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in strong heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them acts like a sunshade, keeping the young trees cool and humid until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ adumɔ baatsu nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Ye obua tsei bibii Ha efee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I tell if the soil is truly ready for planting right after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo diɛŋtsɛ kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain can be deceptive because the deeper ground might still be dry. You should check that the top layer of soil stays damp for several days so your seeds have enough continuous moisture to sprout without drying out.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ. Ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Esa akɛ okwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo. Enɛ ji koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and turn pale?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by small insects like whiteflies that carry a sickness from plant to plant. Removing affected plants early and using healthy stem cuttings for planting stops the sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ hela lɛ jɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni ena hela lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ni okɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ atsu nii beni oduɔ nii koni hela akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɛ akɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ekome lɛ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans have a special ability to pull food from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow better without relying entirely on bought fertilizers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛgbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of the crop seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are damaged, buried too deep in the soil where air cannot reach them, or eaten by underground pests. Plant fresh seeds at a finger's depth in moist soil to help them sprout easily.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛfite. Afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ Dumɔwui heei ni okɛ onine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my cocoa pods and making them rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji miigbɛ eshwa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ ahe ni eha amɛmiigboi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal sickness called Black Pod that thrives in wet, dark places. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight in and air flow through, drying out the wetness that causes the sickness.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ ewo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa kɛji edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy. Watering your plants early in the morning and putting light palm leaves over them helps them stay cool enough to turn flowers into fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ ŋmei baai komɛi awo nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa fɔfɔii feɔ aduawai.

english: Growing the same crop on the same land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the earth until it becomes tired. Switching to different crops each season gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its natural richness.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi anɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛsaa ebɔɔ su ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young crops as soon as they appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ?

english: Weeds are greedy plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from direct sunlight because intense heat burns their sensitive leaves. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa shields them from sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he hulutsoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers drop down and bury themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their pods underground. After pollination, the flower stem grows downward into the soil, where it forms the groundnut pod safety away from birds and hot sun.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ pollination sɛɛ Fɔfɔi ahe tsei baakwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahe tseee kɛjɛɔ okpoi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing seeds properly ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop thick stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to capture maximum sunlight for building big tubers below. Staking also keeps leaves away from wet soil, which prevents rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shishigbɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, drain nutrients and water away from the main plantain tree. Removing most suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main tree to grow bigger leaves and produce heavier bunches.
ga: Tsobii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ baaná baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the young leaves. Spraying the plants with a mild neem seed extract solution or appropriate insecticide controls these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Akɛ neem dumɔwu mli nu ni mli ejɔ baashwie tsei anɔ. loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛwo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the soil dries out completely or when weather temperatures get too high. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass helps keep the soil moist and cool so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: Why are my watermelons splitting open right on the farm before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst open when they receive a sudden heavy watering or rain after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer rind can stretch, so consistent watering helps prevent splitting.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji amɛná nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni akagbala.

english: How can I check if the maize seeds I bought are good quality before I plant them on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can test your seeds by dropping a sample into a bowl of water; good, solid seeds will sink to the bottom, while weak or insect-damaged seeds will float to the top.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui okwɛ kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni oookɛwo nu tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni hi, ni wa lɛ baagbee shi kɛya shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni kooloi efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to cut for planting my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Select mature, hardwood stems from healthy plants that show no signs of disease or pest holes, taking cuttings from the middle section of the stem where the buds are strongest.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni wa ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe okadi ko bɛ he lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to leave proper space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mashi he ko ni sa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced properly, each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, resulting in bigger yields and healthier stems.
ga: Beni aduɔ tsei ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ Tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ ewuuu. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that burn easily under direct sunlight, so planting shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha abu he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it better to plant my seeds right after the early rains start rather than during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ fe nɔ ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moist soil gives seeds the water needed to break open and grow strong roots quickly, helping them establish before any dry period comes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil or the roots are trapped in waterlogged ground and cannot breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he, ni enyɛɛɛ emu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to remove weeds while my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly suck up all the food and water in the soil, leaving your young plants weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. ni ebaaŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why should I cut off the bottom branches and extra shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra leaves and non-fruiting shoots directs the plant's energy straight into making larger, healthier fruits instead of wasting food on useless leaves.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa nɔ lɛ

english: How do I know if my farmland needs animal manure or fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had thin stems, or produced small harvests, your soil is exhausted and needs manure or compost added to restore its nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo, eyɛ tsei bibii, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu baafite ni ehe baahia ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I harvest my vegetables early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa mi-aduawai lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Crops harvested in the cool morning hold more water and stay fresh longer, preventing them from wilting quickly on the way to the market.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkagbo oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves curl during peak heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This natural reaction slows down water loss through transpiration and keeps the plant from drying out until cooler evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ nu ni faaa lɛ nɔ. ni otsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress that can dry out flower pollen and render it sterile. When pollen fails to fertilize the blossom, the tomato plant sheds the flower to conserve water and energy rather than trying to develop a fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ ni baanyɛ aha pollen lɛ agbi ni ekɛ fɔmɔ aba. Kɛ́ pollen nyɛɛɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oná yibii lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate a lack of key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the plant is shedding older leaves to direct water and energy toward growing its tubers under dry conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo akɛ tsei miiho baai ni egbɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛkɛwo bulbs yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do my okra plants grow huge green leaves but produce very few actual okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ okra ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of reproductive growth. This causes lush, tall foliage but delays or reduces flowering and pod formation.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a juɛmi ngɛ fɔmi blɔ nya tomi ɔ hɛ mi. Ehaa tsei ahe tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo ebaa shi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very tall and thin when planted close together under shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants stretch rapidly toward sunlight when crowded or shaded. This causes them to grow thin, weak stems that lack the strength to support heavy bunches when fruiting time arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya kɛya hulu la lɛ he kɛji amɛyi obɔ loo amɛyɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli etse ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ be shɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and stop growing during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air pockets in the soil, effectively suffocating the plant's root system. Without access to oxygen, pepper roots cannot absorb essential nutrients, causing leaves to yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ oxygen bɛ lɛ, Pepper shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛkɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold fungus that thrives in dark, humid, and overly damp conditions. It spreads easily during high rainfall when farm canopy humidity stays trapped.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei, nu mli ŋmei, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli beni ŋmɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli nu lɛ emɔ ehe lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers have small bumps all over their skin and spoil quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Hewolo lɛ nɔ fɛɛ ni efiteɔ oya?

english: Tiny root-knot nematodes in the soil attack yam tubers, causing dark gall-like bumps on the skin. These injuries allow rot-causing bacteria and fungi to enter and destroy the stored yam.
ga: Nematodes ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛtutuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ gallbladder baa hewolo lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ pilamɔi nɛɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ.

english: Why don't seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce good yields like the original seed packet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai tamɔ shishijee dumɔwui akuu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent lines for maximum vigor. The seeds harvested from that crop lose those combined beneficial genetics in the second generation, producing uneven, smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi srɔtoi enyɔ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai wala yibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeee ekome.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted beans right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe ŋmeii ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weed seeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and lie dormant in the soil ready to germinate instantly. They absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crop seeds.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni amɛwɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important plant food. When the soil runs short of nutrients, the maize plant moves remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Abele tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that natural plant food remains in the ground to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that lose water very quickly under direct tropical sun. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains beside them creates a cool environment that keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ daa waa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water in the soil. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔi wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown, dirt-like powder inside the plant center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-ŋmã bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The brown powder is the insect's waste, and catching this early with proper pest management stops the caterpillars from destroying the growing tip of your maize.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Pauda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji kooloi amli jwɛi. Ni ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa nɔ Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa lɛ yitsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave standing water in the soil for too long, the roots suffocate, allowing soil fungus to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself from heat. By curling its leaves inward, the tomato plant reduces the surface area exposed to hot sun so it does not lose too much water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie mli lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu babaoo sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to transfer pollen. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding overuse of harsh sprays helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni mli wa fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight. The pepper plants stretch rapidly upward to reach light, producing thin, weak stems that break easily under the weight of heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Pepper tso lɛ baatsɔ ehe oya kɛya la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fãa oya yɛ aduawai ni tsii ni tsii lɛ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight and convert it into food stored underground in the tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into full sunshine, where they can make maximum food without rotting from soil contact.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛheɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Staking haa ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Baai lɛ baanyɛ ahoo nii kwraa ni amɛgbooo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin stems that dry out easily in direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a living canopy that protects the seedlings from heat and retains moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ egbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls whatever nutrients it has left from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, shrinking, and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches in cassava are caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your crop healthy and prevent this disease.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when extreme heat or lack of water stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination. Adding mulch around the base of the plant retains soil moisture, and providing consistent water keeps the soil cool enough for flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Mulching around Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ni nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant many seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the seedlings to compete against each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in very small ears of corn or no harvest at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa toi lɛ faaa kwraa loo anyɛɛɛ akpa kwraa.

english: Yam tubers are ready for harvesting when the vines and leaves above the ground turn yellow and dry out completely. This signals that the plant has stopped growing leaves and has stored all its energy into developing full-sized tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ adalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow in my pepper farm reduce the size of my pepper harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-pepper ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from pepper plants. Removing weeds regularly ensures that all the nutrients in the soil go directly into making your pepper plants grow bigger and produce more fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa koni eha o-pepper tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do small insects destroy my harvested maize grains after I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain insects like weevils thrive when stored grains still contain moisture or are kept in humid places. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until the kernels are hard before sealing them in airtight bags starves the pests of water and air so they cannot multiply.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmaa mli tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye kɛji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo akɛ amɛ to ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ hulu la shishi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani akɛwoɔ vacuum kotokui amli. Ebaaha nu lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni hi. no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ eha yibɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Saving seeds from hybrid maize is not recommended because hybrid crops are specially bred for one generation only. If you plant the saved seeds, the resulting plants will grow unevenly and yield much less grain than the original high-yielding crop.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ haaa ejaakɛ akwɛɔ tsei ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛhaa yinɔ kome pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ato Tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe blema tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for my farm if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it tired and weak. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egbɔjɔɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong green leaves. Giving the soil compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun because their roots cannot draw water fast enough. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a natural umbrella that protects the cocoa seedlings until they are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops have to fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and nutrients to grow thick stalks and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from under the leaves. Controlling these tiny pests early with proper sprays or neem water stops the leaves from curling and keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛtsɔ neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni eye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat becomes too intense or when the plant receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the plant reduces soil heat and helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tsei lɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli dɔlɛ aba shi ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds away from my cassava plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?
