english: Young cassava plants grow slowly during their first three months and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures the cassava gets all the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients it needs to produce big tubers later.
ga: Yucca tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to lift and tie my yam vines onto wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso nɔ ni mikɛfi tso ko he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Keeping the leaves off the ground also prevents damp soil diseases from damaging the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbe tso lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less maize every year when I plant it on the same spot continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same soil every year drains specific food nutrients that maize needs and lets soil pests build up. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural food back into the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ ekome. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains fall close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting in the soil starves the underground tubers of air, causing them to drown and rot. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to sow my maize seeds after the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: If you squeeze a handful of soil and it forms a ball that holds together without dripping water, the soil has enough moisture for seeds to sprout. Planting in soil that is too dry causes seeds to spoil before growing.
ga: Kɛ́ omimɔ sũ fioo ko lɛ, efeɔ bɔɔlu ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani adu.

english: What causes crop sickness to spread so quickly across my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Crop sicknesses are often caused by tiny germs like fungi, bacteria, or viruses. They spread easily through wind, splash water, insects, contaminated farm tools, or infected seeds, especially when plants are grown too close together.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai bibii tamɔ fungi, bacteria loo virus kɛ tsei helai baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya. loo dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Why is the pesticide I bought at the local market not curing the sickness on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaaa ni etsaaa hela ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Not all crop medicines work for every sickness. Using an incorrect chemical, a fake product, or treating a viral disease with an insect spray will not cure the plant and only wastes your money.
ga: Jeee tsei amli tsofai fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa hela fɛɛ hela. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Amale nibii Loo kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ baatsa hela lɛ ehereŋ tso lɛ yiwala ni ebaafite shika pɛ.

english: Is it possible to cure a cassava plant once its leaves start curling and showing yellow spots?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsa ŋmei tso ko kɛ́ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Once a plant is infected with a viral disease like Cassava Mosaic, there is no chemical cure to make that specific plant healthy again. The best action is to uproot and destroy infected plants so the disease does not spread to healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ná hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ cassava mosaic lɛ Tsofa ko bɛ ni baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ afee ji ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni akpata amɛhiɛ. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do government agriculture officers tell us to cut down cocoa trees that have swollen shoot disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efu lɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot is a deadly virus with no known cure. Cutting down infected trees creates a clear boundary that stops the virus from spreading to healthy cocoa farms in the community.
ga: Cocoa Swollen Shoot ji hela ko ni naa wa ni tsamɔ ko bɛ he. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa husu ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baatsiɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my maize is suffering from a sickness or just needs more fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmã lɛ hela mɔ lɛ loo ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo kɛkɛ?

english: A lack of fertilizer usually causes uniform yellowing across the whole field. Disease usually starts in patches or on specific plants, showing distinct spots, rotting, powdery dust, or sudden wilting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ hei srɔtoi. aloo yɛ tsei komɛi anɔ Kɛtsɔ otii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni etsɔɔ Trukaa fitemɔ, sũ, loo ŋmɔlɔ nɔ

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me when a strange sickness attacks my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ hela ko batutua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers link farmers to agricultural scientists. They can correctly identify the exact disease affecting your field and teach you proven, safe methods to control it before you lose your yield.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi kɛ okwaafoi kɛ okwaayeli he nilelɔi tsaa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛyoo hela pɔtɛɛ ni miigba oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni etsɔɔ gbɛi ni ana he odaseyeli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni oootsɔ nɔ oye helai anɔ dani okɛ onibii ni owoɔ lɛ afite.

english: Can spraying homemade mixtures like soap or ash water cure major plant diseases?
ga: Ani shĩa mli tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii tamɔ samla loo sũ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsa tsei ahe helai wuji?

english: Local mixtures can sometimes wash away light insects like aphids, but they cannot cure serious fungal or viral diseases already inside the plant tissues.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu kooloi bibii ni he waaa tamɔ aphids lɛ ahe nii, shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsa fungal loo virus helai ni naa wa ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ.

english: Why do plant sicknesses become much worse during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai ehiii kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity and wet leaves, which are ideal conditions for fungal spores and bacteria to multiply and travel from plant to plant.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal kɛ bacteria spores koni amɛshwere ni amɛfã gbɛ kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya tso kroko mli.

english: Why do my crops behave differently and yield less when planted in the same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows disease germs and pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the soil. Rotating your crops starves these pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nibii ni adu lɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my farm next season if I ignore a plant disease this season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli kɛji miku mihiɛ mishwie tsei ahe helai anɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: If ignored, disease organisms stay alive in the soil or in dead plant stems. When you plant fresh crops next season, the disease will attack them even earlier and lower your harvest further.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, helai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo yɛ tsei akutsei ni egboi amli. Kɛji odu tsei heei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ Hela baatutua amɛ oya ni ebaaha onibii ni oooha lɛ aba shi babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many leaves when the Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo beni harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during the dry Harmattan season to save water. By shedding leaves, the tree loses less moisture through evaporation and can survive until the rains return.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛyaa la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow after a few days of continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When the ground becomes flooded with water, plant roots cannot breathe and struggle to absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. The yellow color is a sign that the maize is starving for nitrogen.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yellowing ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat, which helps it hold onto moisture and avoid drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme hot weather or lack of water. The plant discards the flowers to save its energy for survival rather than growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he, moŋ lɛ amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the ground with natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall with big green leaves, but giving me very little yield at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yibiiwoo ni anáa yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of putting that energy into making grains, fruits, or tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ peeɔ ngma, a yiblii, aloo ngmahi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide big leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the cocoa trees while they build strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni etswaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Rot happens when cassava is planted in soil that traps too much water. Fungi in the wet ground attack the roots, causing them to turn soft and decay before harvest.
ga: Rot baa kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Fungus ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgboi dani okpa.

english: How do tiny worms end up inside the middle of my maize stalks?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei bibioo ko bote mi-abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Moths fly into the field at night and lay invisible eggs on the leaves. When the eggs hatch, the tiny caterpillars crawl straight into the center of the stem to feed where birds cannot reach them.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi foɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ baai anɔ. Kɛji wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ hei ni okpoi nyɛɛɛ ayashɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing long sprouts while sitting inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni mita mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living stems waiting for the right conditions to grow a new plant. Heat and moisture in the barn trick the yam into thinking it has been planted in the ground, causing it to sprout.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni miimɛ shihilɛ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ tsei heei. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ laka ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛsusu akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ mli. ha ekwɛ̃

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize plants need nitrogen to build strong leaves, so applying urea or NPK fertilizer helps them turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmã tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five corn seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When you crowd many seeds in one hole, the seedlings fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting one or two seeds per hole with proper spacing allows each stalk to grow strong and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo fata bu kome he lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko adara waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I clear all the weeds around my crops before putting fertilizer near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛ.

english: Weeds grow aggressively and will absorb the fertilizer faster than your main crops can reach it. Clearing weeds first ensures that your crops get the full benefit of the fertilizer you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otso titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, onibii lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and moisture, keeping young cocoa cool until it establishes strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni efeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines onto wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to manufacture food for the growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases and resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hulu lɛ nɔ kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi ni ehaa yam ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Should I plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains before planting. Early rains are often 'false rains' followed by dry hot days that can burn up freshly germinated seeds before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani oduɔ nii. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amale’, ni gbii ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my maize plants and leaving small black waste inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ gunk diŋ bibioo ko yɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the plant's growing point (the whorl) to feed on soft new leaves, and applying neem extract or appropriate insecticides early protects the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ hei ni edaa lɛ (whorls) koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. kɛ neem mli nu ni sa loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from excessive heat, strong winds, or sudden periods of dry soil. Providing regular watering and mulching around the roots helps the plant retain flowers and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ tomatoi.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying with a mild soapy solution or recommended insect spray clears the insects so fresh leaves grow straight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Aloo, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rain stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ mihi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy water stays trapped around the roots for days, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen, allowing rot-causing soil fungi to destroy them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ muji lɛ ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when standing in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji amɛdamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures become too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if there are not enough insects like bees visiting to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow better when I plant cowpeas or beans alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas draw nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, feeding the neighboring maize naturally while the tall maize stalks support climbing bean vines.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɔɔ ŋmãa wain tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids feeding on the sap. Sprayers using organic mixtures like neem oil solution help protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem oil solution tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves lifted off the damp soil where diseases spread and gives them maximum exposure to sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ he babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away extra young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: Too many young shoots steal nutrients and water from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the tree has enough energy to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei bibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ afɔ.

english: Why do tiny young cocoa pods turn black and dry up before growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi dani ŋmeii lɛ adara kwraa lɛ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt, where the cocoa tree sheds extra young pods it cannot feed to save energy for the healthiest remaining pods, though pests or fungi can also cause it.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni ji he ni cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni darako ni nyɛɛɛ ahi shi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii hu baanyɛ aha eba moŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need soft, filtered light to survive because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving mature shade trees or planting plantains alongside your cocoa creates a protective canopy that keeps seedlings cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ kane ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli tse koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu yɛ kookoo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmei ni haa dumɔwu lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps green up the leaves so the crop can feed itself and form big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkwɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛyɛ toi wuji.

english: Is it better for me to plant my cassava sticks close together so I can get more plants on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak roots. Giving each plant enough distance lets the roots expand fully into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during peak sun hours to hide their surface area and reduce water loss through evaporation. However, if they stay curled even when cool, it may be a sign that tiny insects like whiteflies are sucking moisture from the plant.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛtee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛbɔle amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i mli lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ miimu nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: My pepper plants are producing plenty of flowers, but why do the flowers keep falling off without forming peppers?
ga: Mi pepper tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the crop gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my land dry out and bake hard just a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: Soil bakes and cracks when it is exposed directly to the sun without a layer of organic material to hold in moisture. Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves keeps the soil cool, spongy, and wet for much longer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi lɛ ŋmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehiɛ ŋmeii, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seed immediately after the very first rain in March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ March mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch delicate new sprouts before they take root. Waiting until the rains become steady and reliable ensures your young seeds have continuous water to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛwo shishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛ ni aaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Ebaaha odumɔwui bibii lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in cold, dark, and excessively wet conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the farm, drying out the pods and stopping the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do I need to spend time guiding my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be kɛtsɔɔ sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ gbɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use leaves to capture sunlight and convert it into energy to build large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves high off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight instead of rotting in the damp shade.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo moŋ fe ni amɛaafite yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when I plant them at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil food faster than domesticated crops can. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from choking your young crops before they can get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni otsei bibii lɛ akafo dani amɛje kpo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen or that the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving water drainage in the field will help restore the green color and keep the plant growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli su lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ewo tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How do I know which way to point cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have tiny raised nodes or 'eyes' where the leaves grow. You should always plant the stem with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the roots grow down easily into the dirt and the new leaves grow straight up.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ nodes bibii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ‘buds’ he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tso lɛ adu be fɛɛ be ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baai heei akwɛ̃ kɛya ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: It is natural for a cocoa tree to produce thousands of flowers and drop most of them. The tree only keeps the number of flowers it has enough water, soil nutrients, and energy to nourish into full cocoa pods.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tso baawo fɔfɔi akpei abɔ ni nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɛɛ baaje mli. Tso lɛ baabua fɔfɔi ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ pɛ naa. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the ground so you do not need to water as often, shields the soil from the hot sun, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need as much sunlight as possible on their leaves to feed the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows them to get full sun and prevents wet leaves from catching diseases on the soil surface.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ awó wein tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa wein tsei lɛ náa hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni ehaa baa ni efɔ lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hela.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the leaves at the center of my young corn plants and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The adult moth lays eggs on the leaves, and once hatched, the caterpillars crawl inside the central shoot to feed; catching them early with natural sprays or recommended pest treatments is key to saving your yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni eda ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni kɛ́ efɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛyatao niyenii. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, enɛ ji nɔ titri ni baaha ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas in the same farm rows as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen gas from the air into the soil, naturally feeding the surrounding maize while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni haa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa ni ebɔle ohe lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni oha bo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaakpa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies, or a plant virus spread by them. Keeping the farm free of wild weeds and controlling tiny insects early keeps the leaves flat and broad.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko, ni akudɔ kooloi bibii mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli atse.

english: Why do I need to cut down some of the small shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stalk, they will steal water and food from it. Leaving only one main stem and one strong replacement shoot ensures you get large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ, Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Shi tso titri kome kɛ tso tso kome ni mli wa pɛ. Enɛ baaha ona aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I wait to plant my seeds instead of putting them in the ground immediately after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni makɛwo shikpɔŋ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain after a dry season usually only wets the top layer of dry earth. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the soil is damp deep down, preventing young sprouted seeds from drying out and dying if a brief dry spell follows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die during the dry season if I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that get scorched easily by the harsh sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to block direct sunlight and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, ani abaatsɔ mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down prevents them from growing properly. The small nodes or buds where leaves branch out should point upwards toward the sky so the roots can grow down into the soil easily and the shoots can grow straight up.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ko shwie shi lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii Esa akɛ baai lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa wɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that grows the big tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves high up into the light and off the hot ground, which helps produce bigger yams and prevents leafy diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ la mli kɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji feɔ ŋmeii ni tsiɔ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa.

english: Why do farmers cut off the top leaves of a young plantain sucker before planting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ plantain bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ dani amɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming the long leaves of a plantain sucker reduces water loss while the shoot is getting used to its new soil. Without big leaves pulling moisture out into the air, the young plant can focus its energy on growing strong new roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afo plantain tsei lɛ ahe baai kakadaji lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miitsɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, baai agboi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei bibii baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama shishifãi heei ni mli wa ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow fast. Heavy rain often washes this food out of the topsoil, so adding compost or fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any small tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato bibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, water is scarce, or tiny pests damage the blossoms. When the plant feels stressed by dry soil or heat, it drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo latsaa miigba tso lɛ naa. Ebaashɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices out of the young leaves, or by a virus carried by these pests. Keeping the farm free of weeds and spraying with safe insect soaps can protect new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ baai heei anaa.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every single season and lets maize-specific pests build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores food to the soil and stops pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How does covering the ground with dry grass around my crops help them in hot weather?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, works like a blanket that shields the ground from the hot sun. It traps moisture in the earth so water doesn't evaporate quickly, keeping root zones cool and wet longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ efooo oya. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fresh chicken dung directly onto my crop roots right after taking it out of the coop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fresh chicken dung is strong and releases high amounts of heat and gas as it decomposes, which can burn delicate plant roots. Leaving the dung in a heap to dry and rot (compost) for a few weeks makes it safe and gentle for crops to absorb.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo kpo beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni egbi ni egbo (compost) otsii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfee blɛoo.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding in the funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo kone mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the growing tip of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments like neem extract or targeted sprays helps save your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaha onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or neem oil stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni miinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaakpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantain trees provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist, acting as natural protection while the cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsuɔ nii koni ebu adebɔɔ he yɛ be mli ni ato cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is it good to rotate my maize crop with cowpeas or groundnuts the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ tsina loo ŋmeii baatsake mi-ŋmã lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil. Rotating them with heavy feeders like maize restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii agboi, tamɔ ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow starting from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting along the center vein usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which plants need for strong green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps green them up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or pollination is poor. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. loo pollination ni ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni shwereɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off (around 9 to 12 months after planting) and the ground right around the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi (aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ) ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu egbi. Tso lɛ mli fã titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. It is safer to wait until the main rainy season is fully established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baagbe naa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away fertilizer before the roots can absorb it, wasting your money and washing nutrients into nearby streams. Apply fertilizer when soil is moist, but not during heavy storms.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eheɔ shika ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee yɛ ahum ni naa wa waa mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops use to build strong stems and stay green, so when soil runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans alongside my maize make the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it directly into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer enriches the soil so future crops like maize can grow stronger without needing as much synthetic fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ sɛɛnamɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ adara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa babaoo atsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees away from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young seedlings from hot direct sun until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu dumɔwu lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ baa mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather becomes extremely hot or when plants suffer from drought stress. High heat dries up the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to shed flowers to conserve its energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants produce big spread-out leaves but refuse to form a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shi ejeee yitsei ni yɔɔ kokroo ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to form when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer or during high heat periods. Excessive nitrogen forces the plant to build big loose leaves very fast instead of wrapping tightly into a solid center.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ efeŋ kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli loo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Nitrogen babaoo baaha tso lɛ awo baai wuji ni shwieɔ shi oya. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ lɛ kɛ fia lɛ saminya kɛ ya si benɛ e maa su te ɔ mi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the field when heavy rain stays on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ enɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain saturates soil without proper drainage, water displaces the soil oxygen, suffocating the tubers and allowing rot-causing bacteria to attack the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ nu ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow bigger tubers when I train them onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers using energy made by leaves exposed to sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage off the dark ground, spreading the leaves toward direct sunlight and preventing moisture-loving leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ tubers. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ. Gbalamɔ baai lɛ amli kɛya he ni hulu la lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. ni atsĩ baa helai ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa

english: Curled, twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking plant sap from beneath the leaf, or from a virus spread by these insects that damages leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea crops start producing small flowers very early when there is a short drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi bibii oya yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When crops experience dry spells, they feel threatened and switch into survival mode. The plant flowers quickly so it can produce seeds to reproduce before it dries up completely.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii na hulutsoo be lɛ Amɛnuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛyaa wala shihilɛ mli. Tsei lɛ fɔɔ mra bɔni afee ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni amɛfɔ dani amɛgbi kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during windy storms after the bunches grow heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni jwɛi lɛ egbɔjɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots like oak trees; they hold onto soil with shallow root strands. When heavy fruit bunches weight down the top, strong winds easily snap the shallow roots and pull the stalk over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ odum tsei. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ he. Kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ ba shi kɛtee ŋwɛi Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. ni ewaaa akɛ aaagbala tso lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and healthy vegetative growth, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help them recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛfeɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ kpakpa baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around crops is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that shades the soil from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating quickly and keeping the soil cool so the plant roots stay healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Koni tso shishifãi lɛ awa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground before I can even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground mainly when water collects around them in soggy soil or during heavy rains without proper drainage. Excess water starves the roots of air and allows fungal diseases in the soil to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye shishifãi lɛ hɔmɔ ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and becoming small and pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe tseee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a plant virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Once infected, the plant's internal sap flow is disrupted, causing the leaves to stunt and curl instead of growing flat to catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji hela lɛ emɔ lɛ pɛ Nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: What is making small holes in the center shoots of my young corn plants and leaving dark dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miifee bu bibii? tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni oshi muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that crawls into the growing tip or 'funnel' of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishi loo ‘agbɛi’ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the trunk is not broken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fãaa moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over easily when tiny microscopic worms called nematodes or insect larvae attack the underground root system. Destroyed roots can no longer anchor the heavy plant in soft, wet soil during strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ tutua shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ tsei ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or a shortage of tiny beneficial insects called midges, which are needed to carry pollen from flower to flower so pods can grow.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ ni bɛ. Enɛ he miihia koni akɛ pollen aya kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the stem right after opening instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛji agbele naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the surrounding air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very wet to very dry suddenly. The plant sheds flowers to conserve its energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni efɔ waa kɛyaa nɔ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stick long wooden poles into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high up into the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Good sunlight exposure on the leaves produces the energy the plant needs to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting mucuna or beans on my field stop stubborn weeds from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mucilage loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cover crops like mucuna grow fast and form a thick leafy carpet over the ground. This heavy shade prevents weed seeds in the soil from getting the sunlight they need to sprout and grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei tamɔ mucilaginous tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli tse ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa nɛɛ haaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. It can also happen when heavy rains log the soil with water, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help improve my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they have a special relationship with soil bacteria that pulls nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the earth. This naturally fertilizes the soil for nearby heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wekukpaa krɛdɛɛ ko. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛha niyenii ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my granular fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ granular fertilizer fataaa he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer off your field into nearby streams before your crops' roots can absorb it, wasting your money and potentially harming local water supplies.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eheɔ bo shika ni ebaanyɛ eye maŋ lɛ mli nu ni akɛhaa lɛ awui.

english: What is causing the center leaves of my corn to look ragged and full of small brown powder?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni eyi kɛ powda bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the central growing leaf (the funnel) of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender young leaves and leaving behind its droppings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai (cones) ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye baai bibii lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward and look tiny during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which multiply very quickly during dry, hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni baagbɛ eshwa oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes up for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Without adequate sunlight, the leaves cannot make enough food to swell the yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛtso lɛ mli tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why did the maize seeds I buried deep in the ground fail to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too deep deprives them of the warmth and oxygen needed to germinate. Even if they sprout, the seedling runs out of stored energy before it can push through a thick layer of soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ po Shi hewalɛ ni ato lɛ sɛɛ fo dani enyɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop their blossoms when stressed by prolonged dry weather, lack of moisture, or insect attacks like mirids (capsids). Managing shade and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers set into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ tamɔ capsids. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli fɛ̃i yelikɛbuamɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni efeɔ pods.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and you see cracks forming in the soil around the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed all their blossoms when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants undergo heat stress, causing the pollen to become sterile. The plant naturally drops its unpollinated flowers to conserve water and energy to survive the heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaná hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi ni adebɔɔ naa amɛwoɔ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and falling off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and protect themselves. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss and keeps its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture stress tomato plants, forcing them to drop their flowers to conserve energy rather than spending vital water and nutrients on developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ nyu kɛ níhi nɛ he hia tsuɔ ní kɛ haa yiblii ɔ waa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes and white patches in the center stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ yɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and light patches inside the leaf whorl are typical signs of fall armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the young growing central stem during the day to feed.
ga: Buu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ahe okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni eyatao niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and twisting up tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Twisting and shrinking leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites, or a virus transmitted by these insects that damages the plant's growth tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ mli fãji lɛ

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, overly shaded farm environments where cool moisture stays on the pods for too long.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ lɛ hiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds early before the vines grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ato mra. Dani wain tsei lɛ baadara

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during the critical early months when yam plants are forming their underground tubers, resulting in smaller harvests if left unchecked.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee nyɔji ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Beni sweet potato tso lɛ miifee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees turn yellow and fall over when water sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni nu damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Standing water suffocates and rots the roots, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients and anchoring itself firmly in the ground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia plantain shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetables wilt even when I water them with water from a stagnant pond on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu ni jɛ nubu ko ni ekã shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ?

english: Stagnant pond water often carries root-rot pathogens and excess salts that damage delicate plant roots, making it impossible for the plant to absorb clean water properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli helai ni haa shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ ŋmei ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni mli tse jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together in the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly initially and matures much later, allowing both crops to share space without competing for resources early on.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni sɛɛ mli lɛ edaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ jaa he ko ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye amɛhe akaŋ yɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe mra.

english: Why should I plant trees on my farmland when I need that space for my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Akɛni he ko he miihia mi koni makwɛ niyenii hewɔ lɛ?

english: Trees protect your farmland by providing shade and holding water in the ground, which keeps the surrounding soil moist and helps your regular food crops survive hot and dry periods.
ga: Tsei buɔ nibii ni odu lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɛ nu ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa oniyenii tsei ni oyeɔ daa lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ bei ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli.

english: How exactly do trees help keep water in the soil on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Tree roots act like deep sponges under the earth that trap rainwater, while their leafy canopy blocks direct sunlight from drying out the top layer of soil.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ ni mɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi.

english: Do young trees planted on the farm require constant daily care, or do they manage themselves?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi loo esa akɛ akɛ niji akwɛ amɛnɔ?

english: Once young trees are properly planted during the rainy season and get established, their roots naturally search deep for groundwater, requiring very little day-to-day attention.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli ni amɛma shi lɛ, Amɛshishifãi lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli shɔŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ebiii daa gbi kwɛmɔ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo.

english: Will planting trees on my farm reduce the amount of sunlight my crops need to grow?
ga: Ani tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha hulu la ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ aba shi?

english: If you space trees properly, their shade helps protect delicate crops from harsh mid-day heat without blocking the light they need to produce food.
ga: Kɛji oto tso lɛ he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shwane mli la ni naa wa lɛ he ni amɛtsĩii la ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii feemɔ lɛ naa.

english: What is the best time of day or season to plant new seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo be mli ni mikɛbaadu dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant early in the rainy season during cool mornings or late afternoons, as the moist soil and gentle sun prevent young plants from drying out immediately.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ leebi loo shwane ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ baatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I plant trees from my existing crops so they do not steal nutrients?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miyɔɔ momo lɛ ahe tɛŋŋ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii?

english: Leaving a gap of several meters allows tree roots to grow deep without competing directly with the shallow roots of your food crops for fertilizer and water.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ ni ji mitai babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ niyenii tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu.

english: Why do some of my young plants wilt and die right after I move them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plants often suffer from transplant shock if their roots are damaged during moving or if they are planted in hot, dry soil without immediate moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei naa hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly even after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposed to full sun loses water rapidly to evaporation, but adding organic mulch or tree shade helps lock moisture into the ground longer.
