ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ organic mulch loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a lack of water before they die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani amɛgboi?

english: Crops usually signal water stress when their leaves start curling up, turning yellow, or wilting during the hottest part of the afternoon.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ kɛji amɛbaai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Can planting trees on my land help restore soil that has become dry and hard?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba?

english: Yes, tree roots loosen hard ground so rainwater can soak in deeper, and fallen tree leaves decay into natural fertilizer that makes the soil rich and soft again.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ koni nugbɔ nu lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni tsei ahe baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni efeɔ blɛoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over whenever there is heavy rain and strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have hard wooden trunks or deep taproots. When heavy rain softens the topsoil, the roots lose their grip, and strong winds push against the broad leaves, easily knocking the entire plant to the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ tsei akutsei ni wa loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shikpɔŋ mlɛo.

english: How can I prevent my plantain stalks from snapping when they start bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi plantain tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛyiɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: You can prop up your plantain trees using sturdy bamboo or wooden poles with a fork at the top. Placing these poles under the bunch against the main stem gives the plant extra support against wind and heavy fruit.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa ni akɛ fɔk ewo nɔ lɛ afi dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei nɛɛ wo tso lɛ shishi kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ buɔ ehe babaoo kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii ahe.

english: Can planting trees around my farm boundary protect my plantains from being blown down?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ abu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ shi?

english: Yes, planting a windbreak of tall trees or hedging around your farm edges reduces the strength of incoming wind, creating a safe zone that keeps your soft plantain stalks standing.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kakadaji ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haa odumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ damɔ shi.

english: Should I trim off dead plantain leaves before the windy season starts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo plantain baai ni egboi lɛ dani kɔɔyɔɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Yes, cutting away dry or dangling leaves reduces the surface area that wind can push against, making it easier for the plantain stem to withstand strong gusts.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egbi loo ni efolɔ shi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa yɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa plantain tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaadamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa lɛ naa.

english: Is a plantain trunk made of solid wood like a mango tree?
ga: Ani akɛ tso ni wa fee plantain tso lɛ tamɔ mango tso?

english: No, a plantain stem is actually a soft pseudostem made of tightly wrapped leaf bases filled with water. Because it lacks solid wood, it is flexible but breaks easily under pressure.
ga: Dabi, plantain tsei lɛ ji amale tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo diɛŋtsɛ. Akɛ baa shishi ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ fee, ni akɛ nu eyi mli obɔ. Ejaakɛ tso ni wa bɛ No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo shi efoɔ oya yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi.

english: Why do tall plantain varieties fall over more easily during storms than shorter ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli fe nɔ ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Taller plantains act like tall sails in the wind—they catch more force high in the air and exert more leverage on their roots, making them far more prone to falling than shorter dwarf varieties.
ga: Plantains ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ lɛlɛi ni kwɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enaa hewalɛ babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfoɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbeeɔ shi fe dwarf henɔi ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ.

english: If strong wind snaps my plantain stem in half, will that stem grow back and bear fruit?
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli wa lɛ, plantain lɛ baatse mli enyɔ. Ani dumɔwu lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni ewo yibii?

english: No, once a plantain stem snaps, that specific trunk is dead and cannot produce fruit. However, you can nurture the young suckers growing from the base underground to replace it.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ plantain lɛ fã lɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ baagbo ni ewoŋ yibii. Shi kɛlɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishigbɛ lɛ koni okɛto najiaŋ.

english: Why do plantain roots fail to hold the plant firmly in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain shishifãi nyɛɛɛ atswa tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallowly near the top of the soil rather than deep underground. When rainwater turns topsoil into soft mud, the shallow roots lose their friction and slide right out.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daaa fioo. Ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Does heavy rainfall by itself damage my plantains, or is it mostly the wind?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ gbe mi diɛŋtsɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ? Aloo bei pii lɛ, eji shwiemɔ?

english: Rain itself is good because plantains need plenty of water to grow. The main damage comes from the strong winds that usually accompany rainstorms, which bend and break the heavy stalks.
ga: Nugbɔ hi ejaakɛ nu babaoo he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛdara. Nɔ titri ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni bei pii lɛ ekɛ nugbɔshiimɔi baa, ni haa tsei ni tsii lɛ fãa lɛ.

english: Why does managing a large plantain farm become so difficult after heavy storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔkwɛmɔ bafeɔ nɔ ni wa yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storms create extra urgent work: fallen plants must be harvested quickly before pests ruin the fruit, damaged trunks must be cleared, and remaining trees must be propped up immediately, which requires many hands.
ga: Ahum lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ko ni he hiaa waa baa: esa akɛ akpa tsei ni egbee shi lɛ oya dani tsɛŋemɔ helai akpata aduawai lɛ ahiɛ. Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni efite lɛ. ni esa akɛ akwɛ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni biɔ niji babaoo

english: Why do cocoa prices change so much from one season to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo jara srɔtoɔ waa yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa prices change based on global demand, total harvest sizes in major producing countries, and standard prices set by government regulatory bodies like COCOBOD to protect farmers.
ga: Cocoa jara tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni jeŋ muu fɛɛ taoɔ lɛ naa. Nibii ni akpaa lɛ fɛɛ falɛ yɛ maji ni feɔ nii lɛ amli kɛ jara ni maŋ nɔyeli nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ COCOBOD lɛ toɔ koni amɛkɛbu okwaafoi ahe.

english: How can I make sure I am getting the correct government price for my cocoa beans?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ minine shɛɔ nɔyeli lɛ jara ni sa nɔ kɛha mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: The government announces an official minimum cocoa price per bag each season, and you should only sell to licensed buying companies using certified, balanced scales.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ tswaa kookoo jara ni baa shi fe fɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ kotoku kome mli lɛ he adafi yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Ni esa akɛ ohɔ̃ɔ oha nitsumɔhei ni aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛheɔ nii lɛ pɛ kɛtsɔ sɛkɛli ni ja ni yɔɔ odaseyeli nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does heavy rain help my cocoa trees produce pods but sometimes also cause them to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii shi bei komɛi lɛ ehaa cacao tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need adequate water to develop pods, but excessive continuous rain creates high humidity that promotes black pod disease, a fungal infection that rots the pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa. ni ji ŋmei ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if the rainy season ends too early?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee mra tsɔ?

english: If the rains stop too early, cocoa trees suffer water stress, causing young developing pods to shrivel and dry up before reaching maturity.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra tsɔ lɛ, Cocoa tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi dani amɛdara.

english: Dropping leaves is the tree's natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation when soil moisture is very low.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ. Koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ.

english: How does the timing of the first rains affect when my crops start flowering?
ga: Te be ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshinii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The onset of rain breaks the dry season dormant period, triggering the crop to absorb water and nutrients necessary to produce flowers and set fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni ebɔi nɛmɔ lɛ eha wɔɔhe be eba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ewo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do extension officers recommend spraying cocoa trees before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afɔse kookoo tsei anɔ nu dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Spraying early protects the cocoa trees against pests like capsids and prevents fungal spores from spreading when wet, humid weather arrives.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra be mli Ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ.

english: How do crop fertilizers help cocoa trees produce larger pods during rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Fertilizers restock essential nutrients in depleted soil, giving the tree the energy it needs to convert rain and sunlight into bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛtsake nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods shrivel and die on the tree even when there is good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koo gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot support due to a lack of sufficient soil nutrients or energy balance.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I plan my planting schedule when rain patterns are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔ beni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ?

english: You can plan by maintaining shade trees to retain soil moisture, clearing weed cover early, and consulting extension officers for seasonal climate forecasts.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛha nɔ mra. ni okɛ extension officers lɛ agba sane koni amɛtsɔɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baafee.

english: Why does cocoa take several years to produce fruit while crops like maize give yields in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani kookoo woɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops have different life cycles. Maize is an annual crop that grows quickly to complete its life cycle in one season, whereas cocoa is a tree crop that spends its first few years building a strong root system and trunk structure before it has the strength to produce pods for decades.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ wala shihilɛi srɔtoi. Abɛi ji tso ko ni daa afi ni daa oya ni egbeɔ ewala be lɛ naa yɛ be kome mli. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo ji tso ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ, eheɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani ekɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa dani enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Is it fine if I harvest my cassava early just because market prices are high right now?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikpa ŋmei mra ejaakɛ jara ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ etee ŋwɛi bianɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Harvesting cassava too early means the tubers will be small, watery, and low in starch content. Allowing the plant enough time to mature fully ensures the roots build up proper weight and quality, giving you a better yield and higher total profit in the long run.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa cassava mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii bibii, ni nu yɔɔ mli, ni starch faaa yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná muji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ kpakpafeemɔ. Enɛ baaha oná nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni fa babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off due to stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like boron and calcium. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ boron kɛ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiihao lɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale yellow even though we are getting good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make their leaves green and healthy. Heavy rains can also wash away soil nutrients from the plant roots, leaving the crop hungry even if it has plenty of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hu baanyɛ ajie sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks the cycle of crop diseases.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa tsei ahelai ni baa lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to local conditions over hundreds of years, making their roots aggressive at grabbing water and soil food. Main crops need extra care and clearing because they put their energy into producing food rather than fighting off weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Tsei titrii lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ amɛhe ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ baawu.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look wrinkled during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a plant's defense mechanism to prevent water loss during hot weather, or it can be caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Checking under the leaves helps determine if the plant needs pest protection or just moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baa lɛ ji gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni nu akafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛba. Kɛ́ akwɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji akɛ ehe miihia ni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing taller once they start producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji ebɔi pepper feemɔ pɛ?

english: Once a pepper plant begins producing fruit, it shifts its energy from growing new stems and leaves into feeding and ripening the peppers. Removing early flowers on very young plants allows them to grow larger and produce much more fruit later.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo Etsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ niyenii mli ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ ajie mra be mli fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take longer to yield when planted during a spell of dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Plantains require steady moisture to establish strong root systems. When planted in dry conditions, the plant enters a survival mode where it slows down root and stem development until sufficient water becomes available again.
ga: Plantains he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa aba. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ, tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. He ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa blɛoo babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up completely before the tubers are ready under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ dani bulb lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaaya shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: As yam plants reach the end of their growing cycle, the leaves stop making food and send all remaining energy down into the underground tuber. The drying of the vine is a natural signal that the tuber has finished growing and is maturing for harvest.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Baai lɛ kpaɔ niyenii feemɔ ni amɛtsuɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa shi kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Wein tsei lɛ ni egbi lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ wein yitsei lɛ egbɔ ni eshwɛ fioo ni ebaaba kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is main food the plant needs to grow. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps nearby crops like maize grow better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why does my soil become as hard as rock during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic material like decaying leaves or animal manure. Adding compost or leaving dry plant leaves on top of the farm keeps the soil soft and helps it hold water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo oshi tsei ahe baai ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, which is a fungus that grows in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and fresh air reach the pods helps keep them dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela, ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves at night?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji nakai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the center of the plant during the hot day and come out at night to eat. Applying early treatment like neem liquid or recommended sprays inside the leaf funnel stops them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ateŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii gbɛkɛ. Tsofai tamɔ neem solution loo sprays ni akɛwoɔ baai kotokui amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ baatsi amɛnaa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my cassava after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to plant cassava after two or three strong rains have thoroughly soaked the soil. Planting in dry or barely damp soil causes the stem cuttings to dry out and die before roots can grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Is it better to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ aaadu tsei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui?

english: Planting in straight rows gives every plant enough space, air, and sunlight to grow strong. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier compared to scattering seeds.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃. Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young plantain suckers so often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? plantain bibii shii abɔ

english: Weeds steal water, light, and nutrients from young plantain plants. Clearing them early ensures the plantain grows a thick stem that can support heavy bunches later.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ aná tsei ni mli tse ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ni tsii sɛɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly very wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch stops the flowers from falling.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots get watery and spoil quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting cassava immediately after a very heavy rain makes the roots absorb too much water, causing them to rot fast. Harvesting when the ground is damp but not soaked keeps the roots firm.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo, ni no haa egboɔ oya. Nikpamɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means your soil is lacking nitrogen. The plant is moving the remaining nitrogen to its new growth at the top to stay alive, which shows your farm needs fertilizer or organic compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ŋta hee ni eda lɛ nɔ koni ehi shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every time I plant maize on the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and restores its strength naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ebɔi hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I seeing tiny holes in the leaves of my young maize plants and saw-dust like dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the plant's growing center during the day to feed on young leaves, and they need to be treated early with approved biopesticides or neem extracts before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii. Ni ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ mra. kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and planting resistant seeds helps protect the plants from getting stunted.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni koolooi bibii eyɛŋ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Ni dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Cocoa flowers fail to form pods when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) in the farm to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by too much direct sun, drought, or lack of essential nutrients.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee pods kɛji kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee amɛ pollination. aloo kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe nine, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting and smelling bad under the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiiho yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining properly. Heavy clay soil without raised mounds traps water around the roots, suffocating them and causing fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni ŋmeii bɛ nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is a strong rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni ahum baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can easily loosen in heavy soil, especially if microscopic worms (nematodes) or stem borers have damaged the roots underground. Planting them deep and mounding soil around the base gives them better support.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baanyɛ agbee shi oya yɛ sũ ni tsii nɔ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo. (Nematodes) loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ baaha amɛye amɛbua amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to clear all bushes and leave my soil completely bare in the hot sun before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Leaving soil completely bare allows the strong sun to bake away moisture and kill helpful soil living organisms. Bare soil also washes away easily when heavy rains start, taking topsoil nutrients with it.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn long before the planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be saŋŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their sleeping period (dormancy) after a few months, especially if the barn is warm and humid. Keeping the barn cool, well-ventilated, and removing early sprouts helps prolong their storage life.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be (wɔ) lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ, titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ. Ni tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has enough moisture to plant my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil from your farm into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping water and crumbles easily when poked, the soil has enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely without drying out or rotting.
ga: Nyɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ko ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiŋ loo amɛgboŋ.

english: Why do extension officers ask me to measure steps between my crop rows instead of planting anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ bi mi akɛ masusu he ni adu amɛ yɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Measuring fixed distances or steps gives every plant equal space to absorb water, light, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring crops, leading to bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ asusu he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ loo gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni anáa.

english: Spacing cassava cuttings about one meter—or one long step—apart leaves enough room for root tubers to grow large without crowding each other underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome loo step kome lɛ, ebaaha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛkafee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and fragile roots that dry out quickly under intense sun; planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them while they are small.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize crop mostly during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather causes maize plants to become weak and stressed, while allowing armyworm pests to multiply faster and feed heavily on leaves to get moisture.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji cutworm lɛ feɔ babaoo oya ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ babaoo koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, causing the plant to move nutrients from older bottom leaves up to nourish new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and droop immediately after I uproot and replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni mijie amɛshishifãi ni midu ekoŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Uprooting breaks tiny root hairs that take up water, causing temporary transplant shock until the plant settles and grows new roots in a few days.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbala shishifãi lɛ, ebaaha yitsɔi bibii lɛ adara. nu ni ekumɔ Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatswa ehe ema shi ni ekwɛ shishifãi heei yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is scarce to save energy and protect themselves from dying of drought.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he lɛ bɛ

english: Which direction should the nodes point when I plant cassava stem cuttings in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ atsɔɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei?

english: Cassava buds must always point upward toward the sky so the leaves grow properly above ground while the roots develop underneath.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji koni baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ adara yɛ shishi.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the season make my maize yield so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa mi-ŋma lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from young crops, so removing them early ensures your maize gets all the food it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, mra be mli ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Enɛ baaha o-abele lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my field yield less food when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa niyenii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests to build up; rotating with legumes like groundnuts restores soil strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Wait until the soil receives steady, heavy rain for two to three days in a row so the ground is thoroughly wet, rather than planting right after the very first light shower which can dry out quickly.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, o duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ ɔ nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbi oya ɔ se.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive strong, direct sunlight; they need partial shade from plantain plants or shade trees to keep their leaves cool and protect the soil moisture while they are young.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves and grow tall, or that the soil is waterlogged from heavy rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ebaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so the rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a rain—not right before a heavy rainstorm—and cover the fertilizer lightly with soil near the plant's root area.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ—jeee dani nugbɔ nɛ waa—ni okɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛshɛɔ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long without proper drainage, creating conditions where harmful organisms in the waterlogged dirt attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why are there small holes in the center of my young maize leaves and tiny worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant; inspecting your farm early and using recommended treatments saves the leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite.

english: How can I produce tomatoes on my farm that grow large and smooth enough to compete with imported ones?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee tomato yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni da ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛ tomato ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ abɔ he akaŋ?

english: High-quality tomatoes require high-yielding certified seeds, consistent watering directly at the soil level rather than over the leaves, and early protection against fruit-boring insects.
ga: Tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ nu ni akɛhaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ aduawai lɛ ahe mra najiaŋ

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of holding onto blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ baai moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together in one small area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ? he kome pɛ

english: Planting seeds too close forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with small yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: Is it better for me to buy fresh certified seeds or save seeds from my previous crop harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli loo makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are carefully produced to resist diseases and give high yields, whereas seeds saved from past harvests naturally grow weaker over time and produce less crop.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ feɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli, ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a protective canopy and preserves soil moisture, allowing the young cocoa trees to establish safely.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it safe for me to grow cassava on the same farm plot as my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava can be grown alongside cocoa, especially in the early stages to provide extra food and shade. However, cassava must be spaced properly so its aggressive root system does not fight with young cocoa roots for water and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmei yɛ kookoo masɛi. Titri lɛ yɛ shishijee bei amli Shi kɛlɛ, bɔni afee ni niyenii kɛ hulutsoo afata he lɛ, esa akɛ aŋmɛ ŋmei lɛ he gbɛ ni sa bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni boteɔ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii lɛ akawuu kɛha nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Will growing plantains, cassava, and cocoa together exhaust the nutrients in my soil faster?
ga: Ani plantain, cassava, kɛ cocoa ni mikɛduɔ ekome lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite oya?

english: Mixing multiple heavy-feeding crops on one plot can reduce soil fertility over time if left unmanaged. Spacing crops correctly and allowing fallen plantain and cocoa leaves to decay naturally into the ground returns key nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni tsii babaoo ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ ni oha plantain kɛ cocoa baai ni egbee shi lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit bunches fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up heavy bunches during strong winds or rain. Staking the plant with a sturdy wooden pole and piling rich soil high around the base helps anchor the plant to the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Okɛ tsei ni wa awo tso lɛ he ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ ato he kɛbɔle he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ tso lɛ ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava crops mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can recognize maturity when the lower leaves begin to yellow and drop off, and the earth around the stem begins to bulge and crack.
ga: Cassava tsei babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oyɔse dalɛ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How long after I plant my cocoa seedlings will I see the first pods growing?
ga: Be enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ? Ani mana klɛŋklɛŋ pods lɛ ni miida gbi ko?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties typically start producing pods within 2 to 3 years, whereas older, traditional cocoa trees take about 4 to 5 years before they yield their first full harvest.
ga: Cacao henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni etsɛ waa lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Clearing away tall weeds and trimming shade branches allows air and sunlight to dry out the trees, preventing the spread of the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Jwɛi kakadaji ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cocoa and food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-kookoo kɛ niyenii tsei lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough plants designed to rapidly absorb available sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds regularly around the base of your crops ensures the food and water go directly to your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛhe hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli oya Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ Otsei lɛ ashishifãi daa lɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu shɛɔ otsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off branches from my cocoa trees after they grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or crowded branches, allowing light and fresh air to reach the inner tree. This sunlight encourages healthier flowering and reduces moisture levels that cause disease.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Hulu la nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɛo, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How does joining a local cocoa farming group help me manage my farming and family expenses?
ga: Te kuu ko ni duɔ kookoo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ mi okwaayeli kɛ weku lɛ shika nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Farmer groups allow members to share farm work, buy supplies like fertilizer together at lower prices, and access financial support or low-interest loans to cover household costs like school fees without selling off immature crops.
ga: Okwaafoi akui ŋmɛɔ amɛmli bii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛjaa okwaayeli nitsumɔi, ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛheɔ nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. ni amɛná shika he yelikɛbuamɔ loo nyɔmɔwoo ni nyɔmɔwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛwo shia shika, tamɔ skul nyɔmɔwoo, ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshɛko.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shield their leaves from heat and keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔ̃ɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to yield a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout properly when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the top surface of dry soil. If a hot spell follows immediately, the sprouted seeds dry up and die. It is better to wait until rains become steady so the soil holds moisture deeper down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji ahum ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which plants need for healthy leaf and stem growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baa kɛ shishifã ni mli wa he miihia. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant maize on the same plot of land every year, why does my harvest keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen and vitality back to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen kɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves or grass over the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter (mulching) keeps the ground cool, traps moisture during dry spells, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into natural soil food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the field, roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ bote shi ni amɛgboi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center shoots of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like Fall Armyworms that feed on the growing funnel of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides protects the growing point before the plant dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ gbɛi ni daa lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he dani tso lɛ agbo.

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil minerals. Regular watering at the base and keeping roots cool with soil cover helps plants retain flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo minerals ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni awoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Extra branches steal plant food and water that should go into making fruit. Removing unnecessary lower branches directs the plant's energy into producing bigger and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji ni fata he lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛ nu ni esa akɛ akɛwo yibii. Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their soft leaves from direct sunlight and to retain soil moisture; without shade trees, intense heat scorches them and causes them to dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shã aahu kɛyashi egbi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food, which directly helps the yam tuber under the ground grow larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Enɛ baaye abua sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, causing the plant to move its remaining nutrients up to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to put chemical fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafata ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away from the crop's root zone into gutters and streams before the roots can soak it up, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Shika ni afiteɔ

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my cassava rots in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels in their stems that send oxygen down to their roots under water, while cassava roots drown and rot without air in the soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii tsuɔ nii kɛyaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant helps the roots grow deeper into the soil for water and stability, while making it easier for new shoots to sprout upward.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ nu kɛ shifimɔ aha. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwereɔ bibii bibii kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving less energy for the main plant to produce large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eha tso titri lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and causing the bush to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni eha jwɛi lɛ miikpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves and spreading plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ tso mli helai ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: This issue, called blossom end rot, happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering while the fruit is developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off before turning into bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ pea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, drought, or attacks by tiny insects like flower thrips that damage the blossoms.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo, hɔmɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ tutua tsei lɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged or if the weather has been extremely dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ loo kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi waa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a natural trick to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing moisture to the hot air and protects its roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋaa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛbaa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebuɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings grow tall and thin instead of remaining bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiifee bibioo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi akɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and weak when they do not receive enough direct sunlight. They stretch upward trying to reach light, so moving them to a sunnier location makes them grow thicker stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee he ko ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off before any fruits develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are not enough insects or wind to move pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop dark, sunken rotten spots on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebote shishi lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit. It often happens when soil water levels fluctuate rapidly, preventing the roots from absorbing calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing leafy stems instead of producing flowers and pods. Reducing nitrogen allows them to flower normally.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi lɛ baaha fɔfɔi aba bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize stalks bend over and fall to the ground when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when their root systems are shallow, when plants are crowded too closely together, or when soil lacks potassium. Heap soil around the base of the stalks to give them extra support.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa babaoo tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he koni ekɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kroko aba.

english: Why does my yam take so long to sprout after I plant the seed yams in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. They will not sprout until this sleeping phase ends naturally, even if they are planted in moist soil.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Amɛkwɛŋ kɛyashi nɛkɛ wɔɔhe be nɛɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ po

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, overly shady conditions. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and air helps keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves develop dark brown spots and dry up quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Dark brown spots on plantain leaves are typically caused by leaf spot fungi like Black Sigatoka. Removing infected leaves promptly prevents fungal spores from spreading to healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tamɔ Black Sigatoka lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist air they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and well-adapted to local soils. Their roots spread very fast to drink up water and fertilizer before your crop seedlings have time to establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã oya koni amɛnu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛto shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the cleared bush and dried leaves on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei bibii ni ajie kɛ baai ni egboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani mikɛduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter on top of the soil and kills earthworms and small soil organisms. Leaving cleared leaves to rot back into the ground builds soil fertility and acts as a cover that keeps soil moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ baai ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ko ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is the practical difference between using animal manure and using synthetic fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni yɔɔ kooloi aŋmei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer acts like fast energy for crops by feeding them immediately, but it does not improve soil quality long-term. Animal manure feeds the plant slowly over time while improving the soil's ability to hold water and nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ ni yaa oya kɛhaa tsei kɛtsɔ niyenii ni amɛhaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Manure haa tsei niyenii fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hu.

english: How can I tell if my crop soil needs water during the dry season without expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni nibii ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: You can push a clean wooden stick into the soil near your plant roots. If the stick comes out dry and clean without dark dirt clinging to it, the soil root zone is thirsty and needs water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi tso ni mli tse awo sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ egbi ni ehe tse ni muji diŋŋ ko bɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ni nu he miihia amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deeper into the ground, away from small crop roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni saa baai lɛ adalɛ he Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. kɛjɛ tsei bibii ashishifãi ahe

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high during hot days or when soil water changes drastically. Heat stress forces the plant to drop its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop making new fruits after I harvest the first batch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ aduawai heei ni mikpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If old or fully ripe peppers are left on the stem too long, the plant shifts its energy to maintaining those seeds instead of blooming again. Regularly picking mature peppers encourages the plant to produce new flowers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ loo ni egbɔ kwraa lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baatsɔ ehewalɛ nɔ kɛya dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ oootse ŋmeii ni eda lɛ daa lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi heei.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and develop tiny white insects underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Those tiny white insects are whiteflies that suck sap from your plant leaves and spread cassava mosaic virus. The virus weakens the cassava plant and prevents roots from growing into large tubers.
ga: ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Nomɛi ji ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso baai amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa. Virus lɛ haa cassava tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly when I store them together indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto he kome yɛ shĩa lɛ?

english: Stored yams rot when placed in hot rooms without good airflow or when stacked directly on damp floors. Good ventilation and cool shade keep harvested roots resting and prevent fungal decay from spreading.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ fiteɔ kɛ akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli loo kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ haa shishifãi ni akpa lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when the sun gets very hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides necessary cover and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aaadu yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nɔ ni he hiaa ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival trick maize uses to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni afoɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing at the base of a young corn plant usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has up to its newest top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ fɛɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yams every season when I plant them on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa be mli ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing yams repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil of specific nutrients that yams need to grow big. Rotating yams with other crops gives the soil time to rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa sweet potatoes koni amɛdara. Sweet potatoes kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ebɔɔ su ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, leaving rich nutrients behind for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ Amɛshiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants give me small roots when I plant the cuttings very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii shwereɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhe akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too closely, their roots must fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which prevents them from swelling into thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ eshishifãi lɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli koni ekafu ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are fully established before sowing my crop seeds in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ anɛ kwraa dani madu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to swell and sprout; planting too early in dry or partially moist soil can cause the seeds to dry out and rot before they can grow roots.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛfuu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or drought because the plant saves its energy to stay alive rather than putting effort into making fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves right out of the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides in the funnel of maize plants where the young leaves are soft and easy to chew before unfolding.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooye dani ogbele.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground when heavy rains flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in flooded ground because stagnant water cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to suffocate and allowing fungal diseases in the wet soil to destroy them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ŋmɔlɔ ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpata ehiɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or receiving too much water. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore the leaves to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: What is causing holes in my corn leaves and small droppings inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji baa ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli? Yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. You can control them by spraying recommended biopesticides or a natural neem leaf extract into the central leaf funnel early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni oooshwie baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava plants are ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaale akɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to climb high towards the sun. When the leaves get direct sunlight, they produce energy that travels down to make the underground yam tubers grow larger and heavier.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo nɔ koni amɛkwɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ hewalɛ ni yaa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ sũ mli nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil moisture consistent and adding compost or agricultural lime helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus carried by them. Spraying the plants with neem oil or insecticidal soap helps clear the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie helai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop and wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Vegetables lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it during peak heat. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives the roots time to soak up water before the intense sun hits.
ga: Aduawai shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛmuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tswaa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space and food to produce maximum yield.
