ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How does mixing dried leaves and animal manure into my soil help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Dried leaves and manure break down into organic matter, which improves soil fertility, helps the soil hold moisture during dry spells, and provides steady food for plant roots.
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ haa tsei ashishifãi

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize repeatedly in the same spot quickly depletes nitrogen and other nutrients from the soil. It also allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in the ground, causing your yields to drop each season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Can I plant soybeans together on the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu soybeans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting soybeans with maize is very helpful. Soybeans capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, soybeans ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Soybeans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few leaves when I sow the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plants stretch quickly upward to beat their neighbors to the sun, making them tall, weak, and easy to break.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛtswa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, egbɔjɔ ni ekumɔ oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen or that heavy rain has washed the plant food deep into the ground where the young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii mli nibii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my farm crops drop their flowers without producing any fruit or pods during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yibii loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of rain stress the crop. To save water and keep itself alive, the plant voluntarily drops its flowers so it doesn't have to spend energy growing seeds or fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ fite ŋmɔshi nibii. Koni okɛ nu ato ni oha ohe ahi wala mli. Tso lɛ jɛɔ etsui mli ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni okɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu dumɔwui loo aduawai.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my field for days and make my plant roots soft and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo lɛ? Ni mahã mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgboi?

english: Heavy clay soils trap water and block air from getting underground. Plant roots need air to breathe, so standing water smothers the roots and causes them to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the soft inner leaves inside the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mligbɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is a common habit of pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant where it is moist and safe from sunlight while eating the tender new leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Enɛ ji su ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei agbɛi amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ amɛye lɛ, yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani ŋmei ko baa.

english: How do weeds growing around my young crops make my plants weak?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi dumɔwui lɛ aha mi tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crop roots get all the food they need to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my soybean crop is fully matured and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybeans lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Soybeans are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and fall off the stalk, and the seed pods turn dry and brown, making a rattling sound when you shake them.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa gbee ni tswaa kɛji okpokpo lɛ

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly on tarpaulins before packing it into bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tarpaulin nɔ dani mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Damp grains grow dangerous molds and aflatoxins inside storage bags. Drying your maize until it is hard prevents rotting and stops storage insects from ruining your grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ aflatoxins yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ewa lɛ, ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ hu fiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or beans helps the crop I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that capture nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored food stays in the soil, helping the next crop grow strong without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many tiny black pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ diji bibii lɛ? lots dani etsɔ agbo

english: This is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods when the tree doesn't have enough water, sunlight, or food to support all of them, ensuring the remaining pods can grow healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, hulu la, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara waa.

english: Why do my maize plants give very small ears when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ toi bibii waa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for the same food, water, and sunlight, leaving no single plant with enough strength to grow full, big ears.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni no haaa tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha toi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to climb and stake my yam vines with sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikwɔɔ ni miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei ni niji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun and prevents fungal diseases that thrive on wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava plant produce flowers, and does that mean the tubers are ready to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ ayeɔ?

english: Flowering is just the plant's natural way of producing seeds to reproduce. It does not always mean the tubers underground are fully mature, so you should check the variety's recommended harvest age instead.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ewoɔ dumɔwui koni efɔ. Enɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ afii ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛkpa ŋmãa lɛ moŋ.

english: Is it bad to water my vegetable garden in the middle of a hot sunny afternoon?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ ko nɔ nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering under the hot sun causes much of the water to evaporate into the air before roots can drink it. Wet leaves in hot sun can also get scorched or attract diseases; watering early morning or late afternoon is best.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Baai ni efɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbala helai. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi loo shwane ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and leaves from my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine yɛ tomato tso mli beni edaa lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra side shoots directs the plant's energy into producing large fruit instead of wasting energy on excess leaves, while also improving airflow to prevent disease.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni helai akamɔ mɔ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, effectively starving them despite good rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. ni ehaa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant leaves during the day, eating the soft leaves and leaving behind dark droppings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ye baai bibii ni oshi ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade to protect young cocoa trees from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why should I trim off healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the tree branches. This prevents damp air from building up—which causes diseases—and forces the tree to direct its energy into producing pods rather than extra leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa. ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee baai krokomɛi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing nitrogen, a crucial food it needs to grow. Heavy rains often wash this nutrient deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: This is caused by a water-loving fungus responsible for Black Pod disease. High humidity and heavy raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil onto the pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni kɛ black pod hela baa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ha amɛgboi

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition makes all the plants weak and produces a smaller total harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster and stronger than my main crops after a rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have naturally adapted to local soil over a long time. They absorb water and plant food faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ. Amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why does spreading dry bush leaves around the base of my crops help them stay green in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi baai ni egbi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ? Mi tsei lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It blocks hot sunshine from evaporating soil water, keeping the roots cool and moist for much longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot make the soil good for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny root swellings containing helpful natural bacteria. These bacteria take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, leaving behind rich soil food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni efuu fioo ni adebɔɔ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mli. Muawai nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green manure, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing energy in thick tubers below the ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ɔ mi ngɛ tso ko nɛ mi wa ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress, such as intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor air flow. The plant drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛhaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods immediately helps control it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ latsaa be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tsei niji lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mli?

english: This is damage from Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the center of the maize plant. Spraying recommended treatments or neem liquid early in the morning effectively reaches and kills them.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa loo neem tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie amɛnɔ leebi lɛ, ebaashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni egbe amɛ.

english: Does my yam crop really need sticks to climb on, or can I let the vines trail on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato lɛ he miihia niji diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkwɔ. Aloo manyɛ mashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Staking yam vines keeps leaves off the ground where damp diseases spread and helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight, which produces much bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni helai ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni da kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize as close together as possible to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ he bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food to grow full ears.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha etoi muu lɛ fɛɛ awo mli.

english: Peppers drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and balancing your fertilizer helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Peppers baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and squishy while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is called Blossom-End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying calcium-rich fertilizer prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ Blossom-End Rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni calcium eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi enaa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt, restoring fertility to the soil naturally for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli?

english: Apply NPK fertilizer within two weeks of planting to help young roots grow strong, and follow up with Urea or SOA when the plants reach knee-height to support leaf and cob formation.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa. ni okɛ urea loo SOA anyiɛ sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni eye ebua baai kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, producing weak plants and much lower yields. It is best to buy certified hybrid seeds every planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the leaf tips inward when the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen if the soil is too dry or waterlogged, which prevents the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely high temperatures, uneven watering, or poor pollination. When the weather gets too hot and dry, the plant sheds flowers to conserve water and survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna haomɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni ehiii Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu ni amɛhi shi.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, as the plant needs a steady supply of soil moisture to carry calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai amli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight and will easily scorch and dry out. They require shade from taller trees or shade crops like plantains during their first two to three years to keep them cool and moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. ni ebaashã oya ni ebaagbi Amɛhe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ loo hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil; if no rain falls for two weeks after, the germinating seeds will dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii enyɔ yɛ no sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce enough energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the young shoots grow around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around the mother plant, they will all compete for the same soil food and water. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in larger, healthier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, amɛ hu amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to local soils and harsh weather. They have strong root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before young crop seedlings get a chance to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo jɛmɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛtswaa amɛhe shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the leaves at the bottom of the stem turn yellow and fall off, and cracks begin to form in the ground around the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko eda kɛji baa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi feemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. shishitoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi

english: Why does spreading wood ash from my kitchen fire onto my farmland help my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso sũ ni jɛɔ mi-kpataashi la mli ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Wood ash contains natural minerals like potassium and calcium that sweeten sour (acidic) soil and feed growing plants. It helps crop roots absorb nutrients better, leading to stronger plants.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ potassium kɛ calcium yɛ tso sũ mli. No yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ (acidic), ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni he wa fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yes, the small buds or nodes on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the plant to struggle to grow and drastically reduces your cassava yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo nodes. Esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda ni ebaaha ŋmei yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my corn seeds very close together to get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants with small cobs and makes it easier for diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure will help green up the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes such as cowpeas and peanuts naturally absorb nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil. Koni ekɛ babaoo aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to erect tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay free from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni helai bɛ nɔ lɛ aba.

english: This is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juices from the plant leaves or spreading a virus. Neem oil spray or approved insecticides help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso baai amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes inside the central funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in maize fields. Spraying early in the morning or late evening with recommended pest controls, or putting clean dry sand/ash into the plant funnel, can help kill them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fɔɔ baa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Okɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii kɛshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Aloo ŋã/ashwishwɛ ni mli tse ni egbi ni akɛfataa ŋã ni aduɔ lɛ he. baanyɛ aye abua ni agbe amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and smell bad during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛhe ŋmɔlɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp environments. Pruning excess cocoa branches and weeding allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine ni aaafolɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ

english: How do I know if the crop seeds I buy at the local market will actually grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good seeds are inspected and certified by official seed units to guarantee high germination rates and freedom from diseases. Buying certified seeds with official approval ensures you get strong plants, whereas uncertified market seeds may fail to sprout or spread disease.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɔ dumɔwui kpakpai amli ni amɛhaa amɛhe odaseyeli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni helai bɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ ahemɔ haa onine shɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ekolɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgbɛ hela amɛshwã.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fall over easily when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light, making them tall, thin, and weak instead of growing strong stems.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná tsitsii ni wa.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension officials lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by soil-borne bacterial or fungal wilt that attacks the roots and blocks water from moving up the plant. Rotating your crops each season prevents these harmful germs from building up in your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii daa be lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabua amɛhe naa yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting any fruit during the hottest months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat and dry air as a survival mechanism to conserve water. Providing shade or adequate watering during hot periods helps the plants hold onto their blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni sa ha tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green or yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants use to build green foliage. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does growing groundnuts or beans on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, this natural fertilizer remains in the ground to nourish the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my yam crop yield small tubers when I plant in hard, packed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ naa bulbs bibii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing outward underground, so they need loose, deep soil to expand properly. Hard, compacted soil restricts tuber growth, leading to small, misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa bulb lɛ ada. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni efite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted on cleared land with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, full sunlight. Interplanting cocoa with shade crops like plantain or banana provides cover and keeps the air humid until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Cocoa ni akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shade tamɔ plantain loo banana baadu. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato ni ehi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the heat of the sun from drying out the ground. It keeps the soil cool and moist for longer, protecting crop roots and reducing the need for constant watering.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ebuɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it better to clear all the large forest trees before planting my new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaajie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ dani adu kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: No, cocoa trees need moderate shade to thrive, especially when young. Leaving select tall forest trees provides canopy shade, retains soil moisture, and protects cocoa leaves from severe sun damage and dry winds.
ga: Dabi, Cocoa tsei biɔ hulutsoo be ni sa koni amɛshwere. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ oji oblanyo fioo. Koo mli tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their productivity naturally declines and they become more susceptible to diseases. Pruning properly, applying recommended fertilizers, or gradually replanted hybrid seedlings helps maintain high farm yields.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, eyibii lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni helai nyɛɔ emɔɔ lɛ oya. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ nibii ni sa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii loo dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi fee lɛ adu fiofio lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers, but severe flower drop occurs when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollination by tiny midges. Maintaining shade and moist soil helps keep pollinating insects active.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji hɔmɔ miigba tsei anaa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo aŋkroaŋkroi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excessive standing water cuts off oxygen to the root system and encourages fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps drain rainwater away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop lacks nutrients before the leaves completely dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ mi-abele lɛ mli dani baai lɛ agbi kwraa?

english: When maize lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning yellow from the tips along the center vein. Identifying this early allows you to apply top-dress fertilizer before overall growth is stunted.
ga: Kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ haa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ woɔ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and split during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbalaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl during dry periods as a natural defense mechanism to reduce surface area and minimize water loss through evaporation. Mulching around the base with dry leaves keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ aba shi ni ekɛbaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same farm plot at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, leaving plenty of space and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to mature afterward.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ anyɛ eda sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young food crops after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsei lɛ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb sunlight, water, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks of planting gives your young crops the head start they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná shishijee ni amɛsumɔɔ.

english: Why does my soil become hard and dry quickly even after a short rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ waɔ ni egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo po lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter, causing rainwater to run off the surface instead of soaking in. Adding compost, organic manure, or crop residues improves soil structure and helps it hold moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, humus, loo tsei amli nibii ni efite fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo, ni ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Early leaf yellowing and drop in cocoa is usually caused by insect damage from pests like mirids (capsids), fungal root infection, or lack of soil moisture. Regular farm inspection and maintaining protective shade help keep leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii tamɔ mirids (capsids), ni ji fungal shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni feɔ ŋmeii mra kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and heavy rainfall, especially when trees are planted too close together and air cannot flow freely.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking the leaf sap, or by a virus transmitted by these insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miiho dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry prematurely when attacked by fungal diseases like anthracnose or when subterranean pests damage the roots, stopping water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baagbi oya kɛji ŋmeii helai tamɔ anthracnose tutua amɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Small insects called flower thrips often attack cowpea blossoms, damaging the flowers so severely that they fall off before forming pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ tutuaa cowpea fɔfɔii. Efiteɔ fɔfɔii waa aahu akɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the leaf tips inward when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build healthy green foliage.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the tubers underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn yellow starting from the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves die early from the bottom up when the plant lacks potassium in the soil or when root-damaging diseases prevent the uptake of water and nutrients.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperature stress is too high or watering is inconsistent, causing the plant to save energy rather than set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be mli haomɔ lɛ fa tsɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits split open right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon yibii lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they receive a sudden heavy rainfall or excess irrigation after a dry period, causing the fruit inside to expand faster than the outer skin.
ga: Watermelon baatswa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo nu babaoo yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Ehaa yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds away from my crops even when the weeds are not touching my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ mi tsei lɛ kpaaa gbee po.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizer from deep underground before your crop roots can reach them, while also harboring harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji shihilɛhe hu kɛha kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it safe to plant groundnuts together on the same field with my cassava?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts and cassava grow well together because groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil, which helps feed the cassava without stealing its growing space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ ŋmei ni ajuɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I mix different chemical fertilizers together in one bucket before applying them to my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afutu mli yɛ tanki kome mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Mixing certain fertilizers together can trigger a chemical reaction that ruins their essential nutrients or produces gas, making the mixture useless or harmful enough to burn your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi futu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ko ni fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ahiɛ loo ekɛ gas aba. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa loo nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I not put fresh chicken manure directly onto my young crop seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee woɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and produces heat and high levels of ammonia as it breaks down, which will burn fragile young roots and ruin your seedlings before they establish.
ga: Manɔ hee mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ammonia ni fa babaoo baa beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baashã shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛda.

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the stalks thin and weak, resulting in smaller cobs and a lower total yield.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa cob lɛ feɔ bibioo ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies carrying a virus into the plant. The virus alters the plant's internal growth, causing leaves to twist and stunting fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ hela ko ni ebote tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus tsakeɔ tsei amli dalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How do I know if the maize seeds I stored from last season are still alive and ready to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu?

english: Wrap ten sample seeds in a wet cloth for five days. If seven or more sprout healthy roots, your stored batch has good potential to grow well in your field.
ga: Akɛ mama ni mli efɔ ha dumɔwui nyɔŋma ni akɛfee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ gbii enumɔ. Kɛji shishifãi kpawo loo nɔ ni fe nakai ni mli wa kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mli Obatch ni ato lɛ yɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do people recommend cutting off some of the healthy side branches on tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ tomato tsei aniji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots stops the plant from wasting food on unnecessary leaves, forcing all its internal energy into producing larger and healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baa niyenii ni he ehiaaa lɛ fiteɔ. Enyɛɔ mligbɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Do weeds growing near my crop roots help shade the soil and keep water in?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli?

english: No, weeds act like thief plants that aggressively drink up soil water and steal nutrients and sunlight, starving your main crops and reducing your yield.
ga: Dabi, jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ nii, ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la. Hɔmɔ aye onibii titrii lɛ anɔ ni oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it up. Drooping is the plant's natural reaction to save water, and it usually recovers as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ koni ekɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plant turning yellow from the middle to the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller corn harvests every year if I plant it on the same plot continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same soil every season drains specific nutrients and lets soil pests build up. Changing crops each season—especially rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts—puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli Titri lɛ, ŋmãa yɛ tsakemɔ ni ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fata he lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because excess moisture cuts off air to the soil and encourages fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam plants need stakes to lift their foliage high into the sunlight, where leaves can manufacture food efficiently. When the leaves get plenty of sun, the plant sends more energy underground to swell the yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Baai lɛ baanyɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open field without tall crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under full sunshine. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that protect seedlings from harsh heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Young cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker should I pick from my old farm to plant a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sucker esa akɛ mahala kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu ŋmɔ hee?

english: You should pick 'maiden suckers'—which are young shoots with broad bases and narrow, sword-like leaves—because they have strong food reserves and establish faster than suckers with wide, mature leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘tsobii bibii’, ni ji tsei bibii ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ klante. Ejaakɛ eyɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni ekɛtoɔ, ni ebaanyɛ etswa ehe shi oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai wuji ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants experience stress from intense heat, dry soil, or extreme weather shifts. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the plant retain flowers and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on plant sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the foliage flat, green, and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes inside the central leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing center of maize plants. Checking your farm early and putting recommended organic or chemical powders into the plant funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ ateŋ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ organic powder loo tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kpaa ŋmɔji nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does covering my farm soil with dry leaves or grass help my crops during hot periods?
ga: Te baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plants—a practice called mulching—acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, preserves moisture, and prevents weeds from growing and competing with your crops.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ—tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by the strong sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide thick shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive its early stage.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli wa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eshishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained on wooden stakes instead of lying on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔse sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines lift their leaves toward the sun when staked. When the leaves get full sunlight, they produce maximum energy, which flows down to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he kɛ́ akɛwo tso nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ejieɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo ni tsii.

english: What happens if I bury my maize seeds very deep in the soil to protect them from birds?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni mikɛtsi okpoi anaa?

english: If maize seeds are planted too deep, they run out of energy before reaching the surface and die underground. Burying them just about a finger-joint deep is enough for them to shoot up safely.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Ehewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afu amɛ tsitsi kome pɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛtu tu kɛya ŋwɛi shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Adding fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he, loo aha nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or pest damage. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so tomatoes can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ miihao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tomatoi lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Does leaving weeds around my pepper plants really harm the crop if I am still watering them?
ga: releasing weeds around Ani pepper tso lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mitee nɔ mikɛ nu wo nɔ?

english: Yes, weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your pepper plants. They also hide insect pests and diseases that will jump onto your crop and reduce your yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baatu kɛba oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ hu teeɔ ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass help my vegetable crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mulching yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil, prevents weeds from sprouting, and keeps the roots cool during hot afternoons.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I trim off the lower branches and extra stems on my tomato bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ tsei ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming removes weak branches that waste plant energy without producing fruit. It also allows air to flow freely through the bush, preventing damp diseases from growing on the leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii lɛ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ hu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ jwɛi lɛ mli oya. Etsiɔ helai ni mli edɔ naa koni ekakwɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Will planting my cassava cuttings very close together give me more tubers at harvest time?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ baaha ŋmeii babaoo aba yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: No, planting cassava too close causes the plants to fight for sunlight and soil food, resulting in thin, tiny roots. Giving them proper space allows each plant to grow big, thick tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa bulbs agboi ni mli tse.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the ground and builds up maize-specific pests in the soil. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efee tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I use leftover farm waste and dry leaves to help my crops grow better without buying expensive fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi ni eshwɛ lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni miheee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can make compost by piling up farm waste like crop stalks, cassava peels, dry leaves, and animal manure. As these decay together over time, they turn into rich organic manure that feeds your soil, holds moisture, and improves crop yields naturally.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi tamɔ tsei ahe tsei, ŋmei, baai ni egbi, kɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni ooobua naa lɛ nɔ. Amɛbafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food crops need to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii fata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil to feed the maize, while the taller maize stalks give climbing bean plants support to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass on the soil around their young crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It acts like a blanket over the soil, keeping it cool under the hot sun, stopping water from drying up too fast, and preventing weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for planting after the dry season ends and the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until you get two or three good rains that soak deep into the dirt before sowing. Planting after just one light rain can cause your seeds to sprout and then quickly dry up and die if the sun stays hot.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni onine ashɛ nugbɔ kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu nii. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ lolo.

english: Crops wilt in the afternoon heat because their leaves lose water faster through the hot air than their roots can suck up from the ground. As long as the soil has moisture, the plants will usually bounce back once the sun sets and the air cools down.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ejaakɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Curled, sticky cassava leaves are often a sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mealybugs. Spraying the leaves with a mixture of water and ground neem leaves can help clear the insects naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni wa lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmeii ahe okadi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to turn black and rot at the bottom before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ dani ekwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Bottom rot on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Water your tomato plants consistently so the roots can move nutrients evenly into the fruit.
ga: Tomato shishi fitemɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aha aduawai lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of producing pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as severe afternoon heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving your plants steady water and light shade during extremely hot periods helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: How can I store my harvested maize seeds so that insects do not destroy them before the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite amɛ dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Make sure your maize seeds are completely dry before storing them in airtight bags or sealed containers. Mixing clean wood ash or dried pepper powder with the seeds helps keep insect pests like weevils away without using dangerous chemicals.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn kernels lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni akɛwo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ ni he tse loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi futu dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Why does maize seed brought from another region sometimes fail to grow well on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops adapt to the specific climate, rainfall, and soil type of the area where their seeds were developed. Moving seeds across regions can cause poor crop performance if local weather and soil conditions do not match what the plant expects.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ pɔtɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ he ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kpokpai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ kɛ nɔ ni tso lɛ kpaa gbɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from a recognized dealer instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni ale lɛ dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Certified seeds are inspected and tested to guarantee strong growth and high yields. Seeds saved from your own harvest lose their strength over time, making plants weaker and yields smaller.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛdara waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and grow strong leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants producing tassels early while they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmeii oya shi amɛji kuku lolo lɛ?

english: When a maize plant suffers from dry weather or heat stress, it thinks it is going to die. It rushes to produce flowers and seeds early to survive, prioritizing reproduction over tall growth.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei naa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo latsaa he haomɔ mli lɛ Esusu akɛ eegbo. Ekɛ oyaiyeli woɔ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui amli mra. koni amɛhi shi Amɛmaa fɔmɔ nɔ mi fe shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: If seeds are planted too close together, the crops stretch quickly upward to compete for light, creating tall but weak stems with shallow roots that easily collapse in wind.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya koni amɛye la he akaŋ. Efeɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ shi amɛhe waaa. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why are the central leaves of my young maize plants chewed up with dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛmli ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm infestation. The caterpillars hide inside the plant's growing center, eating the soft young leaves before they fully unroll.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm hela ko eba. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo kwraa.

english: Why do some of my crops rot on the farm right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Rot happens when excess moisture gets trapped inside the crop husk during humid or rainy weather. Fungal molds thrive in warm, wet conditions and quickly destroy mature grain.
ga: Rot baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bote tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Mold yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni eda lɛ oya.

english: How do crop inspectors decide if a diseased crop needs to be destroyed completely?
ga: Te mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛkpɛ amɛyiŋ kɛji ehe miihia ni akpata tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahiɛ kwraa?

english: Inspectors destroy infected crops when a disease is contagious and airborne, preventing pests or diseases from spreading to surrounding farms and destroying the region's food supply.
