ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii amli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ beni hela lɛ tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni efiteɔ

english: Why do some parts of my field produce big maize cobs while other parts have tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi miiwo ŋmãa wuji lɛ? be mli ni fãi krokomɛi Ayɛ ŋmãa bibioo ko?

english: Soil quality is not uniform across a field. Areas with poor drainage, low nutrients, or rocky soil prevent roots from taking up enough food, leading to uneven crop sizes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ ejaaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, loo shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dalɛi kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing grains instead of full rows of kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni elaaje yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ muu fɛɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels occur during the flowering stage when heat or drought prevents pollen from reaching every silk strand, leaving unpollinated spots on the cob empty.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛji latsaa loo hɔmɔ tsi pollen naa koni ekashɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ahe lɛ, Okɛ he fɛɛ he ni pollen bɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ afɔ shi.

english: Why is it important for me to consult an extension officer before planting my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ extension nitsulɔ ko agba sane dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Extension officers provide expert guidance on land preparation, proper planting distances, and modern farming methods, helping your cocoa trees grow healthy and produce maximum yields.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ haa ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ he. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi Yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni edara waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Where can I get reliable cocoa seeds or seedlings in Ghana that will yield a good harvest?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana kookoo yibii loo dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ Ghana ni baaha yibii kpakpai aba?

english: You can obtain certified, high-yielding cocoa seeds and seedlings directly from the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) nurseries or recognized cocoa research stations located in cocoa-growing areas.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kookoo yibii kɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) ŋmɔji loo kookoo niiamlitaomɔ hei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hei ni aduɔ kookoo yɛ lɛ.

english: How are improved cocoa varieties from research stations better than seeds from my own farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni jɛ wɔ diɛŋtsɛ wɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Seeds from cocoa research stations are specifically bred to grow faster, produce many more pods, resist common diseases, and start fruiting earlier than traditional farm seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ Cocoa Research Station lɛ mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Ha pods lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ. Enyɛɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anaa Ni ebɔi yibiiwoo oya fe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blema ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees should generally be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart so their roots have enough room for nutrients and their branches can spread without crowding each other out.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei lɛ aaafee mitai 3.3 bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni niji lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant cocoa seedlings on my land?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the beginning of the major rainy season (usually around May or June) so the young plants get steady water to build strong roots before dry weather comes.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Afeɔ enɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra (bei pii lɛ, yɛ May loo June mli) koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni hoɔ daa koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees to shield them during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted hybrid cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties from research centers usually start flowering and producing pods in about 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional varieties can take up to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 5.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plant is getting too much direct sunlight, lacks key soil nutrients, or is suffering from root damage or sap-sucking insect pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni efite loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ enaa enɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some small, young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This can happen naturally when the tree sheds excess pods it cannot feed (cherelle wilt), or it can be a sign of Black Pod disease caused by excess moisture and fungal infections during rainy periods.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye lɛ. (wilt disease) loo ebaanyɛ efee black pod hela ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi.

english: Should I apply fertilizer immediately after planting my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: No, you should wait a few months until the seedling establishes strong roots in the field, as applying strong fertilizer right away can scorch delicate young roots.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baatswa shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Can I plant my new cocoa trees right along the edge of the main road?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei heei yɛ gbɛjegbɛ wulu lɛ he?

english: It is better to leave a buffer space from the road. Dust, heat, exhaust fumes, and traffic disturbance along roadsides can dry out the leaves, damage young trees, and reduce your yield.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi he ko ni okɛ ohe wooo mli kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he. Muji, dɔlɛ, lasu ni jɛɔ tsɔne mli kɛ gbɛjegbɛ he tsɔnei ni baa lɛ mligbalamɔ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ agbi. kpata tsei bibii ahiɛ ni oha nibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to block the heat and keep the soil moist while the young trees grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What is the difference between traditional cocoa trees and the newer hybrid cocoa varieties?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ blema cacao kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli lɛ teŋ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees take about five to seven years to start producing fruit and grow very tall. Hybrid cocoa varieties grow faster, start bearing pods in about three years, stay shorter for easier harvesting, and yield more cocoa.
ga: Kusum tsei ni ji cacao lɛ heɔ aaafee afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi ni amɛdaraa waa. Kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya. Ejeɔ shishi efeɔ pods yɛ aaafee afii etɛ mli. Eyɛ be kukuoo ni baaha nikpamɔ afee mlɛo. ni amɛfee kookoo babaoo

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the tree roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding proper fertilizer or improving field drainage brings back healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oyale mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes the dark black spots that spread across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: Black spots are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, wet conditions. Trimming extra branches to let air and sunlight into the farm helps keep the pods dry and disease-free.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they are stressed by hot dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests. Proper watering, feeding the soil with fertilizer, and pest control help the flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Nu ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ mli Kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off branches from a cocoa tree if it looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo nine kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Cutting unwanted branches, called pruning, allows sunlight and fresh air to reach all parts of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to send its energy into growing bigger pods instead of useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni ataooo ni ajieɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ pruning lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amajeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni miida lɛ amli yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do tiny bugs like capsids damage my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids miifite mi-cocoe ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Capsids bite young cocoa stems and pods to suck out juices, leaving dark scars that stop the shoots from growing and cause pods to die. Spraying approved treatments at the right time protects your yield.
ga: Capsids lɛ ŋmɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ eshishifãi koni ekɛnu nu lɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmeii diji ni tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gboɔ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why must I cover and ferment my cocoa beans after harvesting instead of drying them right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni mafee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni akpa amɛkpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation develops the chocolate flavor and rich brown color that buyers look for. It stops the seed inside from sprouting and helps the beans dry properly so they do not spoil.
ga: Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ehaa enáa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkafite.

english: How can I protect my cocoa farm from dying during the long dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekagbo yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Placing dry leaves and plant material around the base of the cocoa trees, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground and keeps the roots cool through dry spells.
ga: Ale baai ni egbi kɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ Cocoa tso lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Maize turns yellow when it lacks key soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, which acts like food for the plant. Water helps the plant drink, but if the soil has no nutrients, the crop starves and cannot maintain its green leaf color.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nii. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ko lɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ ebaa lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli.

english: Why should I stop burning cleared bush on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa tsei ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ashãa dani madu?

english: Burning destroys the natural leaves and organic matter that feed the soil. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose creates rich compost that keeps the soil moist, fertile, and healthy for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe tsei kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do worm-like pests eat the tender leaf centers of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni tamɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworms lay their eggs in the center leaves (the whorl) because that spot is soft, safe from direct heat, and full of fresh nutrients, making it the easiest place for young pests to feed.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) ejaakɛ nakai he lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii heei Enɛ haa efeɔ he ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nii.

english: When cassava gets too much foliage growth or too much nitrogen from the soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to build thick tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ baa lɛ fa babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsu lɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak and thin, producing small or empty cobs instead of full ones.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Feemɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating, causing the plant to drop them to conserve water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. Ha tsei agbee shi koni nu akafite.

english: Yam rot happens when water gathers around the roots without draining away properly. Excess water creates a wet environment where soil fungi and bacteria thrive and break down the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato rot lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni etsɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the rainy seasons no longer starting at the same time every year like they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ ejeee shishi yɛ be kome mli daa afi tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Weather patterns are shifting overall due to changes in global climate. Rising temperatures alter wind and cloud movements, making old farming calendars unreliable without modern weather updates.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi fɛɛ miitsake yɛ jeŋ muu fɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsakeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ atatui lɛ agbɛfaa. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ okwaayeli kalanda momo lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji bɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to rotate our cassava fields with beans or groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them after heavy crops like cassava naturally restores nutrients to the soil so future crops grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ adara waa

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready to be harvested from my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer leaves surrounding the cob turn brown and dry, and the kernels become hard. If you press a kernel with your fingernail and no milky liquid comes out, it is mature enough to be harvested.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe. Kooloi lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbiɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kɛji okɛ onineshi tsɔne nyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni nu ko ni tamɔ mliki ejeee kpo, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: Why is it necessary to thoroughly dry my cocoa beans right after harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-kookoo lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans reduces their moisture so mold cannot grow during storage. It also stops the beans from rotting and allows the rich flavor and dark color to develop, which buyers look for.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ shwereee yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hu fiteɔ, ni ehaa amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense heat to conserve water and protect themselves from burning. As long as the soil has water, the leaves will usually bounce back and stand tall when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ nu lɛ Baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks water. Ensuring the soil stays consistently moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean your cassava plant is running low on essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or is experiencing water stress. Adding organic compost around the base helps supply nutrients and retain moisture.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ. Organic compost ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ haa enine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: When maize is planted too closely, the stalks fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to weak, thin plants that produce smaller ears and a much lower overall yield.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ toi bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cowpeas and maize grow very well together. Cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which nourishes the maize while maximizing your land space.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why are white powdery spots appearing on the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are usually caused by a fungal infection triggered by high humidity and poor airflow around plants. Spacing your plants wider allows wind to pass through and keep leaves dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ mli baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni tamɔ powder yɛŋ. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni da lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my young crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that suck up rainwater and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Removing weeds early ensures your young crops get the water and food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a strong first harvest. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation will grow unevenly and produce much smaller cobs with significantly lower yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ ni mli wa. Kɛji okɛto ni odu ekoŋŋ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do people recommend that I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa plants need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same piece of land as my plantains without harming my yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them, but you must space them properly so that cassava's heavy root system does not compete with the shallow roots of plantains for nutrients and water.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei awo mli. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi ni tsii lɛ kɛ plantain shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ akashi akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu.

english: What causes the leaves of my plantain plants to turn yellow and dry up before bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛwo yibii?

english: This is often caused by leaf spot diseases or fungal infections like Panama disease, which block water flow inside the stem. Proper field sanitation and planting disease-resistant suckers help prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa mli ŋmɔtɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela, tamɔ Panama hela, ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ hetsemɔ ni sa kɛ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: If I see that one plantain plant on my farm is sick, should I leave it to recover or cut it down?
ga: Kɛji mina dumɔwui ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekome hela mɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ maha etsa loo mafo lɛ?

english: It is best to uproot and destroy diseased plants immediately away from the field. Crop diseases spread quickly through air, soil, or tools to healthy plants if left untreated.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ kɛji amɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, shikpɔŋ, loo nitsumɔ dadei anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: How do I select healthy plantain suckers so I do not bring pests to my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui aba miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli

english: Choose strong 'sword suckers' with narrow leaves, peel off the outer roots to check for black spots or insect holes, and avoid suckers from fields that already show signs of disease.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni wa ni eyɛ baai bibii. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii diji loo kooloi bibii yɛ mli. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmɔji amli ni miitsɔɔ hela he okadii momo lɛ ahe.

english: How far apart am I supposed to plant my plantain suckers in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting them about 3 meters apart gives each plant enough room to receive sunlight, gather soil nutrients, and produce large bunches without competing with its neighbors.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la. Bua niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ofee ŋmeii wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ.

english: Is there a simple way to stop stem weevils from destroying my plantain stems?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ nɔ akpa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ?

english: You can use clean suckers free of pests, keep the base of plants clear of decaying leaves, and set simple stem traps made from cut plantain pseudostems to attract and catch the beetles.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni kooloi bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Ha tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni baai ni egboi akafee nɔ ko. ni okɛ tsei ahe tsɔnei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛfee tsei ni afolɔ ni akɛ niji fee koni akɛgbala ŋmeii kɛba ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over during strong wind and rain, and how do I prevent this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. You can prevent lodging by propping up heavy bunches with sturdy wooden poles or bamboos.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. cause a lot weight Obaanyɛ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni wa ni akɛwo mli lɛ afee shĩa lɛ mli la.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains consume a lot of nutrients from the ground. Continuous planting without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer depletes the soil and reduces fruit size over time.
ga: Dares yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ ayibɔ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell the exact time my plantains are ready to harvest so they do not rot on the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-plantains lɛ esa akɛ akpa? Koni tso lɛ akafite?

english: Harvest plantains when the individual fingers look plump and full, and the sharp ridges on the skin start to smooth out, but while the skin is still green.
ga: Kpãa plantains beni nine fɛɛ nine feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shi be mli ni hewolo lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ

english: Why do my sweet potato leaves turn yellow and rot underground when the soil gets too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the crop's roots, preventing them from breathing oxygen. Without oxygen, the tubers begin to rot underground, and the plant cannot take up food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ naa Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Tubers lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does putting too much chicken manure make my cassava grow tall with leafy stems but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmeii babaoo wo mi-cassava lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa mi-cassava lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ baai shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is very rich in nitrogen, which tells the plant to focus all its energy on building green leaves and tall stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots to grow big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ kɛɛ tso lɛ akɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ woɔ tso a sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a kɛ bulb tso nguahi nɛ a wa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The tomato plant rolls its leaves to hide their surface from the scorching sun and trap a small pocket of moisture, preventing the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛtee hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko ahi mli. Koni tomato tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any peppers during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee pepper yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the soil is too dry or the air is too hot, the plant enters survival mode. It drops its blossoms to save its limited water and energy for staying alive rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ato he koni ehi shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii heei.

english: How do I test my field soil with my hands to know if it is wet enough to plant potatoes at the start of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ minine aka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Squeeze a ball of soil in your palm. If it forms a firm ball that crumbles easily when you poke it with a finger without leaking water, the soil has the right balance of moisture and air for planting.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ onine nɔ. Kɛji akɛ efee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kokroo. Efoɔ oya kɛ́ okɛ onine tsɔ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do roaming cattle focus on eating my young tender maize instead of the fully grown stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsinayei ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa mi-ŋmei bibi lɛ yeli nɔ moŋ fe ŋmeii ni eda lɛ?

english: Young maize plants are soft, sweet, water-rich, and easy for cows to chew and digest. Mature stalks become tough, woody, and low in nutrients, making them much less appealing to grazing livestock.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Ni tsinai yeɔ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ mlɛo. Tsoi ni eda lɛ wa, amɛji tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa. Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly attack my green maize fields right after the dry spell breaks and heavy rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni hulutsoo be lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay eggs right before rains. When warm rain arrives, all the eggs hatch together, and the newly born caterpillars flood the fresh, soft green leaves that grow rapidly after the dry spell.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii dani nugbɔ nɛɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ba lɛ, ŋmeii fɛɛ baafee ekome kɛfɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni afɔɔ amɛ ehee lɛ shwieɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together in the field, won't I harvest more food from the same land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely causes the crops to fight each other for limited groundwater, sunlight, and soil food. This competition leaves all the plants weak, short, and producing smaller yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa nitsumɔhei fɛɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ, amɛhe feɔ kuku, ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field leave the soil richer for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in their roots to take nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil, creating free natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains start sprouting and forming white mold inside the storage sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii yɛŋ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: If maize is bagged before it is completely dried in the sun, trapped internal moisture creates heat and humidity inside the closed sack, causing seeds to wake up and mold spores to bloom.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli dani egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ mli ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi ni ŋmei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay green and build energy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin without giving good yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The plants stretch upward to catch sun rays instead of using their energy to grow strong stems and fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, tsei lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛná hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer from your field before the plant roots can drink it in. This wastes your money and can also burn young roots if the fertilizer dissolves too fast all at once.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ shikome.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ koni bulbs wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves are like tiny solar panels that make food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines so all leaves get full sunlight and fresh air, which gives the plant maximum energy to build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small flowers before the pods even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani pods lɛ po feɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers if they do not have enough water or nutrients to support full pods. It is the tree's natural way of saving energy so it does not die from overload.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛkagboi yɛ jatsu ni fa fe nine hewɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over hundreds of years to survive in harsh conditions. Their roots are stronger and faster at stealing water and nutrients from the soil than domesticated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei dumɔwui.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a reaction to extreme heat, lack of water, or attack by tiny pests like whiteflies that spread plant viruses. The plant curls its leaves to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ tutuamɔ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain fills all the small spaces in the dirt for too long, the roots drown and soil fungi attack the weakened tubers, causing them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehaa kpokpaa bibioo ko nɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. ha egbo

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their leaves suddenly after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop leaves under sudden stress, such as a sharp shift from wet to dry weather or severe pest damage to the root system. The plant sheds leaves to reduce water loss and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ haomɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ shishi, tamɔ tsakemɔ ni baa oya kɛjɛɔ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ kɛyaa shihilɛ ni mli egbi mli. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sun heat and harsh winds. Large trees act as natural umbrellas that keep the air cool and moist around young cocoa plants while their roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant cannot produce food efficiently, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow from the leaf tips inwards.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, it matters a lot. Cassava stems have small buds that point upwards; if planted upside down, the shoots must bend unnaturally to reach sunlight, which wastes energy and severely reduces your tuber yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia. Kasava tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛji akɛ adu lɛ etsɔɔ shishi. Esa akɛ abɔle tsei lɛ ahe yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to filter the heat, the sun scorches the leaves and dries out the soil, killing the young seedlings.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baajie dɔlɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii lɛ agbele.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress from irregular watering or severe heat. Keeping the soil consistently damp helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves into the sunlight to make energy for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases and leads to bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there looks like enough space in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Even if space seems available, weed roots aggressively steal water and soil nutrients under the ground, while their leaves block sunlight above, starving your main crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ko yɛ po Shi jwɛi shishifãi lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant juices. Spraying with natural neem oil or appropriate insecticide solves this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring its fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base—are best because they have strong roots and produce fast-growing plants with large bunches compared to broad-leafed water suckers.
ga: Klante ni akɛmuɔ nii ni ŋmeii lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ. Amɛhi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ kui wuji kɛ akɛto tsei ni shwieɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do people advise me to cover the base of my crop plants with dried leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi aha mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter, called mulching, traps moisture in the soil so it stays wet longer during hot days, prevents weed growth, and eventually turns into fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo

english: Do crops need different kinds of nutrients to stay healthy and fight off diseases?
ga: Niyenii srɔtoi he miihia tsei. Koni mɔ ko ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ helai awuu?

english: Yes, just like people, crops need balanced nutrition. Some nutrients help plants build strength to fight off sickness and diseases, while others give them the energy needed to grow big and produce good yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, tamɔ adesai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niyenii ni ja he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Niyenii mli nibii komɛi yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai kɛ helai. Yɛ be mli ni niyenii mli nibii komɛi haa tsei hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but crops also need nutrients from the soil to thrive. When the soil lacks essential nutrients, plants cannot get energy or protect themselves, causing them to turn yellow and become sickly.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi ŋmɔshi nii hu hia niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ana hewalɛ loo amɛbu amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hela mɔɔ amɛ.

english: Can feeding my soil properly stop my crops from falling sick?
ga: Ani niyenii ni mikɛhaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaye hela?

english: Yes, well-nourished plants have stronger natural immunity. Supplying the soil with the right nutrients helps plants resist common crop diseases and recover faster if attacked.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni yeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ. Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ oya kɛji akɛ atutua amɛ.

english: How do crops get the energy they need to grow and yield well?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛnáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Crops generate energy by taking up nutrients and water from the soil through their roots and absorbing sunlight through their leaves, which fuels their growth and fruit production.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni amɛgbalaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbalaa hulu la kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. ni haa aduawai lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛfeemɔ yaa hiɛ

english: What benefit does elephant grass provide if I cut it to feed my animals?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ shwuɔ jwɛi he kɛji ofolɔ koni okɛha kooloi niyenii?

english: Elephant grass is a fast-growing feed that gives farm animals energy and contains about 3 to 5 percent protein, which helps keep livestock healthy and strong.
ga: Shɔ jwɛi ji niyenii ni daa oya ni haa kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ, ni protein aaafee oha mlijaa 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is natural grass just filler for livestock, or does it actually nourish them?
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi ji nɔ ko kɛkɛ ni akɛwoɔ kooloi amli. Aloo ehaa amɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Grass is not just filler; pasture grasses like elephant grass contain essential protein and energy that nourish animals and help them grow body weight.
ga: Jwɛi jeee nɔ ko kɛkɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Koolooi aniyenii jwɛi tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ protein kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni haa kooloi niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ muji.

english: Why should I bother planting elephant grass on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu shwuɔ jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Elephant grass yields high amounts of leafy growth quickly, providing a reliable source of protein-rich fodder for farm animals while helping control weed growth on your farm.
ga: Shɔji jwɛi lɛ haa baai babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa. Eji niyenii ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if the grass on my farm is nutritious enough for my animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpa ni sa kɛha mikooloi lɛ?

english: Nutritious grasses like elephant grass provide moderate protein (around 3 to 5 percent) and good energy levels, which you can see when your livestock remain active, heavy, and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi lɛ haa protein ni fa bɔ ni sa (aaafee oha mlijaa 3 kɛyashi 5) kɛ hewalɛ kpakpa. Anaa enɛ kɛji okooloi lɛ tee nɔ amɛtsu nii, amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa.

english: What actually happens inside a crop when it receives proper plant food?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ aha lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ?

english: When a crop gets proper food, it uses specific nutrients to build green leaves, boost root growth, protect against sickness, and convert sunlight into growth energy.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni sa lɛ Tsei kɛ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ daa, etsiɔ helai anaa, ni etsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ mli kɛha dalɛ.

english: What makes some plants on the farm grow very fast while others remain small?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Plants grow fast when they can easily draw nutrients and energy from rich soil. Smaller or stunted plants are usually struggling with poor soil nutrition or underlying plant sickness.
ga: Tsei daa oya kɛji amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ mli mlɛo. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni darako loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ naa sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo tsei ahe helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ shoo lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil so fast if I store it right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested corn still contains a lot of water inside the grains. If you store it while wet, heat and mold build up quickly inside the pile, causing the corn to rot. Drying removes this extra water so the grain stays good for months.
ga: Abɛi ni akpaa lɛ yɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lolo. Kɛji akɛ okɛto be mli ni edɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa oya yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know when my harvested maize is dry enough to safely put into storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto shweshweeshwe?

english: You can test it by biting a grain or pressing it with your thumbnail; if it leaves a dent or feels soft, it is still wet inside. Dry maize should be hard, crack cleanly when bitten, and make a sharp clicking sound when you rattle a handful together.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwu ko ni oootsɔ mli loo okɛ o-thumbnail lɛ anyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee ŋmeii loo enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Etsɔɔ akɛ emli lɛ mli edɔ lolo. Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa. Efoɔ ehe kɛji akɔmɔ lɛ. ni efeɔ gbee ni naa wa waa Beni ekpokpoɔ nine

english: Why does my shelled corn dry much faster when I spread it in a thin layer instead of keeping it in a big heap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni ajie lɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa kɛ́ migbɛ eshwa ŋmãa bibioo mli moŋ fe ni mabua naa yɛ ŋmãa agbo mli lɛ?

english: Air and warmth need to touch every single grain to carry away moisture. When corn is piled high, air only reaches the top layer, trapping wet air inside the middle of the pile where mold can start growing.
ga: Esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ latsaa ata ŋmei fɛɛ ŋmei he koni ejie fɛ̃i. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ pɛ he. Emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋtayaa baanyɛ aje shishi eda lɛ.

english: Will drying my maize with strong heat damage the grains if I want to plant them as seeds next season?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baafite dumɔwui lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni madu lɛ akɛ dumɔwui yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, if the drying heat gets too high, it kills the tiny living embryo inside the seed, which means it will not sprout when planted. Gentle, controlled heat dries the grain safely while keeping the seed alive for planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ la ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ. Ebaagbe fɔmɔ kotokui bibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ. yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ, ekwɛŋ. Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni akudɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why does my harvested grain get warm and feel hot inside the bag when left sitting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni edɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛ́ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains are actually still living tissues that breathe and release moisture. When packed tightly in a bag, that trapped moisture and natural activity create heat, which will cause spoilage if the grain is not dried first.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ ji fãji ni hiɛ ka lolo ni muɔ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ akɛwo kotoku mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔi haa dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afite kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: What causes that dark mold and sour smell on my stored corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele ŋmɔtɔ ni mikɛto lɛ nɔ lɛ baa?

english: That dark mold comes from microscopic fungi that thrive on moisture. When corn is stored before it is fully dry, or placed in a damp room without good airflow, these fungi grow rapidly and turn into mold.
ga: Mold ni tsuɔ waa lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ooto ŋmãa dani egbi kwraa Aloo okɛwo tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do small beetles start eating my corn after it has been sitting in the storehouse for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɔi mi-ŋmei lɛ yeli beni ehi nitoohe lɛ otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils are attracted to the moisture and smell of grain, often laying invisible eggs on the cobs while in the field. Warmth and hidden dampness in the storehouse cause those eggs to hatch into hungry bugs that eat the grain from the inside.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli fɛ̃i kɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ beni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly and turn yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot and there is no rain, maize leaves roll up to trap moisture and stop water from evaporating out of the plant. If the hot weather continues without water, the leaves turn yellow because the plant cannot make food.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tee nɔ edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii.

english: Why do some of my corn grains start sprouting right on the cob before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: If continuous heavy rain falls when the corn is fully ripe, the water soaking into the husk tricks the mature grain into thinking it has been planted in wet soil, causing it to break out of its shell and sprout early.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tee nɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, Nu ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni eda lɛ susuɔ akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbálaa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the ground, water fills all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing rot bacteria to break them down.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ, eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Rain often washes nitrogen deep into the soil, so applying fertilizer or organic manure helps restore the plant's green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ nɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aná su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to cover the soil around our vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle wɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella and blanket combined. It keeps the ground cool under the hot Ghanaian sun, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and turns into rich organic soil food as it rots.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade kɛ blanket ni akɛfee ekome. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right part of a cassava stem to cut and plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best stem cuttings come from the middle section of a mature, healthy plant that is 8 to 12 months old. The top branches are too weak and dry out quickly, while the bottom base is too woody and slow to sprout.
ga: Niji ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ jɛɔ tso ko ni eda ni ehe wa ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ lɛ ji tso tsɔ ni edaa blɛoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava and maize too close together in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight like children over a single plate of food. They compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, which makes both the maize ears small and the cassava roots tiny.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baawuu tamɔ gbekɛbii. yɛ niyenii kome mli Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibii kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ bibii.

english: Why did many of my bean seeds fail to sprout after I planted them last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean dumɔwui babaoo lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ otsi ni eho lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil is too dry for them to wake up, or if the ground is so soaked in water that the seeds rot before sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ete shi Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do I need to drive long wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tsei kakadaji lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants produce tubers based on how much sunshine their leaves can catch. Staking lifts the vines high off the wet ground so leaves get maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii yɛ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ baanyɛ aná lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: During hot afternoons, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground, causing temporary wilting. If they bounce back in the evening cool, the plant is simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of shade, or when beneficial tiny insects (midges) are not present to pollinate the blossoms. Insect pests like mirids can also damage young flower buds.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hɔmɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hao amɛ. ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids hu baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my young papaya fruits turning yellow and falling off the tree before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop in papaya is usually caused by fruit flies laying eggs inside the fruit or fungal infections brought by damp air. It can also happen if the tree doesn't get enough water or fertilizer while carrying too much fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ papaya aduawai ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji tso lɛ náaa nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that easily burn and die under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and form broad leaves that create living shade to keep young cocoa cool and moist until it gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa koni eha kookoo bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or turn moldy when I keep it inside bags in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli yɛ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize traps moisture inside bags if it is not completely dried before storage. That trapped moisture creates heat and fungal mold, so you must dry the grains in the sun until they crack when bitten before putting them in bags.
ga: Abɛi lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaagbala kɛji okɛ lɛ ŋmɔ dani okɛwo kotoku mli.

english: What is a grain silo and how does it keep my stored maize safer than keeping it on the floor?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmaa silo? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ afee shweshweeshwe fe nɔ ni mikɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A silo is an enclosed metal, plastic, or concrete container designed to protect stored grains from moisture, rats, and insects. Keeping maize off the open floor stops dampness from seeping into the crop and prevents pests from attacking it.
ga: Silo ji dade, plastic, loo kɔnkrit tsinsii ko ni akɛwo mli ni akɛbuɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ kpaa, ni ehaaa ŋmãa lɛ akatutua ŋmãa lɛ.

english: How do tiny insects get inside my dried maize bags even when I tie the tops tightly?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko bote mi-ŋma ni egbi kotoku lɛ mli? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ yitsei lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ.

english: Weevil eggs are often already laid inside the maize grains while the crop is still standing in the field. Tying the bag keeps outside insects away, but the eggs already inside hatch into bugs unless the grain is properly treated or stored in airtight hermetic bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ ŋmeii amli momo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ahe. Shi wɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii. Ja akwɛ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: Why do maize prices usually go up several months after the harvest season is over in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa jara yaa hiɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ beni kpamɔ be lɛ egbe naa yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Right after harvest, almost every farmer is selling maize, so there is plenty of grain in the market and prices drop. Months later, most farmers have sold out their stocks while buyers still need food, so scarcity drives the market price up.
ga: kpamɔ sɛɛ Aaafee okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo hɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmaa babaoo yɛ jara lɛ nɔ ni ejara ba shi. Nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Okwaafoi babaoo hɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni niyenii he miihia mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ lolo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni anaaa lɛ haa jara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I tell that my maize crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn dry and light brown, the cobs turn downward, and the grains become hard with a tiny dark spot appearing at the base of each grain.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni baai lɛ egbi ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Akɛ cob lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shishi. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize plant lacks key nutrients, particularly nitrogen. When the soil is poor or heavy rains wash away nutrients, the plant cannot produce its natural green color and needs fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiii loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ. Tsei nyɛŋ afee amɛ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ, ni amɛbaabi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of growing thick stems and large cobs, they spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the sun.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to store freshly harvested maize cobs immediately without drying them first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ ato? No hewɔ lɛ, amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni agbiko lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ehiii.

english: Freshly harvested maize contains a high level of water inside the grain. Storing wet maize encourages toxic mold called aflatoxin to grow, which makes the food dangerous to eat and lowers its market value.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛtoɔ nu mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii lɛ feɔ oshara kɛ́ aye. ni eha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do grain traders in the market pay less money for maize that has dark spots or insect holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii amli lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Traders pay less because damaged maize weighs less, ground flour made from it tastes poor, and the grains spoil quickly during storage. Clean, unbroken grains command higher prices because they last longer and produce better food.
ga: Jarayelɔi woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni efite lɛ tsiimɔ waaa. Ashikiŋsha ni akɛ ŋmãa fee lɛ ŋɔɔ waa. Ni ŋmaa fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ŋmãa ni he tse ni akumɔko lɛ jara wa waa ejaakɛ ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii kpakpa baa.

english: Why does strong rain cause my mature maize plants to fall over flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mi-abele tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soften the soil and add extra weight to the tops of the plants. If the roots are weak or the soil becomes too muddy, strong winds easily push the heavy plants over because the ground can no longer hold the roots firm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ muji baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tsei waa. Amɛgbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shishifãi lɛ shiŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for healthy leaf growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my farm soil turn hard and crusty like stone after rain dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil compacts and bakes hard when it lacks organic matter and is exposed to direct heat. Adding compost, dry leaves, or crop residues softens the soil, allows air to circulate, and helps it retain moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe wo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai ni egbi, loo tsei amli nibii ni etse lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruit shows up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ, ni akɛ mulch aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are tiny green bugs clustering under my pepper leaves and causing them to curl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Those tiny bugs are aphids that suck the sap out of soft leaves, causing them to wrinkle and curl up. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps wash them away and protect the plant.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ tso lɛ he ni ebu he.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize crop during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars target the tender inner leaves of maize because they are soft and full of moisture. Inspecting plants early and applying neem extracts or recommended insecticides into the central leaf funnel stops them.
ga: Fall caterpillars lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa mli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ baakpa amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the leaves look large and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, cassava plants spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding tubers underground. Loosening the soil deep enough and using balanced nutrients encourages big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ mlɛo tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni akɛ niyenii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaawo bulbs wuji lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves fold up like cups during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in the hot sun as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation. If they open back up in the cooler evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Kɛji amɛgbele ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ koni ekagbi.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi tso bibioo lɛ Ni eji bibioo lolo?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early ensures your crop gets all the resources it needs to establish a strong root system.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. Data mli saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishifã ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit. Planting suckers deep enough, mounding soil around the base, and using wooden props to support fruiting trees prevents them from tipping over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ. Dumɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa, ni okɛ sũ ato shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest give me smaller yields than new packaged seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo mli ehee lɛ?

english: Commercial packaged seeds are often hybrid varieties bred specifically for high yield and vigor in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special yield traits in the second generation, resulting in smaller crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai yibiiwoo sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees turn yellow and weak when water sits on my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa beni nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa roots need air to breathe just like they need water. When water pools around the roots for too long without draining, the roots rot and cannot absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the tree to weaken.
ga: Cocoa shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my land holds too much water to grow healthy cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa tsɔ ni manyɛ madu kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: If rainwater stays pooled on top of the dirt for several days instead of soaking in, or if the soil feels like heavy, sticky clay that stays soggy, the land holds too much water for cocoa roots to survive.
