ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi ni edɔ lolo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How does digging shallow drainage channels help my cocoa farm during the wet season?
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ mlifomɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye abua kookoo ŋmɔji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Shallow channels give excess rainwater a clear path to flow off your land instead of settling around tree trunks, which prevents root rot while still keeping the surrounding soil naturally moist.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Is it good to install pipe irrigation systems in my cocoa farm to keep it watered all year?
ga: Ani ebaafee jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makɛ paipii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ awo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛ nu aba afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Standard pipe irrigation works well for vegetables, but cocoa farms in forest areas usually struggle with structured pipes because tree roots and uneven land break them. Cocoa relies more on natural soil moisture, proper shade, and rainfall.
ga: Nu ni akɛ paipii tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa aduawai. Shi bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ kooi amli lɛ kɛ naagbai kpeɔ yɛ paipii ni akɛfee tsɔne lɛ he ejaakɛ tsei shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ ŋwɛi lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Cocoa damɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ babaoo

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees in open, orderly rows without any big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tso yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ fɛo ni tsei wuji ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Open, neat layouts expose young cocoa trees to direct sunlight and hot winds, which dry out the soil quickly. Cocoa naturally grows best under the partial canopy of larger trees that mimic a forest environment.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ tsei ni eda ni kaseɔ koo mli shihilɛ lɛ fã ko shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cassava or plantain together with my young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ kookoo bibii du ŋmei loo plantain lɛ?

english: Planting fast-growing crops alongside cocoa creates a natural forest environment where tall plants shield young cocoa from intense sun and wind while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli koo shihilɛ baa. Tsei kakadaji buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight. Without shade trees to block the intense sun rays, the leaves dry up and die from extreme heat exposure.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the shade trees on my farm become too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ beni tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: While cocoa needs shade, too much canopy blocks the sunlight cocoa leaves need to make food and flowers. Overly thick shade also traps cool, damp air that encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia Cocoa. Shi ŋwɛi ŋta ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa kookoo baai koni akɛfee niyenii kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ naa. Shade babaoo hu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before pods can form when the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, cocoa trees experience stress and shed their flowers to save energy and water so the tree itself can survive the dry period.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Cocoa tsei kɛ haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast in my cocoa farm during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod fungus thrives in warm, wet air and standing moisture. Raindrops splash fungal spores from wet soil onto lower pods, and humid conditions help the disease infect the pods quickly.
ga: Black pod fungus lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ daa lɛ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Which months of the year mark the beginning of the palm nut season?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli ji nɔ ni akɛ ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii be lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: The early part of the year, from February to June, marks the beginning of the palm nut season before the main yield comes in.
ga: Afi lɛ shishijee, kɛjɛ February kɛyashi June, ji ŋmei be lɛ shishijee dani ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baa.

english: When in the year should I expect the largest amount of palm nuts to be ready on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ ŋmei ni fa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafee klalo akɛ aye afi nɛɛ?

english: The peak production of palm nuts really comes in right after the first period of the year, which ends around June.
ga: Palm nut ni ajieɔ lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ baa yɛ afi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ sɛɛ, ni gbeɔ naa yɛ June mli.

english: Can I expect a full, heavy harvest of palm nuts during the first few months from February to June?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni tsii gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ February kɛyashi June lɛ amli?

english: The period between February and June is just the start of the fruiting work; the heaviest harvest comes after June.
ga: Be ni kã February kɛ June teŋ lɛ ji yibiiwoo shishijee kɛkɛ. Nikpamɔ ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ baa yɛ June sɛɛ.

english: Why am I seeing fewer palm nuts on my trees as the harvest season progresses?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmei tsei fioo komɛi yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: After the main peak period passes, palm nut production naturally declines, causing fewer nuts to mature at the same time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ho lɛ, Palm nut feemɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hoɔ fioo yɛ be kome too mli.

english: How often should I go out to harvest my palm nuts when the trees start producing less?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mayaje kpo kɛyakpa ŋmeii beni ŋmei tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When palm nut yields begin to decline, you can adjust your routine to harvest every two or three weeks to collect what has matured.
ga: Beni ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi lɛ Obaanyɛ otsake bɔ ni okɛkpaa nii lɛ be fɛɛ be. Otsii enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛkpaa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do some oil palm farmers wait up to three weeks between harvests during certain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu-ŋmɔlɔi komɛi mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ otsii etɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Farmers wait two to three weeks during the declining phase because the trees are producing nuts at a slower rate, making frequent harvesting unnecessary.
ga: Okwaafoi mɛɔ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ baa shi lɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii blɛoo. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni akpa nikpamɔ shii abɔ.

english: If my palm nut harvest drops off, does that mean my trees have completely stopped bearing fruit?
ga: Kɛji mi-palm yibii ni mikpaa lɛ ba shi lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ mitso lɛ ekpa yibiiwoo kwraa?

english: No, a drop in yield only means production is declining; if you look closely at the trees, you will see that palm nuts are still present.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baa shi lɛ tsɔɔ nibii ni afee lɛ baa shi pɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, obaana akɛ tɛŋ tsei yɛ jɛmɛ lolo.

english: How can I tell if a palm tree still has fruit when total production is going down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ko woɔ yibii lolo beni ajie yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ shi lɛ?

english: Even when overall production drops, inspecting the tree branches closely will reveal remaining palm nuts that are still available for harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ eba shi moŋ Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ niji lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, obaana ŋmei yibii ni eshwɛ ni esa akɛ akpa lolo lɛ.

english: Does a decrease in palm nut yields happen suddenly or gradually over time?
ga: Ani ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ ji trukaa loo fiofio yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Palm nut production decreases gradually; as yields decline, you will notice fruit ripening slowly enough that harvesting is only needed every two to three weeks.
ga: Palm nut ni afeɔ lɛ miiba shi fiofio; Kɛji akɛ nibii ni afee lɛ ba shi lɛ Obaana akɛ aduawai lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ.

english: What overall pattern should I expect from my palm trees from the start of the year to the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-palm tsei lɛ fɛɛ baafee kɛjɛ be lɛ shishijee kɛyashi naagbee?

english: Palm trees start producing in the first part of the year (February to June), reach their heaviest output right after that, and then gradually decline, yielding smaller harvests every two to three weeks.
ga: Palm tsei jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ mli. (February kɛyashi June) ni ebaawo yibii babaoo yɛ no sɛɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaa shi fiofio, ni ebaaha nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa be fɛɛ be. otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ

english: Why do some yam varieties like 'Nyame' fetch higher prices at the market than other yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi tamɔ ‘Nyame’ lɛ jara wa fe ŋmeii srɔtoi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different yam varieties have distinct textures, taste, shelf life, and cooking qualities that consumers prefer. Varieties that stay firm, taste better, or store longer without spoiling command higher market demand and better prices.
ga: Atomɔ henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha, enaa ŋɔɔ, kɛ be ni akɛtoɔ shĩa mli. kɛ niyeli sui srɔtoi ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ Varieties ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni ŋɔɔ, loo ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee. Enɛ haa jarayeli nibii babaoo kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do crop prices fall so low right when my yams are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Crop prices drop when many farmers harvest and bring the same produce to the market at the same time. When supply is much higher than buyer demand, traders reduce prices, so harvesting slightly earlier or storing crops for later can bring better profits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jara baa shi kɛ́ okwaafoi babaoo kpa ni amɛkɛ nibii ni amɛdu lɛ nɔŋŋ ba jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa babaoo fe nɔ ni hɔlɔ lɛ biɔ lɛ. Jarayelɔi baa jara shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mra fioo loo akɛto koni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai aba.

english: Why does crop disease keep spreading on my farm even after I cut off the sick leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mifolɔ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop diseases are often caused by microscopic fungi, bacteria, or viruses that live inside the plant tissues or in the soil. Simply cutting off visible leaves does not clear pathogens already inside the stem or soil, allowing the disease to continue spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei bibii, muawai, loo muawai ni hiɔ tso mli loo sũ mli kɛ tsei helai baa. Baai ni anaa lɛ ni afolɔ kɛkɛ ejieee helai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Can farm workers spread plant diseases between crops using their hands or cutlasses?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛniji loo dadei agbɛ tsei ahe helai ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: Yes, many plant diseases spread easily through direct contact. When you touch a sick plant or cut it with a cutlass, disease spores stick to your hands and tools, which then infect healthy plants when you work on them next.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni akɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ. Kɛ ota tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ he loo okɛ tsɔne ŋmɔ lɛ Hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ oniji kɛ odɛŋdadei ahe. Enɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná hela be kroko ni okɛ amɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why does disease stay in my soil even during the dry season when no crops are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela lɛ hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli po ni aduuu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Many disease-causing organisms form tough protective coats or survive inside old crop roots left in the ground. They lie dormant in the dry soil and wake up to attack new plants as soon as the rains return.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni kɛ helai baa lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he waa loo amɛhiɔ shi yɛ tsei shishifãi momo ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Amɛkãa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni amɛteɔ shi koni amɛtutua tsei heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for their underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, improves air movement to prevent disease, and helps the tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo

english: Why do my crops produce big green leaves but very small tubers underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi bulbs bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and thick green leaves instead of feeding the underground tubers. Balanced nutrients, especially potassium, are needed for strong tuber development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. niyenii ni ja titri lɛ potassium He miihia kɛha yitso ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops get diseased more easily when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai baanyɛ aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close restricts airflow and traps moisture around the leaves for long periods. Damp, shaded leaves create ideal conditions for fungal diseases to grow and spread rapidly from plant to plant.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. baai lɛ be kakadaŋŋ Baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly while waiting to be taken to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot after harvest if they get bruised during digging, are left in direct hot sun, or are stored in warm, damp spots. Rot-causing fungi and bacteria enter through minor skin cuts and multiply quickly in hot, poorly ventilated conditions.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Aloo okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fungi kɛ bacteria ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ boteɔ hewolo lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my yams are fully mature and ready to harvest for maximum quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ be mli ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up completely. Harvesting too early results in watery tubers that spoil fast, while waiting too long leaves tubers vulnerable to rot and insects in the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi kwraa. Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nu oya. Yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baagboi ni kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baagboi.

english: What is the main difference between hybrid maize seeds and open-pollinated maize (OPV) seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwo mli (OPV) lɛ teŋ?

english: Hybrid maize is created by controlled breeding between two specific parent plants to maximize yield, while open-pollinated maize (OPV) reproduces naturally through wind or insect pollination, keeping its traits stable over generations.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ feɔ ŋmãa kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ateŋ tsakpaa ni akudɔɔ nɔ koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni open pollinated (OPV) ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ bii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ejieɔ ehe kpo be fɛɛ be yɛ yinɔi fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers heavily promote hybrid maize seeds to farmers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ miitswa ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ he adafi waa amɛmiitsɔɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize is heavily promoted because it produces significantly higher yield per acre, grows faster, and copes better with pests and diseases, helping farmers harvest more food and earn more profit.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ he hewalɛ waa ejaakɛ ehaa ŋmãa ni fa babaoo yɛ acre kome mli. shwereɔ oya ni enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ Yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa niyenii babaoo ni amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: No, you should not replant saved hybrid seeds. The second generation loses its special vigor, resulting in uneven plant growth and a severe drop in harvest yields. You must buy fresh hybrid seeds every season.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ duɔ ekoŋŋ. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi waa. Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid daa be.

english: Is it safe for me to save seeds from an open-pollinated maize (OPV) crop for the next planting season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ open pollinated (OPV) ŋmãa mli lɛ ato kɛha ŋmãa ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, you can harvest and save seeds from open-pollinated maize (OPV) to plant next season. They will produce plants similar to the parent crop without a drastic loss in yield, saving you seed money.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa dumɔwui ni jɛ open pollinated (OPV) ŋmãa mli lɛ ni okɛto be ni baa lɛ mli. Amɛbaawo tsei ni tamɔ fɔlɔ tsei lɛ ni yibiiwoo ni he hiaa waa baafite. Enɛ haa okɛ shika baatsu nii yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ mli.

english: Why are hybrid maize seeds more expensive to buy at the agro-dealer shop than regular seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ jara wa waa ni abaanyɛ ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ dɛŋ fe daa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds cost more because seed companies must spend years using specialized human labor and controlled breeding techniques to produce fresh high-performing seeds every single year.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jara wa waa ejaakɛ eheɔ dumɔwui anitsumɔhei lɛ afii babaoo ni amɛkɛ adesai anitsumɔ krɛdɛɛi kɛ fɔmɔ he ŋaai ni akudɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛná dumɔwui heei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ daa afi.

english: Why does hybrid maize require more fertilizer compared to traditional local maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ biɔ ŋmãa babaoo kɛ akɛto akutsoŋ ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ he lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize grows rapidly and produces much larger cobs, which means it needs more nutrients from fertilizer to feed its heavy growth and reach its full yield potential.
ga: Abɛi ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ekɛha edalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do all the plants in a hybrid maize field grow and mature at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni akɛ ŋmãa fee lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds carry identical genetic traits, which makes the plants grow at the exact same rate, reach the same height, and ripen together, making harvesting easier and more efficient.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa yɛ oyaiyeli kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. amɛyɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome ni amɛhoɔ amɛhe ekome Ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does hybrid maize produce bigger cobs than my local traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa wuji fe blema dumɔwui ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds benefit from a scientific phenomenon called 'hybrid vigor,' where combining two strong parent strains results in offspring that grow stronger root systems and larger, fuller cobs.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ náa jeŋ nilee mli nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ ‘hybrid vigor’ lɛ he sɛɛ, he ni akɛ fɔlɔi akutsei enyɔ ni he wa feɔ ekome lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, seshi lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa. kɛ ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ nii babaoo

english: How do I choose whether to plant hybrid maize or open-pollinated maize (OPV) on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kɛji makwɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid loo open pollinated (OPV) yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If you have the money to buy fresh seeds and fertilizer every season, hybrid maize gives you maximum yield. If your budget is tight and you prefer to save your own seeds for next year, open-pollinated maize is the safer choice.
ga: Kɛji oyɛ shika lɛ, hemɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei daa afi. Abɛi ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ obɛ shika babaoo ni oosumɔ ni okɛ dumɔwui komɛi ato koni okɛtsu nii yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Open-pollinated corn ji gbɛ kroko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens if my neighbor plants local maize right next to my open-pollinated maize (OPV) field?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ du maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni agbele naa (OPV) lɛ masɛi hu?

english: Wind will carry pollen from your neighbor's local maize to your OPV field. While this year's harvest won't change, the seeds you save for next year will become mixed and lose their pure OPV qualities.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ baaŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛya o-OPV ŋmɔ lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmaa lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsakeee moŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni okɛto kɛha afi ni baa lɛ baafutu ni amɛ OPV nibii krɔŋŋ lɛ baafite.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly when it stops raining for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during dry spells as a natural defence to trap moisture inside and reduce water loss through evaporation. It is the plant's way of trying to save water until the next rain or irrigation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Eji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato kɛyashi nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are yellowing because of too little water or too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ nu fioo loo nu babaoo mli?

english: When crops receive too little water, the leaves feel dry, brittle, and curl up before turning yellow. When crops get too much water, the leaves turn light green or yellow while remaining soft and soggy, often caused by wet roots rotting underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu fioo tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛgbi, amɛmiigbɔjɔ, ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe dani amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ shi amɛhiɔ shi bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni efɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and bushy after I apply fertilizer, but produce very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ? Shi ani enáa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing stem and leaves. Crops need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to switch energy toward developing strong flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potassium fata he Koni ekɛ hewalɛ atsake kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants growing small and twisted even after I spray pest chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ bibii ni efiteɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves are often a sign of plant stress caused by early insect damage before spraying, or by using chemical inputs that are too strong, which can burn and deform tender young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsake lɛ ji tso lɛ he haomɔ ni kooloi ni fiteɔ mra dani afɔseɔ tsofa lɛ he okadi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsofai ni mli wa tsɔ ni baanyɛ ashã ni eha baai bibii lɛ afite lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or get moldy so quickly inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo efoɔ oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Harvested grain still contains hidden moisture. If it is stored in an airtight or damp room before drying completely under the sun, mold fungi thrive on the warmth and moisture inside the seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lolo. Kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo hulutsoo be mli dani egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fuŋ lɛ daa kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and shrinking while sitting in storage waiting to be sold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni miigbɔjɔ beni mita nitoohe ko ni miimɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue breathing after harvest. Over time, they use up their stored water and starch to produce new buds, causing the main tuber to lose weight and shrivel.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ nu kɛ ŋmei ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii heei. Ehaa bulb titri lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes go soft and spoil so fast in the baskets after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes naturally release a ripening gas called ethylene after harvest. If kept closely packed in warm, poorly ventilated places, this gas builds up and speeds up softening and decay.
ga: Tomato jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ, Gas nɛɛ baabua ehe naa ni eha gas lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni efite oya.

english: How can I know that my cassava tubers are fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare lower stem. Harvesting at this stage ensures the roots are full of starch rather than watery or overly woody.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ shishigbɛ tso lɛ efolo. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ nu loo tso tsɔ.

english: Why do my plantain fruits turn soft and yellow while still hanging on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo dani akpaa lɛ?

english: When plantain bunches are left on the tree past their full maturity, or when the plant suffers from high heat and drought stress, the fruits naturally ripen and break down starch into sugars ahead of time.
ga: Beni ashiɔ plantains lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edara kwraa lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsei miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ hewɔ. Yibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ejaraa starch lɛ mli ewoɔ sugar mli kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Strong sunlight causes them to lose water through their leaves faster than their young roots can draw it from the dry soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops planted close to the edge of the forest grow slower than those in the middle of my open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ koo lɛ naa lɛ daa blɛoo fe nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Large forest trees have deep, massive root systems that steal nutrients and water from the soil around them, and their branches block sunlight. Crops close to the forest boundary miss out on full sun and soil food, making them grow thinner and slower.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ kooi wuji amli lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. ni tsei lɛ aniji tsi hulu la lɛ naa Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ koo lɛ husu lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ daraa mlɛo ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: If I clear my land and leave it uncultivated for a year, will the soil become richer or weaker for crops?
ga: Kɛ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mishi afi lɛ Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni jara wa loo egbɔjɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Leaving cleared land unplanted without cover crops exposes the bare soil to heavy sun and rain, which washes away topsoil nutrients. To make resting land richer, planting cover crops like leguminous beans helps feed the soil and protect it from washing away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni tsei bɛ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulu kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hejɔɔmɔhe lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ, nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekaho.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants use to stay green. As the maize plant grows, it takes whatever nitrogen is left from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing top leaves and cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ Esa akɛ akɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii ni akɛha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava produce smaller tubers when I plant it underneath tall plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ, efeɔ tamɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct, strong sunlight on its leaves to make food and store it in underground tubers. Tall plantain trees shade the cassava, forcing it to spend all its energy growing tall and thin leaves to reach the light instead of expanding its roots.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni naa wa, ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni eho ni ekɛto eshishifãi lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ duŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli koni enyɛ emɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from intense heat stress or dry soil. When the plant feels it doesn't have enough water or energy to nourish growing peppers, it drops the flowers to save its own life.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hewɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ Ebaashɛ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so quickly after rain compared to the young crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, so their seeds sprout fast and grab soil nutrients quickly. Cultivated crops are gentler and grow slower at first, so they need you to clear surrounding weeds so the weeds don't steal their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Tsei ni adu lɛ yɛ mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmiisumɔ ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Bɔni afee ni jwɛi akaju amɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farm give a good harvest right after I burn cleared bushes, but the soil becomes poor in the following seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mishã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ? Shi ani shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bawo wu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Burning cleared bush turns plants into ash, releasing a quick burst of fertilizer into the soil for one harvest. However, the extreme heat kills beneficial earthworms and burns away organic matter, leaving the soil dry and weak for future seasons.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni he tse ni ashãa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee sũ. ni ejieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii shikome. Shi kɛlɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why do some of my corn seeds fail to sprout when I plant them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed contains only a tiny amount of stored energy to push its shoot above ground. If planted too deep, the shoot exhausts all its energy before reaching the surface and dies under the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl and look weak during the afternoon heat even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane mli kɛ́ awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In hot afternoon sun, water leaves the plant's leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. Curling leaves is the tomato's way of shrinking its surface area to trap moisture inside until the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shĩɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tomato tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shi koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ mli kɛyashi hulu lɛ baaha amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do small insects attack my vegetable leaves more during the dry harmattan season than during rainy times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-vegetable baai lɛ babaoo yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains physically wash small insects off leaves and keep plants strong with water. During dry periods, insects multiply quickly because rain isn't knocking them off, and plants are weaker from heat stress, making them easy targets.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ kooloi bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe, ni ekɛ nu woɔ tsei lɛ ahe hewalɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Kooloi babaoo oya ejaakɛ nugbɔ haaa amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he. Ni tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni atutuaa amɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to the newer top leaves to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when there is heavy rainfall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water stays trapped around the roots for too long without proper drainage, the roots drown, suffocate, and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ebɔle he Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbo, amɛbaagbɔjɔ, ni amɛbaafite.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to save energy rather than grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight. Climbing a stake helps the leaves produce more energy, which is directed downward to grow large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Pii ni akwɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. ni abaajie lɛ shi koni eha yitso agbo lɛ ada.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the earth for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why will planting my seeds too close together lead to a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all the plants weak and small.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ bibioo.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and become hard?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Curled, distorted leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap out of the young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your crops. Because weeds grow quickly, they starve your crops of the resources needed to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Ehaa onibii lɛ náaa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why is it important for an officer to measure the exact size of my farm before giving me support or supplies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nitsulɔi lɛ asusu miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ dani amɛkɛ yelikɛbuamɔ loo nibii aha mi lɛ?

english: Measuring your farm land ensures you receive the exact amount of inputs like seeds, fertilizers, or financial assistance needed for your land size, preventing waste or shortages.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ susumɔ haa onine shɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii loo shika he yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsi nibii ni afiteɔ loo nibii ni faaa lɛ naa

english: How does knowing the exact acreage of my land help me care for my crops better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ he pɔtɛɛ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Knowing your exact land size helps you calculate precise planting distances, estimate expected yields, and apply the correct total amount of farm chemicals across your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ da ha pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni obu he ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ lɛ he akɔntaa jogbaŋŋ. Buu nibii ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ abaajie lɛ he akɔntaa ni okɛ tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ ni sa atsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are sick and need medicine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao lɛ hela mɔ lɛ ni tsofa he miihia lɛ?

english: Sick cocoa trees often show clear warning signs like yellowing leaves, dark spots on pods, wilting leaves, swollen stems, or stunted pod growth, indicating pest or fungal infections.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ, baai ni egboi, ŋmeii ni efuu, loo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ ni eyaaa hiɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba.

english: What causes cocoa tree diseases to spread quickly across my farm?
ga: Mɛni ha cacao hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Cocoa diseases are often carried by insects, rain droplets, wind, or contaminated pruning tools, moving easily from infected trees to healthy neighboring plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi, nu mli nu, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ cocoa hela lɛ baa. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: What kind of medicine should I ask for when my cocoa trees get infected with disease?
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela mɔ kookoo tsei lɛ, mɛɛ tsofa esa akɛ abi?

english: You should ask for recommended agrochemicals such as fungicides or insecticides like 'abɔresside' that are specifically formulated to treat common cocoa diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ obi okwaayeli mli tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ ‘Aboreside’ ni afee pɔtɛɛ koni akɛtsa kookoo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: Why do I need to mix my crop medicine with water instead of pouring it straight on the cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ futuɔ nu moŋ fe ni mikɛbaafɔse cacao tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Undiluted chemical medicine is extremely concentrated and can scorch or burn your trees; mixing it with water dilutes it so it safely coats and protects the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsofai babaoo ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã tsei. Kɛ́ okɛ nu futu mli lɛ, ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe shweshweeshwe ni ebu he.

english: How do I know the correct amount of water to mix with one bottle of farm chemical?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nu ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛfutu ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tɔ mli lɛ?

english: Every chemical medicine comes with exact mixing guidelines—for instance, one bottle may require specific water units like two gallons (about 9 liters)—to ensure the mixture works effectively without harming crops.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛ tsofa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi komɛi ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ahaa lɛ he. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, nu pɔtɛɛ ko baanyɛ abi tɔ kome, tamɔ galɔn enyɔ (aaafee litai 9), koni nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: What happens to my crops if I add too much water to my farm spray chemical?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo fata tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Adding too much water makes the chemical mixture too weak, meaning it will fail to kill the disease or pests affecting your cocoa trees, wasting your time and money.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ afee mlɛo tsɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ enyɛŋ egbe helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko. Ehaa ofiteɔ be kɛ shika.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if I don't use enough water when mixing farm chemical spray?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa tsuuu nii ni mikɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Using too little water makes the solution too strong, which can burn leaf surfaces, kill young flower buds, damage pods, and lower your total harvest.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ anɔ ashã. Efiteɔ fɔfɔi bibii, efiteɔ pods ni ebaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ shi.

english: How do gallons convert to liters when I am measuring water for spraying my farm?
ga: Te galɔni tsakeɔ efeɔ lita lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ misusu nu ni mikɛshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: In farm liquid measurements, one standard gallon is equal to roughly 4.5 liters, so two gallons equal about 9 liters of water for your chemical mixture.
ga: Kɛha nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ susumɔ Galɔn kome ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji aaafee lita 4.5, no hewɔ lɛ galɔn 2 kɛ nu ni miihe ashɛ lita 9 yeɔ egbɔ kɛha otsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and need shade to protect their leaves from harsh sunlight and conserve soil moisture. Retaining shade trees creates a cooler environment that allows young roots to establish successfully.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Tso lɛ ni aaaha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ omanye lɛ baa.

english: Why are my plantain plants giving smaller bunches than when I first planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ panicles bibii fe be mli ni midu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stalk, they steal water and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones allows the main stem to produce a larger bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) dara kɛbɔle Plantain ŋmeii titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahiɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow and pale green during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nutrients away, so applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the main dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops leaves to conserve water during dry periods. The root under the soil remains alive, and the plant will grow fresh leaves as soon as regular rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa pɛ.

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the wet soil into direct sunlight so they can make food efficiently, which leads to larger underground tubers and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni hulu lɛ akashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa ni etsiɔ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa.

english: What causes holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's growing funnel. Catching them early and treating the funnels protects the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ shweremɔ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Ni gbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ buɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on plant sap or spreading viruses. Controlling these pests keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, uneven watering, or nutrient imbalances. Consistent watering during dry spells helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks hot sun, traps soil moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop area.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crop prices drop so low right after harvest time in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be sɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: When every farmer harvests and sells at the exact same time, the market gets flooded with produce. Buyers pay less because crops are everywhere, but storing your harvest or processing it lets you sell later when scarcity raises the price.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kpa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayeli lɛ baayi kɛ nibii ni amɛduɔ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Shi kɛ́ okpa loo otsu he nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli beni nibii ni faaa lɛ haa jara yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested produce from spoiling before I get a good buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mikpamɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite dani ená hɔlɔ kpakpa?

english: Drying grains properly, keeping crops in cool and ventilated shade, and using airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) protect crops from humidity, insects, and rot while you wait for better market prices.
ga: Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli Ni akɛ vacuum storage bags (tamɔ PICS bags) tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi, kɛ fitemɔ he yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops for maximum yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready: maize husks dry out and turn brown, peppers reach their full mature color, and soil cracks around root crops like cassava. Harvesting too early or late reduces both weight and market value.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji efee klalo: ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baagbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Pepper lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eshɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa ni bɔle shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei. Nikpamɔ mra loo sɛɛ tsɔ haa shwiili lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ jarayeli jara fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or isn't getting enough water. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores the green color and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or pollinators aren't visiting. Consistent watering and providing light shade during extreme heat help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ eyaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the leaves grow big and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ dara ni amɛlɛ moŋ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil forces cassava to put all its food energy into growing leaves above ground instead of roots below. Balanced nutrients and planting at the right stem angle encourage larger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmei nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Niyenii ni ja kɛ dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by heavy humidity and fungal infection during rainy seasons. Pruning extra shade branches lets in sunlight and air flow, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Eji black pod hela ko ni hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpɛ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. Supporting the main stem with sturdy wooden props or bamboo stakes prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting during storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crops every year even though I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the exact same crop season after season drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil. Rotating crops, especially planting legumes like groundnuts or beans, restores natural nitrogen and keeps soil fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are weeds growing much faster than my planted crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that sprout quickly to grab sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crop can establish itself. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks gives your crops the head start they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly before I can get them to the market to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani mikɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and produce heat after being picked. When they are packed tightly in bags or left in hot sun, heat and moisture get trapped, which speeds up decay and allows rotting fungi to grow fast.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛwo kotoku mli jogbaŋŋ loo ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mɔɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa oya.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into fine powder after a few months in the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize grains turn to powder when tiny pests called weevils eat them from the inside. If the grain was not dried completely before storing, the dampness creates the perfect home for these insects to multiply and destroy the crop.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ powda kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ye amɛ kɛjɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Humidity lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers begin to rot in storage after being transported in heavy sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ beni akɛwo kotokui ni tsii amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rough handling during harvesting and transport creates small cuts and bruises on the skin of the yam. Microscopic rot organisms enter through these tiny wounds and destroy the tuber from within.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo mli waa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ tsɔne mli lɛ, ekɛ fãji bibii kɛ fãji bibii baa. yɛ sweet potato hewolo nɔ Nibii bibii ni fiteɔ ni anaaa lɛ boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii amli. enɛɛmɛi ni efite yitso lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested pepper get covered in white mould while I am drying it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ be mli ni mikɛ hulu lɛ miigbi amɛ lɛ?

english: Mould grows on peppers if they are piled too thickly together or if the weather is humid and cloudy. Without good airflow and strong sun to dry them quickly, trapped moisture allows mould spores to spread.
ga: Fungus baakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni atatu ewo mli. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la babaoo bɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbi oya. Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my harvested leafy vegetables wilt and turn brown within just a few hours of picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikpaa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ?

english: Once cut from the root, green leafy vegetables lose their water supply. Direct sunshine and hot air pull the remaining water out of the leaves rapidly, causing them to lose firmness and decay.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ baafite nu. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya, ni ehaa amɛhe waaa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more plants, why do I end up with small stalks and tiny ears?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ ŋmãa bibioo kɛ toi bibii?

english: Crops need space to share sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When planted too close, the roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other, leaving all the plants weak and starved.
ga: Tsei hia he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛja hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ adu lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ fɛɛ egbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and fall off whenever heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baaha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air from the soil to stay healthy and absorb food. Floodwaters fill all the tiny air spaces in the ground, suffocating the roots so the plant cannot feed its leaves.
ga: Tsei shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ niyenii. Nu afua nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ baai.

english: Why do my garden egg plants drop their flowers before growing any actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress like severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil strength. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to stay alive.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready to harvest so it doesn't spoil under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni egbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base starts to crack. Leaving mature cassava in wet ground too long causes the roots to rot right in the soil.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree branch before they are ready for picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and overly shady conditions. Too much dampness on the pods allows the fungal rot to spread across the tree.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, nu, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli. Fɛ̃i babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: If I get crop seeds from Ivory Coast, will they grow well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ dumɔwui anɔ kɛjɛ Ivory Coast Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Many crops from Ivory Coast grow very well in Ghana because both countries share similar tropical climates, rain patterns, and soil types. However, you should check with an extension officer to ensure the specific variety is resistant to local Ghanaian pests and diseases.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ Ivory Coast lɛ babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana. Akɛni maji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ tropical kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi ni tamɔ amɛhe hewɔ lɛ, shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ o-extension agent lɛ akwɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshiɔ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is suitable for growing a new crop variety I brought from another area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni mikɛjɛ hei krokomɛi kɛba lɛ adumɔ?

english: You can observe how well the soil drains water and check its depth and richness. A local agricultural extension officer can also test your soil's fertility and acid levels to confirm if your new crop will thrive.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ, ni okwɛ bɔ ni emli kwɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ha. Mɛi ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ bɔ ni acidity yɔɔ ha lɛ amɛkwɛ kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ baashwere.

english: Why is it better to start some crop seeds in a nursery instead of planting them directly on the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: A nursery protects young, delicate seeds from harsh sunlight, heavy rainfall, and pests while they are weak. Nursing seeds allows you to care for them closely so only the strongest seedlings are chosen for the main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ooodu lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ahalaa kɛhaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ.

english: How long can young crop seedlings stay in a nursery before they must be planted on the field?
ga: Be enyiɛ dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani ehe baahia ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Most tree and crop seedlings should only stay in the nursery for 3 to 6 months. Keeping them in nursery bags for too long causes their roots to become twisted and bound, which stunts their growth after transplanting.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei amli dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo grow bag mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛdara yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I care for tender young seedlings in my nursery so they do not die before planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ koni amɛkagboi dani amɛdalɛ be lɛ aba?

english: Ensure the nursery has light shade, water the seedlings daily in the early morning or evening, and regularly check under the leaves for pests or signs of disease.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni tsɔsemɔhe lɛ aná hulutsoo be ni mli tse. Okɛ nu awo dumɔwui lɛ amli daa gbi leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi daa kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hela he okadi ko yɛ mli.

english: What should I do if I start a crop nursery but get delayed and cannot plant the seedlings right away?
ga: Kɛji obɔi tsei afɔmɔ shi okɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni onyɛɛɛ odu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Continue watering them regularly, provide adequate shade, and transfer them into larger polybags if their roots begin to overcrowd so they remain healthy until you are ready to plant.
ga: Nu daa Ha hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛwo poly bag agbo mli kɛji shishifãi lɛ bafee nɔ ni fe nine. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu.

english: If I want to test a new crop variety on my land, how many seeds should I plant to see if it works?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni maka tso henɔ hee ko makwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ madu koni mana kɛji ebaatsu nii?

english: Planting a small trial batch of about 30 to 50 seeds on a small plot allows you to observe how the crop responds to your soil and rainfall without risking your entire investment.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ mli lɛ akuu bibioo ko ni aduɔ, aaafee dumɔwui 30 kɛyashi 50, yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he, ni okɛ shika fɛɛ ni okɛwo mli lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: What causes young seedlings to wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock, which happens when delicate root hairs are damaged during moving or when seedlings are suddenly exposed to direct hot sun without enough water.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ yitsɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. aloo kɛ́ hulu la kpɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: How can I prepare nursery seedlings so they survive the stress of being transplanted to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni manyɛ maye haomɔ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Reduce shade over the nursery gradually a few weeks before planting to harden the seedlings, and always transplant them early in the morning or late in the afternoon on cloudy days.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ blɛoo otsii fioo komɛi dani adu koni dumɔwui lɛ awa. ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli yɛ gbi ni atatu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some crop seeds fail to grow even after I plant them and give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu ni miwo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are too old, were stored in hot or humid conditions, or were harvested before fully maturing. Storing seeds in a cool, dry place helps preserve their strength.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni hulu tsoɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ loo akpaa amɛ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa. Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why can't I just plant mango trees anywhere I have land in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu mango tsei yɛ he fɛɛ he ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Mango trees need deep, well-drained soil and plenty of full sunlight to grow strong roots and produce fruit. Planting them in swampy or rocky land will cause the roots to rot or prevent the tree from flowering properly.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni hulu la yɛ jɛmɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ awa ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo loo ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my fruit trees very close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tsei ni woɔ yibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This competition makes them grow tall and weak, yields less fruit, and allows crop diseases to spread easily between branches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa, amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei aniji ateŋ mlɛo.

english: Why does it take several years for a fruit tree to start bearing fruit after I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ jeɔ yibii womɔ shishi beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their first few years building a strong root system and sturdy trunk to support heavy harvests later. Using certified grafted seedlings can help trees start fruiting much faster than planting directly from wild seeds.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni wa koni amɛkɛye amɛbua ŋmaa babaoo ni abaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi oya fe bɔ ni amɛjɛɔ koo mli dumɔwui amli amɛdaraa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my mango tree flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when the tree experiences stress from dry spells, pest attacks, or fungal diseases like powdery mildew during the flowering period, causing the tree to shed its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso ko na haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli, ni no haa tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: What causes my fruit tree to produce plenty of harvest one year and almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi eshɛɛɛ nɔ ko kwraa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: This behavior is called alternate bearing. When a tree produces an unusually heavy harvest, it exhausts its stored nutrients and needs the following year to rest, rebuild its foliage, and gather energy before it can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ sɛɛkuu-kɛsaramɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ wo yibii ni tsii waa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni ato lɛ laajeɔ ni esa akɛ ekɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe, ekwɛ̃ baai heei, ni ebua hewalɛ naa dani ebaanyɛ ewo yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do grafted crop seedlings give better fruit than seeds I pick and dry myself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mibuaa naa ni migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Grafting joins a piece of a high-yielding, healthy adult tree onto a strong root system. This guarantees that the new tree carries the exact good qualities and sweetness of the mother plant, whereas seeds can inherit unpredictable traits.
ga: Grafting kɛ tso ni eda lɛ fãi ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ tso hee lɛ baaná sui kpakpai kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui baanyɛ aná sui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ gboshinii.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers tell me to cut or prune branches on my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko kɛɔ mi akɛ mifo loo mifo mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or crowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. It directs the plant's energy away from unwanted leaves and into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni mli edɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni ataooo lɛ ahe kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I not apply high-nitrogen fertilizer when my fruit tree starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo tsuuu nii kɛ́ aduawai tsei je shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ?

english: High nitrogen encourages the tree to produce lots of green leaves and new shoots instead of flowers. Applying it during flowering can cause the tree to drop its blossoms instead of setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔlii babaoo kɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do fruit flies attack my fruits while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii miitutua mi aduawai lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Female fruit flies pierce the skin of young, ripening fruit to lay their eggs inside. As the eggs hatch into maggots, they feed on the flesh, causing the fruit to rot from the inside and fall before harvest.
ga: Aduawai amli ŋmeii yei tsɔɔ aduawai bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahewolo mli koni amɛwo wɔji yɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ Ebaaye loo. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of a root disease or just lack of rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shishifã hela hewɔ loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Crops suffering from lack of water usually droop during the hot afternoon and recover in the cool evening or after watering. Crops with root diseases turn yellow, wilt permanently regardless of water, and show soft or blackened roots when pulled up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ebaahe ejɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Tsei ni shishifã hela yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Egboɔ daa ni nu kɔɔɔ he eko. Ni kɛ́ ajie kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and burn easily under strong sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun and trap moisture, the leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink, causing them to turn yellow and drop to protect the plant from drying out completely.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni atsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni no haaa tso lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Yam vines produce energy for the root tuber through their leaves, which need as much sunlight as possible. When you allow the vines to climb up a stake, the leaves spread out into the light instead of clumping on the ground, helping the plant make more food to grow bigger yams underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ Kɛ́ oha wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa la lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest because there are more plants?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani onine shɛɛɛ yibii babaoo nɔ ejaakɛ tsei babaoo yɛ?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your total harvest. When maize plants are packed together, their roots fight each other for water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block each other from sunlight, resulting in thin stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bafee ekome lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. ni ebaai lɛ buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How do weeds hurt my cassava crop even if I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers with aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizer faster than young cassava plants can. If you leave weeds in the field, they will drink up the nutrients you intended for your cassava, causing your cassava roots to stay small.
