ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni daa oya ni eshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni yucca tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee. Kɛji oshi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baanu niyenii ni he hiaa bo kɛha ŋmei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of turning them into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off without making fruit when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of small insects like bees to shake the pollen inside the flower. Keeping the soil consistently moist and cool helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be kpe. Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small balls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like mites or aphid pests feeding on the underside of the leaves and spreading plant viruses. As they suck the sap out of the young leaves, the leaf bends and curls up, which stops the plant from making leaves that feed the pepper.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ Baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaabɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee baai ni yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground in the field before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays soaked with excess water for too long during heavy rains. The roots need air in the soil to breathe, and waterlogged soil suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungus to grow and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ akɛ nu ni fa fe nine shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgboi.

english: Beans and cowpeas have special naturally occurring bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the ground. When the bean plant dies and decays, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Muawai krɛdɛɛi ni baa amɛshishifãi amli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize so that the heavy rains do not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied when the soil is damp but not soaked, usually a day or two after a moderate rain. Applying fertilizer right before a heavy downpour will cause the water to sweep the chemical grains away into drains before the roots can swallow it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ shi jeee nɔ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ ajie tsofa dumɔwui lɛ kɛya nubu lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ ami amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong wind blows through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots that spread near the surface. If the soil around the base is soft, or if stem borer insects have damaged the inner trunk, or if you let too many suckers grow around one stem, the heavy weight of the fruit bundle makes the tree top-heavy and easy to blow down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, shi moŋ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo kɛji kooloi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ni efite tso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ. Aloo ha ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he. Bɔ ni tso lɛ yibii akui lɛ tsiimɔ tsii ha lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee tsiimɔ ni egbee shi oya.

english: How can I grow crops that are rich in nutrients so my family stays healthy and doesn't fall sick often?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ koni miweku lɛ aná hewalɛ ni hela akaye amɛ shii abɔ?

english: Crops absorb nutrients directly from healthy soil. Adding organic compost or well-rotted animal manure enriches the soil with minerals, which plants like orange-fleshed sweet potatoes, leafy greens, and beans absorb and pass on to you when eaten, boosting your family's immunity.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni tsei tamɔ sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwieɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa onɔ kɛji aye. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oweku lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What causes some cassava plants to produce large, healthy tubers while others yield small, woody roots?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni wa? yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi komɛi haa shishifãi ni ji tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, rich soil and plenty of sunlight to store energy in its roots. If the soil is hard, choked with weeds, or lacks nutrients, the plant spends its energy surviving rather than swelling its roots into large, food-filled tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni mli edɔ he miihia Cassava. Ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ato hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni jwɛi ehà nɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ wala nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni daa ni amɛfeɔ bulb agbo ni niyenii eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and turn yellow during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense to trap moisture and prevent water loss during extreme heat. Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the plant is short on nitrogen or severely stressed for water, which reduces its ability to produce food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha nu lɛ ahi shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa miipiŋ lɛ. Enɛ baaha nyɛmɔ ni akɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do crops planted under big shade trees grow tall and skinny but produce very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Plants need direct sunlight to produce food through their leaves. When shaded, a crop spends all its energy stretching upwards to reach light instead of using energy to grow thick stems, strong leaves, and fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛna niyenii kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Beni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ Baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts alongside maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that have special bacteria in their roots. These bacteria pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil as natural fertilizer, which feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant tomatoes in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows tomato-seeking pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating tomatoes with corn or beans resets the soil and stops diseases from spreading.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni taoɔ tomato lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake tomato lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaakpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them survive during dry periods?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella that keeps the sun from drying out the earth. It keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture so roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot if the soil is too wet and packed tight, preventing air from reaching the seed, or if they are planted too deep. Seeds need moisture, warm temperature, and oxygen to sprout safely.
ga: Dumɔwui baagbo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. aloo kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ. hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into healthy peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani etsɔ pepper ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients like potassium. When the plant feels stressed, it sheds flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao lɛ, ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere nu ni ehi wala mli.

english: How do crop diseases spread from one sick plant to healthy ones across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Crop diseases are caused by microscopic germs like fungi and bacteria. They travel across your farm through wind, splashing rain, contaminated farm cutlasses or hoes, or insects that bite a sick leaf and then bite a healthy one.
ga: Helai bibii tamɔ fungi kɛ muawai kɛ tsei helai baa. Amɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii loo shɔvel ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Aloo kooloi bibii ni ŋmɔɔ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ no sɛɛ lɛ amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I plant cassava on my farm, will it spoil the soil for the next crops I want to grow?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ebaafite shikpɔŋ kɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a lot of nutrients like potassium out of the ground to form its large tubers. While the land might feel soft and easy to farm right after digging up cassava, growing it repeatedly without adding manure or fertilizer will eventually weaken the soil.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo, tamɔ potassium, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmeii wuji. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni edumɔ waaa yɛ be mli ni atsa ŋmei sɛɛ moŋ, Shi kɛji akɛ adu shii abɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ naagbee.

english: Why do some farmers say cassava ruins the land while my next crops seem to grow fine after harvesting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you harvest cassava, digging up the roots loosens the soil, and leftover leaves rot to release quick nutrients for the next crop. However, over time, cassava draws out deep nutrients, so without resting the land or adding nutrients, later harvests will eventually drop.
ga: Beni okpaa ŋmei Shishifãi lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ koni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ oya. Shi, yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ niyenii ni mli kwɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he lɛ, sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ baa shi.

english: Does cassava leave anything good in the soil after I dig out all the tubers?
ga: Ani ŋmei shĩɔ nibii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni atsa ŋmeii lɛ amli sɛɛ?

english: The tubers themselves remove nutrients from the soil, but the cassava stems and leaves left behind on the field break down into organic matter. Leaving this crop waste on your land returns valuable nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Tubers lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmei tsei kɛ baai ni ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakumɔ ni etsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ nii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does growing plantain on my land help make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, plantains produce large leaves and thick stems that drop to the ground and rot. This natural mulch keeps the soil moist, prevents weed growth, and adds rich organic matter back into the ground for whatever you plant next.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains woɔ baai agboi kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Yes, intercropping plantain and cassava is a good practice. Young plantains benefit from space while cassava grows, and as the plantains grow taller, they provide shade, making good use of the land without hurting each other if spaced well.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Plantains bibii lɛ baaná he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he sɛɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa lɛ. Ni kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Amɛhaa hulutsoo. Nyɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛyeee nyɛhe awui kɛji nyɛtsi nyɛhe kɛjɛ nyɛhe.

english: What is the best crop for me to plant on my land right after I harvest my cassava?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Legumes such as groundnuts, cowpeas, or beans are best to plant after cassava. These crops pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring the nutrients that the cassava crop used up.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, loo ŋmei Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Tsei nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni akɛ niyenii ni ŋmei tsei lɛ efite lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I let my soil rest after harvesting cassava, or can I plant new crops immediately?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe loo abaanyɛ adu ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: While you can plant immediately if you add manure or compost, letting the land rest (fallowing) or planting soil-rebuilding crops like beans gives the soil time to regain its natural strength for higher yields later.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he moŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (tillage) loo aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni saa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛnáa ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my land has become too weak after growing cassava and plantain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ beni midu ŋmei kɛ plantain sɛɛ?

english: If you notice that your new crops have yellowish leaves, grow very slowly, or produce much smaller yields than before, it means the soil nutrients are exhausted and need replenishing.
ga: Kɛji oyɔse akɛ otso hee lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, eedara blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etã, ni ehe miihia ni akɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Do I need to put fertilizer on my farm after harvesting cassava if the soil still looks rich?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo?

english: Even if the soil looks good, cassava drains key nutrients during its long growing cycle. Adding organic manure or crop fertilizer after a cassava harvest ensures the soil stays strong for the next crop.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ Shi ŋmei hu shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛdaraa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to the soil if I clear all the cassava leaves and stems away from my farm after harvest?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mibua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anaa ni migbala ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If you clear away all the plant waste, you lose the free fertilizer that nature gives you. Burning or removing stem cut-offs deprives the soil of organic material that keeps it moist and fertile.
ga: Kɛji ojie tsei amli jwɛi fɛɛ lɛ Obaafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni adebɔɔ kɛhaa yaka lɛ. Niji ni ashãa loo afoɔ lɛ jieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing the small holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars feed on young maize leaves and stems, which reduces your crop yield if you do not control them early using proper management or approved sprays.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi kɛji okudɔɔɔ amɛ mra. kɛtsɔ nitsumɔ ni sa loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi trukaa ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease. The bacteria block the tubes inside the plant stem that carry water, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves even when the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Muawai tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Cassava roots rot in standing water because wet soil starves the roots of air and allows fungal diseases to thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps drain excess water away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to keep clearing weeds away from my yam mounds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, light, and soil nutrients away from your yam vines. Clearing them allows the leaves to catch full sunlight, which feeds the plant and helps build large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani mifee klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when the plant receives a sudden flush of water after a dry period. The inside leaves absorb the water quickly and grow faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ akɛ nu shwie tsei lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛdaraa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he ni etse.

english: Why shouldn't I drop my fertilizer right at the base of my crop stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the outer layer of the plant and damage young roots. Placing it a few inches away in a ring or hole lets the feeder roots absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ ni efite shishifãi bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi yɛ ŋwɛi loo bu mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize, which needs high amounts of nitrogen to produce strong ears.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛná toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out under full sun during the Harmattan. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them protects them from harsh sunlight and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi yɛ harmattan beaŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaabu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If too many suckers grow together, they fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and sunlight. Cutting extra suckers down to leave only one or two strong ones ensures you get bigger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Ekɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu koni ená niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha onine ashɛ ŋmeii ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ nɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for food in the soil, sunlight, and water. This leaves you with tall, thin plants that produce very small cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ nu mli, ni no haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs chemical fertilizer or manure before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu?

english: If your crops from the previous harvest had pale yellow leaves, grew slowly, or gave you very small yields despite good rainfall, it means the soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okpa yɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, eedara blɛoo, loo ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ elaaje, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of the plant usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or from a virus transmitted by those insects that stunts leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the growing center of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the soft leaves, leaving caterpillar droppings behind.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii afɔfɔi ni oooshi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop roll up or fold inward during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛyaa mli yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. During hot weather, the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the direct sun, which helps it save water and survive heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baafo amɛbaai lɛ amli koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba baa lɛ nɔ. ni haa nu baa shi ni ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpeɔ.

english: Why do all the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani egbeeɔ shi ni edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges in the soil to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and fibrous stems rather than deep taproots and hard wood. As the fruit bunch gets heavier, top-heavy weight combined with rain or wind easily uproots the stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ fiber. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ sisi nɛ mi kuɔ kɛ tso nɛ wa. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Muji ni tsii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ fata he lɛ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers reach maturity, excess moisture in waterlogged soil prevents root respiration and creates an ideal environment for soil fungi and bacteria to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ amumɔ naa. ni efee shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abote mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my maize rows help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of plants that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, this nitrogen feeds the soil and helps the maize grow.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei akuu ko ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when it rains heavily for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away vital plant nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them. Without nitrogen, maize plants cannot produce green color and struggle to make their own food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans have tiny living organisms on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, this natural food stays in the soil for future crops like maize to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ beans yɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even when the leaves on top look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard and packed together, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of expanding its storage roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ shiŋŋ tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a haa sisifãhi nɛ a to ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ wa.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines dry up and die completely before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛgboi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants naturally dry up at the end of their life cycle as a signal that the plant has finished sending all its food energy down into the root tuber, meaning the yam is mature and ready to be dug up.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naagbee yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsu eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtee shishifã lɛ shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or when the soil lacks water. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving water to keep itself alive during hot periods.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall with big leaves but produce very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi okra ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Okra plants grow tall without fruiting when they get too much shade or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant gets tricked into spending all its strength building tall stems instead of flowering.
ga: Roselle tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Alakaa tsei koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee tsei ni kɛlɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and turn brown during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves that lose water rapidly in dry winds. To protect themselves, the plants curl and drop older leaves to slow down water loss and keep the main trunk alive until rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ gĩ. koni obu ohe he Tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaajie baai momoi lɛ koni nu lɛ akafite fioo ni eha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do tomato leaves roll up tightly on very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves inward during peak sun to hide their leaf surface from direct heat. This reduces the amount of water evaporating out of the plant so it does not dry out.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbaa lɛ hiɛ akaje la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni ekagbi.

english: Why do seeds sprout much faster when planted right after the first rain than before it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Seeds need a combination of warmth and constant moisture to wake up. Planting right after a rain ensures the seed shell absorbs enough water to soften so the root can break out easily.
ga: Dumɔwui hia dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛte shi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni amɛkumɔ oya.

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, cool, and shaded conditions where air cannot flow freely around the cocoa trees.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as living umbrellas, sheltering the cocoa with shade and keeping the soil moist while the trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Okɛ shade aha kookoo lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe to pull up the nutrients the plant needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu koni amɛjie niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids underneath the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects that stops the plant from growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to catch full sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot temperatures, irregular watering, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji haomɔ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without draining away properly. Excess water suffocates the roots and invites rot-causing fungi that break down the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ nine koni amɛbafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my soil produce better crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for light, water, and nutrients. They waste all their energy stretching upward to reach the sun instead of growing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ amɛhe. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why are my green oranges dropping off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tangerine lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop immature fruit when stressed by sudden dry weather, pest attacks, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to support the heavy weight of ripening fruit.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni eshɛko kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛye abua aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni tsii lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right against the main stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tso titri lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly against the stem can scorch and burn the plant tissue. Placing it a few inches away allows the spreading feeder roots to safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji lɛ ni esha amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha radiating feeder lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to retain soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava next to them protects the seedlings until they are strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less often, prevents weeds from growing, and adds rich nutrients to the soil as the dry grass breaks down.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli babaoo Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he be mli ni jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source maize needs to grow. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas in the same field where I plant my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, cowpeas and other legumes naturally take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This enriches the soil and helps your maize grow bigger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi. Egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water standing in the field suffocates cassava roots and causes fungal rotting. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do the blossom ends of my green tomatoes turn black and squishy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant does not get consistent water, making it hard for the plant to absorb calcium from the soil. Regular and even watering helps prevent this.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ haa ewaa aha tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa ni afeɔ lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What is making ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which feed inside the leaf whorls of maize. Checking your farm early and putting recommended organic extracts or approved control products directly into the leaf center stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni akudɔɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsi amɛnaa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and feeding the plants balanced compost encourages the flowers to stay on and grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ha ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden poles in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to produce food to swell the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up to catch sunlight and lifts them off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ. Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ewoɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ jie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal food and water from the main plant. Pruning them so that only one or two healthy shoots remain allows the main tree to focus its energy on producing big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains akui wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for growth. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where small roots cannot reach it, so adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii daa lɛ. not accessible No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put all my fertilizer into the soil at the same time I plant my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Newly planted seeds do not have roots big enough to absorb large amounts of fertilizer. Applying everything at once causes the fertilizer to wash away in heavy rain before the growing plant can actually use it.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni dara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ tsu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli dani tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛtsu nii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point the cassava stem when planting it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ otsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems have small nodes or buds that must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems have to fight to bend upward, which weakens the plant and reduces the number of roots it produces.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Ehe baahia ni tso lɛ awuu koni ekoto ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni ebaanyɛ ewo lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground based on how much sunlight their leaves catch. Staking gets the leaves off the ground and spreads them out in the sun while keeping them safe from heat on the hot soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni damɔ hulu la ni baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛbuɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Small holes inside the central leaves of corn are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the funnel of the leaves during the day to feed on the tender shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Without balanced moisture and shade from extreme heat, the plant cannot form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the humidity and shade it needs for its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or beans on land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas can take nitrogen from the air and return it to the ground, restoring soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my pepper seeds take so much longer to sprout than my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fe mi-corn dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have a tough outer shell and require warmer, consistently moist soil conditions to break open compared to grain seeds like maize, which sprout rapidly once wet.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ kponɔ ni wa ni ehe hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli efɔ daa koni etswa. Akɛ enɛ toɔ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ edɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start to rot and turn dark inside just two days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni etsɔ duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once dug out of the ground, cassava roots lose water rapidly and react with oxygen in the air, triggering a natural chemical breakdown that turns the flesh dark and spoils it quickly.
ga: Kɛji atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ nu oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni fiteɔ nii baa. Enɛ haa loo lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the top layer of soil. Keeping larger trees provides a protective canopy that cools the plants and holds moisture in the ground.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ akwɛmɔ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain plants grow much faster when I plant them near big trees or shaded areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ahe loo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains thrive in rich, moist soil protected from harsh winds and extreme heat. The shade helps the soil retain water, allowing the plantain's broad leaves to stay hydrated and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni mli efɔ nɔ. Abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Shade yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa plantain lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop even produces ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ po woɔ toi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to make food. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant drains nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha nihoomɔ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei shwieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my pepper farm produce plenty of green leaves but drops all its flowers without giving me fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi shi yibii ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants focus entirely on growing thick leaves instead of fruits. Extreme heat or lack of water can also stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni mli tse ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ahao. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops grow dark green leaves but still fail to produce heavy seeds or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi amɛwooo dumɔwui loo bulbs ni tsii lolo lɛ?

english: Plants need a balance of nutrients. While nitrogen builds green leaves, nutrients like phosphorus and potassium are needed for roots, flowers, and seeds. Without those, the plant stays leafy but empty.
ga: Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Eyɛ mli akɛ nitrogen feɔ baai eŋɔli moŋ, shi niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium hu he miihia kɛha shishifãi, fɔfɔii, kɛ dumɔwui. Tso lɛ baaná baai shi ebaafee efolo.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and weak like ropes when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa tamɔ kpãai beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch rapidly toward the sun, making their stems thin and weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛgbala amɛhe oya kɛtee hulu lɛ he. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: Why does cutting off weak side branches from my tomato plants give me bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afolɔ tomato tsei lɛ aniji bibii lɛ, ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary stems that consume water and food. By removing them, the plant sends all its gathered nutrients directly into expanding and ripening the remaining fruits.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa ni yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ. Tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni abua naa lɛ fɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛgbala yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and hard when I plant them in hard red soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe wa waa kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, soft soil to expand properly. Hard clay or compacted red soil traps the roots, making it difficult for the plant to push the soil away and grow big, fleshy roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ tsuru ni mli edɔ lɛ baamɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ loo.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when the rains stay too long before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil with water. Without air, the roots suffocate, and soil fungi thrive in the wet conditions, causing the tubers to decay.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli obɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and make my vegetable crops look sickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ehaa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong, wild roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops can. When left unchecked, they rob your vegetables of the essential nutrients needed to stay healthy.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaajie niyenii ni he hiaa bo kɛha ohewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ o-vegeduries lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava together in the same nursery with my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi plantain lɛ?

english: No, cassava does not do well in a nursery set up for plantains. Plantains perform much better when they are not mixed up with cassava on the same plot.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji ni ato aha plantains lɛ amli. Plantains tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa kɛji akɛ akɛ cassava efutuuu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are my plantains struggling when I have cassava growing on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cassava does not do well alongside plantains in a plantain nursery setup. Removing all the cassava so that only plantains remain will help the crop grow much better.
ga: Cassava tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ plantains ahe yɛ plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ koni ŋmei lɛ pɛ eshwɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: What should I do if I notice cassava growing in my plantain field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ ŋmei miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-plantain shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should remove all the cassava from the farm. Plantains grow best when cassava is completely cleared out and only plantains occupy the space.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmei fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Plantains daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ajie ŋmei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli ni plantains pɛ yeɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to mix different crops together or keep only plantains on my farm plot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafutu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi loo makpa plantains pɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When a farm plot or nursery is meant for plantains, mixing in other crops like cassava reduces performance. It is better not to mix them and keep only plantains on that plot.
ga: Be mli ni ato he ni aduɔ nii loo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha plantains Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei futu mli lɛ, ebaaha esɛɛnamɔ aba shi. Ehi akɛ okɛ amɛ akafutu ni obua plantains pɛ anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I leave shade trees standing on my plantain farm to protect the crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui aŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: No, this crop does not like trees overhead. Plantains require full exposure to direct sunlight to grow well, so you should not leave shade trees on the farm.
ga: Dabi, nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ sumɔɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi. Esa akɛ plantains lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ oshiɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my plantains not growing well under the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantains do not like shade from trees. They need an open field where they are completely exposed to light to thrive.
ga: Misumɔɔɔ tsei ahe hulutsoo. He ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ ni la babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Do plantains prefer full sunlight or shaded areas?
ga: Ani plantains sumɔɔ hulu ni eyi obɔ loo hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ?

english: Plantains do not like shade trees. They must be left fully exposed to direct sunlight in order to perform well.
ga: Misumɔɔɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Esa akɛ aha hulu la lɛ abote mli tɛ̃ɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my plantains if I leave too many trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantains lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The plantains will not perform well because they do not like shade from trees. They require open land with direct light exposure.
ga: Plantains tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛsumɔɔɔ tsei ahe hulutsoo. He ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ ni kane yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia amɛ.

english: How do I prepare my nursery plot so my plantains give the best results?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa midumɔwui lɛ koni maná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Ensure you remove competing crops like cassava and keep the nursery dedicated to plantains alone, while also clearing away trees to give the crop full sunlight.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni ojie tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ, tamɔ yucca lɛ, ni okɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ ahi shi kɛha plantains pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jiemɔ tsei lɛ koni tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: If I want to focus only on plantains, what changes should I make to my mixed farm?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama plantains pɛ nɔ lɛ Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsake mi-mixed farm lɛ?

english: You should clear out all the cassava plants and remove interfering trees so the plot is left solely for plantains and fully exposed to light.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie yucca tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ashi gbɛ aha plantains lɛ ni aha amɛná la babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die so quickly when I plant them in the open sun without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like small children—their leaves and roots burn easily in intense heat. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby creates a cooler canopy that protects young cocoa from drying out before its roots grow deep.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii. Ebaai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni naa wa he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi dani shishifãi lɛ abote mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize crop turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient in the soil. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to catch maximum light. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing diseases and helping the plant feed itself so it can grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot weather or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Plantain plants have broad, heavy leaves and shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. When the heavy bunch of plantains forms, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to uproot if it is not supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni amɛtsii. kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni dumɔwui babaoo ba Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akɛ ebaajie shishifãi lɛ kɛji ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tso atsu nii ni okɛfi amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and produce very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive unwanted guests at a meal—they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving your crops weak and starved.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ niyenii ashishi. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ha onibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ aye bo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills all the spaces in the soil with water, leaving no air for the roots. This wet condition causes cassava tubers to suffocate and decay from soil rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hei fɛɛ. ni eshiuuu kɔɔyɔɔ ko kɛhaaa shishifãi lɛ Shihilɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn soft and spoil very fast after I pick them on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting vegetables in peak heat makes them retain internal heat and lose water rapidly, which speeds up rotting. Harvesting early in the morning keeps the produce cooler and fresher for a longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsu nii kɛkpa aduawai lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɛɔ mli dɔlɛ mli ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ agbo oya. Nibii ni akpaa lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efeɔ ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do small insects make holes and white powder in my harvested maize after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii feɔ bu kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli beni mikɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs inside the dried maize. Drying your maize thoroughly and using proper storage containers or approved storage dust stops the pests from eating into the stored grain.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛtoɔ mli loo sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaye ŋmaa ni ato lɛ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally recharges the soil nutrients for whatever crop you plant next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops still get diseased even after I apply the crop medicine I bought from the chemical store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mihe yɛ tsofafeemɔ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ etsu nii moŋ?

english: Crop medicines must be matched correctly to the specific disease or pest affecting your plant. Applying the wrong chemical, mixing it incorrectly, or applying it at the wrong stage of plant growth will fail to protect the crop, regardless of how good the chemical claims to be.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ahe tsofai lɛ kɛ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yeɔ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ akpã gbee pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛfutuɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni ejaaa mli lɛ nyɛŋ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni tsofai lɛ kɛɛ amɛhi ha.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Retaining large shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates living canopy shields that protect delicate seedlings and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ahe nitsumɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin with yellow leaves even though it is raining heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green leaf growth. Heavy rains can also wash away surface nutrients from the root zone if fertilizer is not applied in the correct amounts and at the right time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awooo mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do fall armyworms spread and destroy my maize crops so quickly during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs that hatch rapidly in warm, dry weather. The young caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant where they eat new leaf growth, making early detection crucial before the damage becomes widespread.
ga: Moth caterpillars fɔɔ wɔji ohai abɔ ni fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ. he ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni eda lɛ Feemɔ ni ana mra Enɛ he miihia waa titri dani fitemɔ gbɛ eshwa.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, won't I harvest more tubers from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa bulbs babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close forces the plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room underground for its roots to swell into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How can I be sure that a new high-yielding maize seed will actually grow well in my local soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-abele dumɔwu hee ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Before planting an entire farm with a new variety, test a small demonstration plot on your land. Soil conditions, weather, and pests vary by location, so testing on a small scale proves whether the new seed delivers good yields in your local environment.
ga: Dani obaadu ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii heei fɛɛ lɛ Kaa nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko okwɛ. Yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛi srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kaa bibioo baatsɔɔ kɛji dumɔwui heei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and using balanced fertilizer helps flowers stay on the plant so they can turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes black pod disease to spread so fast on my cocoa trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, cool, and wet conditions. Rain drops bounce the fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods, and dense tree leaves trap moisture that allows the disease to multiply quickly across the farm.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ duŋ, he ni ejɔ, kɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Ni tso lɛ yibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi niyenii titrii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legume crops have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil. Intercropping them feeds neighboring plants like maize and improves soil quality naturally.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Kɛ kooloi bibii be mli ni mikɛ amɛ toɔ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevil insects lay hidden eggs inside grains before or during harvest, which later hatch into larvae that eat the inside of the seed. Thoroughly drying grain to low moisture levels and storing it in airtight bags stops these pests from multiplying.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛtee dumɔwui amli dani akpaa loo yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli. Sɛɛ mli lɛ, enɛɛmɛi fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafa babaoo.

english: Why does my crop grow very well on my neighbor's land, but poorly on my farm just across the road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani nakai ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ?

english: Soil can change completely within short distances. Differences in soil depth, water drainage, organic matter, and nutrients mean your farm soil might have different needs than the land right next to it.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ kwraa yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi yɛ srɔtoi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi fe shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: My farm land has dark soil in one section and reddish soil in another; do I need to treat them differently?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ yɛ fã kome kɛ shikpɔŋ tsuru yɛ fã kroko. Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ amɛ aye yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ?

english: Yes, soil color shows what minerals and organic material are inside. Dark soil usually holds more decomposed plants and moisture, while reddish soil often contains more clay or iron and may require different fertilizers or organic manure to perform well.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ su tsɔɔ akɛ shika tsuru kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ mli. Shikpɔji ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni fiteɔ babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Shi shikpɔŋ tsuru lɛ, shikpɔŋ loo dade babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ni ekolɛ amɛbaabi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my sandy soil dry out very quickly after rain compared to clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles with big gaps, allowing water to drain through easily. Clay soil has very small, tightly packed particles that trap and hold water longer, though it can get hard when completely dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmeii wuji, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nu baatsɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ yɛ nibii bibii waa ni ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. ni haa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaawa kɛji egbi kwraa moŋ.

english: How do I determine the right amount of fertilizer to put on my farm instead of just copying standard quantities?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ he mfoniri kɛkɛ?

english: The right amount depends on your specific crop type and what nutrients your soil already has. Using general amounts like 200kg per hectare is a guide, but testing your soil helps you apply the exact amount needed so you do not waste money.
ga: Nɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ kilogram 200 yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ baatsu nii lɛ ji gbɛtsɔɔmɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa baaye abua bo ni okɛ shika pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa bo lɛ atsu nii. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ofite shika.

english: No, adding too much fertilizer can burn the roots, weaken the crops, and damage the soil. Plants only take up what they need, and excess fertilizer gets wasted or washes away with heavy rains.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Tsei kɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ tsuɔ nii. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ loo ehoɔ kɛyaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: I heard standard fertilizer application rates work in other countries; why might those same rates not give me good results in Ghana?
ga: Minu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ. Mɛni hewɔ nakai nyɔmɔwoo lɛ nɔŋŋ haaa maná yibii kpakpai yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Soils in Ghana have different heat, moisture levels, and mineral compositions compared to other countries. Fast heat breaks down nutrients quickly in tropical soils, so local soil conditions require tailored feeding rather than copying foreign standard rates.
ga: Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔɔ. Humidity level Ni shika tsuru ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔto kɛ akɛto maji krokomɛi ahe. Dɔlɛ ni yaa oya lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔji ni mli edɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ biɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee maŋsɛɛ nyɔmɔwoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he mfoniri
