english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so that rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours. Place it near the base of the plant during early growth stages and cover it lightly with soil so the rain carries it down to the roots instead of washing it across the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Okɛwo tso lɛ shishigbɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. ni okɛ sũ fioo aha he koni nugbɔ lɛ aho tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo amɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating from waterlogged soil. This happens when land is farmed continuously without replacing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsakeee.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield every year even though I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every season without giving it time to rebuild. Rotating crops or adding organic matter helps replenish the worn-out soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛma ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni efite lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use animal manure and compost to feed my crops instead of chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, animal manure and compost feed the crop while improving the soil's structure and ability to retain water. While chemical fertilizers work fast, organic manure builds long-term soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. kɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ kɛ nu ni ehiɛɔ lɛ he lɛ he Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya moŋ Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can take up water, causing the seedling to dry up.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo loo dumɔwui bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa waa akafee lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. gĩ dumɔwui lɛ

english: How does providing extra water to my farm during the dry season help my crops produce more?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu kroko ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Water carries essential nutrients from the soil up into the plant's stems and leaves. During dry periods, giving crops water prevents heat stress, keeps leaves green, and ensures pods and fruits keep growing big instead of falling off early.
ga: Nu woɔ niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baaye abua ni ajie dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛjɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ aduawai lɛ daraa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbee shi oya.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain inside my new cocoa farm without harming the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee mli ni miyeee kookoo lɛ awui?

english: Yes, planting plantains alongside young cocoa is actually beneficial because the wide plantain leaves provide temporary shade for young cocoa seedlings while giving you food to harvest while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ agbɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoa trees turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your trees are lacking vital soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the ground is flooded with excess water. When plants lack nutrients, they cannot produce the green pigment needed to make their own food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Ensuring the tree gets proper moisture, nutrients, and protection from pests allows flowers to develop into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa, niyenii, kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why do black spots spread so fast on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates wet, humid conditions that encourage fungal diseases like Black Pod to grow. Splashing rain drops spread fungal spores from infected leaves and soil onto healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa. Ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ he hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra unwanted branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni ataooo kɛjɛ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that suck energy away from pod production. It also lets sunlight and air pass through the tree branches, which lowers moisture and prevents diseases from settling on the crop.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ pod feemɔ mli lɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ehaaa helai akpɛtɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster in soft, moist soil compared to hard, dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Soft, moist soil allows plant roots to spread out easily to drink water and absorb nutrients. In hard, dry soil, roots struggle to penetrate the earth, causing crop growth to slow down.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛnu nu ni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei daa blɛoo.

english: Why do pests attack my farm more when my trees are growing fresh green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ be mli ni mitsei lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Insects prefer soft, fresh leaves because they are tender, easy to eat, and full of rich sap and moisture. When trees produce new growth, insects naturally gather to feed on the tender parts.
ga: Kplukai sumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ehee ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ayeɔ Eyɛ vitreous nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ hee lɛ, ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛye fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: A cocoa pod changes color completely when it matures, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange-yellow. Picking pods only when they change color ensures the beans inside are fully developed and high quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru nɔ kɛyashi yellow-orange nɔ Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ pɛ kɛji amɛhe su tsake lɛ, no haa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant different types of crops on my land instead of just planting maize on all my acres?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Planting different crops, known as crop diversification, protects your farm against pest outbreaks and unpredictable weather. If a pest destroys one crop type, your other crops can still survive, ensuring you do not lose your entire harvest and income for the season.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi adumɔ Ale lɛ hu akɛ tsei amlijaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ ahe. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai kpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko hiɛ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ baahi shi lolo. Enɛ haa onibii fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛ shika ni onáa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why do crops like maize grow faster and healthier when I plant them near cowpeas or beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa daa oya ni amɛnáa hewalɛ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have a natural ability to take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Other crops growing nearby can feed on this natural fertilizer, helping them grow stronger without requiring as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hu baanyɛ aye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest because there are more plants on the farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo ejaakɛ miyɛ tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting crops too close together forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, thin plants that produce smaller fruits or grains compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I finish clearing my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to your local soil and climate, making them very quick to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early gives your main crops the space and food they need to outgrow the wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei titrii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains so the soil absorbs deep moisture. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout, only to dry up and die if the hot sun returns for several weeks.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni mli edɔ waa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi ebaagbi ni egbo kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ ehe ekoŋŋ otsii babaoo.

english: If I finish harvesting my crops today, can I immediately start planting new crops on the exact same land?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɛnɛ Ani manyɛ mabɔi tsei heei dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to let the soil rest or add manure and organic matter before planting again. Continuous planting without restoring nutrients wears out the soil, leading to weaker crops and lower yields in the next cycle.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he dani odu ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baaa lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi yɛ fã ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crop yields getting smaller every year even though I keep using the same land and seed type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients out of the earth every single season. If you keep growing the same crop without adding organic manure or rotating with other plant types, the soil becomes exhausted and can no longer feed new plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ organic fertilizer fataaa he loo okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsakeee lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops so they do not spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready, such as leaves turning yellow or brown, stems drying out, or grains turning hard. Leaving fully mature crops out in the field too long exposes them to insect attacks, mold, and rot from late rains.
ga: Tsei baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji amɛfee klalo, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ, amɛshishifãi ni miigbi, loo dumɔwui ni mli wa. Nibii ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ atutua tsei lɛ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested grains properly in the sun before packing them into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains carry hidden internal moisture. If you seal damp grains in sacks, the trapped moisture creates heat and dangerous fungal mold that will ruin your stored food within a few weeks.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ wo kotoku mli lɛ, nu ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa. Enɛ baafite niyenii ni ato lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: If I expand my farm to a much bigger size, why do my crops seem to catch diseases much faster than before?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mlilɛɛ babaoo lɛ Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe helai oya fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: When you grow crops across large fields, pests and crop diseases can spread uninterrupted from plant to plant. Larger farms require wider plant spacing, crop rotation, and frequent field checks to prevent diseases from spreading quickly.
ga: Beni oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ be fɛɛ be. Okwaafoi wuji biɔ hei wuji ni aduɔ nii yɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ shii abɔ koni helai akagbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why are small holes and sawdust-like dirt appearing inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmei jeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli?

english: That is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the fresh leaves inside the central funnel. The dirt you see is actually their droppings, which shows they are actively feeding inside the growing plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nakai baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Muji ni onaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ Ni no sɛɛ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiye tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from fresh leaves, or by a virus these insects spread to the plant while feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei amli beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ amli

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp weather. Raindrops splash the fungus from the soil onto the low pods, causing them to turn black and decay.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to tall sticks in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso fĩɔ tso nine kakadaŋŋ agbo ko he yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps the vines off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha wain tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay close to the surface. When heavy bunches form at the top, strong winds or soft, rain-soaked soil can easily pull the shallow roots right out of the ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni ŋmeii ni tsii feɔ yɛ ŋwɛi Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient for leaf health. It can also happen during dry spells when the plant drops lower leaves to save water for the cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba yɛ fɛ̃i be mli hu beni tso lɛ shiɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni ekɛ nu ato kɛha ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if it rains continuously for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When soil stays flooded with water for too long, the roots drown, and rotting bacteria quickly attack the soft tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ oya.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Stress makes the plant drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves droop during the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In mid-day heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the warm soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to save water, but usually stand up again by evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu nu he. shi bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, making the plant pull remaining nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko bɛ otso lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good for my farm if I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina loo ŋmeii fata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees and plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ ni midu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong direct sunlight, which scorches their leaves and dries out their tender stems. They need partial shade from plantains or forest trees during their first few years to stay cool and retain moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbiɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo koo mli tsei adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly and stop growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni edaaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaf stops expanding properly, causing it to wrinkle and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Baai ni efite lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry out and fall off without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile, meaning flowers cannot fertilize to form fruits. The plant drops these unfertilized flowers to save energy during extreme heat stress.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi awo fɔfɔi amli koni amɛwo yibii. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ nɛɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa waa baa lɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop yield smaller cobs when I plant during the minor rainy season compared to the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli wa fioo lɛ mli kɛ akɛto be titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season in Ghana has shorter, less predictable rains and lower soil moisture levels. Without enough consistent water during the flowering stage, maize cobs cannot fully develop or fill out with grains.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be yɛ Ghana lɛ faaa kwraa. nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ba shi. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ adara loo amɛbaafee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my sweet orange trees drop half of their young fruits when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yibii lɛ fã fite beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Fruit drop is the tree's natural way of managing its energy. If the tree sets more fruit than its roots, water supply, and leaf energy can support, it sheds the excess tiny fruits so the remaining ones can grow big and ripe.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Kɛ tso ko woɔ yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eshishifãi, nu, kɛ baai ahewalɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ, Ebaafite eyibii bibii lɛ. excess Koni aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting in the barn even before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ po baa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural internal biological clock. Once their natural resting period ends, warming temperatures in late dry season signal to the tuber that it is time to shoot sprouts, even without soil or water.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni wala yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee lɛ haa bulbs lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃, kɛji shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ po.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops immediately after I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, shallow root systems that absorb water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. If you do not clear weeds before fertilizing, the weeds will eat the plant food first and choke your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye tsei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ebaafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem as tubers expand.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to burn the cleared bushes on my land or leave them to rot before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã tsei bibii ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo mahã amɛgboi dani madu?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation to rot creates a natural cover that feeds nutrients back into the dirt and keeps moisture in the soil. Burning clears the land quickly, but it destroys important organic nutrients and leaves the soil dry and exposed to heavy sun.
ga: Tsei ni ajie lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya sũ lɛ mli ni eha sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahi shi. Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi ebaafite niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover. Rotating your maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas rebuilds soil fertility and keeps future harvests high.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake o-ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stems when planting them in my field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems should be planted about one meter apart. Giving them enough space prevents the roots from competing underground for water and soil nutrients, allowing each plant to grow large, heavy tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mita kome. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates living umbrellas that protect the seedlings from sunburn and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni oduɔ nii lɛ

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores their deep green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are naturally tough, allowing them to absorb rainwater and grow rapidly. Early weeding is necessary so these wild plants do not steal light, water, and nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ baakã shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛdaraa oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehe miihia koni nɛkɛ koo mli tsei nɛɛ akaju la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do small worms suddenly appear inside the funnel of my maize plants during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from moth eggs laid on the leaves and feed on the soft, growing heart of the maize plant. Checking your farm early and treating the funnels protects the crop before significant damage occurs.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai anɔ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmei tsei atsuii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni ŋmeii lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani efiteɔ waa.

english: Why do spots appear on my pepper leaves after a few days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cool, wet conditions help fungal and bacterial spores spread across wet leaves. Spacing plants properly allows air to dry the foliage quickly, and removing spotted leaves early prevents the disease from spreading through the whole farm.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ haa fungal spores kɛ bacteria gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's harvest produce smaller crops than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum strength and high yield in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those boosted genetic traits in the second generation, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my crop roots are getting damaged by too much water in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efite mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: When soil stays continuously soaked, roots cannot get oxygen and begin to rot, causing the plant leaves to turn pale, droop, and drop off. Digging small drainage furrows across your field helps excess water flow away safely.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsaa Yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, enɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize leaves get dark spots after heavy rain, and how do I stop it from spreading?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa?

english: Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the plant leaves. Keeping your tools clean, weeding regularly, and removing infected leaves quickly stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eshwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Onitsumɔ dadei lɛ ahe tsemɔ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. ni ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does one sickly tomato plant make all the healthy plants around it turn yellow and wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ naa amanehulu lɛ? Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ?

english: Crop diseases are often spread by tiny insects or fungal spores carried in the air. When an infected plant stays in the field, pests carry the sickness directly to neighboring crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji mɛi ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai. loo fungal spores ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli Beni tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hela yaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I clear away rotten fallen fruits from underneath my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie aduawai ni egboi ni egbee shi kɛjɛ midumɔ nii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Rotting fruit left on the ground attracts fruit flies and pests that lay eggs. These pests multiply quickly and attack the good fruits still growing on your trees.
ga: Yibii ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbalaa yibii amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni woɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ faa oya ni amɛtutuaa aduawai kpakpai. ni miida yɛ otso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ

english: Is it safe to feed leftover cassava peels and crop stalks to my farm animals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, but crop waste must be clean and processed properly. Fresh cassava peels contain natural toxins that can harm animals, so they must be dried thoroughly in the sun or boiled first to make them safe.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashwieɔ lɛ ahe atse ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai fɔji ni baanyɛ aye kooloi awui yɛ cassava ŋmɔji heei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo ahoo lɛ dani ehi.

english: Will planting cassava and maize together in the same field harm my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: If planted too close together, crops compete for water and soil nutrients, which can weaken both. Spacing them correctly allows both crops to feed well without choking each other.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Will applying just a small handful of fertilizer really help my crops if I cannot buy a whole bag?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe baagi ni eyi obɔ?

english: Yes, placing a small, measured amount of fertilizer directly near the root zone of each plant gives the crop maximum nutrients right where it needs it without wasting money.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni asusu he lɛ wo tso fɛɛ tso shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ he ni ehe hiaa amɛ lɛ ni amɛkuuu shikatoohe lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is fertile enough to support a good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture and has earthworms is rich in organic nutrients. Pale, hard, or sandy soil needs compost or organic manure added to help crops grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni wa, loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus afata he koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested corn turn moldy and develop white dust inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mold grows when grains are put into storage while still holding moisture. Thoroughly drying your corn under the sun until it is completely hard keeps it clean and free from harmful toxins.
ga: Mold daa kɛji akɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ mli fũu. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe tseɔ ni tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli.

english: How can smallholder farmers get access to certified seeds and quality fertilizers?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafoi bibii lɛ aná dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: You can register with your local agricultural extension officer or join a recognized farmers' cooperative to receive approved, high-quality inputs distributed through official agricultural programs.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe nine ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. aloo okɛ ohe awo okwaafoi akuu ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli Koni enine ashɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni ajaa kɛtsɔɔ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Are there official rules about which chemical sprays I can use on my food crops before selling them?
ga: Ani mlai komɛi yɛ ni amralo lɛ wo yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ dani mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, agricultural authorities regulate farm chemicals. You must use approved plant protection chemicals and observe the required waiting days after spraying before harvesting so the produce is safe for people to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli nitsumɔhei kudɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. ni okwɛ be ni he hiaa ni akɛmɛɔ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa nii lɛ sɛɛ. Koni nibii ni adu lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbɔmɛi baanyɛ aye

english: Can I plant prekese trees intentionally on my farm, or do they only grow by themselves in the forest?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ Prekese tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli pɛ?

english: You can plant prekese intentionally! While many prekese trees sprout naturally from seeds dropped by wild animals in the forest, you can also collect the seeds, raise them in nursery bags, and plant them on your farm like any other crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ yiŋtoo ko adu prekese po! Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi srɔtoi babaoo daa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni koo mli kooloi shiɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ amli moŋ, shi Obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui hu anaa. Atsɔse lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotoku mli ni okwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fɛɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa farmers keep large forest trees like prekese inside their farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi komɛi kɛ koo mli tsei wuji tamɔ prequese tsei toɔ amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Forest trees like prekese provide beneficial shade that protects cocoa trees from scorching sun and dry winds. Their fallen leaves also rot to feed the soil, and the fruits give farmers extra food or income.
ga: Koo mli tsei tamɔ Prekese haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ hu fiteɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. ni aduawai haa okwaafoi lɛ náa niyenii loo shika kroko

english: If a young prekese tree grows on its own in the middle of my farm, should I clear it or leave it?
ga: Kɛji Prekese tso bibioo ko diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ ko teŋ Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo mashi lɛ?

english: It is usually best to leave it and clear only the weeds around it. Naturally growing economic trees are already well-rooted and adapted to your soil, so caring for them saves you the stress of planting new ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi lɛ kɛkɛ ni okɛ jwɛi awo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Cashew tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ shishifãi yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe esa kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei nɛɛ akwɛmɔ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei heei adumɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I get seeds from wild forest trees to plant them on my own land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana dumɔwui kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli ni madu yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can gather healthy, fully ripe pods that have fallen to the ground under mature trees, crack them open to harvest the hard seeds, and soak or file the seed coat before planting them in nursery soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ anaa. Gbalamɔ amɛ koni okpa dumɔwui ni wa lɛ. Ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ awo mli loo okɛfile mli dani okɛwo ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ.

english: Will growing forest trees next to my cocoa compete with my cocoa trees for plant food?
ga: Koo mli tsei ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi cacao tsei lɛ kɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha tsei niyenii?

english: Deep-rooted forest trees mostly take water and nutrients from far underground, so they do not starve your cocoa. Instead, their deep roots bring up minerals and their leaves drop natural fertilizer onto the topsoil.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo naa amɛnu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhaaa hɔmɔ aye o-cocoa lɛ. Mohu ɔ, sisifãhi nɛ a mi kuɔ ɔ gbalaa sika tsuhi kɛ jeɔ a mi. Ni amɛbaai lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long does a prekese tree take from planting until it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani prekese tso ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: A planted prekese tree typically takes between 5 to 7 years to start producing fruit pods, depending on how fertile the soil is and how much sunlight and water it receives.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, eheɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani Prekese tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ aduawai ŋmɔji ahe shishi. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu hulu la kɛ nu ni anáa lɛ falɛ

english: Why do some trees thrive inside the thick forest but struggle when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli, shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa lɛ?

english: Forest trees are used to cool shade, high moisture, and rich soil made of decomposed forest leaves. When planted in open, hot fields without cover, young seedlings easily dry out and die.
ga: Akɛ koo mli tsei tsuɔ nii koni akɛha hulutsoo, hulutsoo babaoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni akɛ koo mli baai ni fiteɔ fee lɛ haa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Should I cut the lower branches of large shade trees growing on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, pruning lower branches allows filtered sunlight and air to reach your cocoa plants below, preventing mold and diseases while still keeping the farm cool.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ shɛɔ o-cocoa tso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai anaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: If a valuable wild tree grows naturally on my land, do I have the right to harvest its fruits?
ga: Kɛji koo mli tsei ni jara wa lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Ani miyɛ hegbɛ akɛ mikpaa yibii lɛ?

english: Yes, if the tree grows on your private farm or managed land outside a protected forest reserve, you have the right to harvest, use, or sell its fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tso lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ loo he ni okwɛɔ nɔ yɛ koo ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ kponɔ. Oyɛ hegbɛ akɛ okpaa eyibii lɛ, okɛtsu nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I contact an extension officer to visit my farm and advise me on tree planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matswa extension officer ko ni ebasara ŋmɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋaawoo aha yɛ tsei adumɔ he?

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district office, join a local farmers' group, or ask fellow farmers for the contact number of the extension agent assigned to your community.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Okɛ ohe awo okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ mli Aloo bi onaanyo okwaafonyo ko ni ekɛ extension agent ni akɛwo akutso lɛ mli lɛ atswa lɛ nɔmba.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains or keeping tall trees gives them shelter, keeps the soil moist, and helps them grow strong during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, loo tsei kakadaji ni ooodu lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛna he ko ni amɛhi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow when the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ yaa nɔ edaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to stay green and healthy. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or growing beans in the field before planting maize helps restore this nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani aduɔ ŋmei lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam plants need plenty of sunshine on their leaves to produce food for big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground where diseases live and exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi aha he ni agbele ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, protects the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the roots cool, reduces the need for frequent watering, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ efooo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni afɔɔ amɛ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: These pests are fall armyworms that feed on the soft growing center of the maize plant. Checking your crop early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts early in the morning helps control them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa yɛ lɛ anɔ. Okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ tsei nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellowish with light green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. You can prevent it by planting healthy, disease-free stem cuttings and choosing modern cassava varieties that naturally resist the sickness.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni ohala ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over at the roots before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when underground pests like nematodes or stem borers eat away the roots and stem base. Planting clean, treated suckers and keeping the base of the plant free from rotting material keeps the roots strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers ye amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni atsa amɛ, ni aha shishitoo lɛ akafee nɔ ko ni fiteɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off extra branches and water shoots from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ aniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: Cutting unwanted branches, known as pruning, lets air and sunlight flow through the tree. This reduces humidity inside the farm, preventing damp diseases like black pod disease and directing the tree's energy into producing large cocoa pods.
ga: Ale niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hu akɛ tsei ni afoɔ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ helai ni mli edɔ tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven watering. Watering your tomatoes regularly and adding lime or wood ash to the soil helps the plant absorb enough calcium to grow healthy fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow so many green leaves but fail to produce flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen from soil or fertilizer, they spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers. Beans make their own nitrogen, so they need fertilizers richer in phosphorus to encourage flowering and pod formation.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Beans baanyɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ewo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and sensitive to harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa from direct sun and heat until they are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ nuɔ he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená la ni fa babaoo.

english: When is the right time to start giving strong fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ obɔi mi-ŋmei lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔmɔ?

english: Young maize plants only need light nutrients when they are small. Once they reach knee height and grow strong stems, they enter a rapid growth phase where they need stronger, solid fertilizers like NPK or Urea to build healthy cobs.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni ji ŋmãa lɛ biɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ amɛji bibii. Beni amɛshɛɔ amɛkuɛ he ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni wa Amɛbaabote be ko ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni wa tamɔ NPK loo urea koni amɛkɛma ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings look sad and weak for a few days after I plant them in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ feɔ awerɛho ni amɛhe waaa gbii fioo komɛi beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. Moving seedlings from a sheltered nursery bed into the main farm damages their tiny feeder roots and exposes them to hotter sun, causing them to droop until their roots adjust and start drinking water again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi bibii ni haa amɛ niyenii lɛ, ni ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ nu numɔ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are starting to build tubers underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ miibɔi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii akwɛ̃mɔ?

english: In the first few months, cassava spends its energy growing tall and making leaves. After about six months, leaf growth slows down and the stems thicken, which shows the plant is shifting its nutrients downward to swell the roots into large tubers.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ baakwɛ ni ewo baai. Yɛ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, baai lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛmiiya shi koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its blossoms to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛhe. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering washes away essential plant food from the soil and drowns the roots, stopping them from breathing. When roots cannot get air, they cannot absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baaho tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. suffocate Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani midumɔwu titri lɛ je kpo?

english: Yes, you should remove extra suckers so they do not steal food and water from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: My yam vines are flowering, so does that mean the yams underground are ready to harvest?
ga: Mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miikwɛ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: No, flowers on yam vines only show that the plant has matured above ground. The yams underground need a few more months after flowering to store energy and expand, until the leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Dabi, fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ pɛ akɛ tso lɛ edara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ahe miihia nyɔji fioo krokomɛi yɛ fɔfɔii asɛɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛyashi baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my mango tree drop so many small fruits soon after they form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Yibɔ babaoo beni afee lɛ pɛ?

english: Trees often produce far more tiny fruits than they can feed with their water and food supply. The tree naturally drops the extra small fruits so it can focus its energy on growing the remaining ones into healthy, full-sized mangoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii. Nɔ ni fe nɔ ni abaanyɛ aye kɛ nu kɛ niyenii. Tso lɛ baajie aduawai bibii. come out naturally Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ ni efee mango ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my cabbage plant grow leaves for a long time without forming a tight head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni efeee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage plants must first grow strong outer leaves to act as solar panels that capture energy. Once the plant has gathered enough energy and reached the right maturity stage, it begins folding its inner leaves tightly together to form the cabbage head.
ga: Esa akɛ cabbage tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ kponɔgbɛ baai ni mli wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni heɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ bua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa ni eshɛ dalɛ he ni sa lɛ he lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ ejeɔ shishi ekɛ emli baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ koni efee kaabe yitso.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water, which starves the roots of air and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide large leaves that shade the cocoa, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can establish its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shishifãi.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in soil that holds too much water without proper drainage, allowing waterlogging and soil fungi to decay the crop beneath the surface.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi ni sũ mli ŋmeii fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. Without proper soil mounding around the base or wooden props to support them, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli tse. Kɛji muji ni sa ni ato he lɛ bɛ Shishitoo loo tsɔne ko ni akɛ tso fee ni akɛfiɔ esɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when water supply is inconsistent, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a virus transmitted into the plant by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛyaa tsei amli lɛ nɔ

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to climb toward sunlight so their leaves can make food, which is then sent down into the soil to build big, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tsei kakadaji ni amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni akɛ amɛbaai lɛ atsu nii akɛ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli koni efee bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of dirt, and a dry spell usually follows. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then die from lack of deep soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ he okadii nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Dumɔ mra tsɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds heavy-eating crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei ni yeɔ nii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if they are not tall enough to block the sunlight?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa po?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and nutrients underground with their aggressive roots, leaving less food and moisture available for your crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu fioo.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants roll their leaves inward during intense heat to protect themselves from losing water. By shrinking the leaf area exposed to the sun, the plant conserves moisture until the cooler evening.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshã yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They turn yellow and dry up when they lack shade from taller canopy plants like plantains or shade trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from under the leaves. This damages the tissue and can transfer viral diseases that stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni tsiɔ tsei anaa lɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. This stress prevents pollination, causing the flower stem to weaken and snap off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why is my maize growing tall with dark green leaves but making small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa, ni efeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When maize gets too much nitrogen fertilizer but lacks phosphorus or potassium, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems rather than developing full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ shi ebɛ phosphorus loo potassium lɛ ŋmãa kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmãa ni tsii

english: Why do my okra plants produce plenty of big green leaves but very few okras?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ miiwo baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi okra fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ?

english: Excessive manure or leaf fertilizer encourages foliage growth over fruiting. Okra needs balanced nutrients and phosphorus to trigger flowering and pod development.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ baai amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa fe aduawai ni ato lɛ. Okra he miihia niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ fɔsfɔs ni sa koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and fall over easily when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they stretch upward searching for light, making stems weak and thin. They also fight for limited soil nutrients, leaving them fragile against wind.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Ebaakpã kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Ehaa tso lɛ mli gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo. Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ hu koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ oya

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes maximum leaves to sunlight for energy. Keeping leaves off wet soil also prevents fungal diseases from spreading, resulting in larger tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: How do I know my cassava roots are ready before they start rotting in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving mature cassava in overly wet soil leads to tuber rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbɔ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eha oyitso agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop seedlings right after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants with strong root systems adapted to sprout rapidly and absorb surface nutrients before cultivated crops can establish their root network.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ nɔ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dani tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ato shishifãi ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. They need shade trees or food crops like plantains grown nearby to filter the sunlight and retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni ekɛjie hulu la lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete directly with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and light. Pruning away weaker suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ la. Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii lɛ amli ni ashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants flowering at the top when they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Ani no ji kuku kwraa lolo?

english: When maize faces heat or water stress early in its life, it gets shocked into flowering early to reproduce before it dies. Proper watering and timely fertilizer application help the plant grow tall before it flowers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa shɛ hulutsoo loo nu he haomɔ he yɛ eshihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ŋmãa fɔɔ mra ni efɔɔ bii dani egboɔ. Nu ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my upland rice plants turn yellow when rainwater collects and stays on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Upland rice varieties need well-drained soil and cannot breathe properly when submerged in water for too long. Excessive water suffocates the roots, preventing them from taking up plant food, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Don ŋmãa henɔi lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni enyɛɛɛ emu jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ awo lɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and protect itself from drying out. The plant goes quiet to survive the dry spell, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei feɔ dioo koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tsei aniji lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food that grows large tubers underground. Staking holds the vines high, preventing leaf rot from damp soil and ensuring maximum exposure to sunlight.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking the wain tso lɛ nɔ kwɔ Tsi baai ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa ni oha hulu la ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture changes suddenly between very dry and very wet. Consistent watering and light shade help the flowers stay on the plant to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Upward leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking juice from the leaves, or by a crop virus. Controlling insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can produce peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ Mra Be mli Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow so well without needing as much fertilizer as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli tamɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work together with tiny natural organisms in the soil to capture nitrogen directly from the air. This natural process feeds the cowpea crop and enriches the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpea kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ haa tsina tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yes, cassava stems have small eye buds that must point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to grow backward, weakening the plant and reducing crop yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Dumɔ ni akɛ ŋwɛi shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soil before planting seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams grow deep under the ground, so high mounds provide soft, loose soil for tubers to expand easily while protecting roots from waterlogging during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plant roots fight each other for soil food and water, and leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, working like natural food for the maize that will follow them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Extreme weather, such as intense dry heat or heavy water stress, causes pepper plants to drop their flowers to save energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa tamɔ latsaa ni mli egbi waa loo nu mli haomɔ Ha pepper tsei lɛ ashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Excessive moisture and lack of sunlight cause a fungus called Black Pod disease to spread rapidly through water drops on wet trees.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like whiteflies are sucking juice from the plant or that the plant is trying to protect itself from excessive heat and water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, miinu tso lɛ mli nu. Aloo kɛɛmɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture during dry days, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that create living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa plants establish their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to erect stakes or sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tso loo tso kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ?
