english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow big tubers underground. Keeping vines elevated off the damp soil also prevents leaves from rotting and catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ wein tsei lɛ wo ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for leaves to grow healthy and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or waterlog the ground, suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Should I apply my main fertilizer immediately when sowing maize seeds or wait until after they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui loo mamɛ kɛyashi amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait about 10 to 14 days after sprouting before applying your main fertilizer. Seeds carry enough stored energy to sprout, and early fertilizer placed directly on seeds can burn the delicate young roots before they can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awo mli. Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaves. These insects damage the tissue and can pass viruses to the crop, making the foliage twist and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi nɛɛ fiteɔ fãji ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa.

english: What is eating small holes into the central whorl of my maize stalks, and how do I handle it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? kɛtee mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides inside the center leaf whorl of young maize plants. Applying targeted treatments or approved insecticides into the leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening effectively controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo baai lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers soft and rotting underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Tubers rot underground when water collects around the roots for too long, especially in heavy clay soils during heavy rainy seasons. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps water drain away, protecting the roots from fungal rot.
ga: Tubers fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa waa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets extremely hot and dry, or when plants do not receive enough water. Without adequate moisture and moderate temperatures, the flowers fail to set fruit and naturally fall off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing seeds after the major rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil has received several consistent rains and stays damp at least a few inches deep. Planting after a single light rain can lead to poor seed germination if the soil dries out completely during a dry spell.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ shii abɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eha edɔ kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo sɛɛ Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops and slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi tsei titrii lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛdalɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that adapt quickly to the environment, allowing them to rapidly steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crop. Clearing weeds in the first three to four weeks gives your planted crops enough room to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii lɛ oya. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli jwɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like soft baby plants that burn easily in strong direct sunlight and hot winds. Leaving larger shade trees or planting temporary shade like plantains shields the delicate leaves from sun damage and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ tsei bibii ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant mean the crop is lacking nitrogen food in the soil. When soil nutrients are low, the plant takes whatever food it has left in its older lower leaves and sends it up to keep the young top leaves alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are natural soil builders. Their roots work with helpful microscopic organisms in the dirt to suck nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil, leaving behind free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanut tsei ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tswalɔi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛjie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Yam plants create tuber food inside their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground and spreads the leaves wide open to catch as much sunlight as possible, which feeds and swells the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa babaoo koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni baaye ni ebaafutu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off the plant before they turn into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects. When the plant feels stressed or thirsty, it drops its blossoms to save its own strength and survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ loo kumai miiye lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ mli ni ehi shi.

english: Why does my rice crop grow well in swampy flooded water while my maize plants rot and die in the same water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Rice plants have special air passages inside their stems and roots that allow oxygen to travel down to the root tips underwater. Maize plants do not have these tubes, so flooded water suffocates their roots and causes them to rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Abɛi tsei bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. Nu ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small plantain shoots grow together around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli ebɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight each other for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Cutting off extra shoots leaves all the food for the main plant to produce one large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe One plantain Plantains lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli. Kpojiemɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso titri lɛ niyenii fɛɛ koni ekɛfee plantains akuu agbo kome ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall fills up all the air pockets in the soil with water. When cassava roots sit in soaked soil without air for too long, oxygen cannot reach them, and underground soil rot fungus attacks the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ eyiɔ kɛ nu. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ta shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ ashɛ Oxygen he. Ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomato fruits happen when the plant cannot draw enough calcium mineral from the soil into the fruit. This is usually caused by irregular watering, such as letting the soil completely dry out before giving it water again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato aduawai anɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium mineral ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa egbiɔ kwraa dani afɔɔ nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow very big green leaves but fail to make many seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: If soil has too much rich nitrogen fertilizer, cowpeas focus on growing leaves instead of fruits. Alternatively, tiny invisible insects called thrips might be eating the tiny flower buds before they get the chance to grow into pods.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Cowpeas kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Nɔ kroko hu ji akɛ, kooloi bibii ni anaaa amɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ baanyɛ aye fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. Dani amɛbaaná hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and leafy, or that the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. loo shishifãi ni eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but only produce small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ yitsei bibii lɛ? Yɛ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and leafy tops instead of sending energy down to build thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e pee yi nɛ mi wa nɛ e he wa.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so crop roots can drink it in. If applied to dry soil under hot sun, the fertilizer gets hot and burns the roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni nu atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baadɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do people say that planting beans or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the plant harvested, that trapped food remains in the dirt for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni akpa tsei lɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant three or four maize seeds in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ duɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal water, manure, and sunlight from your young plants, starving them before they can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sun so they can make food faster, while keeping the stems off wet soil prevents leaves from rotting and catching fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ koni enyɛ ehoo nii oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akafee nɔ ni sũ ni mli ewo fɔ yɔɔ mli koni baai lɛ akafite ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot or dry. High heat stresses the plant and prevents the flower from getting pollinated to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee tsɔji bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in strong sunshine to hide from the heat and save water from escaping through their leaves; it is the plant's way of protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Koni ekɛtee ehe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he ni ekɛtsi nu gbɛ koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help my soil grow better maize next year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmei kpakpa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ efo. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even after I have already added fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight from the soil before your main plants have a chance to feed on them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otsei titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry period that can dry out and kill new sprouts; it is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha ŋmeii heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize crop to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crops usually leads to weaker plants and smaller yields in the next season, so it is better to buy fresh certified seeds each year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing any fruits when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress to pepper plants, making them shed their flowers to save water and energy instead of spending it on making fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava stems and leaves to curl up and show sticky white spots?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava tsei kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛŋ?

english: Curled leaves and white sticky spots are typically caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or mealybugs, which suck the sap from the plant and spread viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa

english: Why is it important to leave wide gaps between my tomato plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi he ko ni da yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing lets sunlight and air pass between tomato plants, which dries off wet leaves quickly and stops fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya, ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: How do I know when my yams are fully ready to be dug up from underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sweet potatoes lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakumɔ?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves turn yellow and the vines dry up, showing that the plant has stopped growing leaves and put all its strength into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tso lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ bulb ni eyi obɔ woɔ ehe.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and look lifeless immediately after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants suffer from transplant shock when suddenly moved to strong sunlight and new soil. Moving them late in the afternoon and watering them right away helps them adapt gently without dying.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli beni amɛfã kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ trukaa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe blɛoo ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly like straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in the heat. It is a natural defense signal showing that the plant is thirsty and trying to survive the high temperatures.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa be mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tsei ni amɛmiitao amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop during the prolonged dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to reduce their need for water. The plant goes quiet to conserve energy until the rains return to sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu he hiamɔ nii aba shi. Tsei lɛ feɔ dioo koni amɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ni baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my pepper seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry break that can scorch delicate young sprouts. Waiting until the major rainy season truly settles protects your seeds from drying out in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ eba shi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu odumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my yam crop producing lots of big green leaves above ground but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɛ baai agboi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant focuses all its energy on growing thick leaves instead of sending energy underground to build large yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni mli tse ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e kɛ pee yam tso agbohi.

english: Why are the flowers on my cowpea plants falling off before they turn into bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ pea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas drop their flowers when stressed by sudden heat, dry soil, or insect attacks. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve water and survive when conditions are difficult.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why should I prune off the small side branches growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Removing small side branches, or suckers, forces the plant to send its water and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on excess stems.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ lɛ, onyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What will happen to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, tall stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmãa bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds in my garden grow so much faster than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally aggressive at taking water and nutrients from the soil, which is why clearing them early is essential for your crops to succeed.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ basabasa yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why do some of my cocoa seeds fail to germinate even when I keep the nursery soil moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: Cocoa seeds lose their ability to sprout very quickly once taken out of the pod. If they dry out before planting or if the soil stays waterlogged and cold, the seeds will rot inside the earth.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ oya waa kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji egbi dani adu loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni edɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing leaves and stems. This often happens when the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rains wash away the soil's natural food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛyeɔ baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and drop off when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose water fast. Shade trees act like umbrellas that protect cocoa from harsh heat and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts alongside my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are helper crops that trap air-based plant food called nitrogen and feed it into the ground through their roots. When maize grows nearby, it feeds on this extra nitrogen for free.
ga: Beans kɛ peas ji tsei ayebualɔi ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ. ni etsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ yaka.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the soil when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need to breathe under the ground. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil without proper drainage, the roots choke, drown, and get infected by water-loving rot fungi.
ga: Esa akɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni hydrophilic rot fungi lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why does my plantain plant stop producing big bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ feemɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Trunk lɛ fɛɛ

english: The small shoots—called suckers—feed on the same root system as the main plantain trunk. If you leave too many of them, they steal nutrients and water, leaving the main plant with less food to form a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ yeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ plantain tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji oshi lɛ yɛ nɔ babaoo Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ náaa niyenii fioo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ kuu agbo.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber by catching sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high and spreads the leaves out so they catch maximum sun instead of bunching up on the ground in the shade.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni ená hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ

english: Why does cutting off old, dead branches from my mango tree make it bear bigger fruit later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso niji ni egbɔ ni egboi ni afoɔ lɛ haa ewoɔ yibii wuji yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming away non-producing branches stops the tree from wasting water and plant nutrients on weak wood. This redirects all the tree's energy into growing healthy branches that produce large, quality fruits.
ga: Niji ni wooo yibii lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha tso lɛ akafite nu ni ekɛdu niyenii ni haa tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa niji ni he wa ni woɔ yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat or severe water shortage. The plant drops its blossoms to save its own life when it feels it does not have enough water or food to grow actual peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa waa lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere amɛhe yiwala beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when there is water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it out of the ground. The leaves droop temporarily to conserve moisture, but usually stand back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. shi be fɛɛ be lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why does my cabbage plant shoot up flowers instead of forming a tight leaf head during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee baai ayitsei ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cabbage prefers cooler temperatures to form a firm head. When it experiences strong heat stress, it thinks it is going to die, so it skips making a leaf head and quickly sprouts flowers to produce seeds for survival.
ga: Cabbage sumɔɔ he ni mli ejɔ koni efee yitsei ni wa. Beni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kpe lɛ Esusu akɛ eegbo. No hewɔ lɛ efoɔ baa bulbs ni efeɔ lɛ mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya koni ekɛ dumɔwui awo koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my maize plants turn rich green when they get enough water, but turn yellow and pale when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa kɛ́ amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ? Shi etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Water acts as a bus that carries food and nutrients like nitrogen from the soil into the plant. When maize gets adequate water, it can feed properly and produce chlorophyll, which turns the leaves a deep green; without water, the plant starves and leaves turn pale or yellow.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii tamɔ bɔs ni tereɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nibii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops start to droop and wither when there is no rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plants use water to build pressure inside their stems and leaves to stay upright, much like air fills a tire. When the soil dries out, the plant loses moisture to the hot sun and deflates, causing it to droop as a protective attempt to save water.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee nɔnyɛɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi jaŋŋ. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yiɔ tai amli lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, tsei lɛ naaa nu yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛkuɔ shi. Ha egbee shi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni akɛto nu he lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops roll up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's self-defense trick against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun to slow down water loss through evaporation while it waits for cooler temperatures.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko teemɔŋ sane ni ekɛbuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa hulu la ni baa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu ni hoɔ oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does using a motorized pump to bring water to my farm help my crops grow better than relying on rain?
ga: Te pɔmp ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ nu kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A water pump gives you full control over when and how much water your crops receive. Instead of suffering through long dry spells between rains, your crops get a steady supply of moisture, preventing stress and ensuring high yields.
ga: Nu pɔmp haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ be kɛ nu ni otsei lɛ baaná lɛ nɔ kwraa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ daa. Etsiɔ haomɔ naa ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Is it better to pump water to my crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering under the hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant's roots can soak it up.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize if my farm runs out of water right when the plants are producing cobs?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ fo yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Flowering and cob formation are the most delicate times in a maize plant's life. If water drops at this stage, the plant gets severely stressed, leading to poor pollination, tiny cobs, or cobs with missing grains.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni jeɔ kpo lɛ ji bei ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmãa tso ko shihilɛ mli. Kɛji nu lɛ ba shi yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ waa. Enɛ haa pollination ni ehiii, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do some trees and cassava stay green during the dry season while my vegetable crops wither away completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kɛ ŋmei komɛi hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ be mli ni mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root systems; cassava and deep-rooted trees dig deep into the earth to drink underground water reserves, while shallow-rooted vegetables only reach the top layer of soil, which dries out fast.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi srɔtoi. Cassava kɛ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ, ni egbiɔ oya.

english: If my crops have already started wilting from lack of rain, will watering them immediately bring them back to life?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: If the leaves are only drooping but still soft, watering will revive them within hours. However, if the stems and leaves have completely dried out, turned brown, and become brittle, those plant tissues are dead and cannot bounce back.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gbee shi kɛkɛ shi amɛhe yɛ blɛoo lolo Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ baaha ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ baai lɛ egbi kwraa. Etsɔ blɔfo ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, nakai tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ gboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: Can giving my crops too much water from an irrigation pump cause them to wither just like a drought does?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu he pɔmpii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii agbi tamɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, too much water drowns the plant roots by suffocating the air pockets in the soil. Drowned roots begin to rot and can no longer absorb nutrients or water, causing the plant above ground to turn yellow and die.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo baaha tsei ashishifãi atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni eeefo mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni miiho lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii loo nu dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my farmland soil dry out so quickly a day after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposed directly to strong sunlight and hot winds loses moisture rapidly through evaporation. Covering your soil around crops with dry grass or leaves (mulch) traps soil moisture and keeps the ground damp much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. (Mulch) lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs a lot of to grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season gives the plant the food it needs to stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why are my vegetables growing so slowly and staying tiny even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa daa gbi?

english: If your soil is hard and tightly packed, plant roots cannot easily spread out to absorb food and water. Loosening the soil with a hoe and mixing in manure makes the earth soft so roots can grow deep and healthy.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo koni amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmei futu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and become small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and transmit diseases. Spraying early with neem water or insecticidal soap removes these pests before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛkɛ helai baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight into the tree canopy, and harvesting ripe pods quickly stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ abote tso lɛ shishi. Ni ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ haa helai gbɛfaŋ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When water collects on flat ground without draining, the roots drown and decay, which is why planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeee amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or irregular watering stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently damp by covering it with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them easy for wind to push over. Supporting the stems with bamboo poles and planting them in deep, well-drained soil helps keep them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young yam shoots as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Young yam shoots are weak and need maximum sunlight to start climbing their stakes. If weeds cover them early, they steal nutrients from the soil, resulting in small yam tubers at harvest time.
ga: Sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiitao hulu la babaoo koni amɛje tsei anɔ kwɔɔ shishi. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ ha nɔ oya Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas together in the same farm with my maize help my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer for your maize plants, while the tall maize stalks give the cowpeas room to vine.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa tsina ŋmãa hegbɛ kɛha wain tsei.

english: Why do small black insects ruin my harvested maize inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji miifite ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ mi-nitoohe kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those insects are grain weevils, which lay eggs and multiply quickly if corn is stored while still moist. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly under the sun until the grains are hard prevents weevils from surviving.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii, ni woɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshwereɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akahi shi.

english: Why is my maize turning light green and yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient it needs to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni afee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally recharges the soil with nitrogen.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when I plant many seeds in one small spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to develop strong stalks and bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my pepper plants so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ adalɛ miiya hiɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your pepper crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your pepper plants get all the resources they need to produce fruit.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua o-pepper tso lɛ ni ená nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn under direct heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains nearby provides a protective canopy that keeps young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aná nɔ ko ni baaha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings quickly between very dry and very wet. Keeping soil consistently damp helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers soft and rotten when I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged soil that lacks good drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before sowing my cowpea seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be dani madu tsina dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one isolated rain cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns. Waiting for the rainy season to fully settle ensures continuous soil moisture for seed survival.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ni ooomɛ koni etsɔ ais kwraa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: What is eating holes into my maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center shoot of the maize plant to feed. Checking fields early allows you to apply recommended treatments before the plant is destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye nii. He ni okwɛɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani tso lɛ afite.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and collapse around the trunk even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkuɔ shi amɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ he eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: This yellowing and drooping is usually caused by a soil-borne fungal disease that blocks water uptake inside the trunk. Removing infected mats and planting clean suckers prevents the disease from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tsiɔ nu ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni adu ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: What causes holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? Mɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars feed on the growing center of the maize plant, which can stop the crop from producing cobs if not managed early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii akawo cob kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ mra.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays trapped around them in heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bote amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Signs of nutrient-poor soil include weak plant growth, light green or yellowish leaves, and low harvest yields even when weather conditions are good.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ he ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmaa lɛ faaa eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi moŋ.

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baadu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, restoring essential nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize consume.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds aggressively steal soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight from your crops, leaving the main plants with fewer resources to grow big and produce food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ mli waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɛ nibii babaoo ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ agbo ni amɛwo niyenii.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to fight each other for limited soil nutrients and sunlight, resulting in tall, thin stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni hulu la ni baa shi lɛ hu faaa. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi kɛ́ eekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need stakes so their leaves can spread wide in the sunlight, which supplies energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa tso koni ekɛgbɛ baai lɛ eshwa hulutsoo be mli. ni ji hewalɛ jɛɛhe kɛha bulb agboi ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are regular. The first rain is often followed by a long dry period, which can scorch and kill newly sprouted seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ.

english: Why is it better to water my pepper plants early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the morning lets the soil absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun causes rapid evaporation, ensuring the roots get enough water without shocking the leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani enyɛɔ efoɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaaa baai lɛ akpokpo.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛtee shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers without making any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat during the dry Harmattan season, or when tiny insects like mirids attack the blossoms, causing the tree to shed flowers to protect itself.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mirages tutuaa fɔfɔii. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first shower; wait until the rain is heavy enough to soak the soil down to the depth of your hand so the seeds have enough moisture to survive if it doesn't rain again for a few days.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nu lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ oniji. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii fioo krokomɛi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land three times in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls a huge amount of nutrients out of the earth, so planting it continuously on the same spot drains the soil completely, causing your tubers to get smaller and weaker with each harvest.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ kpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ mli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up tightly and crinkling like paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ wolo lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath, or a virus spread by those insects that saps the sap and damages the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ehiɛ amɛshishi. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Ni baamu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni efite tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotting at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛmiitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, which often happens when watering is irregular or when the soil dries out completely between waterings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to suddenly appear and eat the central leaves of my maize field?
ga: Mɛni ha eba trukaa Kplukai bibii ba trukaa ni amɛye baai yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid secretly by flying moths; the young caterpillars crawl into the central leaves of the maize plant where it is dark and soft to feed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛtee lɛ amli. Kplukai bibii shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ duŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut to ensure my new planting grows well?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo koni makwɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni hi?

english: Always choose the thick, mature middle portion of a healthy cassava stem with visible buds, avoiding the soft green tip which rots easily and the very woody bottom which grows slowly.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ halamɔ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fiteɔ oya kɛ shishigbɛ ni tamɔ tsei ni daa blɛoo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam seed pieces sometimes rot in the soil before they even grow leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ baai lɛ?

english: Yam pieces rot in the ground if the soil holds too much water without draining, or if the cut ends of the seed yam were planted wet without being dried or treated to stop soil fungi from invading.
ga: Sweet potato fãi lɛ baagboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji sũ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛjieee nu. Aloo kɛji akɛ akwɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaagbee ni afo lɛ nɔ ni efɔ lɛ ni egbiko loo atsuuu he nii koni ŋmeii akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does leaving dry grass on top of the soil help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool under the strong sun, traps soil moisture so you water less, and prevents rain from washing away your fertile topsoil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree causing the whole stand to grow poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ Midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: The main plantain tree acts like a mother supporting her offspring. When too many shoots (suckers) grow at the base, they compete directly with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, causing wild, weak growth and small fruit bunches. Removing excess suckers allows the main plant to thrive.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ feɔ enii tamɔ nyɛ, ni ekwɛɔ ebii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ suckers (tso) babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Amɛkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa koo lɛ mli dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: When my main cassava plant loses its leaves, why do the young shoots around it also turn yellow?
ga: Beni mi yucca tso titri lɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle he fɛɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, etsɔ ŋmɔŋ hu?

english: Young side shoots rely heavily on the main stem for food and water stored in the system. When the main plant experiences nutrient lack or disease, it can no longer support the young shoots, causing them to suffer and turn yellow as well.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ waa kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni ato yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo hela he amanehulu lɛ Enyɛɛɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛnaa amanehulu ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ hu.

english: Should I trim off the extra young shoots coming out from the bottom of my pepper plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming extra lower shoots helps the plant focus its energy on building a strong stem and producing larger peppers, rather than wasting nutrients on unnecessary leaves close to the ground where pests hide.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a puɛɔ niye ní ɔmɛ a he ngɛ tsohi nɛ a he hia we nɛ a kɛ zugba a he nɛ koolohi nɛ a gbeɔ ní ɔmɛ yaa a he ɔ.

english: Why do the fruit bunches on my banana trees get smaller and weaker with every passing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ mi banana tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ? Ani bei lɛ eho?

english: Over time, old banana mats produce too many new suckers around the original tree. If these suckers are not controlled, the ground becomes crowded and depleted of food, causing each new generation of fruit to be smaller.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Banana ŋmɔ momo lɛ baajie ŋmeii heei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shishijee tsei babaoo tsɔ Kɛji anyɛɛɛ akudɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii hu baafee nɔ ni faaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ ayinɔ fɛɛ yinɔ bafeɔ bibioo.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing moisture in strong heat. Shrinking their leaf surface helps the plant conserve water until the cool evening arrives.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ naa. Baa lɛ hiɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops suddenly wilt and fall over even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ miiho trukaa ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: This usually happens when underground pests or root diseases damage the plant's root system. Even if water is present in the soil, damaged roots cannot take it up, making the plant behave as if it is in a severe drought.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi loo shishifãi helai fite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ amɛnii tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɔɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need taller crops like plantains planted right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller crops provide necessary shade and cool moisture, protecting the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together without leaving proper space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni he ko ni sa bɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their roots fight underground for water and soil food while their leaves block sun from one another. Leaving proper space ensures every plant gets enough light and nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my young tomato plants grow tall and thin instead of bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ miidara ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Fast-growing weeds block sunlight, forcing tomato plants to stretch quickly upward to reach the light. This creates tall, weak stems that break easily and cannot support good fruit.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwereɔ oya koni amɛná la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔ, efoɔ oya ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua yibii kpakpai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ.

english: If one crop in my farm gets a disease, why does it spread so quickly to neighboring plants?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eko mli hela lɛ emɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ egbɛ eshwa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: When plants are grown close together, their leaves touch and their roots share the same damp soil. Fungi and insects can easily travel short distances from an infected plant to infect healthy neighbor plants.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Baai lɛ taa amɛhe ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kome nɔ. Fungi kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aya he ko ni jɛkɛɛɛ. kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyashi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ mlɛo.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient crops need to stay healthy and grow big. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea back into the soil helps restore the green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata sũ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, protects the soil from hot sunshine so water doesn't dry up quickly. It also keeps the soil cool and eventually rots down to feed the plants.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. koni nu lɛ akagbi oya Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when planted in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa gives them shade and keeps the air moist, protecting the young plants during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant make food to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off wet soil where diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ yɛ he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes inside the fresh shoots of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii heei lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside young maize leaves. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening targets the worms before they destroy the growing center of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii baa bibii amli lɛ amli. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baatswa ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and shady environments. Pruning excess branches lets sunshine and fresh air reach the pods, drying out moisture so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Black pods ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the field, the roots get waterlogged and suffocate, allowing rot-causing bacteria to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli Shishifãi lɛ baaho ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they face stress from extreme heat or sudden dryness in the soil. Without consistent moisture during flowering, the plant sheds its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Plantain plants have very shallow root systems and carry heavy bunches near the top. Propping up the main stem with sturdy bamboo forks gives the plant extra support against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni enyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even if I cleared the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Weeds sprout quickly and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growth cycle ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Dalɛ be lɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection commonly called Black Pod disease. It spreads quickly in cool, wet, and heavily shaded farms, which is why letting sunlight and air into your farm by pruning helps prevent it.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni ebote oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naa lɛ.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before they turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers they cannot feed, but losing too many flowers is usually caused by dry weather, lack of soil food, or small insect pests attacking the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii. Shi bei pii lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa fɔfɔii

english: Cassava roots rot mostly when soil stays flooded with water for a long time, or when tiny pests create wounds in the roots under the wet soil, allowing water rot to enter.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Feɔ pilamɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, muji baanyɛ abote mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing nitrogen, which is its main food for growth. Heavy rains can also wash this food out of the reach of the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he ni tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same food nutrients out of the soil continuously. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to rebuild those missing nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatswa niyenii ni elaaje lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is very strong and can burn the tender stem and shallow roots of your crops. It works best when applied in a light ring around the stem where the outer roots can reach it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ eshã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Etsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he, he ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants burn and dry up during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have very sensitive leaves that cannot stand direct full sunlight. They need temporary shade from taller crops like plantains to shield them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni ŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ kwraa lɛ he gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ kɛha hebuu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if it is safe to plant my crop seeds after the very first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three reliable rains so the soil gets deeply wet. Planting after just one rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the sun comes back for weeks.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ otsii babaoo.

english: What causes tiny ragged holes in my maize leaves with little green powder inside the stalk?
