ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni powda bibii eŋɔli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm that crawl deep inside the plant tops to chew tender leaves before the maize ears appear.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii dani ŋmãa toi jeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and choke my crops right after I clear the farm and plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants built to quickly grab available water and sunlight faster than farm crops. Clearing the land exposes buried weed seeds to light, making them sprout all at once.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni ama amɛ koni amɛjie nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli. Ha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara shikome.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their roots are not strong enough to absorb enough water to stay cool. They need shade plants like plantain trees grown next to them to block the harsh heat while they are small.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahe waaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi fɛ̃i. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Wrinkled or twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap, which makes the new leaves grow out deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. ni haa baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe nɔ

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the tips instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and moving down the middle mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize plants need to build strong stalks and dark green leaves.
ga: Kaadii ni ji yellow lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ naagbee kɛyaa teŋgbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná ŋmãa ni wa kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer around my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ehe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a liquid so that plant roots can drink it. If you apply it to bone-dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer sits against the roots and can actually burn and destroy them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ nu bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ okɛ sũ ni egbi ni wui tsu nii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni egbe amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rains fall for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain stays trapped in flat ground, it drowns the roots, causing underground rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haa shikpɔŋ shishi fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my tomato plants without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛmli diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or irregular watering. If the plant feels it doesn't have enough steady water to support growing fruit, it drops its flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii lɛ tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: These caterpillars, known as fall armyworms, target the deep center roll (funnel) of the maize plant because it is soft, moist, and hides them from birds while they feed on the young leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Okɛ ohiɛ afɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ (cones) lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ blɛoo, amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i, ni amɛkɛ amɛhe teeɔ okpoi ahe beni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do tall weeds make my crops produce much smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors; they drink the water, absorb the fertilizer, and block the sunlight that your main crop needs to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛnuɔ nu, amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛhaa hulu la ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need tall sticks to spread their leaves high in the air where they can catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni baanyɛ aná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ̃ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many shoots grow from the same plantain base, they all fight over the same soil nutrients. Removing all but two or three strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida kɛjɛ plantain shishitoo kome mli lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my young mangoes keep falling off the tree onto the ground before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Young fruit drops to the ground when the tree lacks sufficient water during dry spells, when pests like fruit flies attack the skin, or when the tree cannot support all the fruits it produced. Regular watering and pest trapping help keep fruit on the branch.
ga: Yibii bibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua hewolo lɛ loo be mli ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai fɛɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over onto the ground whenever heavy rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (known as lodging) when their root systems are shallow, when stalks are weakened by insects like stem borers, or when seeds are planted too shallowly. Heap soil around the base of the stalks (earthing up) to give the plants stronger support.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa) kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ Be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ stem borers lɛ egbɔjɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ. aloo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (okɛ shikpɔŋ) koni tso lɛ mli awa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant onto the ground without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off without setting fruit when daytime temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Mulching around the roots keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs Mulching ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my yellow corn turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant is short on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and build leaves. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfee baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop in the same place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same field every season drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating crops, such as planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be lɛ Seasons lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct sunlight because intense heat scorches their leaves and dries out their roots before they grow deep. Keeping temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa trees while they establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant multiple maize seeds very close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited light, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small corn cobs. Spacing plants properly gives each seed room to yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha dumɔwui atsu fɛɛ tsu awo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into a tube shape during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves roll up to conserve moisture and reduce heat stress when the sun is very strong. Watering plants early in the morning and applying mulch around the base keeps moisture in the soil through the hot afternoon.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli wa waa. Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ nɔ leebi ni okɛ sũ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves and central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This destruction is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on tender plant leaves. Checking fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil mixtures into the funnel destroys the pests before they kill the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ baafite kooloi lɛ dani amɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the cassava roots, creating ideal conditions for fungal and bacterial rot to set in underground. Harvesting mature cassava promptly before heavy rainy periods prevents root loss.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛfo shikpɔŋ shishi. Kasava ni eda ni akpaa dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away and soaked the roots in too much water.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ nu tsɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sun without planting plantains near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo tsei komɛi bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct heat. Fast-growing plantain trees act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛha kookoo yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough under the ground to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready to harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with prominent scars, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Nɔ ko bɛ tsɔne lɛ mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni kadiɔ mɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants drop off to the ground without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime heat gets too high, when water is inconsistent, or when tiny pests damage the delicate blossom stems before pollination can happen.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii eba lɛ Kpata fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahiɛ dani pollination aba.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees easily fall over during strong windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow, widespread surface roots rather than a deep taproot. When soil becomes soft from rain and the fruit bunch gets heavy, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you prop the plant up with a wooden stake.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ ni aduawai akui lɛ batsɔ tsii Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ tso ko wo tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi.

english: Should I apply my solid fertilizer to the farm when the ground is dry or after rain has fallen?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain. Crops can only take up nutrients dissolved in water, and dry fertilizer placed on dry ground can burn crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tsei baanyɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛwo nu mli pɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early in the farm instead of waiting until the crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during the early weeks. This early competition permanently stunts crop growth even if you weed later in the season.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee otsii lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ mra be mli akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tsei adalɛ aya hiɛ kwraa. Kɛji akɛ okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can spread out to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight powers the leaves to create energy, which is sent down to build big tubers in the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfee hewalɛ. ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why does rice grow so well in flooded swampy ground while my maize dies if water stays on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that bring oxygen from the air down to their roots in wet soil, whereas maize roots suffocate and drown when covered in standing water for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni hiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ nu ni damɔ shi ha amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because it dries out their leaves and soil too fast. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside them provides the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ ni oooshi loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ni ooodu yɛ he kome Ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts alongside my maize will make the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii, ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an important nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season corrects this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in the soil around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rain drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing small, thin bunches compared to other farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa bibii ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ kui amli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: A plantain stem produces multiple small shoots called suckers that steal food and water from the main plant. Cutting away extra suckers and keeping only one or two allows the main plant to produce large, healthy bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers, ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ eko loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni miduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch during hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do tiny holes appear on my young tomatoes before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi tomato bibii lɛ anɔ dani amɛtsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po.

english: These holes are caused by small caterpillars called fruit borers that hatch from eggs laid inside the blossoms. Inspecting leaves early and removing damaged fruits prevents them from spreading to the rest of the crop.
ga: Buji nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ fruit borers ni jɛɔ wɔji ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ amli mra Ni ojie aduawai ni efite lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli hei krokomɛi.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every year strips away specific soil nutrients and lets pests build up. Alternating different crops each season gives the soil time to recover and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ bei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: How do I know it is safe to sow my seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light drizzle often leads to seeds sprouting and then dying if rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ kome pɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. If they do not have shade plants like plantains or Gliricidia growing over them, the harsh sun scorches their tender leaves, causing them to dry out and curl up.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji amɛbɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo glicidia ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ. Ha egbi ni ebɔle ehe.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the tips down to the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of older maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and build large cobs, so yellow leaves are a sign that the crop needs compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of plants called legumes that can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water settles around their roots for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better when I give them tall wooden poles to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ha lɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to reach full sunlight. Guiding the vines onto stakes keeps the leaves spread out to catch light for tuber growth and prevents leaves from touching damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛná la kɛha bulb lɛ dalɛ. ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree stop bearing big bunches when many small shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji feemɔ be mli ni miyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain trunk, they steal water and plant food from the main crop. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main plant to produce larger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Weeds grow faster than crop plants and steal the nutrients, water, and root space out of the soil. Even with good rainfall, your crops will stay small because the weeds are taking the food meant for your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee bibioo lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miitswa niyenii kɛha otsei lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and proper feeding help the plant hold onto its blossoms until peppers form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ niyenii ni sa haa tso lɛ hiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Tight upward curling of tomato leaves is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Spraying neem oil early or using clean seed helps stop whiteflies from spreading this virus across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ baa. Neem fɔ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Loo dumɔwui ni he tse ni oookɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii yɛŋ akagbɛ hela nɛɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell before the main rains set in. Planting right away causes young seeds to sprout, but their small roots quickly dry out when the sun returns before continuous rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ titri lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ akwɛ̃, shi amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi oya kɛ́ hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba dani nugbɔ lɛ tee nɔ nɛ.

english: Can I use water from a river near a galamsey site to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ Galamsey lɛ mli lɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu?

english: River water near galamsey sites often contains dangerous chemicals like mercury and heavy metals. Using this polluted water can poison your soil and make your vegetables unsafe for people to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ mercury kɛ dade ni tsii yɛ faa nu ni bɛŋkɛ Galamsey lɛ mli. Nu ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha o-vegetables lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ gbɔmɛi yeɔ.

english: Will boiling river water from a mining area remove dangerous chemicals before I use it on my crops?
ga: Ani faa mli nu ni mli edɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni atsaa shika tsuru yɛ lɛ baajie tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui dani akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: No, boiling water kills germs and bacteria, but it cannot remove heavy metals like mercury. Boiling actually reduces the water amount through steam, which can make the concentration of heavy metals even stronger.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbeɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ. Shi enyɛŋ ejie dade ni tsii tamɔ mercury. Nu ni shãa lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ lasu lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if the stream water I use for irrigation has harmful metals like mercury in it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ dade ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mercury yɛ faa mli nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu lɛ mli?

english: You cannot see, smell, or taste heavy metals in water. The only way to know for sure is to have your water tested by an agricultural extension officer or a laboratory, especially if there is mining upstream.
ga: Onyɛŋ ona, onu dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ he, loo onu he. Gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ole jogbaŋŋ ji ni oha okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo laboratori ko aka onu lɛ akwɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ yɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow even though I give them plenty of water from the local stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa lɛ mli haa amɛ lɛ?

english: If your water source is contaminated by mining activities, it may contain toxic metals like mercury. These chemicals damage root systems, preventing plants from absorbing nutrients properly even when watered regularly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onu jɛɛhe lɛ mli ewo muji kɛtsɔ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ekolɛ dade ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ mercury yɛ mli. Tsofai nɛɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ afɔse lɛ nu daa po.

english: Is it safe for me to plant maize on land that was previously used for illegal gold mining?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ shika tsuru tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Land used for mining often retains high amounts of heavy metals like mercury in the soil. Maize planted there can absorb these toxins through its roots, so the soil should be tested and treated before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa shika tsuru lɛ hiɛɔ dade ni tsii babaoo, tamɔ mercury, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ aŋɔ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Can cassava or yam plants absorb dangerous metals from polluted soil without showing signs of dying?
ga: Ani ŋmei loo ŋmei tsei baanyɛ ajie dade ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ ni ejieee gbele he okadi kpo?

english: Yes, root crops like cassava and yams can take up heavy metals from contaminated soil and store them in their tubers while still looking healthy on the outside.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie dade ni tsii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛto ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ kponɔgbɛ.

english: Will heavy rains wash away dangerous chemicals left in my soil by nearby mining activities?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni eshwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rain can wash away surface dirt, but heavy metals like mercury bind tightly to soil particles deep underground. They remain in the soil for a long time unless special soil treatment methods are used.
ga: Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shi dade ni tsii tamɔ mercury lɛ fĩɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe. Amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ja akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi tsu nii.

english: How do dangerous metals from mining sites actually get inside the food crops I grow?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni dade ni yɔɔ oshara ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔji amli lɛ boteɔ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ mli?

english: When mining waste mixes with water or soil, crop roots drink up that water just like nutrients. The plant then passes those heavy metals up into its leaves, stems, fruits, and seeds.
ga: Kɛji shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kɛ nu loo shikpɔŋ futu Tso shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ tamɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei kɛ nakai dade ni tsii lɛ yaa amɛbaai, amɛshishifãi, amɛyibii, kɛ amɛdumɔwui amli.

english: If my crops absorb mercury from contaminated soil, will it harm the people who buy and eat my harvest?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwie mercury kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ Ani ebaaye mɛi ni heɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, when human beings eat crops contaminated with heavy metals like mercury, those metals build up in their bodies over time and can cause serious long-term health problems.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adesai ye tsei ni dade ni tsii tamɔ mercury ewo mli lɛ, nakai dade lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni mli wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aba.

english: Why have my crop yields been getting smaller every year since mining activities started near my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi kɛjɛ be mli ni shika tsuru taomɔ nitsumɔi je shishi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Mining pollution contaminates water and soil with toxic metals that destroy beneficial soil organisms and weaken plant root systems, leading to stunted growth and smaller harvests.
ga: Mujiwoo ni jɛɔ shika tsuru tsaa mli lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ dade ni yɔɔ gbeyei. ni kpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa oya, ni amɛkpaa nibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow, and will applying fertilizer solve this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer (like Urea or NPK) restores nutrients to the soil, helping the plants turn green again and produce a healthy yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ (tamɔ urea loo NPK) tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi.

english: If I invest my money to buy store agrochemicals like Agromonte for my farm, how does that yield a profit for me?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ shika wo mli koni mikɛhe okwaayeli tsofai tamɔ Agromonte kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ. Te sɛɛnamɔ baajɛ mli aba aha mi tɛŋŋ?

english: Quality agrochemicals protect your crops from insects, diseases, and weeds while giving them essential nutrients. Healthy, protected plants produce far higher yields and better quality produce at harvest, which easily covers the cost of the inputs and leaves you with higher profits.
ga: Agrochemicals ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi, helai kɛ jwɛi ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa hu. Tsei ni abuɔ he ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo babaoo kɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ feɔ mlɛo. ni eha onine ashɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my new cocoa trees on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but yield very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of roots. Providing balanced soil nutrients and good sunshine encourages the plant to store food underground, giving you large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli. shishifã najiaŋ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ hulu la kpakpa ni akɛhaa lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi. haa bo yitso agbo

english: Will spraying weedkiller on my farm destroy my crop plants together with the weeds?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: It depends on the type of weedkiller you use. Selective herbicides are specially made to target specific weeds without harming your main crop, while non-selective ones kill every plant they touch. You must always select the right product for your specific crop.
ga: Edamɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛtutua jwɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ gbeɔ tso fɛɛ tso ni amɛkɛkpeɔ. Esa akɛ ohala nibii ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by hot dry weather, lack of water, or tiny insect pests attacking the blossoms. Keeping the soil moist and controlling insects allows the flowers to stay on the plant and develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni nu egbi, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi bibii ni akudɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to absorb enough sunlight and nutrients to grow a thick stem and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ená hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again during the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum yield in the first generation, but seeds harvested from those crops lose those special qualities. Planting saved hybrid seeds results in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and a lower overall yield compared to buying certified seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. Ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ lɛ he.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas replenishes soil fertility and breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: How does adding dried animal manure or compost to my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure and compost add organic matter that feeds the soil and helps it hold water longer during dry periods. They slowly release essential plant food over time, making your crops stronger, healthier, and more resilient.
ga: Manure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ fataa he. Amɛbaafee fiofio Ejieɔ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kpo yɛ be ni sa mli. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awa Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okɛ ohe awo mli

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight because their leaves dry out fast. Providing shade trees or planting plantains next to cocoa gives them living umbrellas that keep the air cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade ni akɛhaa loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Cocoa tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni shade lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yam plants make tubers under the ground using energy from sunlight collected by their leaves. Climbing up tall stakes keeps the leaves high above weeds where they can get maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ toɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting beans alongside my maize help my soil stay good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special plants that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This leaves free plant food in the dirt that helps crops like maize grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei aniyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight over soil food and water. Removing the weaker shoots lets the main tree direct all its energy into growing big fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ aduawai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do my vegetable plants drop their leaves and wilt during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. Mulching the soil with dry grass keeps moisture in the ground so the plant stays hydrated.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli fũu mli.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids that hide under leaves and suck out plant juices. Removing infested leaves early or using soapy water sprays can keep the plant growing normal leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Aloo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer from heavy heat, dry soil, or excessive water stress. Giving plants steady water and shade from harsh sun helps flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu he haomɔ babaoo kpe amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulu la ni naa wa ha tso lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does cassava become tough and woody if I leave it in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ tso lɛ?

english: As cassava plants get older, they stop storing soft starch in their roots and start turning it into hard plant fiber. Harvesting cassava at the right maturity time ensures the roots stay soft and tasty.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛtoɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of tiny holes when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyi kɛ akɛto kotoku lɛ mli?

english: Insects like weevils eat through stored maize grains if the seeds are not fully dried before bag storage. Thoroughly sun-drying grains before storage keeps insects away and stops mold from growing.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baaye ŋmãa ni ato. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani okɛ kotoku lɛ ato Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani okɛto koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: If my tomato plants give me a massive harvest very quickly, does that mean they will stop producing earlier?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo oya waa hu? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tomato baakpa yibiiwoo mra?

english: Yes, every plant has a natural limit to how much food and fruit it can produce in its lifetime. If a plant uses up its stored energy quickly to produce a fast, heavy harvest, it consumes its natural yield capacity sooner and ends its productive life earlier.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa husu yɛ niyenii kɛ yibii babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yɛ amɛwala beaŋ lɛ he. Kɛji nitsumɔhe ko kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ tsu nii oya koni ekɛfee nibii ni yaa oya ni tsii lɛ, Nitsumɔhei lɛ kɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ lɛ baatsu nii oya ni amɛbaagbe amɛ nitsumɔ shihilɛ lɛ naa mra.

english: If I give my maize plant extra fertilizer, will it keep producing more and more cobs endlessly?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe Ebaaha ŋmãa babaoo aba. Ebɛ naagbee loo ebɛ naagbee?

english: No, every seed variety has a natural limit built into its genetics for how many cobs it can make. Fertilizer helps the plant reach its maximum natural potential, but it cannot push the plant to produce beyond its built-in capacity.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii ahe husu ko yɛ ŋmeii enyiɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛwo lɛ he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛshɛɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsi tsei anaa koni amɛfee nibii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers instead of turning every single flower into a pod?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree can only support a fixed number of pods with the water and nutrients available to it. It naturally sheds extra flowers because it does not have enough energy reserves to develop all of them into healthy, full-sized pods.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ aye abua pods pɛ kɛji nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, ejieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi ejaakɛ ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants take a break and stop flowering for a while after I pick a heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yaa wɔɔ ni ekpaa fɔfɔi be fioo beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Producing a heavy crop exhausts the plant's internal energy reserves. After a large harvest, the plant pauses flower production to rest, build up new nutrients in its leaves, and rebuild its strength before it can yield again.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Yɛ kpamɔ wulu lɛ sɛɛ Tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔii feemɔ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Bɔɔ niyenii heei yɛ baai lɛ amli ni otswa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani ewo yibii ekoŋŋ

english: If I leave my cassava in the ground long past its maturity time, will the tubers keep growing bigger and better?
ga: Kɛ mishi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Ani yitso lɛ baatsɔ agbo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava roots reach a natural peak in how much starch they can store. Once they pass that stage, the plant starts using up its own stored food, causing the tubers to become woody, fibrous, and lower in quality.
ga: Cassava shishifãi yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ amɛyɛ starch babaoo fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛto. Kɛ nakai be lɛ ho lɛ Nitsumɔhe lɛ baabɔi niyenii ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eto lɛ fɛɛ kɛ nitsumɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafeɔ tsei, ŋmeii ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it recommended to pluck off the very first flowers on my young chili pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ ajie klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi chili tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing early flowers prevents the young plant from spending its limited early energy on a few small peppers. This allows the plant to focus on growing strong roots and branches first, which leads to a much larger overall yield later.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ tsiɔ tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkafite amɛshishijee hewalɛ fioo ko yɛ ŋmeii bibii fioo komɛi ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's high-yielding hybrid maize yield far less when I plant them again this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa beni midu lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created to deliver their maximum yield potential only in their first generation. The second-generation seeds lose that built-in energy boost, resulting in smaller cobs and lower total production.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aha yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛmli lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii baa, ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does fast-growing maize usually give smaller total harvests than long-duration maize varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ woɔ yibii fɛɛ ni baa shi fe ŋmãa henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fast-growing varieties are built to complete their lifecycle quickly to survive dry spells, meaning they have less total time to collect sunlight and nutrients, resulting in a lower maximum yield potential.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbɛ be babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli ni amɛkɛbaabua hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ aná lɛ baa shi.

english: Will my oil palm trees keep producing the same size of fruit bunches as they get older?
ga: Ani mi-oil palm tso lɛ baawo aduawai akui ni dalɛ tamɔ bɔ ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms have a natural production cycle where yield peaks in mid-life and gradually declines. As trees grow older, transporting nutrients to the top requires more energy, naturally reducing the size and number of bunches produced.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ ni nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ amɛwala teŋgbɛ ni ebaa shi fiofio be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ biɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, panicles ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ dalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my watermelon vine produce larger fruits when I pluck off some of the small young watermelons early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon tsei lɛ woɔ yibii wuji beni mifoɔ watermelon bibii lɛ mra lɛ?

english: A vine has a limited amount of food and water to share among its fruits. By reducing the total number of watermelons, the plant directs all its fixed resources into fully filling the remaining ones, making them bigger and sweeter.
ga: Wein tso lɛ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu fioo ko ni ekɛ aduawai lɛ baaja. Kɛtsɔ watermelon lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ Nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ watermelon ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛhe ŋɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and brown, and who should I ask for help before buying chemical spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni namɔ esa akɛ mabi yelikɛbuamɔ dani mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen or is being attacked by pests like fall armyworm. Instead of guessing at agrochemical shops, consulting a local agricultural extension officer helps you identify the exact problem so you don't spend money on the wrong treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm miitutua lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu he yɛ okwaayeli tsofafeemɔ shwapo ko mli lɛ, okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ agba sane lɛ baaye abua bo ni oyoo naagba lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni okafite shika yɛ helatsamɔ ni ejaaa lɛ he.

english: When my tomato leaves start getting black spots and curling up, does that mean the fruit underground or on the stem will also spoil?
ga: Beni tomato baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa ŋmeii diji ni amɛkpãa amɛhe lɛ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hu baafite?

english: Leaf spots and curling are usually caused by fungal or viral diseases. When leaves get sick, the plant cannot produce enough food, which stops the fruits from growing big and causes them to rot before harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal loo virus helai kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ curling baa. Kɛji baai lɛ hela Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ waaa ni amɛgboi dani akpaa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Ensuring steady moisture and seeking officer advice on pest control helps the plant hold its flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni otao ŋaa kɛjɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in a field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under the harsh direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a living umbrella, protecting them until they are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu nakai tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: If my crops are growing slowly, why is it better to consult an extension officer before buying fertilizer at the market?
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobi mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ dani ohé ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Slow growth can be caused by poor soil, bad seeds, hidden root pests, or wrong soil acidity. An extension officer can check your farm first so you don't waste money buying the wrong type of fertilizer that might harm your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha ekwɛ̃ blɛoo. dumɔwui gbohii Shishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni okafite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni baanyɛ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stems rot in the ground when I plant them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need moisture in the soil to form new roots and shoots. If planted in hot, dry soil, the stems lose all their stored water and dry out or rot before they can establish roots.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛfee shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ nu fɛɛ ni ato lɛ ni egbiɔ loo egboɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why do certified seeds from the agriculture office give a better harvest than seeds I save from my previous farm harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases, withstand unpredictable weather, and grow uniformly. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds around my maize crop cause the ears of corn to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle No hewɔ lɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ toi bibii?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients directly from the soil that your maize needs. When weeds grow close to your crops, the maize starves and cannot form full, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa o-ŋmã lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: In intense afternoon heat, water evaporates from plant leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of the plants keeps the soil cool and moist throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: When my yam leaves turn dark early in the season, why does it affect the size of the tuber in the ground?
ga: Beni mi sweet potatoes lɛ su mli tseɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ enɛ saa tuber lɛ dalɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam leaves act like factories that make food for the tuber growing underground. If leaf diseases like anthracnose kill the leaves early, the plant stops making food, leaving you with very small yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ nitsumɔhe, ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ foliar helai tamɔ anthracnose kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ oya lɛ, Tsei lɛ baakpa niyenii feemɔ. Enɛ haa onáa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and developing small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bu bibii lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are often caused by pests like the fall armyworm, while yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Extension officers recommend checking under the leaves early in the morning to catch armyworm caterpillars early before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi leebi koni anyɛ amɔmɔ ŋmeii mra. dani ekpata ŋmei ni miida lɛ hiɛ

english: Black spots on cocoa are caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and shade. Pruning surrounding trees to let in sunlight and air helps dry out the pods and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ shia mli shihilɛi amli. Tsei ni afolɔ abɔle he lɛ Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aye abua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wrinkled during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in hot sun to conserve water by reducing evaporation. If the leaves unfold when the sun goes down, the plant is simply protecting itself; if they stay curled, it may be a sign of sap-sucking insects or severe drought.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe. Kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛkoto lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee kooloi ni nuɔ nu loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa he okadi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together or grown in soil with too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy developing leaves and stems to reach sunlight instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii koni amɛná hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛaato niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli.

english: Healthy soil is usually dark, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well after rain, and contains earthworms or decayed plant matter. Hard, pale, or overly sandy soil lacks organic nutrients and needs manure or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli tseɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ, shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli tse, loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ tsɔ ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmei loo ŋmei afee ŋmei.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land strips the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi bɛ. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ni kɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baa Tsakemɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Beans and legumes pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, serving as a natural fertilizer for the maize. In return, the strong maize stalks give the bean vines something to climb on.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa wain tsei lɛ naa nɔ ko ni amɛkwɔɔ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agro-dealer give better crops than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial seeds are often hybrid varieties bred specifically for high yields, uniform growth, and resistance to local diseases. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over generations, resulting in weaker plants and lower production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekome kɛ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds kill my young crops so quickly if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gbeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ oya kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and aggressively consume water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives young crop roots full access to nourishment so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛyeɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. koni amɛná hewalɛ

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my grain maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Maize is ready for grain harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels become hard with a tiny black layer visible at their base. Harvesting too early causes the kernels to rot during storage.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni nɔ ko bibioo ko ni yɔɔ diŋ yɔɔ mli. Abaanyɛ ana yɛ shishigbɛ Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct heat and harsh sunlight. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the fragile seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛ baa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, cool environments. Pruning overcrowded branches allows air and sunlight into the farm, which helps keep pods dry and reduces fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni edɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shweremɔ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential nutrient that helps plants build green leaves and grow strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground and improves maize yields in the next planting.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is overloaded with bush growth, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing leaves above ground instead of storing food in root tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ fe nine. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunshine to manufacture food for growing thick tubers. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground with stakes maximizes sunlight exposure and prevents leaves from rotting.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni mli tse ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ afite.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any peppers start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat or water stress. Ensuring consistent watering during dry periods keeps the flowers healthy so fruit can develop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during windstorms before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ko mli dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can become unstable if too many shoots grow around one stem. Removing extra suckers leaves enough root strength and nutrients for the main tree to hold its weight.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee nɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo bɔle tso kome he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tso titri lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the amount of crop I harvest if my farm has enough space?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and light from your crops under the ground and above, causing your crops to grow weak and yield far less fruit.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ ekãa juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ ŋwɛi fɛɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why should I trim off extra shoots and branches from my cocoa trees when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii kɛ eniji ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tso nɔ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Trimming removes unproductive branches that consume food meant for pod growth, allowing the tree to direct its energy toward making large, healthy pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii ni yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ kɛha pod lɛ dalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni mli wa.

english: What happens to my crops when the rains do not fall as expected?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: When rain is delayed or light, crops get stressed, their leaves may wilt or turn yellow, and they cannot pull nutrients from the soil, which leads to slow growth or low yields.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ loo la fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe. Baai lɛ baanyɛ agbo loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni enyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo loo ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Maize leaves roll up during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to reduce leaf surface area and prevent water from evaporating off the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ. Bɔni afee ni ajie baa lɛ hiɛ he ni nu lɛ akajɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do cassava plants stay green and survive even when there is no rain for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nyɔji babaoo po lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its upper leaves to conserve water and relies on energy stored deep inside its underground tubers, making it very tough during dry periods.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu he, ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why should I not apply chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ efataaa he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil; applying it to dry ground means the plant roots cannot absorb it, and the concentrated fertilizer can burn and ruin the roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo hei ni egbi lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are yellowing because of missing soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: When crops lack vital nutrients like nitrogen, the older leaves at the bottom turn pale yellow first while the rest of the plant remains small and weak.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Which short-season crops can I plant to harvest quickly before the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu koni maná oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Crops like cowpeas, vegetables, and early-maturing maize varieties grow quickly and can be harvested in 60 to 90 days, providing fast food and income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei, aduawai kɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛ shika ni anáa.

english: Is it wise to plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky because the first rain is often followed by a long dry spell; waiting until the rains become steady ensures your seeds will not dry up after sprouting.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grow much faster towards the middle of the rainy season than at the beginning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ fe shishijee lɛ?

english: In the middle of the rainy season, the soil stays warm and constantly moist, allowing root systems to fully expand and feed the plant efficiently.
