ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass creates mulch, which shields the soil from harsh sunlight, keeps soil moisture from escaping, and keeps root areas cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa eje kpo. kɛ shishifã lɛ he ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i

english: Why are my crop yields getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same piece of farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly uses up the same specific nutrients year after year, exhausting the soil unless you rotate crops or add compost and fertilizer.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Esa akɛ akɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii afi fɛɛ afi. Enɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: How do I separate plants that grow in clumps without damaging their roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbala tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kui amli lɛ amli ni mifiteee amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: To divide clump-forming plants, water the soil first to make it soft, then gently lift the plant out and carefully pull the stems and roots apart with your hands. Making sure each split piece has healthy roots attached helps it grow strong when replanted.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ojara tsei ni abua naa lɛ amli awo kui amli. Nu afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni efee blɛoo, no sɛɛ lɛ, wó tso lɛ nɔ blɛoo ni okɛ oniji agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli blɛoo. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni fã fɛɛ fã ni mli egbala lɛ aná shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛkpɛtɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni edara waa kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of day to split and replant my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aja mitsei lɛ amli ni madu?

english: The best time to split and transplant crops is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is not hot. Planting during cooler hours prevents the newly divided stems from losing water and dying from heat shock.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ agbala mli ni ajie lɛ ji leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ lɛ Dumɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni akatse tsei heei ni mli eja lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite nu ni amɛgboi kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa.

english: How do I know if a plant shoot is big enough to be split off from the mother plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he?

english: A shoot or sucker is ready for splitting when it has formed its own small leaves and visible root buds at its base. If it is too small and lacks roots of its own, it will struggle to survive when separated.
ga: Tso loo tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaajara mli kɛ́ eyɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni anaa yɛ shishigbɛ. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ bibioo tsɔ ni ebɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi Ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi kɛji akɛ agbala mli.

english: Why do my local crop varieties grow differently than foreign seed varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Local Ghanaian crop varieties have adapted over a long time to survive local weather patterns and pests, making them hardy. Foreign crop varieties are often bred for higher yields but usually require more water, fertilizer, and special care to grow properly.
ga: Ghana tsei henɔi lɛ etsake amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ amli. ha amɛhe awa Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi koni amɛná yibii babaoo. Shi bei pii lɛ, ebiɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ dani amɛnyɛ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose between planting a local seed variety and a new improved variety?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Choose local varieties if you want reliable crops that handle heat and poor soil with lower costs. Choose improved varieties if you have access to regular water and fertilizer, as they can grow faster and produce larger harvests.
ga: Halamɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi kɛji oosumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii he nii yɛ shika fioo mli. Halamɔ srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ oyɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How close together should I space my plants when putting them in the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ tsei awo he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miidu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Plants need enough space so their leaves receive sunlight and their roots can gather water and nutrients without competing. Giving them proper spacing leads to larger leaves and stems, while planting too close makes them thin and weak.
ga: He ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia tsei koni baai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni amɛshishifãi lɛ abua nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ gbɛ ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ tsei lɛ adara. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo ni amɛhe ejɔ.

english: Can I plant different types of leafy crops together in the same farm bed?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ baai? Ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwɔ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, you can group different leafy crops together as long as they have similar watering and fertilizer needs. Grouping crops with different heights can also help taller plants provide gentle shade to delicate leafy greens.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ akui. baanyɛ afee ekome Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ yɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiamɔ nii ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ, Tsei ni kɛlɛ srɔtoi lɛ akui baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni amɛha tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aná hulutsoo blɛoo.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to thin out or pull up extra seedlings that grow too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie loo wɔjie dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Thinning out extra seedlings leaves only the strongest shoots in the ground. Removing weak seedlings eliminates competition for plant food, allowing the remaining plants to grow into much larger, healthier crops.
ga: Kɛ́ afee dumɔwui lɛ bibii lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ tsei aniyenii lɛ baa shi. Ye obua tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my leafy green vegetables produce huge leaves while others stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ baai wuji ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ baai bibii lɛ?

english: Broad, large leaves depend on rich soil nutrients—especially nitrogen—and consistent soil moisture. Plants in poor, dry soil will remain small because they lack the energy needed to expand their leaves.
ga: Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ agboi lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ baakã he afee bibii ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛgbala amɛbaai lɛ amli.

english: Why do the outer leaves of my crops turn yellow while the new inner leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mligbɛ baai heei lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Outer leaves turn yellow when the plant is short on water or soil nutrients, causing it to move stored food to the growing tip. Removing yellow outer leaves helps the plant direct its remaining energy into fresh, healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ naa ni miida lɛ. Kpojiaŋ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall sticks instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves up on stakes helps them catch maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to make more food and grow larger tubers underground while keeping leaves safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce weaker crops than certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crop harvests lose their original strength and disease resistance in the next generation. Certified seeds are specially produced to ensure uniform, high-yielding, and disease-resistant plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tso ni akɛfee ekome ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ baafite eshishijee hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni tsei lɛ afee ekome, amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the lower parts of the plant, usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the primary nutrient plants use to stay green and grow vigorously.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ titri jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hei lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess rainwater in poorly drained soil blocks oxygen, causing the roots to suffocate and break down into wet rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ, ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ.

english: Curling leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck plant juices and transmit viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛkɛ helai baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering or poor soil conditions.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii titri yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for nearby plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when plants have established roots and are entering fast growth—usually two to three weeks after sprouting—and when the soil is damp enough to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tso lɛ ehiɛ shishifãi ni eedara oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli nibii

english: Why do crop diseases spread much faster on my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria thrive in wet and humid weather. Raindrops splash disease spores from infected plants onto healthy leaves, and moisture helps those spores grow quickly.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa nakai ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without taller shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees nearby to block the harsh sun, the heat scorches the leaves and dries out the soil, turning the leaves yellow and crisp.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I see tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves of my young maize plants early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ leebi.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides deep inside the funnel or whorl of the maize plant during the cool parts of the day to feed on young leaves. Treating them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the stalk.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ loo amɛmli ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Tsamɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing leaves or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo baai loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves or spreading a plant virus. When these insects suck out the sap, the leaves warp, and the plant loses its ability to make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ, Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. The plant sacrifices the flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and stems on top instead of storing starch in roots below the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ starch kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans before my maize will make the maize yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei dani mikɛ mi ŋmei lɛ wo mi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha mi ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have beneficial bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this natural fertilizer left in the ground.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil lacks nutrients before I even plant my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu?

english: You can look for wild plants and weeds that appear stunted, or check if leaves from previous harvests turned yellow or purple early. A soil test or guidance from a local extension officer can confirm exact nutrient levels.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi ni egbɔjɔ. Aloo kwɛmɔ kɛji baai ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ mra. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo ŋaawoo ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔ ko ŋɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ama niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ mi pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) growing around the parent plantain tree steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main trunk. Removing extra shoots leaves only 1 or 2 strong stems, resulting in larger and heavier bunches of fruit.
ga: Tsobii bibii (tsoji) babaoo tsɔ ni miida yɛ ehe. Dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa aduawai ni dara ni tsii baa.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops underground when they are not touching the crop leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ awui? Be ni eshɛɛɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Underground, weed roots spread rapidly and compete directly with your crop roots for water and plant nutrients. Even if weeds do not shade your crops, their roots eat the food and drink the moisture meant for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi jwɛi shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛkɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii. Shi kɛlɛ, jwɛi lɛ haŋ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yeɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell when it is safe to plant my seeds at the beginning of the rainy season so they don't rot in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ehi akɛ ooodu nugbɔshiimɔ be mli tsei koni dumɔwui lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seeds rot if you plant after a light early rain that is followed by a long dry spell. It is safe to plant when the soil stays continuously moist to the depth of your hand span after two or three steady rains.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi kɛji odu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nɛɔ mra ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooodu be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛyashɛɔ onine mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will give the plants the nutrients they need to grow green and yield well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha baai ni wa aba. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my cassava grow better afterwards?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cassava lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the legume crops finish, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground to nourish the next crop you plant, like cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmãa tsei lɛ anaa Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I wait until after the rainy season starts strong before putting fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can soak it up. If you apply fertilizer to dry soil, the roots cannot take it in, and a sudden heavy downpour might wash it off the farm before it can help your crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and need shade to protect their soft leaves while their roots develop. Leaving large trees or planting plantains provides necessary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa anáa hulutsoo ni he hiaa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it important for me to make soil ridges across a slope instead of up and down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Making ridges across the slope acts as small dams that catch rainwater and slow it down. If you make ridges up and down the hill, heavy rains will run down rapidly, washing away your valuable topsoil and fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ ŋshɔkpɔ bibioo ko. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Kɛji oma ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ ko nɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa shi oya. Ekɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the soft middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer feeding in the moist inner center (whorl) of young corn plants. Catching them early and spraying targeted biological or chemical treatments into the central leaf funnel stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ (rings) lɛ. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii ni akɛshwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ tsitsii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe properly. When heavy rains leave standing water in the soil for too long, oxygen gets trapped out, causing the roots to drown and fungal rot diseases to spread rapidly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen lɛ baatsi mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni fungal rot hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil rapidly switches between being very dry and extremely soaked. Keeping moisture levels balanced in the soil helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ oya lɛ teŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ja lɛ ni abaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up like small tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji bibii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in strong sunshine to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun, which stops the plant from losing too much water. If the leaves open back up in the cooler evening, it is just the plant protecting itself from heat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Koni akɛba he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akafite nu babaoo. Kɛji baai lɛ fã yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Eji tso ko kɛkɛ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why is it bad for me to save seeds from this season's hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ baato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created by crossing specific parent plants to yield heavily in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth and much lower yields in the next season.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What should I apply to my new tree seedling right after putting it in the ground?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo dumɔwui heei ahe beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Applying a specialized root-developer fertilizer right after planting helps the seedling establish strong, mature roots quickly so it can start growing fast.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni he hiaa waa kɛha shishifãi lɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni daa oya koni amɛje shishi amɛdara oya.

english: Why is it important for my young tree to build strong roots early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni midumɔwui lɛ ato shishitoo ni wa mra lɛ?

english: A tree needs strong, well-developed roots to draw nutrients and water efficiently from the soil, which allows the rest of the plant to grow faster and healthier.
ga: Tsei hia shishifãi ni wa, ni eda jogbaŋŋ koni amɛjie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ni edaa oya ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Can I use root-boosting fertilizer on any type of tree crop I plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shishifãi ni akɛwoɔ tsei fɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ atsu nii?

english: Yes, root-developer fertilizers are general feeding products that work effectively across different tree crops to help any newly transplanted seedling establish its roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi amli ŋmɔshi nibii ji niyenii ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei kɛ tsei srɔtoi anɔ. Koni eye ebua dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi.

english: What does NPK fertilizer do for my young tree?
ga: Mɛni NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kɛhaa mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: NPK supplies three main nutrients—nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium—that feed the tree's leaves, roots, and overall stem, giving it the energy needed for rapid growth.
ga: NPK lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii etɛ haa: naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. ni haa tso lɛ baai, shishifãi, kɛ eshishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni eda oya.

english: Is root developer fertilizer different from NPK fertilizer?
ga: Ani shishifãi ahe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, a root developer is specially formulated to jumpstart root strength right after planting, while NPK provides general nutrition to support ongoing stem and leaf growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ aba amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni NPK haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How often should I feed my young trees with fertilizer after planting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha tsei bibii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young trees benefit from regular nutrient intake; following a consistent routine, such as weekly applications, ensures the plant gets a steady supply of food as it grows.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ daa lɛ he sɛɛ. Ni aaaye nɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ nɔ, tamɔ otsi fɛɛ otsi ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ koni aha tso lɛ niyenii daa be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: What steps can I take to make my newly planted seedlings grow faster?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ adara oya?

english: You can speed up tree growth by applying a root-boosting fertilizer right after planting to build a solid root base, followed by routine NPK fertilizer feedings.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha otso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni odu lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛfee shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Does my young tree need fertilizer every week or just once when planting?
ga: Ani mi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii daa otsi loo shikome pɛ yɛ dumɔ mli?

english: While initial root fertilizer gives the tree a start right after planting, keeping up with regular weekly NPK feedings provides continuous energy for fast development.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee shishifãi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eje shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ, shi NPK ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa otsi lɛ baaha ená hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ koni etsɔ oya.

english: Why does my seedling need to focus on root growth before it can grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni midumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama shishifãi lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: A tree cannot support height or heavy branches without a mature root system; developing strong roots first gives the tree the anchor and feed lines it needs to grow tall.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ loo amɛniji ni tsii lɛ anɔ kɛji shishifãi ni eda bɛ. Shishifãi ni mli wa ni anáa klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ naa ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Is it necessary to fertilize right after planting, or should I wait for the tree to settle first?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo esa akɛ mamɛ ni tsei lɛ atswa shi?

english: Fertilizing right after planting with root-developing food helps the seedling settle in immediately, allowing it to start building its root system without lag time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shishifã niyenii wo dumɔwui lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ jeɔ tsumaa shishi ni esɛɛ efooo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct heat. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural canopy that protects the seedlings from drying out in the intense sun until they grow mature and hardy.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Should I leave all the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree, or cut some of them away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he loo mafo ekomɛi?

english: You should trim them down so that only two or three strong suckers remain. If you leave too many suckers, they will steal water and nutrients from the main tree, resulting in very small plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ amɛ koni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which the plant needs to grow foliage. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's life keeps the leaves green and leads to larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen babaoo fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Can I keep seeds from my harvested maize to plant again next season, or do I need to buy fresh seed?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: If you are using high-yielding hybrid seeds, saving them for the next season results in much smaller yields and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seed each planting season ensures high growth and strong yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ Okɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ baaha yibiiwoo fioo aba ni tsei lɛ hu baagbɔjɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibiiwoo ni mli wa.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani nibii babaoo baaba?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight for sunlight and soil food, giving you tall thin stems with tiny roots. Giving each cutting proper space allows the tubers enough room underground to swell up thick and heavy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni sa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam leaves need to reach as much sunlight as possible to build energy. When the vines climb tall stakes instead of trailing on the hot ground, the leaves stay healthy and feed energy down to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Beni wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ akulashiŋi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhaa hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight cups and stop producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa pepper feemɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Controlling these insects early using neem oil or recommended sprays allows the leaves to open up and fruit again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ agbele ni aduawai lɛ aba shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and high humidity wash away pollen and prevent insects from pollinating tomato flowers, while also spreading fungal rot. Planting on raised soil beds with good spacing helps rain drain away and protects the flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hu eshwaa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on a field where I previously grew maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni tsutsu lɛ miduɔ ŋmei mli lɛ mli?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the dirt, but beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil, refreshing your land for future harvests without costly fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa fataaa he.

english: How does covering my bare farm soil with dry grass or palm leaves help my crops survive the hot dry spell?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ahe tsei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground—known as mulching—acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt and prevents the hot sun from baking crop roots, keeping the soil cool and moist for much longer.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaaa hulu lɛ adɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the rain is strong enough for me to start planting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa bɔ ni sa ni mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Wait until the rain soaks the soil deep enough—about the length of your hand—after two or three good rains. Planting right after the very first light shower can kill the seeds if the sun comes back and dries the soil out for a week.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa—aaafee onine lɛ kɛlɛ—yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe dumɔwui lɛ kɛji hulu lɛ tso ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ otsi kome.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep turning yellow and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct heavy sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or temporary shade trees nearby to protect them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out their roots before they can grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baabu amɛhe lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow before the plant has even produced cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ po jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding animal manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and soft when I harvest them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rains start, mature cassava roots absorb extra water and start using up their stored starch to grow fresh leafy stems. This causes the tubers to lose their firm starch quality and turn watery.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ nu kroko ni fata he. ni ebɔi ŋmeii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni ekɛkwɛ baai heei. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot continuously drains all the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil, while allowing pests and diseases that love that crop to build up in the ground, causing poorer yields each year.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi

english: What causes holes in my young corn leaves and sawdust-like dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the deep center (the funnel) of the young corn plant to chew on soft new leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ (cone) ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress or sudden dry spells. When the weather gets too hot and dry, the plant drops flowers to conserve its energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli.

english: Will I get more harvest if I plant my seeds very close together to squeeze more plants onto my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛmi tsei babaoo awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce much smaller cobs or fruits than plants given proper breathing space.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo loo aduawai bibii fe tsei ni yɔɔ he ni sa ni amɛmuɔ lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is plenty of rainfall on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, drinking water, and soil food directly away from your crop's roots. They also serve as hiding spots for insects and diseases that can jump onto your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu ni anuɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛji hei ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai hu teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe. ni baanyɛ atsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots coming out at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Mɛi krɛdɛɛi ni jɛɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, suck away food and water from the main mother plant. Pruning them away and leaving only one or two healthy shoots allows the main plant to produce a larger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, nuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ sɛɛ ni oshi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees or plantains shield them from intense heat, reduce moisture loss from the soil, and create a cool environment that allows the young cocoa roots to grow safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha tso loo tso bibioo lɛ afee hulutsoo koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ daa shweshweeshwe lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip along the middle line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋta lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves is a clear sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. When soil runs short of nitrogen, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for maize in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the crop harvest is done, the roots decay and release that natural nitrogen fertilizer into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ agbe ŋmaa lɛ naa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too little potassium, cassava uses all its energy to build leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in its roots. Balancing soil nutrients and giving crops full sunlight forces energy back down into building large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium fioo tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni ekɛfee tsɔnei wuji.

english: Yam vines climb to expose as many leaves as possible to direct sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf fungal diseases and allows the leaves to make maximum food, which is sent down to grow big, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba tsei lɛ anɔ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, no tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa, ni ehaa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni abaamaje shi koni amɛyadu bulb agboi ni tsii

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall, thin, and fall over easily when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one spot forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Because they are crowded, they stretch thin and weak to reach light, resulting in weak stalks and tiny cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu yɛ bɔ ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛhe ni amɛhe waaa yɛ la ni amɛaana lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed, stealing food and water from the main bearing tree. Leaving only one main plant and one small sucker ensures all nutrients go into producing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso titri kome kɛ ŋmei bibioo kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya ni amɛwo ŋmei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up, twisting, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites, aphids, or thrips hiding on the underside of leaves. As they suck the juices out of the leaves, the damaged leaf tissue distorts and curls upward as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Baai lɛ amli fãji ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni ebɔleɔ ehe be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any small tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato bibii lɛ? Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: When daytime temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry or damaged, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. Because unfertilized flowers cannot turn into fruit, the plant drops them to conserve its energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tomato pollen lɛ baagbi loo ebaafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afee aduawai. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛshiɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing dry grass on the soil, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct heat from reaching the soil, traps moisture so it does not evaporate quickly, and keeps root temperatures cool so plants stay healthy.
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni ekatsɔ oya. ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Plantain shoots, or suckers, steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main parent tree. If you leave too many shoots growing at once, the main tree becomes weak and produces very small bunches. Removing extra shoots leaves energy for one strong stem to yield big fruits.
ga: Plantains, loo tsei ashishifãi juɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ, Tso titri lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni niji lɛ feɔ kui bibii waa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso kome ni wa lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why should I trim big overgrown branches on the trees providing shade to my young cocoa plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji wuji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ koni mikɛha mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ?

english: While young cocoa trees need shade from harsh sunlight, too much heavy shade blocks the light they need to grow and make food. Trimming thick upper branches lets in enough filtered light for the young trees to develop strong trunks and healthy leaves.
ga: Nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he miihia kookoo tsei bibii lɛ. Shi hulutsoo be babaoo tsiɔ la ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ kɛ nihoomɔ naa. Nibii ni afo yɛ ŋwɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa la ni mli tse ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei bibii. Koni afee ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni wa

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and fail to produce big cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ waa ni amɛwooo ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients, and their leaves block light from one another. The plants waste energy growing tall and thin to compete for sunlight instead of using that energy to fill out large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmãa tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ bibioo ni amɛkɛ hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, o kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ nɛ tsu ní nguanguahi a mi.

english: How do weeds actually hurt my cassava crop when they grow in the same field?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Weeds act like competing mouths in your soil. They quickly soak up the fertilizer, water, and space that your cassava roots need to expand, resulting in small, thin tubers at harvest time.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ni ehe hiaa ni o-cassava shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why can't I plant my tomato seeds directly in the main field instead of starting them in a nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny tomato seeds and fresh sprouts are very delicate. Hot sunshine, heavy rain, and insects can easily kill them in the main field. A nursery bed gives young seedlings a safe environment with controlled water and shade until they are tough enough to survive in the open soil.
ga: tomato dumɔwui bibii Kɛ ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ waaa kwraa. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbe amɛ yɛ shia wulu lɛ mli oya. Nursery saatsoi haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. kɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akudɔɔ. Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ ahe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: How do I know when my pepper seedlings are ready to be moved out of the nursery and onto the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pepper seedlings are ready for transplanting when they have grown four to six strong, dark-green leaves and stem that is firm. Transplanting them at this stage ensures their root systems are strong enough to adapt to the new soil without dying from shock.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ kɛji amɛyɛ baai ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ ni wa, ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni miida kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbooo kɛjɛɛɛ nɔ ni amɛtswaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do some of my garden egg plants produce flowers that fall off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when they are not visited by helpful insects like bees to transfer pollen, or when the plant suffers from too much heat and dry soil. Without proper pollination and sufficient moisture, the plant cannot support fruit growth and drops the flower to save its strength.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛnáaa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya. aloo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ. ni oshɛrɛ fɔfɔi lɛ oshwie koni amɛhewalɛ akafite

english: Why do my pumpkin vines have flowers that do not grow fruits behind them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pumpkin wain tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pumpkin vines grow two types of flowers: male flowers on thin stems that only produce pollen, and female flowers that have a tiny bump shaped like a pumpkin at their base. Only the female flowers grow into fruits after bees carry pollen to them from the male flowers.
ga: Pumpkin wain tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi henɔi enyɔ: fɔfɔi hii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii ni woɔ pollen pɛ lɛ anɔ. kɛ fɔfɔi yei ni yɔɔ bɔɔt bibii ni tamɔ pɔmpii yɛ amɛshishi lɛ. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai beni ŋmeii kɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi hii amli lɛ baha amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crops do not retain the high-yielding qualities of the original parents. Planting harvested hybrid seeds usually results in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and weak defense against local pests compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ehiɛɛɛ sui ni haa yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni shishijee fɔlɔi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akpa ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahebuu lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to pull out a single plant that has yellowing and twisted leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie tso kome ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and twisted leaves are often signs of a plant disease caused by a virus or fungus. Removing and destroying the sick plant early prevents insects or wind from carrying the disease to the healthy crop surrounding it.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ tso hela ni muawai loo tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛbaa. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekɛ hela akaya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with mulch acts like a protective roof over the ground. It stops the strong sun from drying out the earth, keeps the soil cool for the roots, and slowly turns into manure to feed the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ muji haa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛitsu ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good practice to plant beans or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on the soil and can wear it out, but beans and groundnuts act as good neighbors by pulling food from the air into the dirt. This naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow strong.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ waa ni ebaanyɛ efite. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii kpakpai kɛtsɔ niyenii ni amɛgbalaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil food. Instead of using their strength to make big fruits, they stretch upward fast just to reach light.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni ekɛfee nɔ ko wulu Moŋ lɛ, ekɛ ehe tsɔɔ oya koni emɔ kane lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots or suckers from my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi plantains lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal food and water away from the main parent plant. Removing them leaves enough energy for the main plant to build a strong stem and produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or is drowning in too much standing water. Feeding the soil with manure or fertilizer gives the leaves back their green health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii tamɔ nitrogen loo amɛbote nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiho ni ekɛmiibɔle ehe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops lose water through their leaves when it is hot outside. Curling up helps the leaves shield themselves from the sun, saving water inside the plant until the cool evening comes.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ. Curling yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ fɛ̃i baa.

english: Why should I not bury my maize seeds very deep in the soil when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu?

english: Seeds carry a small amount of stored energy to sprout. If buried too deep, the shoot gets tired trying to push through heavy dirt and dies before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Mfonirifeemɔ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛ́ oobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni otsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni amɛgboiɔ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ

english: Why do I have to make raised mounds of soft soil before planting my yam seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo nɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to stretch and grow big without fighting hard, packed ground. Raising mounds also lets excess rainwater drain away so the yams do not rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato tubers lɛ koni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee. Nibii ni ato lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ lɛ hu haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops struggle to produce food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná niyenii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and act like uninvited guests, stealing the water, fertilizer, and light meant for your crops. Keeping the field clean ensures your crops get all the food they need to give a high yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni afɔ̃ɔɔ amɛ nine, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛhaa onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔji lɛ amli tse lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. The big shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool, preserving soil moisture, and protecting delicate young leaves from scorching until the trees are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obuɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, cool conditions. When excess rainwater stays on the pods and tall weeds keep the farm damp, the fungus spreads quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ jwɛi kakadaji lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small sucker shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many sucker shoots compete with the main plantain trunk for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. By leaving only two or three strong shoots, the plant focuses its energy on producing larger and heavier bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ esɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to set up tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves high into the air to catch sunlight for growth. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing soil-borne diseases from damaging the crop.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛdara. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small, thin roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: When plants are planted too close together or the soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves to compete for sunlight rather than storing food underground in the roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ lɛ Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ebaai ni miida lɛ anɔ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi ngɛ tso ɔ sisi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the soil becomes waterlogged during heavy rains, the roots drown and soil fungal diseases quickly break down and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi oya ni amɛbaafite.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It commonly happens when watering is irregular, making it difficult for the plant roots to absorb calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward like tiny cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. The leaves distort and curl as a reaction to the pest feeding and viral attack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkotoɔ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ahetoohamɔ mli.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This leaves natural fertilizer in the ground that feeds the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf whorl to eat the soft inner growth. The dark dirt is the pest's droppings, showing it is actively feeding inside the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Muji ni tsuɔ waa ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eeye tso lɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer around the base will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baafata he Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does planting beans in the same field as my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the roots break down, they release natural nutrients into the soil that feed the nearby maize plants.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ fã Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Fast-growing plantains provide wide leaf canopy coverage that shields the baby cocoa trees from intense heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to produce food. Staking keeps the foliage spread out in the air, which allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and produce bigger yam tubers below.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni enyɛ ewo niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. ni ofee sweet potato tuber agbo ko yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches that make them top-heavy. Using strong wooden props to support the main stem prevents wind and fruit weight from snapping or pulling up the plant before harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo egbala tso lɛ dani akpa.

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the full heat of the day. It also lets wet leaves dry quickly in the sun, which prevents fungal diseases from taking hold overnight.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani edɔɔ kwraa nakai gbi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baa ni efɔ lɛ hu ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni fungal hela akahi shi nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water stays trapped around their roots for too long during rainy periods. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rain drain away so the roots remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme midday heat, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps cool the roots so the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies carrying plant viruses, or by stress from sudden heat. Shielding young plants and controlling insects early keeps the foliage flat and active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni baa trukaa lɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ ahebuu mra kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛbuaa lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually slow down their growth?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha amɛdalɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds while your crops are still small gives your main plants full access to the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lolo lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches from shade trees to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling and pale patches on cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings and removing sick plants early protects the rest of your field.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmeii ni etsake yɛ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ. Niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu oyale lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil drops too dry, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer is used. Giving plants consistent water and balanced fertilizer helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop producing leaves after I harvest the first fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ baai beni mikpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants put all their energy into ripening fruit. If ripe peppers stay on the plant too long, the plant stops growing new shoots; picking ripe peppers promptly encourages the plant to produce fresh leaves and flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baakpa ŋmeii heei ni baa lɛ. Pepper ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and loose soil mounds to expand. If the soil is hard, shallow, or full of stones, the growing tuber cannot push through easily, causing it to become small or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, ekɔɔɔ he eko, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsɔ yitsei ni eda lɛ amli mlɛo ni eha amɛfee bibii loo amɛfite.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes plants to lose water from their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves from drying out and usually recover by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear inside the central leaves of my maize after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Early rains signal armyworm moths to lay eggs on tender maize shoots. The eggs hatch quickly into caterpillars that feed on the soft growing center, so checking leaf whorls early helps catch and treat them before major damage occurs.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii baawo ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Wɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii, ni amɛyeɔ he ni gbekɛbii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ amɛ ni atsa amɛ dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil for long periods and are adapted to sprout immediately when exposed to sunlight and rain. Crop seeds take longer because they need time to build strong root systems before growing tall.
