ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ. Dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo ejaakɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná be ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni wa dani amɛdara.

english: Why can't I just wake up and go to plant my seeds whenever I am ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miteee shi kɛkɛ ni mayadu dumɔwui lɛ be fɛɛ be ni mafee klalo lɛ?

english: Successful farming depends heavily on rainfall and weather patterns. If you plant at the wrong time without waiting for the natural rain cycles, your seeds will not get the water they need to sprout and will die in the soil.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yeɔ omanye lɛ damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ waa. Kɛji odu yɛ be ni esaaa mli ni omɛɛɛɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ naaa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when people say we have a major season and a minor season in Ghana?
ga: Kɛ́ mɛi kɛɛ wɔyɛ bei wuji kɛ bei bibii yɛ Ghana lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Ghana has two separate rainy periods each year. The major season brings the primary, heavier rains suited for main crop production, while the minor season brings a second, usually shorter period of rainfall later in the year.
ga: Ghana yɛ nugbɔ bei enyɔ daa afi. Be titri lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa yɛ shishijee mli ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titrii afeemɔ. Yɛ be mli ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ baaná nugbɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ feɔ kuku yɛ afi lɛ naagbee.

english: Why do my fellow farmers tell me to plant around April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ananemɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu amɛ yɛ April afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: April marks the traditional start of the major rainy season in many parts of Ghana. Planting around this time ensures your young crops receive consistent rainfall throughout their growth period to give you a good harvest.
ga: April ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Dumɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa onibii bibii lɛ naa nugbɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ koni eha bo ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: If I plant my crops in April, am I guaranteed to get a good harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei yɛ April mli Ani miyɛ nɔmimaa akɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Planting in April aligns your crops with the main rainy season, which gives them the water needed to mature fully. While proper field care is still required, planting in April greatly increases your chances of a successful harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ April mli lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ akpã gbee. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni sa he miihia lolo moŋ. Shi dumɔ yɛ April mli lɛ haa hegbɛ ni oyɔɔ akɛ obaakpa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Can I plant a second round of crops around August, or is that too late in the year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ yɛ August aaafee loo afi nɛɛ eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant around August because that is when the minor rainy season starts. It allows you to grow a second cycle of crops before the dry season begins.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ August mli ejaakɛ no mli lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Is planting in August the same as planting in April?
ga: Ani dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ August mli lɛ kɛ dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ April mli lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, August is the start of the minor season, which usually has shorter and less intense rainfall than the major season that begins in April, so crops may behave and grow differently.
ga: Dabi, August ji be ni ji enyɔ lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ kuku ni ehiii kwraa fe be titri ni jeɔ shishi yɛ April mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ ni amɛda.

english: Why does it seem like the rains are no longer falling at the exact time they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be ni efɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The weather patterns have changed globally and locally over time, causing rainfall to become irregular. This means rainy seasons may start earlier or later than expected compared to previous years.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ jeŋ fɛɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the start of the August planting season vary from year to year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ August ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee lɛ srɔtoɔ yɛ afi fɛɛ afi mli lɛ?

english: Due to changing weather conditions, the minor season rains in August do not always start on the exact same date every year. Farmers must observe the actual arrival of the rains rather than relying only on a fixed date.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ Jeee be fɛɛ be nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ August mli lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ gbi kome nɔ daa afi. Ehe miihia ni okwaafoi lɛ akwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhe aaafɔ̃ gbi pɔtɛɛ ni ebaa lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them and the rains fail to drop?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Seeds require moisture from the soil to germinate. If the rains fail after planting, the seeds will stay dry in the hot soil, rot, or wither shortly after sprouting, leading to a lost crop.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, ebaagbo loo egbo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni laajeɔ.

english: How do changing weather conditions affect when my crops will mature for harvest?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baaná be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛha kpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: When rainfall is delayed or interrupted by changing weather, crops grow more slowly or stress early, which shifts your harvest timeline and can reduce the overall crop yield.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo efoɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo loo amɛhaoɔ amɛhe mra. Enɛ baatsake be ni okɛbaakpa nii lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Officer, if I cut down a diseased tree, is it safe to leave the stump in the ground?
ga: Ofisa, kɛji mifo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ ni mishi shishifã lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaafee shweshweeshwe?

english: Leaving a diseased stump in the ground allows the sickness to survive deep in the root system. Over time, the disease can live on underground and infect the healthy new crops you plant nearby.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tso ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Hela lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ aba.

english: Is there any chemical spray that can cure my crop once its leaves show signs of a severe virus?
ga: Ani tsofai komɛi yɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni baanyɛ atsa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ amɛbaai lɛ jie hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ he okadi kpo?

english: For major viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot, there is no chemical spray that can cure the tree once infected. The best action is to cut down the infected tree to save the rest of your farm from catching the sickness.
ga: Kɛha helai wuji ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni baanyɛ atsa tsei kɛji amɛhe hela lɛ bɛ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni ofolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni ohere oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ hela mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to destroy trees that still have green leaves on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkpãtã tsei ni baai eŋɔli lolo lɛ ahiɛ lɛ?

english: Some diseases spread invisibly inside a plant long before the entire tree turns brown and dies. Removing a tree that shows initial symptoms prevents the sickness from multiplying and jumping to neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Helai komɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa tso ko mli yɛ gbɛ ni anaaa nɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ. Tsei ni jieɔ shishijee okadii lɛ akpo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa hela lɛ aya hiɛ ni efo kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does applying medicine to a tree stump clean the soil around it?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he tseɔ?

english: Special agricultural chemicals get absorbed through the wood tissue of the cut stump and travel all the way down to the deepest roots, killing the hidden fungal disease living in the underground root system.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli ni amɛyaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Egbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ.

english: How long do I need to wait to replant new crops after treating an infected piece of land?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu tsei heei beni mitsa he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It usually takes several months to over a year after removing infected roots and applying soil treatment for the disease organisms to completely die off, making it safe for new seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi nɔ ni fe afi beni ajie shishifãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsofa ko ewo mli koni hela lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ agboi kwraa. Enɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔwui heei.

english: What early signs tell me that my crop roots are rotting underground before the plant dies?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii tsɔɔ mi akɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani tso lɛ gbo?

english: Look out for leaves that turn yellow prematurely, unexpected wilting during mild sunshine, and slow growth. These indicate the root system underground is failing to draw water and nutrients.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ mra. Nibii ni shwieɔ shi ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni waaa kɛ be mli ni edaa blɛoo lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Can I carry plant sickness from an infected farm to my clear farm on my cutlass or boots?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo tsei ahe helai kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni hela emɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔ ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli mli kɛ dade loo bɔɔlu?

english: Yes, sticky sap, infected plant bits, and soil clinging to your boots or cutlass can carry hidden fungal spores and bacteria directly into your healthy farm. Always wash tools after working on a sick farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, latɛs ni kpɛtɛɔ he, tso mli sũ ni hela emɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ o-boots loo o-dagger lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ fungal spores kɛ bacteria ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aya oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ dɛŋdadei ahe be fɛɛ be kɛ́ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ ni hela mɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If my neighbor's farm is sick and he leaves it untreated, will the sickness jump to my land?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ okutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ ni atsaaa lɛ Ani nakai hela lɛ baatswa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, diseases do not respect farm borders. Insects, wind, flowing rain water, and touching roots underground can easily carry the disease from your neighbor's land onto your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ebuuu ŋmɔ mli husui. Kplukai, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why can a crop disease stay hidden on a farm for years before a farmer notices it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔji amli afii babaoo dani okwaafoi lɛ ayɔse lɛ?

english: Many plant pathogens grow slowly inside the bark or roots. A tree can carry a low level of disease for years without obvious symptoms until severe weather or age weakens the plant enough for the sickness to show.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo daa blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ amli. Tsei baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã yɛ gbɛ ni baa shi nɔ afii babaoo ni okadi ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ he. Kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii loo afii ni eho lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ bɔ ni sa ni ejie hela he okadii akpo.

english: Why do some farms in our community catch a crop sickness while nearby farms remain healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Farms differ in soil quality, shade levels, plant age, and tool cleanliness. Sickness usually attacks farms where plants are stressed or where infected tools and seedlings were introduced first.
ga: Esoro ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, bɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, tsei lɛ afii, kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe tsemɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hela nɛɛ tutuaa ŋmɔji ni tsei lɛ miihao yɛ mli loo hei ni akɛ nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ewo mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and broad, providing live shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant starves for food and pulls whatever nitrogen it has left to the top leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni ebaagbala nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same plot of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize heavily consumes the same nutrients every season. Planting it repeatedly wears out the soil and invites corn-specific pests; rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally to the dirt.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ daa be. Dumɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko baa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which part of a cassava stem is best to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: The middle portion of a mature, healthy stem (about 8 to 12 months old) works best. The top soft stems rot easily in the ground, while the very bottom woody base sprouts root tubers much slower.
ga: Tso lɛ tso ni eda ni ehe wa (ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12) lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Yitsoŋ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ shishi shishifãi lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa.

english: Why do I need to make raised mounds of soil before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep and broad underground. Large, soft soil mounds give the tubers loose dirt to expand easily without pushing against hard earth, while also preventing standing water from rotting the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni abua naa babaoo lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why are small holes appearing on my maize leaves with little caterpillars inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Moths lay eggs on young leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat their way down into the center of the plant, which can stunt the corn's growth if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ wui yɛ baai bibii anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni fɔɔ lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmãa dalɛ naa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, severe drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant gets stressed, it drops its flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛji tsei miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into a cup shape during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is the plant's way of protecting itself from losing water too fast. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sun and heat.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ. Tsei haa hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer in a small ring around my plant instead of touching the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii bibii awo ŋmeii amli lɛ? ebɔle tso lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeeta tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he

english: Putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and damage the plant tissue. Placing it a short distance away puts it right where the outer feeder roots can safely drink it up with soil moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tsei lɛ ahe fãji. He ni akɛwoɔ he ko ni kɛ shɔŋŋ fioo Enɛ baaha kponɔgbɛ niyenii hamɔ shishifãi lɛ anu nu shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. You can pull up one test plant: if the insides of the pods show dark brown or black vein markings instead of white, they are ready to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa tso kome kɛya ŋwɛi: kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunlight; they need shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas that protect them from hot sun and keep the soil moist while they build strength.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtswaa hewalɛ emaa shi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crop plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard like wood if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stays in the soil past its maturity point, the root converts its soft starch into tough fibers, making the tubers woody and difficult to cook.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehoɔ be ni ekɛbaa lɛ he. Shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ starch ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ fibers ni wa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ tso, ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms when the soil gets too dry, temperatures get too high, or the plant lacks key soil nutrients needed to hold and feed the developing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo, tsei bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛto kooloi ni miida lɛ ahe ni akɛha amɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When crops are sown too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil food, stretching upward to reach light instead of building thick stems and large ears.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha la abote mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep planting cassava on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in the earth.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ.

english: Why did my planted seeds rot in the ground after I sowed them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Early rains are often followed by hot dry spells; if the soil dries out after seeds soak up initial water, the germination process stops and the seeds decay underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ahum ni mli edɔ waa ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ leebi nugbɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi beni dumɔwui lɛ eŋɔ shishijee nu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ lɛ kpaɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra small branches growing out from the side of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? Nu ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Removing those extra side branches allows the tomato plant to focus its energy and water into growing bigger, healthier fruits rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ enu lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops more when the crops are tiny compared to when they are full-grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa kɛ́ amɛji bibii fe be mli ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crop plants have small roots and leaves, so fast-growing weeds can easily steal all their water, light, and soil food before the crop gets established.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ aju nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo dani tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to lift and stake my yam vines off the ground using sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines allows leaves to catch full sunlight to feed the root below, while keeping foliage off the damp soil prevents fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii akaye baa helai.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden poles to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber under the soil. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground so they get full sun without shading one another.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: The main plantain stem has to share water and nutrients with every sucker growing beside it. Removing excess shoots leaves only one strong follower, allowing the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ agba nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ ni he wa shwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ feɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants stop producing good pods if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii kpakpai kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cowpeas are crowded, their leaves block sunlight from each other and fight for soil nutrients. Giving them space allows air and light to circulate, which encourages the plant to set more pods.
ga: Beni tsina ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni akɛhaa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee pods babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen or trapped in waterlogged soil. Nitrogen helps the plant create green pigment to absorb sunlight and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen loo ekã shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but only making tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ebatsɔ yitso bibioo ko. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or excess rain early on, it uses all its energy to grow stem and foliage above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná nitrogen babaoo loo nugbɔ babaoo mra Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they form long stems called pegs that push into the dirt because groundnut pods can only form and mature underground in total darkness.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollination sɛɛ lɛ Ejieɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kpo. Bean pods baanyɛ afee ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ duŋ kwraa mli pɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates heavily. When stressed, the plant drops its blooms to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus carried by them. Spraying with organic mixtures like neem oil helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kɛ amɛ baa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in cold, wet, and humid shade. Pruning non-bearing branches lets wind dry out the farm and reduces the spread of fungal spores.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ agbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet weather, especially when cocoa trees are untrimmed and shade is too dense, trapping moisture on the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afolɔɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ewo wu tsɔ. Trap ŋmɔtɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant's juices, or by a virus transmitted by these insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that lay eggs on maize leaves. The hatched caterpillars crawl into the central funnel of the plant to feed, which destroys leaf growth if not treated early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛyaye nii. Enɛ baafite baai lɛ adalɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when dry weather lasts for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi kɛyashiɔ otsii enyɔ lɛ?

english: When the soil dries out, maize roots cannot absorb nitrogen from the ground. The plant moves stored nutrients from lower leaves to top shoots to survive, turning lower leaves yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits when the heat is high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: High temperatures stress tomato plants and dry out the pollen inside the blooms, causing unpollinated flowers to drop off before fruit can set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ fɔɔ.

english: Excess water pooling in heavy or flat soil suffocates cassava roots and encourages soil fungi, causing the tubers to rot under the surface.
ga: Nu ni buaa ehe naa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the large trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out topsoil before their roots grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main stem for water and nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why does fertilizer fail to help my crops when I apply it during a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyeee ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away granular fertilizer from the topsoil into gutters and streams before roots can absorb it, leaving the crop without nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to put their energy into leaf growth rather than producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha cowpea lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with huge leaves, but the roots underneath stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from the soil, it spends all its energy growing lush green leaves on top instead of expanding its roots below. Using a balanced fertilizer with more potassium helps the plant store food in the roots instead.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ato niyenii yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, showing you it needs fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ bo akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more corn from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of getting more harvest, you will end up with thin stalks and tiny, empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la he. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ moŋ fe ni ooona yibii babaoo. Obaaná tso bibioo ko. kɛ ŋmei bibioo ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress tomato plants, causing their pollen to dry up. When flowers cannot be pollinated, the plant drops them to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ pollination Akɛ nu woɔ tsei amli koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new peppers during the dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ moŋ?

english: Light watering only wets the surface of hot soil. Pepper roots go deep, and if they stay warm and dry beneath the surface, the plant enters a survival mode and stops making new fruit.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Pepper shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni amɛgbi yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni ekpaa yibii heei ni ewoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess wetness and darkness allow a fungal disease called black pod to thrive. The fungus moves through water droplets on the pods, rotting the beans inside if the farm is not cleared for sunlight and air.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ duŋ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ daa. Fuji lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli. Ni enɛ haa kɔfi yibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ mli kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the soil mound before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: When heavy soil holds too much water, air cannot reach the yam tuber underground. The roots suffocate in stagnant water, making it easy for rot organisms in the soil to destroy the yam.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akɛ amɛbaafite ŋmeii.

english: Why does my maize mature and dry up much faster in the major season than in the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa ni egbiɔ oya kwraa yɛ shishijee be lɛ mli fe nɔ ni ji enyɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Higher temperatures and longer sunny days in the major season speed up the crop's internal clock, forcing it to flower, fruit, and dry faster than in cooler, cloudier weather.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ hulutsoo gbii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ yaa oya. Nyɛ fɔfɔi, yibiiwoo, kɛ egbimɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni atatu yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit bunches when planted in an old farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui akutsei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ aduawai akui kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ?

english: Old farmlands lose vital nutrients over time from continuous cropping. Without rich soil food, plantain stalks grow slowly and take many extra months to build the strength needed to carry heavy fruit.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi momo lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, Plantain tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni ehe hiaa nyɔji babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees stay healthy while neighboring trees right next to them get sick and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Some individual plant varieties have a natural resistance built into their genes, similar to how some human bodies can resist a cold better than others. These resilient crops can survive attacks from diseases that kill weaker plants.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibii ni teɔ shi woɔ helai. Tamɔ bɔ ni adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ baanyɛ akpee fɛ̃i naa jogbaŋŋ fe kooloi krokomɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi nɛɛ baanyɛ aye amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ atuatsemɔ mli.

english: What should I do if a strange plant sickness starts spreading across all the farms in our district?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tso hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ bɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ ŋmɔji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ amli?

english: You should report the outbreak immediately to your local extension officer without moving infected plant parts off your farm, as experts need to identify the disease early to protect neighboring communities.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ helai ni baa lɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ojie tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni nilelɔi ana hela lɛ mra. Koni abu akutsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe

english: Why do pests and diseases destroy my farm faster when I plant only one single crop across my whole land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai fiteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ oya be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome pɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting just one crop gives pests an endless supply of their favorite food, allowing them to multiply rapidly. Planting different crops together confuses insects and slows the spread of diseases.
ga: Tso henɔ kome pɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa ni bɛ naagbee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa kooloi ayiŋ futuɔ amɛ, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my crops still struggling to grow even after I applied fertilizer and chemicals to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ lolo ni amɛkwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ewo mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer only feeds the crop, but if the soil is too acidic, infested with root-damaging pests, or lacking enough water, the roots cannot absorb the nutrients you put into the ground.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Ayɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on the sloped parts of my farm but yellow and rot down in the valley bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ? Shi etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Valley bottoms collect excess water that drowns plant roots and cuts off their oxygen supply, whereas sloped areas allow water to drain away easily so roots can breathe.
ga: Jɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine, ni no haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, he ni ŋshɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and drop off during heavy rainfall periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil becomes waterlogged from rain, roots lose oxygen and begin to rot, preventing the plant from taking up vital nutrients needed to keep leaves green and healthy.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes when the hot dry weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ paipii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to protect itself from the hot sun, reducing leaf surface area to save internal moisture until rain falls.
ga: Baai lɛ akumɔ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ baa shi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the protective shade cocoa needs in its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers come back to inspect my sick farm a second time instead of giving me a solution right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa koni amɛbakwɛ ŋmɔji ni helatsɛmɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ shii enyɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ tsabaai baaha amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A second visit allows extension officers to track how the sickness develops over time, confirming whether plants are recovering naturally or need specific treatments.
ga: Saramɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ haa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ helatsamɔhe lɛ naa bɔ ni hela lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Emaa nɔ mi kɛji tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ pɔtɛɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seed varieties instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give higher yields and resist local diseases, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over generations and yield smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are my young maize leaves developing ragged holes with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the growing tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee tip ni miida lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest feeds on the central growing shoot of the maize plant, which can stop leaf development and lower grain yield if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kpluka nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black, covered in white fungus, and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ? Akɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ haa nɔ ni egboɔ dani akpaa

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches and clearing weeds lets air and sunlight reach the pods, reducing fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne organism that clogs the water tubes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. ni ji nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa lɛ. Ehaa nu shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young corn plants turn purple along the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple kɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young corn usually mean the soil is low in available phosphorus, or the soil is too cool or wet for the roots to absorb phosphorus properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ loo edɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does growing cowpeas on my land make my next crop of maize grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, they release natural nitrogen fertilizer into the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land become hard and dry out quickly after I clear and burn the bush cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya beni mijie jwɛi lɛ ni mishã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning removes organic crop waste that acts like a sponge to store water. Bare soil exposed to direct sunlight loses moisture rapidly and bakes into a hard surface layer.
ga: Shãa jieɔ tsei amli jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ŋmɛɔ nu lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni etsɔɔ nɔ ni wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants start dropping off as soon as the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during drought to conserve water and survive extreme heat. Once the rainy season returns, the plant produces fresh green leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Staking keeps yam leaves high off the hot ground where they get maximum sunlight to build food, while keeping them away from soil pests and rot, resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo yɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ fitemɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Hot winds and high heat can dry out flower pollen, stopping fruit from setting. Excess chemical nitrogen fertilizer can also cause the plant to put energy into growing green leaves rather than flowers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Ehaa aduawai lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi Tsofai ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo baai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ mli moŋ fe fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my plantain trees take much longer to produce fruit when there are many suckers attached to the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni ekɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots on the same root system compete with the main plantain stem for water and food. Removing extra suckers allows the parent plant to direct all its energy into growing large fruit bunches faster.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shishifã kome mli lɛ kɛ plantain tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ewo aduawai wuji oya.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and high heat. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their foliage and conserve moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni abu baai lɛ ahe ni ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape even though we are in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli eyɛ mli akɛ wɔyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli moŋ?

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant draws nutrients from older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with thick green leaves, so why are the tubers under the soil so thin when I harvest?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive excess leaf-promoting nutrients like nitrogen or are planted too close together, they focus their energy on growing stems and leaves above ground rather than storing starches in the roots below ground.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni haa baai lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen, loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ starch kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: How do I choose the right suckers from my plantain crop if I want high-yielding plants for my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni sa kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli? Ani tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo he miihia mi kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Select maiden or sword suckers that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad corm base. These suckers grow faster and produce larger, heavier fruit bunches than water suckers that have broad, fully developed leaves early on.
ga: Halamɔ obalayoo yitsɔi fɔfɔi loo klante tsei ni baa bibii tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ bulb shishi ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni dara, ni tsii fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ni amɛdaraa mra.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato flowers fall off the stems before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Vegetable flowers drop off due to stress caused by sudden temperature spikes, irregular water supply, or attacks by tiny flower-feeding pests. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant hold onto its blooms until fruits form.
ga: Aduawai fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ atuatsemɔi Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Is it really necessary to stake my yam vines, or can I leave them to spread on the bare ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso lɛ nɔ? Aloo manyɛ maha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight and keeps them away from hot ground soil. Better exposure to light enables the leaves to photosynthesize more effectively, feeding the underground tuber so it grows much larger.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli adɔ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ kpo jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ anɔ koni baai lɛ afee wuji babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning dark brown and soft on the tree before they even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Dark, soft pods are a main symptom of fungal Black Pod disease, which thrives in high humidity and heavy shade. Pruning overgrown tree canopies allows sunlight and airflow to dry out damp pods and reduce fungal growth.
ga: Pods bibii ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji fungal black pod hela lɛ he okadi titri. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Tsoi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: My cowpea crop looks bushy and full of green foliage, but why are the pods coming out empty without seeds?
ga: Mi-cowpeas lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ baai eŋɔli. Shi mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo efolo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sap-sucking insects often attack cowpea plants right at the flowering stage, sucking out vital plant juices before seeds can form inside the pods. Checking plants during early flower bud formation helps catch pests before they destroy seed yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa tsina tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Ekɛ tsei amli nu ni he hiaa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui lɛ baa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei amli yɛ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite dumɔwui ni anáa lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller ears of corn when I pack many seeds closely together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii babaoo wo mli lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the individual stalks to compete aggressively for available soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Giving plants proper spacing gives each stem enough resources to form a thick stalk and full ear.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ehe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni ena niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, enáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso lɛ mli tsei ni mli tse kɛ toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce mostly male flowers and no fruit bunches after long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo ni ji hii ni ewooo yibii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni eho lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palms react to severe dry weather and water stress by shifting their energy into male flower production to survive. Ensuring water conservation around the tree base with organic mulching encourages the development of fruit-bearing female flowers.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ tsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa kɛ nu mli haomɔ he nii kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi hii anɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛbuɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi yei ni woɔ yibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Can I just wake up one morning and start cutting my rubber trees to harvest latex?
ga: Ani manyɛ mate shi leebi ko ni mabɔi rɔbɔt tsei lɛ afomɔ koni mikɛbua nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa?

english: No, you cannot just cut rubber trees whenever you want. Tapping requires specific knowledge and testing to ensure the tree is mature enough and that the cutting is done correctly without damaging the crop.
ga: Dabi, onyɛŋ ofo rɔbɔt tso lɛ be fɛɛ be ni osumɔɔ. Tapping biɔ nilee krɛdɛɛ kɛ kaa koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ eda ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Do I need to pass a test or get approval before I am allowed to tap rubber trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsɔ kaa ko mli loo akpɛlɛ minɔ dani manyɛ matswa rɔba tsei?

english: Yes, you must undergo a test to prove you know how to tap properly, and the tree itself must be inspected to confirm it can be tapped before official permission is given.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ kaa ko mli koni otsɔɔ akɛ ole bɔ ni afoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni esa akɛ akwɛ tsei amli koni ama nɔ mi akɛ abaanyɛ atswa amɛ dani maŋ lɛ aha hegbɛ.

english: How do I know if my rubber tree has reached the right stage to begin tapping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-rɔba tso lɛ eshɛ he ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tswamɔ?

english: Determining readiness requires conducting specific assessments on the tree to verify its maturity and size before you can start harvesting latex.
ga: Hesaamɔ ni ooona lɛ biɔ ni okwɛ tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli koni okwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ yɔɔ ha dani obaanyɛ oje tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kpamɔ shishi.

english: Is tapping a rubber tree the same as cutting any other tree on my farm?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt tso ni oootswa lɛ kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ooofo lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, rubber tapping is a controlled skill. You cannot simply cut into the bark like standard wood; it requires tested techniques so the tree yields latex safely.
ga: Dabi, rɔba tswaa ji ŋaa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Onyɛŋ ofo tso lɛ yibii tamɔ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋaai ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ atsu nii koni akɛ tsei awo latɛs mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is permission required before someone can start tapping rubber on a plantation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi gbɛ dani mabɔi rɔbɔt tswaa yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Permission is required to ensure that only trained individuals tap the trees and that the rubber trees have been properly verified as ready for latex extraction.
ga: Hegbɛ he miihia koni mɛi ni atsɔse amɛ pɛ ata tsei lɛ ahe. ni akwɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni ana akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛha latɛs ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: How many years can I expect a single rubber tree to produce latex once tapping starts?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ rɔbɔt tso kome pɛ baajie latɛs kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ pɛ?

english: Depending on the tree and how well it is managed, a rubber tree can typically be tapped for a production period lasting between seven and ten years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ atswa rɔba tsei yɛ nitsumɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛjɛ afii kpawo kɛyashi afii nyɔŋma mli. Enɛ damɔ tso lɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers say their rubber tree lasts for seven years while others say ten years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ rɔba tsei hiɔ shi afii kpawo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ afii nyɔŋma?

english: The productive lifespan of a rubber tree varies based on individual tree health, environmental factors, and tapping practices, leading some trees to last seven years and others up to ten years.
ga: Rɔba tsei wala be ni woɔ yibii lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni tso fɛɛ tso yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Shihilɛ mli nibii kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ tsei ni atswaa lɛ he Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi eye afii kpawo. Ni tsei komɛi baanyɛ ahi shi aahu afii nyɔŋma.

english: Can experienced family members or local farmers help me figure out how long my rubber trees will last?
ga: Ani weku lɛ mlinyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ loo okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni male be abɔ ni mi-raba tso lɛ baahi shi?

english: Yes, talking with experienced family members and growers who know the crop well can provide reliable insights on expected harvesting lifespans, which usually range from seven to ten years.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ weku lɛ mli bii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dulɔi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni le ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ gba sane lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha wɔná shishinumɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ shihilɛ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ afii kpawo kɛyashi afii nyɔŋma.

english: Will my rubber tree continue to give latex indefinitely once I begin harvesting?
ga: Ani mi rɔba tso lɛ baaya nɔ ejie latɛs kɛya naanɔ kɛji mibɔi ŋmaakpamɔ pɛ?

english: No, rubber trees have a limited active tapping period. Once tapping starts, the productive life for latex collection generally lasts between seven and ten years.
ga: Dabi, rɔbɔt tsei yɛ be fioo ni amɛkɛbaatswa. Kɛji akɛ aje shishi afo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, latex lɛ shihilɛ be ji aaafee afii kpawo kɛyashi afii nyɔŋma.

english: What makes a particular rubber tree stand out as ready and suitable for long-term tapping?
ga: Mɛni haa rɔbɔt tso pɔtɛɛ ko feɔ klalo yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni sa kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtswaa tsɔne lɛ?

english: A great rubber tree is identified through tests that confirm it has met all growth and maturity conditions required to sustain regular tapping over its seven to ten-year productive life.
ga: Ayoo rɔbɔt tsei wuji kɛtsɔ kaa ni maa nɔ mi akɛ amɛshɛɔ dalɛ kɛ dalɛ shihilɛi fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni atswa amɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ yɛ amɛ afii kpawo kɛyashi nyɔŋma ni amɛfeɔ nii lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ he.

english: Can I actually plant and cultivate prɛkɛsɛ on my farm, or does it only grow by itself in the bush?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ni makwɛ prɛkɛsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo ebaada lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe yɛ jwɛi lɛ amli pɛ?

english: Prɛkɛsɛ can be deliberately planted and cultivated on farmland. While traditionally gathered from wild trees in the forest, you can grow prɛkɛsɛ from seeds or nursed seedlings to establish your own orchard.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsɔ hiɛ adu Prɛkɛsɛ ni atsu he nii yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee lɛ abua naa kɛjɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ amli moŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛ prɛkɛsɛ atsu nii kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni adu mli koni okɛfee bo diɛŋtsɛ otso yibii abɔɔ.

english: Why is prɛkɛsɛ so scarce in the market during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaana prɛkɛsɛ yɛ jara nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Prɛkɛsɛ trees fruit seasonally. Because most of the supply comes from wild trees rather than organized farms, availability drops sharply outside the main fruiting season.
ga: Phraeksa tso lɛ yɛ yibii ni baa yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ koo mli tsei amli moŋ fe ŋmɔji ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi oya yɛ yibiiwoo be titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How long does a prɛkɛsɛ tree take from planting until it starts producing fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani price tso ko daa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: A cultivated prɛkɛsɛ tree usually takes between 4 to 6 years to mature and start bearing pods, depending on soil fertility, water availability, and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni adu lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 6 dani amɛdaraa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ

english: How far apart should I space prɛkɛsɛ trees when planting them on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei diɛŋtsɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Prɛkɛsɛ grows into a large tree with wide branches. You should plant them about 8 to 10 meters apart so they do not fight for sunlight and root space as they mature.
ga: Phraeksa daa ni etsɔɔ tso agbo ko ni niji lɛɛ lɛɛ. Esa akɛ odu amɛ aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 koni amɛkaye hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe akaŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my young prɛkɛsɛ trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, while prɛkɛsɛ trees are young and small, you can intercrop with fast-growing crops like maize, vegetables, or legumes. As the tree canopies grow large and create heavy shade, you will need to transition the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ prairie tso lɛ ji gbekɛ ni eyɛ bibioo moŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, aduawai, loo ŋmãa awo mli. Kɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ da ni ekɛ hulutsoo be ni tsii ba lɛ, Ehe baahia ni otsake he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my prɛkɛsɛ seeds taking so long to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi PRɛkɛsɛ dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Prɛkɛsɛ seeds have a hard outer coat that stops water from entering easily. Soaking the seeds in warm water overnight or gently nicking the seed coat before planting helps them germinate much faster.
ga: Praxaceae yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni haaa nu abote mli mlɛo. Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo nu ni mli edɔ mli nyɔɔŋ kome loo okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akpokpo blɛoo. Dani abaadu lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kwraa.

english: Is there enough buyer demand to justify starting a commercial prɛkɛsɛ farm?
ga: Ani nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha jarayeli ŋmɔ shishijee afee nɔ ni ja?

english: Yes, demand for prɛkɛsɛ is high for soups, traditional medicines, and herbal products, but supply is often low. Cultivating it gives you a reliable market, especially during off-peak seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, prɛkɛsɛ ni ataoɔ lɛ fa babaoo kɛha shwiili, blema tsofai, kɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai fee. Shi bei pii lɛ, nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa. Okwaayeli baaha oná jara ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Do I need to prune my prɛkɛsɛ trees as they get bigger?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafo prixet tso ko. Mɛɛ be tso lɛ daa?

english: Pruning lower branches on young prɛkɛsɛ trees helps them form a strong central trunk and a balanced canopy, making future harvesting easier and allowing air to flow through the orchard.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ haa niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso yibii abɔɔ lɛ mli

english: How do I know when prɛkɛsɛ pods are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Mature prɛkɛsɛ pods turn from green to a dark brown, shiny color. They will naturally fall to the ground when fully ripe or drop easily when the branches are gently shaken.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni kpɛɔ. Kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo amɛgbeeɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ akpokpo tso lɛ nine lɛ blɛoo.

english: What type of soil and weather does prɛkɛsɛ need to grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he hiaa prɛkɛsɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Prɛkɛsɛ grows best in warm, humid forest regions with fertile, well-drained soil. It needs good rainfall during its growth phase but can tolerate dry spells once fully established.
ga: Prɛkɛsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehe miihia nugbɔ kpakpa yɛ dalɛ be mli. Shi ebaanyɛ edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji etswa shi kwraa.

english: How do I know if a new crop will grow well on my land before I invest money in a full acre?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ acre muu fɛɛ awo mli?

english: Crops react differently to local soil and weather conditions. Planting a small test plot first lets you see how the crop behaves and copes with local pests without risking your entire investment.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, aduɔ kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. Ehaa onaa bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe nii amɛhaa lɛ, ni okɛ oshika fɛɛ ni okɛwo mli lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Why do some crops take a full year to yield fruit while others produce in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi yeɔ afi muu dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Long-cycle crops spend their first few months building deep root systems and strong stems before producing flowers and fruits. Once established, these mature crops often produce higher yields over a longer period.
ga: Tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Beni adu Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni eda nɛɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: If I put extra fertilizer on my crops, will they automatically give me a bigger harvest at the end of the year?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe Ani amɛbaaná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides essential nutrients for plant growth, but too much can burn the roots or cause the plant to produce lots of leaves instead of fruit. Plants only yield more when given the right amount at the right time.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ. Shi kɛ́ efee babaoo fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha tso lɛ awo baai babaoo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Tsei lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ aha amɛ yibii ni sa yɛ be ni sa mli pɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I pack as many seeds as possible into one acre of land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo acre kome mli bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes them tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller individual fruits and lower total harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni amɛfeɔ nibii fɛɛ ni baa shi.

english: Excess water fills air pockets in the soil, choking the roots and stopping them from breathing. Unable to absorb nutrients, the leaves turn yellow and growth slows down until the soil drains.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa mumɔ. nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa fioo kɛyashiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does one sick plant in my field quickly cause the surrounding crops to get sick too?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu yeɔ hela oya lɛ?

english: Crop diseases produce tiny spores that are easily carried by wind, rain splashes, or insects from plant to plant. Early removal of infected plants prevents the spread to neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Tsei ahe helai haa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ ajie nakai kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi hela lɛ gbɛfaŋ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Can I grow two different crops together on the same piece of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, compatible crops help each other. For example, legumes like cowpeas grab nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps neighboring heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni ewa akɛ aaadu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I trim healthy-looking branches off my crop plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Trimming removes extra stems that drain energy from the main plant. By focusing energy on fewer stems, the crop directs water and nutrients straight into developing larger, higher-quality fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsei fioo komɛi anɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops fall off without turning into fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat forces crops to save water to stay alive, so they shed flowers to reduce energy demand. Providing shade or watering during hot spells helps plants keep their blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛba hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year even though I plant the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating different crops restores organic matter and brings back soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same farm plot where my cocoa is growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, but cassava must be planted at a safe distance from young cocoa. Cassava develops strong, wide roots that can steal water and nutrients from young cocoa trees if they are planted too close together.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Cassava shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ cacao tsei bibii amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Is it good to grow cocoyam alongside plantains on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ kookoo yɛ plantains masɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cocoyam and plantain grow very well together. Plantains provide the soft shade and humid soil conditions that cocoyams need to produce healthy, large tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo kɛ plantains feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Plantains haa hulutsoo be ni mli jɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba lɛ.

english: How do I know if I should cut down an old cocoa tree on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei momo ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: An old cocoa tree should be cut down if it is heavily infected with disease, produces very few pods, or completely blocks necessary sunlight from healthy young trees growing underneath it.
ga: Esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei momo lɛ amli kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa, amɛmli ŋmeii fioo pɛ, loo amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ naa kwraa kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ ahe.

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, while older traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: What is the best way to handle and cut extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe nii ni afolɔ amɛ?

english: You should use clean, sharp tools to cut off dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches close to the main stem. This improves airflow and allows sunlight to reach the pods, reducing disease.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii ni okɛfolɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no haa helai ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they get heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ enine shɛ jwɛi ni mli tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not penetrate deep into the ground, making them prone to falling under heavy fruit weight or strong winds unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ ebaagbee shi yɛ aduawai ni tsii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shishi. ja tso nibii fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoyam plants turning yellow during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cocoyams have large leaves that lose water rapidly under direct sun and heat. Yellow leaves indicate moisture stress, showing that the plant needs shade or extra soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ he haomɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ni ená hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kroko ni fata he.

english: How does cassava behave in the soil compared to other root crops like cocoyam?
