ga: Te ŋmei feɔ enii ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ akɛto shishifãi krokomɛi tamɔ kookoo he?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that drains deep soil moisture and nutrients quickly, whereas cocoyam prefers shallow, rich, moist soils and direct shade.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Cocoa, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baa nii, ni efɔ kɛ shade tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if they receive full direct sunlight all day long?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Without shade, young cocoa trees suffer leaf scorch, stunted growth, and high stress, which severely lowers their survival rate in their early years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaná baai ni shãa lɛ he amanehulu. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ haomɔ ni fa Enɛ haa wala yibiiwoo baa shi waa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my maize plants grow so slow and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiifee bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like uninvited guests at a feast. They steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving the maize with too little food to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni afɔ̃ɔɔ amɛ nine yɛ okpɔlɔŋmɛɛ ko shishi. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ náa niyenii fioo tsɔ ni enyɛɔ edara ni ewaa.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, holds in moisture from the rain, and stops weeds from popping up around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nugbɔshiimɔ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that they are receiving too much or too little water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ nitrogen lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo eji nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ ni enine shɛɔ nɔ?

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon heat even if it rained in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ leebi moŋ?

english: When the afternoon sun gets very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa shwane lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛgboiɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kukuoo ko kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to pinch off extra shoots from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots eat up the plant's energy. Removing them forces the plant to send all its food and water directly into growing larger, healthier fruits or tubers.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ aya tso yibii loo ŋmei ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil food. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to stretch its roots and leaves to grow well.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbala eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests multiply in that field. Rotating crops keeps your soil rich and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy enough to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds water well, and contains living earthworms. Pale or hard soil often lacks the food crops need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Etoɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka yɛ jɛmɛ Bei pii lɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse loo shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu niyenii tsei ahiamɔ nii ahe nii.

english: Do all crops in Ghana need full sunlight all day to grow proper yield?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ biɔ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: No, while crops like maize and sun-loving vegetables need full sun, crops like cocoa need shade from trees when they are young to keep from burning.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni sumɔɔ hulu lɛ biɔ hulu muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo he miihia tsei ahe hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdara koni amɛkashã.

english: How do I know if the crop seeds I buy will survive in my part of Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baahi shi yɛ he ni miyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Certified seed packages are tested for local weather conditions and diseases. Checking for approved government labels ensures you get seeds suited for your region's rainfall and temperature.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli kɛha maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ helai shihilɛi. Nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ooona dumɔwui ni sa kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under direct, intense sunlight. They need shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantains planted alongside them to shield them from sun heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which direction should I point cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first, wasting energy and lowering tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How do I pick the right plantain sucker to plant in a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni mikɛbaadu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. Avoid 'water suckers' that have wide leaves early on, as they produce weaker plants and smaller bunches of fruit.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante tu’ ni baai ni mli tse, tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ he mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaawo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food plant roots need to build strong, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tso shishifãi koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it a bad idea to grow maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot exhausts the same soil nutrients year after year and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plant stems with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and keeps crop roots moist during hot days.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch sunlight better and stay away from damp soil diseases, allowing the plant to store more energy in the underground tuber.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is enough land and dirt for all plants?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ kɛ muji ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal water, light, and soil food away from your crops, which causes your crops to stay small and yield fewer fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when plants don't get enough water, or when small insect pests damage the delicate parts of the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: Why are holes and dark dirt appearing inside the center leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ni mli ewo duŋ kɛ muji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that burrows into the center whorl of young maize plants to eat the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds on my land?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting maize seeds about 25 to 30 centimeters apart gives each plant enough space to gather soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, preventing them from competing with each other for survival.
ga: Abele dumɔwui ni aduɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu mli, ni no haaa abele dumɔwui lɛ akatswa akaŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: What will happen to my cassava plants if I plant too many stems close together in one small area?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he bibioo kome?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their leaves block each other from sunlight and their roots fight for nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ efee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii waa.

english: How do I know the total amount of fertilizer my crops will consume from planting day until harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛbaatsu nii kɛjɛ be mli ni adu kɛyashi be mli ni akpaa nii lɛ?

english: You calculate fertilizer needs by measuring your farm size and checking the crop's growth stages, as young crops need small amounts early on and higher amounts when flowering and fruiting.
ga: Obuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ ni osusuɔ kɛ bɔ ni otsei lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ fioo mra. kɛ babaoo mli kɛ́ ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii

english: Why is it important to calculate all my farming costs before buying my seeds and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abu okwaayeli he nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ he akɔntaa dani ahe dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Planning your total farm expenses upfront prevents you from running out of money mid-season, ensuring your crops receive required weeding, water, and nourishment all the way to harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oto oŋmɔ mli shika fɛɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shika akaho bo yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ naa jwɛi lɛ ahe tsofa, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into thin tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn leaves curl up during extreme heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss, signaling that the plant is thirsty and trying to conserve internal moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli.

english: How many months will my cassava take from planting the stem until it is mature for harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ ebaahe ni mi-cassava lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Depending on the variety, most cassava varieties in Ghana take between 9 to 12 months underground to form fully grown, mature tubers ready for digging.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or missing soil nutrients, causing the plant to drop blossoms to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and moist during their first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and stop growing when weeds cover the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the roots of tomato plants, effectively starving the crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tomato tsei ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves high into the sunlight, allowing the leaves to collect energy to feed and expand the big tubers growing under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ buaa hewalɛ naa kɛhaa niyenii ni amɛgbɛɔ bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops seem to yield so much better on newly cleared forest land compared to old farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo he lɛ?

english: Forest land has built up years of decomposed leaves and organic matter, creating rich black soil full of natural nutrients that feed crops heavily during their first few seasons.
ga: Kooi amli hei buaa baai kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ji ediŋŋ ni eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after I clear the land and rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ ni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to local soil conditions, allowing their seeds to sprout rapidly and absorb water and nutrients faster than newly introduced farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi amli. Enɛ haa amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛba lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ cacao tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight or dry winds; they need canopy trees to provide gentle shade and preserve soil moisture until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao ŋwɛi ŋta ni baaha amɛná hulutsoo blɛoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce smaller fruit bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ eshishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers compete directly with the main mother plant for food and water in the soil, spreading the plant's energy thin instead of channeling it into a single large bunch.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsei ahewalɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa fioo lɛ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu kuu agbo kome pɛ

english: What happens to cassava growth if I accidentally plant the stem cuttings upside down?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava lɛ dalɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ oshara du ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems upside down forces the new shoots to waste vital energy bending upward toward the light, resulting in delayed leaf growth and very poor root development.
ga: Yucca tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ haa ŋmeii heei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ daa blɛoo ni shishifãi lɛ hu edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does lifting yam vines onto wooden stakes really help the tubers grow bigger underground?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves into full sunlight where they can capture light energy efficiently, producing more food that travels down into the root to expand the tuber.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aje kpo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ waa. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen—an essential nutrient for green leaf growth—or that waterlogged soil is suffocating the roots and preventing nutrient uptake.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa niyenii lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when stressed by intense midday heat, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer, choosing to save water and energy rather than setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Amɛhalaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on leaf sap, which damages tender leaves and can transmit viruses that stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai bibii ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni tsiɔ tsei anaa lɛ ashwã.

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air using beneficial bacteria in their roots, leaving nitrogen-rich organic material in the soil after harvest.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or urea fertilizer helps bring back the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I alternate planting beans and maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔtsake wɔhe wɔdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but beans put nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots. Rotating them keeps your field fertile without having to buy as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ otsake amɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if my cassava crop is getting too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If cassava lacks water, its lower leaves will turn yellow and fall off early to save moisture. If it gets too much standing water, the roots underground will begin to rot and soft brown spots will show at the base.
ga: Kɛji nu fite ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ Eshishi baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni amɛbaagbee shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji onine shɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo nɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse baaje kpo yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants stop growing during the dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ moŋ?

english: Hot sun and very dry air make water evaporate rapidly through the leaves. Even if the roots get water, the heat stress forces the pepper plant to pause its growth to protect itself.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa lɛ haa nu tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ná nu po Shi dɔlɛ he haomɔ haa pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: How do shade trees help my young cocoa seedlings survive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn under full sunlight. Plantain or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around the seedlings while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. Keeping soil evenly moist helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out small and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil or rocks beneath your mounds block yam tubers from expanding straight down. Loosening the soil deeply when building mounds allows tubers to grow large and smooth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ beni afee gɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young cocoa trees so often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cocoa trees and steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, causing your cocoa seedlings to grow weak and slow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa o-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over before the fruits are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Nematode pests in the soil can also destroy the roots, making it easy for high winds to blow the plant down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ haa efeɔ tsii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji nematode lɛ hu baanyɛ afite shishifãi. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa tsei kɛshwie shi.

english: Why do bugs attack my cowpeas more when I plant them late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa mi-cowpeas lɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: As the farming season progresses, insect populations build up in nearby fields. Late-planted cowpeas flower right when pest numbers are at their highest, leading to heavy damage.
ga: Beni okwaayeli be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ayibɔ hu baaya hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Cowpeas ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baawo fɔfɔi be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ eshɛ amɛhe fe fɛɛ pɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa baa

english: What is the right way to protect myself when I am spraying pest medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mihe kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Always wear long sleeves, trousers, rubber boots, gloves, and cover your nose and mouth with a mask or cloth so the chemical medicine does not touch your skin or enter your lungs.
ga: Wo atadei ni hiɛ nine kakadaŋŋ agbo, trɔɔs kakadaŋŋ, rɔbɔt atadei, glɔvs, ni okɛ mask loo mama aha ogɔŋ kɛ odaaŋ be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ akashɛ hewolo lɛ he loo akabote fɛ̃i lɛ mli

english: What time of the day is best for me to spray chemical medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is not too hot, so the medicine does not burn the leaves or dry up before working.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulu la lɛ mli edɔɔɔ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsofa lɛ haaa baai lɛ ashã loo amɛgbi dani etsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and getting holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bu lɛ?

english: Holes and yellowing are usually signs that pests like caterpillars are eating your crops, which means you need to identify the exact insect to use the right crop medicine.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii miiye onibii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni oyɔse kooloo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni okɛ tso tsofa ni sa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Can I use the same spray that kills weeds to also kill insects on my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: No, weed killers and insect killers are completely different medicines. Using a weed killer to treat insects will kill your vegetable crops instead of protecting them.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ji tsofai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsu nii kɛtsa kooloi bibii lɛ, ebaagbe o-vegetables lɛ moŋ fe ni eeebu amɛhe.

english: How long do I need to wait to harvest my crops after spraying them with pest medicine?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ?

english: You must wait for the required chemical waiting period—usually between 7 to 14 days depending on the medicine—so the chemical breaks down completely and the harvest is safe to eat.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ be ni ato akɛ akɛbaamɛ tsofa lɛ—bei pii lɛ, gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ—no hewɔ lɛ tsofa lɛ fiteɔ kwraa ni abaanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which makes them stretch tall, stay thin, and produce very little yield.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Leaves curl up in high heat to save water and protect themselves from burning, which is a sign that the plant is under stress and needs adequate soil moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli ni ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Crops that need food usually grow slowly, have pale or yellowing leaves instead of a dark green color, and stay smaller than healthy plants of the same age.
ga: Tsei ni niyenii he hiaa lɛ fɔɔ daamɔ blɛoo. Na baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ kɛ bibii fe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii kome lɛ

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop medicines together in one knapsack sprayer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ atsake yɛ tsɔne kome ni akɛwoɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: You should not mix different farm chemicals unless guided by an extension officer, because mixing wrong chemicals can burn your crops or produce dangerous fumes.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai srɔtoi futuɔ. ja akɛ ŋaawoo ha kɛjɛ hiɛyaa he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii loo ekɛ lasu ni yɔɔ oshara aba.

english: Where is the best place for me to keep leftover pest medicine after spraying my field?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ato beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ efɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Store all farm medicines in their original containers inside a locked shed or box, far away from children, domestic animals, drinking water, and stored food.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai fɛɛ ato amɛ shishijee tsɛnsii lɛ amli yɛ tsũ loo adeka ko ni aŋã mli, yɛ he ko ni gbekɛbii, kooloi ni yɔɔ shia, nu ni anuɔ, kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ bɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves, and heavy rains can wash it out of reach of the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛha amɛbaa lɛ aya hiɛ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ lɛ kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers go soft and rot underground when the soil stays waterlogged for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When soil remains soaked with standing water, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing waterborne fungi to invade and cause rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: How do my groundnut plants produce nuts under the dirt when their flowers grow above the ground?
ga: Te mi-peanut tso lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ewo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni efɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once the groundnut flower is pollinated in the open air, it grows a long downward stem called a peg. This peg naturally bends down, pushes itself into the soft soil, and swells up to form the nut underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ, tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baa shi kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg lɛ baahi. Nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ baabɔle ehe kɛya shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsi ohe kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli. ni efuɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ ebafeɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, dry soil, or poor pollination, which forces the plant to save its strength rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees away from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunshine. They require shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantain to shield them from intense heat and conserve moisture until their roots are deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up toward the sun to capture maximum sunlight. This light energy allows the plant to produce food that gets stored underground, making the tubers grow large.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. La hewalɛ nɛɛ haa tsei feɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight wrinkled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap and transmitting plant viruses, causing the growing leaves to deform and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni miida lɛ efite ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains end up with small holes and full of white powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni eyi kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Grain weevils and tiny pests lay hidden eggs in or on the grain. Once they hatch, the larvae eat their way out from the inside, leaving empty shells and powdery flour behind.
ga: Nibii amli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtee dumɔwui amli loo amɛnɔ. Beni efɔ lɛ Lala lɛ yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ emli. Eshiɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay close to the topsoil. When a heavy fruit bunch develops, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs a strong wooden or bamboo fork for support against wind and weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbiɔ tso loo ŋmei fɔji ni wa koni amɛkɛfi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ muji lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or beans makes my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into free fertilizer that stays in the soil after harvest.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni eshwɛɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the food plants use to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or cause water to sit around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo eha nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: How come my cassava roots stay small and woody even when the leafy top looks big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ

english: Cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy tops when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or if the soil is too hard for the roots to expand. The plant needs loose, well-drained soil and balanced nutrients so energy goes down into swelling the roots.
ga: Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli kɛji nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛji sũ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni no aha amɛfuu.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot daytime temperatures, dry soil, or a lack of key nutrients. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to keep itself alive when conditions are hard.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do some of my watermelons split open on the farm before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ ekomɛi tswaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst open when they get a sudden burst of water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the rind to crack.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji nu lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ehe. gbee ŋshɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall but produce only a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Okra shoots up tall without making pods if it does not get full sunlight throughout the day or if it gets too much leaf-growing fertilizer. Okra needs bright sun and balanced food to trigger flower and pod production.
ga: Okra baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni efeee ŋmeii kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. aloo kɛji amɛná foliar fertilizer babaoo Okra he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ niyenii ni ja ni baaha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii afee.

english: Black, shriveled cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming extra cocoa branches lets in sunlight and air to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kookoo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi mli kɛ eshishitoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feed on the underside of the leaf. It can also mean a virus has been spread to the plant by these insects, making the new leaves grow deformed.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites yeɔ baa lɛ shishi. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai heei lɛ yɛ su ko ni ejaaa.

english: Why does my yam tuber start rotting inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, preventing air from reaching the tuber and allowing damp-loving rot fungi to attack it. Planting on well-raised mounds or ridges helps drain away extra rainwater.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ bulb lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not reach deep into the soil. As the heavy bunch of plantains grows near the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind or heavy rain to pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless supported with bamboo or wood props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ja ŋmei loo tso fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my cowpea vines try to climb and wrap around other crops nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea wain tso lɛ miitao ekwɔ ni ekɛ ehe abɔle ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ? bɛŋkɛ

english: Cowpea plants naturally reach out with long stems to climb over nearby plants or sticks in order to reach higher light. Climbing helps the leaves get more sun to produce the energy needed to grow healthy pods.
ga: Bush beans kɛ amɛ tsei kakadaji lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɔɔ tsei loo tsei niji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛná la ni nɔ kwɔ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko kwɔɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and thin roots that lose water quickly in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain beside them provides living shade, keeping the young trees cool and humid until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ afã lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain sits in flat soil, it drowns the roots and causes rot, so planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaafite. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves mean the maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food that makes leaves green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will feed the soil and turn the plants green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts together with maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the dirt. Maize plants then feed on this extra natural fertilizer, helping both crops grow better without exhausting the land.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the soil water, keeps the ground cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoot stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many small suckers steal food, water, and sunlight from the main plantain tree, which results in smaller fruit bunches. Keeping only two or three strong stems ensures the main tree produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers bibii babaoo tsɔ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii. Tso lɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to reach up high to collect direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the vines off the wet soil where diseases easily attack them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ anyɛ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa wain tsei akatara shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ he ni helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the leaves in the heart of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths during dry spells. Checking plants early and spraying approved neem extract or insecticides into the funnel of the leaves stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli. Ehaa nakai tsei lɛ kpaa nitsumɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before they turn into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist and feeding the soil regularly keeps the flowers attached so they can grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get black spots and wither during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by fungal diseases that spread when rain splashes mud onto the lower leaves. Spacing plants well and trimming lower leaves off the ground stops fungal spores from traveling up the plant.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji muji gbee baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei jogbaŋŋ ni ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni fungal spores lɛ akaya tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do we have to pile the soil into mounds to grow yams instead of planting directly into flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔbua sũ naa wɔwo gɔji amli koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil so their large tubers can expand easily underground without hitting hard soil. Making mounds also improves drainage so excessive rain does not rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni shikpɔŋ ni wa akatswa amɛ. Gɔji ni afee lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Can I plant new yams directly inside the old mounds from last year's harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potatoes heei yɛ ŋtayaa momo ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Reusing old mounds without breaking them down and refreshing the soil usually leads to poor yields because the previous crop exhausted the nutrients, and pests or diseases may still linger in the old mound.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ gɔji momoi tsu nii ekoŋŋ ni akpataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni ahaaa ehe ajɔ lɛ, no haaa yibii kpakpai aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fite. ni kooloi bibii loo helai baanyɛ ahi gɔŋ momo lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant the same large yams that I buy for cooking at the market on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii agboi ni miheɔ koni mikɛhoo yɛ jara nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Large market yams are harvested for consumption, not ideal for planting. Farmers use smaller whole tubers called 'seed yams' or specific cut portions with sprouting buds to start a fresh crop efficiently.
ga: Jarayeli mli ŋmeii wuji ni akpaa koni aye lɛ esaaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Okwaafoi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘Seed sweet potatoes’ loo ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni afolɔ afata ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛje ŋmɔshi nibii heei ashishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a piece of yam is good enough to use as seed for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei fã ko hi bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛduɔ nii?

english: A good seed yam must be healthy, firm, and free from rot or insect damage. It should also have visible 'eyes' or buds from which new vine shoots can easily grow.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni efee shiŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo kooloi akafite amɛ. Esa akɛ ‘hiŋmɛii’ loo hiŋmɛii ni anaa hu ahi shi. Enɛ baaha efee mlɛo aha ŋmeii heei ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yams change color or texture after I store them for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ tsake su loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha beni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. Exposure to heat, light, and air causes natural chemical changes inside, making the skin darken, the flesh change texture, or sprouts begin to form.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ, la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa tsakemɔi baa mli. Ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, etsakeɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha, loo ebɔi dalɛ.

english: How do I keep my stored seed yams from spoiling before the planting season arrives?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ akafite dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Seed yams should be stored off the ground in a shaded, well-ventilated place like a traditional yam barn. Good air movement prevents moisture build-up, rot, and premature sprouting.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ato shikpɔŋ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ tamɔ blema sweet potato ŋmɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya

english: Why do different types of yams produce different colored flesh even when grown in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ woɔ loo ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi eyɛ mli akɛ aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Different yam varieties carry distinct genetic traits passed down over generations. These natural traits determine whether the yam flesh develops as white, yellow, or purple.
ga: Sweet potato henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ fɔmɔ nii sɔrɔtoi ni jɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli sui nɛɛ tsɔɔ kɛji atomo loo lɛ yɛŋ, wuɔfɔ, loo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested yams turn out crooked or odd-shaped compared to the seed yam I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kɛ akɛto sweet potatoes dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: The shape of a growing yam depends heavily on the soil structure. If the mound has hard clay or rocks, the expanding tuber bends around obstacles, resulting in unusual shapes.
ga: Bɔ ni sweet potato ni miida lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛji gɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo tɛi ni wa Yitso ni elɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ gbɛtsii nii ahe, ni no haa efeɔ nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why does the color and texture of my mound soil change after a few months of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: Exposing soil to sun, rain, and plant root activity breaks down organic matter and washes away fine nutrients, changing the soil's color and making it looser or crustier over time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ tsei shishifãi anitsumɔ mli lɛ, efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsakemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do crops grow so well on areas of my land where old farming mounds were left years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni okwaayeli gɔji momoi ni yɔɔ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Old mounds contain buried organic matter, root remains, and topsoil gathered during past clearing, creating localized pockets of rich, concentrated nutrients over time.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni afu, shishifãi ni eshwɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni abua naa yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ahe nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii momoi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli wa baa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees turning brown and dying even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Cocoa trees can die from viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot or root fungal infections, which damage the tree's internal tubes so it can no longer absorb water and nutrients, causing it to dry up regardless of rainfall.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ agboi kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ cocoa yiteŋ ni efuu loo ŋmeii ni baa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haaa enyɛ eŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to cut down sick cocoa trees instead of giving them medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni akɛ tsofa baaha lɛ?

english: Certain cocoa diseases, especially systemic viruses, have no chemical cure. Cutting down the infected tree removes the source of infection and prevents the disease from spreading to neighboring healthy trees.
ga: Kokoo helai komɛi titri lɛ virus ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Tsofa ko bɛ ni tsaa hela. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ hela lɛ jɛɛhe lɛ, ni ehaaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that multiplies rapidly in wet, cold, or overly shaded environments, causing pods to decay quickly if air cannot flow freely around the tree.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, jɛmɛ ejɔ, loo he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle amɛhe. tsei lɛ yɛ heyeli mli

english: Can a cocoa tree recover on its own if the top branches start drying up?
ga: Ani cacao tso ko baatsa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji ŋwɛi niji lɛ bɔi gbimɔ?

english: Top branch drying, often called dieback, usually points to severe root damage, bug infestation, or disease. Without removing the bad parts or addressing the underlying problem, the tree rarely recovers and will eventually die completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni egbi, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ dieback lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite waa, kooloi eba, loo hela eba. Tso lɛ baaná naagba akɛ ebaatsake ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo kɛji ajieee nɔ ni efite lɛ loo asaaa naagba lɛ yɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a defense mechanism. Cocoa trees shed leaves during severe dry spells to reduce water loss through evaporation and protect their main stem from drying out.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi

english: Why do young cocoa saplings need shade crops like plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense daylight. Shade crops act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young trees from direct sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: As cocoa trees pass 25 to 30 years of age, their circulatory system slows down and becomes less efficient at taking up nutrients from the soil, leading to lower yield.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso eye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, lá ni hoɔ yɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi, ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Is it better to cut down a diseased cocoa tree completely at the ground level or just cut off the dry branches?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo abaafolɔ tsei niji ni egbi lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: For serious diseases like swollen shoot, the virus lives throughout the entire plant system including the roots. Cutting only the branches leaves the virus alive in the trunk, so the entire tree must be removed at ground level.
ga: Kɛha helai ni mli wa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, hela lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni shishifãi lɛ fata he. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ nine lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if a tree died because of hot weather or because of a contagious disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko miigbo yɛ latsaa loo hela ko hewɔ?

english: Weather stress typically affects all trees across an entire area equally, whereas diseases start on one or two trees and show distinct symptoms like swollen stems, spotty leaves, or sudden localized dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ saa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ he ko lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ, yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ tso kome loo enyɔ nɔ ni etsɔɔ okadii srɔtoi, tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo gbele ni baa trukaa, yɛ he kome.

english: What should I do to the soil after cutting down dead cocoa trees before I plant new seedlings?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ beni mifo kookoo tsei ni egboi lɛ sɛɛ dani midu dumɔwui heei?

english: After removing dead trees, clear away infected debris, allow the land to rest or plant shade crops, and enrich the soil with organic compost or fertilizers to give new seedlings a healthy start.
ga: Beni ajie tsei ni egboi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Jiemɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui heei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I see a few sick spots on my cocoa leaves, is it safe to ignore them if the tree looks mostly healthy?
ga: Kɛji mina helai yɛ kookoo baai anɔ lɛ Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maku mihiɛ mashwie nɔ kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ bei babaoo mli?

english: Small spots are often early signs of fungal or bacterial diseases like Black Pod. Ignoring them allows the sickness to multiply quietly, eventually spreading throughout the tree and damaging your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ahe hela ko, tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni kɛji oku ohiɛ ofɔ̃ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ aya hiɛ dioo, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can a disease on one sick crop spread to the healthy plant growing right next to it?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, plant diseases spread easily between neighboring plants through wind, rain splashes, insect bites, or shared roots. A single infected plant can quickly pass the sickness to surrounding crops if not treated.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ anɔ. loo shishifãi ni ajaa Tso kome ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ amli oya kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm regularly to inspect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Regular scouting allows you to notice subtle signs like leaf yellowing or pest damage early. Catching issues early prevents major outbreaks, saving you time, labor, and money on heavy treatments later.
ga: Scouting ni ooofee daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona okadii bibii, tamɔ baai ŋmɔŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii, mra. Naagbai ni anaa mra Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ helai ni baa lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ be, mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika baato yɛ helatsamɔ ni tsii he yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How do small insects carry sickness from one plant to another on my farm?
ga: Te kooloi bibii feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛwoɔ helai kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Insects like aphids or mealybugs feed on the sap of infected plants and pick up the disease. When they fly or crawl to neighboring healthy plants to feed, they inject the sickness directly into them.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs yeɔ tso mli nu ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni hela lɛ yeɔ amɛ. Beni amɛfoɔ loo amɛkpãa kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaye nii. Amɛwoɔ hela amɛwoɔ amɛmli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants suddenly look unhealthy just a few days after my neighbor's farm got attacked by pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ trukaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Pests and disease spores travel easily across farm borders through the wind or by crawling. When neighboring crops are infected, your nearby plants become high-risk targets and need immediate protection.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo amɛfoɔ ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ amli oya. Kɛji tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ná hela lɛ Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ baatsɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ oshara waa ni ehe baahia ni abu he amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What should I do immediately if I notice one cassava plant showing signs of disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina hela he okadii yɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ?

english: You should carefully uproot or prune the infected plant and dispose of it far from your field. Removing the source stops the sickness from jumping to the healthy cassava plants standing next to it.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi loo ofolɔ amɛ. ni okɛshɛrɛ kɛjɛ oyale lɛ he. He ni hela lɛ jɛɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa efo kɛya yucca tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni damɔ emasɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some crop diseases take a long time to show visible damage on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛtsɔɔ nɔ ni efite tsei lɛ?

english: Many plant pathogens multiply inside the stem or roots before visible symptoms appear on leaves. By the time you notice severe damage, the sickness may have already spread to adjacent crops unnoticed.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi lɛ amli dani ejieɔ okadii akpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ona nɔ ko ni efite waa lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko eyɔseee.

english: Can weeds growing close to my crops pass diseases or insects to them?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ helai loo kooloi bibii ashwã?

english: Yes, many weeds host the same insects and diseases that attack your main crops. They provide a hiding place for pests to multiply and easily move onto your healthy crops nearby.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi babaoo hiɛ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni tutuaa onibii titri lɛ nɔŋŋ. Amɛhaa he ko ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die so fast even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Rapid wilting is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that clog the plant's water tubes. Once infected, the plant starves for water internally and can spread the soil infection to nearby plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal loo bacteria helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ, nu yeɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does keeping my field clear of old, fallen crop leaves stop diseases from spreading?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔji lɛ amli tsei ni egbɔ ni egbee shi lɛ akafee nɔ ni baaha hela akagbɛ ashwã?

english: Clearing rotten leaves and debris removes the living space where disease spores and pests survive. Clean soil prevents sickness from jumping from old plant waste onto your new, healthy crops.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ sũ ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ shihilɛhei ni helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akajɛ tsei momoi amli jwɛi amli kɛba oŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do farmers in the southern part of Ghana complete their harvest earlier than us in the transitional zone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ miikpa nii oya fe wɔ ni wɔyɔɔ tsakemɔ he lɛ?

english: Southern Ghana receives the major rainy season earlier in the year compared to the transitional zone. Because their rains start earlier, crops mature faster there, allowing southern farmers to harvest while farmers in other regions are still waiting for or just starting their planting season.
ga: Ghana kooyigbɛ naa nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sa kadimɔ waa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli kɛ akɛto tsakemɔ he lɛ he. Ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi mra Nibii ni adu lɛ shwereɔ oya. Enɛ haa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Anaigbɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ miimɛ lolo loo ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ eje shishi pɛŋ.

english: What is the transitional zone in farming, and why is planting time different there?
ga: Mɛni ji tsakemɔ he yɛ okwaayeli mli? Ni mɛni hewɔ nidumɔ bei lɛ yɛ sɔrɔto lɛ?

english: The transitional zone is the area between the thick forest belt and the dry northern savanna (such as around Ejura). It has a unique weather pattern with two rainy seasons, allowing crops to be planted and harvested on a different timeline than in the deep south or far north.
ga: Tsakemɔ he lɛ ji he ni yɔɔ koo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ kooyigbɛ ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ ateŋ (tamɔ Ejura he fɛɛ he lɛ). Eyɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ bei enyɔ mli, ni ehaa aduɔ nibii ni akpaa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli fe Deep South loo North shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know when the rainy season is stable enough for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: You should wait until the ground stays moist for several consecutive days after the early rains begin. Planting after just one short rainfall can cause seeds to germinate and then wither if dry weather returns immediately.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ kuku sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can I plant new seeds immediately in the same field right after harvesting my mature crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, if there is still enough rainfall remaining in the season. However, you must clear old crop stalks and add compost or fertilizer to put back the nutrients that the previous harvest took from the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshwɛ lolo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehe baahia ni ojie tsei akutsei ni egbɔ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛ niyenii ni tsutsu kpamɔ lɛ ná kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my land need extra plant food or fertilizer if I plant two crops in the same year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ?

english: Growing crops continuously without a rest period drains the soil's natural strength. The second crop will grow weak and yield very little unless you feed the soil with organic manure or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni hejɔɔmɔ be bɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ. Tso ni ji enyɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ. Ja okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How should I clear my farm after harvest to make it ready for the next seeds quickly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ majie miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni mafee klalo kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ oya?

english: Clear the remaining leaves and weeds using a cutlass or hoe, but try not to burn them. Leaving cut plant materials on top of the soil helps hold moisture and rots down into natural food for your next batch of crops.
ga: Okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ajie baai kɛ jwɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ. But try not to burn. Tso mli nibii ni afo lɛ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my maize or grains are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa loo mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Grains show physical signs when mature: the leaves and husks turn dry and yellow, the stalks bend, and the kernels become hard when pressed with a fingernail.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii akpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Baai kɛ tsitsii lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, eshishifãi lɛ ebɔle, ni dumɔwui lɛ wa kɛji akɛ nine wa.

english: Is it good to leave my ripe crops standing in the field for a long time after they mature?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni mikwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: No, leaving mature crops in the field exposes them to insects, birds, mold, and sudden rains. Harvesting promptly protects your yield and frees up the land if you plan to plant a second crop.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa kooloi bibii, okpoi, ŋmeii, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ. Nikpamɔ baabu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ebaaha he ko afee mlɛo kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ.

english: Why does farm work become so much more stressful and busy right after the harvest period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ bafeɔ nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The transition between harvesting one crop and planting another happens in a short window. You must quickly harvest mature crops before they spoil while simultaneously clearing land and planting new seeds before the rainfall period ends.
ga: Tsakemɔ ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni akpaa kɛ ekroko ni aduɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ baa yɛ be kukuoo mli kwraa. Esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ oya dani amɛgboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jiemɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni odu dumɔwui heei dani nugbɔ lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Is it better to plant the same type of crop again right after harvest, or should I switch to a different one?
ga: Esa akɛ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Aloo esa akɛ matsake kɛya tsei krokomɛi akwɛmɔ nɔ?

english: It is better to switch crops, such as planting beans or groundnuts after harvesting maize. Changing crop types restores nitrogen to the soil and stops pests that attack maize from multiplying.
ga: Esa akɛ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ atsake tso lɛ henɔ lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds so they grow strong?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: If you plant maize seeds too close together, they fight for food, water, and sunlight, leading to thin stalks and small ears. Giving them proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough nutrients from the soil to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la yeɔ akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and very heavy leaves and fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Planting them deep enough in rich soil and propping up heavy bunches with sturdy bamboo poles prevents strong winds from knocking them down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. The leaves and clusters are very heavy. kɛ muji babaoo baa Amɛdumɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii akui amli. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa amɛ shi.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the plants have developed their first few leaves, usually about 4 to 8 weeks after planting. Adding fertilizer during a dry spell can burn the roots, while applying it right before heavy rain can wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ ebɔi eklɛŋklɛŋ baai lɛ kpojiemɔ, bei pii lɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 8 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Shi okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa koni ekɛfɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kookoo?

english: Healthy soil for cocoa is dark, crumbles easily in your hands, drains water well without getting swampy, and contains earthworms or decaying leaves, which show the soil has rich organic nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ebɛ pudgy. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai ni fiteɔ yɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and drop off during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains are usually caused by waterlogged soil that drowns the roots or fungal diseases that thrive in high humidity. Rain can also wash essential plant nutrients deeper into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ loo ŋmeii helai ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa.
