Nugbɔ hu baanyɛ afɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani midu amɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps flowers stay attached.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haoɔ mɔ waa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Why are my orange trees taking so many years to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Orange trees grown directly from seeds take up to 7 years to fruit because they must go through a long natural growth phase. Grafted orange seedlings bear fruit much faster, usually within 2 to 3 years, because they are made from mature fruit-bearing trees.
ga: Orange tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii kpawo dani amɛwoɔ yibii ejaakɛ amɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Sitrus dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ baawo yibii mra kwraa, bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ejaakɛ tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛfee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Is it good to plant beans and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good because beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural food source that helps the maize grow taller and stronger.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I prevent my yam tubers from rotting in the ground before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa?

english: Yam rot is caused by excess water standing around the tubers or fungal infections entering through damaged skin. Building high soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, protecting the yams.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni egbo baa. Tuberculosis loo fungal hela ni boteɔ hewolo ni efite mli Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Helps protect sweet potatoes

english: Vegetable seedlings have small, delicate roots that dry out quickly. Watering them lightly twice a day—early in the morning and cool late afternoon—keeps the soil damp without washing away the tiny seeds.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Water the plants gently. shii enyɔ daa gbi Leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ yɛ shwane mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the leaves lose water faster than the roots can absorb it, causing the plant to wither and die.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellowish from the tips down the middle, even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the center is a sign of nitrogen hunger in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong; when soil nitrogen is low, the plant takes nitrogen from its older leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots become woody and hard if I leave them in the soil for too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cassava stores food as starch in its roots. Once the plant reaches full maturity, it stops making starch and begins converting the roots into tough woody fibers to survive, making the tubers hard and unpleasant to eat.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii ni ji starch toɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ekpaa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ ni ebɔi eshishifãi lɛ tsakemɔ ewoɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli koni ehi shi. It makes the head hard and unappetizing.

english: Yam leaves produce food for tuber growth using sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows all leaves to capture maximum sunlight while keeping them away from damp soil diseases that cause rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛha tuber dalɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baa fɛɛ baa nine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni haa sũ fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes tomato pollen dry up or become sticky, preventing the flowers from being fertilized. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally drops the useless flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread outward rather than deep into the ground. As the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni plantains babaoo yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize eats up a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil, naturalizing and restoring your farm for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ adebɔɔ ni okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled and tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves. As they suck out the plant juices, the leaf tissue shrinks unevenly, causing the leaf to curl and twist.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Beni ejieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ, baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective shade cover over the dirt. It keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating into the air, keeping moisture near the roots longer.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ebɔle Tsei ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni haa muji nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to yield very small fruits even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer much faster than your crops can. If you do not clear weeds before applying fertilizer, you end up feeding the weeds instead of your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Ebaabi ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Removing overgrown weeds and pruning tree branches lets sunlight and wind dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ tsei aniji lɛ, ebaaha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a vital soil food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new growth, leaving the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks that fall over easily and yield very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of big leaves but produce very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen (often from using the wrong fertilizer), the plant puts all its energy into growing green foliage above ground instead of sending energy down to build big roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ (Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli) Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔlii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die off while the yams are still under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni sweet potato lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: The vine drying up at the end of the rainy season is natural. It means the plant has finished transferring all its nutrients into the underground tuber, signaling that the yam is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Eji adebɔɔ naa nɔ akɛ wain tsei baagbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tightly like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juices from under the leaves, or by viruses they spread. This prevents the leaves from spreading flat to capture sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the days get extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. The plant drops flowers to conserve water and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔi ahe.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are special plants that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them restores soil fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture after the first rain to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Scoop up a handful of topsoil and squeeze it into a ball. If it holds its shape without leaking water, but crumbles easily when you poke it, the soil has just the right moisture for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi. Shi efoɔ oya kɛ́ okɛwo muji lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa bɔni afee ni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Rice thrives in low-lying areas or swampy soils, often called valleys or inland valleys, because these soils hold water well. If your land stays wet or muddy for long periods during the rainy season, it is generally ideal for rice.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ jɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔji nɛɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo eyɛ muji be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What makes yam tubers grow small or bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand downward easily. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tubers struggle to push through, resulting in small, stunted, or crooked yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaawa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii, ni egbɔjɔ loo ni efite lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key food it needs to grow green and strong. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the topsoil, leaving the crop hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nɛkɛ niyenii kpakpa nɛɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown at the edges during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ mli egbi ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large, broad leaves that lose water very quickly in hot weather. When the soil dries out, the plant shuts down water flow to the leaf tips first to protect its trunk and main stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ naa klɛŋklɛŋ koni ebu tso lɛ shishi kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The stress causes the plant to shed blossoms to save energy instead of forming young fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted in very rich soil, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of producing the flowers that turn into seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ fɔfɔi nɛ ba peeɔ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why does my okra plant stop bearing new pods after just a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ ekpa ŋmeii heei feemɔ yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If you leave old, large okra pods on the stalk to mature, the plant assumes its work is done and stops making new flowers. Harvesting young pods regularly encourages the plant to keep producing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshi okra ŋmeii wuji yɛ tso lɛ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, Tso lɛ baabu lɛ akɛ egbe naa ni ebaakpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ daa lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eya nɔ ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How does planting my crops too close together affect how they grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight underground for water and soil food, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. This creates thin, weak stalks and smaller overall harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Weeds are strong competitors that steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight directly from your crop roots. When weeds take over, your crops go hungry and their growth stalls.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni he wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛdalɛ baakpa.

english: What causes cassava roots to become hard and woody instead of soft and starchy?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni amɛfeɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cassava roots turn woody when they are left in the ground far past their maturity time or when the plant experiences severe, prolonged dry spells, causing the root to store tough fibers instead of smooth starch.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa kwraa. aloo beni tso lɛ naa ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni esɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni wa yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize farm turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying the right nitrogen-rich fertilizer at the right time feeds the plant and turns the leaves healthy green again.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ niyenii ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce weak crops now even though the rainfall is always sufficient?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting crops on the same piece of land year after year without resting the soil or adding manure pulls all the food out of the ground. The soil gets starved of nutrients, so plants cannot grow well regardless of how much rain falls.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni akɛ sũ lɛ ejɔɔɔ he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. The soil does not receive enough nutrients. No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛ waa ha lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Big shade trees protect them from burning heat and keep the soil moist, acting like living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo, amɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This competition makes all the plants weak and leads to thin stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Lifting the vines onto stakes allows the leaves to spread out and catch direct sunlight to make food for the growing yam tuber underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni enáa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why are there deep chewed holes inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni ŋmɔɔ yɛ mi-abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide and feed inside the growing center of maize plants. Early treatment with approved pest control methods stops them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsamɔ mra Gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting and smelling bad inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits in the field without draining properly, excess moisture suffocates the roots and causes fungal rot. Planting cassava on mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps tubers healthy.
ga: Beni nu efo ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli ni anyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ mli lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn ni mikpaa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossbred to perform best only in their first generation. Seeds harvested from hybrid plants lose their high-yield power in the second season, resulting in uneven growth and a smaller harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ ŋmaa bibioo baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers stress from extreme heat, uneven watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist and protecting plants from harsh heat helps flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ye dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tomato he.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water and protect themselves from heat. Once the rainy season returns, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni amɛkɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of green leaves but not producing any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai bɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen from soil or fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing foliage instead of flowering. Reducing nitrogen and adding phosphorus encourages the plants to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akɛ phosphorus fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: How can I tell when my maize is fully ready to harvest so I don't pick it too early?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he koni okakpa mra tsɔ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, the silks at the tip of the cob turn dark brown, and a small black spot appears at the base of each kernel when pulled off the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi kɛji ajie kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or companion crops like plantains to protect their tender leaves from burning and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: If I plant my crops very close to each other, will I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce maximum yield.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm help the maize I plant there in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you rotate cowpeas with maize, the maize uses that stored nitrogen to grow stronger without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji otsake tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ŋmãa babaoo awo mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the afternoon heat or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate quickly, allowing the plant roots to drink properly.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni no haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha tsei shishifãi ni amɛnuɔ nu.

english: Why is my combined harvester leaving a lot of rice grains spilled on the ground behind it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-combin harvever lɛ shwieɔ ŋmaa babaoo eshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Grain loss from a combined harvester usually happens if the rice is harvested when it is too dry and brittle, or if the machine's speed and cutting height are not set correctly for the field conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ amli lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa be mli ni egbi tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ atooo tsɔne lɛ oyaiyeli kɛ bɔ ni ekɛfoɔ nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi lɛ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot quickly in the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Yams rot in the soil when water accumulates around the tubers due to poor soil drainage or excessive rain, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases and bacteria to attack the crop.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Tubers ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal kɛ bacteria helai ni baatutua ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do small insects destroy my stored maize even when I dried it in the sun before storing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Sun-drying might not reduce the internal moisture low enough for long-term storage, allowing hidden insect eggs or damp spots to encourage weevils to multiply inside your storage bags or cribs.
ga: Hulu la ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ nyɛŋ aha mligbɛ fɛ̃i lɛ aba shi bɔ ni sa kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii akui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ yɛ obaagi loo okpɔŋɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I clear old bush and wild plants properly before planting new cocoa trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii kɛ koo mli tsei momoi lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu kookoo tsei heei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing the land completely removes aggressive weeds that steal water and soil nutrients, giving young cocoa seedlings a clean environment to establish strong roots and grow fast.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwraa. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli tse koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdara oya.

english: Can using motorized machines help me prepare my land for cocoa planting better than doing it all by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha kookoo dumɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baadu fɛɛ?

english: Machinery speeds up heavy land clearing by uprooting tough tree stumps and clearing dense brush quickly, allowing you to prepare large areas of land in time for the planting season.
ga: Mashiŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ajieɔ hei ni tsii lɛ oya kɛtsɔ tsei akutsei ni wa ni ejieɔ oya kɛ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ shishi lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ osaa hei wuji yɛ be ni sa mli kɛha be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my young cocoa plants if the land is not properly cleared before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ajieee jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu?

english: If the land is not cleared properly, hidden pests and fast-growing weed roots will compete with your young cocoa trees for sunlight and nourishment, causing the seedlings to stunt or die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ jwɛi shishifãi ni miida oya lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afee bibii loo amɛ gboi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need to be pruned when their branches get too thick and crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo mi-cocoa tso lɛ mli be mli ni eniji lɛ ebɔle ehe tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach all branches, which prevents humidity build-up and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ niji fɛɛ niji ahe. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ aba shi ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi babaoo.

english: How does cutting back overgrown branches help my cocoa farm produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Removing excess and unproductive branches allows the cocoa tree to direct its energy and nutrients straight into growing healthy, larger cocoa pods rather than feeding unnecessary leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa cacao tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa cacao tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ foliar niyenii ni he ehiaaa baaha lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do cocoa trees stop bearing good fruits when the farm becomes too dark and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni jwɛi ewo mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need adequate sunlight to make food for pod development. When the canopy is too dense, shade blocks the light, causing flowers to drop and reducing the number of pods that form.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli eyi tsɔ lɛ, hulutsoo tsiɔ la naa, ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni feɔ lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: What benefit does cutting back old, thick cocoa trees bring to a farm that is declining in yield?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni etse lɛ ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nibii ni anáa lɛ miiba shi lɛ mli?

english: Cutting back old or overcrowded cocoa trees stimulates the plant to grow fresh, energetic shoots, effectively renewing the tree so it can bear heavily again in upcoming seasons.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ Koni enyɛ ewo lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei amli.

english: Why would I need petrol on my cocoa farm if I am just growing trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu he hiaa mi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be ni miduɔ tsei kɛkɛ?

english: Petrol is needed to run power tools like motorized pruners, brush cutters, and chainsaws, which make heavy farm jobs like cutting thick branches and clearing debris much faster and easier.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ pɛtrol atsu nii koni akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ atsu nii. brush cutter kɛ electric saw Enɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ tsuɔ nii waa, tamɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni afoɔ. Ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yaa oya ni ebɛ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How does clearing away fallen branches and farm debris help protect my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni egbee shi kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Removing dead wood and plant debris destroys hiding places for pests like mirids and prevents fungal spores from surviving in the ground and infecting healthy trees.
ga: Tsoi ni egboi kɛ tsei amli sũi ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ myrids lɛ hiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hela aba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it better to use power tools for heavy pruning instead of just using a regular cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi fe nibii ni akɛ tsɔne ni akɛtswaa la tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ? Instead of using a normal dagger?

english: Power pruners cut through thick, tough wood cleanly and quickly without splitting the bark, which helps the tree heal faster and reduces the chance of disease entering the cut wood.
ga: Mɔ ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni mli wa ni mli tse lɛ oya ni efolɔɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsaa oya. ni eha hegbɛ ni helai baanyɛ abote tso ni afo lɛ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Why does my farm get overgrown with thick weeds so quickly after I clear it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mli edɔ eyiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya beni mijie mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In tropical regions like Ghana, cleared farmland gets full sunlight and rain, which triggers wild weed seeds already resting in the soil to germinate rapidly alongside your crops.
ga: Yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ, ŋmɔji ni ajie amɛhe lɛ naa hulu kɛ nugbɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave cleared brush to decompose instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miha jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ fite moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and dries out the topsoil, whereas leaving cleared vegetation to decay naturally creates a protective mulch that retains soil moisture and adds natural nutrients.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataa he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight and high heat. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them during their early years to keep their foliage cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli koni amɛbaa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the middle of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which prevents excessive water evaporation during peak heat hours.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fe nine yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge leaves and stems but yielding very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water early on, the cassava plant directs all its energy into lush top growth above ground rather than storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli mra lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat during high sunshine hours or irregular watering stresses the plant, preventing successful pollination and causing the flower stems to weaken and drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. tsiɔ pollination naa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants with lower overall harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibii fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my cassava and maize plants grow well together when I plant them on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows rapidly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first. Intercropping them makes full use of land and sunlight without immediate competition between the two crops.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. As for cassava, it will grow slowly in the beginning. Interplanting allows for maximum use of land and sunlight without immediate competition between the two plants.

english: Why do caterpillars and grasshoppers attack my crops much more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The warm rain causes plants to flush with tender new leaf growth, providing abundant food and humid air that encourages insect eggs to hatch faster.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ blɛoo koni ekwɛ baai heei. Eji niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ kooloi akui hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot quickly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that continue to breathe after harvest. Direct sunlight, high humidity, or small cuts made during harvesting allow fungi to enter and cause rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli wa, loo ŋmeii bibii ni afolɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ abote mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Why does strong wind easily push over and uproot my corn plants during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa oya ni ejieɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn has a shallow root system and grows tall with heavy cobs at the top, making it top-heavy. If the soil is very soft from heavy rain, or if the soil hasn't been heaped around the base of the stems (earthing up), strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the ground.
ga: Corn has a shallow, tall root system with a heavy cob on top. ha efee nɔ ni tsii Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔleko tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ shishitoo), kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaves and grow strong. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil away from young roots, or the soil itself may just be tired and need manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji niyenii bolɔmɔ. especially nitrogen This is what plants need to keep their leaves green and grow strong. Heavy rain can flush nitrogen deep into the soil, away from young roots. Or the soil itself may be tired and in need of manure or fertilizer.

english: Why are the green cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions during the rainy season. When trees are too crowded or weeds are tall, air cannot blow through to dry the pods, allowing the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo jwɛi lɛ kɛlɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's juices. It can also happen when the plant gets infected by a virus carried by these insects during hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ekɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji tsei lɛ ná helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special natural features in their roots that pull food (nitrogen) out of the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil so that your maize can grow bigger without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli su krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni o-abele lɛ adara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Dry grass acts like an umbrella for the soil (called mulching). It blocks the hot sun from baking the earth, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating away quickly so roots stay wet longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. (This is called mulching.) It blocks the hot sun from baking the earth, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly. koni shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water gathers in the ground and cannot drain away. Without air in the soil, the roots drown and soil fungi attack them. Building high soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly very wet. The plant drops its flowers to save its own life when weather conditions make it hard to feed new fruit.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miihao amɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa ewaa akɛ amɛaaha aduawai heei aba lɛ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: The small shoots (suckers) act like children fighting for the same food as the mother plantain stem. If you leave too many, none of them will get enough food. Leaving only one or two strong shoots gives you bigger, heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Tsoi bibii (tsoji) lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii. Tao kɛha niyenii yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni dumɔwui ashishifãi wuɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ eshwɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko nine shɛŋ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting too early inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ oya tsɔ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams wake up and sprout when their environment gets warm and humid, which tricks them into thinking the planting season has arrived. Keeping your storage barn well-shaded, cool, and airy keeps the yams sleeping longer until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ shihilɛ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. ni lakaa amɛ ni amɛsusuɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ ebashɛ. Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli hulutsoo, ni eyɛ fɛ̃i, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ ni amɛwɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: If I bring maize seeds from another town, will they automatically grow well on my farmland?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ba kɛjɛ maŋ kroko mli Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Seeds perform differently depending on local rainfall, soil type, and climate. Just because a crop variety yields well in another region does not mean it will thrive in your soil without testing or checking its suitability first.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Akɛni tso henɔ ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ hewɔ lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okaaa lɛ okwɛɛɛ loo okwɛɛɛ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is good for growing corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Different crops require specific nutrients, moisture levels, and soil types. You can determine suitability by observing how similar crops perform nearby, but getting your soil checked by agricultural officers gives you the most accurate answer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Humidity level kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ Obaanyɛ ona bɔ ni sa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nakai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baakwɛ mli lɛ baaha oná hetoo ni ja fe fɛɛ.

english: If my soil looks dark and rich, does that mean any crop I plant on it will yield well?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni ewoɔ nii Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Soil color alone can be deceiving because crops have hidden needs like proper drainage and balanced mineral levels. Dark soil might be good for vegetables but lack the specific nutrients needed for grain crops like maize.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su pɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hiamɔ nii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ mineral levels ni ja Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha aduawai shi ebɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do crops sometimes fail even on fresh land that has never been farmed before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni awoko nɔ dã po nɔ lɛ?

english: Virgin land is not automatically fertile for every crop. It may naturally lack key nutrients, be too acidic, or retain too much water, so matching the right crop to the natural condition of the soil is still necessary.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ jeee nɔ ni woɔ yibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ acid tsɔ. loo ehiɛɔ nu babaoo mli, no hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi lɛ akpã gbee lɛ he miihia lolo.

english: Why should I bother asking a soil expert to check my farmland before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi shikpɔŋ he nilelɔ ko ni ekwɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani mibɔi dumɔ?

english: A soil expert helps you understand what nutrients your land is missing and what crops will grow best there. Testing your soil saves you money by preventing crop failure and showing you exact fertilizer needs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ he nilelɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni onu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi. kɛ tsei ni bakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai he lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa haa okɛ shika baa shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: What actually happens when soil scientists test the dirt from my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ he nilelɔ ko ka shikpɔŋ ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛ?

english: Scientists analyze samples of your soil to check its richness, acidity levels, and water retention capacity. This reveals whether your land can support crops like corn, cassava, or cocoa, or what treatment it needs first.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi pɛiɔ osũ mli nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ha. Acidity level kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛ nu toɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Aloo tsamɔ ko he miihia bo klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Can I just apply a lot of fertilizer instead of having a scientist check my soil quality?
ga: Mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fataa he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha jeŋ nilelɔi akwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer cannot fix every soil problem, such as high acidity or poor drainage, and adding the wrong fertilizer can waste money or damage your crops. A soil expert tells you precisely what your land needs rather than guessing.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ naagba fɛɛ naagba, tamɔ acidity ni fa loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shika loo efite onibii. Shikpɔŋ he nilelɔ ko baatsɔɔ bo nɔ tuuntu ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu he

english: What is the very first step I should take before clearing a huge plot of land for a new farm?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee dani mafo shikpɔŋ agbo ko nɔ kɛha ŋmɔ hee?

english: Before spending time and money to clear land, you should first confirm if the soil is suitable for the crop you want to plant. Seeking advice from extension officers ensures you do not waste resources on land that will not produce well.
ga: Dani obaafite be kɛ shika ni okɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Esa akɛ okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni otaoɔ odu lɛ. Kɛ́ obi o-extension officer lɛ ŋaawoo lɛ, ebaaha okɛ nibii akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall in one part of my field but stay small in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi amɛfeɔ bibioo yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality can change across different sections of the same land due to variations in depth, water retention, or past farm use. Identifying these soil differences helps you apply targeted treatments or plant better-suited crops in those spots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ hei srɔtoi. shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Yɛ nu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi loo bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ Shikpɔŋ srɔtoi nɛɛ ni oooyɔse lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okɛ tsofafeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii loo odu tsei ni sa babaoo yɛ nakai hei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my new piece of land needs treatment before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni akwɛ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani adu dumɔwui?

english: You can look for signs like poor water drainage, hard packed ground, or weak wild weeds, or ask an extension officer to test soil samples. These signs show whether the land needs lime, organic manure, or proper plowing before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao okadii tamɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. He ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ Aloo bi extension officer lɛ ni eka shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ekwɛ. Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia lime, humus, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa dani adu nii.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. When soil food is low or washed away by heavy rain, the plant moves nutrients from old lower leaves to feed young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa Be mli ni niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ etswa lɛ. Tso lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves roll up during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and drop slightly during hot afternoons to reduce water loss through their skin. It is a normal defense behavior to survive drought until the cool evening or rain comes.
ga: Kasava lɛ baabɔle ehe ni ebaagbee shi fioo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi Eji nɔ ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he koni anyɛ aye wala yɛ hɔmɔ, fɛ̃i loo nugbɔshiimɔ mli.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off before any fruits start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the crop is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Without steady moisture and balanced soil food, the plant discards flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ, Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves each plant weak, causing thin stems and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are adapted to forest conditions and have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct harsh sun. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them until their root systems grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ koo mli shihilɛi amli, ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ko kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Is it safe for me to grow cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the field after the maize is removed.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and wet during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a water-loving fungus that spreads fast in high humidity and heavy rainfall. Wet conditions allow the fungus to enter the pod skin and rot the beans inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛ waa. Shihilɛi ni mli ewo nu lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ pod lɛ hewolo lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers are ready when the leaves and vines on top begin to turn yellow and naturally dry up. This sign shows that the plant has stopped growing leaves and stored all its energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ ebaa lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny holes in my cabbage leaves stop the heads from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabe baa mli lɛ haaa yitsei lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Insects eat holes in leaves, which damages the plant's food factories. Plants use whole leaves to collect sunlight and grow; damaged leaves mean less energy to form large, heavy crop heads.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ bu yɛ baai amli ni efiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbua hulu la naa ni amɛdara. Baai ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ fioo ni akɛbaafee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops start growing fast in the first month but then stop growing completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkpa shweremɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds contain initial energy to push out the first roots and shoots, but once that food runs out, the crop depends entirely on the soil. If the soil lacks nutrients or is hard and compacted, plant growth stalls.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishijee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Shi kɛ́ niyenii lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tso lɛ dalɛ kpaɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to filter the hot sun, the heat burns the tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture that the plant needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ajɛ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Is it true that cocoa crops produce better if I give them a mix of sun and shade instead of full sunlight?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kookoo tsei woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji miha amɛ hulu kɛ hulutsoo yɛ hulu ni yeɔ emuu lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, cocoa thrives best in filtered light—a balance of partial sun and partial shade. Full sunlight causes stress and heat damage, while complete dark shade slows down growth and pod production.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kane ni mli tse mli. ni ji hulu fã ko kɛ hulutsoo fã ko ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa. Yɛ be mli ni shade ni yeɔ emuu lɛ baaha pod lɛ adalɛ kɛ efeemɔ aya hiɛ fioo lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is getting too much shade from the big forest trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo kɛmiijɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: If your farm has too much shade, the cocoa trees will grow tall and thin as they stretch for light, produce fewer flowers and pods, and the damp conditions can encourage fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo Cacao tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ ashɛ amɛhe koni amɛmɔ la lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo Ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe hewalɛ.

english: Do mature cocoa trees need the same amount of shade as newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulutsoo kɛ agbɛnɛ hu hulutsoo. Kɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: No, young seedlings require heavy shade to protect them while establishing roots. As cocoa trees grow bigger and form their own leaf canopy, they can tolerate more light, but they still benefit from scattered permanent shade trees.
ga: Dabi, tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaa lɛ, Amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ la babaoo gbɛ. Shi enáa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ ahe sɛɛ lolo.

english: Should I cut down every single tree on my land before I start planting my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mabɔi kookoo dumɔwui dumɔ?

english: No, clearing all trees leaves your soil exposed to erosion and subjects young cocoa plants to intense sun. It is better to keep selected beneficial shade trees to protect the young crops.
ga: Dabi, tso fɛɛ tso ni ooojie lɛ baafite oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ebaaha hulu lɛ ashɛ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ ato tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe.

english: A heavy windstorm knocked down several large shade trees on my farm; will this affect my cocoa yield?
ga: Ahum ni naa wa ko tswa tsei wuji babaoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amɛshwie shi. Ani enɛ baaná mi-kookoo yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, losing major shade trees exposes the cocoa trees beneath them to sudden direct sunlight, which can stress the plants, scorch their leaves, and lower pod yield until new shade is established.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni baaje mli lɛ baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ashɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ahao, eshã baai lɛ, ni eha pod lɛ nɔ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo hee baaba.

english: Can I plant any tree I find in the forest to provide shade for my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei ni anaa yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ koni mikɛha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Not all trees are good for cocoa. Some trees steal too much water, attract cocoa pests, or grow too dense. It is best to use approved shade trees like leguminous trees or economic trees like avocado and timber species.
ga: Jeee tsei fɛɛ hi kɛha kookoo. Tsei komɛi juɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Egbalaa kookoo mli kooloi loo aduɔ babaoo tsɔ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ hegbɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii, loo shika helɛtemɔ tsei, tamɔ avocado kɛ hickory tsei baatsu nii.

english: Why does the government extension officer recommend keeping shade trees when some farmers say cutting them makes harvesting easier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ mli onukpai ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ? Beni okwaafoi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: While removing trees makes moving around easier, shade trees protect the cocoa long-term by keeping the soil cooler, preserving moisture, and extending the producing lifespan of your farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛfaa feɔ mlɛo moŋ, Shi tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo he yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ejɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be ahi shi ni oha nibii ni afeɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi

english: If I am setting up a large farm, how close together should I space my permanent shade trees among the cocoa?
ga: Kɛji miima ŋmɔ agbo Te esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ ama kookooi lɛ ateŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Permanent shade trees should be spaced roughly 12 to 15 meters apart so they provide an even overhead canopy without blocking out all the light needed for cocoa pod development.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ ajɛ amɛhe aaafee mitai 12 kɛyashi 15 koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ŋwɛi po afee nɔ ni tsiii kane fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweremɔ naa.

english: Why do farms in our community seem hotter and drier now compared to when our elders were farming years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔɔ ni amɛmli edɔ waa kɛ akɛto be mli ni wɔ onukpai lɛ ŋmɔ amɛ yɛ nakai afii fɛɛ ni eho lɛ amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Over time, widespread clearing of big forest trees reduced natural shade and humidity. Without natural tree cover, the local microclimate becomes hotter, making crops dry out faster.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ yɛ kooi amli babaoo lɛ eha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ eba shi. Kɛji adebɔɔ mli tso ko bɛ ni haa nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, jɛmɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo lɛ baafee hulutsoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbiɔ oya.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds so they grow big cobs?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni maná ŋmeii wuji?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing maize roughly 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants gives each stalk enough room to feed and grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75, ni tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 40, ni ehaa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni edara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I measure an acre of land accurately if I do not have modern tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu acre kome pɛpɛɛpɛ? Kɛji obɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii

english: Standard field measurement can be done using a marked rope or by pacing steps. One acre is roughly 70 yards by 70 yards, which is about the size of a standard Ghanaian football pitch.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ kpãai ni akadi loo kɛtsɔ pacing gbɛjianɔtoi anɔ asusu ŋmɔ mli susumɔi ni sa lɛ ahe. Acre kome dalɛ ji aaafee yards 70 kɛ yards 70, ni ji aaafee Ghana bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop fertilizer right against the stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated minerals and salts that can burn delicate plant stems and roots if touched directly. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small ring or side-band a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo sɛɛgbɛ ŋta lɛ kɛ ŋta lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: How many bags of fertilizer do I actually need for one acre of maize?
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kotokui enyiɛ he hiaa mi diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmãa acre 1?

english: For standard maize production, extension guidelines usually recommend about two bags of NPK for planting and one to two bags of Urea or SOA for top-dressing per acre, depending on your soil's existing fertility.
ga: kɛha ŋmãa ni afeɔ daa lɛ Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ ŋmãa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ he lɛ fɔɔ NPK ni miihe ashɛ kotokui 2 he ŋaawoo kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ. kɛ urea loo SOA kotokui 1-2 akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ nɔ yɛ acre kome mli. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them acts as a living shelter to keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. Tomatoes curl their leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to the sun, which prevents the plant from losing too much water during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná nu babaoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmã duɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the surrounding maize crop and improves overall soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my pepper crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha he ni agbele ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter is called mulching. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps root temperatures cool under direct sunlight, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why are tiny worms chewing holes in the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest that lays eggs in the heart of the plant. Early detection and applying approved organic or chemical sprays directly into the whorl helps save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves start turning yellow and dry out. You can also pull up one plant to test: if the inside of the pods has dark veins and the nuts fill the shell completely, it is harvest time.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso kome hu kɛya ŋwɛi ni oka lɛ okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy enough to support a good crop harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly in your hands, holds water without turning into a swamp, and has living earthworms. Hard, pale, or dusty soil needs organic matter like animal manure or rotten leaves added to bring it back to life.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ngɛ nine mi. Ehiɛɔ nu mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋshɔŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hiɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli tse, loo ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ biɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi aŋmei loo baai ni egboi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly after rain, and breaks down over time to feed your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. ni efiteɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for plant food like nitrogen, or that too much standing water around the roots is suffocating them. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha tsei niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe. Shishifãi babaoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it mean my yam crops are dying when the leaves and vines turn brown and dry up?
ga: Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ miigbo beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: No, when yam vines dry up late in the season, it is a natural process showing the plant has finished growing above ground and has transferred all its food into the underground tuber, meaning it is ready for harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ eniyenii fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted to survive harsh soils and droughts over many years, allowing them to sprout instantly after rain, whereas cultivated crop seeds take more time and care to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa kɛ hɔmɔ nɔ afii babaoo. Ha amɛkwɛ̃ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ heɔ be kɛ hiɛdɔɔ koni shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and feel sticky during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and get sticky when tiny pests like whiteflies or mealybugs gather on the underside to suck the leaf sap. The sticky substance is waste left by the insects, which can attract mold and slow plant growth.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs bua amɛhe naa yɛ shishigbɛ koni amɛnu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni ŋmɛɔ lɛ ji kooloi amli jwɛi ni baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii kɛba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.
