english: Twisted or cupped pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny microscopic pests like mites or thrips feeding on the tender young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by sap-sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings need taller plants like plantains grown right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that act as living natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become extremely hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil making the plant grow heavy leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa ni tsii yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: If I add double the amount of chemical fertilizer to my crops, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ toi enyɔ Ani ebaada oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much chemical fertilizer can burn plant roots and ruin the soil, just like putting too much salt in food. Crops grow best when given small, recommended amounts of fertilizer at the right times.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nakai eji yɛ ŋoo babaoo ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ he. Tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: A greenhouse is a plastic or glass house that protects crops from harsh rains, diseases, and insect pests, allowing you to grow high-value vegetables like tomatoes year-round under controlled conditions.
ga: Greenhouses ji plastic greenhouses loo greenhouses ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, helai, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ aduawai ni jara wa waa, tamɔ tomato, afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli.

english: Are greenhouses only meant for cold countries, or can I build one here in Ghana?
ga: Afee greenhouses aha maji ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ pɛ. Aloo manyɛ mama ŋmɔ ko yɛ Ghana biɛ?

english: Greenhouses were originally made for cold climates to trap warmth, but when properly adapted with ventilation nets and shade cloths, they work very well in hot tropical regions like Ghana too.
ga: Shishijee lɛ ama greenhouses kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛhiɛ dɔlɛ mli. Shi kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋtayaa ni haa mɔ mumɔ kɛ mama ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Nɛkɛ ŋtayaai nɛɛ hu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tamɔ Ghana.

english: How do farmers in hot, dry places like Israel manage to grow crops successfully in greenhouses?
ga: Te okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi tamɔ Israel lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Farmers in hot countries like Israel use heat-blocking plastic covers, drip irrigation to conserve moisture, and shade nets with side ventilation to keep the greenhouse cool enough for healthy crop growth.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ maji ni mli edɔ tamɔ Israel lɛ kɛ plastic ni nyɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nu ni hoɔ koni eha hulutsoo kɛ shade netting kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sɛɛ koni eha greenhouse lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why is having mesh netting on the sides of a greenhouse important in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aná mesh netting yɛ greenhouse lɛ afãi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Side netting allows cool breeze to flow through the structure to flush out trapped hot air, while still keeping destructive insects from getting inside to attack your crops.
ga: Mesh ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli koni ejie kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plants get so hot and wilt inside a plastic greenhouse during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ plastic greenhouse lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plastic structures naturally trap heat from sunlight like a closed car. In warm regions, this trapped heat builds up quickly and stresses plants if there isn't enough airflow or shade to cool the inside.
ga: Plastic ni akɛfee lɛ lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ tamɔ tsɔne ni agbe naa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɛɛ Dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ buaa ehe naa oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ haoɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo hulutsoo be ni baaha amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛmli lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I lower the heat inside my greenhouse so my vegetables do not burn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo la ni yɔɔ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ shi koni aduawai lɛ akashã?

english: You can reduce heat by placing a shade net over the top roof, spraying a fine mist of water during peak sun hours, and opening side vents to allow hot air to escape.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha dɔlɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ shade ŋshɔŋ ni oookɛwo ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ nu fioo afɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni ogbele sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops inside a greenhouse need more water on very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures rise inside a greenhouse, plants sweat water through their leaves much faster to cool themselves down, causing them to draw up far more moisture from the soil.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya kwraa koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei baanyɛ agbala nu babaoo kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the delicate pollen inside crop flowers, preventing them from forming fruit. Keeping the temperature cooler helps the flowers stay healthy and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei fɔfɔi amli lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa etsuuu nii Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Which vegetable varieties perform best when grown under high heat?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi?

english: Heat-tolerant varieties of peppers, cucumbers, and sweet tomatoes are specially bred to withstand warm temperatures and produce high yields even during hot seasons.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmeii, kukumbai kɛ tomatoi ni ŋɔɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli po.

english: Is it better to grow my crops in an open field or under a protective shade structure during the dry, hot season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Growing under a protective shade structure during hot seasons shields crops from intense direct sunlight, reduces soil water loss, and protects plants from heavy pest damage better than open fields.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ da yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nu ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsii ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: Leaving proper space between maize plants prevents them from competing with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Giving each seed enough room ensures the stalks grow strong and yield larger ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ kɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmãa babaoo.

english: How deep into the soil should I push seed corn when I am planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Seeds should generally be planted about two to three centimeters deep. This protects them from birds and sun heat while keeping them moist enough to sprout easily.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Enɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my seeds after the first rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays moist a few inches deep after two or three strong rains. Planting too early after a light rain can cause seeds to dry out if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: Cassava leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when the plant receives too much or too little water. Adding organic manure can help replenish the soil.
ga: Cassava baai tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and thin without producing many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants stretch upward and grow thin when they are planted too close together or shaded. They stretch to reach sunlight instead of using their energy to develop fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes some of my planted seeds to never sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni haaa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep for sunlight to reach them, or if insects and pests eat them under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. aloo afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la nyɛŋ abote mli Aloo kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds in my farm make my main crops grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, water, and sunlight from the soil that your main crop needs. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nourishment goes straight to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ ni onibii titrii lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it good to plant beans in the same field next to my pepper plants?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside peppers is beneficial because beans trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the pepper plants grow healthier.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni pepper tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I trim off the small extra shoots growing on the sides of my tomato plants?
ga: Esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ. Ani ajieɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Removing those extra side shoots, called suckers, helps the plant direct all its food and energy into growing bigger fruits rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo yibii wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii.

english: How can I check if my crop's soil has enough water without buying special equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni miheee nibii krɛdɛɛi?

english: You can push a stick or your finger about two inches into the dirt. If the soil feels cool and damp and sticks to your finger, there is enough moisture for your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso lɛ loo onine ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ oniji ahe Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it safe for me to scoop crop chemical powders or liquids using my bare hands?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ miniji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baafolɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli powda loo nu?

english: No, farm chemicals absorb quickly through human skin and can cause serious long-term illness or skin burns. Always wear protective gloves and use proper measuring utensils when handling crop medicines.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ oya. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela ni naa wa loo hewolo nɔ shãa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aba. Wo glɔvs ni buɔ mɔ he be fɛɛ be ni okɛ susumɔ nibii ni sa atsu nii kɛji ootsu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofa he nii.

english: How can I tell if my stored farm chemical or fertilizer has gone bad?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ efite?

english: Farm chemicals and fertilizers lose their effectiveness if they clump tightly, change color, develop an unusual smell, or pass their expiration date. Using spoiled chemicals can damage your crops instead of protecting them.
ga: Tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe, amɛtsake amɛhe su, ni amɛná ŋmɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto. aloo be ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ eho Tsofai ni fiteɔ nii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeebu amɛhe.

english: Leaf yellowing and curling usually mean the plant is suffering from missing soil nutrients like nitrogen or an attack by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids. Inspecting the undersides of leaves helps identify pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids lɛ miitutua lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ana tsɛŋemɔ helai mra.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year even though I plant on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows soil diseases to build up. Rotating crops like maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ekɛ sũ mli helai baa. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars keep eating the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target the soft, growing leaves inside the funnel of young maize plants. Inspecting your field early every morning allows you to catch these caterpillars before they destroy the main growing tip.
ga: Fall worms lɛ kwɛɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii titri ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close to other crops, it puts energy into growing leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Proper plant spacing ensures food is stored in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. He ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa niyenii toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor insect pollination cause tomato plants to drop flowers as a survival response. Mulching around the stem and keeping the soil evenly moist helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ nɔ ni haa amɛhiɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo tsei lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if buried too deep, planted in dry soil, or eaten underground by insects. Planting seeds at a depth equal to two or three times their size gives the highest chance of sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛdalɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ baaha amɛná hegbɛ ni fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves wilt and droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves wilt in afternoon heat because the plant loses water through its leaves faster than roots can absorb it. Applying dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and retains moisture.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ baagboi yɛ shwane mli ejaakɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Mulch ni egbi ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops look pale and grow very slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, soil water, and nutrients directly from young crop roots. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks after planting gives your crops full access to food so they grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hia, sũ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Koni tsei lɛ adara waa

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of small flowers, but only a few turn into pods. Flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi bibii akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Where on the cocoa tree do flowers and pods normally grow?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso nɔ daa?

english: Cocoa flowers grow directly on the main trunk and thick old branches from special spots called flower cushions, rather than at the ends of young green twigs.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ tsei niji momo lɛ anɔ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo kɛjɛɔ hei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ fɔfɔii akutsei lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, e wa ngɛ tso nine ɔmɛ a nya.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees have plenty of flowers but produce very little cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi kookoo fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when tiny pollinating insects like midges are absent, or when the tree does not have enough water or nutrients to support the heavy work of growing pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anitsumɔ ni wa lɛ.

english: How do tiny insects help my cocoa flowers turn into healthy cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from flower to flower while feeding. Without these tiny midges fertilizing the flowers, the blooms dry up and fail to form pods.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi amli muji kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ be mli ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii. Kɛji gbɔmɛi bibii nɛɛ bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Can leaving too much shade on my farm prevent my cocoa trees from flowering well?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi hulutsoo babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha mi-cacao tsei lɛ akafɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, while young cocoa needs heavy shade, mature cocoa trees need balanced sunlight to produce enough energy for healthy flowering and good pod production.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa moŋ. Shi cacao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni sa koni enyɛ ená hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa.

english: What happens if I accidentally cut too deep into the trunk bark of my cocoa tree with a knife?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ oshara tsɔ cacao tso ko shishi tsɔ?

english: Cutting deeply damages the inner bark and flower cushions where nutrients flow and pods grow. Deep wounds also open the tree to fungal diseases and insect attacks that can ruin the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ afo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaafite mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akushin lɛ. Biɛ ji he ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nii hoɔ yɛ ni pods lɛ daa yɛ. Pilamɔi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu haa tso lɛ náa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ afite tso lɛ.

english: How does careful pruning help my cocoa trees produce more flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mifo tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or weak branches, allowing light and air to enter the canopy. This encourages the tree to direct its energy toward forming new flowers and pods on the trunk.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: What is the proper way to remove unwanted shoots from my cocoa tree without damaging the main bark?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ cacao tso ko mli ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ ni afiteee ŋmeii titri lɛ?

english: Cut unwanted shoots cleanly near their base using a sharp tool without gouging or stripping the main bark, keeping the flower cushions on the trunk safe.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ ahe yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade ni mli wa nɔ ni ofolɔɔɔ loo ogbalaaa ŋmeii titri lɛ ahe. Koni fɔfɔi akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why must I avoid scraping the bark when harvesting mature cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ?

english: Scraping the bark destroys the flower cushions located on the trunk. If a flower cushion is damaged, that specific spot will stop producing flowers or pods in future seasons.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji fɔfɔii akushin lɛ fite Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ ekpaa fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii feemɔ yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Does trimming extra branches help my cocoa tree grow stronger stems?
ga: Ani tsei krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ená tso lɛ shishi ni wa?

english: Yes, trimming unnecessary side shoots helps the main stem grow thick and sturdy, ensuring the tree can support the weight of heavy pods once flowering begins.
ga: Hɛɛ, afã tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli tso lɛ mli tseɔ ni ewaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why is it risky if I keep taking seeds directly from my harvested crops to plant for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oshara ko yɔɔ kɛji mijie dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Reusing seeds from previous harvests often leads to lower yields over time because seeds naturally lose their vigor, and you might accidentally pass hidden diseases from the old harvest into your new soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akpa tsutsu lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ. Ni ekolɛ okɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ baaya shikpɔŋ hee nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to buy cheap seeds from local market traders or spend extra money on certified seeds from authorized dealers?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni jara waaa kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ? Aloo ofite shika babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ?

english: Certified seeds cost more upfront, but they are specially tested to germinate quickly, resist common plant diseases, and produce higher yields, making them cheaper in the long run compared to untested market seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ nyɔmɔwoo ni nɔ kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Shi aka lɛ akwɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Enɛ haa amɛjara waaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akako amɛ akwɛ ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers recommend treating my seeds before putting them into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ atsa midumɔwui lɛ dani adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Treating seeds acts like a protective shield that kills insects and fungal spores living in the dirt, preventing your seeds from rotting underground before they even have a chance to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ po ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a disease or if they just need more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emɔ hela loo nu babaoo he miihia amɛ?

english: A thirsty crop will generally wilt during the heat of the day and recover in the evening, whereas a diseased plant shows specific signs like dark spots, yellow rings, or leaf curling that stay even when the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii komɛi tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ akpo. aloo baai ni shwieɔ shi ni yaa nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Apart from causing physical damage to leaves, what actual harm do crop diseases do to my farm?
ga: Kɛfata gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ ni ekɛbaa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ he lɛ, Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai miifite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases stop the crop from properly digesting food and taking up nutrients, which stunts the plant's growth, prevents fruits or grains from swelling, and drastically reduces the total weight of your harvest.
ga: Helai tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ada Etsiɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkafu. ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ baa shi waa.

english: Can insects moving through my farm actually bring diseases to my healthy crops?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni nyiɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ hela aba miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, insects like aphids and whiteflies feed on diseased plants and carry plant viruses on their mouthparts, spreading infections to healthy crops across your field as they fly around.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids kɛ whiteflies yeɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛdaaŋ woɔ tsei amli helai. Gbalamɔ hela lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ beni amɛfoɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Does giving my crops too much water hurt them just as much as a dry spell?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui tamɔ bɔ ni nu ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ loo daabi?

english: Excess water drowns plant roots by cutting off oxygen in the soil, which causes the roots to rot and creates a damp environment where dangerous fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing on older, lower leaves usually means your soil is lacking nitrogen; the plant is forced to steal nitrogen from its older leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Anyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛju nitrogen kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli bɔni afee ni baai bibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I keep planting the same crop on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests and diseases targeting that plant to build up in the ground season after season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tsei amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small fruit when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, air, and soil food, causing them to stretch tall for light rather than producing full, healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I save seeds from my own maize harvest this year, will they yield the same good crop when I plant them next season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpa afi nɛɛ to Ani dumɔwui lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ nakai nɔŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Not always. Hybrid seeds lose their vigor after the first generation, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants if replanted. It is usually best to buy fresh certified seeds each season or use open-pollinated varieties (OPVs) if you plan to save seeds.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Aloo okɛ open pollinated (OPV) henɔi lɛ atsu nii kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaahere dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow at the bottom during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same field, or will they fight each other for nutrients?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaatswa amɛhe akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he?

english: Yes, you can plant them together. Maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first. By the time cassava needs more space and light, the maize is already harvested, allowing you to maximize your land use.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, ebaakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli. No mli lɛ, he ko kɛ la babaoo he hiaa yucca lɛ. Agbɛnɛ abaakpa ŋmãa lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop mostly due to heat stress, dry soil, or lack of pollination. When temperatures get too high or water is irregular, the plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni bɛ lɛ baa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How can I test if the seeds I stored are still good before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ hi lolo dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test. Wrap 10 seeds in a damp cloth or tissue paper and keep them in a warm place for 5 to 7 days. If 8 or more sprout, your seeds are strong and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee kwɛ̃mɔ he kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo: Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ loo tissue wolo abɔ dumɔwui 10 he. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto he ko ni mli edɔ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of maize. Checking your field weekly and applying recommended organic or chemical treatments directly into the plant funnel early will protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa otsi ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ awoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture for planting seeds at the start of the rains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil from your farm into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping water and crumbles easily when gently pressed, the soil has ideal moisture for planting.
ga: Nyɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ko ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, humid conditions. You can prevent it by pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and air, and removing affected pods immediately so it does not spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba mli lɛ nɔ. Ni jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant too early before the major rainy season fully settles?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ mra tsɔ, dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ ba naagbee?

english: Planting too early during irregular rains can cause your seeds to dry out in the soil and fail to germinate, or young seedlings to wither. Waiting until the rains are steady ensures consistent moisture for roots to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ odu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha odumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkakwɛ̃. loo dumɔwui bibii ni gboiɔ Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Should I place fertilizer right against the stem of my plant so it feeds faster?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛye nii oya?

english: No, putting fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant. Place it in a small ring or hole a few inches away from the stem so the spreading roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ. Okɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli. loo buji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ he koni shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Spacing seeds properly ensures each root system gets enough nutrients and light to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no plantains or shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and need shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Plantains grow fast and provide living umbrellas that keep the ground moist and cool until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest yield less food than the packaged hybrid seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for strength and high yields, but those special qualities are strongest in the first generation. When you save and replant seeds from a hybrid harvest, the resulting plants lose that energy and produce smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Shi nakai nibii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli wa fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ mli. Beni okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid kpamɔ mli lɛ toɔ ni okɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Tsei ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color so the plant can produce food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away off the surface of the land before the roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp so the nutrients dissolve directly into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ koni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does leaving dry plant leaves and weed clearings on top of my soil help my crops during dry heat?
ga: Te baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with plant waste, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from drying out the soil, keeps the ground cool, and slowly decays into food for the crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants and chewing holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that lays eggs on maize shoots. The caterpillars eat the young leaves from the inside out, and catching them early with recommended control measures prevents complete loss of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. kɛ emɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ tsei ni baafite kwraa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground when the soil stays very wet after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground stays soaked for too long, oxygen cannot reach the tubers, allowing waterborne rot and fungi to destroy the roots before harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Ha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ afite shishifãi lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before they ever turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can naturally feed. If the tree experiences prolonged heat, lack of water, or insect damage, it drops extra flowers to save its water and strength to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ, Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and light directly from your crops. Even with good rain, crops surrounded by weeds are starved of nutrients and will grow slowly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ fiofio.

english: Can onions actually grow well here in Ghana, or do they only thrive in drier countries like Burkina Faso?
ga: Ani sabolai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Ghana biɛ, aloo maji ni mli egbi tamɔ Burkina Faso pɛ amli ebaanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Onions can grow very well in Ghana. While drier neighboring countries produce a lot of onions, areas in Ghana like Agogo have fertile soil and good weather conditions that allow farmers to produce high yields locally.
ga: Sabolai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana. Eyɛ mli akɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni mli egbi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo moŋ, shi hei ni yɔɔ Ghana tamɔ Agogo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni hi ni haa okwaafoi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ amɛmaŋ lɛ.

english: Why are so many young farmers in places like Agogo entering onion farming instead of growing traditional crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi oblahii kɛ oblayei babaoo ni yɔɔ hei tamɔ Agogo lɛ miibɔi sabala okwaayeli yɛ blema ŋmɔshi nibii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Onions have a fast growth cycle of about three to four months and enjoy high market demand across Ghana all year round, allowing farmers to earn income faster than with long-term tree crops.
ga: Onions lɛ daa oya aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni jarayeli nibii babaoo taoɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa shika oya fe tsei ni amɛduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I know when my onions are mature and ready to be pulled out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-onions lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Onions tell you they are ready when their green tops turn yellow, weaken at the neck, and fall over onto the ground. This signals that the bulb underground has stopped growing and is ready for harvest.
ga: Onion ko kɛɔ bo akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni etsitsi lɛ fee blɛoo, ni egbee shikpɔŋ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do some onion bulbs stay very small while others grow large and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi daraaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni yitsei komɛi dara ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Bulb size depends on plant spacing, sunlight, and proper timing. If seedlings are planted too close together, they fight for nutrients and space, resulting in small bulbs.
ga: Yitso lɛ dalɛ damɔ bɔ ni tsei lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha, hulu la kɛ be ni sa nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: What type of soil is best for growing onions so the bulbs do not rot underground?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Onions prefer loose, well-drained sandy loam soil. Heavy clay soil holds too much water, which causes the bulbs to rot underground and makes it difficult for them to expand.
ga: Sabolai sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ehaa ewaa akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Is it better to plant onion seeds directly in the main field or start them in a nursery bed first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu sabolai dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to start onion seeds in a nursery bed and transplant healthy seedlings to the main field. Onion seeds are very small, so nursing them protects young plants from being washed away by rain.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobɔi onion dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli. Onion dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akwɛ sabala dumɔwui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ lɛ akashwie amɛ.

english: How much water do onion crops need while they are forming bulbs in the ground?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa onion tsei beni amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Onions need light, regular watering while growing, but you must stop watering completely about two weeks before harvest so the outer bulb skins can dry out and form a protective layer.
ga: Sabala biɔ ni afɔ lɛ nu daa kɛ daa be mli ni edaa lɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni okpa nu lɛ shwiemɔ kwraa aaafee otsi enyɔ dani okpa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ he lɛ feɔ.

english: What type of fertilizer should I use to get big onion bulbs instead of just lots of green leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii koni maná ŋmeii wuji yɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo najiaŋ?

english: Early on, onions need nitrogen to grow green leaves, but as the bulb forms, they need fertilizer rich in phosphorus and potassium. Too much nitrogen late in the season produces bushy leaves but small, soft bulbs.
ga: Mra mli lɛ, nitrogen he miihia sabolai koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli. Shi beni onion lɛ Amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji shi bulbs lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛfee blɛoo.

english: How can I store my harvested onions so they do not go soft or rot quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ ato koni amɛkafee blɛoo loo amɛkafite oya?

english: After pulling up onions, you must 'cure' them by spreading them out in a shaded, well-ventilated area for one to two weeks until the skin becomes papery and the neck dries completely, which prevents rot.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ‘otsa’ ŋmei lɛ kɛtsɔ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni ooogbɛ eshwa otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ kɛyashi hewolo lɛ baatsɔ wolo ni ŋmei lɛ baagbi kwraa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite.

english: Why are the leaves of my onion plants turning silvery and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion baai lɛ miitsɔ shika ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by tiny insects called thrips that feed on the leaf juice. Spraying early with neem oil or recommended insecticides keeps the leaves healthy so they can nourish the growing bulb.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii kɛ enɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ thrips ni yeɔ baa nu. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni enyɛ eha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How long does it take for fertilizer to start working on my maize crops after I put it in the soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ nitsumɔ shishi yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: It usually takes a few days to a week to see changes. For fertilizer to work, the soil must be moist so the nutrients can dissolve and be absorbed by the roots. You will notice greener and stronger leaves a few days after applying it with enough water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii fioo kɛyashi otsi kome dani onaa tsakemɔi. koni ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli ni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Obaana baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni okɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa tsu nii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to spray pesticide on my crops early in the morning instead of in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Insects are active in the cool morning before hiding from the heat, so spraying early hits them directly. Also, the strong afternoon sun can make the chemical evaporate too quickly or scorch the wet leaves.
ga: Kplukai tsuɔ nii waa yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli dani amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaatutua amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo ashã baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my dry fertilizer right before a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa lɛ baa?

english: A heavy downpour will wash the fertilizer away off the surface of your farm before it sinks into the ground. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp or when light rain is expected so the roots can take it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe dani eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ fioo. koni shishifãi lɛ abote mli

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: Plants lose water very fast through their leaves in intense heat to stay cool. Even if the soil has water, the roots cannot suck it up fast enough during peak heat, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself until evening.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu moŋ Shi shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ oya bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ gbiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ehe kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: If my crops are suffering from a long drought, will giving them water once make them fully recover immediately?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ na hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ani nu kome ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Recovery takes a little time. While water helps instantly stop further drying, the plant needs a few days to repair its internal cells and restress before it can start growing new shoots and leaves again.
ga: Hewalɛwoo heɔ be fioo. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu baaye abua ni akpa ŋmɔlɔ kroko amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná gbii fioo komɛi koni amɛsaa amɛmli wala yibii lɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe dani amɛje ŋmeii kɛ baai heei akwɛmɔ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow when there is too much heavy rain for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much rainfall drowns the plant roots by filling all the tiny air pockets in the soil with water. Without air, roots cannot breathe or absorb food, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa tsei ashishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ nu ni ekɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge green leaves but produce very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. The plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build thick, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ amɛbaai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee kasava sisi nɛ mi wa nɛ e he wa.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to sprout out of the dirt after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep in the dirt, they run out of energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching sunlight. Planting seeds at a shallow depth lets them sprout quickly into the air.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, which is a fungus that grows fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning extra branches lets air and sunlight into the farm to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does my soil produce less food if I plant maize in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until the ground becomes weak. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts goodness back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ kpakpafeemɔ kuɔ sɛɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same land where I want to grow young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni madu kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and dry out easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that create protective shade and keep the soil moist for the young cocoa plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛhaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Can direct heat and sunlight damage my cocoa plants if I don't give them shade?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ afite mi-kokoo tso lɛ kɛji mikɛ hulutsoo be haaa lɛ?

english: Yes, high heat and direct sunshine can burn young cocoa leaves and dry up the soil, which stunts the tree's growth or causes the seedling to die early.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai bibii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekada loo ebaaha dumɔwu lɛ agbo oya.

english: Can I harvest and sell plantains while I am still waiting for my cocoa trees to grow and produce?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa plantains ni mahɔ̃ɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ lolo ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains mature much faster than cocoa, giving you food and income to support yourself during the years it takes for the cocoa trees to start producing pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains daa oya kwraa fe kookoo. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika ni okɛkwɛɔ ohe yɛ afii ni cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: How does the weather and air temperature affect when I should start planting my crops?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa lɛ saa be ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need a balanced mix of warm air and moisture in the soil to sprout roots. Planting when the air is too dry or hot causes seedlings to suffer from heat stress.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni akɛfutuɔ tsei lɛ he miihia koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: Why do my crops fail to grow well if I plant them at the wrong time of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli lɛ?

english: Each crop has specific weather conditions it prefers. If you plant out of season when rainfall is low or heat is excessive, the crops struggle to establish strong root systems.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he hiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ be ni sa mli beni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ loo latsaa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: What happens to cocoa plants if the heat becomes too intense during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tsei anɔ kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Excessive heat causes cocoa plants to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, leading to leaf wilting, reduced growth, or complete drying up of the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa cacao tso lɛ mli nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. eha tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi loo eha tso lɛ agbi kwraa

english: Why are many extension officers encouraging farmers to grow cassava these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi babaoo miiwo okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu ŋmei yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava has high market demand because it can be eaten fresh or processed into products like gari and flour, making it a reliable source of income.
ga: Cassava he miihia waa yɛ jara nɔ ejaakɛ abaanyɛ aye lɛ ŋmɔŋ loo afee lɛ nibii tamɔ gari kɛ ashikishaŋ, ni no haa efeɔ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Does cassava require as much shade and rainfall as cocoa and plantain to survive?
ga: Ani hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ he miihia ŋmei tamɔ bɔ ni kookoo kɛ plantain he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi?

english: No, cassava is a much tougher crop that tolerates direct sunlight, higher heat, and lower rainfall better than cocoa or plantain.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ji tso ko ni kpɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ hi fe kookoo loo plantain.

english: Is cassava a good crop to grow on land where other demanding crops struggle?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ji ŋmãa kpakpa ni esa akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa krokomɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava can grow in poorer soils and warmer environments where crops like cocoa might fail, making it a safe option for different soil types.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. He ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha shikpɔŋ srɔtoi.

english: How do I know if my farm land has the right conditions before I start planting plantain suckers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Plantains thrive best when the soil is deep, fertile, and moist, and when planting is done at the beginning of the rainy season so the suckers can take root quickly.
ga: Plantains daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli mra bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi oya.

english: Why should I spend extra money to buy certified seeds from the market instead of just using seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kroko koni mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jara nɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ i je mi nitsɛ ye ngmlɛfia a mi pɛ tsu ní.

english: Certified seeds are officially tested to ensure they are clean, free of diseases, and guaranteed to give high germination rates. Starting with clean, certified seed gives your crops the strongest start and ensures maximum yield compared to seeds saved from your farm.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ koni ana akɛ amɛhe tse, helai bɛ amɛhe, ni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni awo he odase lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná yitso ni mli wa fe fɛɛ. ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he nɔmimaa.

english: How can I be sure that the seeds I buy at the store are clean and high quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ahe tse ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ?

english: True certified seeds come in sealed bags bearing an official government tag or seal. This shows the seeds have been professionally inspected, cleaned, and treated to protect them from early diseases and pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni akɛ naatsii ewo mli ni maŋ nɔyeli lɛ okadi loo naatsii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, akwɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ, atsumɔ amɛhe, ni atsa amɛ koni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akaje shishi yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvest this year to plant again during the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can plant them, but your yield will likely drop. Seeds harvested from crops—especially modern or foreign varieties—lose their strength after the first year, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests in following seasons.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔ. Shi nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba shi. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Titri lɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ loo maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi. Ehewalɛ baaje edɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei amli lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I keep replanting seeds saved from my previous crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: When you continuously replant saved seeds, the crop gradually loses its special genetic strength. By the second or third year of replanting, the plants become less vigorous and yield much less grain than the original seed.
ga: Beni oduɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, fiofio lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ he waaa ni ebaawo dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee nɔ lɛ.

english: How many times can I harvest and replant seeds from a single bag of certified seed?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ni madu dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kotoku kome mli?

english: It is best to buy fresh certified seed every single season. While saved seeds will still grow in the second or third year, the quality and amount of harvest will decline sharply after the first year.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baaya nɔ ada yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ mli moŋ. Shi ŋmaa lɛ mlihilɛ kɛ bɔ ni efa ha lɛ baa shi oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If my saved seeds still grow tall and green in the field, why am I getting smaller cobs and fruits?
ga: Kɛji mi dumɔwui ni mihere lɛ lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ aduawai anɔ?

english: A plant growing tall leaves does not guarantee a good harvest. Replanted seeds often retain the ability to grow vegetative parts like leaves and stems, but lose the power to produce heavy grains or large fruits.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ baai kakadaji lɛ haaa ana nɔmimaa akɛ abaakpa nii jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ hiɛɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ tsei ahe nibii tamɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli, shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui ni tsii loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do extension officers discourage farmers from continuous planting of saved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui be fɛɛ be koni amɛkadu dumɔwui ni ato lɛ?

english: Continuous planting weakens the crop line over time, making plants more vulnerable to local weather changes, pests, and diseases, which ultimately reduces the farmer's yield and profits.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa tsei srɔtoi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Enɛ baaha okwaafoi lɛ anitsumɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni amɛnáa lɛ aba shi yɛ naagbee.

english: What is the difference between foreign hybrid seeds and our local traditional seeds when saving them for replanting?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli shishijee dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ akɛto koni akɛdu ekoŋŋ?

english: Foreign hybrid seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants in controlled conditions for one-time performance. Local seeds stay relatively stable, but replanted hybrid seeds break down genetically, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Akɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome aba lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akɛhaa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ baafite yɛ fɔmɔ su mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why do foreign seed varieties perform so well in the first year but fail after two or three seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi amɛtsuuu nii yɛ bei enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Foreign varieties are specially cross-bred for maximum yield in their first generation. When you save and plant seeds from that harvest, the original breeding balance is broken, causing performance to drop in subsequent years.
ga: Akɛ maŋsɛɛ tsofai srɔtoi lɛ tsɔɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni anyɛ ana yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Beni okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni oduɔ lɛ Shishijee fɔmɔ he shika ni ato lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do crops grown from my saved seeds get sick more easily than crops grown from new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔɔ amɛ oya fe tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from old harvests can carry hidden plant diseases and pest eggs from the previous season into your new field. Fresh certified seeds are disease-free and often treated to withstand common crop illnesses.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ awo oshikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ bɛ hela, ni bei pii lɛ, atsaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my crops in neat rows instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, evenly spaced rows gives each crop enough room to absorb sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How does leaving the right amount of space between my crops keep them healthy?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Proper spacing allows air to flow freely between plants, which keeps the leaves dry and prevents fungal diseases from spreading easily across your field.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why should I try planting new improved seed varieties instead of using the seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time and produce smaller yields. New improved seed varieties are bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and yield more food on the same size of land.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ewoɔ babaoo yɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How do early-maturing crop varieties help my farm when the rains stop early?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra lɛ?

english: Early-maturing varieties grow faster and produce their harvest in a shorter timeframe, allowing them to complete their life cycle before the rains dry up.
ga: Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ egbeɔ ewala shihilɛ naa dani nugbɔ lɛ gbiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color so they can make food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni anyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water during high heat by reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the sun and dry air.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbuɔ nu he yɛ dɔlɛ bei amli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers staying small even though the leaves on top look big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ baai moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leafy tops instead of expanding its underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ potassium lɛ, tsei lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my field yield less food every year when I plant maize in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that target that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating crops restores soil balance and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans alongside my grain crops help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for neighboring plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during prolonged dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dry conditions weaken plants from water stress, lowering their natural defenses against pests, while warm weather speeds up the breeding cycle of many harmful insects.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nu he haomɔ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi bibii babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ amɛhe oya.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests now even though I use the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa afi moŋ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same land every season drains the soil of its natural food, making the ground tired. Without resting the land or adding nutrients, plant growth and yields naturally decrease over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be. Bei lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ lɛ fiteɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Tsei adalɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans trap nutrients from the air and put them back into the soil. This naturally refreshes the dirt so your next crop, like maize, has rich soil to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni eyeɔ.

english: How does putting dried leaves or straw around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni mikɛfataa mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dried plant leaves acts like a blanket. It keeps the sun from drying out the dirt, holds moisture near the roots, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ akagbi muji. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: If my farmland is small, can I just plant my maize seeds very close together to get more food?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in tall, weak plants that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stop growing when weeds grow near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are very aggressive and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. When weeds take over, your crops starve and turn yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa waa ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does growing cassava and maize together on one plot benefit my farm harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Growing two crops together makes full use of your land. Fast-growing maize is harvested early, leaving room for slow-growing cassava to expand later, giving you two different food harvests from the same plot.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Akpaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ mra. Shi gbɛ aha ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa sɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow long stems but very small roots when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛɔ shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to make energy and store food in its underground tubers. Heavy shade forces the plant to stretch upward for light instead of growing thick roots.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shade ni mli wa baaha tso lɛ ashɛ ehe koni ekɛ la lɛ awo mli moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt faster during a dry spell compared to my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛ akɛto mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have short roots that only drink from topsoil, which dries out quickly in the sun. Cassava plants have deeper roots that can reach water buried far beneath the surface.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ Cassava tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why do crop insects and sicknesses spread so fast when everyone in the village plants the same crop at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi kɛ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ miidu tso kome yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When a large area has only one type of crop, it creates an endless supply of food for specific bugs and diseases, allowing them to multiply quickly and move easily from farm to farm.
