ga: Kɛji akɛ he ko ni da yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii henɔ kome pɛ Ehaa niyenii ni bɛ naagbee baa kɛha kooloi kɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛfãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ kroko mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops suffer more from pests when the soil is poor and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii ni egbi lɛ?

english: Just like human beings get sick easily when hungry, plants growing in weak, dry soil become stressed and lack the strength to fight off insect attacks and diseases.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni adesai yeɔ hela oya kɛ́ hɔmɔ miiye amɛ lɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbi nɔ lɛ naa haomɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawu amɛshi kooloi bibii kɛ helai.

english: How can I tell if my crop flowers have been pollinated and are actually starting to grow into fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mifɔfɔi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ? Ni eje shishi eda ni etsɔ aduawai?

english: Before pollination, the flower remains fully open and fresh. Once successful pollination happens, the flower petals will naturally wither and drop off, and you will see the tiny base of the flower start to swell into a fruit or seed pod.
ga: dani pollination Fɔfɔi lɛ egbele kwraa lolo ni amɛhe efee ehee. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ ye omanye lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi. Ni obaana shishitoo bibioo ko. Fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfuɔ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui ŋmɔji.

english: Why do the flowers on my garden egg plants sometimes drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off if they were not pollinated by insects or wind, or if the plant is stressed by extreme heat or drought. Without pollen transferring from one part of the flower to another, the plant discards the flower instead of spending energy on fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ pollen ko bɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã kome mli kɛyaa fã kroko mli. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii shi yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛaafite yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What is the purpose of the soft silks coming out from the top of my maize ears?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ tsɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni jɛɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Each individual silk string is connected to a single potential kernel of maize. For a full cob to grow, pollen falling from the top tassels must land on each silk thread so the grain underneath can develop.
ga: Akɛ siliki kpãa fɛɛ kpãa tsa ŋmãa dumɔwu kome ni baanyɛ afee ŋmãa nɔ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ adara kwraa lɛ, esa akɛ Pollen ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ aba shi yɛ siliki ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Does spraying chemical pesticides when my crops are in full flower harm my harvest?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ baafite mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, spraying during flowering can kill bees and other friendly insects that pollinate your crops. If these pollinators are destroyed, many of your flowers will dry up without producing any seeds or fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ. ni baanyɛ aha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji akpata ŋmɔtɔ nibii nɛɛ ahiɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbi ni dumɔwui loo aduawai ko bɛ he.

english: Why do groundnut plants flower above the ground, but the actual nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After the yellow groundnut flower is pollinated in the open air, it wilts and sends out a small stem called a peg. This peg bends downward and pushes itself into the soil, where the nut safely grows away from heat and sun.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi ni ji yellow lɛ pollin yɛ kpo nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Ebaagbo ni ebaatsu ŋmeii bibii kɛje kpo. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ pin ni jeɔ kpo. Nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ baakoto shi ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ ni hulutsoo kɛ hulu la akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my shea tree yield plenty of nuts in one season but very few in the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shea tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Shea trees naturally follow a pattern where a heavy fruiting season drains the tree's energy, requiring the tree to rest and rebuild nutrients during the next season before it can flower heavily again.
ga: Shea tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ko sɛɛ he ni yibiiwoo be ni mli wa lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are some fruit bunches on my oil palm tree filled with tiny, hard nuts that have no oil in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni wa ni fɔ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there are not enough pollinating insects, like small weevils, in the farm during flowering. Without proper pollination, the palm fruit cannot develop its thick, oil-rich outer flesh.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ Palm yibii lɛ nyɛŋ afee kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni mu eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees produce flowers directly on their thick trunks instead of on the small leafy branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei niji bibii ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees flower on the main trunk so that tiny pollinating midges living in the damp ground leaf litter can easily reach the flowers, and so the heavy cocoa pods have strong support as they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ koni amɛha ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ baai amli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ fɔfɔi ahe oya. Ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsii hewɔ lɛ, amɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of green leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of transferring sugars down into the roots to make thick tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ sugars lɛ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni efee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why are the seeds in the middle of my sunflower heads completely empty even though the plant looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi hulutsoo yitso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ efee efolo lɛ? Ani nakai tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: The outer flowers on a sunflower open first and get pollinated easily by insects, but if rain or a lack of bees prevents the center flowers from getting pollinated when they open later, those middle seeds remain empty shells.
ga: Hulu fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gbeleɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ŋmeii shwieɔ amɛhe oya. Shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ loo ŋmeii faaa lɛ, etsĩɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii beni amɛfɔlɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwu ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baafee ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lolo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle strong direct heat; they need temporary shade trees or plantains to shield them from the sun and keep the soil moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm, or will it harm the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ? Aloo ebaaye kookoo tso lɛ awui?

english: Cassava roots spread heavily underground and consume massive amounts of nutrients and water, which can starve young cocoa trees and slow down their growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi waa ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and soft during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads quickly through splashing rain and high humidity when water sits on the pods for too long.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops roll up tightly during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward to reduce their exposure to dry air and hot winds, which helps the plant trap internal moisture and prevent water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ akabote mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree if those branches could potentially grow more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi kɛji akɛ nakai niji lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes weak and overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can freely flow through the tree, which prevents diseases and directs the tree's energy into making fewer but larger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii fioo, shi amɛdaraa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more blossoms than they can support, dropping up to 95 percent of them so the tree saves enough energy and water to nourish the few pods that do set.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua, ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ oha mlijaa 95, no hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ toɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaahã fɔfɔii fioo ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and root space away from your crops before your main plants get a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani tso titri lɛ náa hegbɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer just by looking at their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When cocoa trees lack key soil nutrients, their leaves often turn pale yellow, grow smaller than usual, or show brown burnt-like edges instead of a rich, healthy green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. bibioo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ loo ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshã yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick a cocoa pod so the beans inside aren't spoiled?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Enɛ ji koni kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its outer husk changes completely from green or deep red to a solid, bright yellow or orange color, showing that the beans inside are mature.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo yibii lɛ egbɔ kwraa.

english: Why must I pile my fresh cocoa beans under banana leaves for several days instead of sun-drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii heei toɔ banana baai ashishi gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo hulu lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heap fermentation under banana leaves uses heat and natural yeasts to kill the seed germ inside the bean and create the rich chocolate flavor and brown color before drying.
ga: Mound fermentation ni yɔɔ banana baa shishi lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa dani egbiɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantains near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight and will dry out or burn. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas to protect young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ebaanyɛ egbi loo eshã. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni hiɛ ka koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Yellowing maize leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛyeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔji lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave plant remains to rot on my field instead of burning them after land clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic food and good insects in the soil. Letting plant remains rot on top of the field adds nutrients back to the soil and keeps it moist during hot weather.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ kooloi kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi tsei lɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the middle leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks young maize leaves. Finding them early and applying recommended insecticides or neem extracts can protect your crop from damage.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii. Ni ooona amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when temperatures are too high, when there is not enough water in the soil, or when small insects attack the blooms. Regular watering during hot periods helps flowers stick and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, nu ni oooha amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I planted maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooodu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmã yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes nutrients out of the soil, while legumes like beans and cowpeas naturally put nitrogen back into the soil. Rotating them keeps your soil healthy without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ otsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and soft soil to expand easily. Hard or stony soil squeezes the growing tuber, causing it to become twisted and small.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ bulbs ni miida lɛ anaa. Ha efee nɔ ni efite ni efee bibioo.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the inside lining of the shell turns dark brown or black when you crack open a pod.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni pod lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛ́ ogbele pod lɛ.

english: Maize powder is caused by tiny insects called weevils that bore into dried grains. Drying your maize properly until it is very hard and using safe grain storage dust or airtight bags prevents weevil damage.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ ŋmãa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni egbi. Abɛi ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa waa. Ni kɛ akɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo vacuum bag tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas planted nearby to protect them from heat and hold soil moisture while they grow strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with small caterpillars hiding inside the central leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo baa lɛ shishi yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize leaves and stems. Catching them early and applying approved organic or chemical treatments directly into the leaf funnels will protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ abele bibii ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, suffocating the underground tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rainwater drain away faster and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb upward so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber. Staking also keeps the foliage off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and resulting in larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi fungal helai ni haa yams wuji baa lɛ naa

english: Why is it bad for me to leave tall weeds growing around my young pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ ehiii kɛha mi.

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your pepper plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your peppers get all the strength they need to grow large and produce plenty of fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-peppers lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Hybrid seeds lose their special yield strength and disease resistance after the first harvest. Replanting saved hybrid seeds usually leads to small, weak cobs and a much lower crop yield compared to buying certified fresh hybrid seeds.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ yibiiwoo hewalɛ kroko kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ adumɔ haa ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kwraa baa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-rotted animal manure will restore their dark green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland help improve the soil?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decompose, they leave this free fertilizer in the soil for future crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛshiɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulching and watering helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get destroyed by tiny insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kpata mi-abele ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ahiɛ beni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These tiny insects are maize weevils, which bore into dried grains to lay eggs and eat the inside. Thoroughly drying your maize until it is hard and storing it in airtight hermetic bags protects your harvest from insect damage without chemical sprays.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmei ŋmeii. Amɛfoɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛwo wɔji ni amɛyeɔ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu onibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This feeds the maize and keeps the soil fertile without forcing you to buy extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni eye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa ni enyɛŋ onɔ ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Heavy rain often washes this key nutrient out of the topsoil, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and twisted instead of growing straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they run into hard or rocky soil underground. Making soft, loose soil mounds or high ridges gives the tubers room to expand smoothly without obstacles.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛjo foi kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni etse ehe loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha yitso he lɛ mli alɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight in and drying out the field helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la abote mli ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the fresh leaves inside the central tops of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of maize leaves to feed on new growth. Applying targeted treatments or neem extract into the center funnel early destroys them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa heei ni eda lɛ. Tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ kpataaa amɛhiɛ mra. dani efite ŋmɔ lɛ

english: Wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or recommended insecticides keeps these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ohe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. Mulching the base of plants with dried grass keeps the soil cool and moist so flowers can form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water fills the air spaces in the soil, suffocating cassava roots and letting rot fungi grow. Planting on high mounds allows excess water to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and droop in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water faster through heat than roots can take up from the soil. The plant droops to protect itself from drying out, usually recovering as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe koni ekagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in dry soil before the rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to wake up and start growing. If you plant in completely dry soil without rain, the seeds either dry out and die before sprouting, or stay hidden in the ground where insects and birds eat them.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃. loo akɛtee shikpɔŋ ni kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi yeɔ amɛ yɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant doesn't get enough water, it enters survival mode to protect itself. Dropping flowers prevents the plant from wasting precious water and energy on growing fruit it cannot support.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ebaaya wala shihilɛ mli koni ebu ehe he. Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite nu ni jara wa kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ aduawai ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry period. If young seeds germinate during that brief wet spell, their fresh roots will scorch and die as soon as the dry days return.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, amɛshishifãi heei lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi kɛji gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba pɛ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I move them into the field on a bright sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Moving young plants damages their delicate feeder roots, making it hard for them to soak up water. Strong heat causes the leaves to lose moisture faster than damaged roots can replace it, making the plants wilt quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baafite shishifãi ni haa niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni efite lɛ baanyɛ atsake lɛ. Ehaa tsei gboɔ oya

english: Why do crops like cassava handle dry weather better than vegetables like tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi he nii jogbaŋŋ fe aduawai tamɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that dig into the earth for hidden moisture, along with tough leaves. Vegetables have shallow roots and tender leaves, so they run out of water very quickly when it stops raining.
ga: Yucca yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ afata baai ni wa lɛ ahe. Aduawai lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ baaho oya waa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella against the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating into the air, keeping moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day to water my crops when using bucket or dam irrigation?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ mikɛ tanki loo dam nu miitsu nii?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Watering during hot afternoons causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can take it in.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Can I put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry and there is no rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nugbɔ enɛko lɛ?

english: No, fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can scorch and burn root tips, doing more harm to the plant than good.
ga: Dabi, nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã ni ekɛ shãa aba. Enɛ yeɔ tso lɛ awui fe nɔ ni hi.

english: Why does my land become hard like concrete after a long period without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil contains clay and small particles that shrink and pack tightly together when dry. Without water or organic matter to create air spaces, hot sun bakes the soil into a hard crust.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ kɛ nibii bibii ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ekome beni egbiɔ lɛ. Kɛji nu loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui afee lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa.

english: Why do tomatoes get more leaf diseases during heavy rain seasons compared to controlled watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi náa baa helai babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nu ni akudɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves dislike constantly wet conditions. Heavy rain splashes soil-borne fungi onto the leaves and creates damp air, which helps fungal diseases spread rapidly on the plant.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ sumɔɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ baai anɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei anɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for the next crop season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, this nitrogen stays in the ground and feeds the next crops you plant, such as maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, overly shady, and wet conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches to let sunlight in and clearing weeds helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, shade, ni efɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli, ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant juice, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling these pests early helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize leaves right inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutua mi ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide inside the central leaves (funnel) of young maize plants where it is moist and safe from predators. Checking the funnels early allows you to crush them or apply appropriate treatments before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli mra Ehaa okɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ shwieɔ shi loo okɛ tsofa ni sa tsuɔ nii dani okpãtãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when temperatures are extremely high or when the plant does not get enough water consistently. Excess nitrogen fertilizer can also cause the plant to grow leaves instead of holding onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akwɛ baai moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because too much water cuts off oxygen to the roots and encourages soil fungus. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu babaoo ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam tubers grow twisted when the soil is too hard, compact, or filled with stones. Making soft, deep mounds of loose topsoil gives the tubers space to expand easily without hitting hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni etswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: Planting maize on the same land every year drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans or cassava keeps the soil healthy and reduces pest problems.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be Daa afi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ abele mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai baa shi.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to sow my seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sowing seeds right after the very first rain can kill them if a long dry spell follows. It is best to wait until the rain has wet the soil deep enough—about the length of your hand—so young roots can survive even if it doesn't rain for a few days.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui lɛ kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ—aaafee onine lɛ kɛlɛ—koni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi po.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overwatering. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by heat stress. Protecting seedlings with insect netting or using neem oil spray helps reduce insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa he haomɔ mli Kɛ akɛ kooloi ŋmeii abuɔ dumɔwui ahe loo akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava plants shed leaves during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from heat. The plant is still alive, and it will sprout new green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Ni ebaakwɛ baai heei eŋɔli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that lose moisture quickly under strong sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around young cocoa provides shade and maintains humidity until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha hulutsoo ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and produce big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Clearing them early prevents weeds from choking your young crops and reducing your yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi ni tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anaa lɛ anaa ni ebaaha yibiiwoo aba shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing fungal diseases and encouraging the growth of bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant whorl. Applying approved treatments or neem extracts early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaagbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture before I plant my pepper seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa dani madu ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a handful of moist soil into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping water and easily crumbles when touched, the moisture level is right for seeds to germinate.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ ata he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil and get insects when I store them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains high moisture that encourages mold growth and attracts storage insects. Thoroughly sun-drying the grains until they are hard before bagging keeps them safe for long storage.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni haa ŋmɔtɔ daa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ewa dani akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does strong wind keep knocking down my maize crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa mi-ŋma lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Strong winds push against top-heavy crops like maize. Without natural windbreaks or border trees around your field to slow the air down, strong gusts hit the stalks directly and snap them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei loo tsei ni ebɔle oyale lɛ he bɛ ni baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko baatswa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni ebaakumɔ.

english: How can I use trees to protect my farm from heavy winds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsei abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he?

english: Planting a line of tall trees or dense plants along the edge of your field creates a living windbreak. This barrier slows down harsh winds so they pass gently over your crops instead of destroying them.
ga: Tsei kakadaji loo tsei ni mli tse ni ooodu yɛ oyale lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ atswa. Nɛkɛ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ yaa oya bɔni afee ni amɛnyiɛ blɛoo yɛ onibii anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: Why is the wind destroying crops in only one section of my farm while the rest is safe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kpata miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã kome pɛ hiɛ yɛ be mli ni fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ?

english: Solid structures or uneven tree lines block wind unevenly, forcing strong gusts to funnel violently through open gaps. Creating long, continuous, and evenly spaced barriers keeps wind moving smoothly across your entire land.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ loo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛtsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa. Gbɛtsii nii ni kɛlɛ, ni yaa nɔ, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ ni ooofee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I leave small openings in a long row of boundary trees planted to block the wind?
ga: Esa akɛ gbɛ bibioo ko ahi mli. Ani eyɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ ni adu koni akɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, because a completely solid wall forces heavy wind to jump over and crash down hard on crops behind it. Allowing small, uniform spaces lets wind filter through gently without causing damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ gbogbo ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nyɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ koni efo kɛho ni etswa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛ lɛ waa. He bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli blɛoo ni ekɛ nɔ ko baaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees struggle to grow when planted near large open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko ni mli tse lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out and tear easily under direct, harsh winds. Planting shade trees or tall border crops around the field creates a calm environment that shields young cocoa plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbalaa oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ waa ni amɛtswa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ he ni ŋmɔji lɛ yɔɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ toiŋjɔlɛ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: How far down my field will a tall line of border trees protect my crops from wind?
ga: Te tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he kɛyashi tɛŋŋ?

english: A windbreak generally protects a field area equal to about ten times its height. For example, a tree line that is two meters tall will protect crops up to twenty meters behind it.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔne ko baabu ŋmɔ lɛ mli he ko ni kɛ aaafee elɛɛmɔ toi nyɔŋma yeɔ egbɔ lɛ he. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, tso ni kɛlɛ ji mitai 2 lɛ baabu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛyashi mitai 20 yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Does the length of my crop rows affect how well my plants survive strong winds?
ga: Ani bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ha lɛ saa bɔ ni mitsei lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa lɛ he?

english: Longer and continuous rows help distribute wind movement evenly across the farm. Short or patchy rows create open gaps where wind can rush in and knock down vulnerable crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi kakadaji ni yaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejaa kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi kukuji loo ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ Ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa kɛbote mli ni etswa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin and fall over when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they stretch upward quickly to fight for sunlight, making their stems weak. When strong winds blow, these thin stems cannot hold the weight of the plant and fall over.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa lɛ, nɛkɛ tsei akutsei bibii nɛɛ nyɛŋ atere tso lɛ muji lɛ ni amɛgbee shi.

english: What can I plant on my farm boundaries to stop dry winds from drying out my soil?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi akaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ agbi?

english: You can plant tall grasses like elephant grass or fast-growing boundary trees. They slow down dry winds, reducing water evaporation from both the soil and your crop leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu jwɛi kakadaji tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi loo fɛ̃i tsei ni daa oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ baa shi Ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants bend and snap during sudden rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava becomes top-heavy as its leaves grow thick. Without windbreak trees around your field to absorb sudden wind gusts, the heavy leafy stems snap easily near the base.
ga: Cassava bafeɔ nɔ ni tsii be mli ni ebaa lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ. Kɛji tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he ni baanyɛ ajie kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa trukaa lɛ. Tsoi ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse lɛ fãa oya yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave some big trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist during dry seasons, and drop leaves that turn into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni okɛ baai ni bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Will planting other trees near my crops steal all the water and nutrients from the soil?
ga: Ani tsei krokomɛi ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Deep-rooted shade trees pull nutrients up from deep underground and drop leaves that feed the topsoil, actually helping your crops access better nutrients without stealing their water.
ga: Shade tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛjieɔ baai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ niyenii. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛjuuu nu.

english: Why do heavy winds snap my cocoa branches, and how can trees on my farm boundary help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbá mikokoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall trees act as windbreaks that slow down strong storm winds, creating a calm barrier that shields fragile crops like cocoa from breaking or losing their flowers.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ahum ni naa wa waa lɛ naa. Bɔɔ gbogbo ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ, tamɔ kookoo, he kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔii ni akumɔɔ loo amɛlaajeɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green growth, or that heavy rain has washed the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up under strong direct sun, so they droop temporarily to protect themselves until the cooler evening.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, waterlogging, or a lack of essential soil nutrients.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, nu ni hoɔ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie dumɔwui wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep their leaves cool and preserve soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sun so they can catch more light to build big underground tubers, while also keeping the leaves dry and away from soil diseases.
ga: Staking Wo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni enine ashɛ la babaoo nɔ ni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sweet potato baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging everything up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack, and the plant is around 9 to 12 months old.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12.

english: Why should I place fertilizer right near the root of the crop instead of scattering it across the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone ensures your crop gets direct access to the nutrients before weeds can steal them or heavy rain washes them away.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani jwɛi lɛ aju amɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahoɔ amɛ.

english: Why didn't all the maize seeds I buried in the ground sprout out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ ekwɛko lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are old or damaged by insects, if they were buried too deep in the soil, or if the soil was too dry or flooded with water.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛŋ kɛji amɛgbɔ loo kooloi bibii efite amɛ. Kɛji akɛ afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu afua eba.

english: Why are there small holes in my cabbage leaves and tiny green caterpillars under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: The green caterpillars are pests that hatched from eggs laid by moths; they eat the leaves to grow, which prevents the cabbage from forming a firm, healthy head.
ga: Green caterpillars ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai koni amɛdara. Enɛ haaa cabbage lɛ yitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adara.

english: Why does wild grass grow so much faster than my pepper crop after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds and wild grasses have deep, tough roots that allow them to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops, allowing them to overpower your crops if not cleared early.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ onibii anɔ kunim kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Just like a person needs regular grooming to stay healthy and clean, trimming cocoa trees removes dead or unwanted branches. This lets sunlight and fresh air reach the whole tree, preventing moisture buildup that causes fungal diseases.
ga: Taakɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ wɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ wɔ nɔ daa koni wɔná hewalɛ ni wɔhe atse lɛ. Afoɔ kookoo tso lɛ koni akɛjie niji ni egboi loo ni ataooo lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds away from around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kooloo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition for soil nutrients and water, while also eliminating hiding places for insect pests that can attack your cocoa pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atutua o-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need extra nutrients or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Just as a person shows signs of tiredness when undernourished, cocoa trees signal they need feeding through yellowing leaves, slow growth, or a sudden fall in the number of pods they produce.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi jieɔ tɔlɛ he okadii kpo kɛ́ amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Cacao tsei hu tsɔɔ amɛbaai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛtsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia amɛ. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ ayibɔ baa shi trukaa

english: What are the early signs that my cocoa tree is getting sick?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miibɔi hela mɔmɔ?

english: Early warning signs include small black spots on the pods, strange swollen areas on the branches, or leaves wilting suddenly even when there is enough water in the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ mra lɛ ahe ji ŋmeii diji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ. Aloo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle when exposed to full direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh sun, so they need temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them while their root systems establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during a long dry season without rain?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: To survive extreme dry weather, cocoa trees try to conserve water by dropping their leaves and shedding small pods so the main trunk can stay alive.
ga: Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi waa lɛ amli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛgbalaɔ lɛ nɔ. koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by poor soil, drought, or lack of pollination, naturally reducing their workload when they do not have enough energy to mature the fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, hɔmɔ, loo ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ akwɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: As cocoa trees age, their internal energy systems slow down just like the human body, requiring specialized pruning, fertilizer, or eventual replanting to maintain high production.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da Tamɔ adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ, amɛmli hewalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi. Enɛ biɔ ni afolɔ tso krɛdɛɛ ko, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo yɛ naagbee lɛ adu ekoŋŋ koni yibii babaoo ahi shi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When a cocoa pod is ripe, its skin color changes from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange, signaling that the beans inside are fully mature and ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ lɛ Ehewolo nɔ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do cocoa research officers come to inspect my farm and examine my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo he niiamlitaolɔi miikwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛmiikwɛ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Research officers inspect farms much like doctors checking patients—they look for hidden tree diseases early, test your soil, and bring you updated knowledge to help keep your farm healthy and high-yielding.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ nitsulɔi kwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli tamɔ bɔ ni datrɛfoi kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli lɛ. Amɛtaoɔ tso helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ mra. Kaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ ni ekɛ nilee hee aba bo koni eye ebua ni oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that drains the soil of food, especially nitrogen. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, resting and rebuilding the earth naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele ji niyenii ni tsii ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛjɔɔ ohe ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ama ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. When maize doesn't get enough food from the soil, it pulls nutrient reserves from its old bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, signaling that fertilizer or manure is needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Egbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia.

english: If I plant my cassava stem cuttings closer together, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani nibii babaoo baaba?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your harvest. When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in many small, thin tubers instead of big, thick ones.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi. Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe tseee yɛ agboi ni amɛhe tseee lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by sudden high heat, dry soil, or a lack of key nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and feeding the plant during flower growth helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha tso lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miida lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow early and the trunk splits near the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miikumɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Panama disease or fungal wilt, which lives in the soil and blocks water from moving up the plant. You can prevent this by planting disease-free suckers and avoiding moving soil from infected farms to clean fields.
ga: Enɛ ji Panama hela, loo fungal wilt, ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haaa nu aya tso lɛ nɔ lɛ he okadi. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni helai bɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni oootsi kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni hela emɔ mli lɛ amli kɛya ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know that my yams under the ground are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams tell you they are ready above ground: when the vines and leaves naturally yellow and dry up completely, it means the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ: beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi kɛtee eyitso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and turn pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and destroying infected plants stops the virus from spreading across your entire vegetable farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ akpãtãmɔ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa o-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around the base of my young oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds around the base steal water and plant food intended for the palm. Clearing a ring around the base prevents weed competition and keeps away rodents that like to nest near the stems and chew young palm bark.
ga: Jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ jwɛi akaŋshii naa. ni otsi ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛfee amɛ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow better when there is standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa folo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice roots are specially built to thrive in submerged soil, where standing water drowns out competing land weeds and helps the rice plant easily suck up minerals from the wet earth.
ga: Afee ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ nɔ. He ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni amɛjieɔ minerals kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ mli mlɛo

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the shade and moist climate young cocoa needs to survive its first few years, while also giving you food and quick income.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be. Ehe miihia baby cocoa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii kɛ shika ni akɛhaa oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the season helps restore the green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the plants harvest and break down, they leave nitrogen behind, which acts as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji akpa tsei ni amɛgbee shi Ebaashi nitrogen yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: You can check the maturity by looking at the age of the variety (usually 9 to 12 months after planting), observing if the lower leaves have started turning yellow and falling naturally, or gently removing a bit of soil near the stem to see if the root is full.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ afii abɔ ni oookwɛ nɔ (bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ), ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, loo ojie sũ fioo ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ blɛoo koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to the local environment, so their seeds respond instantly to water and steal nutrients from the soil faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crop a fair chance to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ená shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are there small holes and chewing marks inside the funnels of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmɔtɔ he okadii yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar that feed on the soft, growing leaves inside the plant's central funnel. Spraying an approved pesticide directly into the center of the plant early in the morning or evening helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper and tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant is stressed, which usually happens due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or pest attacks. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protecting the blossoms from sap-sucking insects helps flowers set into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni abuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to catch direct sunlight to produce food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing maximum sunlight to hit the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha hulu la babaoo ashɛ baai lɛ ahe bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: Why does paddy rice need so much flooded water around it while cassava roots rot in too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsɔ nu awo ŋmãa mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nu babaoo mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally adapted to aquatic environments and can breathe through specialized tissues even when flooded, which also stops competing weeds. Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy and will suffocate and decay if submerged for long.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu mli shihilɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ fãji krɛdɛɛi amli emu kɛji nu eyi mli obɔ po. Enɛ haaa jwɛi kɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafite kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun rays. This reduces water evaporation, keeps the soil cool, prevents weed growth, and keeps your crops hydrated longer during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ baaha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ahiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from drying out. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the weather cools down or rain falls.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ loo nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Is it better to pour water directly on top of my tomato leaves or at the base near the roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ tomato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: It is best to water at the base near the roots. Wetting tomato leaves creates a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive and quickly spread, which can destroy your entire harvest.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu yɛ shishigbɛ, ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tomato baai lɛ ni efɔ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii fɛɛ ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: If I leave diseased plants in my cassava farm, will it affect the healthy ones?
ga: Kɛji oshi tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli Ani ebaana tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, leaving sick or rotting plants in your field allows diseases and pests to spread through the soil, wind, or rain to healthy crops. Clearing and destroying infected plants protects the rest of your farm from damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ loo amɛgboi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo nugbɔ nɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ofite lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why should I clear away dead leaves and weeds from around the base of my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Dead leaves and thick weeds create dark, damp hiding places for dangerous pests like plantain weevils. Keeping the base clean allows air and sunlight to reach the plant, keeping it strong and healthy.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni mli ewo muji lɛ feɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli efɔ kɛha kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ plantain weevils lɛ. Kɛ́ aha shishitoo lɛ he tse lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Ehaa tsei feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ

english: How does keeping my field clean prevent my whole crop investment from failing?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fɛɛ akafite?

english: Proper field sanitation removes pest breeding grounds and disease-causing fungi before they can multiply. Just as good hygiene prevents sickness in humans, a clean field prevents sudden disease outbreaks that could destroy your entire yield.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ hetsemɔ ni sa jieɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baa lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ kɛyaa dani amɛshwereɔ. Taakɛ hetsemɔ kpakpa tsiɔ hela naa yɛ adesai amli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. He ni he tse lɛ hu tsiɔ helai ni baa trukaa ni baanyɛ afite onibii fɛɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the young cocoa trees I planted turning yellow and dropping their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni miduɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ miiho lɛ?
