english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and dry winds. Yellow leaves usually show that they are getting scorched and need shade plants, like plantains, to shield them while they establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshã ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight. Sun exposure helps the plant make food efficiently, which results in larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, dry soil, or improper care. Giving your plants consistent water and protecting them from extreme heat helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni abu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed new leaves at the top, showing that your soil needs nutrients or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ ahe hɔmɔ koni eha gbɛ aha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava too closely forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall with very small tubers because there is not enough space or food for proper development.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛkwɔ kɛ yitsei bibii waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, he ko loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ kɛha shweremɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas, protecting them from heat stress and preserving soil moisture during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ

english: Yellowing in a V-shape along the center of older maize leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is necessary for healthy green growth, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost will restore plant vigor.
ga: He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni tamɔ V yɛ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce large, bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ baai wuji ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen relative to potassium and phosphorus, cassava plants direct all their energy into vegetative leaf growth rather than storing starch in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium kɛ fɔsfɔs he lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ sisi a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year produce smaller harvests each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting maize on the same plot exhausts specific soil nutrients—especially nitrogen—and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target maize to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. titri lɛ nitrogen Ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees yield smaller bunches when I allow all the shoots to grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plantain stem for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to leave only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main stem gets enough resources to form large bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee panicle agbo.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground instead of letting them spread on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can catch maximum light to build large tubers, while keeping foliage off wet soil prevents fungal leaf spot diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato baai lɛ wo hulu lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ lɛ, amɛfee bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni fungal leaf spot hela lɛ akaye bo.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly and look stunted when weeds are growing close to their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miida blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-spreading roots that aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and space from your crops, starving the crops even if rain and sunlight are plentiful.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋwɛi kɛjɛ onibii amli oya Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la fa babaoo moŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly humid, and dark conditions. Heavy rains allow fungal spores to spread rapidly across pods when branches are overly dense and unpruned.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni afolɔko amɛ.

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes temperature stress that dries up tomato pollen, preventing successful pollination. Without pollination, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy and moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni haa tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ baa. Enyɛŋ etsĩ pollination naa. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Is borehole water safe to use on my vegetable crops, or do I need piped tap water?
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni jɛɔ nubu lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe. Aloo ehe miihia ni mikɛ paipi mli nu atsu nii?

english: Borehole water is generally very safe and rich in natural earth minerals that benefit crops. Piped tap water often contains added chemicals like chlorine, which can reduce beneficial bacteria in your farm soil over time.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ nubui amli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe waa, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai krokomɛi fataa nu ni akɛwoɔ paipii amli lɛ he, tamɔ chlorine, ni baanyɛ aha helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why did the shallow hand-dug well on my farm dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nubu ni akɛ niji tsu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shallow wells only capture water near the top layer of soil, which drops or evaporates when the rains stop. Deep boreholes reach deep underground aquifers that hold water all year round regardless of surface weather.
ga: Nubui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ toɔ nu he yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. ni baaho loo ebaatsɔ la kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Bui ni akumɔ mli kwɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni akɛtoɔ nu mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ mli, ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji.

english: How do I know if my crops are wilting because of hot weather or because they lack water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Crops that wilt under hot sun but bounce back by early morning are just protecting themselves from heat. If your crops remain limp and dry early in the morning, their roots are completely out of ground water.
ga: Tsei ni gboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa leebi maŋkpa lɛ miibu amɛhe kɛmiijɛ latsaa lɛ he kɛkɛ. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni amɛgbi leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eshishifãi lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kwraa.

english: Can I irrigate my maize field using underground borehole water during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu awo ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, using pumped borehole water allows you to farm year-round, keeping the soil moist so maize can develop full cobs even when there is no rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni akɛ pɔmpi tsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ atsɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why do deep-rooted trees like mangoes stay green in dry months while my tomatoes dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ mango lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni mi-tomato lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Deep-rooted trees act like natural boreholes by pushing their roots meters deep into underground water tables, while shallow-rooted crops like tomatoes can only reach water near the dry surface.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nubui kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ tomato lɛ, baanyɛ aná nu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ pɛ.

english: Does giving my crops too much ground water cause any harm to them?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, overwatering fills all the air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Without air, roots rot, turn dark, and can no longer feed the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyiɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaatsɔ duŋ. ni enyɛŋ eha tsei niyenii dɔŋŋ

english: Is it better to pump borehole water to my crops in the morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo nu kɛjɛ bu ko mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots absorb moisture before the afternoon heat causes the water to evaporate into the air.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ aha nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Do different crops require different amounts of water to survive?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi biɔ nu babaoo koni amɛhi shi?

english: Yes, leafy vegetables and rice need constant moisture to produce well, whereas crops like cassava and sorghum are hardy and can survive extended periods with very little water.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai kɛ omɔ biɔ nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Will drilling a borehole on my land guarantee that my crops won't fail during a drought?
ga: Ani bu ni mifoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha miná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efoŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: A borehole provides a dependable water source for manual or pumped irrigation, giving your crops the steady supply of moisture they need to survive even when natural rains fail.
ga: Boreholes ji nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha mɔ diɛŋtsɛ loo pɔmpi ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plants turn yellow when water drops in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, the plant intentionally drops its older bottom leaves to conserve moisture for its young top leaves and growing stem.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ eshwieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and curling up in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get burned easily by full, direct sunlight. Yellowing and curling leaves mean the plant is losing water faster than its young roots can absorb it, which is why shade trees or plantains are needed to shelter them in their first few years.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni aha tsei loo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: When maize lacks enough food or nitrogen in the soil, the plant starves its older, lower leaves and sends whatever nutrients it has left to the fresh green leaves at the top to keep growing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bɛ niyenii loo nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni egbɔ ni baa shi. ni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ majeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the cassava roots inside the soil are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its strength into growing tall branches and lush foliage above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛba shi koni amɛfee bulbs ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon weather gets too hot or when the soil goes dry, because the plant drops its blooms to conserve water and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ shwane mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why do I need to put tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa shwɛmɔ wulu koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need to reach up into sunlight to produce food for the crop; letting vines crawl on the hot soil makes them exposed to dirt, diseases, and shade, which stops the tuber from growing big.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ wein tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkplekeshi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa muji. Hela kɛ shade ni haaa yitso lɛ adara

english: Why should I cut off extra young shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Having too many suckers growing around one main stem creates crowd competition for water and soil nutrients, which leaves the mother tree too weak to bear large plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etere etsitsii wuji lɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water around the stems while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔleɔ ŋmãa lɛ he kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in waterlogged conditions because the shallow standing water suffocates unwanted weeds while keeping the soil cool and continuously supplying nutrients to the root zone.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ muɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli niyenii kpakpai daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward into cup shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is a clear sign that tiny pests like thrips or mites are underneath sucking the sap out of the young leaves, causing them to distort as they expand.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites eba. Nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni anuɔ lɛ haa amɛtsakeɔ be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ

english: How does growing cowpeas in my farm help make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with tiny beneficial soil organisms to pull natural nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛgbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: During extreme afternoon heat, leaves release moisture faster than the roots can drink from the soil. The plant droops on purpose to reduce its exposure to the hot sun and will recover when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ gboiɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. ni ebaaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and turning brown during the bright afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without protective shade crops like plantain or shade trees, sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the moisture they need for healthy growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and thin without producing many fruits when I plant them under shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need full sunlight to produce energy for flowers and fruit. In the shade, the plant stretches upward searching for light, spending all its energy on stems rather than fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii lɛ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Efiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller fruit bunches when I leave many small shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for food, water, and nutrients in the soil. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to grow large, healthy bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛdaraa ni edaa ni ehaa ehe waa.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and produce small cobs when I plant them too closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, their roots crowd each other out and fight for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak plants and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the hot part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a maize plant's survival trick to protect itself from water loss during intense heat. By closing up, the leaves reduce the surface area exposed to the hot air, saving moisture until conditions cool down.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni eŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ shihilɛi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper fertilization. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nyɛɛɛ aya lɛ Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb up wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makudɔ sweet potato wain tso ko kɛya tso tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How do I know if my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest when they are hidden underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves naturally turn yellow and begin to drop off as the plant reaches maturity, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting. You can also carefully dig near the base of one plant to inspect the size of the tubers before harvesting the full field.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbee shi beni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso kome shishi lɛ hu koni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of dark green leaves but fail to produce fruits after applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi nɔ ko nɔ ko jɛɛɛ mli baa yɛ be mli ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using fertilizers with too much nitrogen encourages leafy top growth while delaying flower and fruit development. Crops need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to form healthy flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa baa lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa yɛ be mli ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ daalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Nɔ ni fata he ji fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛfeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni mli wa

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants curl up and feel sticky when small green insects appear on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ je kpo yɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Small insects like aphids suck the sweet sap out of the leaves, causing them to curl up and weaken. As the insects feed, they release a sugary fluid called honeydew, which makes the leaves sticky.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ aphids, nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo. be mli ni kooloi yeɔ niyenii Ejieɔ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar ni atsɛɔ lɛ nectar. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: How do I measure the trunk of my young trees to know if they are growing properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe koni mana kɛji amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can measure the thickness (girth) of a tree trunk near its base using a flexible measuring tape every year. Steady growth in centimeters shows that the tree is absorbing nutrients well and developing a strong structure.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ lɛ asusu tso ko shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ (ebɔlemɔ) lɛ he daa afi. Tso lɛ ni yaa nɔ edaa yɛ sɛntimita mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni enáa tsɔne ni mli wa.

english: Why is it important to track the growth of my tree trunks every year instead of just looking at the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ afi kɛya afi moŋ fe ni oookwɛ baai lɛ?

english: Leaves can change quickly with the weather, but trunk thickness shows the true long-term health and strength of the tree. Keeping track each year helps you know if the crop is maturing on schedule.
ga: Foji lɛ baanyɛ atsake oya yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ji lɛ naa. Shi bɔ ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse ha lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ daa afi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ be naa.

english: How thick should a tree trunk be before I can expect it to bear heavy fruit?
ga: Te esa akɛ tso ko shishi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aha tɛŋŋ dani abaanyɛ akpa gbɛ akɛ ebaawo yibii ni tsii?

english: Most commercial tree crops need a solid trunk circumference—often reaching between 30 to 50 centimeters—so the trunk is strong enough to support heavy branches and carry water and nutrients up from the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo aná tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛlɛɛmɔ ji sɛntimita 30 kɛyashi 50, no hewɔ lɛ, amɛtso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii aya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cashew trees growing very tall but their stems remain thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ daa shɔŋŋ shi eshishifã lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Trees often grow tall and thin when they are planted too close together because they are competing for sunlight. Spacing them out allows sunlight to reach the lower trunk, encouraging it to grow wider and stronger.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ shweremɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ewaa.

english: Do I have to measure every single tree on my farm to understand how my crop is doing?
ga: Esa akɛ masusu tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he koni manu bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ shishi.

english: No, you don't need to measure every tree. Selecting a sample group of about 50 to 100 trees across different parts of your farm gives you a clear picture of how the entire field is performing.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni osusu tso fɛɛ tso he. Ahala tsei aaafee 50 kɛyashi 100 he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ona bɔ ni ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ miitsu nii eha lɛ he mfoniri ni mli ka shi faŋŋ.

english: Why do some trees in the same field grow much faster than others planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Differences in growth usually happen because soil quality, water drainage, or shade varies across your land, or because some roots encountered underground rocks or pests early on.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ sɔrɔtoi baa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, nu ni hoɔ, loo hulutsoo lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Aloo akɛni shishifãi komɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kpe mra hewɔ.

english: Why do landowners or officers check the size of trees when inspecting farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi loo onukpai kwɛɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji lɛ?

english: Tree size provides proof that the land is being actively farmed and well-maintained. Reaching specific target sizes confirms that the farm is properly established under local land or agricultural agreements.
ga: Bɔ ni tsei lɛ dara ha lɛ ji odaseyeli ni tsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ okwaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ashɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko he lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ ato ŋmɔ lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ loo okwaayeli he kpaŋmɔ ko shishi.

english: How do I know if my land is ready to support permanent tree crops like cocoa or rubber?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo loo rɔba?

english: Land is suitable if the soil is deep, drains excess water easily, and allows young roots to expand freely so the trees can achieve steady trunk expansion year after year.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ mlɛo ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ eshishifã lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my trees seem to stop increasing in trunk size during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifã lɛ dalɛ eyaaa hiɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, trees slow down their trunk expansion to conserve water and energy. Once the rains return, water fills the plant cells again, and trunk growth resumes.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ haa amɛtso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Nu baayi tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. ni tso lɛ tso lɛ ku esɛɛ eda ekoŋŋ

english: How can I tell if a young tree trunk is strong enough to survive without shade plants around it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli wa lolo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ebɔle ehe lɛ bɛ he?

english: When the trunk reaches a healthy thickness and its bark darkens and hardens, the tree has developed sufficient internal water storage and root depth to endure full sunlight without scorching.
ga: Beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni eshishifãi lɛ efee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ ená nu ni akɛtoɔ emli kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa ni eshãaa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away essential nitrogen nutrients from the soil or waterlog the roots so the crop cannot breathe, causing the maize leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen nibii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eha shishifãi lɛ afee nu. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amu Ehaa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: When is the best time for me to plant cassava so I get big tubers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei koni maná ŋmeii wuji?

english: Planting cassava at the start of the main rainy season gives the roots enough water to establish strong tubers before the dry Harmattan season arrives.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa dani harmattan be ni egbi lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why should I put fertilizer near the roots instead of scattering it everywhere on my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone ensures your crops get direct access to nutrients before weeds steal them or rain washes them away.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Dani jwɛi lɛ baaju lɛ loo nugbɔ lɛ baaho tsei lɛ.

english: Very hot weather, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer causes stress to the tomato plant, making it drop its flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow so tall with many leaves but has very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes the cassava plant spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does a yam plant know when to stop growing leaves and start growing the yam underground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato tso ko leɔ be ni esa akɛ ekpa baai lɛ kwɛ̃mɔ ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam plants react to changing rain and sunshine patterns; when the rain slows down, the plant naturally shifts its energy from leaves into swelling the underground tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsei hereɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la tsakemɔi anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ba shi lɛ Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems, which makes them top-heavy and easy for wind to push over unless supported with strong stakes.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni tsii, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli mlɛo. ja akulashiŋi ni wa ko yɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do caterpillars always attack the fresh center leaves of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ateŋ baai heei lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm target the center leaves because that is the softest, most tender, and most nutritious part of the growing maize plant.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ nomɛi ji fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ. Abɛi tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves curl up and dry during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not have deep roots yet, so during the hot, dry Harmattan, they curl their leaves to stop losing water through their foliage.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is tired and needs compost or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, look pale, and produce smaller yields even with good rains, the soil lacks natural nutrients and needs organic matter like compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa lɛ, amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehe miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and dying before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea early in the season can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking the sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these small pests early with neem oil spray or recommended insecticides helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Heavy rains and high humidity create the ideal environment for black pod fungal disease. Pruning excess tree branches to let air and sunlight reach the pods, along with removing infected pods immediately, helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod fungus hela lɛ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is growing, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the tomato plant take up calcium properly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my rice crop need standing water in the field during its early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water suppresses weeds that would otherwise compete with young rice plants for sunlight and soil nutrients, while keeping the soil cool and moist for healthy root growth.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ abɔ he akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa waa.

english: How should I position cassava stem cuttings in the soil so they grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plant cassava cuttings at a slight slant or horizontally under moist soil, ensuring the small growth buds on the stem point upward so the new shoots can emerge easily toward the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni etse fioo loo ejɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ shishi. kɛtsɔ hiŋmɛii bibii ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ yiteŋ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei anyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes to expose maximum leaf surface to sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to manufacture food, which is then transferred underground to build bigger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he babaoo. Hulu la haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, aduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ready to harvest since the pods grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are generally ready when the plant leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. You can pull up a sample plant; if the inside of the pod shells has darkened veins and the seeds fill the shell completely, it is time to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso ko he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji pod lɛ mli yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why is it beneficial to cover the soil around my plantain suckers with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and gradually rots to feed the soil with organic matter.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start losing their leaves and looking weak around March every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ March beaŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: March comes at the tail end of the dry season in Ghana. Because the ground is dry and water is scarce, cocoa trees drop some of their leaves to reduce water loss and protect themselves from dying of heat stress.
ga: March baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee yɛ Ghana. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nu faaa yɛ jɛmɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni haa mɔ gboɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop many of their flowers without growing into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces far more flowers than it can feed. If there is not enough rain or nutrients in the soil, the tree drops extra flowers so it can save its strength for the few pods it can actually support.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nugbɔ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi ashwie shi bɔni afee ni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli kɛha ŋmeii fioo ni tso lɛ baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ lɛ.

english: Why do older cocoa trees handle the dry season better than young ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ hɔmɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Older cocoa trees have deep taproots that reach far underground to find water, and their thick leaves create a cool environment under the canopy that holds moisture even when it has not rained for weeks.
ga: Cacao tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu. Ni tsei lɛ ahe baai ni mli ewo wu lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa tsei lɛ ashishi ni haa nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo po.

english: I just got access to a piece of family land to start cocoa farming, so how long will I wait before harvesting my first crop?
ga: Etsɛko tsɔ ni minine shɛ weku shikpɔŋ nɔ koni mikɛje kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees take about 3 to 5 years to start bearing fruit, but improved hybrid varieties can begin producing pods in about 2 to 3 years if they get good care and water.
ga: Kusum mli cacao tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aha amɛ nu.

english: What is the best month of the year for me to plant my cocoa seedlings in the field?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni akɛduɔ kookoo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the start of the main rainy season around May or June. This gives the roots enough time to grow deep into the soil before the dry season comes.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee, aaafee May loo June. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my family's land is good enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miweku lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kokoo?

english: Good cocoa soil is usually dark, soft, and deep enough for roots to grow without hitting hard rock. It should hold moisture well after rain without staying flooded or turning into thick, sticky mud.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni enaaa tɛi ni wa lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. Esa akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni nu afua loo etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi, ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are experienced farmers telling me not to cut down all the large trees on my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikafolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani midu kookoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need shade, especially when young. Leaving select large trees protects cocoa leaves from scorching in the harsh sun and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei hia hulutsoo, titri lɛ kɛ́ amɛji bibii. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni edara ni ahala lɛ ni abu he lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai lɛ ahe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã amɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Can I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees, or will they steal food from the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ kookoo lɛ mli?

english: Planting plantains alongside young cocoa is actually helpful. The broad leaves of the plantain provide quick shade to shield the young cocoa from strong sun, and you can harvest the plantains for food while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii feɔ ekome kɛduɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo oya koni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ni obaanyɛ okpa plantains akɛ niyenii beni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ lɛ.

english: What simple step can I take to keep my young plants from drying up when the dry season begins?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Koni mi dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You can cover the ground around the base of your plants with dry grass or leaves, which is called mulching. This acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the water in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ko ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Why do some cocoa pods turn yellow and dry up when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni amɛdarako kwraa lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree gets stressed by bad weather, lack of water, or limited plant food. The tree naturally lets small pods dry up to save energy for the healthiest ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii, nu ni bɛ, loo tsei aniyenii ni faaa lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Tso lɛ shĩɔ ŋmeii bibii. Eyɛ adebɔɔ mli ni egbi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha gbɔmɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when there is direct sunlight on my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tswa miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle full, intense sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly with broad leaves, acting like umbrellas that shade young cocoa and keep the surrounding soil moist until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la fɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my cassava farm grow very tall leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, cassava plants focus all their energy on growing lush green foliage instead of storing food in the roots. Using fertilizer rich in potassium encourages the plant to direct its food down into expanding the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yucca tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ potassium ni fa babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni baa shi lɛ atsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: These are fall armyworms, which hide inside the tight center funnel of young maize plants where it is moist and safe from predators. Spotting them early and applying organic or recommended sprays directly into the inner funnel stops them before they destroy the growing shoot.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli wa lɛ amli, he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ona amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ mli lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants roll up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which traps moisture inside and prevents water loss. Watering early in the morning and putting dried leaves or grass around the stems helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ mli ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ he Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my tomato plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather is too hot or when they do not get steady water. When the plant experiences sudden drought or extreme heat, it saves energy by dropping its blossoms instead of trying to nourish fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Kɛ tsei na hɔmɔ trukaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa Ebaaha hewalɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni eeefo lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in the first generation. If you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the new crop will grow unevenly and produce much smaller yields, so it is best to buy fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn yellow and the vines dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: When a yam plant reaches full maturity, it stops growing new leaves and transfers all remaining energy from its stems down into the underground tuber, causing the vine to die back naturally to signal that the yam is ready to dig up.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ekpaa baai heei adalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ koni ekɛtsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with seeds and roots already resting in the soil, ready to absorb water instantly. Clearing your field early and planting your crops with proper spacing helps the main crops grow fast enough to shade out the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. Efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ni ejieɔ he lɛ mra Ni tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni edaa oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves show yellow spots and twist up like a hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbɔle amɛhe tamɔ niji lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the sap. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers prevents the virus from damaging your yield.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Whiteflies bibii ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into powder and develop small holes inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mi shĩa lɛ mli

english: Grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside maize kernels, and if the grain is stored while still damp, the insects hatch and eat the inside of the kernels. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until it is hard before storing it in sealed bags keeps the weevils out.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui amli Ni kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, kooloi lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa lɛ loo lɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa dani akɛwoɔ kotoku ko mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do I have to wait several years before I can start harvesting from a rubber tree after planting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛmɛ afii babaoo dani amɛje rɔbɔt tsei lɛ akpamɔ shishi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rubber trees need time to build a thick, strong trunk and deep root system so they can continuously produce latex without dying. Tapping a tree too early will stunt its growth and ruin its productivity for the future.
ga: Rɔba tsei he miihia be ni amɛkɛma tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛya nɔ amɛfee latɛs ni amɛgbooo. Kɛ́ otswa tso ko mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaafite wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it possible for me to plant food crops like cassava or plantain on the same land with my young rubber trees?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-raba tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow short-term crops between young trees for the first few years. This gives you quick food and income while the trees are small, and it also helps keep weeds down on your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraaa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do tree crops like rubber or cocoa cost more money to start compared to planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ rɔba loo kookoo heɔ shika babaoo kɛjeɔ shishi fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Tree crops require an initial investment in seedlings, land preparation, and years of care before they yield anything, but unlike maize, once they start producing, they bring in money for decades without needing to be replanted every year.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ biɔ shishijee shika yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ mli, shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ, kɛ afii babaoo ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ, kɛ́ abɔi feemɔ Amɛkɛ shika baaba afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ daa afi.

english: Why do my young tree seedlings dry up and die when I plant them directly under the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small, delicate roots that cannot pull up enough water to replace what the strong sun evaporates from their leaves. Giving them partial shade helps them survive until their roots grow deep.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ efo kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. Shade fioo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the small lower branches of my young trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Mi tso bibioo lɛ shishi?

english: Trimming the lower branches forces the plant to send its food and energy upward, helping it grow a tall, straight, and strong trunk that is easier to manage when it matures.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsotso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni kwɔ, ni ja, ni wa ni enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my trees very close together so I can fit more of them on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If trees are planted too close together, their roots fight over nutrients in the soil and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This results in thin, weak trees that produce very little yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: How do I know if my land is good for planting tree crops that will stay in the soil for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Tree crops need deep, soft soil that lets roots grow far down and drains excess water easily so the roots do not rot during heavy rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ. Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the soil, it pushes out all the air that roots need to breathe. Without air, the roots cannot suck up plant food like nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests every year if I keep planting the same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ hei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest a crop, it takes nutrients out of the soil. If you plant the same crop repeatedly without adding manure or fertilizer, the soil runs out of the specific nutrients that crop needs.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ.

english: Why do bugs and plant diseases spread so much faster when I plant only one single type of crop on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya waa kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When an entire field is made of just one crop, pests and diseases have an endless supply of their favorite food, allowing them to multiply quickly and move easily from plant to plant.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ ji tso henɔ kome pɛ Gbeyei kɛ helai Eyɛ niyenii ni esumɔɔ waa ni bɛ naagbee. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛfãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko mli mlɛo.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help my crops grow better than planting them directly in my open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a light structure covered with clear plastic or mesh that protects crops from heavy rain, extreme sun, and destructive insects. Inside, the plants experience less physical stress and fewer pests, allowing them to grow faster, stay healthier, and yield higher-quality fruits.
ga: Greenhouses ji tsũi ni tsiimɔ waaa ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ baafee fioo, ni kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hu baafee fioo. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara oya. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni owo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do vegetables like tomatoes grow much bigger and cleaner inside a plastic shelter than on my normal land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tamɔ tomatoi daa ni amɛhe tseɔ yɛ plastic shĩai amli fe mishikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Inside a shelter, crops receive a stable environment free from sudden heavy downpours that cause soil splashes and diseases. Because the plants do not spend energy fighting weather stress or insect attacks, all their strength goes into producing bigger, unblemished fruits.
ga: yɛ shĩa lɛ mli Akɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ helai baa lɛ bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuuu nii ni amɛkɛwuuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ haa amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni tɔmɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Can I safely grow delicate vegetables like sweet peppers during the heavy rainy season in Ghana without them rotting?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ bell peppers yɛ Ghana nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli shweshweeshwe ni mikɛhaaa amɛgboi?

english: Yes, by using protective plastic covers or basic greenhouses, you shield crops from excess rain that causes fungal diseases and fruit rotting. The cover keeps the leaves dry while allowing you to control water directly at the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ ko nɔ loo shishijee ŋmɔ ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Obaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba lɛ he. Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni etsɔɔ nu lɛ hu kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How does growing crops inside a net structure reduce my need to buy expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ trellis mli lɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni jara wa lɛ?

english: The fine mesh net acts as a physical wall that keeps destructive insects like whiteflies and caterpillars away from your crops. When pests cannot reach the plants, you do not need to spray chemicals frequently to protect your harvest.
ga: Mesh kpakpa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he Ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofa afɔ shi shii abɔ. koni okɛbu onibii ahe

english: Why is drip irrigation better for my crops than watering them with a bucket or hose?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ hi fe nu ni akɛ baagi loo hose shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drip irrigation delivers water slowly directly to the plant's roots through thin pipes. This stops water from evaporating in the sun, keeps the leaves dry to prevent fungal sicknesses, and saves you time and labor.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ nu baa blɛoo. Kɛtsɔɔ tsɔnei bibii amli kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akafee lasu yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ hela akamɔ amɛ. ni ekɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ akafite

english: Is it possible for me to harvest and sell fresh vegetables during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa aduawai heei ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Yes, by combining controlled watering like drip irrigation with shade nets or greenhouse covers, you can supply water directly to crops and shield them from harsh heat, allowing you to farm year-round and sell when market prices are high.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu ni akudɔɔ tamɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ shade net loo greenhouse nɔ ni akɛaafata he lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu aha onibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara lɛ nɔ wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruits during very hot hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, heat dries out the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form seeds. To save energy, the plant drops the unfertilized flower. Providing partial shade or cooling reduces this heat stress so flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ebɔ dumɔwui. koni akɛ hewalɛ ato Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo fɛ̃i fã ko ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop on hot afternoons even after I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot afternoons, leaves lose water to the dry air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Drooping is the crop's natural way of curling its leaves to expose less surface to the sun; plants usually stand back up as temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ baai lɛ koni hulu la akashɛ enɔ. Tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛte shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops turn yellow and burn during the sunniest months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Intense sunlight and high soil heat can scorch delicate leaves and prevent roots from taking up food properly. Using shade nets filters the harsh sunlight, keeping leaves green and cool while maintaining steady growth.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ akaye nii jogbaŋŋ. Shade nets ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe jɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ mlihiɛmɔ.

english: How do crop diseases spread so fast from one sickly plant to healthy ones across my field?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases spread mainly through splashing rain droplets, wind, or flying insects that carry germs from sick leaves to healthy leaves. Protecting crops from rain splashes and insect vectors stops disease spores from traveling across your farm.
ga: Helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo kooloi bibii ni fɔ̃ɔ ni hiɛɔ helatsɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ ahe Etsiɔ helai ahe nibii ni baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, their roots compete heavily for food, light, and water in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients and sunshine to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant is missing nitrogen, which is a major nutrient it needs to build strong tissues, or when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa koni akɛma fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from hot weather or dry soil. The plant sheds flowers to protect itself and conserve energy until conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium from the soil while the fruit is growing, usually caused by irregular watering that stops the plant from absorbing nutrients smoothly.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be ni haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and dry up when I clear all the tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ? Ha hulutsoo abɔle tso lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn under strong sunlight. Leaving taller trees provides canopy shade and keeps the air and soil moist enough for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce smaller fruit bunches when many small shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, drink water and steal nutrients from the main plantain tree. Removing most of the extra shoots lets the main tree direct all its energy into making larger plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Ebaanu nu ni ebaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow better when there is standing water on the field compared to dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi he lɛ?

english: Swamp rice varieties are naturally built to thrive in water, which kills off competing weeds and makes key soil nutrients easier for the rice roots to take in.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni bɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa henɔi koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nu mli. Enɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ, ni ehaa niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but fail to produce seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi jeee dumɔwui ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: When cowpea gets too much water or nitrogen in the soil, the plant thinks it should keep growing vines and leaves rather than starting to make flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea nine shɛ nu loo nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ susuɔ akɛ esa akɛ ekwɛ wain tso kɛ baa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔi fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi feemɔ

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to produce large tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ko ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to manufacture food that fuels tuber growth. Climbing up stakes lifts the leaves into the sunlight and off the wet ground where they could easily catch diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná niyenii ni haa tuber lɛ daa. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli, ni ebaaje hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft and rotting if I leave them in the soil too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers reach full maturity, wet soil and natural bacteria begin to break them down, causing the roots to absorb excess moisture and rot underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efiteɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some new yam varieties grow and produce tubers so much faster than the traditional ones I used to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato henɔi heei lɛ ekomɛi daa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii oya fe blema ŋmeii ni midu lɛ?

english: Newer yam varieties are specifically bred for fast growth, early maturity, and resistance to common soil pests, allowing them to produce heavy harvests in a shorter farming season.
ga: Afee sweet potato henɔ hee lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekwɛ oya, ekwɛ oya ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fɔɔ baa lɛ akpee naa. Enɛ haa amɛkpaa nibii babaoo yɛ okwaayeli be kukuoo mli.

english: How do I start turning my small farm from just feeding my family into a real business that sells to larger markets?
ga: Mibaaje ŋmɔ bibioo ko tsakemɔ shishi. Te fee tɛŋŋ ni mijɛ weku ko ni mikɛkwɛɔ mihe lɛ mli kɛtee jarayeli nitsumɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni mihɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ jarayelihe wulu ko mli lɛ mli?

english: Commercializing your farm means focusing on high-demand staple crops, using certified fast-growing seed varieties, organizing proper storage, and planting on a schedule that aligns with peak market prices.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ ni ooofee jarayeli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ baama ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni daa oya ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa kɛ dumɔwu yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ naa.

english: Is it good for me to plant crop seeds or yam setts that come from neighboring countries like Nigeria?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii akui ni jɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ mi tamɔ Nigeria lɛ amli?

english: Yes, many crops from nearby West African countries perform very well in Ghana because we share similar rainfall and soil conditions, though you should always make sure the seeds are certified free of disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni jɛ Afrika Anaigbɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana. Ejaakɛ wɔyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ okwɛ be fɛɛ be akɛ hela bɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli moŋ.

english: What kind of crops should I focus on if I want to make sure my household doesn't face hunger during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni hɔmɔ akaye mishiabii lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Focusing on high-yielding, storeable root crops like yams and cassava ensures your family has a reliable food supply, as these crops store energy underground and can be kept for months after harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ ema nɔ ji shishifãi ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni anyɛɔ atoɔ tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava. Ye obua oweku lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ toɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛto nyɔji babaoo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Staking holds their leaves up toward the sunlight, allowing the plant to make maximum energy through its leaves to feed the tuber growing underground.
