ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Staking haa ebaai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ kpeɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ etsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ efeɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛhaa bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do yams require so much deep soil preparation and heavy mounding compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato biɔ ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋtayaai ni tsii kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Yams build large, long tubers underground, so they need deep, loose soil mounds to expand freely without hitting hard ground, which requires more labor up front but yields bigger harvests.
ga: Sweet potatoes feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kɛlɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná gɔji ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ hiɛgbɛ. Shi ehaa yibiiwoo ni da fe no.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting quickly before buyers come to my village?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya dani mɛi ni baahe lɛ abashɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Store your yams in a shade-covered, well-ventilated structure off the ground, handle them carefully during harvest to avoid cuts, and keep them away from direct heat and rain.
ga: Okɛ sweet potato ato he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ amɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli koni akafolɔ. Ni okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ he.

english: What happens to my yam harvest if I make my mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ? Kɛji mifee gɔji lɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: If mounds are too close, the yam leaves will shade each other and the roots will fight for the same soil nutrients and water, resulting in smaller, weaker tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋtayaa lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ sweet potato baai lɛ baafee amɛhe shade. Ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning yellow and drying up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Premature yellowing is usually caused by leaf diseases, nutrient shortages in the soil, or sap-sucking insects, all of which weaken the plant and reduce the size of your ultimate harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya lɛ baa. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ Enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to plant my crops at the very start of the main rains instead of waiting a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni amɛmɛ otsii fioo komɛi

english: Planting with the first rains allows young plants to establish deep roots while the soil is moist and warm, giving them the maximum growth time needed before the dry season sets in.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛshɛɔ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ he dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves in dry weather to save water and keep their underground roots alive. The plant is not dying; it is simply resting until the rains return to grow new leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahi shi. Tso lɛ gbooo, ejɔɔ ehe kɛkɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa koni ebakwɛ baai heei.

english: How should I position cassava stick cuttings in the ground when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava stems should be planted vertically or at a slanting angle with the growth buds pointing upward toward the sky. Burying about two-thirds of the stem under moist soil helps roots form quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi loo yɛ koŋ nɔ ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ ofu tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aaafee mlijaa enyɔ mli ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ama shi oya.

english: How do I know when my young rubber trees are mature enough to start tapping for liquid?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-gum tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni mabɔi nu tswamɔ?

english: Rubber trees are usually ready for liquid tapping about 5 to 7 years after planting, once the tree trunk grows thick enough to reach about 50 centimeters in circumference.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha nu ni akɛtswaa amɛ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ sɛɛ, beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli etse bɔ ni sa ni ebɔle ehe aaafee sɛntimitai 50 lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like pepper or cassava between my young rubber trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmei. Mi rɔba tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years while the rubber trees are small and haven't created heavy shade, you can grow short-term food crops between the rows to earn money while the rubber grows.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛfeee hulutsoo ni tsii lɛ, Obaanyɛ odu niyenii kukuji yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ateŋ koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and garden egg plants look normal in the morning but wilt during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper kɛ egg tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ daa leebi lɛ? Shi ani ebaagbi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun because their leaves lose water faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. They usually bounce back in the evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Tsei gboɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: What causes the leaves on my garden egg plants to turn yellow and curl downwards?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa shi?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a lack of essential nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa

english: Why do non-native foreign vegetables need more water and shade compared to our local Ghanaian crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ tsei ni jeee maŋbii lɛ biɔ nu kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ akɛto wɔ Ghana tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Foreign vegetables originate from cooler climates, so heat causes them to lose water very fast. Giving them extra shade and regular water protects them from heat stress.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ aduawai jɛɔ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, latsaa lɛ baaha nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ amli nu lɛ afite oya. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when soil moisture is uneven, or when the plant lacks nutrients to support fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeee ekome loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii

english: Why do my okra pods quickly become hard and woody before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei oya dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Okra pods grow very rapidly and become tough if left on the stalk too long. They should be harvested young and soft, usually just 3 to 5 days after the flower opens.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛbaafee ais kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Esa akɛ akpa amɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo, bei pii lɛ, gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper fruits coming out smaller than usual and changing color early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ daraaa fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya lɛ?

english: Pepper plants produce small, early-ripening fruits when they face stress from hot weather, poor soil, or drought, causing them to rush their life cycle to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei woɔ aduawai bibii ni shwereɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyaa amɛshihilɛ mli oya koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant's foliage. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or logs the roots with water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni haa tso lɛ baai lɛ niyenii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo ekɛ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ.

english: Why does adding animal manure or decomposed leaves make my crops grow better than planting in bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛduɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Manure and compost act like sponges that hold moisture in the soil while slowly releasing essential natural nutrients to the roots over time.
ga: Muji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejieɔ lɛ fiofio. Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under strong sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to stay cool and retain moisture in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo tsei amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, overly wet, and crowded conditions where air cannot flow freely between the branches.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji ateŋ oya lɛ.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? Akɛtee tso lɛ shishi?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which eat young maize leaves and crawl into the central shoot to feed and protect themselves from heat.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he lɛ.

english: Weeds steal vital food, water, and sunlight from your crops, competing for the same resources the crops need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋshii nɔ.

english: Underground rot occurs when heavy water stays pooled in the soil without draining, causing oxygen loss and encouraging fungi to decay the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa kɛji muji bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ekanyaa ŋmei lɛ ni efoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make food for the tubers while keeping the foliage away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or improper fertilizer, saving energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaaa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain often creates a brief hot spell in the dry soil afterward; waiting for steady rains prevents seeds from burning or drying out underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mlimɛmɔ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã loo amɛkagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for the cocoa trees during their early growth.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why is it important to heap soil into mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abua sũ lɛ naa ni afee gɔŋ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, soft soil to expand properly. Mounding loosens hard dirt, improves drainage so roots do not rot in heavy rains, and gives the tubers space to grow long and thick.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. improve drainage No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ egbooo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa. ni ehaa yitso he lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Planted too closely, maize stalks will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce tiny corn cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: planted too close Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kwɔlɔɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa abɛi bibii baa. loo cob ko bɛ kwraa

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly filled with holes and looking eaten overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu trukaa ni etamɔ nɔ ni aye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant's growing center during the day and chew through leaves at night. Early treatment with recommended organic or chemical sprays helps save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe teeɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ yɛ shwane mli ni eyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Mra be mli tsamɔ Kɛ organic loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: How do wild weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough rain for everything to grow?
ga: Te koo mli jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ eye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal sunlight, fertilizer, and soil water. They also shelter insect pests and diseases that easily spread onto your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii titrii lɛ amli oya lɛ hu naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant lacks vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that waterlogged soil around the roots is suffocating the plant and preventing food absorption.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa niyenii ashɛ ehe.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences environmental stress, such as intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil minerals like calcium needed to support fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. aloo nibii ni he hiaa waa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium, ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off the extra small shoots growing on the sides of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Special ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ afã ni yɔɔ tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Removing side shoots forces the plant to direct its energy and nutrients into growing larger, healthier fruit rather than wasting energy on excess leaves and small branches.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ atsu nii koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai krokomɛi kɛ tsei niji bibii anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In hot afternoon sunshine, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. Drooping is a self-defense mechanism to reduce sunlight exposure, and the plant usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hiŋmɛii ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni hulu la ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if planted too deep in the soil, if the soil is overly dry, or if the seeds were stored in hot conditions and lost their vigor before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni mli edɔ ni amɛhewalɛ sɛɛ fo dani adu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create living shade, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and protecting the soil from drying out until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi kɛyashi be mli ni cacao lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and provides essential food for your maize crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa o-corn tsei lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the upper leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants automatically pull stored nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking plant juices from the undersides of the leaves. It can also be caused by viral infections spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Virus hela ni nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: My tomato plants have produced many flowers, so why are they falling off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Mɛni hewɔ egbeeɔ shi ni edaaa ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience stress, such as extreme heat, poor watering, or lack of insect pollination. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing light shade during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni esaaa lɛ kpe. loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and allowing fungal diseases to attack. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ tutuaa mɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Covering soil with dry organic material (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops soil water from evaporating under the sun, prevents weed growth, keeps the soil cool, and adds nutrients as it decomposes.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ hulu lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataa he be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ

english: At what growth stage should I apply my main dose of fertilizer to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ be mli esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize needs fertilizer early in its development. A small application is done at planting or within two weeks after germination, followed by the main nitrogen feed when the plant is knee-high (about 4 to 6 weeks after planting) when it grows fastest.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mra beni edara lɛ, ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ loo yɛ otsii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ nitrogen niyenii ni ji shishijee nɔ lɛ sɛɛ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ etsitsi nɔ (aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ) beni edaa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing two specific parent lines to get high yields. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose these traits in the next generation, leading to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower total yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly if I delay clearing weeds until late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie shi kɛyashi be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight during the critical early stages of crop growth. Removing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks lets young crop roots grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la oya yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adara waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can flood the soil and trap air, preventing the roots from breathing properly. Rain also washes nitrogen deep into the ground where young roots cannot reach it, causing the leaves to turn yellow from nutrient starvation.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afua ni emɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ hu hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. High temperatures destroy the pollen inside the flower, so the plant sheds the flower because it cannot produce a seed.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ bɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava in straight rows instead of scattering them randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋsɔɔdoi ni ja mli moŋ fe ni dumɔ ŋmãa?

english: Planting in straight rows gives every plant equal space to catch sunlight and gather nutrients from the soil. It also leaves clear pathways for you to walk, weed, and harvest without damaging the growing roots.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ koni enyɛ ená hulu la ni ebuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ onyiɛ, ojie jwɛi, ni okpa ni ofiteee shishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I stop my harvested yams from going soft and rotting in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when kept in dark, damp places without moving air. Storing them on raised wooden slatted racks in a shaded, airy shed keeps them dry and cool, which prevents fungi and rot from taking over.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ewo duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto slat shɛlɛf ni awó nɔ yɛ shĩa ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛha amɛgbi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akaye nɔ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping your maize grow stronger without requiring as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa atsu nii.

english: Why do my young plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread out near the soil surface rather than going deep. When the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top and the rain softens the ground, strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of the earth.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why are my pepper seeds taking so long to come up out of the nursery soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ejɛɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds need constant warmth and soft, moist soil to sprout. If the seeds are buried too deep or if the top layer of soil forms a hard crust from drying out, the tiny sprouts cannot break through to the light.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui taoɔ dɔlɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni efɔ koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa ni baaha amɛkagbi lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ nyɛŋ abote la lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my bean plants fold up during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean leaves fold or tilt away from direct sunlight during hot hours to save water. By reducing the surface area exposed to the hot sun, the plant prevents moisture from evaporating too quickly from its leaves.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ajieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ ajie he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekajie nu ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Large shade trees protect young cocoa by filtering the harsh sun and keeping the surrounding air humid and cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo, ni amɛbuɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I clear the weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Every crop you harvest takes good nutrients out of the soil. If you do not put nutrients back using animal manure, compost, or fertilizers, the soil becomes exhausted over time and cannot support full crop growth.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ kwraa.

english: Why does my cocoa farm require constant attention compared to my cassava or maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be kɛ akɛto mi-cassava loo ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are long-term, sensitive perennial plants that continually produce leaves, flowers, and pods throughout the year. Unlike quick seasonal crops like maize or cassava, cocoa trees are constantly vulnerable to pests, weed competition, and fungal diseases like black pod if not routinely inspected.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni ehiɛ kã shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ewoɔ baai, fɔfɔi, kɛ ŋmeii be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Esoro cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ oya yɛ be mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ. Jwɛi akaŋshii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ mli daa.

english: How many times in a year can I expect my cocoa trees to yield mature pods?
ga: Pods enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tso ko baawo yɛ afi mli?

english: In Ghana, cocoa trees typically have two main fruiting seasons each year: the main crop harvest, which runs from October to February, and a smaller light crop harvest that occurs around May to July.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii titrii enyɔ daa afi: kpamɔ be titri lɛ, ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ October kɛyashiɔ February; kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ be bibioo lɛ, ni baa yɛ May kɛyashi July mli lɛ.

english: Why do many small cocoa flowers drop off the branches without ever growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ Amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support. Many drop off because they were not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or because the tree is saving its energy and water for existing pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Mɛi babaoo kpaɔ skulyaa ejaakɛ kooloi bibii shwieee amɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu toɔ kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are some of my tiny green cocoa pods turning shriveled and black before they even grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi aduawai lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which is the tree's natural way of thinning out excess pods it cannot feed, or by Black Pod disease caused by too much dampness and shade on the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛɛɛ eye lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ black pod hela ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli

english: Will my cocoa crop still produce well if I only visit and work on the farm once a month?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji akɛ miyasara ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome pɛ yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ ni mitsu nii yɛ mli?

english: No, cocoa trees require frequent supervision. Monthly visits leave too much time for weeds to choke young trees, shade canopy branches to get overcrowded, and diseases or insects to spread through the entire farm unnoticed.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa. Nyɔji amli saramɔi lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ yeɔ be babaoo tsɔ koni amɛtsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa. Ha ŋwɛitsu lɛ niji lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. kɛ helai loo kooloi bibii ni baagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko yɔseee.

english: Can I clear all large trees on my land when planting cocoa, or do cocoa trees behave differently in full sun?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛji midu kookoo? Aloo ani kookoo tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ?

english: Cocoa naturally grows under larger forest trees. Young cocoa trees burn easily and will stress or die in full sunlight, so they need temporary shade plants like plantains and permanent forest trees to protect them.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛbaahao loo amɛbaagboi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains kɛ koo mli tsei ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ koni ebu amɛhe.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off new suckers and side branches growing from the base of the cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei heei kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Suckers (chupons) steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk and branches where cocoa pods grow. Removing them helps the tree focus all its energy on pod production.
ga: Suckers (chupons) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do cocoa beans need to be kept under banana leaves for several days right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ kookoo yibii lɛ ato banana baai ashishi gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving wet cocoa beans under leaves allows them to ferment. Fermentation heats up the beans, stops them from germinating, kills bitter flavors, and develops the rich chocolate smell and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ. Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ. Ehaa edaa, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa, ni ehaa enáa nakai tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to wet cocoa beans if I leave them inside a sack for a day or two before spreading them out?
ga: Mɛni baa cocoa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ dani migbɛ amɛshwã?

english: Trapping wet cocoa beans inside a closed bag causes bad heat and moisture buildup, which leads to mold, bean rotting, and off-flavors that ruin the crop quality for sale.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ kotoku ko mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are receiving too much water or sitting in waterlogged soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: When cocoa roots stay in overly wet soil for too long, the leaves will turn yellow and droop, tree growth stops, and the roots begin to rot because they cannot breathe underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. Tso lɛ kpa dalɛ. Ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What happens if I leave my maize in the field for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving maize in the field too long causes the stalks to dry out completely and break easily, while strong sun and pests like insects or birds will destroy the kernels before you can collect them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛkumɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ kooloi bibii loo okpoi baafite dumɔwui lɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my okra pods become so hard and woody if I wait extra days to pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji mimɛ gbii babaoo dani mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Okra pods mature very quickly; once they pass their ideal harvest window, the plant focuses on making hard seeds, turning the pod tough, fibrous, and unfit for cooking.
ga: Okra ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa. Kɛ amɛho kpamɔɔ be ni sa lɛ he Nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛaaha amɛwa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni esaaa akɛ akɛhooɔ nii.

english: Is it bad to harvest my leafy green vegetables in the afternoon when the sun is very strong?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ oookpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting during peak afternoon heat causes vegetables to lose water rapidly, making them wilt, snap easily, and spoil much faster than if harvested in the cool morning.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmaa ni akpaa yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ haa aduawai amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkuɔ oya, ni amɛfiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni akpaa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young tomato leaves curl up and dry out during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely hot sun causes plants to evaporate water faster than their roots can take it up, so they curl their leaves to shade themselves and protect against heat burn.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he.

english: Why do my garden egg plants drop their flowers when the afternoon weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ shwane mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Intense heat and bright sun put the plant under severe stress, forcing it to drop flowers to save water and survival energy instead of producing new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ woɔ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii heei

english: Why do my pepper seedlings snap so easily when I am moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young stem tissues are soft and brittle; handling seedlings roughly or transplanting them under harsh midday sun weakens them further, making stems break easily.
ga: Oblahiaŋ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ Loo ni ajieɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehaa tsɔne lɛ fãa mlɛo

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil within a few days if they get bruised or cut during digging?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ fite loo afo yɛ be mli ni mitsaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots have a very short natural shelf life, and any cracks or bruises allow air inside, triggering a rapid breakdown process that rots the root.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala ni yɔɔ kuku waa. kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii fɛɛ Shi kɛlɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes my ripe watermelons to split open on the farm before I even touch them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-watermelon ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwie shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mita he po?

english: When watermelons experience intense dry sun followed by sudden water intake, internal pressure builds up faster than the hard outer skin can stretch, causing them to crack.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli egbi waa ni nu ni anuɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ, mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ lɛ buaa ehe naa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji watermelon lɛ mligbalamɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to dry my wet cocoa beans under extremely harsh direct sunlight without turning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ magbi mi-kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛtsakeee amɛ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans too fast under scorching heat hardens the outside while trapping moisture inside, which leads to internal mold growth during storage.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ oya tsɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha kponɔgbɛ lɛ afee shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot faster when left exposed on hot bare ground after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ beni atsa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Direct contact with sun-baked ground cooks the tissue of the tuber, weakening its outer protection and opening it up to quick fungal infection.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tsɔne lɛ mli fãji lɛ. ehaa kponɔgbɛ hebuu nibii lɛ baa shi ni egbeleɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa oya

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings do not have strong foliage to protect themselves from intense sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ baai ni mli wa ni baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and slimy during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight flow through, which keeps the pods drier and reduces fungus growth.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with small caterpillars hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo shoo lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Your crop is likely attacked by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft growth center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying approved neem-based or chemical sprays into the leaf whorls stops them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ tutuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ awo baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain stalks snapping near the base and falling over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fãa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa po bɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by banana root borers or nematodes attacking the root system and underground corm. Without stable underground roots anchoring the plant and absorbing nutrients, the heavy plantain stalk quickly weakens and falls over.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji banana shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi loo nematodes ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Plantain tsei ni tsii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy leaf growth, but the tubers under the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes the plant to put all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. Using balanced nutrients or shifting to phosphorus and potassium-rich soil helps tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo shikpɔŋ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same plot as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baawo mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil with nitrogen, reducing your need for expensive commercial fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛkɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is low on plant food before my crops start showing yellow leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tsei ahe niyenii faaa dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje baai ŋmɔŋ kpojiemɔ shishi?

english: You can observe early indicator weeds, test the soil texture, or bring a small soil sample to the local agricultural extension officer for simple soil testing to check nutrient and acidity levels before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona jwɛi ni tsɔɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Kaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ okwɛ Aloo okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko aya maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Koni afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Koni akwɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ acidity dani adu.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward into tiny cups during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excessive water loss through evaporation during extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tso lɛ baafolɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu ni laajeɔ fe nine lɛ naa kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and rotting before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it develops, often made worse by irregular watering where the soil dries out rapidly between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ haa enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ teŋ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I put three or four seeds of maize together in a single hole?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds per hole causes intense competition among the plants for sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems and tiny cobs. Planting one or two seeds per hill with proper spacing gives larger, healthier cobs and a better total yield.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa tsei ateŋ kɛha hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwu kome loo enyɔ yɛ gɔŋ fɛɛ gɔŋ nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui wuji aba. Ehi kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ

english: Can using dirty stream water to water my cassava crops make the plants sick?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛhaa ŋmei tsei lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, water contaminated with chemicals or harmful bacteria can weaken crops, turn their leaves yellow, and introduce root diseases that eventually destroy the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni tsofai loo muawai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɔjɔ. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekɛ hela baa shishifãi lɛ amli ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaakpata tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my borehole water is damaging my tomato leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni yɔɔ mi-borehole lɛ mli lɛ miifite mi-tomato baai lɛ?

english: If water has too much salt or harmful minerals, the edges of your tomato leaves will turn brown and crisp, and you may see a white salty crust on top of the soil.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ mli ŋmei loo minerals ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, tomato baai lɛ ashishigbɛi baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ekolɛ obaana ŋmei yɛŋ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize crops dying suddenly in the field even though there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ trukaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Sudden dying despite rain is often caused by root rot fungal diseases in the soil, which destroy the roots and prevent the crop from taking up food and water.
ga: Gbele trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when water collects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water cuts off air to the soil, choking the roots and allowing destructive decay bacteria to attack and rot the yam tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: What causes my pepper fruits to turn soft and rot right on the plant before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Fruit rot is usually caused by fungal spores that thrive in warm, overly wet conditions or poor water drainage around the base of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal spores ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ tso yibii fitemɔ baa. nu ni mli efɔ tsɔ loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he

english: If my crops die in the exact same spot every year, is my soil poisoned?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii gboi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafee poison?

english: It usually means pest or fungal diseases have permanently infected that specific spot in the soil, which happens when you grow the exact same crop there without resting the land.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he pɔtɛɛ ko daa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe.

english: Should I abandon my land and move to a new farm if all my crops keep failing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni maya ŋmɔ hee mli kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ fite?

english: You do not always have to move; adding organic manure, letting the land rest, and planting different crops in rotation can heal sick soil and restore your yields.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ehe hiaa ni otsi ohe. Organic fertilizer ni akɛbaafata he lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsa shikpɔŋ ni hela mɔ lɛ ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can spray chemicals washed down from a neighboring farm kill my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbe miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, heavy rain can carry harsh weedkillers or toxic chemical runoff from nearby land directly into your root zone, burning and killing your plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa loo tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ bo fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa he ni oshishifã lɛ yɔɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shãa otsei lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: How does leaf sickness spread so fast from one plant to the whole field?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ mli?

english: Plant sickness spreads rapidly through wind-blown fungal spores, rain splashes splashing dirt onto leaves, infected farm tools, or insects moving from plant to plant.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ anɔ. Nugbɔ lɛ shwie muji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi adɛŋdadei loo kooloi ni hela emɔ amɛ ni miijɛ tso kome mli kɛmiiya ekroko mli

english: Is it safe to feed my goats crop leaves that grew near polluted water?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaaha too tso baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ niyenii?

english: No, crops growing in polluted or chemical-filled water absorb those toxins into their stems and leaves, which can poison and kill livestock that eat them.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni adu yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli loo ni tsofai eyi mli obɔ lɛ shwieɔ nakai tsofai fɔji lɛ amli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. ni baanyɛ awo tsofa fɔŋ ni egbe kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my cocoa trees to keep them healthy?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ nu koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa trees for water and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds every two to three months keeps your soil rich, improves airflow, and prevents pests from hiding on your farm.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi fɛɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my cocoa farm if I leave it unattended during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Leaving your farm unattended allows weeds to overgrown rapidly and block airflow. Excess moisture gets trapped around the cocoa pods, creating the perfect environment for black pod disease to spread quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi oŋmɔ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ adara oya ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsi ehe kɛbɔle kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do extension officers recommend cutting off some of the branches on my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ afolɔ mi kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so sunlight and air can reach the inner part of the tree. This directs energy away from excess leaves and into growing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I properly prepare my soil before planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: You should clear heavy debris, loosen the topsoil, and incorporate organic matter or compost. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beforehand helps keep the soil moist and fertile for new seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni tsii kɛjɛ ohe. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui heei.

english: How does adding fertilizer to my land help my cocoa crop perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the soil, replacing lost nutrients like nitrogen and potassium. Healthy soil feeds the roots, which leads to stronger trees and larger cocoa pod harvests.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ waa ni amɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods in some years compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ afii komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees reduce their pod yield when they are stressed by poor soil nutrients, lack of water, or shade imbalance. Regular pruning and soil nourishment help trees bear fruit consistently year after year.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baaha amɛ pod yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, nu ni bɛ, loo hulutsoo ni ejaaa hao amɛ. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii ni yaa nɔ daa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Do my cocoa trees grow better in open direct sunlight or under tree shade?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulu la ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ tsei ashishi?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from burning, while mature trees need balanced light to produce flowers. A mix of partial shade keeps the ground cool and prevents heat stress.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, la ni sa he miihia kookoo tso ni eda lɛ koni enyɛ efee fɔfɔi. Shade komɛi ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: What key signs show that a cocoa farm is well-managed and doing well?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii titrii ni tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: A well-managed farm has clear walking paths, low weed growth, properly pruned cocoa trees with open canopy space, and trees free from disease spots or insect damage.
ga: Okwaafoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ, jwɛi fioo pɛ, ni afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni agbele naa lɛ yɔɔ mli. ni helai loo kooloi ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ bɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How many years of consistent care does a cocoa tree need before it gives a full harvest?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ cacao tsei anɔ daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Most cocoa trees start bearing pods around 3 to 5 years after planting. With continuous weeding, pruning, and protection from pests, they can give high yields for 25 years or more.
ga: Kookoo tsei babaoo jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ, ni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yaa nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo yibii babaoo afii 25 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: How can I spot early signs of disease on my cocoa trees before the pods get ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana hela he okadii mra yɛ cacao tsei anɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ afite?

english: Look for small dark spots on young pods, wilting leaves, or swollen stems. Identifying these signs early allows you to remove infected pods before disease spreads to the rest of your farm.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii diji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii, baai ni egbo, loo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ anɔ. Ehe hia ni oyoo okadii nɛɛ mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi lɛ.

english: Why should I measure the distance between my maize plants instead of just scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Measuring planting distance ensures each plant gets enough space, sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil. When crops are planted too close together, they fight for food, resulting in thin stalks and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ asusu he ni aduɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaaye niyenii he akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need soft, filtered light and humidity to survive. Without shade plants like plantains or larger trees to protect them, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil around their roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui hia kane ni mli jɔ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually show that the plant is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, suffering from water stress, or being attacked by pests like whiteflies that carry cassava mosaic disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni nu he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ. aloo ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ baa lɛ baatutua lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: How do I know if fall armyworms are attacking my maize leaves before the crop is ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall cutworms miitutua mi-corn tsei lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtã?

english: You will notice tiny pinholes in the young leaves and small, sawdust-like droppings inside the central shoot or funnel of the maize plant where the worm hides.
ga: Obaana bu bibioo ko. yɛ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Etamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso ko teŋgbɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ŋmei lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller harvests even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow strong, leaving your plants weak and underfed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off side shoots and extra leaves from my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo sɛɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra shoots forces the plant to send its energy and food directly into growing larger, healthier fruit rather than spending energy on leafy stems.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛyaa aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully grown and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, indicating the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from last year's maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and diseases and produce uniform, high yields, whereas saved seeds often grow into weaker plants with smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kpamɔ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get full of holes when I store them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni eyɛ bu kɛji mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when they are bagged before being fully dried, creating moist conditions where mold grows and weevils reproduce quickly.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ yɛ kotokui amli dani amɛgbiɔ kwraa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient plant roots need to grow green leaves. This often happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or when heavy rains wash the plant food deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei shishifãi ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Enɛ fɔɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tsei aniyenii hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect itself from drying out. The plant goes into a resting state to survive heat, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly into cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense reaction by the plant, often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids, or sudden changes in heat and soil moisture. The leaves curl to protect themselves from losing water and from further pest attack.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni tso lɛ feɔ kɛbuɔ ehe. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. aloo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai krokomɛi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling to the ground without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efeee pepper ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Instead of spending energy to produce fruit, the plant sheds the blossoms to preserve its own strength to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee Tsei fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods even though the trees look bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ?

english: When cocoa trees grow too many dense branches, sunlight cannot reach the inner trunk where flowers bloom. The tree spends all its food making leaves and branches instead of sending energy to grow cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ yɛ niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ, Hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ he ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ niji moŋ fe ni eeetsu hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Yams twist and stay small when the soil under them is packed hard or filled with stones. The roots cannot push easily through hard earth, so you need to make loose, deep mounds to give the tubers room to expand.
ga: Sweet potatoes baatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli ekpɛ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Shishifãi nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni ofee gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe koni eha bulbs lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my plantains produce tiny bunches when I squeeze many suckers together in one area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ ŋmeii babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close together, their roots and wide leaves fight with each other for sunlight, soil water, and manure. Because every plant gets only a small share, none of them get enough energy to make large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ bibioo ko nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special legumes that pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots. When grown near maize, groundnuts share this free nutrient with the soil, feeding the maize without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛ adu yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jaa niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ. Ha ŋmãa niyenii ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why are ragged holes appearing in the center leaves of my young maize plants after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ni mli ewo muji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, which lay eggs on new maize shoots after the first rains. The worms feed inside the moist, folded leaves at the top of the stem before the leaves unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ baai ni mli efɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ dani baa lɛ gbeleɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my vegetable plants have swollen lumps on them underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Swollen root lumps are caused by tiny microscopic worms in the soil called nematodes that burrow into the roots. These lumps block the channels that bring water and food from the soil up into the rest of the plant, causing it to look stunted.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Nɛkɛ kui nɛɛ tsiɔ gbɛi ni tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ naa. ni ehaa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ

english: Can I grow cocoa, maize, and cassava together on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them, especially when your cocoa trees are young. The fast-growing maize and cassava provide quick food harvests and temporary shade for the young cocoa seedlings, but as the cocoa trees mature and grow big, they will need all the space and light for themselves.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei lɛ awo mli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ o-cacao tsei lɛ darako lolo. Abɛi kɛ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa niyenii baa oya, ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Shi kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ eda ni etsɔ agbo lɛ, He kɛ la fɛɛ he baahia amɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant it right next to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli tse ni ewoɔ toi bibii lɛ? Be ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Cassava grows broad branches and deep root systems that aggressively take up sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil. Maize needs direct sunlight and heavy feeding to grow strong, so planting them too close causes the cassava to crowd out the maize.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ niji ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa ayi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense direct sun and heat. Without shade plants like cassava, plantain, or tall shade trees covering them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo tsei kakadaji ni tsiɔ hulu naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: If I keep planting maize and cassava on the exact same plot every single year without resting the land, what will happen to my crops?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ, Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Continuous planting drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish naturally. Over time, your crops will grow weaker, yields will drop significantly, and pests and diseases will build up in the soil.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Be ni be hoɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa. ni kooloi kɛ helai srɔtoi baafa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Does planting cassava continuously spoil the land for other crops later on?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baafite jɛmɛ koni aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Cassava pulls a heavy amount of potassium and nutrients out of the earth when you harvest the tubers. If you continuously grow cassava without adding organic manure or fertilizer back into the earth, the depleted soil will struggle to support picky crops like maize afterwards.
ga: Cassava jieɔ potassium kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji okpa ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ oya nɔ odu ŋmei ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, sɛɛ mli lɛ shikpɔji ni efite lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Is it good practice to plant new cocoa seedlings directly into the exact spots where old cocoa trees have died?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni kookoo tsei momoi lɛ egboi yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is risky because the soil where old trees died often harbors hidden root diseases and has run out of vital nutrients. It is best to treat the soil with manure, let it rest, or plant food crops for a season before replanting cocoa.
ga: Oshara yɛ he ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsei momoi gboiɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ baatsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii, ashi lɛ, loo adu niyenii be kome dani adu kookoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods now than they did twenty years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their natural productivity drops, and decades of continuous harvesting drain the soil of key nutrients unless you regularly feed the soil with compost or fertilizers.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ daraa kɛhoɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛkpaa nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ eha niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo mli. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ daa.

english: If I have used up all my land and cannot buy more, how can I still get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mifite mishikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ ni minyɛɛɛ mahe babaoo hu? Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa babaoo lolo?

english: You can produce more on the land you have by using improved seed varieties, applying proper plant spacing, using organic manure to improve soil fertility, and controlling weeds before they steal nutrients from your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ owo yibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni ka tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ atsu nii. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔ dani amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the plant stems and leaves grow huge?
