ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ baai lɛ dara moŋ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen—which makes the plant focus entirely on leaf growth—or when the ground is packed too hard for the tubers to swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa aahu akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efu yɛ amɛshishi lɛ.

english: Out of cocoa, maize, and cassava, which crop takes the most work and people to harvest properly?
ga: Kɛjɛ kookoo, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ nitsumɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi fe fɛɛ koni amɛkpa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cocoa takes the most manual labor during harvest because it requires constant hand-picking of ripe pods, careful pod-breaking to avoid damaging seeds, and several days of manual turning for fermentation and drying, unlike maize and cassava which are harvested much faster.
ga: Cocoa ji nɔ ni tsuɔ nii waa fe fɛɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli ejaakɛ esa akɛ akɛ niji akpɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli be fɛɛ be. Gbalamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni akafite dumɔwui lɛ. ni esa akɛ akɛ niji atsɔ mli gbii babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa mra kwraa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the maize lacks nitrogen food from the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This makes them grow tall and skinny with small roots instead of big tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed—usually from very hot afternoon temperatures, lack of consistent watering, or when small insects attack the delicate flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do I know if the early rains are strong enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: You should wait until the rain wets the soil deep enough that a handful squeezed together stays in a soft ball. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry heat returns.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ashɛ nine kome he ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji latsaa ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are the yam tubers in my farm growing bent and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become bent when the soil is too hard and compact underneath. If the expanding root hits hard ground or stones, it bends to find soft paths to grow.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔ. Kɛji shishifãi ni alɛɛ mli lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi Ebaaku shi koni ena gbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ebaakwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very big and leafy but fail to bring out fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Giving tomato plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them focus all their energy on growing heavy green leaves instead of producing flowers and setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha otomato tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛjwɛŋmɔ ahi baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get small holes and turn into powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea dumɔwui ni ato lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay hidden eggs in the seeds. After harvest, these eggs hatch inside the stored grain, eating the seed from the inside out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ fɔɔ amɛwuji ni akɛtee dumɔwui amli. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. ni oye dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after clearing the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni ajie jɛmɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that naturally survive harsh conditions. Their seeds lie hidden in the soil and sprout instantly when exposed to rain and sun, taking up food before crop roots are strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni hiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Akɛ edumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ kɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ye niyenii dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered when the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked with water unevenly.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why are the rains no longer coming at the exact same months they used to when my father was farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ enɛɛɛ yɛ nyɔji ni Ataa tsuɔ okwaayeli nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Climate patterns have shifted globally over the decades, causing rainfall in Ghana to become less predictable. Farmers now need to adjust their planting calendars based on current weather forecasts rather than relying solely on traditional calendar months.
ga: Jeŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi etsake yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ewa akɛ aaatsɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ Ghana. Amrɔ nɛɛ ehe miihia ni okwaafoi lɛ atsake amɛ ŋmaa kalanda lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ naa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ kusum kalanda nyɔji pɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize when the start of the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Kɛjɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, etsakeɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Wait until the soil receives steady, deep rain for a few days rather than planting after the very first light shower, which prevents seeds from germinating and then drying up in the soil.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii fioo komɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsĩɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ.

english: Why do the old crop seeds that my family used decades ago yield less harvest today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui momo ni miweku lɛ kɛtsu nii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Weather conditions, temperatures, and soil health have changed over time. Older crop varieties may not be suited to modern hotter temperatures or erratic rainfall patterns like newer, heat-tolerant varieties are.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ekolɛ tsei srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ esaaa ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ latsaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba, tamɔ tsei heei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without producing any pods during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miijie fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause severe stress to the plant. To survive and conserve moisture, the cocoa tree intentionally sheds its flowers to save energy until better conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhiɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi kpakpai baaku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and curling up during long periods without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are defensive reactions to water stress and high heat. The plant reduces its leaf surface area to stop water from evaporating too quickly from its system.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu mli haomɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei baa baa lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi koni nu akajɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why am I seeing more insect pests on my farm during dry and hot weather than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Warmer temperatures speed up the lifecycle and reproduction rate of many agricultural pests, allowing their populations to multiply much faster during hot dry seasons.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ baaha okwaayeli mli kooloi babaoo ashihilɛ kɛ amɛfɔmɔ aya hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ fɔɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of clearing all big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli moŋ fe ni majie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Shade trees protect crops from harsh direct sunlight, lower the surrounding air temperature, and keep moisture in the soil, helping crops withstand hotter climatic conditions.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli dɔlɛ aba shi ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast after rain, and how can I keep it wet longer for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Uncovered soil loses water rapidly to high heat and sun. Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) acts as a barrier that traps soil moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ yiteŋ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo mli. Akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ koni etsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do plantain stalks bend or break easily when the weather gets unusually dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are made mostly of water. During prolonged dry periods, the stem loses internal water pressure, making the plant weak and prone to snapping under its own weight or light wind.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ plantain tsei lɛ babaoo. Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli hewalɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni esumɔɔ ni efo yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi loo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko mli.

english: Why is it helpful to test a small patch of my land with a new crop variety before planting my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aka he bibioo ko akwɛ? Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he kɛha mi kɛ tsei srɔtoi heei dani mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ adu.

english: Trying a small test plot allows you to observe how a new seed variety behaves in your specific soil and current weather without risking your entire season's investment.
ga: Kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni oooka okwɛ lɛ haa okwɛɔ bɔ ni odumɔwui heei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ shikawoo be muu fɛɛ wooo oshara mli

english: How much water do my oil palm trees actually need throughout the year to give a good harvest?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi-oil palm tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Oil palms need a continuous and steady supply of water every month from January to December, rather than just heavy rainfall concentrated in a short rainy season, because they produce fruit continuously.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ ni afeɔ daa daa nyɔŋ kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December. Mohu ɔ, nugbɔ nɛ wa nɛ nɛ ngɛ nugbɔ be kuku ɔ mi ɔ pɛ ji nugbɔ nɛ nɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ nii

english: Why is it bad for my oil palm crop if it rains heavily for a few months and then stays completely dry for the rest of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa nyɔji fioo komɛi, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ehi shi ni egbi kwraa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palms develop fruit bunches all year round, so long dry gaps interrupt fruit formation and cause young fruit bunches to drop, even if the trees received heavy rain earlier in the year.
ga: Mu tsei feɔ aduawai akui yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ aduawai anaa ni ehaa aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ ná nugbɔ ni naa wa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli moŋ.

english: Why do oil palms grow and produce much better in southern Ghana than in drier regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ fe hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Southern regions generally receive consistent rainfall spread across many months of the year, which fulfills the oil palm's constant requirement for soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔ mu tso lɛ he lɛ kpeɔ.

english: It feels like the rains are much more irregular now than in past decades; how does this shift affect my palm oil yields?
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be bianɛ fe bɔ ni eji yɛ afii nyɔŋma ni eho lɛ mli. Te tsakemɔ nɛɛ baaná mi-palm oil lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Irregular rain causes prolonged water stress in oil palms, leading to fewer fronds, smaller fruit bunches, and overall lower harvests compared to years with reliable rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa nu mli haomɔ baa ŋmei fɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji baai fioo Yibii akui bibii kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ ba shi kɛ akɛto afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing very small fruit bunches or no fruit at all during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii waa loo ewooo eko kwraa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the oil palm enters a survival state and reduces the energy spent on fruits, causing bunches to stay small or flowers to fail to develop.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Mu tso lɛ baabote wala shihilɛ mli ni ebaaha hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi akuu lɛ feɔ bibioo loo fɔfɔi lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: What early signs should I look for to know if my oil palm trees are stressed from lack of water?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii esa akɛ matao koni mana kɛji mi-oil palm tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ hewɔ?

english: Early signs of water stress include lower fronds dying off early, new fronds remaining folded together instead of opening, and young female flowers dying before fruiting.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ he mra lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ agbele mra. Baai heei lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbele. ni fɔfɔi yei lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: If my oil palms go through a long dry spell, how long will it take for them to start yielding normal fruit again after the rain comes back?
ga: Kɛji mi-oil palm lɛ tsɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani ebɔi yibiiwoo ni sa ekoŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ eku esɛɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Because fruit bunches take several months to form inside the tree, it can take anywhere from a few months up to a year of good rain for oil palms to fully recover their normal yield.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai akui heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛfeɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ ekolɛ ebaahe he fɛɛ he kɛjɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi afi mli nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa dani mu tsei lɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ he.

english: Can I irrigate my oil palm farm during dry periods, or do the trees only respond well to rainwater?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo mi-palm oil ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Aloo ani nugbɔ pɛ tsei baakpɛlɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Oil palms respond very well to artificial irrigation during dry months because their main requirement is continuous soil moisture, regardless of whether it comes from rain or watering systems.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ tsuɔ nu ni akɛ niji fee lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ titri ni he hiaa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛji ejɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ mli.

english: What simple things can I do on my farm to help the soil retain moisture for my trees during dry spells?
ga: Mifeɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Applying mulch—such as dry palm leaves or empty fruit bunches—around the base of the trees helps shade the soil, keeping it cool and preventing rain water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching tamɔ ŋmei tsei ni egbi loo aduawai ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: When is the best month to plant new young oil palm seedlings in my field?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu oil palm dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young oil palms should be planted at the very beginning of the main rainy season so their roots can establish deeply in constantly moist soil before any long dry period begins.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ aje shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key food they need to grow strong. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the roots helps restore their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ baawo mli Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with small tubers when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need full sunlight to make energy and grow big tubers underground. When planted in deep shade, the plant wastes all its energy reaching upward for light instead of expanding its roots.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni etsɔɔ la mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to grow crops without buying expensive fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa aheee?

english: Dark, soft soil that crumbles easily and stays moist usually has good fertility. You can also look at the wild plants growing on your land—if plants like wild sunflowers or guinea grass grow thick and dark green, the soil is generally healthy.
ga: Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiteɔ oya ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Obaanyɛ ona koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu. Kɛji tsei tamɔ koo mli hulutsoo loo guinea jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree drop many of its small pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? babaoo dani etsɔ agbo

english: Cocoa trees shed young pods when they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all the fruit, especially during dry spells. Proper pruning and adding organic manure help the tree hold onto more pods until harvest.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ amli kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ he tsemɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa tso lɛ.

english: What makes my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai jeɔ kpo?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot and dry or when the plant lacks adequate water. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root area during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying the plants early with soapy water or neem oil helps stop these insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ baashwie tsei anɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in soft soil without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow off, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Weed seeds rest in the soil and are adapted to sprout immediately after the first rain. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops space and stops weeds from stealing water and plant food from your crop.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekpa jwɛi ni baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to soak up moisture before the hot sun evaporates it. Watering in the hot afternoon can waste water through evaporation and scorch delicate plant leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite nu ni jɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni eshã tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why did many of my cowpea seeds fail to come up out of the soil after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds often fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the soil, if insects eat them underground, or if the soil dries out completely after planting. Planting seeds about two finger-joints deep in moist soil gives them the best chance to sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kplukai yeɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ aaafee inchi 2 yɛ inchi kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an important food in the soil that helps plants grow green and healthy. It can also happen when too much rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Beans have a special superpower where they pull food called nitrogen directly out of the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the nearby maize plants so they grow stronger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Beans yɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ aná niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why are my watermelon vines growing plenty of leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon wain tsei lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: When you give your watermelons too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant gets confused and spends all its energy producing leaves and branches instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ oha o-watermelon lɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Tso lɛ futuɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and rotting before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives during wet, rainy seasons when sunlight cannot reach the pods due to overgrown tree branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Hulu la lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and wrinkle?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the leaves, or by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted instead of smooth and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become small or misshapen if the soil is too hard for them to expand easily, or if tiny invisible worms in the soil called nematodes attack the growing roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii loo amɛbaafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa amɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water while it is flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cassava roots are ready for harvesting under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest when the plant is around 9 to 12 months old, the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ tsei lɛ eye aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ, kɛ́ tsei lɛ eye aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ, esa akɛ akpa amɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily whenever a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over easily if the seeds were planted too shallow, preventing the root system from digging deep enough into the soil to hold the weight of the stalk.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifã lɛ akafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfi tso lɛ shishifã lɛ muji lɛ naa.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall down just as the fruit heavy bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi be mli pɛ ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are very shallow and sit near the top of the soil, so when a fruit bunch grows heavy, the tree loses balance and pulls out of wet soil unless supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛtaraa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, beni aduawai akuu lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni esaaa ni ebaatsi ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or rotating your maize with beans helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ daa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cowpeas produce mostly leaves if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. While nitrogen grows leaves, the plant needs phosphorus nutrients to make flowers and full pods.
ga: Cowpeas baawo baai babaoo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nitrogen haa baai lɛ daa moŋ Shi tsei hu he miihia phosphorus koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. Giving your plants consistent water and shade during very hot weather helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers splitting open while they are still in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miikwɛ̃ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Yams split when a heavy rain comes right after a long dry season. The sudden flush of water makes the inside of the yam grow faster than its outer skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potatoes tswaa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Nu ni ajieɔ trukaa lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ mli fã lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ehe.

english: Why is my cassava producing thin, skinny roots instead of big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the soil is packed too hard or lacks potassium. Loosening the soil deeply before planting gives the roots room to expand and absorb nutrients.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my cocoa pods in the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, rainy weather. Clearing weeds around your trees and harvesting infected pods immediately stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Tsei kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ akpamɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants covered in a white powdery substance?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda yɛŋ ehà mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This white coating is a fungal disease called powdery mildew that develops when crop leaves are packed tightly together. Trimming extra branches lets air flow through and stops the fungus.
ga: Nɛkɛ nɔ yɛŋ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew, ni baa kɛji tso baai lɛ ebɔ he. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my watermelon plants curl up and feel sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Sticky, curled leaves mean tiny insects called aphids are sucking the juice from the leaves and leaving behind a sugary liquid. Spraying soapy water or neem oil gets rid of them.
ga: Baai ni ekɔ, ni wa tsɔɔ kooloi bibii. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Amɛmiinu nu kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛmiishi nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants close their leaves tightly every night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ jogbaŋŋ daa gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally fold their leaves at night to reduce moisture loss and protect themselves from cold night air, conserving energy for daytime growth.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni baa gbɛkɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛha dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant food. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little food it has left from its older lower leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛye baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them stay alive during heatwaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around crop stems with dry leaves or straw, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It prevents direct sunlight from baking the ground, keeps the soil cool, and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha he ni tso lɛ tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehãaa hulu la akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why is my cassava producing very tall stems with thick leaves but only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai ni mli tse, shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium. Nitrogen causes the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto potassium he. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young maize early instead of waiting until they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ gbekɛbii abele mli mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaamɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink up the water and fertilizer from the soil faster than young crops can. Removing them early allows your maize to establish deep roots without competing for food and light.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ ni nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei bibii. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmei lɛ shishifãi shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ niyenii kɛ la akaŋ.

english: Why are the small cocoa pods on my tree turning black and drying up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and shaded conditions, or by natural thinning called cherelle wilt, where the tree drops extra pods it doesn't have enough food to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Aloo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel Wilt Hela. Tsei lɛ baawo ŋmeii babaoo, ni no baaha amɛnáŋ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed, usually by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that spread a virus, or it can be the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss during intense sun and dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa. Aloo ekolɛ eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and collapsing around the trunk before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ he dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually a sign of a root or stem disease, like Fusarium wilt or banana weeping pests, which block the plant's internal pipes so water can no longer travel from the roots up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji shishifã loo shishifã hela ko he okadi, tamɔ Fusarium wilt loo banana tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yaafo. ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa Nu nyɛŋ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I stake my yam vines on wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the direct sunlight so they can process sunlight into energy efficiently, while keeping the leaves off damp ground where fungal diseases like to grow.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu hulu la lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in high numbers in that area.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are climbers that need to lift their leaves up high to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant make more food, which leads to bigger yam tubers underground and prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It often happens when the soil is worn out or after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo beni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant it where I harvested cowpeas last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ he ni mikpa tsina ŋmãa yɛ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays behind in the ground and feeds the next crop like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni atsĩ naa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the afternoon sun even when it rained heavily the day before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbi ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, crops lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Wilting is the plant's natural trick to curl its leaves and slow down water loss until the heat passes.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baaho.

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign of tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the undersides of the leaves. As they suck the plant's sap, they inject saliva that makes the leaves twist and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli. be mli ni amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit or irregular watering. When the plant experiences dry spells followed by heavy water, it cannot transport calcium to the fruit fast enough.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ, ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli baa. Beni tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ. Enyɛŋ ekɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ amli oya bɔ ni sa kɛkɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers under the ground are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem bark turns greyish-brown. You can gently dig around one plant to check if the roots are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he tsɔi lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔlɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo abɔle tso kome he koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a few get visited by tiny insects called midges that pollinate them. If there are few insects, dry weather, or poor tree health, the tree sheds unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ baasara. Kɛji kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ ehiii Tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava produce very thin tubers if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cassava lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop. If weeds surround the cassava during its early months, the plant spends energy competing rather than building big starch tubers.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi komɛi ebɔle ŋmei lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ akaŋ fe ni amɛkɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my maize seeds as soon as the very first rain falls in April?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ yɛ April mli pɛ?

english: It is risky to plant immediately after the first rain because early rains can be unreliable and stop for weeks, causing young seeds to dry up and die in the hot soil. It is better to wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays consistently moist.
ga: Eyɛ oshara akɛ ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ, ni ekpa otsii babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ anɛ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand properly. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tubers struggle to push through and become small or twisted, which is why making high, soft mounds or ridges is essential before planting.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Tubers lɛ baaná naagba ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee bibii loo amɛbaatsake. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani adu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and soft at the bottom while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni eyɛ shishigbɛ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, which often happens when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil moisture consistent helps the plant move calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very high heat, dry soil, or insect damage. Keeping the soil moist and giving young plants shade during harsh heat reduces this stress.
ga: Pepper tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eha tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and leaves the ground weak. Beans and groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Abele yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh soil and weather with very little water or fertilizer, whereas cultivated crops rely heavily on special care, soft soil, and extra nutrients to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔji ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and develop yellow patches during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that multiply in warm weather. The virus weakens the leaves, making it hard for the plant to manufacture food and produce large tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaawo niyenii ni amɛwo bulb agbo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their young flowers without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifite amɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni amɛjieee cacao ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midge flies to pollinate them. If the farm is too dry, lacks shade, or has been sprayed with heavy chemicals, these beneficial insects disappear and the unpollinated flowers fall off empty.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ŋmei koni ekɛwo ŋmeii amli. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, ebɛ hulutsoo be, loo akɛ tsofai ni tsii efɔ nɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ laajeɔ ni fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close together so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in many weak plants with tiny tubers rather than a high yield of large, healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa. Yɛ yibiiwoo babaoo najiaŋ lɛ, anáa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaf centers of my maize plants chewed up with little dirt-like grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ dumɔwui bibii shwieɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Etamɔ muji yɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the growing tip of the leaf stem and eats young leaves, leaving behind dark waste that looks like damp sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ ni eyeɔ baai bibii. Eshiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves when the dry harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ miifite yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to save water and protect itself from dying. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts new green leaves and keeps growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eŋɔli ni eda oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips along the center line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋta lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves shaped like a 'V' from the tip inward mean your soil is low on nitrogen. The plant is moving nutrient energy from older leaves to keep young top leaves green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ ‘V’ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛyaa mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei miitsi niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and wilt during the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often bacterial wilt. Bacteria enter the roots from the soil and block water channels inside the stem, stopping water from moving up to the leaves even if water is in the soil.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt kɛbaa Bacteria boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Ehaa nu nyɛɛɛ aya ŋwɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ, kɛji nu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo po.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed, usually from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. The plant sheds flowers to preserve energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: How do I know when my underground yams are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kwraa?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the green leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and completely dry up. This signals that the plant has stored all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto eyitso.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a strong, high yield only in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest will produce weak, uneven plants with much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii ni mli wa, ni fa babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛsoro amɛhe ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of big green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen in the soil. Adding extra nitrogen fertilizer makes them focus on growing leaves instead of spending energy on making flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha amɛjwɛŋmɔ ahi tsei ahe tsei lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ kɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ tsei ahe tsei.

english: Why are my sweet potatoes covered in deep holes and tasting bitter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli bu lɛ mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This damage comes from sweet potato weevils. These tiny insects lay eggs in soil cracks, and their grubs tunnel through the tubers to feed, making the potato produce a bitter defense chemical.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ sweet potato ŋmei lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ fɔɔ amɛwɔlɔi yɛ sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii amli. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyitsei amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ feɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Are there fast-growing crops I can plant late in the rainy season that will mature in just three months?
ga: Ani tsei komɛi yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni manyɛ madu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli?

english: Yes, crops like short-duration maize, cowpeas, and certain vegetables are bred to mature in about 90 days. If you plant them right before the rains wind down, they can fully develop and yield a harvest before the main dry season sets in.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kukuoo, tsina ŋmãa kɛ aduawai komɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ aaafee gbii 90 mli kɛji odu amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi. Amɛbaatsɔ hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops perform differently if I plant them in July compared to planting early in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ srɔto kɛji midu yɛ July mli kɛ nɔ ni midu yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: July marks the transition towards the tail end of the major rainy season in many parts of Ghana. Crops planted around this time receive less total rainfall, so they need shorter maturity periods and quick root development to survive as moisture reduces by October.
ga: July ji tsakemɔ ni he hiaa waa kɛyaa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Nibii ni adu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ ni edalɛ be kukuoo kɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya koni enyɛ ehi shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi yɛ October mli.

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick maize plants use to protect themselves from hot weather. By curling their leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which helps it hold onto its water.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni ŋmãa tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Without larger plants like plantains nearby to provide shade, the harsh sun scorches the leaves and dries out the plant.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛji tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ekãa ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or drought stress. When the plant senses it does not have enough water to support fruits, it sheds the flowers to keep itself alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ bɛ lɛ Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi bɔni afee ni eya nɔ ehi shi.

english: Why do my cowpea crops start dying when rainwater sits on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots need oxygen from the soil to stay healthy. When heavy water stays on the land without draining, it drowns the roots by cutting off air, causing root rot and killing the plant.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu babaoo eshwɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to survive tough conditions. Their roots suck up soil nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to burst out of the ground quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ heɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leafy tops above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why will my crops produce smaller food if I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for limited sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. This competition weakens all the plants, resulting in small leaves and low harvest yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa baa bibii kɛ ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout out of the soil even after I plant them in moist land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep in the soil, they run out of stored energy trying to push through the dirt before reaching sunlight, causing them to rot underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani hulu la lɛ ashɛ enɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Do I need a lot of physical strength to tap latex from my rubber trees properly?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ babaoo koni manyɛ matswa rɔbɔt tsei amli nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, tapping rubber trees relies on precise technique and a sharp tapping knife rather than strength. Using too much force cuts into the inner wood, which damages the tree and destroys its ability to produce sap in the future.
ga: Dabi, rɔba ni akɛtswaa lɛ biɔ ŋaa pɔtɛɛ kɛ kakla ni naa wa fe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaafo tso ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baafite tsei lɛ ni ebaafite nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaafee nu wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: How deep should I cut into the bark of my rubber tree when harvesting latex?
ga: Be ni esa akɛ akpa latex lɛ Te esa akɛ mafo gum tso lɛ shishi kɛyashɛ he ko tɛŋŋ?

english: You should cut just deep enough to reach the sap veins without hitting the hard wood underneath. Leaving a thin layer of inner bark protects the tree so the bark can heal and grow back smoothly.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni oshɛ rɔba lɛ he ni okɛ ohe akataa tso ni wa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he. Ni ashiɔ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ ni efee bibioo Ebuɔ tso lɛ he koni ŋmei lɛ anyɛ atsa ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it fine for me to cut off young branches that are sprouting randomly from the lower trunk?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, removing lower side shoots allows the tree to direct its food and water toward the main trunk and leaves, which leads to better growth and higher latex production.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛyaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ latɛs ni afeɔ lɛ babaoo baa.

english: What is the best way to cut back damaged branches so the tree can heal quickly?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tsei niji ni efite lɛ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni etsa oya?

english: Make a clean, smooth cut close to the main stem using a sharp tool. Clean cuts heal much faster than rough or torn cuts and prevent rot from setting into the trunk.
ga: Kɛ dɛŋdade ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ he. Pilamɔi ni he tse lɛ tsaa oya fe nɔ ni mli edɔ loo nɔ ni etse lɛ. ni etsĩ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa

english: If I cut off the bark to collect sap, will that same bark ever grow back?
ga: Kɛji mifo tso lɛ yibii lɛ koni mikɛbua nu lɛ naa lɛ Ani shishijee tso lɛ yibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, rubber tree bark naturally regenerates over time. Once a section of bark is tapped, you allow it to rest for a few years so new bark can grow back thick enough to tap again.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, rɔba ŋmei lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji oofo ŋmei lɛ fã ko Ha ehi shi afii fioo komɛi koni ŋmei hee lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ ofo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do young rubber stems bend so easily in the wind without snapping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni rɔbɔt tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ ni ekuuu lɛ?

english: Young rubber stems are naturally flexible and elastic because of their high moisture and natural latex content. This flexibility keeps them from breaking easily during strong weather.
ga: Rɔba tso lɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni enyɛɔ efoɔ yɛ emli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latɛs ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nɛkɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe nɛɛ haaa efo oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli.

english: How long can one rubber tree keep producing latex before it dies?
ga: Be enyiɛ rɔbɔt tso baanyɛ afee latɛs dani egbo?

english: A healthy rubber tree can produce latex for 20 to 30 years if tapped gently and cared for properly, though its yield will naturally slow down as the tree gets older.
ga: Rɔba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ afee latɛs afii 20 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ blɛoo. ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Eyɛ mli akɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ moŋ, shi.

english: Why does the latex flow from my tree slow down during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ latex hoɔ blɛoo kɛjɛɔ tsei amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rubber sap needs water to flow. During dry weather, the tree loses moisture and drops its leaves to save water, which naturally reduces the amount and flow of latex.
ga: Rubber trees need water to flow. Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ekɛ ebaa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli latɛs lɛ falɛ kɛ bɔ ni ehoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I just cut a branch from an old rubber tree and plant it in the soil to grow a new tree?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ rɔbɔt tso momo ko mli ŋmeii ni mawo shikpɔŋ koni tso hee ko akwɛ̃?

english: Direct branch cuttings rarely form the strong taproot needed to anchor a heavy rubber tree. It is better to plant certified grafted saplings from a nursery to get healthy, high-yielding trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni afoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa shishifã ni mli wa ni he hiaa koni akɛfi rɔbɔt tsei ni tsii lɛ anaa lɛ aba. Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe koni ana tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How should I cut and bring a sample of a sick tree branch to your office for advice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ tso nine ni hela mɔ lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni mikɛba o-ɔfis lɛ koni miwo mi ŋaa?

english: Cut a fresh branch sample that shows both the healthy part and the diseased area, wrap it in a damp cloth inside a bag, and bring it the same day so the leaves do not dry out before inspection.
ga: Kpãa nɔkwɛmɔnɔ hee ko ni tsɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ hei ni hela yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ abɔ he, ni okɛwo kotoku mli, ni okɛba nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ koni baai lɛ akagbi dani okwɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a shape like a V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow from the tip along the middle stem, the maize is lacking nitrogen. The plant is taking nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyashiɔ amɛteŋgbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. Tso lɛ miiye nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛmiiha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy green leaves, but the roots underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure makes cassava put all its energy into growing big leaves and branches above ground, leaving little energy to build rich, bulky tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ niji wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji ni woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the young cocoa roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce smaller yield when I do not train the vines to climb poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ? Akɛni mitsɔseee wain tsei koni amɛkwɔ tsei hewɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for making food. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and safe from rotting on the damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛkafiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap and transmitting plant viruses that ruin leaf growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa tso lɛ mli helai ni fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why are holes appearing overnight in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli yɛ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the tender leaf funnel during the day and come out at night to chew the leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli shɔŋŋ yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Extreme afternoon heat or erratic watering stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to survive rather than spending energy making seeds.
ga: Shwane dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni ejaaa haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛwo dumɔwui

english: Why do my plantain bunches stay small when many shoots are growing around the main mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main mother stem for soil food, fertilizer, and water. Cutting back excess suckers lets all nutrients flow into making big fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, loo suckers, kɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ aduawai wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during short dry spells even when I watered them heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ waa moŋ.

english: Light, sandy soil loses water quickly through drainage and heat evaporation. Adding decomposed manure or compost acts like a sponge to keep moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔji ni mli tse ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ fata he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cereal crops stunted and pale even though I do not see insects eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Ni onaaa kooloi bibii ni miiba koni amɛbaye lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Striga weed, a parasitic plant attached underground to crop roots that steals water and nutrients before the weed even emerges from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Striga jwɛi, ni ji tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyaa tsei ashishifãi anɔ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani jwɛi lɛ po ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: If I load my harvested maize into a tightly packed truck and leave it overnight, will it spoil before reaching the market?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ wo lɔle ko ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli ni mishi jɛmɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, Ani efiteŋ dani eshɛ jara nɔ?

english: Freshly harvested maize still holds moisture and 'breathes'. When packed tightly in a closed vehicle or thick bags without airflow, heat builds up overnight, causing sweating and rapid mold growth that ruins the grain quality.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ‘emuɔ’ kɛ́ akɛwo tsɔne ni atsĩ naa loo kotoku ni mli wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa nyɔɔŋ kome mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ oya ni fiteɔ ŋmaa lɛ kpakpa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn dark and rot just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ efee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a protective outer skin like yams. Once pulled from the ground, exposed oxygen triggers a natural chemical breakdown inside the root, causing it to spoil within 48 to 72 hours unless processed immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Oxygen ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ. Efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli ja atsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my raw cashew nuts are dry enough to sell to transport buyers without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cashew ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛmaje mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ni efiteee?

english: Properly dried cashew nuts make a sharp metallic sound when poured together, and you can hear the kernel rattle slightly inside the shell. If they sound soft or heavy, moisture remains inside, which causes mold during transport.
ga: Cashews ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa dade gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli tse baa kɛji akɛ awo mli ekome. Ni obaanu kernel fioo ko ni tswaa yɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli. Kɛji egbɛɛmɔ waaa loo eyɛ tsii lɛ Moisture baahi mli. ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I pack harvested tomatoes into deep sacks when transporting them to town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ woɔ kotokui ni mli kwɔ amli beni mikɛyaa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have delicate skins. Stacking them deep in tall sacks causes the weight of the top tomatoes to crush the bottom ones, releasing juices that trap heat and cause the entire batch to rot quickly on the road.
ga: Tomato yɛ hewolo ni waaa. Tomato ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Yɛ kotoku kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ muji lɛ shwieɔ shishigbɛ tomato lɛ nɔ. ni ejie nu ni mɔɔ dɔlɛ Ni tomato muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with neighboring plants for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plant spends all its energy stretching upward to catch sunlight instead of building strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting shoots while sitting inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ beni mita mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go to sleep after harvest, but as temperatures rise or humidity changes in the barn, the tuber senses the coming planting season and breaks dormancy to start growing a new vine.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ wɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo hulutsoo be lɛ tsake yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potato tubers lɛ baanu be ni baa lɛ he. ni amɛfo dormancy mli koni amɛje wain tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi.

english: Will leaving harvested produce directly under the hot sun for a long time help preserve it?
ga: Ani nikpamɔ nii lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni abu he?

english: While mild sun helps dry grains, leaving harvested vegetables or fruits in intense, direct sunlight overheats them, strips away their internal moisture too fast, and causes rapid wilting and spoilage.
ga: Be mli ni hulu la lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashi aduawai loo aduawai ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha edɔ fe nine. Ejieɔ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ oya tsɔ ni ehaa egboɔ oya ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp environments. If the tree canopy is too thick and prevents sunlight and air from drying water off the pods, the fungus quickly destroys them.
