ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni etsĩ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekaha nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ agbi lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baafite lɛ oya.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking pests like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by the plant trying to reduce water loss during intense heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during rainy weather often mean underground plantain roots are being damaged by microscopic worms called nematodes or fungal rot, which stop the roots from pumping water and nutrients up into the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo rot fungi lɛ efite plantain shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ akajie nu kɛ niyenii kɛyaa baai lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and burn easily. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ toi bibii waa beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and allowing the plant to create enough energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa helai baaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or palm leaves around the roots of my vegetables help them stay healthy?
ga: Jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi ni akɛshwieɔ he lɛ Te mishishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants—known as mulching—acts like a blanket. It protects the ground from hot sun so moisture stays in the soil longer, keeps weeds from growing, and cools the roots.
ga: Mulch ni bɔle tso lɛ he, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ

english: Cassava stems should be planted with the small growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems have to twist around to grow up, which weakens the plant and reduces root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔ ehe koni eda, ni no haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ baa shi.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Without stable water and nutrients, the plant saves energy by shedding flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ daa Tsei kɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my crop start rotting after heavy rainwater collects on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ebua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need to breathe air contained in the soil just as much as they need water. When water sits on the field for too long, it drowns the roots by blocking oxygen, causing them to decay.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ

english: What is causing small ragged holes and powdery waste inside the center whorl of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Torn kɛ sũ ni etse ehe yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ ring lɛ mli.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl deep inside the funnels of young maize to feed on the tender fresh leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ dani amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize, especially starting from the middle of the leaf down to the stalk, usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ Titri lɛ kɛjɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛyashi shishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do groundnuts help make my soil rich for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have tiny bumps on their roots filled with helpful bacteria. These bacteria pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for crops like maize or cassava planted next.
ga: Peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Muawai nɛɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing long, thin roots instead of big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin when planted in hard soil that hasn't been loosened, or when the soil lacks potassium, which is the nutrient responsible for swelling the roots into heavy tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieee lɛ lolo lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni ji niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground with stakes also prevents fungal leaves diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai helai ni ji fungal lɛ anaa.

english: Why do most of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support. Many fall naturally due to lack of water, poor pollination by tiny insects, or stress caused by too much direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Kplukai babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Pollination ni kooloi bibii feɔ loo haomɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo kɛbaa.

english: Why do my small, green cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ji No hewɔ ni minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi beni eji bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' a natural process where the tree drops small pods it cannot feed due to nutrient lack, though insect damage or black pod fungus can also cause it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii. Enyɛɛɛ eye niyenii yɛ niyenii ni esaaa ni enáa lɛ hewɔ Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo black pod fungus hu baanyɛ ekɛba moŋ.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit, which happens when watering is irregular or soil gets too dry between rains.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies spreading plant viruses, or by the plant trying to protect itself from excessive heat and dryness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy winds even when bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ bɔ ni etsii waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can be destroyed by tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem borers, leaving the heavy plant without strong anchors in wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ afite. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does rice grow better when kept in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ akɛwo nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ŋmãa daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Standing water keeps weeds from growing and competing with rice for sunlight, keeps the soil soft for easy root growth, and keeps soil nutrients dissolved so roots can easily drink them.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu mlɛo

english: Why are my crops growing slowly even though I put animal manure in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko lɛ? Nɛgbɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifãi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Manure breaks down naturally over time to release nutrients slowly into the soil. Unlike chemical fertilizers that give quick results, organic matter builds long-term soil health and feeds your crops gradually without burning their roots.
ga: Manure fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli koni ejie niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiofio kɛya sũ lɛ mli. Esoro lɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni haa nɔ ko baa oya lɛ he. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni yaa hiɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ. Ha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii ni okɛshãaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when I stop using chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ akpa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your plants lack nitrogen. When you stop using synthetic fertilizers suddenly without replacing them with natural compost or manure, the plants run out of quick food. Adding rich organic matter restores the natural nutrients they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Beni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ trukaa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ etsakeee lɛ. Niyenii baaho yɛ tsei ahe oya. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does decomposing farm waste turn into rich food for my crops?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Tiny natural living organisms in the ground break down plant leaves, crop residues, and animal droppings into dark, rich compost. This process creates natural plant food that protects soil moisture and improves crop yield.
ga: adebɔɔ mli bɔɔ nii bibii Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, efoɔ tsei ahe baai, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, kɛ kooloi ashishifã mli ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ baai ni egbi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves (known as mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, stops soil water from evaporating under hot sunlight, and slowly rots to feed the soil naturally.
ga: Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my soil wash away so easily whenever heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ?

english: Bare soil has no natural protection against rain drops. When you leave the soil uncovered or remove all trees and roots, the rain carries away the top layer of rich soil, which holds most of your crops' natural food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ahe. Beni oshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nɔ ko shwieee nɔ loo ojie tsei kɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo adebɔɔ mli niyenii shwapoi lɛ toɔ.

english: How can I protect my vegetable leaves from being eaten by insects without buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetable baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can protect your crops naturally by making a spray from crushed neem tree leaves mixed with water. Neem naturally repels insect pests without harming your soil, your crops, or the insects that help your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ neem baai ni atswa ni akɛ nu efutu mli lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Neem shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their branches block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight over water and soil nutrients, leaving the trees weak and unable to produce plenty of healthy pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted to local soil and weather over many years. They naturally absorb water and plant food faster than cultivated crops before your plants can grow strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Amɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli amɛjieɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛ̃ dani otso lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it back into the ground through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil so your next maize crop grows strong without needing costly inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-maise ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do my naturally grown cassava roots stay fresh longer after harvest than cassava grown with heavy chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ fe cassava ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Crops grown with natural compost absorb nutrients at a balanced rate, leading to firmer roots with higher dry matter. This balance makes the harvested produce naturally stronger and less prone to quick rot.
ga: Tsei ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ nibii ni egbi babaoo baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ mli waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni efiteee oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when water sits around the roots for too long without proper drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛji nu tara shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to shake and pollinate the blooms. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted slanted into the ground with the small raised buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the new shoots to grow weak and reduces the number of tubers you get.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ odu amɛ ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch full sunlight, which feeds the growing yam tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing diseases and allowing the plant to make bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni ji sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil or soapy water early can protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ shwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ Baanyɛ abu baai ahe

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli ewo bu ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant. Checking your field weekly and applying ash, sand, or recommended bio-pesticides early in the funnel can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa otsi ni okɛ sũ, ŋã loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ atsu nii mra. Yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not right before a heavy downpour, so the rain does not wash the nutrients away into the gutter. Early morning after a light rain is ideal for roots to drink up the nutrients.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieŋ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa nubui lɛ amli. Leebi maŋkpa yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to water my vegetable garden during the hot sun at noon?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaaha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Midday watering causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can absorb it, and sudden temperature changes can stress the delicate plants.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane. Nu ni afɔɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni hulutsoo be mli tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni nuɔ he waa lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Why are my heavy plantain trees falling over before the bunches are ripe for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold heavy bunches, especially in strong winds or when soil pests weaken the stem base. Supporting the main stem with a Y-shaped wooden pole prevents the tree from snap-falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa loo kɛ́ sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miigbɔjɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni tamɔ Y fi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: How can I tell if cassava tubers underground are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mifooo jɛmɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the soil around the main stem starts to crack from expanding roots, lower leaves turn yellow and fall off naturally, and the crop reaches its maturity age (usually 8 to 12 months depending on the variety).
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ efee klalo. Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ mli. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabote fɔmɔ afii amli. (Be pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ.)

english: How far apart should I space my cashew seedlings when planting a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo cashew dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Cashew trees spread out wide as they mature, so planting them about 10 meters by 10 meters apart ensures their branches and roots do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã babaoo be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee mitai 10 x 10 lɛ, ebaaha niji kɛ shishifãi lɛ akashi akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Can I grow crops like cassava or maize between my young cashew trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mi-cashew tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years when cashew trees are still small, planting food crops between them helps suppress weeds, keeps the soil moist, and gives you food to eat while waiting for the cashews to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli lɛ, cashew tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo. Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akabote mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa bo niyenii be mli ni omɛɛɔ cashew ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can cashew trees grow and survive in poor soil with very little rainfall?
ga: Ani cashew tsei baanyɛ ada ni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ nɔ?

english: Cashew trees are tough and can tolerate poor or sandy soil and dry spells, but giving them fertile soil and good moisture when they are young helps them produce far more nuts.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ŋã kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Shi kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How long does a cashew tree take before it starts giving me nuts?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cashew tso ko jeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi?

english: Standard cashew trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start producing nuts after planting, though grafted varieties can start producing much earlier, often within 2 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsoi srɔtoi ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa moŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ afii 2 mli.

english: Why do my cashew flowers drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds bring hot, dry air and heavy dust that can dry out delicate cashew flowers or stop bees from pollinating them, causing the unpollinated flowers to drop naturally.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli baa, ni baanyɛ aha cashew fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. loo ekpa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkafee pollen Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Is the big juicy fruit above the cashew nut safe to eat, or will it harm me?
ga: Ani aduawai wuji ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ cashew lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ayeɔ loo amɛbaaye mi awui?

english: The juicy cashew apple is completely safe and full of healthy juice, but the hard shell around the nut underneath contains a harsh oil that must be removed through roasting before touching or eating the nut inside.
ga: Cashew apple ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa, ni nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ eyi mli obɔ. Shi mu ni mli wa yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni esa akɛ ajie kɛtsɔ shãa nɔ dani ata ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe loo aye.

english: Should I trim or cut off the lower branches of my cashew trees as they grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yes, cutting off lower branches lets air flow freely around the trunk, prevents fungal diseases from spreading from the ground, and makes it much easier to collect fallen nuts later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle amɛhe. trunk freely Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaaŋɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What causes the leaves on my young cashew trees to turn yellow and curl?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or sap-sucking insects attacking the leaves, or a lack of water during extended dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa baai lɛ. loo nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: How do I know when my cashews are fully ripe and ready for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ cashew ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cashews are fully ripe when the cashew apple turns bright red or yellow and drops to the ground naturally; picking nuts directly off the tree before they fall damages the quality of the nut inside.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ batsɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛgbee shi lɛ, ebaafite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested cashew nuts under the sun before selling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbi cashew ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Drying raw cashew nuts under the sun reduces internal moisture so they do not grow mold or spoil during storage and transportation, ensuring buyers accept them at top quality.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii ni agbi yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo fitemɔ baaa beni akɛtoɔ kɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpɛlɛ nɔ kɛ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and burn easily under the strong heat of the sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the cocoa trees with necessary shade and moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get plenty of sunlight, they produce more energy, which travels down into the ground to build larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. Enɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow full ears. The plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they get red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is forming, causing the bottom cells of the tomato to break down.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛnaa nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by very small insects, such as aphids or thrips, sucking the vital sap from the underside of the leaves. This damages the leaf tissue and distorts its normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni efiteɔ amɛdalɛ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I spray liquid chemicals on my crops during the hot midday sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli?

english: Spraying during midday heat causes chemical liquids to evaporate too quickly before they can work properly. Additionally, liquid droplets on leaves can act like small magnifying glass lenses under full sun, burning the leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ dani amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɛlɛ bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from drying up quickly under the sun, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu la shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas makes the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans belong to the legume family, which can draw nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant finishes growing, it leaves this natural fertilizer behind in the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he, ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ adara.

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the growing plants must compete intensely for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This struggle makes all of the plants grow tall, weak, and produce small or empty ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Ta nɛɛ haa tsei muu fɛɛ daraa, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛnáa toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava roots are generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are mature when the lower leaves natural turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the main stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛdara kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso titri lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi tu lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted under shade like plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi akɛ dumɔwu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, hot sun. Fast-growing plants like plantains act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist until the young cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops while they are still tiny seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii Ni eji dumɔwu bibioo ko kɛkɛ lolo?

english: Young crop seedlings grow very slowly if they have to fight with weeds. Weeds steal the small plant's soil food, water, and sunlight, so removing them early gives your seedlings all the resources they need to grow strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa kɛji ehe bahia ni amɛkɛ jwɛi abɔ. Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni tsei bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged, making it hard for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil get better?
ga: Te ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a family of crops called legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, this natural fertilizer feeds the maize plants and improves the quality of the soil for free.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei ni ji legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baaha o-corn tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo yaka.

english: Yes, planting cassava cuttings upside down causes the new buds to grow downwards first before turning up toward the light. This wastes the plant's energy and results in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, yucca niji ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛkɛ la lɛ akpee. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa bulbs bibii baa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants end up competing with each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall with very small maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for making food to grow heavy tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage off wet ground, protecting the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, usually from very high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food. Consistent moisture helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ Nu ni mli edɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into tight rolls?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a viral disease carried by whiteflies. Controlling these small bugs early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni whiteflies kɛbaa lɛ mli kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to drink water before the afternoon heat sets in, while giving the foliage time to dry during the day so wet leaves do not rot or develop fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ baa, yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ be ni amɛgbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni baai ni efɔ lɛ akafite loo akaná tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle out to the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and moving down the middle vein usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize is a heavy feeder, and without enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii. ni nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my groundnut shells look full from the outside but have no seeds inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ shi dumɔwui bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium. Groundnuts absorb calcium directly through their underground pods to form the nuts inside, so adding agricultural lime or wood ash to your soil before planting helps fill the shells.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘poppy’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium. Peanuts shwieɔ calcium lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: People in my community say planting cowpeas makes the soil better for maize next season. Is this true?
ga: Mɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Ani enɛ ji anɔkwale?

english: Yes, it is true. Cowpeas and other beans have tiny bumps on their roots containing friendly bacteria that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji anɔkwale. Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni helai ni haa mɔ feɔ naanyo lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji nitrogen lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their leaves when the dry Harmattan wind begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during the dry Harmattan season as a self-defense trick to stay alive. Leaves release water into the air, so dropping them helps the tree conserve whatever moisture is left in its trunk and roots until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he koni amɛhi wala mli. Baai lɛ jieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛshwie shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ etsitsi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When day temperatures get too high or night temperatures stay very hot, tomato pollen becomes sticky and dry, preventing the flowers from self-pollination. When a flower isn't pollinated, the plant simply sheds it to save energy.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo gbɛkɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbi. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe pollination Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ efeee pollination Tsei baajie lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots inside the storage barn even when there is no rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems with an internal biological clock. After resting dormant for a few months after harvest, the tuber automatically senses it is time to start growing again and uses its stored water and nutrients to push out new sprouts.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mligbɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Beni ajɔɔ ehe kɛkɛ Nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ Yitso lɛ nuɔ he diɛŋtsɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ. ni okɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ mli.

english: Does it matter if I plant cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe ehiaaa ni madu ŋmei nine ni mikɛ mihe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, it matters very much. Cassava stem buds must point upward toward the sky; if planted upside down, the new shoots have to waste energy growing down and looping back up, resulting in weak stems and very small root yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso lɛ, esa akɛ tsei heei lɛ afite hewalɛ ni amɛdara yɛ mli lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbɔle amɛhe kɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni shishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee nibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites hiding on the undersides of leaves and sucking out the plant sap, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii yɛji shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the center shoot leaves of my young rice plants turning white and dying while the rest stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ eyɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: This condition is called 'deadheart' and is caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves, bore inside the stem, and eat the plant from the inside out, stopping water from reaching the leaf tip.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘tsui gbele’ ni stem borers ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa. shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni eyeɔ tsei kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ Koni nu akashɛ baai lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my mature plantain stems snap and fall over at ground level during strong winds even when fruits are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei ni eda lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai lɛ faaa moŋ?

english: This happens when stem borers or tiny soil worms called nematodes weaken the base and roots of the plantain. They tunnel inside the corm and stem base, making the foundation hollow so it cannot hold up the heavy trunk.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi loo sũ mli ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa shishitoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsɔne ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or urea helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have small nodules on their roots filled with helpful bacteria. These bacteria capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural food in the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ Helai nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields the cocoa leaves from excessive heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji hulu la tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft rot in the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves the ground waterlogged for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing fungal rot to set in underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ ni efuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my garden egg and vegetable leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot afternoons, plants lose water through leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its pores and save water, usually bouncing back once the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ nu akafite. Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shi kɛji edɔ pɛ.

english: What causes the central leaves of my young maize crop to look ragged with holes and full of saw-dust like waste?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides deep inside the funnel (whorl) of the maize plant during the daytime and feeds on the tender leaves as they expand.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii (rings) lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii beni amɛmli shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting, curling upwards, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe, ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by those insects. Treating the insects early prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kooloi lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when soil water supply goes suddenly from dry to wet. This extreme heat or moisture stress prevents the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Dɔlɛ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi awo yibii.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni amɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out toward the sun. Capturing full sunlight allows the vine to produce maximum food energy, which travels down to swell the underground yam tuber.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa wain tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni baatsi kɛya shi ni eha sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Mɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers ensures the main plant has full energy to produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know which crops will bring me good money before I start planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baaha maná shika dani mabɔi amɛdumɔ?

english: You can find out by checking market demand in nearby towns, asking local traders what crops are scarce, and focusing on crops that grow well in your soil and sell easily.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kɛtsɔ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ. Bi maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ewa akɛ aaana. Ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔmɔ waaa lɛ anɔ.

english: What steps can I take to make sure market buyers are interested in my produce when harvest time comes?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aná minibii lɛ ahe miishɛɛ kɛ́ kpamɔ be lɛ shɛ?

english: Focus on growing good quality crops, harvest them at the right maturity stage, and inform buyers or local market women a few weeks before harvest so they can plan to purchase from you.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ adumɔ nɔ. Kpaa yɛ be ni sa mli ni shwereɔ lɛ mli. ni oha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ loo maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli yei lɛ ale otsii fioo komɛi dani kpamɔ lɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛto gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhe nii kɛjɛ odɛŋ.

english: Can I plant any profitable crop on my land, or does my soil limit what I can grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Aloo ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ lɛ naa?

english: Different crops need specific soil types and moisture levels to yield well. Plant crops that match your land's soil type or adjust your soil fertility with manure and fertilizer to suit the crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni anyɛ adu nibii kpakpai. Dumɔ tsei ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why do some of my crops grow fast in a few weeks while others take years to produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like vegetables or maize have fast life cycles for quick cash, while long-term cash crops like cocoa or cashew take time to establish deep roots before bearing fruit for many years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmãa yɛ wala shihilɛ ni yaa oya ni haa anáa shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo cashew ŋmeii lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or the roots are flooded with too much water and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ nitrogen niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo po

english: Under strong heat, crops lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They droop to protect themselves, but usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkotoɔ amɛyitsei koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe jɔɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What causes small holes in my crop leaves, and will it reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi tso lɛ baai amli Ni ani ebaaha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Leaf holes are caused by pests like caterpillars or beetles eating the foliage. If too many leaves are eaten, the plant cannot make enough food for itself, which lowers your yield.
ga: Kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa buji baa. Kɛji oye baai babaoo lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afee lɛ aba shi.

english: When is the best time for me to ask an extension officer to come inspect my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabi mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to invite an extension officer during farm preparation, right after crops germinate, or immediately when you spot pests or unusual plant behavior.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ̃ nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nine yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ be mli. beni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ loo beni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tso lɛ subaŋ ni yɔɔ srɔto pɛ.

english: How can my family members help me keep proper records of our farming work?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miweku lɛ mli bii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ wɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ he saji awo wolo nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Your family can help by writing down daily activities in a notebook, tracking how much money is spent on inputs, and recording total harvest quantities and sales.
ga: Oweku lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kɛtsɔ nibii ni ofeɔ daa gbi lɛ ni oooŋmala owo wolo ko mli lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ shika ni afite yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe. ni aŋmala nibii ni akpa kɛ nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ awo mli.

english: How do I prevent my harvested cassava or vegetables from spoiling before I sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-cassava loo aduawai ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Keep harvested produce in a cool, shaded spot away from direct sunlight, avoid bruised handling, and arrange quick transport to the market right after harvesting.
ga: Okɛ okpamɔ nii lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. He ni hulu la shɛɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛtswaa mɔ he lɛ he. ni ato gbɛjianɔ oya kɛya jara nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: How does using chicken manure on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. When mixed into the soil, it feeds your crops naturally, improves soil structure, and helps the soil hold moisture longer during dry periods.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hia tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam eyi obɔ yɛ wuɔ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii aya hiɛ ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Can I keep farm animals like chickens on the same land where I grow crops without damaging them?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi, tamɔ wuɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Yes, you can integrate poultry with cropping, but you must control their movement. While their manure enriches the soil, free-roaming chickens can scratch up young plant roots or eat tender leaves if left unmonitored around young crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ afata he. Shi esa akɛ okudɔ amɛnyiɛmɔi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ, shi kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi anɔ loo amɛye baai bibii kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tsei bibii ahe ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Will keeping birds or animals around my fields help reduce insects that attack my plants?
ga: Okpoi loo kooloi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ akwɛmɔ Ani ŋmɔji baaye abua ni kooloi ni tutuaa mi tsei lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, poultry like chickens naturally feed on pest insects, caterpillars, and weed seeds in the farm, which helps reduce crop damage as long as the birds are kept away from delicate young shoots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi, tamɔ kooloi, yeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ŋmeii, kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, be fɛɛ be ni okpoi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What makes a farm keep giving good harvests year after year without the soil getting exhausted?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔ ko woɔ yibii kpakpai daa afi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ etãaa?

english: Consistent soil care—such as regularly adding organic manure, clearing aggressive weeds, and protecting the soil from harsh sun—replenishes lost nutrients so the ground stays fertile for continuous yearly harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ daa, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa Jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hebuu kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he Ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ daa afi.

english: Why do some crops take up to three years of constant care before giving a full harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi aheɔ afii etɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ be fɛɛ be dani amɛshɛɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Perennial crops like cocoa or fruit trees focus their energy on building strong root systems and sturdy branches during their early years. Once the plant structure is strong enough, it shifts its energy to producing heavy yields.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ kookoo loo aduawai tsei lɛ, kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ niji ni wa ni amɛmaa yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa lɛ, abaatsake Hewalɛ lɛ awo nibii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops produce very little yield in their first year compared to older, established farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji momoi ni ato ama shi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young plants are still adapting to the environment and developing roots. Older farms yield more because their deep roots can reach deeper water and nutrient reserves in the soil.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ miitsake ehe kɛmiiya shihilɛ ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ mli lolo ni eshishifãi miiya hiɛ. Okwaafoi ni etsɛ waa lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage where roots are drowning in waterlogged soil and unable to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach sunlight instead of growing thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu lɛ, moŋ lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: How can I keep my soil moist during the dry season so my crops do not dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi?

english: Mulching—covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or plant stalks—acts as a blanket that traps soil moisture and shields roots from hot sun rays.
ga: Mulching—ni ji jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ashishifãi ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ—tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How often should I clear weeds around my young plants to make sure they survive?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ tsei bibii ahe koni makwɛ akɛ amɛhi shi?

english: Young plants should be weeded every 3 to 4 weeks during their early growth stage because fast-growing weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the crops, slowing their growth.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei bibii lɛ amli daa otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. ni haa dalɛ baa shi lɛ

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant's main food for green growth, and when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant pulls it from the older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ koni amɛdara. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful microscopic organisms living in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop season ends, those roots decay and leave natural fertilizer behind in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop repeatedly eats up the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply. Changing crops each season gives the soil time to recover and breaks the lifecycle of pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Amɛbaaye niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ naa shia ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ yɛ daa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural defense against heat and drought. Leaves release water into the air, so by shedding them, the plant stops losing water and goes to sleep until the rains return, keeping its valuable underground tubers alive.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ji ŋmei lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ naa. Baai lɛ jieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ ajie lɛ Tsei lɛ baakpa nu ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ ni amɛbaawɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Koni akɛbu eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni jara wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries up and dies before it can fertilize the flower. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the flower to save its energy rather than attempting to grow a fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ dani enyɛɔ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni odu aduawai

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants evolved to grow under forest canopy and cannot handle direct sunlight. Intense heat scorches their delicate leaves and dries out their shallow roots, which is why they need shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ koo lɛ shishi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbiɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ, no hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to capture energy and make food, which gets sent down underground to build the tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the dark ground and spreads them out into the light so the plant can make enough food for a large harvest.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfee niyenii. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ ni egbeleɔ amɛ koni la aba koni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo.

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots like oak or mango trees; instead, they have a shallow carpet of root fibers near the surface. When the heavy bunch of fruit grows on top, the plant becomes top-heavy and easily pulled out of the soft soil by wind.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ oak loo mango tsei. Mohu ɔ, sisi fãhi nɛ a mi kuɔ we mi ɔ ngɛ kapɛti ko nɛ ngɛ e hɛ mi nyami ɔ he. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or a virus spread by those insects. The feeding damages the leaf veins, causing them to twist and stunt the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why does swamp rice survive in flooded water while my maize rots and dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu afua mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems and roots that act like straws, allowing air from above the water to reach down to their roots. Maize roots lack these air tubes, so when buried under standing water, they suffocate from lack of oxygen and rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifã lɛ mli kɛ amɛshishifãi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo shishi lɛ Amɛbaagbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛ fitemɔ hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the young seedlings from heat damage and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the plants regain their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant beans in the same farm plot where I just harvested my corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli kɛkɛ nɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting beans after corn is very good for your soil. Corn feeds heavily on nutrients, while beans pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, refreshing your land naturally for the next crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ha ohegbɛ lɛ afee fɛo kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and fall off during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during long dry periods to reduce water loss. It is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to survive drought, and it will grow new leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Ni ebaakwɛ̃ baai heei kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight through, and picking infected pods early, helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. kɛ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaabuamɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves of my pepper plants, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Small holes are usually caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars. Spraying a natural neem leaf extract or an approved insect spray on the leaves helps repel these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my corn seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Corn seeds may fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if insects eat them underground. Planting seeds about two finger-joints deep in moist soil gives them the best chance to sprout.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa dumɔwui Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ aaafee inchi 2 yɛ inchi kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my tomato garden early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha tomato abɔɔ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can drink before the heat sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei lɛ nu leebi koni oha amɛnu nu dani latsaa lɛ aba.Kɛ́ oooha nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why should I clear weeds before planting my crops instead of waiting until after they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi lɛ dani madu moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil. Clearing them before planting ensures your crop seedlings have all the space and nutrients they need to start strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my sweet potatoes are ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready when the vines and leaves start turning yellow and dying back, usually 3 to 4 months after planting. You can carefully dig up one mound to check if the tubers are full-sized before harvesting the whole farm.
