ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu gɔŋ kome he nii koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil food, and their leaves block light from each other. Spacing them correctly gives each plant enough room to grow tall and produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant my seeds right after the first big rains start rather than waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ?

english: Early planting allows seeds to drink moisture while the soil is warm, helping roots grow deep early on so the crop can survive short dry spells later in the season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ mra. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main food plants need to grow. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores the green color so the plant can make energy from sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji koni amɛnyɛ amɛfee hewalɛ kɛjɛ hulu la mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants droop and wilt during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: During peak heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it from the ground. If the soil is moist and the plant recovers by evening, the drooping is just the plant's natural way of saving water.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ he wa kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Foi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ kɛkɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and getting yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curl is caused by a disease spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems prevents the virus from taking over your farm.
ga: Hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe nɛɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Those are Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central leaf roll. Applying proper treatments directly into the center of the plant early on stops them before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Amɛji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ ateŋ. Tsamɔi ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ mra lɛ Kpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out and crack so fast a few days after rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil cracks easily when it lacks organic matter like decayed plants or animal manure. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and traps water in the root zone longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbalaa oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tsei ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha nu ahi shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of plant food. Consistent watering and feeding keep the flowers attached until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi jɛmɛ kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Why do small insects appear and turn my harvested maize grains into dust during storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo ni amɛtsakeɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amɛfeɔ sũ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Weevils lay eggs in grain that still contains moisture. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until it is hard before storing it in sealed bags prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Weevils woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lolo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ewa dani akɛwo kotoku ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa ni ji ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekafa babaoo.

english: How deep should I place a palm nut in the ground so that it sprouts properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-palm tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Palm nuts should not be buried too deep in heavy soil. Placing them at a shallow depth in loose, moist soil allows heat and air to reach the seed, helping the nut sprout faster without rotting.
ga: Esaaa akɛ afuɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli tsɔ. Kɛ akɛwo he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni etse lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do my palm nuts take a very long time to sprout after placing them in the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Palm nuts have a very hard outer shell that takes time to break open. Maintaining consistent soil warmth and moisture helps soften the shell so the young seedling can push through.
ga: Palm ŋmeii yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa waa ni heɔ be dani efoɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Is it better to plant palm nuts directly in the field by hand or start them in a nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nine nɔ loo yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli?

english: Starting palm nuts in a polybag or nursery first allows you to care for the delicate sprouting seeds before moving the strongest young plants into the main field.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔi ŋmeii lɛ awo poly bag loo nursery mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ okwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ. Dani abaadu dumɔwui ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ

english: What can I do to help my young cocoa plants gain strength and take root in the soil?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛshishifãi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa needs protection from high heat and dry soil. Adding mulch around the base and providing light shade helps the young roots establish firmly in the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo bibioo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛmaa shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow strong when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sun. Like human babies, young cocoa trees need initial shade so they can focus energy on growing strong roots before taking full sun.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nakai eji yɛ adesai abifabii hu ahe. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo shishijee mli bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ dani amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my newly planted cocoa has properly taken hold in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ni midu ehee lɛ etswa shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When cocoa takes firm hold, you will notice fresh green leaf shoots appearing and the main stem becoming firm and upright rather than drooping.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo lɛ kpɛtɛ ehe jogbaŋŋ lɛ Obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ ni miije kpo. Ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbee shi.

english: Can I grow palm trees alongside my young cocoa trees on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei tso yɛ kookoo tso bibioo ko masɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops or palm trees near young cocoa can provide beneficial shade to help cocoa establish, as long as they are spaced far enough apart so they do not fight over soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii loo ŋmei tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni eye ebua kookoo lɛ ni etswa shi. Shii abɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How close can I place other crops to my cocoa trees without harming them?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma du ní kpahi. Te ebaanyɛ ebɛŋkɛ kookoo tso lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ ni eyeee kookoo tso lɛ awui?

english: You should leave enough space—usually at least three meters—between cocoa and companion plants so the roots have room to spread and take strength from the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa. (bei pii lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ mitai 3) yɛ kookoo tso lɛ kɛ mate tso lɛ teŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know how much cocoa beans I will get from inside my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kookoo ŋmeii enyiɛ ni maná kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: The amount of cocoa beans inside a pod depends on tree health, regular weeding, and proper nutrition. Well-cared-for trees produce full, healthy pods filled with solid beans.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ damɔ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa Tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii ni wa eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to produce fewer or smaller beans inside?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo loo bibii yɛ amɛmli?

english: Poor soil nutrients, lack of rainfall, or diseases like black pod reduce the energy the cocoa tree puts into pod development, leading to smaller or missing beans inside the pod.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, loo helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji haa hewalɛ ni cacao tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ pods lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛlaaajeɔ.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect its underground roots. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why does my maize crop produce flowers at the top before the corn ears appear on the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The flowers at the top are called tassels, which produce pollen. The wind carries this pollen down to the silk on young corn ears lower on the stalk to fertilize them so grain can form.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ akɛ tassel. ni feɔ pollen Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa pollen nɛɛ kɛyaa siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii atoi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui aba.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or plantains because direct heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots are fully established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aba shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a plantain stem stop growing and die after I harvest the fruit bunch from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ akpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpa aduawai akui kɛjɛ amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once in its lifecycle. Cutting down the mother stem after harvest allows nutrients to flow to the young shoots at its base for your next yield.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo nyɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ hoɔ kɛyaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does a buried seed yam know when it is time to shoot out sprouts underground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni afu amɛ yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛtswa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Seed yams go into a resting state after harvest and naturally wake up when they sense the increased soil temperature and moisture that comes with the arrival of the rains.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui boteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ mli mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Amɛbaate shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛnu hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ ni kɛ nugbɔ baa lɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of wind and insects needed to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ kooloi ni he hiaa koni amɛha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, providing natural fertilizer that helps future crops like maize grow healthy.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa wɔsɛɛ tsei, tamɔ abele, koni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to the soil, allowing them to absorb nutrients and water faster than cultivated crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to direct sunlight, helping the plant conserve water during high heat.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni eba baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when rainwater stays pooled on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When standing water covers the land, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate, stop feeding the plant, and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. suffocate Kpaa tsei lɛ niyenii. kɛ fitemɔ

english: Why does rainwater sink away so fast on my farmland instead of staying in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles with wide spaces between them, allowing water to drain straight through quickly rather than trapping it near the roots for your crops to use.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii wuji ni gbɛ babaoo yɔɔ amɛteŋ. Ehaa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ oya. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ mɛ ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a he konɛ ngmamihi kɛ tsu ní.

english: Which crops grow best if my land has loose, sandy soil?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋã?

english: Crops like cassava, groundnuts, sweet potatoes, and cowpeas perform well in sandy soil because their roots or tubers expand easily in loose earth and they do not like sitting in excess water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Ni amɛsumɔɔɔ ni amɛyɔɔ nu lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: Is land where water settles and stays wet good for growing crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Land where water accumulates is ideal for crops like swamp rice, but most standard crops like maize, peppers, and cassava will develop root rot and die if submerged in standing water.
ga: Hei ni nu ebua naa lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ babaoo tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ awo nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: How can I check if my farmland soil is mostly sandy using my hands?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli babaoo ji ŋã kɛ miniji?

english: Take a handful of moist soil and squeeze it in your palm; if it feels gritty and crumbles instantly without forming a firm shape or ball, your soil is largely sandy.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ ni okɛmimɔ onine mli. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbee shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe ebɔko loo ekɛ ehe ebɔko he lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ji ŋã babaoo.

english: How can I help my dry, sandy soil hold onto water for a longer time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Adding compost, animal manure, or decomposed leaf litter into sandy soil creates organic sponge-like material that traps water and keeps moisture accessible to plant roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egboi wo sũ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ nu mli lɛ baa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hulutsoo.

english: Do I need to water my crops more often if my land drains water very quickly?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu shii abɔ kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya waa?

english: Yes, crops planted on fast-draining, sandy ground require light, frequent watering or regular rainfall, because the soil cannot store water for long periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ la fioo, nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sũ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the dirt around their plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or plant residue—a practice called mulching—shields the ground from direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation and keeping root zones cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ni afolɔ - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why does fertilizer seem to disappear quickly when I apply it on sandy land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Because sandy soil cannot easily bind to nutrients, heavy rains quickly wash applied fertilizers deep underground below the root zone, a process called leaching.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe mlɛo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ. Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching.

english: How should I apply fertilizer so it doesn't get wasted in sandy soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he ni mikɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ lɛ efiteee?

english: Instead of applying all your fertilizer at once, split it into smaller, more frequent applications throughout the growing season so crop roots absorb it before rain washes it away.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mli shikome lɛ, Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ fãi bibii amli ni okɛwo mli shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I protect my loose soil from being washed away during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ naa koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho?

english: Planting cover crops like legumes or leaving crop residue on the surface binds loose soil together with plant roots, protecting the topsoil from heavy rain erosion.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ Loo tsei ahe nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ kɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cassava and maize together on the same farm instead of just one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ fe ŋmãa kome pɛ?

english: Maize grows tall quickly and uses sunlight from above, while cassava grows deeper roots and matures much later. Because they feed at different soil depths and mature at different times, they share land and soil nutrients without fighting each other.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni ekɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ, ni edaa blɛoo kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi, ni amɛdaraa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ sũ mli lɛ ni amɛwuuuu.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my main crops help my farm produce more?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Cowpea plants act like natural fertilizer factories by taking nitrogen from the air and feeding it into the soil. Their low leaves also cover the ground like a blanket, keeping the soil moist and stopping weeds from taking over.
ga: Cowpea tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔhe kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Baai ni baa shi lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kuntu. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—their leaves burn easily under full sun. Tall shade trees or plantain plants act like umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the air humid so the cocoa seedlings can survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually show that your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow strong cobs. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will feed the plant and restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same spot for three seasons straight make my crop yields get smaller every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ he kome bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots suck up large amounts of nutrients from the earth to grow big tubers. If you do not rotate the crop with plants like groundnuts or let the land rest, the soil loses its food and cannot support healthy cassava crops.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmei tsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shi ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my plantain bunch stay small when I leave many shoots growing around one main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ be mli ni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Tso titri kome

english: All the extra shoots fight with the main plant for soil food, water, and light. Cutting back the extra shoots so only two or three strong ones remain allows the main plant to send all its energy into making a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi fɛɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my pepper seedlings right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, tough roots that react instantly to rain and steal nutrients from the upper soil. Clearing weeds early removes this competition so your pepper plants get enough food and light to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa nugbɔ nɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ o-pepper tso lɛ ná niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda oya.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any peppers during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain makes the soil waterlogged and cold, which stresses the pepper plant and causes it to drop its flowers. Creating good drainage channels lets excess water run off so the plant stays healthy enough to hold its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔɔ. Enɛ haa pepper tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he gbɛ kpakpa ni afee lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ ebua fɔfɔi anaa ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my tomatoes develop black, rotten spots on the bottom while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often because water levels go up and down too quickly. Watering your crops regularly keeps the soil damp and helps fruit form correctly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebaa shi oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my mango tree drop most of its small young fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ ayibii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A mango tree naturally produces many more flowers than it has energy to turn into full fruit. It drops the weak fruits it cannot feed, but giving the tree organic manure and water during flowering helps it retain more fruit until harvest.
ga: Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Ekɛ aduawai ni edako ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shi kɛ́ aha tso lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ aduawai babaoo kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important nutrient for healthy growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer that feeds your maize, helping it grow bigger without requiring as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-corn lɛ niyenii. Ye obua ni eda ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa atsu nii.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long, causing fungal diseases to grow. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa trees turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease or attacks from small insects called capsids. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight and air in, which dries out the farm and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids lɛ tutuamɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny whitefly insects that spread a plant virus, or by the soil drying out completely in hot heat. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants from insects helps prevent leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli loo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ kwraa yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be eaten away underground by microscopic pests called nematodes. Using clean, healthy suckers for planting and propping up heavy fruiting trees with bamboo poles keeps them upright.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni akɛ ŋmei tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. Watering your pepper plants regularly during dry spells helps the flowers stay on and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crop stems with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps moisture around the roots longer, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ umbrella kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifã lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are my stored yams sprouting shoots long before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miikwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ dani mifee klalo akɛ madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally wake up and sprout when stored in warm, dark environments after a few months. Storing your yams in a cool, airy yam barn raised off the ground slows down sprouting and keeps them fresh to eat or sell.
ga: Sweet potatoes baate shi ni ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni mli edɔ ni duŋ yɔɔ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii to ŋmeii atsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ blɛoo ni eha ehi shi ehee kɛha niyeli loo jarayeli.

english: Why do maize seeds saved from my previous harvest yield much less grain than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are hybrid varieties specifically bred to grow very well in their first planting. When you save and replant seeds from that crop, they lose their hybrid power, leading to smaller yields than fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui amli. Beni okɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dumɔwui toɔ ni okɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni ji hybrid lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or if excess water gets trapped around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can check by looking for cracks in the soil around the base of the stem or gently removing a little soil to feel if the tubers are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli ŋmeii ni oootao lɛ nɔ, loo kɛtsɔ sũ fioo ni ooojie blɛoo koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by high heat, lack of water, or dry winds. Ensuring your farm has shade trees helps keep the air humid and protects the flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni oŋmɔ lɛ aná tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines with wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can catch more energy to grow bigger tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and leaf rots.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi hela kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my plantain crop start producing smaller bunches after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: As a plantain stem grows, it produces many small shoots called suckers that compete with the main plant for food and water. If you cut off extra suckers and leave only two or three, the main plant gets enough food to grow big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain lɛ tso lɛ da Ebaawo ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛji ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ tso titri lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli buji ni ekumɔ lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. They hide deep inside the top leaves of the maize plant where they eat the soft green tissues before the leaves unwind.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ fãji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ dani baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. When the soil goes from very dry to very wet, the plant cannot absorb and move calcium evenly to the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni amɛkɛya aduawai lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans actually put nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots. Planting them after maize restores soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii, kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni ooodu yɛ abele ni odu sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery spots or black rot spread on my crop leaves during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ diŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves during the rainy season create perfect conditions for fungi to grow and spread. Keeping proper spacing between plants allows wind to blow through and dry the leaves faster, reducing fungal outbreaks.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmei lɛ dalɛ kɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni eha baai lɛ agbi oya. Ha fungal helai ni baa lɛ aba shi

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and wrinkling like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus they carry. They suck the sap from under the leaves, causing the leaf tissue to twist and distort as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ tsɔɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn turn bad so quickly when water touches it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ekɛ nu kpe lɛ?

english: When harvested corn gets wet, it creates a damp environment where mould, fungi, and bacteria multiply rapidly, causing the grains to rot and spoil within a short time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Is it a good idea to spread my freshly harvested maize on mats on the bare ground to dry?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa ehee lɛ nɔ yɛ tsɔne ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni egbi?

english: Spreading mats directly on the ground can trap moisture underneath, allowing dampness from the soil or unexpected rain to soak into your maize and spoil it.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to dry our corn on raised wooden platforms instead of on mats on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛkuu-kɛsaramɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ wɔgbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised platforms allow air to flow underneath the crops and keep them away from damp soil, protecting your harvest from ground moisture and sudden runoff water.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi. ni okɛ ohe akabɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ trukaa lɛ he.

english: How can a sudden rainstorm ruin my entire season's corn harvest in just one afternoon?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ afite mi-be lɛ mli ŋmãa fɛɛ yɛ shwane kome mli?

english: If wet corn is left piled together without dry shelter, the water gets trapped inside the pile, raising the temperature and causing the whole batch to mould and rot rapidly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmãa ni efɔ yɛ ŋtayaa ko mli ni nɔ ko ni egbi bɛ nɔ lɛ, Nu baakpã ŋtayaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa oya ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: What should I do with my maize right after harvesting if I do not have a proper storage structure yet?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mi-ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ he ko ni sa ni mikɛ nibii baato lolo hu?

english: Immediately after harvest, keep your maize elevated off the ground in a well-ventilated, covered area that keeps out rain while you arrange for proper storage.
ga: Beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Wo o-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni ŋwɛitsu yɔɔ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nugbɔ he yɛ be mli ni osaa ohe kɛha nitoohe ni sa lɛ.

english: Why is fresh maize so easily ruined by moisture right after I pick it from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ ŋmãa hee oya lɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize naturally contains high moisture inside the cob, making it extremely sensitive to dampness, heat, and mould growth if it isn't kept dry.
ga: Abɛi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ hulutsoo, latsaa, kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe waa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must my corn be completely dry before I seal it inside sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-ŋma lɛ agbi kwraa dani akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Sealing damp corn inside sacks traps moisture and creates a warm, humid environment, which causes fast mould growth and rots the entire bag of grain.
ga: Kɛ́ otsi ŋmãa ni mli efɔ lɛ awo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaamɔ nu lɛ mli ni eha shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa oya ni ehaa dumɔwui kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I tell if my corn has started spoiling because of water exposure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛjɛ nu mli?

english: Spoiling corn will develop a musty smell, change colour, feel sticky or damp, and show white, green, or black fuzzy spots, which are signs of mould.
ga: Abɛi ni egbo lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebaatsake su, ni enu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ediŋŋ ni bɛ faŋŋ, ni ji ŋmɔtɔ he okadii

english: Is it safe for my family or livestock to eat corn that got wet and developed fuzzy spots?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku loo kooloi lɛ baaye ŋmãa ni mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: No, mouldy corn produces harmful toxins that can make both humans and animals very sick, so water-damaged mouldy corn should not be consumed.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ni efite lɛ jieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ aha adesai kɛ kooloi fɛɛ aná hela ni naa wa. No hewɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ ayeɔ ŋmãa ni nu efite lɛ.

english: How does moisture from the floor penetrate crops left on a woven mat?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ tsɔne ni akpɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Woven mats have tiny gaps and absorb liquid, so dampness from the ground or spilled water easily passes through the mat straight into the grain resting on top.
ga: Mat ni akpɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo nu ni eshwie shi lɛ baanyɛ abote tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛbote tso ni akɛwo nɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential plant nutrient needed to build healthy green leaves and produce food for crop growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa niyenii kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season to fully begin before sowing my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain can trap seeds in hot, drying soil if the rains pause, causing the seeds to rot or dry up before they can grow roots.
ga: Tso kome ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgbiɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps soil temperatures cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa oya kɛ́ hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves scorching and turning brown during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants do not have tough leaves yet, so direct sunlight dries them out rapidly unless they are shaded by temporary companion crops like plantains.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɛ baai ni wa lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha kookoo tsei lɛ agbi oya. ja tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains lɛ eha ehiɛ edɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that nest inside the tender central growth tip of maize plants and require early treatment to protect your yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni feɔ amɛ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni esa akɛ atsa amɛ mra koni abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes develop dark, rotten black spots before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, which occurs when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or when watering is irregular while the fruit is forming.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas alongside my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, providing natural fertilizer for the maize while maximizing farm space.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli he lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo.

english: How do weeds growing near my crop roots slow down my total yield?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ aha mi yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, groundwater, and fertilizer nutrients, effectively starving your main plants and reducing crop sizes.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to use long bamboo stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight for building big tubers while keeping foliage off wet soil to prevent fungal infections.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop under the ground is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa?

english: Cassava roots are typically mature when the lower stem leaves yellow and drop off, and visible cracks appear in the soil near the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛji shishigbɛ tso lɛ kɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How can digging a water collection pool on my farm help my crops during dry days?
ga: Te nu ŋtayaa ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A collection pool traps rainwater during heavy downpours, storing moisture in the soil so your crops do not suffer from water stress during hot daytime periods when rain is scarce.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi ni abua naa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaná nu he haomɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli beni nugbɔ enɛɔ fioo lɛ.

english: How big does a water retention pond need to be to help keep my young trees healthy?
ga: Te esa akɛ nutoohe lɛ adara aha tɛŋŋ koni mi dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Even a simple small farm pond dug at the highest point of your farm can catch enough runoff water during rains to keep several young trees hydrated throughout short dry spells.
ga: Oŋmɔ mli nubu bibioo ko ni atsa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ po baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. koni akɛfee tsei bibii Tsei babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I direct rainwater towards my tree roots instead of letting it wash off my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ tsei ashishifãi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can dig shallow trenches or make soil basins around the dripline of your trees to capture running surface water and force it down into the soil near the roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Aloo feemɔ muji nubu ko ni ebɔle he. Tsei lɛ amli nu ni hoɔ lɛ buaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does manual irrigation take up so much of my time every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ heɔ mi gbi lɛ mli be babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Carrying water buckets by hand to individual plants is labor-intensive; using simple gravity-fed pipes or drip channels allows water to flow directly to your crop roots automatically while you work on other farm tasks.
ga: Nu ŋtayaai ni akɛ niji woɔ nɔ kɛyaa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo. Kɛtsɔ paipi loo drip chamber ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii Ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni otsuɔ nitsumɔi krokomɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my crops early in the morning or during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening prevents the sun from evaporating the water before the plant roots have time to draw it up.
ga: Nu ni oooha tso lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ nu lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛjie nu lɛ.

english: Why do my tree crops grow much bigger when they get consistent water compared to relying only on scattered rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daraa babaoo waa kɛ́ amɛnáa nu daa lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni egbɛ eshwa pɛ nɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: Water acts as the carrier for soil nutrients into the tree's roots; consistent moisture allows the tree to feed continuously and expand its branches, foliage, and fruit.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa koni eshɛ tsei ashishifãi ahe. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ eniji, baai, kɛ aduawai lɛ niyenii ni amɛdaraa daa.

english: What happens to my tree crops during the daytime if the soil runs completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa?

english: When the hot daytime sun heats up the farm, plants lose water through their leaves; if there is no moisture in the soil, the leaves wilt, growth stops, and the plant gets stressed.
ga: Beni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ. Tsei baatsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛjie nu. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. dalɛ kpaɔ ni tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ

english: Do young fruit trees need water managed differently than shallow-rooted crops like maize?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ he miihia nu ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, shallow crops like maize need frequent surface moisture, whereas young tree crops require water directed deeper into the soil so their deep taproots can establish firmly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tamɔ abɛi hia nu ni yɔɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Nu ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ he miihia tsei bibii koni shishifã ni mli kwɔ lɛ anyɛ ama shi shiŋŋ.

english: As my cocoa or fruit trees grow larger, do I need to change where I apply water?
ga: Kɛ mi koko tso loo aduawai lɛ eda Ani ehe miihia ni matsake he ni mikɛ nu lɛ haa lɛ?

english: Yes, as trees grow larger, their feeding roots spread outward, so you should direct water further away from the main trunk and closer to the edge of the tree's leaf canopy.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ da Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ otsi nu lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ he, ni ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa.

english: Can standing water around my crop stem cause harm, or is more water always better?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye mɔ awui? Aloo kɛ okɛ nu babaoo tsu nii Ani ehiɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: While crops need adequate water, standing pool water left touching the stem for too long can rot the roots and block oxygen, so water should be channeled near the roots rather than allowed to suffocate the stem.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ he hiaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Pool nu ni ashiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. No hewɔ lɛ ha nu lɛ aya nɔ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni oooha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize once the rains begin in April?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ April mli lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the ground is still warm and dry underneath. Wait until the soil receives two or three good rains so there is enough moisture deep down to help the seeds germinate and survive.
ga: Kaadu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi yɛ shishi. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa fioo koni eha nu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwie shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani amɛmiigboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during Harmattan to save water and protect itself from the hot, dry winds. It is not dying; the plant goes dormant and will grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Egbooo. Tso lɛ yaa wɔɔ ni ebaajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: If I cut off excess branches from my cocoa tree, will it damage the plant or help it yield more?
ga: Kɛ mifo niji ni eshwɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, Ani ebaafite kookoo tsei lɛ loo ebaaye ebua ni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Pruning does not harm the tree if done correctly. Removing dead or overcrowded branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main trunk, which prevents black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeee tso lɛ awui. Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing disease and helping the plant feed the tuber growing under the soil so it becomes large.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyeɔ bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying organic manure or a nitrogen fertilizer will turn the leaves dark green and help the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by hot dry weather, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the roots moist and adding compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo, shihilɛi ni mli egbi, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛ́ oha shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it better to burn the cleared bushes on my field or leave the dry grass on top of the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã brɔshi ni ajie lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mashi jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving the cleared weeds on top of the soil as mulch protects the ground from drying out under the hot sun and decays into natural food for your crops, whereas burning destroys beneficial soil organisms.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa onibii. yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land where I harvested cassava last year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava in the same spot continuously exhausts the soil's specific nutrients and attracts pests. Rotating your crops by planting beans or cowpeas first restores fertility back to the soil.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be, ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more plants on my small land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mihe bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small corn ears or no grain at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: How many years does a newly planted hybrid cocoa seedling take before it starts bearing its first pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani hybrid cocoa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ feɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing their first pods within 2 to 3 years after being transplanted into the field, provided they get adequate shade and protection from pests during their early growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ amɛná hulutsoo ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crop turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green leaves and capture light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛmɔmɔ la.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it back into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for the crops you plant afterward.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with very small cobs when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo futuɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely together, they compete for the same sunlight, soil water, and plant nutrients, causing them all to become weak and yield small produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu, kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni falɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce the food energy necessary to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches if you leave too many attached.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii baa kɛji oshi amɛ ni amɛdara tsɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade from plantains when they are newly planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli kɛ́ adu amɛ ehee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and easily scorched by harsh sunlight; fast-growing plants like plantains provide shelter and keep the soil moist until cocoa gets stronger.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do people spread dry grass around the roots of pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwereɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the roots, keeps moisture in the soil, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akagbi shishifãi lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When farmland stays flooded, the excessive soil moisture prevents roots from breathing oxygen, causing rot-inducing fungi to thrive in the soil.
ga: Beni nu eyi okwaayeli hei lolo Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ babaoo lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Extreme sun heat or drought stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers early to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Hulu mli dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: What is causing large holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ mli bulɛi wuji baa ni eshiɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, caterpillars that hide inside the central growing point of maize plants and eat the fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai heei.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Giving them nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in their growth helps them regain their green color and produce strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ha amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them on fully cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive strong, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a canopy, protecting the young cocoa from heat while they establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them in heavy or flat soils. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ebɔle amɛhe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too high or when water supply is irregular. Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from forming into a tomato.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa fɔfɔii amli fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ tomatoi lɛ afeemɔ naa.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my seed maize very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and space to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding on the undersides of leaves. These pests suck the plant's sap and spread plant diseases, stopping new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa koni amɛkpa tsei heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer on the farm right before a big downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes loose fertilizer off the topsoil into rivers or down deep beyond where roots can reach. It is better to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain so the plant roots can soak it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa faai amli loo shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. koni tso shishifãi lɛ abote mli

english: How do weeds actually reduce the amount of crop I harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Te jwɛi feɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight your plants need to grow. Keeping your farm clean early in the season makes sure all soil nutrients go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse mra Enɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on all their leaves to create food that gets stored in the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off damp soil where fungal diseases can easily destroy them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ oya lɛ.

english: Why does planting my crops late in the rainy season result in lower yields even if rain is still falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ haaa yibiiwoo aba lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lolo?

english: Crops need a long, consistent period of moisture and warm sunlight during their early growth stage. Planting late means your crops run out of rain right when they are filling their seeds or fruit, leading to poor yields.
ga: Tsei biɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛ dalɛ shishijee bei amli. Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ baaa onibii lɛ anɔ yɛ dumɔwui loo aduawai ni odu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under direct heat. They need shade trees or fast-growing shade crops like plantain to block harsh sunlight, cool the air, and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the center leaves of my young maize with small dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni muji bibioo ko yɛ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing whorl of the maize plant. Catching them early with appropriate sprays or natural remedies helps protect your maize before the stems are destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Abɛi ni ooomɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa loo adebɔɔ mli tsofa nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ o-abɛi lɛ he dani ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil becomes too dry, or when the soil stays too wet. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulching helps flowers stay on the plant and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper and vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops hot sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking light and food away from your plants.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ agbala la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: It is safer to wait until the rain becomes regular and penetrates deep into the soil. The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can bake seeds in hot, dry ground before they grow properly.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui agbi yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni egbi dani amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall with small harvests when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants proper space ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow fat stalks and large yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Tso he gbɛ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wood branches so my yam vines can climb on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and spreading soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛgboi ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the tips while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eshishigbɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing tips on lower leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen food up to save the newest young leaves, leaving the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen ni tsiɔ naa lɛ naa kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛbu baai bibii heei ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe. Ha baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: What is the difference between dry manure from poultry or cattle and bagged fertilizer from the store?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni jɛɔ kooloi loo tsina mli kɛ kotoku mli ŋmei ni jɛɔ shwapo mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil over a long time and keeps it soft and spongy so it holds water better. Store-bought chemical fertilizer gives plants a fast burst of food but does not build long-term soil health.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya shi ehaaa sũ lɛ aná hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmatta be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry weather as a survival trick to stop losing water through their leaves. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and resume growing tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛhi shi koni amɛkpa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: How long can I leave my cassava in the ground after it matures before it starts to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ dani ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: Cassava roots act as natural underground storage, so you can safely leave mature plants in the ground for several months up to a year. However, leaving them too long makes the roots tough, woody, and harder to process into food.
