ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oshi o-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi afi shweshweeshwe. Shi, kɛ́ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, amɛfeɔ tso, ni ewaa akɛ aaafee niyenii.

english: If I plant garden eggs, will the plants produce food for many months or just once?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli Ani tso lɛ baawo niyenii nyɔji babaoo loo shikome pɛ?

english: Garden egg plants are continuous pickers. If you keep watering them, feeding the soil, and picking the ripe fruits regularly, a single plant can keep producing new flowers and fruits month after month for up to 5 or 6 months.
ga: Egg tsei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji dɛŋdade ni akɛbuaa egg be fɛɛ be kɛji akɛ okɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, okɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni okpaa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa. Tso kome baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ kɛyashi nyɔji 5 loo 6.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep flowering and producing peppers for months while my maize only yields once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ woɔ yibii shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is a single-harvest crop that finishes its life cycle after producing cobs. Vegetables like pepper and garden eggs are continuous growers that keep flowering and producing new fruit as long as the weather and soil nutrients support them.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa shikome ni gbeɔ ewala be lɛ naa beni ewo ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ. Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii heei be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do planting beans or cowpeas make my soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings need to be planted under plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs during its early development.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl inward during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. Plants roll their leaves up during hot hours to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which prevents them from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ akafite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients. Dropping flowers allows the plant to save its energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant. It usually happens when watering is irregular, which prevents the roots from carrying calcium up into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ calcium aya tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and twisted instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, well-mounded soil to expand. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tubers cannot push through easily and will bend or remain small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni ebɔle ehe jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo. ni ani ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ebaafee bibioo lolo?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. This often happens when soil nutrients are low or after heavy rain washes them away, and applying fertilizer like urea or NPK can help fix it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo nakai niyenii lɛ sɛɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa enɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I plant seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough nourishment to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up all the plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kwraa kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ yitso ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: Why must I put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs sunlight to make energy for growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to reach the sun, preventing leaf rot and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. When the plant gets too stressed from heat and drought, it sheds flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed new tomatoes.
ga: Nɔ titri ni haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ miihao tsɔ kɛjɛ latsaa kɛ hɔmɔ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha tomatoi heei niyenii.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from young leaves. Controlling these pests early stops the leaves from twisting and keeps the plant growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekatsi ehe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why do small insects attack my cowpea flowers before the bean pods even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like flower thrips are attracted to the sweet nectar inside cowpea blossoms. Protecting the crop during the flowering stage prevents these insects from causing the flowers to fall off before bean pods can grow.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips Nibii ni yɔɔ tsina fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa amɛ. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ aba.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in cool, humid weather when there is too much shade. Pruning unnecessary branches, clearing weeds, and removing diseased pods helps air flow and stops the spread.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle he ni ekpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily in strong winds even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily if pests like stem borers or nematodes have damaged the underground roots and corm. Planting pest-free suckers and mounding soil around the base provides strong support against wind.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji kooloi tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes fite shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Adumɔ tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli kɛ sũ ni abua naa kɛbɔleɔ amɛhe Shishitoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu kpakpa.

english: Why does my rice crop grow better in flooded or very wet soil compared to dry land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in wet conditions because their roots are specially adapted to handle saturated soil, and standing water naturally smothers weeds that would otherwise steal light and fertilizer from the rice.
ga: Omɔ tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ etsɔ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛye amɛbua shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my rice field need so much water compared to my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice naturally grows best in wet or flooded soil because standing water smothers competing weeds and helps the plant roots absorb essential nutrients continuously.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why is my electricity bill so high when I use a pump to irrigate my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi srawa hewalɛ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ fa babaoo beni mikɛ pɔmp tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ?

english: Pumping water into a dry field takes many hours because dry soil acts like a sponge, absorbing huge amounts of water before the field fills up, which keeps the electric pump running longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔ ni egbi mli lɛ heɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ekɛ nu babaoo shwieɔ shi dani ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyiɔ. Enɛ haa srawa hewalɛ pɔmp lɛ tsuɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does running my water pump for extra hours automatically make my crops grow bigger?
ga: Ani nu pɔmp lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee wuji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: No, once the soil is completely soaked and covered with enough water, adding more water just wastes electricity and money without giving your crops any extra boost.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ehà nɔ. Nu babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ fiteɔ sarawa hewalɛ kɛ shika kɛkɛ ni ehaaa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know when my rice field has received enough irrigation water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Your field is fully irrigated when a thin, even layer of water covers the entire land surface and no dry patches of soil are visible.
ga: Nu shwieɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli kwraa kɛ́ nu bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni enyɛɛɛ ena shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei ni egbi

english: Should I keep water sitting on my rice farm all the way until harvest day?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha nu ahi ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli kɛyashi kpamɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: No, you should stop irrigating and drain the water out a few weeks before harvest so the rice grains can dry properly and the ground becomes firm enough for harvesting.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa nu ni okɛshwieɔ shi kɛ nu ni okɛshwieɔ shi lɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani kpamɔ lɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants start turning yellow when my irrigation water dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mi-irrigation nu lɛ gĩ lɛ?

english: Rice plants need moist soil to absorb food like nitrogen from the earth; when the soil dries out, the roots get trapped and the leaves turn yellow from hunger.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he hiaa omɔ tsei koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why does my farm absorb so much water the very first time I irrigate it in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: After a long dry spell, the soil develops deep hidden cracks and pockets that must be completely filled with water before any water can sit on top of the ground.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmeii kɛ bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. ni esa akɛ nu awo mli dani nu lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will flooding my land with water before planting help control weeds?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Yes, flooding cuts off air to land weeds and their seeds in the soil, suffocating them and making it much easier to clear a clean field for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu afua lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛduɔ jwɛi kɛ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. suffocate Ni ehaa he ni he tse ni oootsi kɛha onibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why is it important to level my farmland properly before I start irrigating my rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ jogbaŋŋ dani aje ŋmãa lɛ nɔ nu shwiemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: If your field is uneven, high spots will stay dry while low spots flood too deep, leading to wasted water, extra pumping costs, and uneven crop growth across the farm.
ga: Kɛji he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ejaaa lɛ, hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbi yɛ be mli ni hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baaho nu afua tsɔ. kɛ nu fɔŋ baa Nu ni akɛwoɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo etee ŋwɛi. ni tsei lɛ adalɛ yeee egbɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I put fertilizer on my rice field while the irrigation water is actively flowing into the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔji amli be mli ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho kɛmiiya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the water stops moving, because flowing water will wash your expensive fertilizer away into the drains before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nu lɛ baakpa nyiɛmɔ. No ji akɛ, nu ni hoɔ lɛ baajie o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ awo nu tsɔne lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do crops planted close to my house often grow faster than the ones far away on my bush farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishia lɛ masɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ mi ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil near the house naturally gets nutrients from food scraps, household sweepings, and wood ash, making it richer and better at holding moisture than cleared bush land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ oshia lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ, jwɛi kɛ tso sũ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fe hei ni ajie tsei bibii lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I improve poor soil before planting my new crop seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ dani madu tsei ahe dumɔwui heei?

english: You can mix organic matter like animal manure or well-rotted compost into the planting hole so the young roots have rich food to feed on right away.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afutu dumɔ bu lɛ mli koni eha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni amɛye amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does it take so many years for a planted mango tree to start giving fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mango ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Perennial trees like mangoes need several years to establish strong roots and build thick branches before they have enough stored energy to produce heavy fruit.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mango lɛ he miihia afii babaoo dani amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ niji ni mli wa dani amɛná hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: How do I protect my small tree seedlings from the harsh heat and sun?
ga: Mabu tso bibioo lɛ he Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mihe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: You can erect a simple shade canopy using palm fronds or grass over young seedlings to shield them from hot sunlight until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi afee ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui bibii anɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni eha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my newly planted tree seedling is actually growing well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for new green leaf shoots, bright leaf buds, and a firm stem within a few weeks of planting; these are signs the roots have settled into the soil.
ga: Taomɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. fɔfɔii ni kpɛɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ema shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo.

english: Apart from planting the trees, what other work must I do regularly on my land?
ga: Kɛfata tsei adumɔ he lɛ Mɛɛ nitsumɔ ehe miihia ni matsu lolo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa?

english: Tree farming requires continuous clearing of weeds around the base, monitoring for pests, pruning dead branches, and ensuring adequate water and nutrients.
ga: Tsei akwɛmɔ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. shishitoo ni yaa nɔ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ asɛɛdii Afolɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ amli kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around the trunk of my growing fruit tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ yibii lɛ shishifã lɛ he miihia.

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from young roots, which slows down the tree's growth and makes it weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ edaa oya, ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune branches from my fruit trees once they start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji loo majie amɛ be mli ni amɛdara momo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or diseased wood, opens up the tree for air and sunlight, and helps direct energy toward producing bigger and healthier fruit.
ga: Tsoi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Gbelemɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stop growing even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can I plant quick-growing food crops on the same piece of land while waiting for my tree crops to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping short-term crops like legumes, maize, or vegetables between young trees makes full use of space and provides food while your main trees grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ tsei bibii ateŋ. Ebaakɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baaha be mli ni otso titri lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. They need temporary shade trees, like plantain or cassava, to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. kɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the plant regain its bright green color and make healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew holes through the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that burrows into the growing central core of the maize plant. Catching them early by inspecting your field weekly allows you to apply recommended pest control methods before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oookwɛ daa otsi lɛ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsɔ nɔ akudɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the leaves above ground look very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, they focus all their energy on growing tall leaves instead of storing energy underground in the roots. Proper spacing ensures the roots have room and nutrients to swell.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ebaakɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa amɛfuɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and heap soil into mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ofee gɔji dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adu lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to grow long and thick underground without resistance. Creating soil mounds improves drainage so the seeds do not rot in heavy rain and allows air to reach the developing roots.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛdara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fiteee kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around one plant stem, they steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ Tso kome fa tsɔ. Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ awo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise planting groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally restores soil fertility, making the land richer for the next crop without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil and climate, making them very fast at absorbing available water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early stops them from crowding out your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni otsei bibii lɛ akafee mɛi babaoo.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting during the right window helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni odu yɛ samflɛ ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plantain is lacking essential soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, or it is experiencing drought. Regular weeding and applying compost or balanced fertilizer will help keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo amɛmiina hɔmɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔji ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the main stem will start to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi fãmɔ.

english: Is it good practice to plant cassava and plantain together on the same land?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ abaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and plantain works well. However, you must space them properly so their root systems do not compete fiercely for soil nutrients and water during the growing season.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akatswa akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for me to plant on a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a strong bulb—are the best choice. They grow faster, withstand harsh weather better, and produce healthier plantain bunches than broad-leaved water suckers.
ga: Sword suckers, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance kɛ yitsei ni wa lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛ daa oya. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli ni ehaa plantain panicles ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni nuɔ nu ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ

english: It is best to leave only 2 or 3 healthy suckers of different ages around the main stem. Pruning away excess suckers ensures the main plant gets enough water and nutrients to produce large fruits.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei bibii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: How long does a plantain crop take from planting until I can harvest the bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa plantain tsei lɛ?

english: Plantain usually takes between 11 to 15 months from the day you plant the sucker to the day the bunch is ready for harvest, depending on soil quality and rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ gbi ni oduɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my plantain stem falling over on its own even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by plantain root nematodes or stem borers. These pests weaken the root system and hollow out the base of the stem, causing the plant to collapse under its own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛboteɔ tso lɛ shishi. ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ shishi

english: How should I store my cut cassava stems before planting so they do not dry out?
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni afo lɛ ato tɛŋŋ koni amɛkagbi?

english: Store cassava stems upright in a cool, shaded area under a tree, with the bottom ends resting on damp soil. This keeps the stems alive and fresh for up to two weeks before planting.
ga: Too sinava tsei lɛ ahe yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ tsei ashishi. ni shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi fɛfɛo ni amɛhe feɔ ehee kɛyashiɔ otsii enyɔ dani aduɔ.

english: Why do some of my harvested cassava tubers taste bitter while others taste sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi ŋɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Bitterness in cassava is caused by higher levels of natural chemical compounds called cyanogenic glucosides. Drought stress or poor soil can increase these levels, whereas sweet cassava varieties naturally have much lower levels.
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ mli baa ji tsofai ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ cyanogen glucosides ni fa babaoo lɛ. Hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii baanyɛ aha nɛkɛ yibɔi nɛɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei henɔi ni ŋɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ yɛ nɔ ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my crop yields decrease when I plant cassava on the same soil year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava absorbs large amounts of nutrients from the soil, especially potassium. Planting it continuously on the same plot without adding manure or fertilizer drains the soil's natural fertility.
ga: Cassava ŋmɛɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ potassium Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if the crop medicine I buy from the market seller is genuine and safe to use?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Check for an official registration batch number, an unspillable safety seal, and an expiration date on the bottle. Always buy from approved agro-dealers, as fake or expired chemicals can destroy your crops instead of protecting them.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nɔmba ni aŋmalaa awoɔ wolo nɔ lɛ. Shweshweeshwefeemɔ he okadi ni shwieee shi kɛ gbi ni ekɛbaatsu nii yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Hemɔ be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni ji amale loo tsofai ni efite lɛ baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni amɛaabu amɛhe.

english: Why did my crop leaves burn and turn brown after I sprayed them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying during the hot afternoon sun causes chemicals to dry too fast and scorch leaves. It can also happen if you mix the medicine too strong or use a chemical meant for a different type of crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ agbi oya tsɔ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashã. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsɔ futu mli loo okɛ tsofai tsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding well-timed fertilizer or manure will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they face heat stress, lack of consistent watering, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil, which makes the plant focus on leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: This happens when plants receive too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer without enough phosphorus and potassium, or when side branches (suckers) are not trimmed to let energy go into fruiting.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ aha tsei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. aloo be mli ni afolɔɔɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ (tso lɛ yibii) koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha aduawai.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings fight for sunlight and stretch upward rapidly. Spacing them properly ensures strong stems and healthy branches.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei kɛ niji ni he wa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves with dark dirt in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel (whorl) and feeds on tender leaves, leaving behind dark droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli (whorl) ni amɛyeɔ baa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ esɛɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing light yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this problem.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Adumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers have dark rot and holes inside them when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii diji kɛ bu yɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by microscopic soil pests called nematodes or fungi that enter through bruised seed yams. Using clean, healthy seed yams and rotating crops keeps soil clean.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo fungi ni tsɔɔ sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ amli boteɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into fine powder while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storage insects like grain weevils burrow inside the kernels and eat them from within. Properly drying maize to a hard crunch before storing it in airtight bags prevents insect multiplication.
ga: Picker kooloi tamɔ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui amli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen or getting too much water in the soil. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea and ensuring good field drainage will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for too long, encouraging fungal diseases. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do the vines of my yam plants start drying up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miije shishi amɛgbi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by yam beetles, leaf spot diseases, or severe dry spells. Staking your vines high off the ground and managing pests keeps the leaves green so the yam tubers can grow large.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii, baa mli hela, loo ŋmeii ni mli wa waa emɔ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ wain tsei lɛ tee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni sweet potato tsei lɛ atsɔ agbo.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or pests like mirids (capsids). Providing proper shade, keeping soil moist with mulch, and controlling insect pests allow flowers to turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii (capsids), ni haa hulutsoo ni sa Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii. ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa fɔfɔi feɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over easily during light winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when pests like banana weevils or nematodes damage the underground root system. Using clean planting suckers and keeping the base of the plant clean keeps the root system strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo nematodes fite shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ sucker ni he tse tsu nii ni oha shishitoo lɛ he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifã lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, rotten spots on the bottom of the fruit while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Watering your tomato plants consistently and adding agricultural lime to the soil prevents these dark spots.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ lime wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil or recommended insecticides controls these pests so healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ koni tsei ahe tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy rains have deeply soaked the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the dry weather returns for a week.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsi kome.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, holds water in the soil longer, stops weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the ground as it rots.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Can I put fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop to make it grow faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against the stem will burn and damage the plant. It is best to place fertilizer in a ring a few inches away from the stem so the roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ ŋtayaa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or leaves the roots standing in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni efee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shishifãi lɛ damɔ nu babaoo mli.

english: Why does my yam crop produce huge leafy vines above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ wain tsei wuji ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the yam plant puts all its energy into growing big green leaves on top instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Atomɔ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi eŋɔlii yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions during heavy rains when air cannot move freely through the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji amli oya lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms always attack the inner funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli gbɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The worms hide inside the tight center leaves of the corn plant because it keeps them safe from bird predators and hot sunlight while they eat the softest part of the plant.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ okpoi ni yeɔ amɛ awui kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ahe beni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored grains develop small holes and turn to powder after just a few months in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ ni ekɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ

english: Weevils and insects lay tiny, invisible eggs on the grain before harvest or during drying. Once inside the storage bag, the eggs hatch into insects that eat the inside of the grains.
ga: Kplukai kɛ kooloi bibii woɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ dumɔwui anɔ dani akpaa loo yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Beni yɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ Awui lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when water is irregular, or when there is not enough wind or insects to shake the pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akpokpo pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and stop growing during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from intense heat and conserve moisture, but leaf curl can also be caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant sap.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi. Shi kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ aba.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and stay alive until the rains return, at which point it quickly grows new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaajie baai heei oya.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts together in the same farm with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the cassava and keeps the ground covered so weeds cannot grow easily.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji ŋmei niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ oya

english: Why does the witchweed plant only show up in fields where I grow maize or sorghum?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ witchweed jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmɔji ni miduɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Witchweed seeds lie asleep in the dirt for years and only wake up when they smell chemical signals released by the roots of cereal crops like maize, which they then attach to and feed on.
ga: Witchweed dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. ni eteɔ shi pɛ kɛji enu tsofafeemɔ he okadii ni jɛɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he ni ayeɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jieɔ lɛ he.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient maize needs to grow strong. It can also happen if the soil holds too much water, which smothers the roots and prevents them from feeding.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa adara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and get light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are symptoms of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. Using disease-free stems for planting and removing sick plants early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ ŋmeii ni hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛji oodu ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing shade trees like plantains and keeping the soil covered helps retain moisture so flowers stay on to produce pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛwoɔ shade mli kɛ mulching ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Yams grow crooked or small when the soil is too hard and compact, or when tiny pests in the soil attack the growing root. Building soft, high mounds or ridges gives the tubers loose soil to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo bibioo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutua shishifãi ni miida lɛ. Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ yitso lɛ afee mlɛo ni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baashɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn the delicate stem and roots if placed directly against them. It should be placed in a small ring a few inches away from the stem so the roots can absorb it safely through moist soil.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni waaa lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛma shi shiŋŋ. Okɛ amɛ awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and low humidity pull moisture rapidly out of plant leaves. To survive without drying out, plants slow down their growth to save their remaining water and energy.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ gbalaa hulutsoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Bɔni afee ni Tsei ahi shi ni amɛgbiŋ lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why should I wait until the main rains start before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ abɔi nɛmɔ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Seeds planted in dry ground can rot or sprout briefly and wither under the hot sun before rain arrives. Waiting for steady rains ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to sprout and establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli. ni egboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani nugbɔ lɛ baa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny worms or weevils eat away the roots and the underground bulb, destroying the tree's anchor in the soil. Without healthy roots, the heavy top easily topples the tree.
ga: Dumɔwui shwieɔ shi kɛji ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii gboi. Ye shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ lɛ Yiteŋ ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ shi mlɛo.

english: Why are caterpillars hiding inside the top funnel of my young maize plants and eating the new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, and they hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant because it is moist and safe from predators. They chew on young leaves before they unfold, which damages the plant's growth.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛmli edɔ ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo. ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the ears are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which crops need to stay green and build energy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the stems helps the plant green up and yield better.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaafata he lɛ He tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What happens to my crops if I pluck too many leaves off them while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mijie baai babaoo kɛjɛ mli be mli ni amɛmiida lolo lɛ?

english: Taking off too many leaves—often called over-priming—weakens the plant because leaves act like tiny solar panels that make food. Removing too many leaves starves the plant, causing slow growth and smaller harvests.
ga: Baai babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ over-priming. Ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii. ni tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee niyenii Kɛ́ ajie baai babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Ehaa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting plantains next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the strong sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that create shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa plants survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are there small holes all over my cassava leaves, and will my tubers still grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ amɛyitsei fɛɛ lɛ? Ani yitsei lɛ baafee wuji lolo?

english: Holes in cassava leaves are usually caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating the plant. If too many leaves are damaged, the plant cannot feed itself properly, which results in smaller tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ cassava baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛji baai lɛ efite tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aye amɛhe niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and weak instead of strong and sturdy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight. They stretch upwards too fast trying to get light, making the stems thin and easy for strong winds to blow down.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe oya tsɔ bɔni afee ni amɛha la aba. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa lɛ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees curl up and dry out during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry harmattan weather, trees lose moisture quickly through their leaves. Cocoa leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to dry winds and conserve water inside the plant.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ harmattan Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baa shi lɛ shi, ni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat or water stress, such as sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil regularly watered and using organic mulch keeps the root zone cool so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ he, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ organic mulch ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why is my farm giving me smaller cassava roots this year compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii shishifãi fioo pɛ yɔɔ afi nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cassava takes nutrients out of the soil each season. Planting on the same soil without adding organic manure or letting the land rest exhausts the nutrients, resulting in smaller yields over time.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ gbɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll upwards during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves roll upwards in high heat to protect themselves from losing water too fast. It is a natural self-defense action, but watering the crop early in the morning helps prevent permanent heat damage.
ga: Akɛ tomato baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ la ni mli wa nɔ koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ obu ohe he. Shi kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hulutsoo akafite amɛ daa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting fast once I bring them home from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli miba lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvesting or stored in a warm, airless space. Keeping them on raised bamboo racks in a shaded, well-ventilated barn allows wounds to heal and prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni pilamɔi lɛ atsa ni ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from harsh heat and keep the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Bɔni afee ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Small insects called stem borers or root pests can also weaken the base, so propping the trees up with strong wooden poles stops them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers loo shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans and groundnuts in the field before your maize helps bring back their dark green color and health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo adu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry ground around my pepper plants with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi aha he ni egbi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture so you water less, cools the roots down, and rots over time into natural manure.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my cassava help both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi-cassava lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen food directly from the air and store it in the soil. This extra food feeds the cassava roots, while groundnut leaves carpet the ground to stop weeds from taking over.
ga: Peanuts gbalaa niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain sits in the field without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows water mold to rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni nu lɛ efooo Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha nu mli ŋmeii lɛ agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: The first rain often heats up dry soil without soaking deep enough, which can burn fragile seeds. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures the soil stays wet enough to keep young seeds alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ashã. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: What causes tiny worms to eat holes through the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ni yɔɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that lay eggs inside the growing shoots of young maize. Catching them early and spraying approved treatments or neem leaf water stops them before they destroy the stem.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem baa mli nu afɔ nɔ. baatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ shishi.

english: Leaf curl happens when tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feed on the leaves and pass a virus into the plant. Controlling these tiny insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Leaf curl baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ye baai lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ mli. ŋmeii bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when there are no bees around to move pollen between flowers. Regular watering and gentle shade during hot mid-days help fruit form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ lɛ nu daa kɛ hulutsoo gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct Ghanaian sunlight burns their soft leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides a cool umbrella that protects them until their roots are deep and strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, Ghana hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe waa.

english: Why do I need to clear away most of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the mother plant. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main stem gets enough food to grow large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for green leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and build large corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔlii lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi ŋmɔji amli ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside or after maize enriches the soil with natural food, reducing the need for expensive artificial fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: How does spreading dry grass over my vegetable beds help my plants during the dry season?
ga: Te jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so water doesn't dry up quickly in the heat. Over time, the dry grass decays and turns into rich plant food.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni ebafeɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices out of the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Spraying the leaves early with neem oil or mild soapy water helps kill the pests and stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ Mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ekpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes right in the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the growing tip of young maize plants. Checking your farm early and placing a small handful of clean sand, wood ash, or safe botanical pesticides into the plant's funnels can destroy the pest.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo, tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe awo tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmei lɛ hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience extreme heat stress, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the root level early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tomato nɔ nu daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture energy. Lifting the vines off the wet ground also prevents leaf fungal diseases and allows the tubers beneath the ground to swell up bigger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does water stay on top of my land for days after it rains, and will it kill my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni ani ebaakpãtã midumɔ nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: When soil is too packed or full of clay, rainwater cannot sink into the ground. Standing water chokes crop roots by cutting off air, which causes roots to rot and plants to die.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nu nyɛŋ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ gbeɔ tsei shishifãi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: What crops can I plant on the parts of my farm that always get flooded during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Crops like swamp rice, cocoyam, and sugarcane handle wet soil well, unlike cocoa, maize, or cassava, which rot easily when submerged in water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, kookoo kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ, etamɔɔɔ kookoo, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. ni fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo nu mli

english: How can I stop heavy rains from gathering and destroying the plants on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekabua tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa ni efite amɛ?

english: You can dig simple drainage channels or shallow gutters across your farm to guide excess water away from your crop roots and off the land.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ loo nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ koni ejie nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi amli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Do I need to clear all my food crops like cassava and plantain before I plant new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie niyenii tsei fɛɛ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei dani madu kookoo tsei heei?

english: No, you do not need to clear them all. Food crops like plantains provide necessary shade for young cocoa plants while giving you food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ojie fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. Niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade trees to protect them from heat, keep the air humid, and prevent the soil from drying out.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hɔɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi

english: Is it safer for me to farm only cocoa or mix it with other food crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikome too matsu kookoo loo mikɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ baafata he?

english: Mixing cocoa with food crops is safer because it gives you food and money while waiting years for cocoa to produce, and protects your income if cocoa prices drop or pests attack.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ kookoo futu niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ afii babaoo dani kookoo lɛ baawo yibii. ni obu oshika ni onáa lɛ he kɛji akɛ kookoo jara ba shi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai batutua bo.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is good for cocoa before I waste my money planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani mafite shika yɛ nɔ?

english: Good cocoa land has deep, soft soil that lets water drain easily, is sheltered by moderate shade, and never stays flooded after heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa nu hoɔ oya. Eyɛ shade ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ. ni nu afua eshɛko ehe pɛŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: If heavy machinery or many people crush the ground on my farm, how does it harm my crops?
ga: Kɛji tsɔnei ni tsii loo mɛi babaoo shwie shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Te ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy weight presses the soil tight and destroys air space underground. Hard ground makes it difficult for plant roots to grow deep and absorb nutrients.
ga: Muji ni tsii lɛ nyɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa ni efiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ shɔŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop turn yellow when there is too much water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water prevents roots from taking in air and nutrients from the soil. The leaves turn yellow because the crop is suffocating and starving.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye amɛ.

english: High moisture and lack of sunlight cause the Black Pod fungus to spread. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight in and helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ haa blackpod fungus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la abote mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow leaves. Heavy rains can wash this food deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee wuji.

english: Will putting twice the recommended amount of fertilizer on my crops make them produce twice as fast?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha efee oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer can burn the roots and dry out the plant, similar to giving too much medicine to a baby. Following the recommended dose gives the crop just the right amount of food to grow strong without harming its roots.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha tso lɛ agbi. Etamɔ tsofa babaoo ni akɛhaa abifao. Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee eshishifãi lɛ.
