english: Young cocoa plants are like small children—their tender leaves get scorched easily under intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or larger canopy trees to shield them from high heat and retain soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii. Ebaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant proper spacing allows every stem to get enough food to develop large, full cobs instead of thin, weak ones.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ. Mohu ɔ, niji ɔmɛ ngɛ gbɔjɔɔ nɛ a he wa we.

english: Why do insects keep attacking my tomato plants as soon as the flowers start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi tomato tsei lɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je shishi amɛjie amɛhe kpo pɛ?

english: Flowers release sweet scents and bright colors that attract insects looking for nectar and places to lay eggs. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or neem oil early protects the blossoms so they can turn into healthy tomato fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ahe muji ni ŋɔɔ kɛ amɛhe sui ni kpɛɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni taoɔ nu kɛ he ni amɛwoɔ amɛwɔlɔi lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooofɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ lɛ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes the roots of my yam tubers to rot underwater during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yam roots rot when excess water stays around the soil for too long, cutting off oxygen to the tubers. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy and dry.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers grow out of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience sudden stress, such as extreme heat, very dry soil, or too much strong fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Why are my crop yields smaller when I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest instead of new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du dumi ehehi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved over seasons lose their strength over time and can carry diseases from old plants. Certified seeds are specially selected to resist common local pests and grow evenly to yield more food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ tsei momo amli lɛ aba. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛha niyenii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my land is ready for planting cassava after the long dry season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmei yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: The ground is ready when the first heavy rains break open the hard dirt and soak deep into the earth. Planting cassava stems while the soil is still baked dry will cause the cuttings to dry out before roots can sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwie shi ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ miiho lolo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tsei lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Why does my cassava yield small tubers if I harvest it early during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akpa mra yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, cassava puts most of its energy into producing green stems and fresh leaves rather than storing food underground. Waiting until the right maturity window allows the tubers to store starch and grow thick.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ baai heei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi Mɛɛ kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔji lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛmlilɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the right season to plant my plantains so that the shoots do not dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu plantains? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi?

english: Plantains need a lot of water when they are young. It is best to plant them at the beginning of the major rainy season around March or April, or early in the minor rainy season (Adɔbrɛpɛ), so the roots can establish before the dry season comes.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains beni amɛdarako lɛ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni adu lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ shishijee mli, aaafee March loo April. loo fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli (Adɔbrɛpɛ) koni shishifãi anyɛ akwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why does planting crops at the exact same time my parents used to plant no longer work for me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni mifɔlɔi duɔ lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: The weather patterns are changing over time, causing rainfall seasons (Asesa) to become unpredictable. Relying solely on old calendar months can cause crops to fail, so it is now safer to wait until the rains become steady before planting.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ nugbɔ be (Asesa) lɛ mli. Kalanda nyɔji momo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii akafite. No hewɔ lɛ amrɔ nɛɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani odu nii.

english: What is the difference between the main rainy season and the minor season for growing crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ nɔ ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana lɛ teŋ?

english: The main rainy season brings heavier, longer rains suitable for slow-growing crops like cassava and yam. The minor season (Adɔbrɛpɛ) has lighter, shorter rains best suited for quick-maturing crops, vegetables, and establishing plantain suckers.
ga: Nugbɔ be titri lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Be ni ji enyɔ (Adɔbrɛpɛ) lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo, ni eshɛɛɛ kuku. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. ni amɛto plantain tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my young plantain trees turning yellow during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water quickly in the sun. Yellowing during dry periods means the plant is thirsty and heat-stressed, which can be prevented by covering the base of the plant with dry organic mulch to trap soil moisture.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛhe lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Yellow yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni eyɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishi ni akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni akɛbaatsu nii koni ekɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my soil moist for my crops when the rain stops earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or cocoa husks. This layer acts as a blanket that blocks the sun from drying out the dirt, keeping the soil cool and moist for much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa muji akagbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What type of manure is best to help my plantains produce big bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni baaye abua mi plantains lɛ ni amɛwo jwɛi wuji?

english: Decomposed poultry manure or well-rotted cow dung is excellent for plantains. They need high amounts of potassium and nitrogen, which organic manure provides to help them grow thick stems and large fruit bunches.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi kɛha dumɔwui. Potassium kɛ nitrogen babaoo he miihia amɛ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haa amɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai tsei wuji.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when I plant many of them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their large leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Spacing them about 3 meters apart ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni amɛbaji wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. He ni jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadara yɛ kui wuji amli.

english: How should I prepare a plantain sucker before planting it in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ masaa plantain tsei lɛ ahe tɛŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should trim off the old roots and peel away damaged outer layers of the corm (the bulb at the bottom) to remove hidden pests like root worms. Leaving the sucker in the sun for a day or dipping it in hot water helps ensure clean growth.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ shishifãi momoi lɛ ni ojie tsei lɛ asɛɛ fã ni efite lɛ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ mli gbi kome loo okɛ amɛ awo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni amɛdara ni amɛhe tse.

english: This usually happens because tiny worms called nematodes or stem-boring weevils are eating the roots and underground bulb. Without healthy roots, the plant loses its grip in the soil and falls under the weight of its own leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ miiye shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ ni egbeeɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaai lɛ ashishi.

english: Can I plant maize or vegetables inside my new plantain farm during the minor season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ plantain ŋmɔ hee mli yɛ sɛkɛndre be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, intercropping short-season crops like beans or maize with young plantains works well while the plantains are small. The shorter crops provide quick food and harvest before the plantain leaves grow big enough to shade the ground completely.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmeii bibii baadu lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ haa niyenii baa oya ni akpaa dani plantain baai lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food. It means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong, or that heavy rain has washed the food away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii he foomɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eho niyenii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it dangerous to place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baawo ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong, like salt. If it touches the soft stem directly, it draws out moisture and burns the skin of the plant, which can weaken or kill it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he wa waa tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛji akɛ eta tso lɛ tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni eshãa tso lɛ hewolo. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ gbɔjɔmɔ loo gbele aba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their stems compete with each other for sunlight and their roots fight for food in the soil, resulting in thin stems and very small tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Ashishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii waa baa.

english: Cowpeas are natural soil fixers. Their roots capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, which feeds the maize and keeps your land fertile for longer.
ga: Cowpea ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni kɛ nibii kpaa gbee. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that spread plant sicknesses, or by extreme heat when the plant is trying to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli beni tsei miitao ni amɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and tough by nature, so they act fast to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crop roots have time to spread out and establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli jwɛi ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛtsuɔ nii oya koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛbaalɛɛ amɛmli ni amɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before they can form pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they get stressed by dry weather, lack essential soil food like potassium, or get attacked by sap-sucking insects during early flowering.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni bɛ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni jeɔ shishi mra lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; their roots stay close to the topsoil. When heavy bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and easy for wind to push over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ shwere yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná muji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough water before I put my seeds in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds together without dropping water or crumbling straight into dry dust, the moisture level is right for seed germination.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni nu ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli loo efo mli ni etsɔ powda ni egbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: How do I know that my cassava underground tubers are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground right around the base of the main stem begins to crack upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do I have to cut down my cocoa trees when only a few leaves are showing sick yellow marks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo kookoo tso lɛ? He ni baai fioo komɛi pɛ yɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Even if only a few leaves show symptoms, diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot are already deep inside the tree's roots and stem. Removing the affected tree completely prevents the virus from spreading through mealybugs to the rest of your farm and destroying your overall yield.
ga: Kɛji baai fioo ko pɛ jie okadii kpo po lɛ, helai tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ eshɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ momo. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akatsɔ mealybugs nɔ egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my plants are dying from a disease or just drying up from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela miigbe mitso lɛ loo hulu lɛ miigbi kɛkɛ?

english: Plants suffering from heat will perk back up in the cool evening or early morning after watering. If a plant stays wilted, spotty, or yellow even during cool hours, it is infected with a disease or root problem rather than just reacting to sunshine.
ga: Tsei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli po lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hela loo naagba ko yɛ eshishifãi ahe moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ko kɛkɛ kɛji hulu la lɛ tso lɛ.

english: Yam rot is caused by tiny soil pests called nematodes or fungi that thrive in overly wet, poorly drained soil. Planting on raised mounds and selecting clean seed yams stops these hidden organisms from ruining your harvest.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni egbo baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo fungi lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ ni ohala ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land yield fewer cassava tubers now than it did a few years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe afii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when the same crop is grown on it repeatedly without resting or replacing lost nutrients. Cassava draws heavy food from the earth, so rotating with legumes or adding organic manure restores soil power.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ejɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ atsake Cassava gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the bottom while the top is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen food in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in their growth keeps the whole plant dark green and productive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Is it safe to keep planting seeds saved from my previous harvest every single year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato daa afi?

english: Saving seeds continuously over many seasons causes the crop line to weaken, yielding smaller harvests and becoming more vulnerable to local pests. Refreshing your farm with certified seeds gives you stronger plants and better income.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo kɛ oshara ni jɛɔ jɛmɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni shika ni anáa lɛ hu aya hiɛ.

english: Where do the caterpillars eating my young maize leaves come from every season?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ jɛɔ daa be mli?

english: These caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, hatch from eggs laid by night-flying moths that travel long distances on the wind. Checking leaf undersides early helps catch them before they devour the growing center of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ, fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii ni foɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ amɛ dani amɛye tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I weed around my crops even when the crops are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe, kɛji tsei lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo po?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, moisture, and root space from your crops no matter how tall the crop gets. They also harbor destructive insect pests that transfer diseases directly into your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni amɛkwɔ ha. Amɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa onibii titrii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hu jɛɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by hot, dry soil or extreme temperatures. Mulching the soil with dried grass keeps the roots cool and moist so the flowers turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi loo hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Black bottom spots, called blossom end rot, happen when tomato plants cannot draw enough calcium from dry soil. Irrigating regularly and evenly prevents this damage and saves your market value.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa ni afeɔ daa lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa ni eye ebua ni oha jara ni oyɔɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they get direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. They require partial shade from fast-growing companion crops like plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nanemɛi tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green, healthy leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are fully grown underground and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack upward due to the expanding tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and collapse just as they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: This sudden collapse is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial wilt. These microscopic germs block water from moving up the plant stem, causing the entire vine to wilt even when the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo muawai ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ gbee shi trukaa nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi bibii nɛɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa wain tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or beans in the same field as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they share this natural soil food, helping the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛjaraa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: The first rain is often a 'false start' followed by a dry spell. If you plant too soon, the seeds will germinate, but the hot, dry soil in the following weeks will wither the young sprouts before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale shishijee’ ni nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi yɛ otsii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ Kɛ́ oya shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba.

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to create food for the underground tubers. Raising the vines on stakes keeps the foliage spread out, increases yield, and prevents rotting from sitting on damp ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni ehaaa efite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: This practice is called mulching. The dry grass shades the topsoil from the scorching sun, keeps moisture trapped in the dirt for longer, and stops wild weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekaha obɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small cobs if I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots crowd each other and fight for the exact same pool of soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to make big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui shishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ, hulu la, kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do tiny beetles start eating my stored maize grains even when I store them inside a dry bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ebɔi mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yeli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni egbi amli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weevils often lay tiny eggs inside the grain cobs while they are still standing in the field. Once harvested and kept warm indoors, those hidden eggs hatch into insects that eat the stored grain unless treated or kept in airtight containers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ dumɔwui akui lɛ amli beni amɛdamɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akpa ni akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ, nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛto lɛ. ja atsu he nii loo akɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli

english: When I clear all the bushes off my land before planting, why shouldn't I burn them all?
ga: Shikome pɛ mijieɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ. Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mashã fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter that feeds your crops and dries out the soil. Leaving cleared leaves and grass to rot (mulching) retains moisture and enriches the soil naturally.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi (mulch) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep wilting and turning yellow when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves are delicate and their roots are shallow. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat stress while getting established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu mli ekɔɔɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he be mli ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: No, planting too close forces the maize plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller or missing corn cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛlaajeɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when I plant them near the valley where water stays after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ jɔɔ ko ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ masɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. Standing water suffocates the roots and encourages fungal rot, so cassava grows better on well-drained or sloped land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ loo yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the ground, which naturally fertilizes the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that feed on plant sap and spread viruses, preventing healthy fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tso mli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to settle before planting my seeds instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell. If seeds sprout right after the first rain and no water follows for days, the young seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni nu bɛ gbii babaoo. Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers allows the main plant to produce a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to build high mounds of earth before planting my yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to expand downwards easily. Mounds keep the soil loose, improve air circulation around roots, and prevent waterlogging.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi oya. Gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year when I plant the same crop over and over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil faster than nature can replace them. Rotating crops or resting the land lets the soil rebuild its fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ atsake amɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: When maize plants are packed too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This causes them to grow tall and weak with small or empty ears instead of big, healthy corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ toi bibii loo nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: What happens if I bury my bean seeds too deep in the dirt when planting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-beans lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they run out of energy trying to push up through the heavy soil before reaching sunlight, which causes them to rot or die underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ etsɔ ŋwɛi dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I don't give them shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mikɛ hulutsoo haaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Shade crops like plantains protect them from high heat and retain moisture in the air until the trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he waaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot dry spells to save water and keep the roots alive underground. As soon as the rains return, fresh green leaves will grow back.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai eŋɔli heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy in the afternoon heat even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot days, pepper leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. The plant temporary wilts to save water and will usually recover by the evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei baagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely high or when they suffer from uneven watering, because the plant tries to protect itself rather than spend energy making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ miitao ebu ehe moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant groundnuts on the land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they feed nitrogen into the soil naturally. This enriches the ground and acts like natural fertilizer for the maize crop planted in the next season.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛhaa nitrogen lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them lets the main stem grow faster and produce larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ada oya ni ewo plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: How do weeds harm my tomato crops if they are just growing next to them?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi tomato tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi?

english: Weeds steal the plant food, water, and sunlight that your tomatoes need to grow, while also providing a hiding place for insects and diseases that can destroy your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tso lɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otomoi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai náa he ko ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe. ni baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize leaves while leaving nearby cassava untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ miifite mi-corn tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ yucca tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛtaaa amɛhe lɛ?

english: Armyworms prefer cereal crops like maize because of their sweet, tender leaves and stems, whereas cassava leaves contain natural chemicals that armyworms cannot easily digest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele yɛ amɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋɔɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahewɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii nyɛŋ aŋɔ mli mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii baai amli.

english: How many days should I wait to see my crop seeds start coming out of the ground after planting?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni mana aduawai dumɔwui ni je shishi amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most seeds like maize, beans, or pepper will start sprouting and showing above the soil within 4 to 10 days after planting, provided the soil is warm and moist.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, baaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbaaje kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 10 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant my crops during the major rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant right after the first two or three heavy, steady rains begin—usually around March or April in southern Ghana—so the seeds get enough soil moisture to germinate properly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ, bei pii lɛ yɛ March loo April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ ana shikpɔŋ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my seeds do not sprout after two weeks in the soil, does it mean they are dead?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ ni mikɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ hu? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egboi?

english: Yes, if seeds do not emerge within 14 days, they have likely rotted from too much dampness, been eaten by insects, or dried out due to heat, and you will need to re-plant that area.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ gbii 14 mli lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo hewɔ. ŋmeii yeɔ loo egbiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ Ni ehe baahia ni okɛ nakai he lɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I pour plenty of water on my seeds every single day while waiting for them to sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse nu babaoo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ daa gbi be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You should keep the soil lightly damp, but do not flood it with water every day, because soaking the seeds too much starves them of air and makes them rot underground.
ga: Esa akɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ fioo. Shi kaahã nu afua miiho daa gbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ amɛmli, ni ebaaha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted pawpaw tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani papaya tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Most high-yielding pawpaw varieties will begin flowering within 5 to 6 months after planting, and you can start picking ripe fruits around 8 to 10 months.
ga: Papaya henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi yɛ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Ni obaanyɛ oje aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anaabuamɔ shishi yɛ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 mli.

english: Do I plant pawpaw seeds directly into my main field or raise them in nursery bags first?
ga: Ani miduɔ papaya dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo miduɔ yɛ dumɔwui kotokui amli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is better to start pawpaw seeds in nursery bags for about 6 to 8 weeks so you can protect the delicate young shoots from severe sun and pests before moving them to the field.
ga: Esa akɛ aje papaya dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii amli aaafee otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 ni eho nɛ bɔni afee ni onyɛ obu ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe dani okɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ mli.

english: Can I plant pawpaw during the dry season, or must I wait for the rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu papaya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: You can plant pawpaw in the dry season only if you have irrigation or a reliable water source to water them daily; otherwise, wait for the early rainy season so the young roots do not dry up.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu papaya yɛ hulutsoo be mli pɛ kɛji oyɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ daa gbi. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, mɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee koni shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: How long after my pawpaw tree produces flowers will the fruit be ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eho kɛjɛ be mli ni mi papaya tso lɛ ewo fɔfɔi? No hewɔ lɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Once small green pawpaw fruits appear after flowering, it takes about 4 to 5 months for them to fully swell and show the first yellow spots that mean they are ready to harvest.
ga: Beni paw paw yibii bibioo ni ji eŋɔli lɛ Jeɔ kpo yɛ fɔfɔii ni ewo lɛ sɛɛ. Ebaahe aaafee nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 5 dani ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa ni ejie eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi lɛ akpo, ni tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he ni ebaakpa.

english: How will I know that my tomato plants are about to start producing fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miibɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Your tomato plants will first show small, bright yellow flowers along the stems; once these flowers fall off, small green fruit bubbles will start growing in their place.
ga: O tomato tsei lɛ baatsɔɔ fɔfɔi bibii. Yellow ni kpɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ Kɛ́ fɔfɔi nɛɛ gbee shi lɛ, aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baabɔi edamɔ moŋ

english: How can I tell if my cassava stems underground are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a long bare main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni obaanyɛ ole be ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni eshiɔ tso titri kakadaŋŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava beside them provides protection from direct sun heat and keeps the moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they compete with it for food, fertilizer, and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main plant yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Is it necessary for me to put sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsei niji awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yams lifts their leaves toward the sunlight so the plant can make food efficiently. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also prevents foliage diseases and results in larger tuber growth beneath the soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potatoes lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai helai anaa, ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: The best planting material comes from the mature, woody middle section of a healthy cassava stem. Avoid the soft green top section and the overly hard bottom, cutting pieces with clear, healthy buds pointing upward when planted.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso mli lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishi ni wa tsɔ lɛ he. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛji adu.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the tips down to the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves. Applying organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ okɛ organic compost loo nitrogen fertilizer tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do groundnuts form under the ground when the flowers open above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated on the stem above ground, the plant grows small stalks called pegs that bend down and push themselves deep into the soil. Once buried, the tips swell up to form the groundnut pods.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ewo ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko. atsɛɔ lɛ pins Ni baabɔle ehe ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afu lɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ naa baafu aahu kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋshɔŋloo.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny pests like mites or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by uneven watering. Spraying neem oil or organic insecticide and maintaining steady watering helps prevent leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baashwie nɔ ni akɛ nu aha daa lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving the plants steady water and mulching the base helps keep the soil moisture balanced so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni aduawai aba.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains specific nutrients rapidly and allows maize-loving pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ oya. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops receive all the nourishment available.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How do I know when my pineapple is ready to harvest so it does not rot on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei ko eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni egboŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A pineapple is ready for harvesting when the skin at the base starts changing from green to a light golden-yellow color and smells sweet. If you harvest it when it is completely green, it will not get any sweeter after being cut.
ga: Afee klalo akɛ abaakpa pineapple kɛji akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛbatsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse ni eŋɔɔɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ beni amɛfee ŋmɔji kwraa lɛ, Ebaafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fe nɛkɛ beni afolɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant the shoots from my old pineapple plant instead of planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmei tsei momo amli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui?

english: Pineapple seeds grow very slowly and often produce weak or unpredictable fruits. Planting the small shoots (called suckers or slips) from an existing plant gives you faster growth and guarantees sweet fruit just like the parent plant.
ga: Pineapple dumɔwui lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. ŋmeii bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers loo suckers) ni ooodu kɛjɛ tso ko ni yɔɔ momo mli lɛ baaye abua bo ni oda oya ni aná nɔmimaa akɛ ebaawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why are my pineapples turning yellow and soft on one side while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ efã kome be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by sunburn from long hours of intense sunlight. Farmers often cover the growing pineapples with dry grass or wrap them with their own leaves to shade the fruit while it ripens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe loo amɛkɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛha aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my ginger plant turn yellow and dry up after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ginger tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: When ginger plants reach 8 to 10 months old, yellowing and dying leaves are a natural sign that the underground ginger roots are fully mature and ready for harvest, not that the plant is sick.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Jeee akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do my ginger roots turn soft and rot underground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ginger roots rot when water settles around them for too long because stagnant water starves the roots of air and attracts soil fungi. Planting ginger in raised beds or well-drained soil prevents water from standing.
ga: Ginger shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ saatso ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ naa.

english: Can I grow ginger under the shade of my bigger fruit trees or does it need full sun?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ginger yɛ aduawai tso agbo ko shishi? Aloo oosumɔ hulu la babaoo?

english: Ginger grows very well in partial shade under taller fruit trees because harsh, direct sunlight can burn its leaves and dry out the topsoil too quickly.
ga: Ginger kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ aduawai tsei kakadaji ashishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why are tiny green oranges dropping off my tree before they grow into big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tangerine bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ aduawai wuji lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit when they do not get enough water, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium. The tree sheds extra fruit to save energy for the remaining ones.
ga: Orange tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baawo yibii krokomɛi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my orange tree curling up and developing shiny white lines on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling with shiny lines is caused by leafminer pests—tiny insect larvae that tunnel inside the leaf tissue. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or soap water helps protect new shoots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni linei ni kpɛɔ lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii heei ahe.

english: Why do my pineapples taste very sour in some harvest seasons and very sweet in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ kpamɔɔ bei komɛi amli, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ ekrokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pineapples produce sugars using bright sunshine during their final weeks of growth. If rain or cloudy weather occurs right before harvest, the fruits store less sugar and end up tasting sour.
ga: Pineapple kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ sugar yɛ amɛnaagbee otsii ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ loo atatu eba dani akpa yibii lɛ toɔ sugar fioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is the best way to handle my harvested fruits so they do not spoil quickly on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsu mikpamɔ lɛ he nii? Bɔni afee ni ekafite oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fruits spoil quickly when bruised because cracks in the skin let air and rot in. Harvest them gently with clean tools, leave a small stem attached, and keep them in cool, shaded crates away from direct heat.
ga: Yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ ejaakɛ hewolo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Kɛ nibii ni he tse akpa nii blɛoo. Shi tso bibioo ko ni okɛto adeka ko ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli ni la akatswa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. When soil food runs low, the plant takes nitrogen from its old lower leaves and moves it up to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the stems grow very tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or soft moisture, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of sending food down into the ground to swell the starchy roots.
ga: Be mli ni nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa zugba a mi konɛ e ha nɛ shishifãhi nɛ a ngɛ starch ɔ mi ɔ nɛ fu.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up like little cups and stop producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni okpa yibiiwoo feemɔ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like mites or thrips that suck the sap from under the leaves. This damages the leaf tissue and can spread viruses that stop the plant from making flowers and peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ amli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni haa tsei lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ naa lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the stem before any tomato fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, poor watering, or lack of nutrients like calcium. If the plant feels it cannot support growing seeds, it sheds the flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ mli lɛ, kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ enyɛŋ edu dumɔwui. Ebaafɔse efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I clear away all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees and plantain plants trap moisture and block high heat, giving cocoa the cool environment it needs to grow healthy roots during its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ Shade tsei kɛ plantains hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhaa hulutsoo baa waa. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my garden eggs grow very long, weak stems without fruits when planted directly under giant timber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa lɛ? Tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Vegetable crops like garden eggs need direct sunlight to produce food for flowers and fruit. Under dense tree shade, they spend all their energy stretching upward to search for sunlight, leaving no energy to grow strong stems or produce vegetables.
ga: Aduawai tsei, tamɔ abɔɔ mli wɔji, he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha amɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛtao hulu la. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ tsei ni wa loo akɛbaawo aduawai.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves during peak heat to shrink the surface area exposed to the sun. This is a survival trick that reduces water loss through evaporation so the plant stays hydrated until the cool evening.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaawoo ni haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the mound when the rain becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gɔji amli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soil that lets air circulate around their roots. When heavy rains fill the soil with water for days without proper drainage, the tuber suffocates from lack of air and rots due to fungal attack.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tubers lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ fitemɔ mli yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls free nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural nitrogen left behind.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield every year after heavy rains wash over the sloping areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eha gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away the topsoil, which is the rich, dark layer of dirt containing most of the organic matter and plant nutrients. Without topsoil protection, your crops struggle to find nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ tsei amli niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji abuuu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ he Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛna niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if the farm chemicals I buy from local sellers are genuine and safe for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋbii ni hɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Genuine agro-chemicals have official registration seals, clear expiration dates, and printed instructions on the bottle. Buying only from licensed agro-dealers protects your crops from fake chemicals that can burn your plants or fail to kill pests.
ga: Okwaayeli tsofai diɛŋtsɛ yɛ maŋ woloŋmaa stamp. clear expiration date Ni aŋmala gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ awo tɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ohe nii kɛjɛ okwaayeli he jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɛ adɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsofai amalei ni ekolɛ shãŋ otsei lɛ loo egbeee tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe.

english: Is it true that using too much chemical fertilizer will spoil my soil after a few years?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ?

english: Yes, overusing chemical fertilizers can make the soil acidic and destroy healthy soil life over time. Mixing proper chemical fertilizer amounts with natural manure keeps the soil strong and fertile for long-term farming.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee acid ni efite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ futu adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How long should I wait to harvest my vegetables after spraying them with insect chemicals?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie shi lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa?

english: Every chemical has a safety waiting period, usually between 7 to 14 days, printed on the container. Waiting for this time allows the chemical to break down so the harvested crops are safe for people to eat.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni akala yɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ be nɛɛ ni tsofai lɛ akumɔ koni tsei ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbɔmɛi baanyɛ aye.

english: Why did the insect spray I bought fail to kill the caterpillars on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni mihe lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemicals may fail if they are fake, mixed with too much water, or sprayed at the wrong time. Spraying in the early morning or late evening when pests are active ensures the pesticide works properly.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ amɛji amalei. Akɛ nu babaoo loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ futuɔ mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli Ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is weak and needs extra nutrients to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni maná niyenii krokomɛi koni ekɛkwɛ nii kpakpai?

english: Weak soil causes crops to grow slowly, stay short, and turn light green or yellow. Adding fertilizer or organic compost restores nutrients so the land gains strength to support healthy crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ baaha tsei lɛ adara blɛoo, amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after rain falls on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong wild roots that quickly grab water and soil nutrients before your crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the rainwater and soil food they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: When is the best time for me to ask an extension officer to visit my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabi mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni ebasara miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: It is best to invite an extension officer before planting to test your soil, during crop growth to catch early pest problems, and before applying new chemicals so you get proper usage advice.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ̃ sɛɛkwɛlɔ ko nine dani odu koni eka shikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛ. yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ be mli koni ana naagbai ni kɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ yɛ shishijee mli kɛ dani okɛ tsofai heei baatsu nii koni ekɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni sa ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ aha bo.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, air, and soil food. Proper plant spacing gives each crop enough room to expand and produce a large harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during short dry spells even when the soil looks dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ moŋ

english: Dark soil can still lose moisture quickly if it lacks organic matter to trap water. Adding organic manure or leaving crop residues on the surface helps the soil hold moisture longer during dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ afite ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha nu ahi mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo ashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.
